overview: When a doubting young boy takes an extraordinary train ride to the North Pole, he embarks on a journey of self-discovery that shows him that the wonder of life never fades for those who believe.
tagline: This holiday season... believe.
title: The Polar Express
plot:
The Polar Express is a 2004 animated film directed by Robert Zemeckis, produced by Castle Rock Entertainment, and based on the children's book of the same name by Chris Van Allsburg.

The story follows a young boy who lives in a small town with his parents. On Christmas Eve, he lies awake in bed, feeling lonely and disconnected from the magic of the holiday season. As he drifts off to sleep, he is visited by a mysterious train called the Polar Express, which arrives at his house and whisks him away on an adventure.

The boy boards the train, where he meets other children who are also traveling to the North Pole. They are greeted by the conductor, who welcomes them aboard with a warm smile. As they journey through the night, the boy experiences incredible sights and sensations: snow-covered landscapes, sparkling stars, and even a visit from Santa Claus himself.

However, not all of the passengers on the train are what they seem. One boy is revealed to be a "bad boy" who has been naughty throughout the year, and he is punished by being forced to sit in a cold, dark room with no toys or treats. The other children, including our protagonist, are rewarded for their good behavior.

As the journey continues, the boy begins to question whether the entire experience was just a dream. He wonders if he really did board the Polar Express, or if it was all just his imagination. But as he looks out the window of the train, he sees the Northern Lights dancing in the sky, and he knows that something magical is real.

The film's climax features a heartwarming moment when Santa Claus presents each child with a special gift: a golden ticket to ride on the Polar Express forever. The boy returns home, feeling transformed by his experience and filled with a newfound sense of wonder and joy.

Throughout the film, Zemeckis uses innovative visual effects to bring the world of the Polar Express to life. The animation is stunning, with beautifully rendered landscapes and characters that seem almost real. The voice cast, including Tom Hanks as the narrator and several other notable actors, adds depth and warmth to the story.

Overall, The Polar Express is a timeless tale of childhood wonder and the magic of the holiday season. It's a film that will leave audiences of all ages feeling inspired and uplifted, with its themes of kindness, generosity, and the power of imagination.

overview: A 17-year-old girl uses her wits, survival skills, and compassion to fight for her life, and those of her fellow classmates, against a group of live-streaming school shooters.
title: Run Hide Fight
plot:
Run Hide Fight is an American action thriller written and directed by Kyle Rankin, premiered in 2020, about a teenage girl who fights back against a group of shooters who take over her high school. Its title comes from the "Run. Hide. Fight." guidance for active-shooter situations. Isabel May stars as Zoe Hull, with Thomas Jane as her father Todd, Radha Mitchell as her late mother Jennifer, Eli Brown as the ringleader Tristan Voy, Olly Sholotan as her friend Lewis, Treat Williams as Sheriff Tarsy and Barbara Crampton as Mrs. Crawford.

Zoe, still grieving her mother, has a strained relationship with her father. On her way to school she sees classmate Chris Jelick planting a device in a field, but dismisses it as a prank. As incendiary devices go off around town to distract first responders, a van carrying four shooters, Tristan, Chris, his sister Anna and Kip Quade, smashes into the cafeteria. Tristan forces Lewis to livestream the attack and takes most of the students hostage, admitting that he simply craves notoriety; he kills the principal and lets an unarmed guard flee. Zoe, who escaped through a bathroom ceiling, returns to warn students and lead them out, realising that the lockdown only helps the attackers corner their victims.

Zoe kills Anna in self-defence and overpowers Kip, who confesses he was avenging middle-school bullying; she reminds him that his victims had nothing to do with it. She asks the sheriff to pull the media cameras away so students can escape, but Tristan sees through the ruse and threatens to kill hostages unless she shows herself. A remorseful Kip agrees to ambush his partners and is killed, while Zoe rescues the wounded Lewis and admits she returns his feelings. Lewis warns her that the van is packed with explosives. Todd, who has taken up a sniper position outside, shoots Chris before he can execute Zoe, and Zoe takes over the livestream to deny Tristan his fame, then reverses the rigged van so that it explodes in an empty car park. Tristan fakes his own death, but Zoe, reconciled with her father, spots him fleeing into the woods, shoots him with her father's rifle and leaves him to die.

Shot in Red Oak, Texas, on a budget of about $1.5 million, the film premiered at the Venice Film Festival on 10 September 2020 and was released by The Daily Wire on its subscription platform in January 2021. Reviews were largely negative, with 30% on Rotten Tomatoes, though some critics praised its young cast.

overview: A celebrated military contractor returns to the site of his greatest career triumphs and re-connects with a long-ago love while unexpectedly falling for the hard-charging Air Force watchdog assigned to him.
tagline: Sometimes you have to say goodbye before you can say hello.
title: Aloha
plot:
Aloha is a 2015 American romantic drama film directed by Cameron Crowe. The movie explores complex and often conflicting emotions, particularly in the context of love, loyalty, and cultural identity.

At its core, Aloha delves into the theme of unrequited love and the pain it can cause. The protagonist, Allison Ng (played by Emma Stone), is a young lawyer who returns to her hometown on the island of Oahu after years away, only to find herself rekindling an old flame with her former best friend, Captain Steve Edwards (played by Bradley Cooper). As their relationship deepens, Allison must confront the choices she made in the past and the consequences that have shaped her present.

The film also grapples with issues of cultural identity and the complexities of belonging. The character of Captain Steve is a quintessential American, while Allison's family has been deeply rooted in Hawaiian culture for generations. This dichotomy serves as a backdrop for exploring themes of assimilation, tradition, and the tension between preserving one's heritage and embracing change.

Furthermore, Aloha touches on the theme of guilt and redemption. The character of Captain Steve is haunted by past mistakes, particularly those related to his business dealings with Allison's family. As their relationship progresses, he must confront these demons and find a way to make amends and start anew.

Throughout the film, Crowe masterfully weaves together these themes, creating a nuanced and thought-provoking exploration of the human experience. The result is a movie that is both poignant and humorous, with a strong focus on character development and emotional depth.

original_title: 劇場版 HUNTER×HUNTER 緋色の幻影
overview: Gon, Killua, Kurapika and Leorio reunite to face a dangerous opponent who was once a member of the Phantom Troupe.
title: Hunter x Hunter: Phantom Rouge
plot:
Hunter x Hunter: Phantom Rouge is a 2013 Japanese anime film directed by Tsuyoshi Tozuka and produced by Madhouse. The movie serves as a sequel to the original Hunter x Hunter series.

The main themes of Hunter x Hunter: Phantom Rouge include:

1. **Redemption and Sacrifice**: The story revolves around Killua's quest for revenge against Meruem, the King of the Chimera Ant Kingdom. However, as Killua delves deeper into his mission, he begins to question whether his desire for revenge is truly justified. This theme explores the consequences of seeking revenge and the importance of finding redemption through selfless acts.

2. **Friendship and Loyalty**: The film highlights the strong bonds between the main characters, particularly Killua's relationships with Gon, Kurapika, and Leorio. Their loyalty to one another drives the plot forward and serves as a reminder that true friends will go to great lengths to protect each other.

3. **Power and Corruption**: Meruem's character represents the corrupting influence of power, as he uses his abilities to manipulate and control others. The film critiques the dangers of unchecked ambition and the consequences of allowing power to consume one's soul.

4. **Personal Growth and Self-Discovery**: Throughout the story, the characters face various challenges that force them to confront their own strengths, weaknesses, and motivations. This theme emphasizes the importance of self-awareness, growth, and embracing one's true potential.

5. **The Nature of Evil**: The Chimera Ant Kingdom serves as a metaphor for the destructive nature of evil, highlighting its ability to corrupt and consume everything in its path. The film raises questions about the origins of evil and whether it can be eradicated or if it is an inherent part of human nature.

Overall, Hunter x Hunter: Phantom Rouge explores complex themes that add depth to the story, while maintaining the action-packed and suspenseful elements that fans of the series have come to expect.

keywords.name: based on myths, legends or folklore

overview: Perseus tries to live a quieter life as a village fisherman while - dangerously weakened by humanity's lack of devotion - the gods are losing control of the long-imprisoned Titans and their ferocious leader, Kronos.
tagline: Feel the Wrath
title: Wrath of the Titans
plot:
Wrath of the Titans is a 2012 American fantasy adventure film directed by Jonathan Liebesman and written by Dan Abnett, Andy Bean, and Stephen Morgan. The movie is a sequel to the 2010 film Clash of the Titans.

The story begins with Perseus (Sam Worthington), the demigod son of Zeus, living in ancient Greece with his wife, Andromeda (Rosamund Pike), and their daughter, Helen (Talia Balsam). However, their peaceful life is disrupted when Hades (Danny Huston), the god of the underworld, kidnaps Perseus' wife and threatens to marry her unless Zeus sends one of his own children as a ransom.

Perseus sets out on a perilous journey to rescue Andromeda, accompanied by the wise man Cratus (Liam Neeson) and the warrior Athena (Gemma Arterton). Along the way, they encounter various mythological creatures, including the Minotaur, Medusa, and the Cyclops Polyphemus.

As Perseus navigates the underworld, he discovers that Hades has stolen Zeus' lightning bolt, which gives him immense power. The gods of Olympus are powerless without their most powerful weapon, and Hades plans to use it to conquer the world.

Perseus eventually reaches Hades' throne room, where he confronts his father-in-law and engages in a fierce battle with the god of the underworld. With the help of Athena and Cratus, Perseus manages to defeat Hades and shatter his helmet, rendering him powerless.

However, the journey is not without its costs. Perseus' mother, Queen Calliope (Polly Shannon), is killed by Hades, and he also suffers a mortal wound. As he lies dying, Athena uses her powers to heal him, but at great personal cost.

The movie concludes with Perseus returning to Greece as a hero, having saved the world from Hades' tyranny. However, the film ends on a somber note, suggesting that Perseus' journey has changed him forever and that he may not be the same demigod who set out at the beginning of the story.

Overall, Wrath of the Titans is an action-packed adventure film with plenty of mythological creatures and epic battles. While it received mixed reviews from critics, fans of the original Clash of the Titans were pleased to see their favorite characters return in a new and exciting way.

overview: A young teacher inspires her class of at-risk students to learn tolerance, apply themselves, and pursue education beyond high school.
tagline: Their story. Their world. Their future.
title: Freedom Writers
plot:
Freedom Writers is a 2007 American biographical drama film written and directed by Richard LaGravenese, starring Hilary Swank as teacher Erin Gruwell, with Scott Glenn, Imelda Staunton, Patrick Dempsey and Mario. It is based on the 1999 book The Freedom Writers Diary, compiled by Gruwell and her students from the real diary entries they wrote in her English class at Woodrow Wilson Classical High School in Long Beach, California. The title plays on the Freedom Riders, the multiracial civil rights activists who tested the desegregation of interstate buses in 1961.

In 1994, two years after the Los Angeles riots, Erin begins teaching freshman English to at-risk students at Woodrow Wilson High, a once prestigious school where racial tensions now run high. Her class is divided along gang and racial lines, the students ignore her, and fights break out constantly. When Paco, the boyfriend of her student Eva Benitez, opens fire outside a convenience store and kills the boyfriend of Eva's Cambodian classmate Sindy, another student, Grant, is arrested for the crime, and Eva prepares to protect her own in court. Erin's breakthrough comes when she turns a racist caricature drawn by a student into a lesson about the Holocaust, of which nearly all of them have never heard. Through exercises such as "the line game", the students recognize the traumas they share, and Erin gives each of them a composition book to use as a diary, in which they write about eviction, abuse and the deaths of loved ones. She takes on two part-time jobs to pay for books and activities, organizes visits from Holocaust survivors and a trip to the Museum of Tolerance, and helps the class raise money to bring Miep Gies, who sheltered Anne Frank's family, to speak to them. Inspired, Eva tells the truth at Grant's trial, at great personal risk. Erin's devotion, however, puts a strain on her marriage to Scott and earns her the hostility of colleagues, including department chair Margaret Campbell, who resent her unorthodox methods, and she must fight the administration for the chance to keep teaching her students as they move through school, while they compile their writings into a book.

Freedom Writers premiered at the Westwood Village Theatre on January 4, 2007, and was released by Paramount Pictures the next day. It received positive reviews, with 69% of 124 critics' reviews positive on Rotten Tomatoes, and was a modest commercial success, grossing $43.6 million worldwide on a budget of $21 million.

overview: After breaking up with Mark Darcy, Bridget Jones's 'happily ever after' hasn't quite gone according to plan. Fortysomething and single again, she decides to focus on her job as top news producer and surround herself with old friends and new. For once, Bridget has everything completely under control. What could possibly go wrong? Then her love life takes a turn and Bridget meets a dashing American named Jack, the suitor who is everything Mr. Darcy is not. In an unlikely twist she finds herself pregnant, but with one hitch she can only be fifty percent sure of the identity of her baby's father.
tagline: Relationship status: beyond complicated
title: Bridget Jones's Baby
plot:
Bridget Jones's Baby (2016) is a romantic comedy film directed by Sharon Maguire, produced by StudioCanal and Working Title Films, not Miramax.

The main themes of Bridget Jones's Baby (2016) include:

1. **Love and Relationships**: The movie explores the complexities of love, relationships, and parenthood. Bridget navigates her feelings for Mark Darcy and Jack Qwant, while also learning to co-parent with them.
2. **Self-Discovery**: As Bridget embarks on a new journey as a single mother, she discovers more about herself, including her strengths, weaknesses, and desires.
3. **Identity**: The film delves into the theme of identity, particularly for women, as Bridget struggles to balance her personal life with her responsibilities as a mother.
4. **Friendship**: The movie highlights the importance of female friendships, as Bridget's relationships with her friends, including Shaz and Jude, provide support and guidance throughout her journey.

The film received mixed reviews from critics but was a commercial success, grossing over $140 million worldwide.

overview: Robert Neville is a scientist who was unable to stop the spread of the terrible virus that was incurable and man-made. Immune, Neville is now the last human survivor in what is left of New York City and perhaps the world. For three years, Neville has faithfully sent out daily radio messages, desperate to find any other survivors who might be out there. But he is not alone.
tagline: The last man on Earth is not alone
title: I Am Legend
plot:
I Am Legend is a post-apocalyptic science fiction film directed by Francis Lawrence, based on the novel of the same name by Richard Matheson. The movie stars Will Smith as Robert Neville, a military scientist who finds himself to be one of the last humans on Earth.

The story begins in 2006, where Robert Neville (Will Smith) is working for the United States Army at a biological research facility in New York City. He is part of a team that has been studying a virus known as the "Krippin Virus" which causes its hosts to become violent and zombie-like creatures after infection. The virus was created by a scientist named Dr. Krippin, who had been experimenting with it before his death.

As the outbreak occurs, Robert Neville is one of the few survivors, but he soon realizes that he is not alone on Earth. He finds himself surrounded by hordes of infected humans, which he has dubbed "Virals." The Virals are fast, agile, and seemingly unstoppable, making them a formidable threat to human survival.

As the years pass, Robert Neville becomes increasingly isolated, with no contact with other humans. He spends his days scavenging for food and supplies, while also trying to find a cure for the virus. He sets up traps and defenses around his home in an attempt to protect himself from the Virals, but he knows that it's only a matter of time before they break through.

One day, Robert Neville receives a package containing a small dog, which becomes his companion and friend. The dog helps him to stay sane and provides emotional support during his lonely existence. As the years go by, Robert Neville begins to notice changes in himself, as he starts to exhibit some of the same characteristics as the Virals.

The turning point comes when Robert Neville discovers that the virus is not just a simple infection, but rather a complex genetic mutation that has altered his own DNA. He realizes that he may be one of the few remaining humans who are immune to the virus, and that he may hold the key to finding a cure.

As Robert Neville delves deeper into the mystery of the virus, he becomes increasingly obsessed with finding a way to restore humanity to its former glory. He sets out on a perilous journey across New York City, searching for any signs of life or clues to the virus's origins.

In the end, Robert Neville discovers that the only remaining human survivor is a young girl who has been living in an abandoned church. Together, they form a bond and work towards finding a cure for the virus. However, as they near their goal, Robert Neville realizes that he may be too late to save humanity, and that the world may never be the same again.

The movie ends with Robert Neville and the young girl escaping from New York City in a helicopter, leaving behind the ruins of civilization. As they fly away, Robert Neville looks out at the desolate landscape, knowing that he has lost his way and that the world will never be the same again.

overview: A provocative and edgy radio host must play a dangerous game of cat and mouse with a mysterious caller who's kidnapped his family and is threatening to blow up the whole station.
tagline: A dangerous game. Played live.
title: On the Line
plot:
On the Line is a 2022 American thriller written, produced and directed by Romuald Boulanger. Mel Gibson stars as Elvis Cooney, a Los Angeles radio shock jock, with William Moseley as the intern Dylan, Alia Seror-O'Neill as the switchboard operator Mary, Paul Spera as the mysterious caller Gary and Kevin Dillon as Justin, a rival host.

Elvis leaves his wife and daughter for his midnight show at the station KLAT, where he welcomes the new intern, Dylan, with a prank. Partway through the broadcast, a caller named Gary claims to be at Elvis's house holding his wife Olivia and daughter Adria hostage, and threatens to kill them if he is cut off. Gary blames Elvis for the suicide of Lauren, a former switchboard operator who was the target of his abuse and crude jokes. He forces Elvis to admit on air that he has slept with Mary, then orders him to jump from the roof. A faked jump fails, and gunshots ring out over the line. Gary then reveals that the family is alive and inside the building. He has been there all along, has killed the security guard and has rigged the station with explosives. Elvis has 40 minutes to find them.

Elvis and Dylan search the building, which Gary watches through security cameras. Elvis refuses Gary's order to kill Tony, an old friend caught stealing computers. In the control room they find Justin, the host of the time slot Elvis covets, apparently shot dead, and later Tony hanging in a hallway. Elvis overpowers Gary with a box cutter, but Gary holds a dead man's switch, and Olivia and Adria are wearing bomb vests on the terrace. Gary forces a SWAT officer to transfer the vests to Dylan, shoots the officer and releases the switch, and nothing happens. Elvis and Gary burst out laughing as the supposed victims reappear: the whole night was an elaborate prank on the intern. When the crew chases the stunned Dylan with a microphone, he falls down the stairs and appears to die. The next morning, a shattered Elvis swears he is quitting radio, only to learn that Dylan, really a stuntman named Max, faked his death in a second prank aimed at Elvis himself for his birthday, which he believed everyone had forgotten. Elvis promises revenge.

Filming began in Paris in June 2021. Saban Films acquired the American rights in May 2022 and released the film that November. Reviews were negative. Rotten Tomatoes reported 20% approval, with its consensus saying a solid premise is undone by a story that stumbles over its own twists toward a disastrous ending.

original_title: ゴブリンスレイヤー -GOBLIN'S CROWN-
overview: Goblin Slayer and his party head up to the snowy mountains in the north after receiving that request from the Sword Maiden to find any information on the Noble Fencer that disappeared after leaving to slay some goblins. A small village gets attacked, they encounter a mysterious chapel, and something about how these goblins are acting bothers the Goblin slayer.  In order to save the captured Noble Fencer, the Goblin Slayer and his party head to an ancient fortress covered in snow to face off with a powerful foe and a horde of goblins!
tagline: He does not let anyone roll the dice
title: Goblin Slayer: Goblin's Crown
plot:
Goblin Slayer: Goblin's Crown is a 2020 Japanese animated dark fantasy film based on Kumo Kagyu's light novel series Goblin Slayer, illustrated by Noboru Kannatsuki. Produced by White Fox with the returning staff and cast of the 2018 television anime, it was directed by Takaharu Ozaki from a screenplay by Hideyuki Kurata, with music by Kenichirō Suehiro, and adapts the fifth volume of the novels. Yūichirō Umehara voices the title character, with Yui Ogura as Priestess, Nao Tōyama as High Elf Archer, Yuichi Nakamura as Dwarf Shaman, Tomokazu Sugita as Lizard Priest, Maaya Uchida as Guild Girl and Yuka Iguchi as Cow Girl.

In a fantasy world where adventurers take contracts from the Guild, the nameless Goblin Slayer is a silver-ranked warrior devoted solely to exterminating goblins, having survived as a child the goblin raid that destroyed his village. The Sword Maiden asks him and his party to travel to the snowy mountains of the north to learn what became of the Noble Fencer, a young noblewoman whose party of novice adventurers vanished after setting out to hunt goblins. Along the way they find a small village under attack and a mysterious chapel, and Goblin Slayer is troubled by the unusual way these goblins behave. They rescue the Noble Fencer, who has survived horrific abuse at the hands of her captors but refuses to abandon the fight, determined to recover the sword they stole from her and take revenge. The trail leads to an ancient fortress buried in snow, which the goblins defend like an army, and there the party must face a goblin leader able to wield magic, an ability previously believed to belong only to the human-like races. The Noble Fencer finds strength in her bond with Priestess and High Elf Archer as the battle unfolds.

Goblin's Crown premiered in Japanese theaters on 1 February 2020 and was licensed by Crunchyroll. Its main story runs about an hour, preceded by a recap of the television series. Reviews were mostly unfavorable. Kim Morrissy of Anime News Network gave it a D, arguing that condensing an entire novel into roughly sixty minutes left its emotional moments without weight and made the Noble Fencer's recovery abrupt; she also criticized the goblins' convenient intelligence, the stilted animation and the decision to make the creatures increasingly human-like, though she praised the music and ending theme. Other reviewers enjoyed the snowy setting and the action but also noted the long recap and rushed character development.

overview: Frank Martin puts the driving gloves on to deliver Valentina, the kidnapped daughter of a Ukranian government official, from Marseilles to Odessa on the Black Sea. En route, he has to contend with thugs who want to intercept Valentina's safe delivery and not let his personal feelings get in the way of his dangerous objective.
tagline: This time, the rules are the same. Except one.
title: Transporter 3
plot:
Transporter 3 is a 2008 action film directed by Pierre Morel and starring Jason Statham as Frank Martin, a professional driver for hire. The movie takes place three years after the events of the second installment.

The story begins with Frank Martin (Jason Statham) living in Paris, where he has retired from his high-stakes driving business. However, his peaceful life is disrupted when an old acquaintance, Anna (Léa Seydoux), arrives at his doorstep. She informs him that her sister, Emma (Nina Foreman), a wealthy and beautiful woman, has been kidnapped by the Russian mafia.

The kidnappers demand that Frank deliver a package to the United States within 48 hours in exchange for Emma's safe return. Unbeknownst to Anna, the package contains a deadly virus that could wipe out millions of people if it falls into the wrong hands. As Frank agrees to take on the job, he is unaware of the true nature of the package and the danger it poses.

As Frank embarks on his mission, he encounters a new adversary, the ruthless and cunning Anatoly (Max von Sydow), who will stop at nothing to get what he wants. Along the way, Frank must use his exceptional driving skills and combat abilities to evade Anatoly's henchmen and stay one step ahead of the game.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Anna is not what she seems. She has her own motives for wanting Emma back, and Frank begins to suspect that she may be working with Anatoly. The tension builds as Frank navigates a complex web of deceit and betrayal, all while trying to deliver the package safely.

In the climactic final act, Frank faces off against Anatoly in an intense showdown at a cargo ship docked on the Seine River. With his driving skills put to the ultimate test, Frank must use every ounce of skill and cunning to outmaneuver Anatoly's henchmen and prevent the package from falling into the wrong hands.

In the end, Frank successfully delivers the package, but not before discovering that Anna was indeed working with Anatoly all along. The movie concludes with Frank returning to Paris, his reputation as a driver for hire intact, but his personal life forever changed by the events of the film.

Overall, Transporter 3 is an action-packed thrill ride that delivers on its promise of high-octane driving sequences and intense hand-to-hand combat. While it may not be as memorable as some of Jason Statham's other films, it remains a solid addition to the Transporter franchise.

overview: Ella lives in a magical world in which each child, at the moment of their birth, is given a virtuous "gift" from a fairy godmother. Ella's so-called gift, however, is obedience. This birthright proves itself to be quite the curse once Ella finds herself in the hands of several unscrupulous characters whom she quite literally cannot disobey. Determined to gain control of her life and decisions, Ella sets off on a journey to find her fairy godmother who she hopes will lift the curse. The path, however, isn't easy -- Ella must outwit a slew of unpleasant obstacles including ogres, giants, wicked stepsisters, elves and Prince Charmont's evil uncle, who wants to take over the crown and rule the kingdom.
tagline: Get enchanted
title: Ella Enchanted
plot:
Ella Enchanted is a 2004 jukebox musical fantasy comedy film directed by Tommy O'Haver and written by Karen McCullah Lutz and Kirsten Smith, loosely based on Gail Carson Levine's 1997 novel. A satire of the fairy tale genre, it stars Anne Hathaway as Ella of Frell and Hugh Dancy as Prince "Char" Charmont, with Cary Elwes as his scheming uncle Sir Edgar, Vivica A. Fox as the fairy Lucinda, Joanna Lumley as Ella's stepmother Dame Olga and Jimi Mistry as Benny. An international co-production between the United States, Ireland and the United Kingdom, it was filmed in Ireland at Ardmore Studios and on location in County Wicklow in 2002.

At her birth, Ella receives a misguided "gift" from the fairy Lucinda: she must instantly and literally obey any command she is given. Before dying, Ella's mother warns her to keep it secret and tells her that something in her is stronger than any spell. Years later, Ella's father marries the cruel socialite Dame Olga, whose daughter Hattie discovers the secret and uses it to humiliate her. Having caught the eye of Prince Char, a reluctant teen heartthrob who invites her to his coronation ball, Ella sets out to find Lucinda and have the spell lifted, taking along Benny, the boyfriend of the household fairy Mandy, who has accidentally turned him into a talking book. On her journey she rescues Slannen, an elf who dreams of becoming a lawyer, and when ogres capture them, Char comes to the rescue. As they travel together, Ella opens Char's eyes to the unjust laws against elves and giants passed by Sir Edgar, the King Regent, and the two fall in love. Learning of Ella's curse, Edgar, who secretly murdered Char's father, orders her to kill the prince at midnight and keep it secret, so that he can take the throne. Ella has herself chained to a distant tree to wait out the command, but Lucinda frees her, insisting that Ella must break the spell herself, leaving her to find the inner strength her mother spoke of before the coronation.

Released by Miramax Films on April 9, 2004, Ella Enchanted received mixed reviews and holds a 51% rating on Rotten Tomatoes. It grossed about $27.4 million worldwide and was considered a box-office bomb.

overview: Like millions of kids around the world, Santiago harbors the dream of being a professional footballer... However, living in the Barrios section of Los Angeles, he thinks it is only that--a dream. Until one day an extraordinary turn of events has him trying out for Premiership club Newcastle United.
tagline: Every Dream Has A Beginning
title: Goal!
plot:
Goal!, also known as Goal! The Dream Begins, is a 2005 British sports drama film directed by Danny Cannon from a screenplay by Mike Jefferies, Adrian Butchart, Dick Clement and Ian La Frenais. The first installment of the Goal! trilogy, it stars Kuno Becker as Santiago Muñez, an amateur player who gets an unlikely chance at professional football, with Alessandro Nivola, Stephen Dillane and Anna Friel. Made with the cooperation of FIFA, it features real teams and players, and Adidas reportedly contributed $50 million toward its budget and marketing.

Santiago, an undocumented Mexican immigrant in Los Angeles, plays for a local team while working as a gardener with his father, Hernan, and as a busboy. Glen Foy, a former player and scout, spots him and arranges a trial with Newcastle United. Hernan, who doubts his son's prospects, takes Santiago's savings to buy a truck, but his grandmother, Mercedes, secretly gives him the money to go. In Newcastle, Santiago struggles in the mud and under pressure from teammate Hughie McGowan, but manager Erik Dornhelm grants him a month's trial. Fearing rejection, he hides his asthma from the club nurse, Roz Harmison. Before the decisive reserve match, Hughie destroys his inhaler, and after a poor performance Santiago is let go.

On the way to the airport, his taxi picks up Gavin Harris, a talented but undisciplined recent Newcastle signing, who learns about the asthma and tells Erik. Erik keeps Santiago on condition that he receives treatment, and Santiago moves in with Gavin. Coming on as a substitute against Fulham in his first-team debut, he wins a penalty that secures victory, as Hernan watches proudly on television, though Erik scolds him for selfish play. A night out with Gavin lands the pair in The Sun, Santiago's friend Jamie suffers a career-ending injury, and his friendship with Gavin frays. When Hernan dies of a heart attack, Santiago nearly flies home but stays after talking with Roz, with whom he begins a relationship. Picked to start the final game of the season against Liverpool, he sets up Gavin's late equalizer and then scores a free kick to win 3–2, earning Newcastle a Champions League place.

Buena Vista International released Goal! in the United Kingdom on 1 October 2005. Reviews were mixed, with 42% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 53; critics praised the football sequences but found the story full of sports film clichés.

overview: Inside a snowflake exists the magical land of Whoville. In Whoville, live the Whos, an almost mutated sort of Munchkin-like people. All the Whos love Christmas, yet just outside of their beloved Whoville lives the Grinch. The Grinch is a nasty creature that hates Christmas, and plots to steal it away from the Whos, whom he equally abhors. Yet a small child, Cindy Lou Who, decides to try befriending the Grinch.
production_companies: LUNI Productions GmbH and Company KG
tagline: He puts the mean in green.
title: How the Grinch Stole Christmas
plot:
How the Grinch Stole Christmas, also titled Dr. Seuss' How the Grinch Stole Christmas, is a 2000 American Christmas comedy film directed by Ron Howard and written by Jeffrey Price and Peter S. Seaman, loosely based on Dr. Seuss's 1957 children's book. The second adaptation of the book after the 1966 animated television special, and the first Dr. Seuss book adapted as a live-action feature, it stars Jim Carrey as the Grinch, a misanthropic green creature who sets out to ruin the Christmas celebrations of Whoville, with Jeffrey Tambor, Christine Baranski and Taylor Momsen, and narration by Anthony Hopkins.

The Grinch lives in a cave on Mount Crumpit and despises Christmas and the cheerful Whos below. After meeting him at the post office, young Cindy Lou Who learns his story: raised by two elderly Who women, he had a crush on his classmate Martha May Whovier, but when the bully Augustus MayWho mocked his hairy face, he tried to shave, cut himself, and fled to the mountain after the class laughed at him. Hoping to set things right, Cindy nominates the Grinch as the town's Holiday Cheermeister, over the objections of MayWho, now mayor. The Grinch accepts after learning that Martha will attend, and he begins to enjoy the festivities, until MayWho humiliates him with a gift of an electric razor and proposes to Martha with a new car. The Grinch denounces the Whos' materialism, wrecks the celebration and returns to his cave.

Learning that the Whos will celebrate anyway, the Grinch disguises himself as Santa Claus, dresses his dog, Max, as a reindeer, and descends on Whoville to steal every present, decoration and scrap of food. On Christmas morning, MayWho blames Cindy, but her father, the postmaster Lou Lou Who, reminds the town that Christmas means more than presents, and the Whos gather to sing. Hearing them from the mountaintop, the Grinch realizes the true meaning of Christmas, and his heart grows three sizes. He saves Cindy and the sleigh from falling into a gorge, returns everything and apologizes. Martha gives back MayWho's ring and declares her love for the Grinch, who hosts the Christmas feast in his cave.

Released by Universal Pictures on November 17, 2000, the film grossed $350.6 million worldwide, the sixth-highest gross of the year. Reviews were mixed, with 50% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 46; critics praised Carrey but preferred the animated special.

overview: Poe Dameron and BB-8 must face the greedy crime boss Graballa the Hutt, who has purchased Darth Vader’s castle and is renovating it into the galaxy’s first all-inclusive Sith-inspired luxury hotel.
tagline: Rest in pieces.
title: LEGO Star Wars Terrifying Tales
plot:
Lego Star Wars: Terrifying Tales is a 2021 animated special based on the Star Wars franchise, produced by Lucasfilm Animation and The Lego Group with Atomic Cartoons. Like The Lego Star Wars Holiday Special, it was directed by Ken Cunningham from a script by David Shayne, and it serves as a stand-alone sequel to the Star Wars sequel trilogy. The voice cast includes Jake Green, Raphael Alejandro, Dana Snyder, Tony Hale and Christian Slater.

Long before the events of the original trilogy, Emperor Palpatine and Darth Vader leave Vader's loyal servant Vaneé in charge of Castle Vader on the volcanic planet Mustafar. After the events of The Rise of Skywalker, Resistance pilot Poe Dameron and his droid BB-8 make an emergency landing on Mustafar, where they meet the crime boss Graballa the Hutt, who has bought the castle and is turning it into the galaxy's first all-inclusive Sith-themed luxury hotel. Poe befriends Graballa's young mechanic Dean, who dreams of becoming a pilot, and agrees to record a promotional video for the hotel in exchange for Dean repairing his X-wing. While they wait, the castle's caretaker Vaneé and his assistant droid lead the visitors on a tour, telling three eerie tales tied to ancient artifacts and famous villains from across the saga. The first, told with the helmet of Ren, shows how the young Ben Solo was drawn to the dark side by the leader of the Knights of Ren. The second, centered on the ancient Sith lightsaber known as the Saber of Scardont, follows Maul and General Grievous as they compete for the weapon to win Palpatine's favor. The third, a twist on the classic story "The Monkey's Paw", imagines Luke Skywalker granted wishes by a Wookiee's paw that send him to the dark side alongside his father. All the while, Vaneé is manipulating the Force-sensitive Dean into unlocking the castle's vaults and the Temple of Mustafar, and Poe begins to suspect that the caretaker has sinister plans for the Sith relics he is gathering, leading to a battle for the boy's future.

The special was released exclusively on Disney+ on October 1, 2021. All five critics' reviews counted by the aggregator Rotten Tomatoes were positive.

original_title: Don't Be Afraid of the Dark
overview: A young girl sent to live with her father and his new girlfriend discovers creatures in her new home who want to claim her as one of their own.
tagline: Fear is never just make believe
title: Don't Be Afraid of the Dark
plot:
Don't Be Afraid of the Dark is a 2010 fantasy horror film that delves into the complexities of family dynamics, childhood fears, and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy. The movie follows a young girl named Gretchen who moves to a new home with her father and stepmother, only to discover that their house has a dark history.

At its core, Don't Be Afraid of the Dark is a film about the fragility of childhood innocence and the devastating consequences of unresolved family conflicts. The story explores how past traumas can shape our perceptions of the world and ourselves, often manifesting in irrational fears and phobias.

The movie also touches on themes of isolation and disconnection, as Gretchen struggles to form connections with her stepmother and father, who seem more interested in their own relationships than in nurturing a sense of belonging for their daughter. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that each character is hiding secrets and fears, which ultimately lead to a descent into darkness.

The film's use of fantasy elements serves as a metaphor for the complexities of human emotions and the ways in which our inner demons can manifest in unexpected ways. The dark creatures that inhabit the house represent the repressed fears and anxieties that we all try to keep hidden, but which can ultimately consume us if left unaddressed.

Overall, Don't Be Afraid of the Dark is a thought-provoking film that explores the darker aspects of human nature, family dynamics, and the fragility of childhood innocence.

belongs_to_collection.name: LEGO DC Comics Super Heroes Collection

original_title: LEGO DC: Shazam! Magic and Monsters
overview: It’s high time the Justice League took notice of Shazam, but joining the world’s greatest team of superheroes is a lot harder when they’ve all been turned into kids.
title: LEGO DC: Shazam! Magic and Monsters
plot:
LEGO DC: Shazam! Magic and Monsters is a 2018 animated film, not 2020, produced by Warner Bros. Animation. Here's the detailed plot:

The movie begins with Billy Batson, a teenager who discovers he has the power to transform into the adult superhero Shazam when he says the magic word "Shazam." However, this power comes with a warning from his mentor, Dr. Thaddeus Sivana: if Billy ever loses control of his powers, it could lead to catastrophic consequences.

As Billy struggles to balance his life as a teenager and a superhero, he is approached by a group of supervillains who are also seeking the power of Shazam. The main villain, Black Adam, is revealed to be Sivana's arch-nemesis from ancient Egypt. Black Adam seeks revenge against Sivana for stealing an ancient artifact that would grant him immense power.

The movie takes a turn when Billy and his friends, including Mary Bromfield (Wonder Woman), Pedro Peña (Blue Beetle), Darla Dudley (Batgirl), and Eugene Fitzpatrick (Aquaman), are transported to the world of Shazam. There, they meet the adult version of Billy, who is struggling to control his powers.

As Black Adam's plan unfolds, he unleashes a magical storm that threatens to destroy both worlds. The heroes must work together to stop Black Adam and save their respective worlds from destruction.

Throughout the movie, the characters face various challenges and obstacles as they navigate their new surroundings. Billy struggles to balance his life as a teenager with his responsibilities as Shazam, while the other heroes learn to adapt to their new powers and abilities.

In the end, the heroes successfully defeat Black Adam and shatter the magical artifact that was fueling his power. The movie concludes with Billy returning to his normal life as a teenager, but with a newfound appreciation for the responsibility that comes with being Shazam.

Overall, LEGO DC: Shazam! Magic and Monsters is an action-packed animated film that brings together iconic superheroes from the DC Universe in a fun and entertaining way.

overview: The amazing true story of Billy Moore, an English boxer incarcerated in Thailand’s most notorious prison. Thrown into a world of drugs and violence, he finds his best chance to escape is to fight his way out in prison Muay Thai tournaments.
tagline: The fight starts from inside.
title: A Prayer Before Dawn
plot:
A Prayer Before Dawn is a biographical drama film directed by Jonathan Hensleigh, based on the memoir of the same name by Billy Moore. The movie follows the true story of Billy Moore, an American prisoner who becomes a Muay Thai champion while serving time in Thailand's notorious Bang Kwang Prison.

The film begins with Billy (played by Joe Cole), a young American man from a troubled home, who is sentenced to 20 years in prison for armed robbery. After being transferred to the infamous Bang Kwang Prison, Billy struggles to adapt to the harsh conditions and brutal treatment meted out by the prison authorities.

One day, while exploring the prison's grounds, Billy stumbles upon a group of Thai prisoners who are practicing Muay Thai. Intrigued by their discipline and skill, Billy begins to learn the art form from one of the older inmates, Nong (played by Petchtai Wongkamlao), also known as "The Tiger".

As Billy delves deeper into the world of Muay Thai, he finds solace in the physical training and mental focus required for the sport. He quickly becomes a skilled fighter, earning the respect of his fellow inmates and even some of the prison guards.

However, Billy's newfound passion is threatened when he is forced to participate in a brutal fight against a group of rival prisoners. Despite being outnumbered, Billy uses his Muay Thai skills to emerge victorious, but not without sustaining serious injuries.

Throughout the film, Billy's journey is intercut with flashbacks of his life before prison, showcasing his troubled relationships and struggles with addiction. As he navigates the harsh realities of prison life, Billy finds a sense of purpose and redemption through his training and fighting.

As the story unfolds, Billy faces numerous challenges, including conflicts with rival prisoners, corrupt guards, and even a violent riot that threatens to destroy the fragile peace in the prison. Despite these obstacles, Billy perseveres, using his newfound skills to protect himself and those around him.

Ultimately, Billy's determination and skill lead to his release from prison after serving only 10 years of his sentence. The film ends with Billy returning home to the United States, forever changed by his experiences in Thailand and armed with a newfound sense of purpose and self-discipline.

Throughout the film, the cinematography is stunning, capturing the brutal beauty of the Thai landscape and the harsh realities of life in prison. The performances are also noteworthy, particularly from Joe Cole, who brings a depth and nuance to Billy's character that is both compelling and heartbreaking.

Overall, A Prayer Before Dawn is a powerful and moving film that explores themes of redemption, perseverance, and the transformative power of sport.

overview: Dating coach Alex 'Hitch' Hitchens mentors a bumbling client, Albert, who hopes to win the heart of the glamorous Allegra Cole. While Albert makes progress, Hitch faces his own romantic setbacks when proven techniques fail to work on Sara Melas, a tabloid reporter digging for dirt on Allegra Cole's love life. When Sara discovers Hitch's connection to Albert – now Allegra's boyfriend – it threatens to destroy both relationships.
tagline: The cure for the common man.
title: Hitch
plot:
Hitch is a romantic comedy film released in 2005, directed by Andy Tennant and produced by Columbia Pictures.

The movie follows the story of Alex Hitchens (played by Will Smith), a professional "date doctor" who helps men improve their dating lives. With his unique approach, he teaches them how to attract women and build relationships. However, despite his success with clients, Alex has never been able to find true love himself.

One day, Alex meets Sara Melas (played by Eva Mendes), a journalist assigned to write an article about him and his unconventional methods. Initially, their encounter is adversarial, as Sara is determined to expose the truth behind Alex's claims. However, as they spend more time together, they begin to develop feelings for each other.

As their relationship deepens, Alex must confront his own emotional baggage and learn to open up to Sara. He also has to deal with the challenges of being a "date doctor" in the public eye, as Sara's article threatens to expose his secrets.

Throughout the movie, Alex's character undergoes significant development. We see glimpses of his troubled past, including his difficult childhood and his struggles with commitment. As he falls for Sara, he begins to realize that true love requires vulnerability and trust.

The plot thickens when Sara's article is published, revealing Alex's true identity as a "date doctor." However, instead of being met with ridicule, the public responds positively to Alex's unique approach to relationships. This newfound acceptance allows him to be more open about his feelings for Sara.

In the end, Alex and Sara confess their love for each other and share a romantic kiss. The movie concludes on a hopeful note, suggesting that true love can conquer all, even for someone like Alex who has struggled with commitment in the past.

Overall, Hitch is a charming romantic comedy that explores themes of love, vulnerability, and self-discovery. Will Smith's performance as Alex Hitchens brings humor and heart to the film, making it an enjoyable watch for audiences.

original_title: Miraculous World : New York, les héros unis
overview: During a school field trip, Ladybug and Cat Noir meet the American superheroes, whom they have to save from an akumatised super-villain. They discover that Miraculous exist in the United States too.
title: Miraculous World: New York, United HeroeZ
plot:
Miraculous World: New York, United HeroeZ (Miraculous World : New York, les héros unis) is a 2020 French computer-animated superhero television film directed by Thomas Astruc, the creator of the series Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug & Cat Noir. Produced by Zagtoon, Method Animation and SAMG Animation in an international co-production that also involved TF1, Disney and Toei Animation, it was the first of a planned series of Miraculous World specials sending the characters to cities around the world. It premiered on Disney Channel in the United States on 25 September 2020 and in France the following day, and runs about 52 minutes. Anouck Hautbois and Benjamin Bollen voice Ladybug and Cat Noir in French, with Cristina Valenzuela and Bryce Papenbrook in the English version.

Set between the third and fourth seasons, the film follows Marinette Dupain-Cheng and her Parisian classmates on a school trip to New York for French-American Friendship Week. Marinette persuades Adrien Agreste's overprotective father, Gabriel, to let him come along, unaware that Gabriel, secretly the villain Hawk Moth, has his own reasons to travel: a Miraculous has surfaced in New York, an ancient eagle talon he hopes will help him revive his wife. On the flight the students are attacked by the technology-stealing villain Techno-Pirate and rescued by the United HeroeZ, the city's openly public superheroes, among them Majestia, the vigilante Knightowl, his rebellious young protégé Sparrow and the artificial intelligence Uncanny Valley. When Hawk Moth akumatises Techno-Pirate, Ladybug and Cat Noir must join forces with their American counterparts, who are not powered by Miraculouses, while Marinette struggles with her lingering feelings for Adrien.

Critics generally regarded it as an enjoyable outing for fans. Craig Holton of What The Craggus Saw called it slickly animated, wholesomely adventurous and full of invention, a successful leap to feature length that expands the show's mythology, though it offers little help to newcomers. Frédéric Bègue of Chronique Disney praised the comedy and drama between Ladybug and Cat Noir, the new heroes and the action scenes, but found the villain forgettable, the returning supporting characters sidelined and the rushed ending in need of more scenes. Marley Crusch of Bubbleblabber gave it 6 out of 10, deeming it a kids' superhero film that breaks no new ground but is worth watching.

overview: Contact between most towns on Earth has been severed. A small ring-like area in Eastern Europe still has electricity, and maybe even life is being reported from space. What military forces find outside the ring is shocking.
tagline: Who's going to save you when the world falls into darkness?
title: The Blackout
plot:
The Blackout (Russian: Аванпост, romanized: Avanpost, literally "Outpost") is a 2019 Russian science fiction action thriller film directed by Egor Baranov and starring Pyotr Fyodorov, with Lukerya Ilyashenko, Svetlana Ivanova, Aleksey Chadov and Kseniya Kutepova. It concerns a mysterious event that plunges the world into darkness, wiping out life everywhere except a small area of Eastern Europe. Originally conceived as a series, the project was reshaped into a feature after the first episode was shot, and about 70% of its running time involves computer graphics. Baranov described it as more anti-war than military spectacles such as Transformers and Top Gun, and real soldiers took part in the shoot, which wrapped in May 2019.

Shortly after a serviceman named Oleg goes on a date with Alena, the whole planet except Moscow and parts of Belarus, Ukraine and Finland is suddenly cut off and engulfed in darkness. Communications fail, the fate of billions is unknown, and the survivors in the region that becomes known as the Circle of Life build a defensive perimeter of military outposts while reconnaissance teams sent beyond it fail to return. The defenders face strange enemies, including a herd of bears that attacks one outpost after it loses power. In Moscow it emerges that some survivors from near the edge of the zone have developed psychic abilities, and one of them, Sasha, has a link to the attackers. A mysterious being named Eid approaches Sasha and a group of soldiers led by Marina, claiming that his immortal race seeded Earth 200 millennia ago with humanity as a weapon to destroy native intelligent life, and that his brother Ra is now mind-controlling the people outside the Circle in order to exterminate the remaining humans before an alien colony ship arrives. Joined by other surviving soldiers, including Oleg and Yura, Eid leads a mission to Kirov to destroy Ra, but his callousness and true intentions raise doubts about whether humanity has found a savior or a new master.

The film premiered at the Cinequest Film & Creativity Festival in San Jose, California, on 15 March 2019, and opened in Russia on 21 November 2019; Shout! Factory released it on VOD in 2020 as The Blackout: Invasion Earth. It received mixed reviews and grossed $2.8 million worldwide against a budget of about $4 million.

overview: Two warring gang families (one African-American, the other Chinese) maneuver for bragging rights to the Oakland, California, docks. Hang Sing and Trish O'Day uncover a trail of deceit that leaves most of the warring factions dead … or worse!
tagline: In the city ruled by criminals, two families have forgotten their fear. He will make them remember.
title: Romeo Must Die
plot:
Romeo Must Die is a 2000 martial arts action film directed by Andrzej Bartkowiak and starring Jet Li, Aaliyah, and Jason Statham.

The movie begins with the introduction of Han Song (Jet Li), a Chinese-American martial artist who seeks revenge against the Triads for killing his father. Han's quest for vengeance is motivated by a personal tragedy: his father was killed in a fight with the Triads when he was just a child, and Han has been training to avenge him ever since.

Meanwhile, in Los Angeles, a young woman named Trish O'Day (Aaliyah) becomes embroiled in a gang war between the Chinese and Japanese Yakuza. The conflict escalates into violence, with both sides seeking to gain control of the city's underworld.

As Han navigates the treacherous world of organized crime, he meets Keiko (Mai Takara), a Japanese woman who is somehow connected to his father's death. Through her, Han discovers that his father was involved in a secret alliance between the Chinese and Japanese Triads, which aimed to take down their common enemy: the Yakuza.

As tensions rise, Han finds himself caught in the middle of a deadly conflict between the two rival gangs. With the help of Keiko and her brother, Jax (Jason Statham), Han must use his martial arts skills to survive and bring justice to those responsible for his father's death.

Throughout the movie, the action unfolds at a breakneck pace, with intense fight scenes that showcase Jet Li's impressive martial arts abilities. The film also explores themes of loyalty, honor, and family, as Han struggles to reconcile his own identity as a Chinese-American with his desire for revenge against the Triads.

As the story reaches its climax, Han confronts the leader of the Triads, Tiger Chen (John Lone), in an epic showdown that will determine the fate of both gangs. In the end, Han emerges victorious, but not without scars – both physical and emotional.

Ultimately, Romeo Must Die is a classic action movie with a richly detailed world and memorable characters. While it received mixed reviews from critics at the time of its release, the film has since become a cult classic, celebrated for its innovative blend of martial arts and gangster cinema.

overview: Pinnacle records has the perfect plan to get their sinking company back on track: a comeback concert in LA featuring Aldous Snow, a fading rockstar who has dropped off the radar in recent years. Record company intern Aaron Green is faced with the monumental task of bringing his idol, out of control rock star Aldous Snow, back to LA for his comeback show.
tagline: Aaron Green has 72 hours to get a Rock Star from London to L.A. Pray for him.
title: Get Him to the Greek
plot:
Get Him to the Greek is a 2010 American comedy film directed by Nicholas Stoller and written by Jon Lucas and Scott Moore. The movie stars Russell Brand, Jonah Hill, and Sean Combs.

The main theme of Get Him to the Greek revolves around the journey of Aaron Green (played by Jonah Hill), a young record executive who is tasked with getting rock star Aldous Snow (played by Russell Brand) to perform at a series of concerts in Greece. Along the way, Aaron learns valuable lessons about responsibility, friendship, and finding one's true purpose.

The film explores themes of:

1. **Self-discovery**: Aaron's journey is also one of self-discovery as he navigates his way through the music industry and confronts his own insecurities.
2. **Friendship**: The bond between Aaron and his mentor, Danny Miller (played by Kevin Hart), serves as a catalyst for growth and learning.
3. **Redemption**: Aldous Snow's character arc is one of redemption, as he seeks to revive his career and reconnect with his fans.
4. **The highs and lows of fame**: The film offers a satirical take on the excesses and superficiality of the music industry, highlighting the tension between artistic expression and commercial success.

Throughout the movie, these themes are woven together through a series of comedic misadventures, heartwarming moments, and poignant reflections. Get Him to the Greek is a coming-of-age story that balances humor with substance, making it a memorable and engaging film experience.

overview: In the midst of a marital crisis, a High Court judge must decide if she should order a life-saving blood transfusion for a teen with cancer despite his family's refusal to accept medical treatment for religious reasons.
tagline: We all make choices. Hers make history.
title: The Children Act
plot:
The Children Act is a 2017 drama directed by Richard Eyre and produced by Duncan Kenworthy, with a screenplay by Ian McEwan based on his 2014 novel. Emma Thompson stars as Fiona Maye, a High Court judge, with Stanley Tucci as her husband Jack and Fionn Whitehead as Adam Henry.

Fiona sits in the Family Division of the High Court of England and Wales. She is assigned the urgent case of Adam, a 17-year-old with leukemia whose doctors want to give him a blood transfusion so they can continue treatment. Adam and his parents are Jehovah's Witnesses and refuse on religious grounds. Fiona visits him in the hospital to find out whether the decision is truly his. Adam says he understands that refusal could leave him disabled rather than dead, and he would accept that. When he plays "Down by the Salley Gardens", Fiona sings along, and Adam, deeply drawn to her, begs her to stay. She rules under the Children Act 1989 that Adam's welfare is paramount and allows the transfusion without his or his parents' consent.

Meanwhile, Fiona's marriage is collapsing. Jack, tired of her devotion to work, openly announces an affair with a younger colleague, insisting he still loves her, and leaves. Fiona changes the locks; when Jack returns two days later, they argue bitterly. The transfusion works, and Adam, now recovering, bombards Fiona with messages, poems and letters, saying she has changed his view of the world. He follows her to Newcastle, where she attends a ceremony, and says he wants to live with her, unable to understand why his parents were willing to let him die. She sends him home, though they share a kiss. Later, just before Fiona performs at a lawyers' concert, she learns that Adam has relapsed. She plays "Down by the Salley Gardens" and rushes to see him, but he has refused another transfusion. At home, Fiona breaks down in front of Jack and falls asleep holding his hand. After Adam dies, she attends his funeral and leaves with Jack.

Filming took place in London in late 2016, with Sir Alan Ward, a judge in a conjoined twins case that had inspired the novel, serving as an adviser. The film premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival on 9 September 2017. Entertainment One released it in the United Kingdom on 24 August 2018, and A24 gave it a limited U.S. release that September. Reviews were positive. Rotten Tomatoes reported 74% approval, saying Thompson's powerful performance elevates a flawed film into an affecting adult drama.

overview: When Rumpelstiltskin tries to take over Earth once and for all, The Avengers Grimm must track him down through time in order to defeat him.
tagline: The original wonder women!
title: Avengers Grimm: Time Wars
plot:
Avengers Grimm: Time Wars is a 2018 American fantasy superhero film directed and edited by Maximilian Elfeldt from a screenplay by Jeremy M. Inman, and produced by David Michael Latt for The Asylum. A sequel to Avengers Grimm (2015), it was conceived as a "mockbuster" of Marvel's Avengers: Infinity War while also drawing on the television series Once Upon a Time. Eric Feltes plays Rumpelstiltskin, with Lauren Parkinson as Snow White, Marah Fairclough as Sleeping Beauty, Elizabeth Eileen as Red Riding Hood, Christina Licciardi as Alice, Michael Marcel as Prince Charles Charming III, Katherine Maya as Magda and Randall Yarbrough as the Mad Hatter.

Years have passed since the magic mirror portal shattered, scattering shards across the world. Each fragment is a gateway to a different fairy-tale realm with its own timelines, part of a vast multiverse, and an organization called Looking Glass has been formed to combat threats from those kingdoms. Alice, whose sanity is kept in check by medicine prepared by the Hatter, guards the shards, while the fairy-tale princesses and Red Riding Hood, an archer combining the look of the storybook heroine with the skills of Robin Hood, work to collect them so that they can rebuild the portal and return home.

Prince Charming, who survived Rumpelstiltskin's attempt on his life, is on the run from Magda, the power-hungry ruler of Atlantis, and washes up near a large city. Magda follows and unleashes her soldiers from the sea, hoping to force him to marry her, because whoever weds the prince and wears his ring will gain infinite power and rule the world. To fight back, Alice has the Hatter thaw Snow White from a block of ice, and the heroines, reunited after a brawl with Magda's followers in a warehouse, are astonished to find her alive. Rumpelstiltskin, meanwhile, manipulates Magda into an alliance in exchange for control of Atlantis. When the heroines find the prince, Snow White shields his escape with a wall of ice, but Rumpelstiltskin overpowers him and takes his appearance. Magda then uses her magic to cast the princesses into separate dimensions that warp space and time; once they find each other again, they set out for the realm beyond the mirror to stop Magda's wedding to the prince.

Shot in downtown Los Angeles, the film was released direct to DVD in the United States on 1 May 2018. Critics were unkind, with the German magazine Cinema calling it even sillier than its predecessor.

overview: Ken Park focuses on several teenagers and their tormented home lives. Shawn seems to be the most conventional. Tate is brimming with psychotic rage; Claude is habitually harassed by his brutish father and coddled, rather uncomfortably, by his enormously pregnant mother. Peaches looks after her devoutly religious father, but yearns for freedom. They're all rather tight, or so they claim.
tagline: Who are you?
title: Ken Park
plot:
Ken Park is a 2002 psychological teen film directed by Larry Clark and Edward Lachman and written by Harmony Korine, who built the screenplay from Clark's journals and stories after Clark became dissatisfied with his own draft. Set in Visalia, California, it portrays the abusive and dysfunctional lives of four teenagers connected by the suicide of an acquaintance, the title character. James Ransone plays Tate, Tiffany Limos plays Peaches, James Bullard plays Shawn and Stephen Jasso plays Claude, with Adam Chubbuck as Ken Park and a supporting cast including Maeve Quinlan, Amanda Plummer, Wade Williams, Julio Oscar Mechoso and Richard Riehle. Although planned for digital video, it was shot on 35 mm film.

The film opens with Ken Park, a teenage skateboarder, riding into a skate park, setting up a camcorder and shooting himself. His death frames the story, which cuts between four other teenagers who knew him and the failures of the adults around them. Shawn, the most stable of the four, is secretly having an affair with his girlfriend's mother, while her family remains unaware. Claude endures physical and emotional abuse from his alcoholic father, who despises him for not being masculine enough, while his pregnant mother does little to protect him; after a disturbing drunken advance by his father, Claude runs away from home. Peaches lives with her intensely religious widowed father, who sees her as the embodiment of her dead mother; when he discovers her with her boyfriend Curtis, he beats the boy, punishes her harshly and forces her into a disturbing mock wedding ritual. Tate, a volatile and sadistic youth who lives with grandparents he resents, eventually murders them over petty grievances, records a confession explaining his actions for the police, and is arrested. The separate strands converge only at the end, when Shawn, Claude and Peaches come together, and a final flashback returns to Ken in the days before his death, revealing that his girlfriend was pregnant.

Ken Park premiered at the Telluride Film Festival in 2002 but has not been released in the United States since, which Clark attributed to the producer's failure to secure music rights. It was refused classification in Australia in 2003 because of its graphic sexual content and depictions of underage sexual activity, and police shut down a protest screening in Sydney hosted by critic Margaret Pomeranz. Critical reception was mixed, with a 46% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes.

overview: An immigrant from Hong Kong now lives in Los Angeles. He deals with his homesickness and sense of loss after encountering a strange old man.
tagline: Something good is gonna happen.
title: Cloudbusting
plot:
The Land Before Time VII: The Stone of Cold Fire is an animated adventure film that explores several significant themes. At its core, the movie delves into the complexities of friendship and loyalty, as the main characters navigate the challenges of growing up and facing new responsibilities.

One of the primary themes present in the film is the struggle for independence. As the young dinosaurs transition from childhood to adulthood, they must confront their own limitations and learn to rely on themselves. This journey is fraught with self-doubt, fear, and uncertainty, as the characters grapple with the idea of leaving behind the comfort and security of their youth.

The movie also touches upon the theme of sacrifice and the importance of putting the needs of others before one's own desires. The main character, Littlefoot, must make difficult choices that test his courage and loyalty to his friends, ultimately leading him to discover the value of selflessness and the power of friendship in overcoming adversity.

Furthermore, The Stone of Cold Fire explores the idea of identity and self-discovery. As the characters face new challenges and experiences, they are forced to re-evaluate their sense of purpose and belonging within their community. This theme is particularly relevant for Littlefoot, who must come to terms with his own destiny and the weight of responsibility that comes with being a leader.

Throughout the film, these themes are woven together to create a narrative that is both entertaining and emotionally resonant. The movie's use of stunning animation and engaging storytelling brings the prehistoric world to life, immersing audiences in a richly detailed and immersive environment that is both captivating and heartwarming.

overview: The modern world holds many secrets, but by far the most astounding is that witches still live among us; vicious supernatural creatures intent on unleashing the Black Death upon the world and putting an end to the human race once and for all. Armies of witch hunters have battled this unnatural enemy for centuries, including Kaulder, a valiant warrior who many years ago slayed the all-powerful Witch Queen, decimating her followers in the process. In the moments right before her death, the Queen cursed Kaulder with immortality, forever separating him from his beloved wife and daughter. Today, Kaulder is the last living hunter who has spent his immortal life tracking down rogue witches, all the while yearning for his long-lost family.
tagline: Live forever. Hunt forever.
title: The Last Witch Hunter
plot:
The Last Witch Hunter is a 2015 supernatural action film directed by Breck Eisner and starring Vin Diesel, Rose Byrne, and Michael Caine.

In the late 17th century, a powerful witch hunter named Kaulder (Vin Diesel) lives in medieval Europe. He is tasked with eradicating witches from the world, but as he delves deeper into his work, he begins to question the morality of his actions. Kaulder's sister, Bridgette (Angelica), was killed by a witch when he was just a child, and this event sets him on a path of revenge against those who practice magic.

As Kaulder grows older, he becomes one of the most feared witch hunters in Europe, earning the nickname "The Last Witch Hunter." However, his life takes a dramatic turn when he meets a young woman named Isabelle (Rose Byrne), who is being pursued by a group of witches. Despite initial reservations, Kaulder agrees to protect Isabelle and help her defeat the witches.

As they journey together, Kaulder begins to realize that there may be more to his sister's death than he initially thought. He discovers that Bridgette was not killed by a witch, but rather by a powerful sorcerer named Valentin (Michael Caine) who seeks to destroy all magic in the world. This revelation sets Kaulder on a quest for revenge against Valentin and his followers.

Throughout their journey, Kaulder and Isabelle face numerous challenges as they battle witches and other supernatural creatures. Along the way, Kaulder begins to question his own morality and the true nature of good and evil. He also develops feelings for Isabelle, which complicates his mission and forces him to confront his own emotions.

As the story unfolds, Kaulder and Isabelle discover that Valentin's plan is more sinister than they initially thought. The sorcerer seeks to destroy all magic in the world, believing it to be a threat to humanity. However, Kaulder and Isabelle soon realize that magic is not inherently evil, but rather a natural part of the world.

In the end, Kaulder and his allies launch a final attack on Valentin's stronghold. In a climactic battle, Kaulder faces off against Valentin and ultimately defeats him, saving the world from destruction. Along the way, he also finds redemption and a new sense of purpose, one that allows him to balance his desire for revenge with a greater understanding of the world and its complexities.

Overall, The Last Witch Hunter is a thrilling supernatural action film that explores themes of morality, redemption, and the nature of good and evil. With its engaging storyline, memorable characters, and impressive action sequences, it is a must-see for fans of the genre.

belongs_to_collection.name: 新海誠作品  シリーズ

overview: Takao, who is training to become a shoemaker, skipped school and is sketching shoes in a Japanese-style garden. He meets a mysterious woman, Yukino, who is older than him. Then, without arranging the times, the two start to see each other again and again, but only on rainy days. They deepen their relationship and open up to each other. But the end of the rainy season soon approaches...
title: The Garden of Words
plot:
The Garden of Words is a 2013 Japanese animated drama film written and directed by Makoto Shinkai, produced by CoMix Wave Films. The movie takes place on a rainy day in April, where we meet the main character, Taku Morino, a high school student who has just returned to Tokyo after spending three years abroad.

Taku's life is marked by loneliness and disconnection from others. He struggles to form meaningful relationships with his peers and family members. On this particular rainy day, he meets a mysterious woman named Yukino Nakamura, who sits alone on a bench in the park. They strike up a conversation, and despite their initial awkwardness, they find themselves drawn to each other.

As the story unfolds, we learn that Taku and Yukino have a deep emotional connection, but their relationship is complicated by their past experiences. Taku's mother has recently passed away, leaving him feeling lost and disconnected from his family. Yukino, on the other hand, has been struggling with her own emotions after being abandoned by her boyfriend.

Throughout the film, Shinkai uses beautiful animation to bring the characters' inner worlds to life. The movie is a poignant exploration of love, loss, and the human condition. Taku and Yukino's conversations are interspersed with flashbacks of their past experiences, which reveal the depth of their emotional scars.

As the story progresses, we see Taku and Yukino grow closer, but their relationship is also marked by uncertainty and fear. They struggle to open up to each other, fearing that they will be hurt again. The film's climax features a heart-wrenching scene where Taku must confront his own emotions and make a choice between holding onto the past or embracing the present.

The Garden of Words is a beautifully crafted film that explores themes of love, loss, and redemption. Shinkai's direction is masterful, using animation to convey the characters' inner worlds in a way that feels both intimate and universal. The movie's ending is both poignant and hopeful, leaving the audience with a sense of longing and possibility.

Overall, The Garden of Words is a powerful and moving film that explores the complexities of human relationships. With its beautiful animation and poignant storytelling, it is a must-see for fans of anime and drama.

overview: The 47-year old Al Capone, after 10 years in prison, starts suffering from dementia and comes to be haunted by his violent past.
tagline: We all pay for our crimes in the end.
title: Capone
plot:
Capone is a 2020 biographical crime drama film that delves into the life of Al Capone, the infamous American gangster. The movie explores the darker aspects of Capone's personality and his struggles with mental health, particularly his struggles with depression and paranoia.

The film portrays Capone as a complex character, both charismatic and ruthless, who is haunted by his own demons. As he navigates the treacherous world of organized crime, Capone becomes increasingly isolated and withdrawn, leading to a downward spiral of self-destruction.

One of the main themes of the movie is the blurred lines between reality and delusion. Capone's mental health issues lead him to become detached from reality, causing him to see conspiracies everywhere and becoming convinced that he is being hunted by his enemies. This theme is expertly woven throughout the film, adding depth and nuance to Capone's character.

The movie also explores the consequences of Capone's actions on those around him, particularly his family and loved ones. As he becomes more and more entrenched in his world of crime, Capone pushes away those who care for him, leading to a tragic downfall.

Ultimately, Capone is a film about the destructive power of unchecked ambition and the devastating consequences of living a life of crime. The movie presents a thought-provoking portrayal of one of America's most infamous gangsters, offering a nuanced exploration of his complexities and flaws.

overview: In the heat of the summer lays a lonesome house in the countryside where nine year old twin brothers await their mother’s return.  When she comes home, bandaged after cosmetic surgery, nothing is like before and the children start to doubt whether this woman is actually who she says she is.
tagline: A mother should look out for her sons.
title: Goodnight Mommy
plot:
Goodnight Mommy is a psychological horror film that delves into the complexities of identity, trauma, and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy. The movie tells the story of two young boys who are left alone with their mother after she returns from a trip, only to discover that something is amiss.

As the narrative unfolds, it becomes clear that the mother's return is not what it seems, and the boys' perceptions of her identity begin to unravel. This sets off a chain reaction of events that exposes the dark secrets and traumas that have been hidden beneath the surface of their seemingly idyllic family life.

The film expertly weaves together themes of identity, exploring how our sense of self is shaped by our experiences, relationships, and perceptions. The mother's dual identity serves as a metaphor for the fragility of human identity, highlighting how easily it can be manipulated and distorted.

Furthermore, Goodnight Mommy critiques the notion of childhood innocence, suggesting that children are not as naive as they seem. The boys' growing awareness of their mother's true nature forces them to confront the harsh realities of adulthood, including the darkness that lurks beneath the surface of seemingly ordinary lives.

The film also touches on the theme of trauma and its lasting impact on individuals and families.
