The mother's past is slowly revealed, exposing a history of pain and suffering that has left her with emotional scars. This serves as a reminder that trauma can be passed down through generations, affecting not only the individual but also those around them.

Ultimately, Goodnight Mommy is a thought-provoking exploration of the human psyche, delving into the complexities of identity, trauma, and the fragility of human relationships.

overview: When a man is diagnosed with terminal cancer, he takes custody of his misanthropic teenage son, for whom quality time means getting high, engaging in small-time prostitution, and avoiding his father.
tagline: Seen from a distance, it's perfect.
title: Life as a House
plot:
Life as a House is a poignant and introspective drama that explores the complexities of family relationships, identity, and the human condition. The film delves into the emotional struggles of its protagonist, George Beckett, played by Kevin Kline, who returns home after being diagnosed with terminal cancer to reconcile with his estranged son, Sam.

As George navigates his final days, he sets out to complete a long-held dream of building a house for his son, which becomes a metaphor for the unfinished business and unspoken emotions between them. Through this journey, the film masterfully weaves together themes of love, forgiveness, and redemption, highlighting the intricate web of relationships within a family.

The movie also touches on the idea of identity and how it is shaped by our experiences, relationships, and personal struggles. George's character serves as a catalyst for Sam to confront his own desires, fears, and aspirations, ultimately leading him to discover his own path in life.

Furthermore, Life as a House explores the concept of legacy and the impact we have on those around us. As George faces his mortality, he comes to realize that it is never too late to make amends, forgive, and show love to those who matter most. The film's narrative is both heart-wrenching and uplifting, leaving audiences with a profound sense of empathy and understanding for the complexities of human relationships.

Overall, Life as a House is a powerful exploration of the human experience, tackling themes that are both universally relatable and deeply personal.

overview: A young man who arrives at a remote island finds himself trapped in a battle for his life.
tagline: We are never too far from those we hate
title: Cold Skin
plot:
Cold Skin is a 2017 Spanish horror film directed by Salvador Mallo. The movie follows a team of scientists who investigate a mysterious, ancient creature that has washed up on the coast of a remote island in the Galician Sea.

The main theme of Cold Skin revolves around the idea of the unknown and the unexplained. The film delves into the concept of an ancient, prehistoric creature that defies human understanding, sparking both fascination and terror in those who encounter it. As the story unfolds, the team's obsession with the creature leads to a descent into madness and chaos.

The movie also explores the theme of hubris and the dangers of scientific arrogance. The scientists' initial excitement and curiosity about the creature soon give way to fear and uncertainty as they realize that they are dealing with something far beyond their comprehension. This serves as a cautionary tale about the limits of human knowledge and the importance of humility in the face of the unknown.

Furthermore, Cold Skin touches on the idea of isolation and confinement. The remote location of the island, combined with the team's own psychological vulnerabilities, creates an atmosphere of claustrophobia and desperation. As the creature begins to exert its influence over the team, they are forced to confront their deepest fears and insecurities in a desperate bid for survival.

Overall, Cold Skin is a tense, atmospheric horror film that explores the darker aspects of human nature and the unknown, leaving audiences with a sense of unease and uncertainty long after the credits roll.

overview: Two former backup soul singers, Louis and Floyd, have not spoken to each other in 20 years, and reluctantly agree to travel across the country together to a reunion concert to honor their recently-deceased lead singer. Cleo, a beautiful young woman who is believed to be Floyd's daughter, accompanies them as a new singer.
title: Soul Men
plot:
Soul Men is a 2008 American comedy film directed by Reginald Hudlin. The movie follows two former soul singers, Odell and Louis, who are reunited for one last performance at a benefit concert to raise money for their friend's funeral expenses.

The main theme of Soul Men revolves around the power of music and its ability to bring people together, heal emotional wounds, and transcend time and circumstance. Through the story of Odell and Louis, the film explores the complexities of male friendship, loyalty, and the sacrifices that come with it.

As the two men navigate their past and present, they must confront their own personal demons, including regret, resentment, and the consequences of their choices. Along the way, they learn to let go of their differences and find common ground, ultimately discovering that music has the power to reunite them and bring them closure.

The film also touches on themes of identity, community, and the importance of finding one's purpose in life. Through Odell and Louis's journey, Soul Men shows how music can be a source of comfort, inspiration, and connection, even in the face of adversity and hardship.

Overall, Soul Men is a heartwarming and entertaining film that celebrates the transformative power of music and the bonds of male friendship.

overview: The Guardians must fight to keep their newfound family together as they unravel the mysteries of Peter Quill's true parentage.
tagline: Obviously.
title: Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2
plot:
Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2 is a 2017 American superhero film directed by James Gunn and produced by Marvel Studios. The movie follows the story of Peter Quill, also known as Star-Lord, who is still trying to find his place among the Guardians of the Galaxy.

The film begins with Peter (Chris Pratt) living on Morag, a planet where he was raised by Ego (Kurt Russell), a powerful Celestial being. However, it soon becomes apparent that Ego's intentions are not pure, and Peter discovers that he is actually the son of Ego, making him the most powerful being in the galaxy.

As Peter struggles to come to terms with his true identity, the Guardians receive a distress signal from the planet Ego, which they believe is under attack by Ronan the Accuser (Lee Pace). However, upon arrival, they find that Ego has been using his powers to create an army of super-soldiers, known as the Sovereign.

The Guardians soon discover that Ego's true intention is to use Peter's DNA to become even more powerful. Meanwhile, Yondu Udonta (Michael Rooker), a skilled archer and Peter's adoptive father, tries to protect him from Ego's plans.

As the story unfolds, we see flashbacks of Peter's childhood on Morag, where he was raised by Ego, who taught him about his Celestial heritage. However, these memories are not entirely accurate, and Peter begins to question his true identity.

The Guardians also encounter Mantis (Pom Klementieff), a powerful empathic being with the ability to sense and manipulate emotions. Mantis joins the team, and together they hatch a plan to stop Ego's plans.

In the climactic final battle, the Guardians face off against Ego and his army of super-soldiers. Peter ultimately discovers that he is not just a human, but a Celestial being with incredible powers. With the help of his friends, Peter defeats Ego and shatters his ego (pun intended).

The movie concludes with Peter coming to terms with his true identity and finding a new sense of purpose among the Guardians. The film ends on a hopeful note, setting the stage for the next installment in the Guardians of the Galaxy franchise.

Overall, Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2 is a visually stunning and action-packed film that explores themes of identity, family, and belonging. With its talented cast, witty dialogue, and heartfelt moments, it's no wonder why this movie has become a fan favorite among Marvel enthusiasts.

overview: The Baker brood moves to Chicago after patriarch Tom gets a job coaching football at Northwestern University, forcing his writer wife, Mary, and the couple's 12 children to make a major adjustment. The transition works well until work demands pull the parents away from home, leaving the kids bored -- and increasingly mischievous.
tagline: Growing pains? They've got twelve of them!
title: Cheaper by the Dozen
plot:
Cheaper by the Dozen is a family comedy film released in 2003, directed by Tom Shadyac and produced by 20th Century Fox. The movie is based on the 1948 book of the same name by Frank B. Gilbreath.

The main themes of Cheaper by the Dozen revolve around the importance of family, love, and learning to adapt to change. The story follows the Baker family, a loving but chaotic household with 12 children, as they navigate their daily lives and learn valuable lessons about themselves and each other.

One of the primary themes is the power of family bonds and the unconditional love that exists within them. Despite the challenges and chaos that come with having a large family, the Bakers always find ways to support and care for one another. The movie showcases the unique relationships between the parents, Tom (Steve Carell) and Kate (Brenda Strong), and their children, as they work together to create a harmonious home environment.

Another significant theme is the importance of flexibility and adaptability in family life. As the Bakers face various challenges, including financial struggles and personal conflicts, they learn to be more flexible and accommodating with each other. This theme is exemplified through Tom's efforts to balance his career ambitions with his role as a father and husband.

The movie also explores the idea of embracing change and finding joy in the everyday moments. Despite the chaos that comes with having 12 children, the Bakers learn to appreciate the simple things in life and find happiness in their daily routines.

Overall, Cheaper by the Dozen is a heartwarming film that celebrates the beauty of family life and the importance of love, acceptance, and adaptability.

original_title: St Trinian's 2: The Legend of Fritton's Gold
overview: The girls of St. Trinians are on the hunt for buried treasure after discovering headmistress Miss Fritton is related to a famous pirate.
title: St Trinian's 2: The Legend of Fritton's Gold
plot:
St Trinian's 2: The Legend of Fritton's Gold is a comedy film that explores several themes, primarily revolving around the mischievous and anarchic nature of its titular school. At its core, the movie delves into the idea of rebellion against authority and societal norms.

The story follows the students as they embark on a treasure hunt to uncover the hidden riches of Fritton's Gold, which serves as a metaphor for their own desires for freedom and independence. As they navigate through various obstacles and challenges, they must confront the constraints imposed upon them by the adult world and the expectations placed upon them by society.

Throughout the film, the characters' actions are driven by a desire to break free from the shackles of conformity and forge their own paths in life. This theme is expertly woven throughout the narrative, often resulting in humorous and chaotic situations as the students' antics lead to unexpected consequences.

The movie also touches on the idea of class and social status, highlighting the disparities between the wealthy elite and those from more humble backgrounds. The students' quest for Fritton's Gold serves as a symbol of their desire to level the playing field and challenge the existing power structures.

Ultimately, St Trinian's 2: The Legend of Fritton's Gold is a lighthearted and entertaining film that uses humor and satire to comment on the human desire for freedom and self-expression.

overview: Pop star Christopher Wilde has fame, fortune and a big-budget Hollywood movie awaiting him. But after meeting Jessica Olson, a down-to-earth girl from the Midwest, he is faced with following his heart or doing what's best for his career.
title: Starstruck
plot:
Starstruck, stylized as StarStruck, is a 2010 American teen musical drama television film starring Sterling Knight as pop idol Christopher Wilde, alongside Danielle Campbell, Brandon Mychal Smith, Chelsea Kane and Maggie Castle. It premiered as a Disney Channel Original Movie on February 14, 2010, and was shot on location in Los Angeles in 2009.

Jessica Olson, a teenager from Kalamazoo has little patience for her older sister Sara's obsession with teen heartthrob Christopher Wilde. During a spring break visit to their grandmother in Hollywood, Sara drags Jessica along on her quest to meet the star. Christopher, meanwhile, is close to landing a major movie role, but the director is wary of his growing reputation as a "spoiled punk" who brawls with paparazzi, so he promises to stay out of the tabloids. When the sisters sneak into a birthday party for his model girlfriend Alexis Bender, Christopher, slipping out unnoticed, accidentally knocks Jessica down with an exit door. He takes her to a hospital to check for a concussion, then to his Beverly Hills mansion, and after the paparazzi pick up his trail, Jessica lets him hide in her grandmother's garage. The next day she recognizes him in disguise on a Malibu beach, and the two spend the day exploring Los Angeles, escaping photographers and stranding her grandmother's car in a mud pit. Christopher admits he enjoys being with someone who sees him as a person rather than a celebrity, but when they nearly kiss, he panics about being recognized and tells her no one can ever know about their day together. When photos of the pair surface, his parents, who also serve as his managers, persuade him to dismiss Jessica as just a fan, leaving her branded a liar by the media back home. Encouraged by his best friend Stubby to make his own choices, Christopher must decide whether his career matters more than the girl who liked him for himself.

The premiere drew 6.0 million viewers, making it Disney Channel's most-watched February original movie premiere, and 987,000 viewers watched its UK and Ireland premiere in May 2010. The soundtrack, released by Walt Disney Records, peaked at number 23 on the Billboard 200; most of its songs are sung by Drew Ryan Scott rather than Knight.

overview: The story of the miraculous evacuation of Allied soldiers from Belgium, Britain, Canada and France, who were cut off and surrounded by the German army from the beaches and harbour of Dunkirk between May 26th and June 4th 1940 during World War II.
tagline: Survival is Victory
title: Dunkirk
plot:
Dunkirk is a 2017 war drama film directed by Christopher Nolan, produced by Warner Bros. Pictures, and distributed by Warner Bros. The film is set during World War II and tells the story of the Dunkirk evacuation, also known as the Miracle of Dunkirk.

The film begins on May 26, 1940, with a dramatic sequence showing the German army's invasion of France. The British Expeditionary Force (BEF), led by General Lord Gort, is trapped in Dunkirk, a coastal town in northern France. As the Germans close in, the BEF is surrounded and outnumbered.

The story then shifts to three main plot threads: the evacuation of Allied soldiers from Dunkirk, the rescue efforts by the Royal Air Force (RAF), and the experiences of a young British soldier named Tommy (Fionn Whitehead). The film's narrative is presented in a non-linear fashion, with each thread intersecting and overlapping at various points.

The evacuation of Allied soldiers from Dunkirk is depicted as a chaotic and desperate effort. Thousands of soldiers are stranded on the beaches of Dunkirk, with no clear way to escape. The British Navy, led by Admiral Bertram Ramsay (Kenneth Branagh), launches a massive rescue operation, with ships and boats converging on the beach to evacuate the soldiers.

Meanwhile, the RAF is engaged in a fierce dogfight with German aircraft, trying to protect the evacuation fleet from enemy attack. The film's aerial sequences are intense and suspenseful, showcasing the bravery and skill of the RAF pilots.

Tommy, who has been separated from his family during the evacuation, finds himself on the beach, struggling to survive amidst the chaos. He joins a group of other soldiers, including Mr. Dawson (Mark Rylance), a civilian who is helping to evacuate the soldiers. As they try to escape, Tommy and Mr. Dawson face numerous challenges, including treacherous terrain, enemy fire, and personal losses.

As the evacuation continues, the film's narrative builds towards a dramatic climax. The British Navy launches a final push to clear the beach of German forces, while the RAF provides cover with its aircraft. The soldiers are finally able to escape, but not before many have lost their lives or been separated from their loved ones.

The film ends with Tommy, who has survived the evacuation, watching as the last of the ships depart from Dunkirk. He is reunited with his family, who had been searching for him throughout the ordeal. The final shot is of a small boat, which is revealed to be carrying Mr. Dawson's body, symbolizing the sacrifice and bravery of those who helped evacuate the soldiers.

Throughout the film, Nolan uses innovative cinematography and editing techniques to create a sense of tension and urgency. The film's score, composed by Hans Zimmer, adds to the emotional impact of the story. Overall, Dunkirk is a powerful and moving tribute to the bravery and sacrifice of those who fought in World War II.

overview: Criminology student Chloe fakes her own death to break into a morgue, in order to retrieve a piece of evidence that ties her younger brother to a crime gone wrong. Once inside, she quickly learns that the fearsome Coroner uses the morgue as a front for a sick and twisted business. As a frightening game of cat and mouse ensues, Chloe will discover that the scariest thing about the morgue is not the dead, but the living.
tagline: Some things are worse than death.
title: Play Dead
plot:
Play Dead is a 2022 American horror thriller directed by Patrick Lussier and written by Simon Boyes and Adam Mason. Bailee Madison stars as Chloe Albright, a criminology and forensics student, with Anthony Turpel as her brother T.J., Chris Lee as Ross and Jerry O'Connell as a coroner with a terrible secret.

Chloe and T.J. have lost their father, whose death was ruled a suicide, voiding his life insurance, and debts are about to cost them their home. T.J. believes he has found a solution: he and his friend Ross, Chloe's ex-boyfriend, plan a robbery with a fake gun. Ross goes into the store while T.J. waits behind the wheel, but the owner opens fire, Ross is shot down and T.J. flees. But Ross's phone, now held by police, contains evidence that will incriminate T.J. Desperate to keep her brother out of prison, Chloe comes up with a daring plan. She injects herself with a drug that slows her vital signs until she appears dead, so that she will be taken to the morgue, where the phone has been logged as evidence.

The plan works until Chloe discovers that the coroner on duty is a cold-blooded killer. He runs a lucrative sideline harvesting and selling organs and body parts from the dead, and he justifies it as a way of ridding society of its "bottom feeders". Strapped to a gurney, Chloe is told that everything she is and has done is worth less than the sum of her parts. Trapped inside the locked building with no easy escape, she must outwit him in a cat-and-mouse game through examination rooms, corridors and underground passages.

In May 2022, Voltage Pictures pre-sold the film to buyers at the Cannes Film Festival. Critics acknowledged the implausibility of the premise but found the film tense and effective. Phil Hoad of The Guardian gave it three stars out of five, praising Madison's performance as a determined final girl and especially O'Connell's controlled turn as the sharpest tailored killer since Patrick Bateman, calling the film "a terrible advert for organ donation but a compact and resourceful thriller." Adam Sweeting of The Arts Desk wrote that despite its low budget the film never felt cheap. He praised Lussier's assured pacing and described O'Connell's coroner as a chilling embodiment of the banality of evil.

overview: After a virus of epic proportions overwhelms the planet—with more infected than uninfected—humanity is losing its grip on survival and its only hope is finding a cure and keeping the infected contained. Lauren, a doctor, arrives in Los Angeles with her crack team to lead the hunt for uncontaminated civilian survivors, but nothing can prepare them for the blood-soaked mayhem they witness as they head into the Californian streets where everything is considered a trap.
tagline: You are humanity's last stand.
title: Pandemic
plot:
Pandemic is a 2016 American science fiction thriller film directed by John Suits and written by Dustin T. Benson. Shot from a first-person point of view in the manner of a first-person shooter video game, it stars Rachel Nichols as a woman who joins a military team searching for survivors of a deadly global pandemic.

A woman wearing the badge of Dr. Lauren Chase tries unsuccessfully to reach her daughter, Megan. Briefed by Dr. Greer at a military base, she learns that the mysterious infection progresses through five stages, ending in extreme aggression, and that her job is to test anyone the extraction team brings back so that no infected people reach the base. Her team includes the driver, Wheeler, the navigator, Denise, and Gunner, whose wife disappeared with a previous team sent to rescue survivors barricaded in a school. On the way, Gunner finds his wife's half-eaten body in an abandoned bus. At the school, Lauren finally reaches Megan, who says she is at their house in the Los Angeles suburbs, and promises to come for her. The survivors in the school turn out to be infected, and Gunner sacrifices himself so that the others can flee, while Wheeler runs off.

Sheltering together, Lauren confesses to Denise that she is not a doctor but stole the badge; her real name is Rebecca Thomas, and Denise promises to help her find Megan. Wheeler returns and saves them, saying he has found a doctor at a nearby hospital who needs convincing. On the way, infected people seize Denise and kill her beneath a bridge, and Rebecca kills one of them in a rage. At the hospital, the doctor recognizes that Rebecca is not Lauren Chase, whom he has met, and drives away with the survivors. Rebecca and Wheeler reach her home, where she finds her husband dead in the garage and Megan alive but infected. When infected people attack, she makes Megan put on her protective suit, and they escape, leaving the badly wounded Wheeler behind at his urging. At the compound, soldiers see Rebecca carrying a figure in a doctor's suit and shoot her. Dr. Greer, believing Megan to be Lauren Chase, orders that she be taken inside and treated.

Pandemic premiered at FrightFest Glasgow on February 26, 2016, as a last-minute replacement for Cell, and was released by XLrator Media in limited theaters on April 1 and on video on demand days later. Reviews were mostly negative, with 44% on Rotten Tomatoes; critics praised its energetic action but not its characters.

overview: A group of unwitting sorority sisters accidentally awaken the serial-killing Leprechaun after they build a sorority house on his hunting grounds.
tagline: Be careful what you wish for.
title: Leprechaun Returns
plot:
Leprechaun Returns is a 2018 supernatural horror film that serves as a sequel to the original Leprechaun series. The movie delves into the theme of revenge and the consequences of playing with forces beyond human control.

The story revolves around a young woman named Ophelia, who unwittingly unleashes the vengeful spirit of the Leprechaun, Mr. Knuckles, from his ancient prison. As the film progresses, it becomes clear that Mr. Knuckles is driven by a desire for revenge against those who wronged him in life.

The movie explores the idea of karma and the cyclical nature of violence. Mr. Knuckles' actions are motivated by a deep-seated anger and hurt, which he seeks to inflict upon others. However, as the story unfolds, it becomes apparent that his quest for revenge is also fueled by a twisted sense of justice.

Throughout the film, the theme of female empowerment is also present. Ophelia, who initially unleashes Mr. Knuckles' wrath, must navigate a treacherous world and confront her own vulnerabilities in order to survive. Her journey serves as a metaphor for the struggle women often face in overcoming patriarchal oppression and reclaiming their agency.

Ultimately, Leprechaun Returns is a cautionary tale about the dangers of meddling with forces beyond human understanding. The film warns against the consequences of playing with fire and the devastating repercussions that can result from seeking revenge or trying to control the uncontrollable.

overview: In 1909, Willie Boy and his love Carlota go on the run after he accidentally shoots her father in a confrontation gone terribly wrong. With President Taft coming to the area, the local sheriff leads two Native American trackers seeking justice for their “murdered” tribal leader.
tagline: In 1909, they entered the desert. Now, the truth will finally emerge.
title: The Last Manhunt
plot:
The Last Manhunt is a 2022 American Western directed by Christian Camargo and written by Thomas Pa'a Sibbett from a story by Sibbett and Jason Momoa, who also served as an executive producer. It retells the legend of Willie Boy, previously filmed as Tell Them Willie Boy Is Here with Robert Redford, drawing on Native accounts. Martin Sensmeier stars as Willie Boy, with Mainei Kinimaka as Carlota, Zahn McClarnon as her father William, Raoul Max Trujillo as Hyde, Camargo as Sheriff Wilson and Momoa as Big Jim.

In 1909, Willie Boy, a young Paiute man, and Carlota slip away together during a Ghost Dance, only to be caught by her father, who objects because the two are cousins. In a struggle over a gun, William is accidentally shot dead. His wife urges the couple to run, but she later asks the sheriff to pursue them. The lovers flee across the desert, and blame for the killing falls on them. Wilson leads a posse of white men and Native trackers, insisting that Willie be taken alive. Hyde, William's friend, wants Willie dead.

After days on the run, Carlota is bitten by a snake and falls ill. Willie leaves her at Ruby Mountain and goes to Clara True for medicine. While he is gone, a member of the posse spots Carlota from a distance, mistakes her for Willie and shoots her dead. Willie lures the posse into a desert enclosure ringed by cliffs and fires down on them, aiming only at their horses. When the sheriff shouts that Carlota is dead, Willie holds his rifle under his chin but decides to keep running. The posse then stages a photograph of Willie's death for the newspapers, with Big Jim posing as the corpse. Closing text, based on Chemehuevi oral history, says that Willie survived, lived in isolation near Pahrump, Nevada, and later died of tuberculosis. It adds that the pair covered some 600 miles in about 26 days, the last great manhunt of the Wild West, and that press claims that Willie killed Carlota were false.

The film opened the Pioneertown International Film Festival in May 2022. Saban Films acquired worldwide rights that June and released it in November. Reviews were largely negative, and Rotten Tomatoes reported 20% approval from a small number of critics. Luke Y. Thompson of The A.V. Club praised the scenery around Joshua Tree and welcomed the film's correction of the historical record but found the lovers underdeveloped and the storytelling meandering. He noted that Momoa appears in only a few scenes.

overview: Early 18th century. Cartographer Jonathan Green undertakes a scientific voyage from Europe to the East. Having passed through Transylvania and crossed the Carpathian Mountains, he finds himself in a small village lost in impassible woods. Nothing but chance and heavy fog could bring him to this cursed place. People who live here do not resemble any other people which the traveler saw before that. The villagers, having dug a deep moat to fend themselves from the rest of the world, share a naive belief that they could save themselves from evil, failing to understand that evil has made its nest in their souls and is waiting for an opportunity to gush out upon the world.
tagline: The truth is in you
title: Forbidden Empire
plot:
Forbidden Empire is a 2014 historical adventure film directed by Peter Flinth and produced by Russian Film Group. The movie is set in 13th-century China during the reign of Kublai Khan.

The main themes of Forbidden Empire include:

1. **Cultural Exchange and Understanding**: The film explores the interactions between Chinese, Mongol, and European cultures, highlighting the complexities and misunderstandings that arose from these encounters.
2. **Power Struggles and Politics**: The movie delves into the intrigue and politics of Kublai Khan's court, showcasing the ruthless ambition and cunning of its characters as they vie for power and influence.
3. **Identity and Belonging**: The protagonist, a young Chinese warrior named Jia, must navigate his own identity and sense of belonging in a world where he is caught between his loyalty to his family and his duty to the Khan.
4. **Warfare and Conquest**: The film depicts the brutal realities of war and conquest, highlighting the devastating consequences of conflict on individuals and communities.

Throughout the movie, these themes are woven together to create a rich tapestry of historical drama, adventure, and cultural exploration.

overview: After a bad blind date, a man and woman find themselves stuck together at a resort for families, where their attractions grows as their respective kids benefit from the burgeoning relationship.
tagline: Single Dad, No Clue. Single Mom, Flying Solo.
title: Blended
plot:
Blended is a 2014 American romantic comedy film directed by Frank Coraci and written by Ivan Menchell. The movie stars Adam Sandler and Drew Barrymore as two single parents who end up on a disastrous blind date, which ultimately leads to them spending the entire summer together with their kids.

The story begins with Jim Friedman (Adam Sandler), a divorced father of three, who is trying to find love again. He meets Lauren Reynolds (Drew Barrymore) at a singles bar, where they agree to go on a blind date. However, things don't go as planned, and the two end up getting drunk together, leading to a series of awkward moments.

Despite the initial disaster, Jim and Lauren decide to give their relationship another chance and meet again with their kids in tow. They spend the summer together at a family resort, where they try to navigate their feelings for each other while also dealing with their own personal issues.

As the summer progresses, Jim and Lauren start to develop feelings for each other, but their past relationships and fears hold them back. Meanwhile, their kids, who are initially hesitant about their parents' relationship, eventually warm up to the idea of having two moms or dads.

Throughout the movie, Jim and Lauren face various challenges, including a series of hilarious misadventures with their kids, a rival suitor for Lauren's affections (played by Kevin Nealon), and their own personal demons. Despite these obstacles, they continue to grow closer and eventually realize that they have fallen in love.

The movie culminates with Jim and Lauren confessing their feelings to each other and sharing a romantic kiss. The film ends on a heartwarming note, with the two couples (Jim's kids and Lauren's kids) embracing their blended family and looking forward to a bright future together.

Overall, Blended is a lighthearted, comedic take on love, family, and relationships. With its witty dialogue, relatable characters, and hilarious moments, it's a fun and entertaining movie that will leave audiences smiling.

overview: Atop the ruins of war, top commander Jiang Ziya is given the task to banish the Nine-tailed Fox Demon who threatens all mortals' very existence. When he discovers the Nine-tailed Fox's life linked to the soul of an innocent girl, he is faced with a challenging decision: follow the will of heaven or find his own path to righteousness.
title: Jiang Ziya: The Legend of Deification
plot:
Jiang Ziya (Chinese: 姜子牙), released internationally as Jiang Ziya: The Legend of Deification, is a Chinese animated fantasy adventure of 2020 directed by Cheng Teng and Li Wei. A follow-up to Ne Zha (2019), it is loosely based on the 16th-century novel Investiture of the Gods and centres on the mythological figure Jiang Ziya, voiced by Zheng Xi, with Yang Ning as the fox girl Xiao Jiu, Tutehameng voicing Shen Gongbao and Yan Meme Si Bu Xiang, the nine-tailed fox demon voiced by Ji Guanlin and Shan Xin, and Jiang Guangtao as Yuanshi Tianzun.

After a fox spirit brings down the Shang dynasty and plunges the three realms into war, the demon is captured, and Jiang Ziya, a mortal hero of the conflict, is ordered to execute it. The fox reveals an innocent girl trapped within her, and Jiang hesitates before apparently killing the creature as it tries to flee. Refusing to accept that the girl was merely an illusion, he is stripped of his powers and exiled to the North Sea. Ten years later, dejected and accompanied by his friend Shen Gongbao and his creature Si Bu Xiang, he meets Xiao Jiu, an amnesiac young fox spirit who resembles the girl, and agrees to escort her to Youdu Mountain, where she hopes to find her father, battling demons and lost souls along the way.

At the mountain, King Zhou explains that Xiao Jiu is bound to the original fox spirit and must die for it to be destroyed. Jiang's attempt to kill her summons the fox, which reveals that the girl was Su Daji, abandoned by her father to become a royal concubine. Si Bu Xiang dies in the ensuing fight, and Shen Gongbao spends some of his power to send Jiang to heaven, where the Master reveals that Jiang was denied godhood for being willing to risk the world to save the girl. Jiang leads Xiao Jiu to the Gate of Reincarnation, only to discover that it is an abyss imprisoning the innocent dead of the war and that the fox had been promised godhood, then made a scapegoat. He frees the girl, but she is slain by a heavenly guillotine. Disgusted by heaven's corruption, Jiang refuses godhood and destroys the bridge between the realms. Years later, reincarnations of Xiao Jiu and Si Bu Xiang play together.

Delayed from Chinese New Year by the COVID-19 pandemic, the film opened on 1 October 2020 and set a record for an animated opening day in China, earning about 308 million yuan.

overview: Having escaped years of imprisonment, vampire warrioress Selene finds herself in a changed world where humans have discovered the existence of both Vampire and Lycan clans and are conducting an all-out war to eradicate both immortal species. Now Selene must battle the humans and a frightening new breed of super Lycans to ensure the death dealers' survival.
tagline: Vengeance Returns
title: Underworld: Awakening
plot:
Underworld: Awakening is a 2012 American action horror film directed by Måns Mårlind and Björn Stein, from a screenplay by Len Wiseman, John Hlavin, J. Michael Straczynski and Allison Burnett based on a story by Wiseman and Hlavin. The fourth Underworld film, it stars Kate Beckinsale as the vampire warrior Selene, with Stephen Rea, Michael Ealy, Theo James, India Eisley and Charles Dance.

After humanity discovers vampires and Lycans, a program to study them becomes an extermination campaign, the Purge, and Selene and her lover Michael are captured. Selene is kept in cryogenic suspension for twelve years, during which both species are hunted almost to extinction. Breaking free, she learns another subject has escaped and begins seeing through someone else's eyes. Following them, she meets David, a young vampire, and fights off Lycans hunting the other escapee, a frightened girl. When a Lycan bites the girl, she partly transforms and tears it apart, and Selene realizes the girl is her daughter with Michael. The girl had freed Selene from her tank.

David takes them to his coven, where the girl's wound finally heals after she drinks blood. The coven distrusts her. When Lycans attack, Selene is overpowered by a giant "Super-Lycan" that heals instantly and is immune to silver, and David's father Thomas surrenders the girl to the Lycans. Selene revives the dying David with her blood. With Sebastian, a sympathetic human detective, she traces the Lycans to Antigen, the corporation behind the facility. Antigen is secretly run by Lycans, and its director, Dr. Jacob Lane, needs the girl's DNA to perfect his race. The Super-Lycan is Lane's son Quint. Selene and Sebastian storm the building to rescue the girl, whom they call Eve. Selene begins thawing Michael, Subject 0, but must leave him to save Eve. David, now immune to sunlight thanks to Selene's blood, joins the fight. Selene kills Quint with a silver grenade, and Eve kills Lane. When they return for Michael, his tank is empty, and they vow to find him first.

Shooting began in Vancouver in March 2011 without a finished script. Scott Speedman did not return as Michael and appears only in archive footage. Sony released it in January 2012. It opened at number one and grossed about $160 million worldwide on a $70 million budget, the highest total in the series. Rotten Tomatoes reported 25% approval and judged it heavy on action and light on story. Underworld: Blood Wars followed in 2016.

overview: A discount store clerk strikes up an affair with a stock boy who considers himself the incarnation of Holden Caulfield.
tagline: It's her last best chance... is she going to take it?
title: The Good Girl
plot:
The Good Girl is a thought-provoking drama that delves into the complexities of female identity, societal expectations, and the struggle for self-discovery. The film tells the story of Holly, a quiet and unassuming woman who feels trapped in her mundane life as a saleswoman at a small-town supermarket.

As the narrative unfolds, it becomes clear that Holly's existence is marked by a sense of disconnection and disillusionment. She feels suffocated by the monotony of her daily routine and the lack of personal fulfillment in her relationships. Her marriage to Phil, a seemingly perfect but unfulfilling partner, serves as a catalyst for her introspection.

The film expertly explores the tension between societal expectations and individual desires, highlighting the ways in which women are often forced to conform to narrow norms and stereotypes. Holly's desire for excitement, passion, and autonomy is constantly at odds with the mundane reality of her life.

Through Holly's character, the movie sheds light on the struggles of women who feel trapped by their circumstances, struggling to find a sense of purpose and identity in a world that often seems determined to constrain them. The film also touches on themes of loneliness, isolation, and the search for human connection in a seemingly indifferent world.

Ultimately, The Good Girl is a poignant exploration of the human condition, one that invites viewers to reflect on their own desires, aspirations, and sense of fulfillment.

overview: When 17-year-old Makoto Konno gains the ability to, quite literally, "leap" backwards through time, she immediately sets about improving her grades and preventing personal mishaps. However, she soon realises that changing the past isn't as simple as it seems, and eventually, will have to rely on her new powers to shape the future of herself and her friends.
tagline: There is a future that we can't wait for.
title: The Girl Who Leapt Through Time
plot:
The Girl Who Leapt Through Time is a 2006 Japanese science fiction film directed by Mamoru Hosoda, produced by Happinet Pictures, and distributed by Toho. 

The movie revolves around the life of Makoto "Makie" Tsuda, a high school girl who discovers she has the ability to time-travel after witnessing a tragic event in her past. As Makie navigates her newfound power, she must confront the consequences of altering events in her timeline.

Some of the main themes present in The Girl Who Leapt Through Time include:

1. **Self-discovery and growth**: Throughout the film, Makie struggles to understand herself and find her place in the world. Her time-traveling ability forces her to confront her own emotions, desires, and relationships.
2. **Love and relationships**: The movie explores the complexities of human connections, particularly between Makie and her friends, family members, and romantic interests. Makie's experiences with time travel lead her to reevaluate her relationships and prioritize what truly matters.
3. **Free will vs. determinism**: As Makie manipulates events in her timeline, she begins to question the nature of free will and whether her actions are predetermined or if she has control over her choices.
4. **Trauma and grief**: The film tackles themes of loss and trauma, particularly through Makie's experiences with her mother's death. Her time-traveling ability allows her to relive moments from her past, but also forces her to confront the pain and guilt associated with that event.
5. **Identity and belonging**: Makie's journey is also one of self-discovery, as she navigates her place within her community and finds a sense of belonging among those around her.

Overall, The Girl Who Leapt Through Time is a poignant exploration of human emotions, relationships, and the complexities of time itself.

overview: It's the year 2707. Earth's natural resources have all but been exhausted by mankind. Battles rage for the remainder between the competing Corporations. During one such battle the seal is broken and awakens an ancient and deadly machine that was once defeated thousands of years ago. The order that awaited its return must now lead a small group of soldiers to destroy it once and for all.
tagline: Welcome to the 23rd century.  The new dark ages.
title: Mutant Chronicles
plot:
Mutant Chronicles is a 2008 science fiction action film set in a post-apocalyptic future where humans have been genetically engineered to become super-soldiers known as mutants. The movie follows a group of mutants, including Connor (played by Aaron Eckhart), who are on a mission to prevent the outbreak of war between rival factions.

At its core, Mutant Chronicles explores themes of humanity and what it means to be alive in a world where technology has created a new breed of super-soldiers. The film delves into the consequences of playing god with genetic engineering, raising questions about the ethics of creating beings that are superior to humans but still possess human emotions and vulnerabilities.

The movie also touches on the idea of identity and self-discovery, as Connor struggles to come to terms with his own past and purpose in a world where he is no longer fully human. The film's narrative is driven by action and adventure, but beneath its surface lies a thought-provoking exploration of what it means to be alive and to find one's place in a world that values strength and power above all else.

Overall, Mutant Chronicles is a visually stunning film with a richly detailed world and complex characters, but its true value lies in its thought-provoking themes and commentary on the human condition.

overview: Becca, an anxious, non-vampire teen is torn between two boys. Before she can choose, Becca must get around her controlling father, who embarrasses Becca by treating her like a child. Meanwhile, Becca's friends contend with their own romantic issues - all of which collide at the prom.
tagline: Some sagas just won't die.
title: Vampires Suck
plot:
Vampires Suck is a 2010 American comedy horror film directed by Brian Duffield and written by Duffield and Paul S. Kemp. The movie is a parody of the Twilight Saga, specifically focusing on the vampire romance genre.

The main themes of Vampires Suck include:

1. Satire: The film uses humor to poke fun at the conventions of vampire movies and the Twilight series in particular, exaggerating the melodramatic elements for comedic effect.
2. Teenage angst: The movie explores the struggles of high school life, particularly the challenges faced by teenagers in love, as embodied by the main characters, Becca (Jenna Dewan) and Mark (Christopher McDonald).
3. High school social hierarchy: Vampires Suck critiques the social cliques and hierarchies present in high schools, using the vampire world as a metaphor for human teenage relationships.
4. Love vs. obsession: The film highlights the blurred lines between love and obsession, particularly in the context of vampire-human relationships, where the line between desire and possession becomes increasingly ambiguous.

The movie follows Becca, a high school student who falls in love with Mark, a vampire who is trying to resist his thirst for human blood. As their relationship deepens, they must navigate the challenges of being together while dealing with the pressures of high school life and the dangers posed by other vampires.

Overall, Vampires Suck uses humor and satire to explore themes that are relatable to teenagers, making it a lighthearted and entertaining take on the vampire genre.

original_title: Talladega Nights: The Ballad of Ricky Bobby
overview: The fastest man on four wheels, Ricky Bobby is one of the greatest drivers in NASCAR history. A big, hairy American winning machine, Ricky has everything a dimwitted daredevil could want, a luxurious mansion, a smokin' hot wife and all the fast food he can eat. But Ricky's turbo-charged lifestyle hits an unexpected speed bump when he's bested by flamboyant Euro-idiot Jean Girard and reduced to a fear-ridden wreck.
tagline: The story of a man who could only count to #1.
title: Talladega Nights: The Ballad of Ricky Bobby
plot:
Talladega Nights: The Ballad of Ricky Bobby is a comedy film released in 2006, directed by Adam McKay and starring Will Ferrell as the titular character. The movie follows the story of Ricky Bobby, a NASCAR driver who becomes a media sensation and a symbol of Southern American culture.

The film begins with Ricky Bobby (Will Ferrell) driving for a small racing team in North Carolina. He is a talented driver, but his lack of sophistication and poor manners often get him into trouble. After a series of victories, Ricky Bobby catches the attention of Cal Naughton Jr. (John C. Reilly), a fellow driver who becomes his friend and confidant.

Ricky Bobby's life changes when he meets IRL (Indianapolis Racing League) driver Jean Girard (Sacha Baron Cohen). The Frenchman is a highly skilled driver, but his arrogance and condescending attitude towards Ricky Bobby make him an instant rival. As the two drivers compete against each other, their rivalry becomes increasingly heated.

Meanwhile, Ricky Bobby's personal life begins to unravel. His wife, Carley (Leslie Bibb), feels neglected by her husband's increasing fame and attention from Jean Girard. The couple's relationship is put to the test as Ricky Bobby becomes more and more consumed by his racing career.

As the story unfolds, Ricky Bobby faces a series of challenges both on and off the track. He must confront his own ego and learn to balance his love for racing with his personal relationships. In the process, he also learns valuable lessons about humility, friendship, and the importance of staying true to oneself.

The film's climax features an intense showdown between Ricky Bobby and Jean Girard at the Talladega Superspeedway. The two drivers engage in a fierce battle, but ultimately, it is Ricky Bobby who emerges victorious.

In the end, Ricky Bobby learns a valuable lesson about the importance of humility and staying grounded. He also comes to appreciate his relationships with those around him, including Cal Naughton Jr. and Carley. The film concludes on a heartwarming note, as Ricky Bobby returns home to North Carolina, where he is welcomed back as a hero.

Throughout the film, Will Ferrell's comedic genius shines through in his portrayal of Ricky Bobby. His over-the-top performance brings humor and wit to the story, making Talladega Nights: The Ballad of Ricky Bobby a hilarious and entertaining ride from start to finish.

overview: Ba'al travels back in time and prevents the Stargate program from being started. SG-1 must somehow restore history.
tagline: History may never repeat itself again.
title: Stargate: Continuum
plot:
Stargate: Continuum is a science fiction film that delves into the complexities of time travel and its consequences on human relationships. The movie explores the theme of sacrifice, as the protagonist, Samantha Carter, must make difficult choices to ensure the survival of humanity.

The film also examines the concept of free will versus determinism, as the characters navigate through different timelines and confront the possibility that their actions may be predetermined. This raises questions about the nature of choice and whether individuals have control over their destinies.

Furthermore, Stargate: Continuum touches on the theme of redemption, particularly in the character of Jack O'Neill, who grapples with his past mistakes and seeks to make amends. The movie also highlights the importance of trust and loyalty among friends and allies, as they work together to overcome seemingly insurmountable challenges.

Ultimately, Stargate: Continuum presents a thought-provoking narrative that delves into the intricacies of time travel, human relationships, and personal growth, leaving audiences with a sense of introspection and contemplation.

overview: Four small gangsters from Copenhagen trick a gangster boss: they take over 4,000,000 kroner which they were supposed to bring him. Trying to escape to Barcelona they are forced to stop in the countryside, in an old, wrecked house, hiding there for several weeks. Slowly, one after another, they realize, that they would like to stay there, start a new life.
title: Flickering Lights
plot:
Flickering Lights (Danish: Blinkende lygter) is a 2000 Danish black comedy crime film written and directed by Anders Thomas Jensen in his feature directing debut. Søren Pilmark stars as Torkild, with Ulrich Thomsen as Peter, Mads Mikkelsen as Arne and Nikolaj Lie Kaas as Stefan, four small-time Copenhagen criminals. Iben Hjejle plays Torkild's girlfriend Therese, Sofie Gråbøl plays Stefan's girlfriend Hanne and Peter Andersson plays a menacing gangster from the Faroe Islands.

Torkild leads a gang of petty but ruthless thieves, and his 40th birthday goes badly. His girlfriend leaves him, he nearly shoots friends when he mistakes his surprise party for a hit, and his present is a new submachine gun. Longing for one last score that will let him retire abroad, he and his three friends are hired by the Faroese gangster to steal a bag of money. One of them is wounded in a shootout with security guards, but they escape with the loot. When they find that the bag holds more than four million kroner, they decide to double-cross their employer and flee with it to Barcelona.

On the way their car breaks down in the countryside, and they take refuge in an old, abandoned house that was once a restaurant. Hiding there for weeks, the four gradually realize they do not want to leave. Torkild comes up with the idea of restoring the building and reopening it as a restaurant, and one by one the others embrace the chance to start a new life. Meanwhile, the trigger-happy Arne roams the woods with an eccentric local, shooting at every animal in sight. A series of flashbacks reveals the troubled and often abusive families in which the four grew up, and how gang life became a substitute family for them. Their past eventually catches up with them, however, when the Faroese gangster and his men come looking for Torkild, while an unexpected visitor also arrives at the restaurant.

The film was a runaway hit in Denmark on its release in November 2000. Variety's Gunnar Rehlin praised Jensen's assured direction, the rapid pacing, the deft action scenes and the excellent cast, describing the film at heart as a celebration of friendship between men, though he warned that its dark, brutal humor might offend conventional sensibilities. Cinematographer Eric Kress won the cinematography prize at Gothenburg. At the 2001 Robert Awards, the film received the Audience Award and the award for Best Cinematography. Jensen had previously written In China They Eat Dogs and Mifune.

overview: When Lois Lane is killed, an unhinged Superman decides to take control of the Earth. Determined to stop him, Batman creates a team of freedom-fighting heroes. But when superheroes go to war, can the world survive?
title: Injustice
plot:
Injustice is an American adult animated superhero film of 2021 loosely based on NetherRealm Studios' Injustice video games, adapting elements of Injustice: Gods Among Us (2013) and its prequel comic. Directed by Matt Peters from a script by Ernie Altbacker, it is the 47th DC Universe Animated Original Movie. Justin Hartley voices Superman and Anson Mount Batman, with Laura Bailey as Lois Lane, Janet Varney as Wonder Woman, Kevin Pollak as the Joker, Gillian Jacobs as Harley Quinn, Zach Callison as Robin and Anika Noni Rose as Catwoman.

On an alternate Earth, the Joker and Harley Quinn murder Jimmy Olsen, kidnap the pregnant Lois Lane and link a stolen nuclear bomb to her heartbeat. After killing the Flash with a trap, the Joker doses Superman with fear toxin laced with kryptonite, so that the hero believes he is fighting Doomsday when in fact he is killing Lois. Her death triggers the bomb, which destroys Metropolis and kills eleven million people. When the Joker gloats to Batman that he chose Superman as his new target, Superman kills him, then reveals his identity at the United Nations and vows to impose peace by force. The Justice League splits: Wonder Woman backs him, Batman keeps his rule against killing, and others withdraw altogether.

Superman's regime grows harsher. Robin defects to him and accidentally kills Nightwing, who is resurrected by Rama Kushna as Deadwing, while Batman builds an underground Insurgency. A raid on the Fortress of Solitude for a red-sun weapon fails, and when Green Arrow's arrow is deflected and kills Jonathan Kent, Superman murders him. Turning the world into a surveillance state, Superman allies with Ra's al Ghul, whose android Amazo turns on him and kills Hawkman and Cyborg before the heroes destroy it, and Robin, repentant, defeats Ra's. Superman moves to arrest the Insurgents, but Mister Terrific summons heroes from other worlds: an alternate Superman, who is beaten, and an alternate Lois, who lost her own Superman and reminds him that all life is sacred. Realising how far he has fallen, Superman surrenders, and Batman begins rebuilding the world with Catwoman at his side.

Announced in mid-2021, the film leaked online ten days before its release on Blu-ray, 4K and digital on 19 October 2021. Reviews were mixed, with 50% on Rotten Tomatoes; critics liked the action and voice work but faulted the pacing and departures from the source material.

overview: In 1970s Iran, Marjane 'Marji' Statrapi watches events through her young eyes and her idealistic family of a long dream being fulfilled of the hated Shah's defeat in the Iranian Revolution of 1979. However as Marji grows up, she witnesses first hand how the new Iran, now ruled by Islamic fundamentalists, has become a repressive tyranny on its own.
title: Persepolis
plot:
Persepolis is a powerful and poignant film that explores the complexities of identity, culture, and politics through the eyes of its protagonist, Marjane Satrapi. The movie delves into the tumultuous years following the Iranian Revolution in 1979, as Marjane navigates her way through adolescence amidst the societal upheaval.

At its core, Persepolis is a deeply personal and introspective film that grapples with the tensions between tradition and modernity, as embodied by Marjane's own conflicted identity. The movie masterfully weaves together elements of coming-of-age narrative, social commentary, and autobiographical storytelling to create a rich tapestry of themes.

One of the primary concerns of Persepolis is the struggle for self-discovery and autonomy in the face of oppressive societal expectations. Marjane's journey is marked by her desire to break free from the constraints of her traditional upbringing and forge her own path, even as she grapples with the complexities of her own cultural heritage.

The film also explores the devastating impact of war and politics on individuals and communities, particularly in the context of Iran's tumultuous history. Persepolis offers a searing critique of the Iranian Revolution and its aftermath, highlighting the ways in which ideology can be used to control and manipulate individuals, often with disastrous consequences.

Throughout the movie, Satrapi's distinctive visual style and narrative voice serve as powerful tools for conveying the emotional intensity and psychological complexity of Marjane's experiences. The film's use of vibrant colors, bold lines, and expressive characters creates a sense of immediacy and intimacy, drawing the viewer into Marjane's inner world and inviting them to share in her struggles and triumphs.

Ultimately, Persepolis is a deeply moving and thought-provoking film that offers a nuanced and multifaceted exploration of identity, culture, and politics. Through its powerful storytelling and memorable characters, the movie provides a searing indictment of oppression and a testament to the resilience and strength of the human spirit.

overview: Connected by phone in the same home but 20 years apart, a serial killer puts another woman’s past — and life — on the line to change her own fate.
tagline: A call from a serial killer... She'll begin to hunt your past.
title: The Call
plot:
The Call is a 2020 South Korean psychological thriller film directed by Lee Joon-myeong and produced by Next Entertainment World.

The main themes of The Call revolve around the complex relationships between mothers, daughters, and the societal expectations placed upon them. The story follows a mother-daughter duo who are struggling to cope with their troubled past, and how they navigate through their complicated emotions towards each other.

One of the primary themes is the exploration of the complexities of mother-daughter relationships, particularly in the context of trauma, guilt, and forgiveness. The film delves into the emotional scars that can be left on individuals after experiencing traumatic events, and how these experiences can shape one's perception of themselves and their relationships with others.

Another significant theme is the societal pressure placed on women to conform to traditional roles and expectations. The mother-daughter duo in the film are forced to navigate through a patriarchal society that often prioritizes men's needs over women's, leading to feelings of resentment and frustration.

The film also touches upon themes of mental health, particularly depression and anxiety, which are often stigmatized in Korean culture. The protagonist's struggles with her mental health serve as a catalyst for the events that unfold, highlighting the importance of acknowledging and addressing these issues.

Throughout the film, the director skillfully weaves together these themes to create a complex and thought-provoking narrative that challenges societal norms and expectations.

overview: Laurie Strode comes to her final confrontation with Michael Myers, the masked figure who has haunted her since she narrowly escaped his killing spree on Halloween night four decades ago.
tagline: Face Your Fate.
title: Halloween
plot:
Halloween is a 2018 American slasher film directed by David Gordon Green, who co-wrote it with Jeff Fradley and Danny McBride. The eleventh installment in the Halloween series, it is a direct sequel to John Carpenter's 1978 original that disregards every other film in the franchise. Jamie Lee Curtis reprises her role as Laurie Strode, and James Jude Courtney plays Michael Myers, with Nick Castle returning to the role for a cameo; Judy Greer, Andi Matichak, Will Patton and Haluk Bilginer co-star.

On October 29, 2018, Michael, confined at Smith's Grove psychiatric hospital for four decades, is about to be transferred to another facility. True crime podcasters Aaron Korey and Dana Haines visit him. In Haddonfield, Laurie still lives in fear, drinking heavily inside her fortified house. Her daughter, Karen, was taken from her by the state at age twelve and remains estranged, while Laurie's granddaughter, Allyson, tries to stay close to her. On the night of October 30, the transfer bus crashes and Michael escapes. The next day he murders the podcasters at his sister Judith's grave, kills a mechanic for his overalls and recovers his mask.

That Halloween night, Allyson leaves a party after finding her boyfriend cheating; Michael kills her best friend. Laurie and Deputy Frank Hawkins, who arrested Michael in 1978, respond to the scene, and Laurie shoots Michael before he escapes. Karen and her husband, Ray, are taken to Laurie's house for protection. Hawkins subdues Michael and tries to kill him, but Michael's psychiatrist, Dr. Ranbir Sartain, who secretly arranged Michael's escape to study him in the wild, attacks Hawkins and drives toward Laurie's home with Michael and Allyson in the back seat. Michael wakes, kills Sartain, the officers guarding the house and Ray. In the final confrontation, he stabs Laurie and throws her from a balcony, but when he looks down her body has vanished, echoing their first encounter. Karen shoots him, and the three women trap him in the basement safe room and set the house on fire. A post-credits scene suggests Michael survived.

The film premiered in the Midnight Madness section of the Toronto International Film Festival in September 2018 and was released on October 19. It grossed $259.9 million worldwide. Critics responded favorably, with 79% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 67, praising its return to basic but effective ingredients.

overview: In the small village where Amadeo lives there is no one good enough to challenge his skills at Table Football. But, while Amadeo may be a genius as a table football player in real life he's a loser. He's in love with Lara, his childhood friend, but he's so shy that he can't bring himself to confess his love for her. So he just hangs out in his quaint, timeless village. When Amadeo beats the village bully Flash at Table Football. The scene is set for an epic rivalry. Consumed with anger Flash vows to get even and 10 years later he returns as an International Superstar, a Football Icon and Galatico determined to wreak his revenge.
tagline: There's only one team this summer.
title: Underdogs
plot:
Underdogs (Spanish: Metegol, meaning "table football"; released in the United Kingdom as The Unbeatables) is a 2013 Argentine-Spanish animated sports comedy film co-written, produced, directed and edited by Juan José Campanella. It is loosely based on the short story "Memorias de un wing derecho" ("Memoirs of a Right Winger") by Argentine writer Roberto Fontanarrosa, and Campanella developed the screenplay with co-writer and producer Gaston Gorali and Eduardo Sacheri, his collaborator on The Secret in Their Eyes. Costing $21 million, it became the most expensive Argentine film ever made and the most expensive Latin American animated feature.

A father tucking his son into bed tells him a story, asking him to use his imagination. Years earlier, in a quiet little town, a shy boy named Amadeo works in a bar and is the best table football player around. He is secretly in love with Laura, a girl he met there. One day a bully named Grosso challenges him to a match in front of her, and despite his reluctance Amadeo wins to the applause of the whole bar. The humiliated Grosso is soon taken on by a manager, and seven years later he returns as the most famous soccer player in the world, determined to avenge the only defeat of his life. He buys the entire town, sending the mayor fleeing by helicopter, builds a gigantic stadium on its site, plans to tear down the bar where he lost, takes possession of the old table and sets out to win Laura's affection. Just when Amadeo has lost everything, he discovers something magical: the little players of his table football game come to life, able to talk and make plans. Together they set off on an adventure to rescue Laura and save the town, and along the way they learn to become a real team. Amadeo then forms a soccer team of his own and challenges Grosso's squad to a match for the town's future, in which skill, teamwork and sportsmanship are put to the test against Grosso's arrogance.

Released by Universal Pictures in Argentina on 18 July 2013, the film opened at number one with a record opening for an Argentine film, outperforming Despicable Me 2 and Monsters University. An English version reached British cinemas in August 2014, while the North American version, voiced by a cast including Ariana Grande, Nicholas Hoult and Mel Brooks, was released on Netflix and on DVD in 2016 after a planned theatrical release was scrapped. The original version was well received, while the American version earned mixed reviews.

original_title: 名探偵コナン 迷宮の十字路
overview: Mouri Kogoro is called to a special case in the ancient capital of Kyoto. There, Conan meets Heiji and they team up once again to solve the case, recover the stolen Healing Buddha statue, and even discover the identity of Heiji's first love.
title: Detective Conan: Crossroad in the Ancient Capital
plot:
Detective Conan: Crossroad in the Ancient Capital is a thought-provoking mystery film that delves into the complexities of time travel, identity, and the consequences of one's actions. The movie follows Shinichi Kudo, who finds himself transported back to ancient Heian-era Japan, where he must navigate a complex web of intrigue and deception.

At its core, the film explores the theme of identity and how it is shaped by our experiences and relationships. Shinichi, as both Conan Edogawa and Shinichi Kudo, grapples with his dual identities and the consequences of his actions in each timeline. This internal conflict serves as a metaphor for the human experience, where our sense of self is often fragmented and influenced by external factors.

The film also touches on the theme of time travel and its potential consequences. The ancient capital's unique energy allows Shinichi to move through time, but this power comes with great responsibility and risks. As he navigates different eras, Shinichi must confront the possibility that his actions in one timeline could have far-reaching effects on others.

Furthermore, Detective Conan: Crossroad in the Ancient Capital explores the idea of loyalty and friendship. Shinichi's relationships with his friends and allies, particularly Ran Mori and Sonoko Suzuki, serve as a source of strength and motivation for him as he navigates the complexities of ancient Japan.

Throughout the film, these themes are woven together to create a rich tapestry of intrigue and suspense. The movie's use of time travel as a narrative device allows it to explore complex ideas in a unique and engaging way, making it a compelling watch for fans of the Detective Conan series.

overview: When Martians suddenly abduct his mom, mischievous Milo rushes to the rescue and discovers why all moms are so special.
tagline: Mom needs a little space.
title: Mars Needs Moms
plot:
Mars Needs Moms is a 3D science fiction comedy film directed by Simon Wells and produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie was released on March 18, 2011.

In the beginning of the story, we are introduced to Milo (played by Seth Green), an 11-year-old boy who lives with his mother, Marta (played by Mindy Sterling), in a suburban town. Milo's life is ordinary and uneventful, but he longs for adventure and excitement. One day, while out on a walk, Milo discovers that Marta has been abducted by aliens from Mars.

The aliens, known as the Martian Moms, arrive on Earth to collect human mothers to take back to their planet. They use a device called the "Moms' Transporter" to abduct the mothers, leaving behind only one child per family. The Martian Moms believe that human children are inferior and will eventually grow up to be loyal servants.

Milo soon discovers that his mother has been taken by the aliens and sets out on a journey to rescue her. He meets a robot named Gadget (voiced by Dan Fogler), who was also left behind by his own mother, and together they embark on a quest to Mars to find Marta.

Upon arrival on Mars, Milo and Gadget encounter various obstacles and challenges as they navigate the planet's harsh environment. They meet a group of Martian kids who are being raised by the alien mothers, but have grown up to be rebellious and independent. The kids, led by a character named Lopax (voiced by Elisabeth Harnois), join forces with Milo and Gadget to help them on their mission.

As they journey deeper into Mars, Milo and his new friends face numerous challenges, including treacherous terrain, hostile aliens, and the harsh conditions of the Martian environment. Along the way, Milo learns valuable lessons about responsibility, loyalty, and the importance of family.

In the end, Milo and Gadget successfully rescue Marta from the clutches of the Martian Moms. However, in a surprising twist, it is revealed that the Martian Moms' plan was not to enslave humans, but to protect them from an even greater threat: a massive asteroid that is on a collision course with Earth.

With the help of the Martian kids and their mothers, Milo and Gadget are able to deflect the asteroid and save humanity. The movie ends with Milo returning home to his mother, who has been reunited with him, but not before learning about the incredible adventure he had on Mars.

Overall, Mars Needs Moms is a fun and action-packed sci-fi comedy that explores themes of family, loyalty, and responsibility. While it received mixed reviews from critics, the movie has its fans and offers a unique blend of humor, adventure, and heart.

overview: A gallerist risks her family and flourishing career when she enters into an affair with a talented painter and slowly loses control of her life.
tagline: Every Woman Needs an Escape
title: Addicted
plot:
Addicted is a 2014 American drama film directed by Bille Woodruff and starring Shannen Doherty, Tika Sumpter, and Keesha Sharp.

The main themes of Addicted include:

1. **Codependency**: The movie explores the complex relationships between women who are addicted to men, often referred to as "codependent" relationships. These relationships can be emotionally, physically, or financially abusive.
2. **Trauma and Abuse**: The film delves into the traumatic experiences of the characters, particularly those who have been victims of domestic violence and emotional abuse. It highlights the long-lasting effects of these experiences on a person's life.
3. **Empowerment and Self-Discovery**: As the characters navigate their relationships and personal struggles, they begin to discover their own strengths, values, and identities. This journey is marked by moments of growth, self-awareness, and empowerment.
4. **Sisterhood and Support**: The movie showcases the importance of female friendships and support networks. The characters form strong bonds with each other, which helps them overcome their individual struggles and find a sense of belonging.

The plot follows a group of women who meet at a support group for people struggling with codependent relationships. As they share their stories and experiences, they begin to realize that they are not alone in their struggles. Through their interactions, the characters learn to let go of their toxic relationships and discover new paths to healing and self-discovery.

Overall, Addicted is a thought-provoking drama that sheds light on the complexities of codependent relationships and the importance of female empowerment and support.

overview: A young man’s difficult entry into adulthood, who experiences the highs and lows of his first love, while dealing with the familial fallout spurred by the financial crisis of 2008.
title: First Love
plot:
First Love is a 2022 American romance film written and directed by A. J. Edwards, starring Hero Fiennes Tiffin as Jim Albright and Sydney Park as Ann, with Diane Kruger and Jeffrey Donovan as Jim's parents, Kay and Greg Albright, and Diane Venora as Kay's Aunt Irene. Filmed in Los Angeles, it follows how two young people meet in high school, drift apart and find their way back to each other over the following years, while Jim's family struggles through hard times.

When the 2008 recession costs his father Greg his bank job, high school senior Jim hopes to apply to colleges that might offer him at least a partial track scholarship. Racing to finish a paper in the school library, he catches sight of a fellow senior, Ann, through a bookcase and is instantly smitten. Too shy to approach her normally, Jim pulls her out of Spanish class with a fake note from the administration just so he can talk to her, and after school she asks him for a ride, which turns into an afternoon spent at a spot overlooking the ocean. As Greg searches for work and Kay wrestles with caring for her Aunt Irene, who raised her, and endures criticism of Greg from her brother, Jim and Ann's romance deepens; he brings her home to meet his parents and tells her he loves her. Ann's mother, however, urges her to keep the relationship casual so that she can be free when she goes to college, and when Ann reveals she will attend college in New York while Jim stays in California, she asks to keep things light. The couple drift apart, they graduate, and Jim leaves for UCLA as his unemployed parents are forced to downsize their home. Two years later, Jim finds his parents worn down by financial hardship, just as an unexpected voicemail from Ann gives the pair a chance to discover whether their first love can survive the realities of adult life.

The film was released in theaters and on demand in the United States on June 17, 2022. Its original score by Richard Reed Parry was replaced with one by George Kallis. It holds a 33% rating on Rotten Tomatoes from six reviews, and Matt Zoller Seitz of RogerEbert.com noted the film's considerable untapped potential while finding it watchable thanks to its cinematography and performances.

overview: A young elf mistakes a tiny alien for a Christmas gift, not knowing her new plaything has plans to destroy Earth's gravity — and steal all the presents.
title: Alien Xmas
plot:
Alien Xmas is a 2020 stop-motion animated science fiction comedy film directed by Seth Green and produced by Chiodo Bros. Productions, in association with Universal Pictures.

The main theme of Alien Xmas revolves around the idea of an alien invasion during Christmas time. The story follows a group of humans who are trying to survive when an alien spaceship crash-lands on Earth, bringing with it an extraterrestrial creature that wreaks havoc on their holiday celebrations.

Throughout the film, the characters face various challenges and obstacles as they try to outsmart the alien and save Christmas. Along the way, they learn valuable lessons about teamwork, friendship, and the true meaning of the holiday season.

One of the main themes of Alien Xmas is the idea that even in the most chaotic and unexpected situations, there is always hope for a happy ending. The film's lighthearted tone and comedic moments help to balance out the tension and danger posed by the alien invasion, making it a fun and entertaining holiday watch.

Another theme present in the film is the importance of family and community during the holidays. As the characters work together to defeat the alien and save Christmas, they also come to appreciate the value of their relationships with each other and the people around them.

Overall, Alien Xmas is a heartwarming and humorous holiday film that explores themes of hope, teamwork, and the importance of family and community during the most wonderful time of the year.

overview: In the post–World War II South, two families are pitted against a barbaric social hierarchy and an unrelenting landscape as they simultaneously fight the battle at home and the battle abroad.
title: Mudbound
plot:
Mudbound is a powerful and poignant film that explores the complexities of racial tension, family dynamics, and the struggles of rural life during World War II. The movie delves into the lives of two families, one black and one white, living in the Mississippi Delta region.

At its core, Mudbound is a story about the devastating consequences of racism and the long-lasting impact it has on individuals and communities. The film sheds light on the brutal realities faced by African Americans during this period, including forced labor, segregation, and violence. Through the characters' experiences, the movie highlights the ways in which systemic racism can destroy lives and relationships.

The film also explores themes of family, love, and loyalty, as both families grapple with their own demons and struggles. The white family's patriarch, Henry, is a complex character whose troubled past and sense of entitlement are slowly revealed throughout the story. In contrast, the black family's matriarch, Florence, is a strong and resilient woman who holds her family together despite the hardships they face.

One of the most striking aspects of Mudbound is its portrayal of the interconnectedness of these two families. Despite their differences, both families are bound together by their experiences as farmers in the rural South, and their struggles are deeply intertwined. The film shows how the actions of one family can have far-reaching consequences for another, highlighting the devastating effects of racism on individuals and communities.

Ultimately, Mudbound is a powerful exploration of the human condition, revealing the complexities and nuances of life in the American South during World War II. Through its thought-provoking themes and well-developed characters, the film offers a nuanced and empathetic portrayal of two families struggling to survive and thrive in a society marked by racism and oppression.

original_title: Scooby-Doo! Mask of the Blue Falcon
overview: The Mega Mondo Pop Cartoon-a-Con in sunny California marks the spot for mystery in this all-new original Scooby-Doo adventure! Herculoids Frankenstein Jr. and Space Ghost are just a few of the celebrated comic book characters headlining at the unconventional convention plus there's a megabucks movie premiere starring Scooby-Doo and Shaggy's all-time favorite super heroes Blue Falcon and Dynomutt! So when the gruesome villain Mr. Hyde unleashes monster bats howling hounds and sinister slime upon the festivities it's time for Mystery Incorporated to follow the clues and set their monster traps.
