Filmed in Limousin and Paris in 2014, Summertime premiered at the Locarno Film Festival, where it won the Variety Piazza Grande Award, and opened in France on 19 August 2015. Critics admired it, giving it 92% on Rotten Tomatoes.

overview: When an attack on the Kingsman headquarters takes place and a new villain rises, Eggsy and Merlin are forced to work together with the American agency known as the Statesman to save the world.
tagline: Reports of my death have been greatly exaggerated.
title: Kingsman: The Golden Circle
plot:
Kingsman: The Golden Circle is a 2017 action spy comedy film directed by Matthew Vaughn, produced by 20th Century Fox. The movie serves as the sequel to the 2014 film Kingsman: The Secret Service.

The story begins with Eggsy Unwin (Taron Egerton), now a full-fledged agent of Her Majesty's Secret Intelligence Service (MIS), working alongside his mentor Harry Hart (Colin Firth) and their colleagues. However, during a mission in Mexico, Harry is killed by the villainous Poppy Adams (Julianne Moore).

Poppy, a former CIA operative turned global terrorist, has created a deadly virus that she plans to unleash on the world. Eggsy is recruited by Statesman, an American spy agency, to help stop Poppy and her organization, known as Golden Circle.

Eggsy travels to the United States, where he meets Arthur (Jeffrey Wright), the head of Statesman, and his team, including Whiskey (Pedro Pascal) and Ginger (Halle Berry). Together, they embark on a mission to infiltrate Poppy's inner circle and gather intelligence on her plans.

As Eggsy navigates this new world, he discovers that Poppy has created a network of loyal followers, known as the Golden Circle, who are brainwashed into carrying out her orders. The team soon realizes that Poppy's ultimate goal is to create a deadly virus that will wipe out half of the world's population.

The plot thickens as Eggsy and his new allies work to stop Poppy and her minions. Along the way, they encounter various characters, including a young American agent named Roxy (Sophie Cooker) who becomes Eggsy's love interest.

As the story unfolds, Eggsy faces numerous challenges, from high-stakes battles with Poppy's henchmen to navigating the complexities of Statesman's bureaucracy. Meanwhile, Arthur and Whiskey work behind the scenes to undermine Poppy's plans and gather intelligence on her organization.

The film's climax features an epic showdown between Eggsy and Poppy, as well as a confrontation between Statesman and Golden Circle. In the end, Eggsy and his team successfully stop Poppy from unleashing the virus, but not before she exacts a personal revenge on Arthur.

Throughout the movie, Vaughn pays homage to various spy franchises, including James Bond and Mission: Impossible. The film's action sequences are fast-paced and thrilling, with plenty of humor and wit to keep audiences entertained.

Overall, Kingsman: The Golden Circle is an entertaining and action-packed sequel that expands on the world introduced in the first film. With its talented cast, witty dialogue, and over-the-top action sequences, it's a must-see for fans of spy thrillers and comedy.

overview: When her father unexpectedly passes away, young Ella finds herself at the mercy of her cruel stepmother and her daughters. Never one to give up hope, Ella's fortunes begin to change after meeting a dashing stranger in the woods.
tagline: Midnight is just the beginning.
title: Cinderella
plot:
Cinderella is a 2015 American musical fantasy film directed by Kenneth Branagh, produced by Walt Disney Pictures, and based on the classic fairy tale of the same name. The film stars Lily James as Cinderella, Richard Madden as Prince Charming, Cate Blanchett as Lady Tremaine, and Helena Bonham Carter as Fairy Godmother.

The story begins with Cinderella's father, a widower, who marries Lady Tremaine (Cate Blanchett) and her two daughters, Drizella and Anastasia. After Cinderella's father passes away, Lady Tremaine treats Cinderella poorly, forcing her to do all the household chores while making her stepdaughters spoiled and lazy.

One day, an invitation arrives from the palace announcing a royal ball, where Prince Charming (Richard Madden) will be attending. Lady Tremaine is determined for one of her daughters to attend the ball and marry the prince, but Cinderella is not allowed to go.

Fairy Godmother (Helena Bonham Carter), who has been watching over Cinderella from afar, appears and helps Cinderella get ready for the ball by transforming a pumpkin into a beautiful carriage, mice into horses, and a rat into a coachman. She also gives Cinderella a stunning gown and off she goes to the palace.

At the ball, Cinderella and Prince Charming dance and fall in love, but Cinderella must leave before midnight when the magic wears off. In her haste, she loses one of her glass slippers, which Prince Charming finds and vows to find the girl whose foot fits it.

The next day, Prince Charming visits all the eligible maidens in the kingdom, trying the glass slipper on each foot until he finds Cinderella's. When he arrives at Cinderella's house, Lady Tremaine tries to fit her own daughters into the slipper, but it doesn't fit either of them. When Cinderella finally gets a chance to try the slipper, it fits perfectly.

Prince Charming and Cinderella get married in a grand ceremony, with Fairy Godmother watching over them. The film ends with Cinderella and Prince Charming living happily ever after, surrounded by their friends and family.

Throughout the film, Kenneth Branagh's direction brings a new level of depth and emotion to the classic story, while Lily James shines as the kind and gentle Cinderella. The film's visuals are stunning, with beautiful costumes and sets that bring the fairy tale world to life.

Overall, Cinderella (2015) is a delightful retelling of the classic fairy tale, with a strong focus on character development and a beautiful soundtrack by Patrick Doyle.

overview: Aphrodite was made famous back in the day for performing THE timeless love song of the era. The song that everyone plays at their weddings, in every sappy commercial for diamonds or rings or puppies or soldiers coming home. It made her a ton of money, but Aphrodite HATES this song. She’s now the meanest judge on Pop The Question but her life changes when Brianna, becomes the breakthrough contestant, exuding love and purity. When Aphrodite reluctantly becomes her mentor, she does everything possible to steer her away from love and love anthems and so is visited by three spirits who take Aphrodite on a journey through love (and Christmas) past, present and future to try and shake her out of her funk and let love back in!
title: A New Diva's Christmas Carol
plot:
I couldn't find any information on "A New Diva's Christmas Carol" released in 2022 by Blue Ice Pictures. 

However, I can tell you that there is a movie called "A New Diva's Christmas Carol" released in 2017, not 2022, and it was produced by Blue Ice Pictures.

If this isn't the one you are referring to, please provide more information or clarify which movie you are looking for.

overview: After his brother dies in a car crash, a disgraced MMA fighter takes over the family nightclub — and soon learns his sibling's death wasn’t an accident.
title: Bartkowiak
plot:
Bartkowiak is a 2021 Polish action thriller directed by Daniel Markowicz from a screenplay by Australian writer Daniel Bernardi. Józef Pawłowski stars as a disgraced mixed martial arts fighter who takes over his late brother's Warsaw nightclub and discovers that the crash that killed him was no accident, with Zofia Domalik, Szymon Bobrowski, Bartłomiej Topa and Janusz Chabior in supporting roles. Netflix released it on July 28, 2021.

Tomek Bartkowiak is on the verge of beating the heavily tattooed Repeć when he is apparently drugged; he loses, is branded a doper, and his coach Paweł Sozoniuk loses the large sum he bet on him and turns to drink. Tomek retreats to a cabin in the mountains near Zakopane, where his elder brother Wiktor offers him a place running Ring, the family nightclub in Warsaw. Soon afterwards Wiktor dies in a high-speed collision with a truck belonging to a company called Sanstal. Tomek takes charge of the club with Paweł's daughter Dominika, his former girlfriend, and they reopen it, rekindling their romance. Ring, however, stands in an old district coveted by powerful developers planning a glittering office tower, among them the refined but sadistic Rafał Kołodziejczyk, who is also Repeć's uncle. Offered two million to sell, Tomek spots Sanstal's stamp on the contract and tears it up. He fires the club's corrupt staff and, after a drunken brawl that clears the air, recruits the now-sober Paweł to handle security. When thugs with baseball bats attack the club, Paweł fights them off but is stabbed, and bribed police side with the attackers. Tomek realises his downfall in the ring, Wiktor's death and the pressure on local businesses are all connected. Captured by Kołodziejczyk's men and forced to sign over the club, he is saved when the wounded Paweł reappears, and together they rescue Dominika. In a final reckoning Tomek defeats Repeć, records evidence of the conspiracy, and Kołodziejczyk meets his end. Three months later Paweł is coaching again and Tomek returns to fighting.

Pawłowski plays Tomek, with Domalik as Dominika, Bobrowski as Paweł, Topa as Kołodziejczyk, Chabior as Ireneusz Parzych, Damian Majewski as Repeć and Antoni Pawlicki as Wiktor, while Danuta Stenka and Rafał Zawierucha appear in supporting roles. Decider's Johnny Loftus likened its plot to Road House and found it standard and light on fights, but recommended it for its solid performances, singling out Topa's menacing villain.

overview: Exactly one year after Tom meets Violet, he surprises her with a wedding ring. By all accounts, Tom and Violet are destined for their happily ever after. However, this engaged couple just keep getting tripped up on the long walk down the aisle.
tagline: A comedy about the journey between popping the question and tying the knot.
title: The Five-Year Engagement
plot:
The Five-Year Engagement is a romantic comedy that explores the complexities and nuances of love, relationships, and commitment. At its core, the movie delves into the theme of unrequited love and the struggles that come with it.

The film follows the story of Tom (played by Jason Segel), a man who falls deeply in love with his fiancée, Violet (played by Emily Blunt), but ultimately loses her to another man. This experience leaves Tom heartbroken and uncertain about his ability to find true love again.

As the movie progresses, it becomes clear that Tom's obsession with Violet is rooted in his own insecurities and fears of being alone. His fixation on her stems from a deep-seated need for validation and acceptance, which ultimately leads him down a path of self-discovery and growth.

Throughout the film, the director, Nicholas Stoller, masterfully weaves together themes of love, loss, and redemption, creating a narrative that is both poignant and humorous. The movie's portrayal of Tom's journey from heartbreak to healing is both relatable and endearing, making it easy for audiences to become invested in his story.

Ultimately, The Five-Year Engagement is a film about the power of love to transform and redeem us, even in the face of adversity. It reminds us that true love requires vulnerability, trust, and commitment, and that sometimes, it takes time and effort to find our way back to ourselves and to each other.

original_title: Scooby-Doo! and the Legend of the Vampire
overview: The Yowie Yahoo starts kidnapping musicians at a concert attended by Scooby and the gang in Vampire Rock, Australia.
title: Scooby-Doo! and the Legend of the Vampire
plot:
Scooby-Doo! and the Legend of the Vampire is a 2003 animated mystery comedy film that follows the classic Scooby-Doo formula, but with a unique twist. The main theme of this movie revolves around the idea of identity and how it can be manipulated to achieve one's goals.

The story centers around Fred Jones, who becomes obsessed with vampires after being bitten by one, leading him to believe he is now a vampire himself. As the gang tries to uncover the truth behind the mysterious vampire attacks, they begin to question their own identities and whether they are truly what they seem.

Throughout the film, the characters grapple with the idea of self-discovery and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy. The movie also explores the theme of peer pressure and how it can lead people to conform to certain expectations or behaviors.

The film's use of humor, satire, and social commentary adds depth to its themes, making it a fun and engaging watch for both children and adults. Overall, Scooby-Doo! and the Legend of the Vampire is a lighthearted and entertaining film that explores complex themes in a way that is accessible to all ages.

overview: Cosmoball is a mesmerizing intergalactic game of future played between humans and aliens at the giant extraterrestrial ship hovering in the sky over Earth. A young man with enormous power of an unknown nature joins the team of hot-headed superheroes in exchange for a cure for his mother’s deadly illness. The Four from Earth will fight not only to defend the honor of their home planet in the spectacular game, but to face the unprecedented threat to the Galaxy and embrace their own destiny.
title: Cosmoball
plot:
Cosmoball, also known as Goalkeeper of the Galaxy (Russian: Vratar Galaktiki), is a 2020 Russian 3D superhero space opera written and directed by Dzhanik Fayziev, based on the animated series Galactik Football. Yevgeny Romantsov stars as Anton, with Viktoriya Agalakova as Natasha, Maria Lisovaya as Anya, Ivan Ivanovich as Pele, Yelizaveta Taychenacheva as Fan and Yevgeny Mironov and Elena Yakovleva in supporting roles.

In 2071, galactic wars have destroyed the Moon and shifted Earth's poles, transforming the climate: Moscow lies in a tropical jungle, while New York is buried in ice. A gigantic alien spaceship hovers over Moscow and serves as the stadium for Cosmoball, an intergalactic sport combining football with gladiatorial combat. Only athletes with extraordinary powers can play, and they are worshipped like gods by spectators across the galaxy, because the outcome of each match decides the fate of entire worlds, including Earth.

Anton is an ordinary young man who grew up without a father and despises Cosmoball. To help his sick mother, he steals medicine from guarded pharmacies. While hiding from the police in the slums, he meets Anya, a shapeshifter who shares his hatred of the sport and pushes him toward rebellion. Everything changes when Anton is discovered to possess the hidden power of teleportation, which he does not yet know how to control, and he is recruited as goalkeeper of Earth's national team. His teammates include its determined captain, Natasha, the fast and powerful striker Pele, from a now snowy Brazil, and the tiny, elusive Fan. Unaware of the destiny awaiting him, Anton grows into the team's leader, and the final match becomes a battle for the future of the planet.

The leads were cast for their athletic backgrounds. Filming took place at Mosfilm in Moscow from June to September 2017, with motion capture and CGI creating over 50 digital characters. After several delays, it premiered in Moscow on August 25, 2020, becoming the first major Russian release after the COVID-19 lockdown. It earned only about 106.6 million rubles against a budget of roughly 786 million. Russian critics were mostly lukewarm, faulting the weak story and flat dialogue. Nikolai Kornatsky of Film Art found the effects comparable to Valerian and Guardians of the Galaxy but felt a sense of déjà vu, and Anton Dolin wrote that its three stories, a Frankenstein tale, a messiah story and a sports competition, never fit together.

overview: Confined to a claustrophobic hotel room, the heir to a hotel empire and the dominatrix who has primed him for success become locked in a battle of wits and wills as he tries to end his relationship with her.
tagline: Play by her rules.
title: Sanctuary
plot:
Sanctuary is a 2022 American dark comedy psychological thriller film directed by Zachary Wigon from a screenplay by Micah Bloomberg. Margaret Qualley stars as Rebecca Marin, a dominatrix, and Christopher Abbott as Hal Porterfield, her wealthy client, who share an emotionally explosive final session as he prepares to take over his late father's hotel empire. The casting of Qualley and Abbott was announced in September 2021, and principal photography took place in New York City.

Hal orders room service in a luxurious hotel suite as Rebecca arrives, apparently to interview him for the job of chief executive of the hotel chain. Her questions grow increasingly personal and humiliating, and it becomes clear that she is a dominatrix following a script that Hal himself has written. Over dinner afterward, out of character, Hal explains that with his father's death he is about to become CEO of the family company, that their relationship no longer fits his new life, and that this must be their last session; he offers her an expensive watch as a farewell gift. Insulted, Rebecca storms out, only to return and turn the tables, arguing, with the help of his father's management book, that Hal is unfit to lead and demanding a large share of his first year's salary, under threat of releasing recordings of their sessions. What follows is a long night of shifting power in which Hal veers between nonchalance and fury, tearing the suite apart in search of a hidden camera, while Rebecca alternates between mockery, seduction and vulnerability. Each tries to gain control over the other through money, threats and violence, and the line between real emotion and role play blurs as Rebecca insists that she has given up her old life because she only feels fully herself during their sessions. Even their safe word fails to end the game, and with Hal at breaking point, the pair are forced to confront what they truly mean to each other.

Sanctuary premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival on September 11, 2022, and was acquired by Neon, which gave it a limited theatrical release in the United States on May 19, 2023. Critics praised the two lead performances; it holds an 88% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus says it confounds expectations with élan, and a Metacritic score of 67.

overview: The world is full of zombies and the survivors have barricaded themselves inside a walled city to keep out the living dead. As the wealthy hide out in skyscrapers and chaos rules the streets, the rest of the survivors must find a way to stop the evolving zombies from breaking into the city.
tagline: The dead shall inherit the Earth.
title: Land of the Dead
plot:
"Land of the Dead" is a 2005 zombie film directed by George A. Romero, and it's the fourth installment in the "Dead" series. The movie takes place in an alternate universe where a zombie apocalypse has occurred, and society has collapsed.

The main themes of "Land of the Dead" include:

1. Social commentary: The film is a commentary on social class and economic inequality. The wealthy live in a fortified community called Fiddler's Green, while the poor are forced to scrounge for food and shelter in the surrounding wasteland.
2. Class struggle: The movie depicts a clear divide between the haves and have-nots, with the wealthy living in luxury and the poor struggling to survive. This theme is reflected in the character of Big Daddy (Simon Baker), a wealthy survivor who becomes embroiled in a conflict with the zombies.
3. Survival vs. Humanity: As the characters navigate the zombie-infested landscape, they are forced to confront their own humanity and what it means to survive in a world that has lost all sense of morality.
4. Politics and power: The film explores the idea of power and control in a post-apocalyptic world. Big Daddy's character is driven by a desire for revenge against the zombies that have destroyed his life, while the leader of Fiddler's Green (Dennis Hopper) seeks to maintain his grip on power.
5. Redemption and sacrifice: Throughout the movie, characters are forced to confront their own mortality and make difficult choices in order to survive. This theme is reflected in Big Daddy's ultimate sacrifice at the end of the film.

Overall, "Land of the Dead" is a thought-provoking and visually stunning film that explores themes of social commentary, class struggle, survival vs. humanity, politics, and power.

original_title: 劇場版ポケットモンスター 結晶塔の帝王 エンテイ
overview: When Molly Hale's sadness of her father's disappearance gets to her, she unknowingly uses the Unown to create her own dream world along with Entei, who she believes to be her father. When Entei kidnaps Ash's mother, Ash along with Misty & Brock invade the mansion looking for his mom and trying to stop the mysteries of Molly's Dream World and Entei!
tagline: This spring the Unown spells adventure.
title: Pokémon 3: The Movie
plot:
Pokémon 3: The Movie is a 2000 animated film produced by OLM, Inc., and TV Tokyo. The movie takes place after the events of the second Pokémon film, Pokémon: The Power of One.

The story begins with Ash Ketchum, Brock, and Misty on their way to the Indigo League's final tournament in Ecruteak City. However, they soon find themselves lost in the wilderness due to a severe storm. As they try to find shelter, they come across a mysterious island called the "Island of the Hall of Fame," which is said to be the resting place of all Pokémon.

Upon arrival, Ash and his friends discover that the island is actually a testing ground for the Hall of Fame, where Pokémon are judged on their strength and worthiness. The main antagonist, Lawrence III, a wealthy and arrogant collector, has taken over the island and is using it to capture rare and powerful Pokémon.

Lawrence's plan is to use the Hall of Fame to create an army of powerful Pokémon that he can control and exploit for his own gain. Ash and his friends soon realize that they must stop Lawrence and save the island from destruction.

As Ash navigates through the island, he meets a new character, Suicune, a rare and powerful Water-type Pokémon who is also being hunted by Lawrence. Throughout the movie, Ash forms a bond with Suicune, learning about its unique abilities and strengths.

The plot thickens as Ash and his friends face various challenges and obstacles on the island, including fierce battles against Lawrence's minions and treacherous terrain. Along the way, they meet other Pokémon who are also being hunted by Lawrence, including a group of wild Pokémon that have been captured and are being held in captivity.

As the story unfolds, Ash and Suicune work together to stop Lawrence and save the island. In the climactic final battle, Ash faces off against Lawrence's powerful Pokémon, including a massive Tyranitar. With Suicune by his side, Ash is able to defeat Lawrence and shatter the Hall of Fame, freeing all the captured Pokémon.

In the end, Ash and his friends are hailed as heroes for saving the island and stopping Lawrence's evil plans. The movie concludes with Ash reflecting on the lessons he learned from his adventure, including the importance of friendship, teamwork, and understanding the value of different Pokémon.

Overall, Pokémon 3: The Movie is a thrilling adventure that explores themes of friendship, perseverance, and the power of teamwork. With its engaging storyline, memorable characters, and stunning animation, it remains a beloved classic among Pokémon fans worldwide.

overview: The movie covers the events which occurred in between the downfall of The Company and the finale of the TV series (SEASON 4). It details the arrest and incarceration of Sara Tancredi, the final escape plan which Michael devises for Sara, and reveals the ultimate fate of Gretchen Morgan.
tagline: Prepare yourself for the truth
title: Prison Break: The Final Break
plot:
Prison Break: The Final Break is a television film of 2009 in the Prison Break franchise, directed by Brad Turner and Kevin Hooks, which covers the events between the fall of the Company and the revelation of Michael Scofield's death in the fourth season's finale. Wentworth Miller plays Michael and Sarah Wayne Callies Sara Tancredi, with Dominic Purcell as Lincoln Burrows, William Fichtner as Alexander Mahone, Amaury Nolasco as Fernando Sucre, Robert Knepper as T-Bag, Jodi Lyn O'Keefe as Gretchen Morgan and Lori Petty as the inmate Daddy.

The pregnant Sara is arrested for murdering Christina Scofield and held in an overcrowded Miami prison where Gretchen is also an inmate, while T-Bag and General Krantz are locked in the adjacent men's wing. The General places a $100,000 bounty on Sara, who survives a poisoning and learns that her baby will be taken from her after birth. When the warden refuses to protect her, Michael resolves to break her out with Lincoln and Sucre. Gretchen spots them and demands to be included. Mahone, offered his FBI job back if he can incriminate Michael, offers his help, while FBI agent Todd Wheatley searches Michael's flat and finds prison plans. Inside, Sara joins the gang of an inmate called Daddy, and Gretchen protects her, hoping to escape and see her daughter, Emily.

Michael devises a plan to parachute into the prison, paying T-Bag with the bounty money, stolen by Lincoln and Sucre, to set off a fire alarm. Mahone leaks the parachute plan to Wheatley, but on escape night the FBI shoots a dummy while Michael slips in beneath the agent's car. Gretchen stalls the guards and is taken away, leaving Sara a necklace for Emily. When the money transfer falls through, T-Bag betrays them and the alarms are shut off, as Michael had expected. Unable to open an electronic lock, Michael sends Sara on and short-circuits the door, electrocuting himself. Sara escapes to Lincoln, Sucre and Mahone, who reveals he was part of Michael's real plan all along. As Lincoln and Sara sail for the Dominican Republic, they watch a video in which Michael reveals that his brain tumour had returned and asks them to look after each other and the child.

Made available shortly after the series finale, the film aired on Sky1 in the United Kingdom on 27 May 2009 and was released on DVD and Blu-ray in the United States on 21 July. MovieWeb praised Callies' spirited performance.

overview: With the world now aware of his dual life as the armored superhero Iron Man, billionaire inventor Tony Stark faces pressure from the government, the press and the public to share his technology with the military. Unwilling to let go of his invention, Stark, with Pepper Potts and James 'Rhodey' Rhodes at his side, must forge new alliances – and confront powerful enemies.
tagline: It's not the armor that makes the hero, but the man inside.
title: Iron Man 2
plot:
Iron Man 2 is a 2010 superhero film directed by Jon Favreau, produced by Marvel Studios, and based on the Marvel Comics character Tony Stark/Iron Man. The movie takes place after the events of the first Iron Man film.

The story begins with Tony Stark (Robert Downey Jr.) facing pressure from the government to share his Iron Man technology, which he is reluctant to do. Meanwhile, a new villain emerges in the form of Ivan Antonovich Vanko (Mickey Rourke), a Russian physicist who seeks revenge against the Stark family for past wrongs.

As Tony struggles with the moral implications of his actions and the weight of his responsibilities as a superhero, he also faces personal challenges, including a strained relationship with his business partner and friend, Pepper Potts (Gwyneth Paltrow). Additionally, Tony's health begins to decline due to the physical toll of being Iron Man.

The government, led by Secretary of Defense Justin Hammer (Sam Rockwell), tries to take control of the Iron Man technology for their own purposes. Meanwhile, Natasha Romanoff (Scarlett Johansson), a.k.a. Black Widow, is introduced as a new character who becomes entangled in Tony's life.

As Ivan Vanko gains power and notoriety, Tony must confront his past and the consequences of his actions. The film culminates in an epic battle between Iron Man and Whiplash (Mickey Rourke), with Tony ultimately emerging victorious but not without scars.

Throughout the movie, Favreau explores themes of identity, responsibility, and the blurred lines between heroism and villainy. The film also delves into the personal struggles of Tony Stark, who must navigate his relationships and his own demons in order to save the world from Ivan Vanko's destructive plans.

Overall, Iron Man 2 is a thrilling and action-packed sequel that expands on the Marvel Cinematic Universe while introducing new characters and plotlines. The film sets the stage for future Marvel movies, including The Avengers, which brings together some of the most iconic superheroes in the MCU.

original_title: ちいさな英雄－カニとタマゴと透明人間－
overview: Two tiny, aquatic humanoids search for their missing father, a boy battles a lethal allergy to eggs, and an invisible salaryman tries to become a hero.
title: Modest Heroes
plot:
Modest Heroes is a 2018 Japanese animated anthology film produced by Studio Ponoc and Yoshiaki Nishimura, the first volume of the studio's Ponoc Short Films Theatre. It collects three short films written and directed by former Studio Ghibli artists Hiromasa Yonebayashi, Yoshiyuki Momose and Akihiko Yamashita, each centered on an unlikely hero. The Japanese voice cast includes Fumino Kimura, Rio Suzuki, Sōta Shinohara, Machiko Ono, Kentaro Sakaguchi, Joe Odagiri and Min Tanaka.

In Yonebayashi's 18-minute fantasy adventure "Kanini & Kanino", two tiny freshwater crab siblings live with their father, Toto, in a stream while their mother, Kaka, is away giving birth. When their father suddenly disappears, leaving them alone, Kanini and Kanino set out on a perilous journey to find him. The characters speak only an invented language, and the music is by Takatsugu Muramatsu, the director's collaborator on When Marnie Was There and Mary and the Witch's Flower.

Momose's 16-minute drama "Life Ain't Gonna Lose", scored by Masanori Shimada in his first film work, follows Shun Yashima, a young boy born with a life-threatening allergy to eggs. His family's daily life revolves around protecting him: he must eat special meals at school, his classmates must take care not to spread egg-tainted saliva, and even a school trip requires careful planning, while his mother tries to keep up her career as a dance teacher. One day, while his parents are away, Shun accidentally eats something containing egg.

Yamashita's 13-minute action short "Invisible", with music by Yasutaka Nakata, follows a man who is literally overlooked by everyone around him. Ignored throughout his day, he begins to lose his physical hold on the world, until an unexpected encounter with a stranger, a blind old man, gives him a sudden chance to become a hero.

The anthology was originally planned with a fourth segment by Ghibli director Isao Takahata, but it was reduced to three after his death in April 2018. Its ending theme, "Chiisana Eiyū", is sung by Kaela Kimura. The film was released in Japan on 24 August 2018 and in North America by GKIDS on 10 January 2019, with an English cast including Maggie Q and Liam O'Brien, and it later streamed worldwide on Netflix.

overview: Annie Wilson, young widow and mother of three, makes her living foretelling others' futures⁠—though her own has become cloudier than even she can see. Threatened by a client's violent husband and plagued by visions of a missing local woman, Annie finds herself pulled into a thicket of lies and deception in which her extraordinary gift may ultimately get her killed.
tagline: The only witness to the crime was not even there.
title: The Gift
plot:
The Gift is a 2000 American independent Southern Gothic supernatural thriller film directed by Sam Raimi and written by Billy Bob Thornton and Tom Epperson, who wrote the screenplay before Thornton's 1996 breakthrough with Sling Blade; Thornton drew on his own mother's reported psychic experiences. Cate Blanchett stars as Annie Wilson, a widowed mother and clairvoyant in the small Georgia town of Brixton, with Giovanni Ribisi as Buddy Cole, Keanu Reeves as Donnie Barksdale, Katie Holmes as Jessica King and Greg Kinnear as Wayne Collins. It was filmed in the Savannah area of Georgia in early 2000.

Raising three sons alone after her husband's death, Annie earns a living giving psychic readings to her neighbors. Among her regular visitors are Buddy, an emotionally fragile young mechanic, and Valerie Barksdale, who suffers abuse at the hands of her violent husband Donnie; because Annie advised Valerie to leave him, Donnie has repeatedly threatened Annie and her children. When Jessica King, the fiancée of school principal Wayne Collins, disappears, the reluctant sheriff is pressured by her wealthy father into consulting Annie, whose fragmented visions lead police to a pond on Donnie's property, where Jessica's body is found. Donnie admits to an affair with Jessica at his trial and is convicted of her murder. Meanwhile, the tormented Buddy, whose anger toward his father stems from childhood abuse, sets his father on fire in front of Annie and is committed to a mental hospital. Annie's visions continue, however, suggesting that Donnie is innocent and foreshadowing her own death. She pressures prosecutor David Duncan, whose own affair with Jessica she witnessed, to reopen the case, and confides her doubts to Wayne. When the two go to the pond at night, Annie has a vision that exposes the real killer, and her own life is put in grave danger, leading to a startling revelation about the fate of Buddy.

Paramount Classics released The Gift theatrically in the United States on December 22, 2000. It grossed about $12 million at the US box office against a $10 million budget. It holds a 58% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 62, indicating generally favorable reviews.

overview: A dramatised examination of the health issues and social consequences of America's love affair with fast food.
tagline: Do you want lies with that?
title: Fast Food Nation
plot:
Fast Food Nation is a 2006 drama directed by Richard Linklater, who wrote it with Eric Schlosser as a loose adaptation of Schlosser's 2001 non-fiction book. It tells interlocking stories about the fast food industry. Greg Kinnear plays Don Anderson, Ashley Johnson plays Amber, Catalina Sandino Moreno plays Sylvia, Wilmer Valderrama plays Raúl and Bobby Cannavale plays Mike. Bruce Willis, Kris Kristofferson and Ethan Hawke also appear.

Don, marketing director of the Mickey's burger chain, helped create its hit "Big One". When independent tests find fecal matter in the meat, he travels to the fictional town of Cody, Colorado, to inspect Uni-Globe, the chain's main meat supplier. Shown only spotless areas, he seeks out Rudy, a rancher who once supplied the plant, and learns that safety rules are ignored to keep up production, letting manure reach the meat. A Mickey's executive, Rydell, admits knowing but does not care.

Amber, a cheerful Mickey's employee saving for college, lives with her mother Cindy. Her uncle Pete urges her to leave town and pursue a real future. Amber falls in with young activists who plan to free cattle from Uni-Globe, but when they tear down a fence, the animals refuse to leave their pen. Meanwhile, Raúl, his girlfriend Sylvia and her sister Coco cross illegally from Mexico and seek work at the plant. Raúl becomes a cleaner and Coco works on the processing line, while Sylvia, unable to bear the conditions, takes a job as a hotel maid. Coco develops a drug habit and begins an affair with Mike, their exploitative supervisor. When a co-worker's leg is mangled in a machine, Raúl is badly injured trying to save him, and Sylvia is told he was on amphetamines. With Raúl unable to work, Sylvia sleeps with Mike to get a job at the plant. She is assigned to the kill floor, and as cattle are slaughtered around her, she breaks down in tears at what her life has become.

Schlosser preferred a fictional feature to a documentary, and he and Linklater modeled its structure on Winesburg, Ohio. The film was shot in Texas, Colorado and Mexico. It premiered in competition at the 2006 Cannes Film Festival and was released by Fox Searchlight on November 17, 2006, grossing about $2.2 million worldwide. Reviews were mixed. Rotten Tomatoes reported 49% approval, judging the book more effective than the film, while A. O. Scott of The New York Times called it a rich critique of American life, as necessary and nourishing as a meal.

overview: After thirty years of marriage, a middle-aged couple attends an intense, week-long counseling session to work on their relationship.
tagline: Sometimes to keep the magic, you need to learn a few tricks.
title: Hope Springs
plot:
Hope Springs is a 2012 American romantic comedy-drama film directed by David Frankel and starring Meryl Streep, Tommy Lee Jones, and Steve Carell.

The movie follows the story of Kay Gardner (Meryl Streep), a woman who has been married to her husband Arnold (Tommy Lee Jones) for over 40 years. On their 38th wedding anniversary, Kay decides that she wants to rekindle the romance in their marriage by hiring a couples therapist, Dr. Wilbur (Steve Carell). However, things don't go as planned, and the therapy sessions become a catalyst for a series of events that challenge the status quo of their relationship.

The main themes of Hope Springs include:

1. Marriage and relationships: The movie explores the complexities of marriage and relationships, highlighting the challenges and rewards of building and maintaining a long-term partnership.
2. Communication and intimacy: Kay's desire to rekindle romance in her marriage is driven by her need for communication and intimacy with Arnold. However, their inability to express themselves effectively leads to misunderstandings and resentment.
3. Personal growth and change: As the therapy sessions progress, both Kay and Arnold are forced to confront their own flaws and weaknesses, leading to a journey of personal growth and self-discovery.
4. The power of love and forgiveness: Ultimately, the movie suggests that true love and forgiveness can overcome even the most entrenched patterns of behavior, allowing relationships to heal and evolve.

Overall, Hope Springs is a heartwarming and humorous exploration of the complexities of marriage and relationships, with a strong focus on character development and emotional depth.

overview: An eccentric, if not charming Southern professor and his crew pose as a band in order to rob a casino, all under the nose of his unsuspecting landlord – a sharp old woman.
tagline: The greatest criminal minds of all time have finally met their match.
title: The Ladykillers
plot:
The Ladykillers is a 2004 American black comedy crime film written, directed, produced and edited by Joel and Ethan Coen, a remake of the 1955 Ealing comedy written by William Rose. It is the Coens' first remake and their only film with Tom Hanks. Hanks stars as Professor G. H. Dorr, with Irma P. Hall as Marva Munson, Marlon Wayans as Gawain MacSam, J. K. Simmons as Garth Pancake, Tzi Ma as the General and Ryan Hurst as Lump.

Mrs. Munson, a devout, strict elderly widow, rents a room to Dorr, a self-styled classics professor who asks to use her root cellar for rehearsals of his early music ensemble. The musicians are actually criminals. Lump is a dim former football player, Pancake is a demolitions expert with irritable bowel syndrome, MacSam is a foul-mouthed janitor and the gang's inside man at a riverboat casino, and the General is a silent, chain-smoking tunneling expert. They plan to dig from the cellar into the casino's underground vault, dumping the dirt each night onto a garbage barge passing under a nearby bridge. Despite mishaps, including Pancake blowing off a finger that Mrs. Munson's cat carries away, they reach the vault and take the money.

Mrs. Munson discovers the plot and demands that Dorr return the money and come to church, or she will call the police. Dorr's arguments fail. The gang decides she must die and draws straws. MacSam cannot go through with it because she reminds him of his mother, and in the ensuing fight with Pancake he is shot dead. Pancake then tries to escape with the loot and his girlfriend, Mountain Girl, but the General strangles them both. Preparing to kill Mrs. Munson in her sleep, the General is startled by a cuckoo clock, swallows his cigarette, trips over the cat and falls to his death. Lump decides to do as Mrs. Munson says, but he accidentally shoots himself while trying to shoot Dorr. Dorr is knocked off the bridge by a falling piece of gargoyle and dies when his cloak catches on the railing. All of their bodies land on the barge. Mrs. Munson finds the money, and when the police laugh off her story, she gives it to Bob Jones University.

The barge replaces the original's freight train. Buena Vista released it on March 26, 2004, and it grossed $76 million worldwide. Many critics considered it a lesser Coen film. Rotten Tomatoes reported 54% approval, calling Hanks's performance inspired but the film minor. Roger Ebert gave it two and a half stars, singling out Hall as its most successful performer.

overview: Man-eating crocodiles return to the lake as two males and one aggressive female crocodile, which is protecting her nest, wreak havoc on the locals.
title: Lake Placid 2
plot:
Lake Placid 2 is an action-comedy horror film that explores several themes, primarily revolving around the dangers of playing with nature and the consequences of human arrogance. The movie delves into the idea of a seemingly idyllic setting being turned upside down when a monstrous creature emerges from the depths of Lake Placid.

The film also touches on the theme of small-town secrets and the hidden dangers that can lurk beneath the surface of seemingly tranquil communities. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the town's residents are not as innocent as they initially appear, and that there are darker forces at play.

Furthermore, Lake Placid 2 critiques the notion of scientific hubris and the dangers of underestimating the power of nature. The movie's portrayal of a team of scientists who underestimate the creature's intelligence and ferocity serves as a cautionary tale about the risks of playing with forces beyond human control.

Ultimately, the film is a thrilling adventure that combines elements of horror, comedy, and action, all while exploring themes of nature, community, and the dangers of underestimating the power of the unknown.

overview: A dad forms a bitter rivalry with his daughter's young rich boyfriend.
tagline: Of all the guys his daughter could have chosen...
title: Why Him?
plot:
Why Him? is a 2016 American comedy film directed by John Hamburg and written by Hamburg and Dan Sterling. The movie stars James Franco, Bryan Cranston, Megan Mullally, and Zoey Deutch.

The story revolves around Ned Fleming (Bryan Cranston), a software engineer who lives in San Francisco with his wife Barb (Megan Mullally) and their teenage daughter Mary (Zoey Deutch). Ned is a loving but awkward father who wants to give his daughter the best life possible. He's recently been laid off from his job, which has left him feeling anxious about providing for his family.

One day, Ned discovers that Barb has been secretly dating Laird Mayhew (James Franco), a wealthy tech entrepreneur who owns a popular social media platform called "Laird & Taylor." Laird is charming and confident, but also somewhat arrogant and entitled. Despite their differences, the couple seems to be happy together.

However, things take a turn when Ned discovers that Laird has been trying to buy out his daughter's favorite online gaming company, which he believes will help him expand his business empire. Ned is appalled by Laird's motives and feels that he's trying to exploit Mary for his own gain. He decides to confront Laird about his intentions.

As the story unfolds, Ned becomes increasingly obsessed with stopping Laird from buying out the gaming company. He enlists the help of his friend Ron (Adam Pally) and together they hatch a plan to sabotage Laird's deal. Meanwhile, Mary finds herself caught in the middle of her parents' conflict, struggling to navigate her own relationships with both Ned and Laird.

Throughout the movie, Hamburg uses humor to explore themes of class, privilege, and the challenges of modern parenting. The film features a talented cast, with standout performances from Cranston and Franco. While some critics found the movie's tone uneven, many praised its witty dialogue and comedic chemistry between the leads.

Ultimately, Why Him? is a lighthearted comedy that uses satire to poke fun at the excesses of Silicon Valley culture. The film's climax features a series of hilarious misunderstandings and mishaps as Ned and Laird engage in an escalating game of one-upmanship. In the end, Mary finds her own way to navigate her relationships with both parents, and the family is able to come together despite their differences.

Overall, Why Him? is a funny and entertaining movie that explores the complexities of modern family life. With its talented cast and witty dialogue, it's a great choice for fans of comedy and satire.

overview: Right before his daughter's wedding, a mild-mannered foot doctor discovers that his new in-laws are international smugglers.
tagline: He's not losing his daughter. He's gaining a madman.
title: The In-Laws
plot:
The In-Laws is a comedy film that revolves around the complex and often humorous relationship between two families who are brought together through marriage. At its core, the movie explores the theme of identity and how it can be both a source of comfort and a point of contention.

As the story unfolds, we see the main character, Harry Sanborn (played by Albert Brooks), struggling to come to terms with his own sense of self-worth and purpose in life. His marriage to a younger woman has led him to feel like he's lost touch with his own identity, and he finds himself feeling inadequate and insecure.

On the other hand, we have Marisa (played by Patricia Clarkson), Harry's wife, who is portrayed as a confident and independent individual. However, as the story progresses, it becomes clear that she too has her own set of insecurities and fears, particularly when it comes to her relationship with Harry.

The movie also explores the theme of generational differences and how they can lead to misunderstandings and conflicts between people from different age groups. The character of Jack (played by Richard Dreyfuss) serves as a catalyst for these tensions, as he brings his own set of values and expectations to the table, which often clash with those of Harry and Marisa.

Throughout the film, the authorship of the main theme is not clear-cut, but it can be argued that the movie ultimately presents a nuanced exploration of how identity is shaped by our relationships with others. The In-Laws is a witty and engaging comedy that uses humor to explore deeper themes about human connection, vulnerability, and the complexities of family dynamics.

overview: A tight-knit team of FBI investigators, along with their District Attorney supervisor, is suddenly torn apart when they discover that one of their own teenage daughters has been brutally murdered.
tagline: The truth lies in the most unexpected places.
title: Secret in Their Eyes
plot:
Secret in Their Eyes is a 2015 thriller written and directed by Billy Ray, a remake of the 2009 Argentine film of the same name; both are based on Eduardo Sacheri's novel La pregunta de sus ojos. A co-production between the United States, the United Kingdom, South Korea and Spain, it stars Chiwetel Ejiofor, Nicole Kidman and Julia Roberts, with Dean Norris, Michael Kelly, Joe Cole and Alfred Molina in supporting roles.

In 2002, soon after the September 11 attacks, FBI counterterrorism agent Ray Kasten and his friend Jess Cobb, an investigator for the Los Angeles district attorney's office, meet the new assistant district attorney, Claire Sloan. Called to a body dumped near a mosque Ray has been watching, they find that the victim is Jess's eighteen-year-old daughter, Carolyn, raped, murdered and bleached to destroy DNA evidence. Ray, who was late to meet Carolyn that day, blames himself. Studying photos from a police picnic, he spots a young man staring at Carolyn and identifies him as Anzor Marzin, an informant in the terrorism investigation. District Attorney Martin Morales is unwilling to pursue him, and Officer Reggie Siefert frames another suspect to protect Marzin. Ray and Detective Bumpy Willis arrest Marzin at Dodger Stadium, where Claire goads him into confessing and he attacks her, but after Ray beats him, Morales orders him released. Jess rejects Ray's suggestion that they kill Marzin, saying death would be too easy, and Siefert burns Marzin's van to destroy the evidence.

Fourteen years later Ray, now head of security for the New York Mets, returns to Los Angeles, where Claire is now district attorney and a withdrawn Jess is her top investigator. Ray believes Marzin is living as Clay Beckwith, but a shootout in which Siefert dies proves Beckwith is someone else. Jess then tells Ray and Claire that she killed Marzin years earlier. Following her into her barn, Ray finds Marzin alive, caged there for more than a decade. Ray leaves his gun with Jess and begins digging a grave outside; she shoots Marzin, and Claire officially closes the case.

STX moved the release from October to November 20, 2015. The film grossed $32.2 million worldwide against a $19.5 million budget. Critics praised the performances but compared it unfavorably with the original; it holds 39% on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 45.

overview: In a post-apocalyptic wasteland, an orphaned teen must battle a ruthless warlord to save the girl of his dreams.
tagline: This is the future... This is the year 1997.
title: Turbo Kid
plot:
Turbo Kid is a 2015 Canadian science fiction action film directed by François Simard, Anouk Whissell, and Yoann-Karl Whissell.

The movie's main theme revolves around the struggle for identity and self-discovery in a post-apocalyptic world. The protagonist, Turbo (played by Munro Chambers), is a young man who lives on a farm with his abusive father. After being bullied and belittled by his father, Turbo finds solace in an underground fighting tournament where he discovers his unique fighting style.

As the story unfolds, Turbo's journey becomes one of self-discovery and empowerment. He must confront his troubled past and learn to accept himself for who he is, flaws and all. The film explores themes of toxic masculinity, abuse, and the importance of finding one's own path in life.

The movie also touches on the idea of community and found family, as Turbo forms bonds with a group of misfits who become his allies in the fight against their common enemies. Through its blend of action, humor, and heart, Turbo Kid presents a powerful exploration of identity, self-acceptance, and the human need for connection and belonging.

Overall, Turbo Kid is a visually stunning and energetic film that balances action and drama with a strong narrative focus on character development and emotional depth.

overview: Kate is a young woman who has a habit of making bad decisions, and her last date with disaster occurs after she accepts work as Santa's elf for a department store. However, after she meets Tom there, her life takes a new turn.
tagline: Who doesn't have a little Christmas baggage?
title: Last Christmas
plot:
Last Christmas is a romantic comedy film released in 2019, directed by Paul Feig and written by Bryan Cox and Emma Thompson. The movie stars Emilia Clarke as Kate, a young woman who struggles to find purpose after her mother's death.

The story begins with Kate (Emilia Clarke) working at a Christmas shop, where she is surrounded by festive decorations and holiday music. Despite her efforts to be cheerful, Kate feels unfulfilled and disconnected from the world around her. She spends most of her time alone, lost in thought, and struggling to find meaning in her life.

One day, while working at the shop, Kate meets Tom (Henry Golding), a charming and handsome stranger who enters the store looking for a gift for his blind date. As they strike up a conversation, Kate is drawn to Tom's kindness and warmth, and he becomes an instant distraction from her melancholy mood.

As Kate and Tom spend more time together, they begin to form a connection that goes beyond their initial encounter. They bond over their shared love of Christmas music, and Tom introduces Kate to the magic of the holiday season. Through their interactions, we see glimpses of Kate's past, including her complicated relationship with her mother, who died of cancer.

As the story unfolds, we learn more about Kate's struggles to cope with her loss. Her mother was a kind and caring person who always put others before herself, and Kate feels guilty for not being able to live up to her expectations. Tom, sensing Kate's emotional pain, becomes a source of comfort and support for her.

As the holiday season progresses, Kate and Tom grow closer, and their relationship deepens. They share laughter, tears, and moments of vulnerability, and we see them navigate the ups and downs of romance together. Through their interactions, we are reminded that love can be found in unexpected places and that it's never too late to find happiness.

The movie takes a poignant turn when Kate reveals her past to Tom, sharing stories about her mother and the pain she has been carrying for years. Tom listens with empathy and understanding, and his presence helps Kate confront her grief and find closure.

In the end, Kate and Tom share a romantic kiss under the mistletoe, surrounded by the festive decorations of the Christmas shop. The movie ends on a hopeful note, suggesting that love can heal even the deepest wounds and bring joy back into our lives.

Overall, Last Christmas is a heartwarming and uplifting film that explores themes of grief, loss, and the power of love to transform our lives. With its witty dialogue, charming performances, and festive atmosphere, it's a holiday classic that will leave you feeling merry and bright.

overview: After an all-night graduation beach party, a group of hung-over students wakes up under the blazing sun to find their numbers somewhat depleted. An enormous alien creature has burrowed down deep and anyone foolish enough to make contact with the sand finds themselves at the mercy of a sea of flesh-eating tentacles. Will they ever be able to escape its carnivorous clutches?
tagline: This Beach is Killer
title: The Sand
plot:
The Sand, also released as Killer Beach, is a 2015 American horror film directed by Isaac Gabaeff and starring Brooke Butler, Meagan Holder and Mitchel Musso, with Dean Geyer, Cleo Berry and Cynthia Murell among the cast. Some versions of the opening credits use the title Killer Beach, while the closing credits call it The Sand.

A large group of friends holds an all-night beach party, locking their phones in a car trunk so that nobody can post embarrassing pictures online. Two of them find a large ball covered in a sticky substance and bring it back to the party. The next morning Kaylee wakes in the lifeguard hut, her estranged boyfriend Jonah wakes in a convertible beside Chanda, with whom he slept, and others wake on a picnic table or stuck in a trash barrel. Everyone who fell asleep directly on the sand has vanished. When a bird is sucked into the beach, Kaylee realizes the danger, but Marsha steps onto the sand and is trapped, and Vance, falling face first while trying to help, has his skin dissolved before both are dragged under. Kaylee notices nearly invisible tendrils rising toward her hand, and Jonah finds the ball split open and concludes it was an egg whose occupant has burrowed into the beach.

With their phones out of reach, the survivors test the creature's limits. Jonah is slashed while crossing on surfboards, and they notice that it avoids the ashes of the bonfire. A beach patrol officer dismisses their pleas as drug-induced and walks safely in his boots, but he is killed when he reaches for his dropped keys. Mitch dies trying to cross with towels wrapped around his feet, and blood from injuries suffered by Ronnie and Gilbert draws the creature to them. Kaylee confronts Chanda, who admits she slept with Jonah out of jealousy. That night Kaylee, Chanda and Jonah use a raft to reach the patrol car, and Kaylee fights off a huge glowing tentacle by setting it alight with gasoline. Jonah dies of his wounds inside the car. In the morning a man finds the two women, the creature having gone, and they walk off the beach as the monster, revealed to be an enormous jellyfish, swims toward the Santa Monica Pier.

Reviews were mixed, with many critics noting the film's low budget and cheap computer effects. Eye for Film praised its pacing, characterization and rational protagonists, calling it smarter than it looks, while Horror Society rated it eight out of ten and called it a campy good time.

overview: Raised on tales of a Djinn fairy princess, Azur, a young Frenchman goes to North Africa in search of the sprite, only to discover that his close childhood friend, Asmar, an Arab youth whose mother raised both boys also seeks the genie.
title: Azur & Asmar: The Princes' Quest
plot:
Azur & Asmar: The Princes' Quest is a beautifully crafted animated film that weaves together elements of adventure, fantasy, and coming-of-age themes. At its core, the movie explores the complexities of identity, belonging, and self-discovery.

The story follows Azur, a young prince who feels suffocated by his royal duties and longs for freedom and adventure. As he embarks on a perilous journey with his companion Asmar, they encounter various challenges that test their courage, wit, and loyalty to one another. Through their experiences, the film delves into the theme of finding one's place in the world and embracing one's true nature.

The movie also touches upon the idea of identity formation, as Azur struggles to reconcile his royal heritage with his desire for independence and individuality. This internal conflict is mirrored in Asmar's own journey, as he grapples with his own sense of purpose and belonging.

Furthermore, the film explores the importance of friendship and camaraderie, highlighting the transformative power of relationships in shaping our experiences and perspectives. The bond between Azur and Asmar serves as a beacon of hope and support, allowing them to navigate the complexities of their quest together.

Ultimately, Azur & Asmar: The Princes' Quest is a poignant and engaging film that invites viewers to reflect on their own journey of self-discovery and growth. With its richly detailed world-building and memorable characters, the movie offers a captivating exploration of the human experience.

overview: The Spanish deep South, 1980. A series of brutal murders of adolescent girls in a remote and forgotten town bring together two disparate characters - both detectives in the homicide division - to investigate the cases. With deep divisions in their ideology, detectives Juan and Pedro must put aside their differences if they are to successfully hunt down a killer who for years has terrorized a community in the shadow of a general disregard for women rooted in a misogynistic past.
tagline: Life, Death, Redemption.
title: Marshland
plot:
Marshland is a Spanish crime drama film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the consequences of corruption. The movie takes place in 1980, during a severe drought in Spain, and follows two detectives, Juan Marichal and José Luis Salinas, as they investigate a series of gruesome murders in the rural town of Marshland.

At its core, Marshland is a film about the corrupting influence of power and the devastating effects it can have on individuals and communities. The movie exposes the rotting underbelly of small-town Spanish society, where the wealthy elite exploit the poor and vulnerable, and the authorities turn a blind eye to their crimes.

The film also explores themes of masculinity, toxic masculinity, and the objectification of women. The characters are often portrayed as brutish and aggressive, with a deep-seated need for control and dominance. This toxic masculinity is reflected in the way the detectives treat the victims and each other, highlighting the darker aspects of male nature.

Furthermore, Marshland touches on the theme of social inequality and the struggles faced by rural communities. The movie portrays a society where the wealthy few live in luxury, while the poor struggle to survive. The drought serves as a metaphor for the economic and environmental crises that ravage the region, leaving many without access to basic necessities.

Throughout the film, the director weaves together these themes, creating a complex and thought-provoking narrative that challenges the viewer to confront the darker aspects of human nature.

overview: Madrid, June 1991. After celebrating a session of Ouija with her friends, Verónica is besieged by dangerous supernatural presences that threaten to harm her entire family.
tagline: Someone answered your call.
title: Veronica
plot:
Veronica (Spanish: Verónica) is a Spanish supernatural horror film of 2017 directed by Paco Plaza, who wrote it with Fernando Navarro. Loosely inspired by a 1991 case in Madrid's Vallecas district, in which a teenager died mysteriously after a Ouija board séance, it stars Sandra Escacena as Verónica, with Bruna González and Claudia Placer as her twin sisters Lucía and Irene, Iván Chavero as her little brother Antoñito, Ana Torrent as her mother Ana and Consuelo Trujillo as the blind nun known as Sister Death.

The film opens with a panicked emergency call from a young girl on 15 June 1991, then jumps back three days. Fifteen-year-old Verónica lives in working-class Vallecas, and since her father's death she has looked after her younger siblings while her mother works long hours. On the day of a solar eclipse, after a lesson about ancient cultures summoning dark spirits during eclipses, she and her friends Rosa and Diana hold a séance in the school basement, hoping to contact her father and Diana's dead boyfriend. As the eclipse peaks, the glass shatters, Verónica's blood drips onto the board, and she falls into a trance and screams.

Paranormal events follow her home, and her friends shun her. Sister Death tells her that a dark spirit has attached itself to her and that she must protect her siblings, and later reveals that she blinded herself to escape her own visions. Verónica finds body-shaped burn marks on the children's mattresses, and is horrified to discover that the hand choking Lucía was her own. Learning that a séance must be closed by bidding the spirit farewell, and that she whispered during the first one that she would die in three days, she holds a new séance with her siblings, but Antoñito copies the wrong symbols and the spirit refuses to leave. Fleeing with the children, she realises she is only imagining Antoñito beside her, and when she sees the demon in the mirror she understands that she herself has been possessed all along. The police burst in to find her levitating under an invisible attack; she dies, and a shaken detective records that he witnessed unexplained events, said to be the first such police report in Spain.

Released in Spain on 25 August 2017 and later on Netflix, Veronica grossed about $6.1 million worldwide. Critics found it genuinely frightening, giving it 86% on Rotten Tomatoes, and it earned several Goya Award nominations.

original_title: Barbie and the Magic of Pegasus
overview: Princess Annika escapes the clutches of the evil wizard, explores the wonders of Cloud Kingdom, and teams up with a magnificent winged horse - who turns out to be her sister, Princess Brietta - to defeat the wizard and break the spells that imprisoned her family.
title: Barbie and the Magic of Pegasus
plot:
Barbie and the Magic of Pegasus is a 2005 animated fantasy adventure film directed by Greg Richardson, in his feature directorial debut, and produced by Mattel Entertainment with Mainframe Entertainment. The sixth entry in the Barbie film series and the first with an original story not based on earlier material, it stars Kelly Sheridan, who again voices Barbie, here in the role of Princess Annika, with a voice cast that includes Kathleen Barr, Lalainia Lindbjerg, Colin Murdock and Mark Hildreth. Brie Larson recorded the song "Hope Has Wings" for the film.

On her birthday, the adventurous Princess Annika alarms her overprotective parents, King Marcus and Queen Elvina, by slipping out to go ice skating and bringing home a polar bear cub named Shiver, and they forbid her to skate again. Annika sneaks out anyway to a village skating festival, where the powerful sorcerer Wenlock appears and demands that she marry him. When she refuses, he turns the entire village, including her parents, to stone, warning her that the spell will become permanent unless she agrees to marry him within three days. Annika is rescued by Brietta, a winged horse, who flies her to the Cloud Kingdom of Queen Rayla, where Annika learns that Brietta is in fact her sister, transformed into a pegasus by Wenlock years earlier for refusing his own proposal, which explains her parents' protectiveness. The Cloud Queen reveals that only a Wand of Light can defeat Wenlock, and that it must be made from a measure of courage, a ring of love and a gem of ice lit by hope's eternal flame. With Shiver and Brietta, Annika journeys into the Forbidden Forest, where they meet Aidan, a young blacksmith who ran away from home after gambling away his parents' money. Together they escape a giant's stew pot, travel to a cavern filled with ice gems and gather the pieces of the wand, which Annika first uses to restore Brietta to human form. Wenlock, however, pursues the sisters, and Annika must learn that the wand's power cannot be used for vengeance if she is to free her family and her kingdom.

The film premiered on Nickelodeon on September 18, 2005, and was released on VHS and DVD two days later. Its official description presented it as Barbie's first original princess fairy tale, in which the heroine and her new friends travel through forbidden forests, skate through icy caverns and fly above the clouds to save her family.

overview: An exorcist comes up against an evil from his past when he uses his skills to enter the mind of a nine year old boy.
tagline: Faith has failed us.
title: Incarnate
plot:
Incarnate is a 2016 American supernatural horror film directed by Brad Peyton and written by Ronnie Christensen, produced by Blumhouse Productions and WWE Studios. Aaron Eckhart stars as Dr. Seth Ember, a man who frees people from demonic possession by entering their minds, with Carice van Houten as Lindsay Sparrow, David Mazouz as her son Cameron, Catalina Sandino Moreno as Camilla Marquez, a Vatican representative, Keir O'Donnell and Emily Jackson as Ember's assistants Oliver and Riley, and Matt Nable as Cameron's father Dan.

Ember, who uses a wheelchair in the waking world, has an unusual way of dealing with possession: rather than performing exorcisms, he enters the subconscious of the possessed and helps them realize that they are dreaming, since demons cannot truly control their hosts but instead lull them into comforting dreams while using their bodies. His assistant Oliver warns him that the demons are adapting to his methods. When Camilla, sent by the Vatican, asks him to help 11-year-old Cameron, Ember refuses at first, until she suggests that the demon inside the boy may be one he knows. A priest confirms his suspicion that it is Maggie, the entity he has hunted for years, and offers him a vial of a possessed man's blood that would give him a few seconds of lucidity, just enough time to take his own life, an offer Ember declines. Ember and his team induce a near-death state that lets him synchronize with Cameron's brain, giving him only minutes before his heart fails. Inside the boy's dream, Ember finds Cameron with his father, and he insists that Dan, who left the family after breaking his son's arm in a drunken rage, be brought in to help, with tragic results. Pressed by Lindsay, Ember reveals that a possessed driver killed his wife and child in a car crash and left him unable to walk, and that he has been pursuing Maggie ever since. As he plunges again into Cameron's mind for a final confrontation, the line between dream and reality begins to blur, and Ember must decide how far he will go to destroy the demon.

Released in the United States on December 2, 2016, by Blumhouse Tilt and High Top Releasing, Incarnate grossed $2.5 million in its opening weekend, finishing ninth. Critics were largely negative: Rotten Tomatoes gives it 18% from 34 reviews, and Metacritic a score of 30.

overview: An ex-mercenary known for finding missing children is hired by a mixed martial arts fighter whose daughter has been kidnapped.
tagline: The greater the sinner, the greater the saint.
title: 6 Bullets
plot:
6 Bullets (also styled Six Bullets, and developed as The Butcher) is a 2012 action thriller directed by Ernie Barbarash, who had previously directed Jean-Claude Van Damme in Assassination Games, from a screenplay by Chad and Evan Law. Van Damme stars as the mercenary Samson Gaul, with Joe Flanigan as Andrew Fayden, Anna-Louise Plowman as his wife Monica, Charlotte Beaumont as their daughter Becky, Steve Nicolson as Inspector Kvitko and Louis Dempsey as Stelu. Van Damme's real-life son and daughter, Kristopher Van Varenberg and Bianca Bree, play Samson's son Selwyn and Amalia.

Samson specialises in finding and rescuing missing children. At the start of the film he is deep undercover on a mission to free a young boy from slave traffickers; he saves the boy, but two young girls die in the operation, and at the urging of his friend Kvitko, the only honest police officer he knows, he retires and leaves police work to the police, settling into a quiet life as a butcher.

Some time later, the mixed martial arts fighter Andrew Fayden arrives in Moldova for a big match with Monica and their young daughter Becky. Soon after they check into their hotel, Becky disappears, and it quickly becomes clear she has been kidnapped by human traffickers. Lost in a country whose language and customs they do not know, the couple turn to Selwyn, who works at the American embassy, and he sends them to his father. Samson at first refuses and tells them to go to the police, but he soon agrees to help, and he and Becky's parents track her to an abandoned Soviet-era prison. The plot reaches up to Stelu, a senior internal security officer who plans to trade the girl to a wealthy foreign buyer, and Samson, haunted by his past failures, takes on the criminal network that preys on children.

Sony Pictures Home Entertainment released the film on DVD in the United States on 11 September 2012, and StudioCanal released it in Britain that October. Reviewers found it derivative of Taken and longer than necessary at almost two hours, but generally judged it one of Van Damme's better direct-to-video films of the period. DVD Talk called it a serviceable, entertaining action film with well-staged fights, though one dealing largely in clichés, while City on Fire praised Van Damme's committed, brooding performance and the warmth between him and his son, noting that its grim human-trafficking story leaves little room for escapism.

overview: Mathias Gold is a down-on-his-luck New Yorker who inherits a Parisian apartment from his estranged father. But when he arrives in France to sell the vast domicile, he's shocked to discover a live-in tenant who is not prepared to budge. His apartment is a viager—an ancient French real estate system with complex rules pertaining to its resale—and the feisty Englishwoman Mathilde Girard, who has lived in the apartment with her daughter Chloé for many years, can by contract collect monthly payments from Mathias until her death.
tagline: He's in the will. She's in the way.
title: My Old Lady
plot:
My Old Lady is a heartwarming drama that explores the complexities of human relationships and the power of love to transcend time and circumstance.

At its core, the film delves into the theme of identity and how it is shaped by our experiences, memories, and connections with others. The story follows Renée Belson (played by Maggie Gyllenhaal), a widow who has been living in Paris for many years, and her unlikely friendship with Maud (played by Judy Davis), an elderly woman who claims to be Renée's long-lost mother.

As the narrative unfolds, it becomes clear that Maud is not just any ordinary woman; she is a complex and multifaceted individual with a rich inner life and a deep sense of vulnerability. Through their interactions, we see how Maud's presence in Renée's life forces her to confront her own past, her grief, and her sense of identity.

The film also explores the theme of love as a transformative force that can bridge gaps between people from different backgrounds and generations. The relationship between Renée and Maud is built on mutual respect, trust, and affection, which ultimately leads to a deeper understanding of themselves and each other.

Furthermore, My Old Lady touches on the idea of home and belonging, highlighting how these concepts are deeply tied to our emotional experiences and connections with others. As Renée navigates her complicated feelings towards Maud, she is also forced to re-examine what it means to be at home in a place that has been her sanctuary for so long.

Overall, My Old Lady is a poignant exploration of the human experience, one that celebrates the complexities and nuances of relationships, identity, and love.

overview: A young man in a tricky situation follows the advice of his unconventional best friend and uses social media to create a fake boyfriend to keep his awful ex-lover out of his life. But everything backfires when he meets the real love of his life, and breaking up with his fake boyfriend proves hard to do.
tagline: Real love is hard to find.
title: My Fake Boyfriend
plot:
My Fake Boyfriend is a 2022 American romantic comedy film directed by Chris Peckover and written by Chris Peckover and Katie Silberman.

The movie follows the story of Amanda, a successful businesswoman who hires an actor to pretend to be her boyfriend for social media purposes. However, things get complicated when she starts developing real feelings for him.

Some of the main themes in My Fake Boyfriend include:

1. Identity: The film explores the theme of identity and how people present themselves online versus their true selves. Amanda's character is particularly interesting in this regard, as she struggles to reconcile her professional persona with her personal life.
2. Love and relationships: The movie delves into the complexities of love and relationships, highlighting the challenges of navigating modern dating and the pressure to present a perfect image on social media.
3. Self-discovery: Through Amanda's character, the film encourages viewers to reflect on their own values, goals, and aspirations. As she navigates her fake relationship, she is forced to confront her own desires and what she truly wants in life.
4. Authenticity vs. appearance: The movie touches on the tension between authenticity and appearance, particularly in the context of social media. Amanda's character must navigate this dichotomy as she tries to balance her online persona with her real-life feelings.

Overall, My Fake Boyfriend is a lighthearted, entertaining film that explores themes relevant to modern audiences.

overview: Ideologies collide with fatal results when a military drone contractor meets an enigmatic Pakistani businessman.
tagline: Choose your target wisely.
title: Drone
plot:
Drone is a 2017 Canadian thriller directed by Jason Bourque. Sean Bean stars as Neil Wistin, a private contractor who flies drones for the CIA, with Patrick Sabongui as Imir Shaw, a Pakistani businessman, Mary McCormack as Wistin's wife Ellen, Maxwell Haynes as their son Shane and Joel David Moore as Gary.

In March 2016, a drone strike in Pakistan kills its target but also several innocent bystanders. A year later, on the anniversary of the strike, Shaw arrives in the American town where Wistin lives. Wistin is grieving his father and struggling with a eulogy and his distant son. While Wistin clears out his father's room at a care home, Shaw follows Ellen and photographs her meeting another man, revealing an affair. When Wistin returns home, he finds Shaw outside and is told that the visitor wants to buy the boat Wistin has put up for sale, which once belonged to his father. The two go inside to negotiate. At the same time, the CIA traces Shaw as the source of a leak that has exposed the identities of Wistin and other secret contract drone pilots.

Over dinner with the family, Shaw reveals that this is the first anniversary of the deaths of his wife and daughter, killed by a drone operator, and it is implied that Wistin was that operator. Wistin takes a phone call in his office, learns of the leak and checks his records for the date, which confirms his fears about his guest. When he confronts Shaw and moves to call the police, Shaw produces what appears to be a detonator and claims that the briefcase he left on the kitchen table, beside Ellen and Shane, contains explosives equivalent to a drone missile. He demands that Wistin tell his family the truth about his classified work. Wistin complies, and Shaw in turn tells him about Ellen's affair. A CIA tactical team surrounds the house and prepares to kill Shaw, but the two men start fighting, and Wistin stabs Shaw several times. As Shaw dies, Wistin discovers that there was no bomb. Changed by what he has done, Wistin publicly reveals the secret work of the CIA's contract drone operators, and he is hailed by some as a hero and condemned by others as a traitor.

 It premiered at the Vancouver International Film Festival in April 2017 and was released in U.S. theaters and on digital platforms on May 26, 2017. Reviews were generally unfavorable. Rotten Tomatoes reported 27% approval from 11 critics, and Metacritic gave it a score of 49 out of 100.

overview: When an in-flight collision incapacitates the pilots of an airplane bound for Los Angeles, stewardess Nancy Pryor is forced to take over the controls. From the ground, her boyfriend Alan Murdock, a retired test pilot, tries to talk her through piloting and landing the 747 aircraft. Worse yet, the anxious passengers — among which are a noisy nun and a cranky man — are aggravating the already tense atmosphere.
tagline: Something hit us... The crew is dead... Help us, please, please help us!
title: Airport 1975
plot:
Airport 1975 is a 1974 American disaster film directed by Jack Smight, produced by William Frye and written by Don Ingalls, the second installment in the Airport series. Charlton Heston stars as Captain Al Murdock and Karen Black as stewardess Nancy Pryor, with George Kennedy as Joe Patroni, Efrem Zimbalist Jr. as Captain Stacy, Dana Andrews as Scott Freeman, Roy Thinnes as Urias and Ed Nelson as Major John Alexander. Gloria Swanson, in her final film, Linda Blair and Helen Reddy, in her debut, also appear.
