They decide to investigate a rumor about a "Summer Ghost" that appears at night on an abandoned airfield whenever fireworks are lit. The ghost really does appear: a young woman named Ayane. She tells them she can only be seen by people who have already reached out toward death. Flashbacks show why each of them qualifies. Tomoya has lost hope because his controlling mother is forcing him to give up his love of art and concentrate on his studies. Aoi is suicidal after being bullied. Ryō has a terminal illness and less than a year to live.

Tomoya returns alone and learns how Ayane died. She was struck by a car, and the driver hid her body in a suitcase and buried it to avoid punishment. Tomoya becomes obsessed with finding her remains so that her mother can have closure. When Aoi happens to see him searching, she and Ryō join the effort, and together the three eventually succeed. A year later, in the summer, Tomoya and Aoi return to the abandoned airfield. Their friendship has given Tomoya the courage to stand up to his mother and pursue his artistic ambitions, and Aoi has found the confidence to confront her bullies. Ryō, however, has died in the hospital with the two of them at his side, and they have come to the airfield to meet him again, this time as a ghost.

Loundraw announced the project in June 2020 as part of the Project Common multimedia project and unveiled it in February 2021. Akira Kosemura, Itoko Toma, Guiano and Hideya Kojima composed the music. Avex Pictures released the film in Japanese theaters on November 12, 2021, the same day as its international premiere at the Leeds International Film Festival in England. GKIDS screened it in North America in 2022, including a premiere at Anime Expo on July 3, and released it on Blu-ray and digital platforms with Shout! Factory on November 1, 2022. A Japanese limited-edition Blu-ray, released in March 2022, included an 80-minute documentary about the production.

overview: The CIA’s hunt is on for the mastermind of a wave of terrorist attacks. Roger Ferris is the agency’s man on the ground, moving from place to place, scrambling to stay ahead of ever-shifting events. An eye in the sky – a satellite link – watches Ferris.  At the other end of that real-time link is the CIA’s Ed Hoffman, strategizing events from thousands of miles away. And as Ferris nears the target, he discovers trust can be just as dangerous as it is necessary for survival.
tagline: Trust no one. Deceive everyone.
title: Body of Lies
plot:
Body of Lies is a thought-provoking spy thriller that delves into the complexities of human nature, loyalty, and the blurred lines between good and evil. The film's narrative is driven by the cat-and-mouse game between CIA operative Roger Ferris (Leonardo DiCaprio) and MI6 agent Jason Hawkins (Russell Crowe), as they navigate the treacherous world of Middle Eastern politics.

At its core, Body of Lies explores the theme of moral ambiguity, where characters are forced to confront their own values and loyalties in a world where right and wrong are not always clear-cut. Ferris's character, in particular, grapples with the consequences of his actions, as he becomes increasingly entangled in a web of deceit and corruption.

The film also examines the theme of cultural identity and the complexities of understanding different cultures. The protagonist's journey takes him from the United States to Jordan, where he must navigate the intricate politics of the Middle East, confronting his own biases and assumptions along the way.

Furthermore, Body of Lies touches on the theme of loyalty and betrayal, highlighting the ways in which individuals can be torn between their personal loyalties and their professional obligations. The film's climax is a heart-wrenching exploration of the consequences of these choices, leaving the audience to ponder the true cost of loyalty and the nature of sacrifice.

Overall, Body of Lies is a gripping thriller that probes the complexities of human nature, challenging viewers to confront their own assumptions about right and wrong, loyalty, and identity.

original_title: The Perks of Being a Wallflower
overview: Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, 1991. High school freshman Charlie is a wallflower, always watching life from the sidelines, until two senior students, Sam and her stepbrother Patrick, become his mentors, helping him discover the joys of friendship, music and love.
tagline: We are infinite.
title: The Perks of Being a Wallflower
plot:
The Perks of Being a Wallflower is a 2012 American coming-of-age drama written and directed by Stephen Chbosky, based on his 1999 novel. Logan Lerman stars as Charlie, a withdrawn freshman, with Emma Watson as Sam and Ezra Miller as Patrick. Mae Whitman, Nina Dobrev, Kate Walsh and Paul Rudd, as his English teacher, co-star.

In 1991, Charlie, depressed since childhood and recently out of a psychiatric hospital, starts high school with no friends but his English teacher. He meets two seniors, the stepsiblings Patrick and Sam, who invite him to a party after the homecoming dance. There he discovers that Patrick is secretly seeing Brad, the closeted star quarterback. When Charlie reveals that his best friend killed himself the year before, Sam and Patrick take him into their group. Driving home, Sam stands in the back of the pickup in the Fort Pitt Tunnel as an unknown song plays. Charlie tutors Sam for the SAT so she can get into Penn State, and they grow close. Learning he has never been kissed, she gives him his first kiss, despite her crush on Craig. At a New Year's party, Charlie takes LSD and is overwhelmed by memories of his beloved Aunt Helen, who died in a car crash while buying his seventh birthday present.

Dating Mary Elizabeth, Charlie kisses Sam on a dare in front of her, and the group shuts him out. After Brad's father catches him with Patrick, Brad publicly turns on Patrick. When Brad's friends beat Patrick in the cafeteria, Charlie blacks out and fights them off, regaining his friends. The night before she leaves, she and Charlie kiss, but her touch triggers a disturbing flashback. Once she is gone, his mental state collapses, and he calls Candace, blaming himself for Helen's death. Candace sends the police. In the hospital, a psychiatrist helps him recover the repressed memory that Helen sexually abused him. When he is released, Sam and Patrick return, and the three drive through the tunnel to the now-identified song, David Bowie's "Heroes". Charlie stands in the truck bed, feeling alive and infinite.

Chbosky insisted on writing and directing. Filming took place in Pittsburgh in 2011. The film premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival to a standing ovation and was released by Summit Entertainment on September 21, 2012, grossing about $33.4 million worldwide. Critics praised Chbosky's script and direction and the three lead performances. Rotten Tomatoes reported 85% approval, and Roger Ebert gave it three and a half stars.

overview: A look at the relationship between Mike and Sulley during their days at Monsters University — when they weren't necessarily the best of friends.
tagline: School never looked this scary.
title: Monsters University
plot:
Monsters University is a 2013 animated comedy-adventure film produced by Pixar Animation Studios and released by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie takes place about six years before the events of the original Monsters, Inc.

The story follows two young monsters, Mike Wazowski (voiced by Billy Crystal) and James P. Sullivan (Sulley, voiced by John Goodman), who are roommates at Monsters University (MU). Mike is a small, one-eyed green monster with a big personality, while Sulley is a large, furry blue monster with a gentle giant demeanor.

The two monsters meet on their first day of college and quickly become friends. However, they have different aspirations: Mike wants to attend the prestigious Scar School for Scaring, while Sulley dreams of becoming a Scarer at Monsters, Inc., the largest scream-processing factory in Monstropolis.

Despite their differences, Mike and Sulley decide to join the same fraternity, Oozma Kappa (ΩK), which is struggling to find its place on campus. The fraternity's president, Terry Perry (voiced by Peter Sohn), is a laid-back monster who wants to focus on partying rather than scaring.

As Mike and Sulley try to fit in with the ΩK fraternity, they face numerous challenges, including rival fraternities like the Roar Omega Roar (ROR) and the Scare Games. The ROR fraternity, led by Don Carlton (voiced by Steve Buscemi), is determined to win the Scare Games and prove their superiority.

Throughout the movie, Mike and Sulley learn valuable lessons about teamwork, friendship, and believing in themselves. They also discover that they have a unique bond that allows them to scare together more effectively than any other monster duo.

The climax of the movie takes place during the Scare Games, where Mike and Sulley face off against their rivals from ROR. In a thrilling finale, the two friends use their combined skills to outscare their opponents and win the Scare Games.

In the end, Mike and Sulley become an unstoppable team, and their friendship is cemented as they graduate from Monsters University with honors. The movie concludes with a heartwarming moment of Mike and Sulley's graduation ceremony, where they are celebrated as heroes by their fellow monsters.

Overall, Monsters University is a fun and entertaining film that explores the early days of two beloved characters. The movie's themes of friendship, teamwork, and believing in oneself make it a great addition to the Monsters, Inc. franchise.

overview: A psychiatrist, whose client commits suicide, finds his family life disrupted after introducing her surviving brother to his wife and daughter.
tagline: Such things still happen
title: Every Breath You Take
plot:
Every Breath You Take, also known as You Belong to Me, is a 2021 psychological thriller directed by Vaughn Stein from a screenplay by David Murray. Casey Affleck plays psychiatrist Philip Clark, Michelle Monaghan his wife, Grace, and Sam Claflin the stranger who enters their lives, with Veronica Ferres, India Eisley and Emily Alyn Lind in supporting roles.

Philip, Grace and their daughter, Lucy, have drifted apart since the death of the younger child, Evan, in a car accident three years earlier. One of Philip's patients, Daphne Flagg, has escaped an abusive relationship with the help of his therapy and is writing a book about her mental illness. After telling Philip that her best friend, Joan, was killed in a hit-and-run, Daphne is found dead outside her home in an apparent suicide. Philip comforts her distraught, estranged British brother, James, who soon visits the Clark home and is invited to dinner by a sympathetic Grace. Philip orders a copy of a book James has written, Shadow Cast.

James grows close to Grace, who confesses that Philip has never faced his grief, and despite trying to end things she sleeps with him. He files a complaint that gets Philip suspended pending investigation, and he also seduces the troubled Lucy. Later he picks up Grace when her car breaks down, drives erratically and knocks her unconscious, but Philip catches up and rescues her. Told that James has committed himself to a psychiatric facility with auditory hallucinations, Philip visits him and learns that he has read Daphne's notes on her therapy and on Philip's family. When Shadow Cast finally arrives, the author photo reveals that the real James Flagg is someone else: the impostor is Eric Dalton, Daphne's abusive American ex-boyfriend, who killed Joan to break Daphne down and then murdered her when she refused to return, and has targeted Philip for helping her leave. Eric escapes the facility after killing a guard and attacks Lucy at home, and after a violent struggle Grace kills him with the blade of Evan's old ice skate.

The project was announced in 2012 with Rob Reiner attached to direct; Stein replaced Christine Jeffs in December 2019, and filming took place in Vancouver. Vertical Entertainment released it in theaters and on demand on April 2, 2021. Critics were largely negative, with 20% on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 32.

overview: Bella once again finds herself surrounded by danger as Seattle is ravaged by a string of mysterious killings and a malicious vampire continues her quest for revenge. In the midst of it all, she is forced to choose between her love for Edward and her friendship with Jacob, knowing that her decision has the potential to ignite the ageless struggle between vampire and werewolf. With her graduation quickly approaching, Bella is confronted with the most important decision of her life.
tagline: It all begins... with a choice.
title: The Twilight Saga: Eclipse
plot:
The Twilight Saga: Eclipse is a 2010 American supernatural romance film directed by David Slade, based on the fourth novel by Stephenie Meyer. The movie stars Kristen Stewart, Robert Pattinson, and Taylor Lautner.

The story takes place after the events of New Moon (2009). Bella Swan (Kristen Stewart) is still in love with Edward Cullen (Robert Pattinson), but their relationship is threatened when Victoria (Rachelle Lefevre), James' partner from the first film, seeks revenge against Bella and the Cullens. Victoria has created an army of "newborn" vampires to attack Bella.

Meanwhile, a group of "tracker" vampires, led by Riley Biers (Xavier Samuel), is also on the hunt for Bella. The Cullens form an alliance with the werewolf pack, led by Jacob Black (Taylor Lautner), to protect Bella from both the newborns and the tracker vampires.

As the threat escalates, Bella finds herself caught in the middle of a love triangle between Edward and Jacob. She begins to develop feelings for Jacob, which puts her at odds with Edward's possessiveness and jealousy.

The movie culminates in an epic battle between the Cullens, werewolves, and newborns at an amusement park. The Cullens use their unique abilities to fight off the newborns, while Bella and Jacob work together to take down Riley Biers, who is revealed to be a human possessed by Victoria.

Throughout the film, the characters grapple with their own identities and loyalties. Edward struggles with his desire to protect Bella at all costs, while Jacob tries to balance his friendship with Bella with his growing feelings for her.

The Twilight Saga: Eclipse received mixed reviews from critics but was a commercial success, grossing over $698 million worldwide. The movie's climax features an intense action sequence and a dramatic confrontation between the characters, setting the stage for the final installment of the series, Breaking Dawn – Part 1 (2011).

overview: A searing look at a day in the life of an assistant to a powerful executive. As Jane follows her daily routine, she grows increasingly aware of the insidious abuse that threatens every aspect of her position.
title: The Assistant
plot:
The Assistant (2020) is a thought-provoking drama that delves into the darker aspects of power dynamics and the consequences of unchecked ambition. The film follows Jane, a young and ambitious assistant who becomes embroiled in a toxic work environment at a prestigious law firm.

At its core, The Assistant explores the theme of gaslighting and emotional manipulation, as embodied by the firm's ruthless and cunning leader, Martha. This character serves as a symbol of the ways in which women can be silenced, belittled, and exploited in the workplace. As Jane navigates this treacherous landscape, she must confront the ways in which her own self-worth has been eroded by her boss's constant belittling and manipulation.

The film also touches on the theme of identity and how it is shaped by our relationships with others. Jane's struggle to assert herself and find her place in the world serves as a powerful metaphor for the ways in which we often seek validation from those around us. As she grapples with her own desires and ambitions, Jane must confront the tension between her need for recognition and her desire to maintain a sense of self-worth.

Furthermore, The Assistant critiques the patriarchal norms that perpetuate inequality and sexism in the workplace. The film's portrayal of a male-dominated industry where women are often relegated to secondary roles serves as a scathing commentary on the ways in which systemic power structures can perpetuate oppression.

Ultimately, The Assistant is a powerful exploration of the human cost of ambition and the importance of self-care and emotional intelligence. Through Jane's journey, the film offers a nuanced and thought-provoking examination of the ways in which we navigate complex relationships and confront our own vulnerabilities.

overview: Despite his family’s baffling generations-old ban on music, Miguel dreams of becoming an accomplished musician like his idol, Ernesto de la Cruz. Desperate to prove his talent, Miguel finds himself in the stunning and colorful Land of the Dead following a mysterious chain of events. Along the way, he meets charming trickster Hector, and together, they set off on an extraordinary journey to unlock the real story behind Miguel's family history.
tagline: The celebration of a lifetime
title: Coco
plot:
Coco is a beautifully crafted animated film that pays homage to Mexican culture, traditions, and history. The movie follows the story of Miguel Rivera, a young boy who dreams of becoming a musician like his idol, Ernesto de la Cruz.

Miguel lives with his family in a small town in Mexico, where music is an integral part of their daily lives. However, Miguel's family has a long-standing ban on music due to a past tragedy that led to the death of his great-great-grandfather, Papá. According to legend, Papá was a famous musician who abandoned his family and left them with nothing.

On the Day of the Dead (Día de los Muertos), Miguel decides to sneak out of the house to fulfill his dream of becoming a musician. He steals his family's most prized possession, a magical guitar that supposedly belonged to Ernesto de la Cruz, and sets off on an adventure to find him.

As Miguel travels through the Land of the Dead, he meets various characters who are trapped between worlds, including his deceased relatives and a charming trickster named Héctor. Together, they embark on a journey to uncover the truth about Papá's past and the reason behind the family's ban on music.

Throughout their adventure, Miguel learns valuable lessons about the importance of family, tradition, and following one's dreams. He also discovers that his great-great-grandfather was not the musician he thought he was, but rather a complex individual who made sacrifices for his family.

As the story unfolds, Miguel must confront his own identity and the expectations placed upon him by his family. In the end, he finds a way to honor his ancestors while still pursuing his passion for music.

Coco is a heartwarming film that celebrates Mexican culture and traditions, while also exploring universal themes of identity, family, and the power of music. The animation is stunning, with vibrant colors and intricate details that bring the Land of the Dead to life. The characters are well-developed and relatable, making it easy for audiences of all ages to become invested in their stories.

Overall, Coco is a beautifully crafted film that will leave you smiling, laughing, and maybe even shedding a tear or two. It's a must-see for anyone who loves animation, music, or just great storytelling in general.

overview: In an attempt to win back her ex-boyfriend on Christmas Eve, Kate ends up ruining her blind date with Miles, a handsome guy she's been set up with. In a strange twist of fate, Kate is given the chance to re-live Christmas Eve twelve times.
tagline: Twelve chances to get it right.
title: 12 Dates of Christmas
plot:
Cabin Fever: Patient Zero is a 2014 horror film that explores several themes, primarily centered around the concept of isolation and its effects on human behavior.

The movie takes place in an isolated research facility where a mysterious virus is being studied. As the characters begin to fall ill, they are forced to confront their own dark pasts and the true nature of their relationships with each other. The film's setting, which initially appears to be a secure and controlled environment, slowly descends into chaos as the characters' primal instincts take over.

One of the main themes of Cabin Fever: Patient Zero is the breakdown of social norms and the emergence of primal behavior in the face of extreme stress and isolation. As the characters succumb to the virus, they begin to exhibit increasingly savage and violent tendencies, revealing a darker side to their personalities.

The film also explores the theme of guilt and redemption, as the characters are forced to confront their past mistakes and the consequences of their actions. The movie's use of a mysterious virus serves as a metaphor for the destructive power of unchecked emotions and the devastating effects of unresolved trauma.

Furthermore, Cabin Fever: Patient Zero touches on the idea of the "other," highlighting the fear and mistrust that can arise when individuals are forced to confront those who are different from themselves. The film's portrayal of the virus as a catalyst for this breakdown serves as a commentary on the dangers of xenophobia and the importance of empathy and understanding in breaking down social barriers.

Overall, Cabin Fever: Patient Zero is a tense and unsettling horror film that explores the darker aspects of human nature, revealing the primal fears and desires that lie beneath the surface of even the most seemingly civilized individuals.

overview: Set in a gritty and decadent 1970s America, American Boogeyman follows the elusive and charming killer and the manhunt that brought him to justice involving the detective and the FBI rookie who coined the phrase ‘serial killer’.
tagline: America's most notorious serial killer.
title: Ted Bundy: American Boogeyman
plot:
Ted Bundy: American Boogeyman is a psychological thriller that delves into the dark and twisted mind of one of America's most infamous serial killers, Ted Bundy. The film masterfully weaves together themes of trauma, manipulation, and the blurring of reality.

At its core, the movie explores the concept of identity and how it can be distorted by traumatic experiences. Bundy's character is a complex web of contradictions, with a charming exterior hiding a sinister and violent interior. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Bundy's actions were not just driven by a desire for power or control, but also by a deep-seated need to cope with his own emotional pain.

The film also examines the theme of gaslighting, where Bundy expertly manipulates those around him, including his victims and even some of his acquaintances. This manipulation is a key aspect of his modus operandi, allowing him to present himself as a normal, even likable person, while concealing his true nature.

Furthermore, Ted Bundy: American Boogeyman touches on the idea of how trauma can be passed down through generations, with Bundy's actions serving as a manifestation of his own traumatic experiences. This theme is expertly woven throughout the narrative, adding depth and complexity to the story.

Overall, the movie presents a thought-provoking exploration of the human psyche, delving into the darker aspects of human nature and the devastating consequences of trauma and manipulation.

overview: The former World Heavyweight Champion Rocky Balboa serves as a trainer and mentor to Adonis Johnson, the son of his late friend and former rival Apollo Creed.
tagline: Your legacy is more than a name
title: Creed
plot:
Creed is an American sports drama of 2015 directed by Ryan Coogler, who wrote it with Aaron Covington. The seventh film in the Rocky franchise and a spin-off sequel to Rocky Balboa (2006), it stars Michael B. Jordan as Adonis Creed, son of the late champion Apollo Creed, and Sylvester Stallone as Rocky Balboa, with Tessa Thompson as Bianca, Phylicia Rashad as Apollo's widow Mary Anne, the real boxer Tony Bellew as "Pretty" Ricky Conlan and Graham McTavish as Conlan's trainer.

In 1998, Adonis Johnson, Apollo's son from an extramarital affair, is in a Los Angeles youth detention centre when Mary Anne offers to take him in. Years later, despite a comfortable finance job, he fights in amateur bouts in Tijuana, and he quits to box professionally. Rejected by a Los Angeles gym run by the son of his father's trainer, and against Mary Anne's fears, since Apollo died in the ring, he moves to Philadelphia and asks Rocky, his father's rival and friend, to train him. Rocky reluctantly agrees, revealing that Apollo won their secret third fight. At the Front Street Gym Adonis trains with Rocky's old friends and falls for Bianca, a singer facing progressive hearing loss.

Fighting as Adonis "Hollywood" Johnson, he beats a local boxer, but the news that he is Apollo's son leaks. The camp of light-heavyweight champion Ricky Conlan, who faces prison and wants a final bout, offers Adonis a title shot on condition he fight under the Creed name, and with Bianca's encouragement he accepts. Rocky collapses and is diagnosed with non-Hodgkin lymphoma; having lost Adrian, Paulie and his friends, he refuses chemotherapy. After a quarrel, a jail stint and a reconciliation, Adonis makes Rocky's treatment a condition of fighting. At Goodison Park in Conlan's home city of Liverpool, wearing American flag trunks sent by Mary Anne, Adonis knocks the champion down for the first time in his career and goes the distance, losing a split decision but winning the crowd's respect. The film ends with Adonis helping the weakened Rocky climb the steps of the Philadelphia Museum of Art.

Released by Warner Bros. on 25 November 2015, Creed grossed $173.6 million worldwide on a $35 million budget and drew rave reviews, with 95% on Rotten Tomatoes. Stallone won the Golden Globe for Best Supporting Actor and an Oscar nomination, and two sequels followed.

overview: Batman discovers a mysterious teen-aged girl with superhuman powers and a connection to Superman. When the girl comes to the attention of Darkseid, the evil overlord of Apokolips, events take a decidedly dangerous turn.
tagline: The end is near.
title: Superman/Batman: Apocalypse
plot:
Superman/Batman: Apocalypse is a 2010 American animated superhero film directed by Lauren Montgomery, based on the Superman/Batman comic book storyline "The Supergirl from Krypton", with an art style partly inspired by that of Michael Turner, who drew the comic. The ninth entry in the DC Universe Animated Original Movies line, it is a standalone sequel to Superman/Batman: Public Enemies (2009). Tim Daly voices Superman, Kevin Conroy Batman, Summer Glau Kara Zor-El, Andre Braugher Darkseid, Susan Eisenberg Wonder Woman, Julianne Grossman Big Barda and Ed Asner Granny Goodness. Despite the title, the film focuses mainly on Supergirl and Superman, with Batman in a supporting role.

Weeks after the downfall of President Lex Luthor, a spaceship crashes into Gotham City Harbor, and a young girl emerges who wreaks havoc with her powers until Superman and Batman subdue her. She turns out to be Kara Zor-El, Superman's cousin, who has spent decades in suspended animation. While Superman welcomes her, teaches her English and helps her adapt to life on Earth, Batman remains suspicious, and with Wonder Woman and her ally Lyla he arranges for Kara to train on the island of Themyscira. On the dark planet Apokolips, the tyrant Darkseid learns of Kara's existence and orders Granny Goodness to bring her to him as a potential leader of his elite Female Furies. Two months later, an army of Doomsday clones attacks Themyscira as a diversion; Lyla is killed and Kara is abducted and brainwashed into becoming captain of the Furies. With the reluctant help of the warrior Big Barda, Superman, Batman and Wonder Woman travel to Apokolips. While Wonder Woman and Barda battle Granny and the Furies in the arena, Superman confronts Darkseid and is forced to fight his own cousin, and Batman threatens to destroy the entire planet unless Darkseid frees Kara and promises to leave her alone. Yet once the heroes return to Earth, Darkseid finds a loophole in his promise, setting the stage for a final battle.

The film was released by Warner Premiere and Warner Bros. Animation on September 28, 2010, with a special edition including an animated short featuring Green Arrow. Reviews were mixed, with IGN rating it 8 out of 10 and others criticizing Braugher's Darkseid. It earned about $8.25 million from domestic DVD and Blu-ray sales.

overview: In a magical faraway land, in a picturesque little village nestled among green meadows and rolling hills, lives a flock of carefree sheep. But their pastoral and stress-free life is interrupted when a pack of wolves sets up camp in the nearby ravine.
tagline: You can be whatever you want. The main thing is you remain yourself!
title: Sheep & Wolves
plot:
Sheep and Wolves (Russian: Volki i ovtsy. Be-e-e-zumnoe prevrashchenie) is a 2016 Russian 3D animated fantasy comedy directed by Andrey Galat and Maxim Volkov, their directorial debut, and produced by Wizart Animation with CTB Film Company. The studio's first original story, conceived by Volkov, draws on the fairy tale The Wolf and the Seven Young Goats and the idea of a wolf in sheep's clothing. Alexander Petrov voices the hero, Grey, and Elizaveta Boyarskaya his love interest, Bianca, in the Russian version, while Tom Felton and Ruby Rose take those roles in the English dub.

A pack of wolves settles in a ravine near a village of sheep. Its wise old leader, Magra, announces his retirement, and two candidates must fight to succeed him: the cruel, selfish Ragear and the carefree joker Grey, who is in love with Bianca. When Grey's immaturity leads Bianca to leave him, he visits a gypsy camp, where an eccentric hare named Mami gives him a potion he hopes will win her back. Instead it turns him into a ram. Knocked out while fleeing his former pack, he wakes in the sheep village in the care of Lyra, older sister of the lamb Shia, whom Grey had once spared. Grey struggles with his new form, offends the flock by biting during a tournament, but wins their friendship after protecting Lyra and Shia from two wolves.

Ragear murders Magra and seizes the pack, then learns of Grey's transformation and resolves to destroy the village. After a photograph seems to show Grey as a spy, he leaves the sheep, but Mami tells him of the coming attack and that he can become a wolf again by reaching a certain tree by noon. Grey instead returns to warn the flock and leads its defense, and the wolves are trapped in a flooding cave, from which Grey rescues them. Shia exposes Ragear as Magra's killer, and Grey challenges him. A potion brought by Mami and Bianca seems to fail, but after being buried under rocks Grey emerges as a wolf and sends Ragear over a waterfall to his death. Grey marries Bianca, wolves and sheep live together in peace, and Mami reveals that the potion was only spring water and that his change came from learning responsibility.

The film had a budget of about $3.4 million. It opened at number two in Russia on 1,892 screens and earned over 143 million rubles during a 19-week run. Russian reviews were warm, but critics elsewhere were largely negative, attacking its writing, pacing, characterization and lore while giving some praise to the animation.

overview: Called to Rome to stop an imminent terrorist bombing, a soldier desperately seeks news of his imprisoned brother — a rebel with knowledge that could thwart the attack. Navigating the capital's darkened streets, he races to a series of ominous encounters to keep the Vatican from being blown to bits.
tagline: It's always deadliest before the dawn.
title: Zeros and Ones
plot:
Zeros and Ones is a 2021 thriller written and directed by Abel Ferrara and shot in Rome, the director's adopted home, during the COVID-19 lockdown. Ethan Hawke stars in a dual role as JJ, an American soldier, and his twin brother, with Cristina Chiriac, Phil Neilson, Valerio Mastandrea, Dounia Sichov, Babak Karimi, Stephen Gurewitz and Ferrara's daughter Anna in supporting parts. Developed from an older Ferrara script idea about the post-9/11 war on terror, it was produced by Maze Pictures, Rimsky Productions and Almost Never Films, with cinematography by Sean Price Williams; cast and crew worked in masks and social bubbles, and masks, hand sanitizer and video calls appear on screen.

The film opens and closes with Hawke speaking directly to the audience as himself about the picture. In the story, a gaunt, bearded JJ arrives in a deserted, locked-down Rome on a murky undercover mission, called there to stop an imminent terrorist bombing. He is desperate for news of his twin brother, a messianic revolutionary who is being held captive and tortured and whose fate shifts with each unreliable witness; the brother, glimpsed in brief scenes, rants about fascism and asks why no one sets themselves on fire anymore. Moving through the city at night with armed soldiers and foreign agents on his trail, JJ exchanges terse instructions with strangers in black cars, holds cryptic conversations in a mosque, shares a fraught intimacy with a young mother and her child and buys drugs in a seedy club.

His shadowy errands finally come together when he is caught up in a massive bombing of the Vatican, apparently a staged false-flag operation designed to inflame an ancient conflict between rival civilizations, while the film's dialogue repeatedly casts Jesus as a radical soldier and war casualty. It ends on a hopeful note, with footage of Anna Ferrara running through Rome at sunrise as life returns to the city.

Zeros and Ones premiered in competition at the 74th Locarno Film Festival on August 12, 2021, where Ferrara won the Pardo for Best Direction, and Lionsgate released it in select US theaters and on digital platforms on November 19, 2021. Reviews were mixed, with a 54 percent Rotten Tomatoes rating. The Hollywood Reporter found it a minor, cryptic work rescued in part by Hawke's committed performance and its eerie, lo-fi images, while RogerEbert.com described it as on-the-nose but driven by Ferrara's blunt elemental force, likening it to a kind of action painting.

overview: The true story of Captain Richard Phillips and the 2009 hijacking by Somali pirates of the US-flagged MV Maersk Alabama, the first American cargo ship to be hijacked in two hundred years.
tagline: Out here survival is everything.
title: Captain Phillips
plot:
Captain Phillips is a 2013 American biographical thriller film directed by Paul Greengrass, based on the 2009 book "Captain Richard Phillips and the True Story of Maersk Alabama" by Richard Phillips. The film stars Tom Hanks as Captain Richard Phillips, a merchant mariner who becomes the target of Somali pirates.

The film begins with an introduction to Captain Phillips (Tom Hanks), a seasoned sailor who has spent his entire life at sea. He is married to Andrea (Catherine Keener) and has two children. The story then shifts to April 2009, when Phillips' ship, the MV Maersk Alabama, sets sail from the port of Aden in Yemen.

As the ship navigates through the Indian Ocean, it becomes a target for Somali pirates. On April 8, 2009, the ship is hijacked by three pirates, led by Abduwali Abdukhadir Muse (Barkhad Abdi). The pirates take Phillips and four crew members hostage, demanding a ransom in exchange for their safe release.

The film then follows the events that unfold as Phillips tries to negotiate with the pirates. He attempts to reason with them, but they are unwilling to listen. As tensions rise, Phillips realizes that he must find a way to escape or be killed by the pirates.

Meanwhile, the US Navy is alerted to the hijacking and begins to track the ship's location. The Navy sends a team of SEALs, led by Lieutenant Michael Murphy (Taylor Kitsch), to rescue the hostages. However, the operation is complicated by the fact that the pirates are hiding in a remote area with limited communication.

As the standoff between Phillips and the pirates continues, it becomes clear that Muse has no intention of releasing his captives alive. In a tense and dramatic confrontation, Phillips manages to outsmart the pirates and escape from the ship. However, he is left stranded in a lifeboat, adrift in the ocean with limited supplies.

The film's climax features an intense and suspenseful rescue operation, as the SEALs finally reach the location of the Maersk Alabama. In a daring move, Murphy sacrifices himself to distract the pirates and allow the other SEALs to board the ship and rescue Phillips.

In the aftermath of the rescue, Phillips is hailed as a hero for his bravery and cunning in outsmarting the pirates. The film ends with Phillips reflecting on the experience, realizing that he has been forever changed by the ordeal.

Overall, Captain Phillips is a gripping and intense thriller that showcases Tom Hanks' remarkable acting abilities. The film's tense and suspenseful plot, combined with its well-developed characters and themes of bravery and sacrifice, make it a compelling watch.

overview: A mother desperate to reconnect with her troubled daughter becomes embroiled in the urban legend of a demonic witch.
tagline: Pray she doesn't answer.
title: Don't Knock Twice
plot:
Don't Knock Twice is a 2017 supernatural horror film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the consequences of meddling with forces beyond one's control. The movie revolves around a young mother, Katie, who embarks on a perilous journey to rescue her son from an evil presence that has taken him.

At its core, Don't Knock Twice explores the theme of desperation and the lengths people will go to for their loved ones. Katie's actions are driven by her unrelenting desire to save her child, which ultimately leads her down a path of self-destruction. The film also touches on the idea of grief and loss, as Katie grapples with the trauma of losing her son and the guilt that comes with it.

The movie also delves into the concept of temptation and the dangers of succumbing to one's darker impulses. As Katie navigates the treacherous world she has entered, she is forced to confront the evil presence head-on, which serves as a metaphor for the internal struggles we all face when faced with difficult choices.

Furthermore, Don't Knock Twice can be seen as an exploration of the blurred lines between good and evil, highlighting how even the most well-intentioned actions can have devastating consequences. The film's use of atmospheric tension and eerie visuals adds to the sense of unease, making it a deeply unsettling viewing experience that lingers long after the credits roll.

Overall, Don't Knock Twice is a thought-provoking horror film that delves into the complexities of human nature, exploring themes of desperation, grief, temptation, and the consequences of playing with forces beyond one's control.

keywords.name: based on myths, legends or folklore

overview: An epic fantasy adventure based on the timeless Arthurian legend, The Green Knight tells the story of Sir Gawain, King Arthur's reckless and headstrong nephew, who embarks on a daring quest to confront the eponymous Green Knight, a gigantic emerald-skinned stranger and tester of men.
tagline: When honor was everything.
title: The Green Knight
plot:
The Green Knight is a 2021 medieval fantasy film directed by David Lowery, based on the 14th-century poem "Sir Gawain and the Green Knight" by Pearl. The movie stars Dev Patel as Sir Gawain, a young knight from King Arthur's court, and Ralph Ineson as the enigmatic Green Knight.

The story begins with King Arthur (played by Sean Harris) hosting a tournament to celebrate his birthday. During the festivities, a mysterious figure appears, known only as the Green Knight (Ineson). The Green Knight challenges any knight who can strike him with an axe, but with one condition: that the knight must return to the Green Knight in a year and receive a second blow in exchange for the first.

Sir Gawain, eager to prove himself, accepts the challenge. He strikes the Green Knight with his axe, beheading him. However, instead of dying, the Green Knight picks up his head and rides away on a horse, leaving Gawain to pick up the pieces of his own life.

The story then shifts to a year later, where Gawain sets out on a journey to find the Green Knight and fulfill his end of the bargain. Along the way, he encounters various characters who test his courage, loyalty, and wits. These include a mysterious woman named Lady Bertilak (played by Saoirse Ronan), her husband Sir Bertilak (played by Barry Keoghan), and a group of traveling performers.

As Gawain journeys deeper into the forest, he begins to realize that the Green Knight's challenge was not just about physical bravery but also about moral integrity. He is forced to confront his own flaws and weaknesses, including his pride and arrogance.

Upon arriving at Lady Bertilak's castle, Gawain is treated with hospitality and kindness, but he soon discovers that she is actually the Green Knight in disguise. The two engage in a series of games and challenges, which serve as a metaphor for Gawain's inner struggle.

In the end, Gawain is forced to choose between his loyalty to King Arthur and his own sense of honor. He ultimately decides to leave the castle and return home, but not before receiving a final blow from the Green Knight, which serves as a symbol of his own mortality.

The movie ends with Gawain returning to King Arthur's court, where he is met with both praise and criticism for his actions. The film concludes on a somber note, suggesting that Gawain has learned a valuable lesson about the importance of humility and self-awareness.

Throughout the film, Lowery explores themes of chivalry, honor, and the human condition. The Green Knight is a complex and nuanced character who serves as a symbol of both good and evil. The movie's use of symbolism, imagery, and metaphor adds depth and complexity to the story, making it a thought-provoking and visually stunning film.

Overall, The Green Knight is a haunting and introspective film that challenges its audience to confront their own flaws and weaknesses. With its stunning visuals, complex characters, and thought-provoking themes, it is a must-see for fans of medieval fantasy and adventure films.

overview: Prot is a patient at a mental hospital who claims to be from a far away planet. His psychiatrist tries to help him, only to begin to doubt his own explanations.
production_companies: IMF Internationale Medien und Film GmbH & Co. 3. Produktions KG
tagline: Change the way you look at the world.
title: K-PAX
plot:
K-PAX is a thought-provoking science fiction drama film that delves into the complexities of human identity, reality, and the blurred lines between sanity and madness.

At its core, the movie explores the theme of self-discovery and the search for meaning in a seemingly chaotic world. The protagonist, Prot (played by Kevin Spacey), is a mysterious figure who claims to be an alien from the planet K-PAX, but as the story unfolds, it becomes increasingly unclear what is real and what is just a product of his imagination.

The film also touches on the idea of isolation and loneliness, highlighting the difficulties of forming connections with others in a world that often seems hostile or indifferent. Prot's struggles to find acceptance and understanding serve as a powerful metaphor for the human experience, where we all yearn for connection and belonging.

Furthermore, K-PAX raises important questions about the nature of reality and perception, encouraging viewers to think critically about their own understanding of the world. The film's use of surreal and dreamlike sequences adds to the sense of disorientation and confusion, mirroring Prot's own experiences as he navigates this complex web of reality.

Ultimately, K-PAX is a movie that challenges its audience to confront the complexities of human existence, inviting us to question our assumptions about identity, reality, and the human condition.

overview: During the Japanese colonial era, roughly 400 Korean people, who were forced onto Battleship Island (‘Hashima Island’) to mine for coal, attempt to escape.
tagline: 1945 Hashima. We called it hell on earth.
title: The Battleship Island
plot:
The Battleship Island is a 2017 South Korean war film directed by Ryoo Seung-wan. The movie tells the story of a group of prisoners who are sent to a remote island, where they must fight for survival against the Japanese forces during World War II.

At its core, The Battleship Island explores themes of resilience, camaraderie, and the human spirit in the face of overwhelming adversity. The film delves into the psychological effects of war on individuals and the bonds that form between people in extreme circumstances. As the prisoners navigate their treacherous surroundings, they must confront their own demons and learn to trust each other in order to survive.

The movie also touches on the theme of colonialism and the exploitation of colonized peoples by imperial powers. The Japanese forces are depicted as ruthless and merciless, highlighting the brutal realities of war and the devastating impact it has on innocent civilians.

Furthermore, The Battleship Island is a film about the power of hope and redemption in the darkest of times. Despite being trapped in a desperate situation, the prisoners find ways to maintain their dignity and sense of purpose, often through acts of defiance and rebellion against their captors.

Overall, The Battleship Island is a gripping and intense war drama that explores complex themes and emotions with nuance and sensitivity.

overview: A group of archaeological students become trapped in the past when they go there to retrieve their professor. The group must survive in 14th century France long enough to be rescued.
tagline: They had to travel into the past to save the future
title: Timeline
plot:
Timeline is a 2003 science fiction adventure film directed by Richard Donner and starring Paul Walker, Frances O'Connor, and William Fichtner.

The main themes of Timeline include:

1. **Time Travel and its Consequences**: The movie explores the concept of time travel and its potential consequences on human relationships and personal growth. The protagonist, Dr. Alex Andrews (Paul Walker), travels back in time to 14th-century France, where he becomes embroiled in a conflict between the French king and his nobles.

2. **Identity and Self-Discovery**: As Alex navigates through different historical periods, he begins to question his own identity and sense of self. He struggles with the idea that his actions in the past may alter the course of history, leading to changes in his present life.

3. **Human Connection and Sacrifice**: The film highlights the importance of human connection and sacrifice. Alex's relationships with his colleagues and loved ones back in the present are put to the test as he faces challenges in the past that require him to make difficult choices.

4. **Power and Corruption**: The movie touches on the theme of power and corruption, particularly in the context of medieval politics. The French king's desire for absolute power and control leads to conflict with his nobles, highlighting the dangers of unchecked ambition.

5. **The Butterfly Effect**: Timeline explores the idea that even small actions can have significant consequences, a concept known as the butterfly effect. Alex's decisions in the past start to alter the course of history, leading to unexpected outcomes.

Overall, Timeline is a thought-provoking film that delves into complex themes and ideas, making it more than just an action-adventure movie.

overview: Forlorn heiress Penelope Wilhern is cursed, and the only way out is to fall in love with someone of suitable stock. But how can she find her soul mate when she's sequestered inside her family's estate with only her parents to keep her company. This untraditional fairy tale about a girl who bucks convention to create her own happy ending.
tagline: A fairytale like no other.
title: Penelope
plot:
Penelope is a fantasy romantic comedy directed by Mark Palansky from a screenplay by Leslie Caveny, first shown in 2006. Christina Ricci is Penelope Wilhern, an heiress born with a pig's snout because of a family curse, with James McAvoy as Johnny Martin, Catherine O'Hara and Richard E. Grant as her parents Jessica and Franklin, Peter Dinklage as the tabloid reporter Lemon, Simon Woods as the suitor Edward Vanderman III and Reese Witherspoon, who also produced the film, as the delivery girl Annie.

Generations ago, a servant, Clara, became pregnant by the aristocrat Ralph Wilhern, who married another woman at his parents' insistence; after Clara killed herself, her mother, a witch, cursed the family so that the next Wilhern daughter would have the face of a pig until loved by "one of her own kind". After five generations of sons, Penelope is born. Her mortified mother pretends the baby died and hides her in the family's London mansion, and once Penelope turns eighteen, a matchmaker parades blue-blooded suitors before her, convinced that marrying one will break the spell. All flee in horror, Edward among them, and he teams up with Lemon to prove she exists by hiring a gambler posing as the aristocrat Max Campion to photograph her with a hidden camera.

Talking through a one-way mirror, Penelope and "Max" fall for each other. When he sees her face he is startled but not afraid; ashamed, he destroys the camera, but refuses her plea to marry him. Fed up with confinement, Penelope runs away into the city with her face hidden by a scarf, selling photographs of herself to Lemon and befriending Annie. When her face is exposed in a pub, the public adores her, and Edward's father pressures his son into proposing. At the altar, Penelope realises she does not want to marry merely to lift the curse and declares that she likes herself as she is; because she has been loved by one of her own kind, herself, her snout vanishes. Now a schoolteacher, she learns that "Max" is really Johnny Martin and finds him at a Halloween party, where they kiss. The family butler, revealed to be the witch, silences Jessica with a last spell, and Lemon chooses not to photograph the happy couple.

Shot in London and at Pinewood Studios in early 2006 as Witherspoon's first production, Penelope premiered at the Toronto festival in September 2006, with Summit Entertainment later handling its American release. It grossed $21.2 million worldwide and drew mixed reviews, with 53% on Rotten Tomatoes.

overview: In the late 1950s and early '60s, artist Walter Keane achieves unbelievable fame and success with portraits of saucer-eyed waifs. However, no one realizes that his wife, Margaret, is the real painter behind the brush. Although Margaret is horrified to learn that Walter is passing off her work as his own, she is too meek to protest too loudly. It isn't until the Keanes' marriage comes to an end and a lawsuit follows that the truth finally comes to light.
tagline: She created it. He sold it. And everyone bought it.
title: Big Eyes
plot:
Big Eyes is a 2014 biographical drama film directed by Tim Burton, starring Amy Adams as Margaret Keane and Christoph Waltz as Walter Keane. The movie is based on the true story of Margaret Keane's life and her artwork.

The main themes of Big Eyes include:

1. **Identity and Self-Discovery**: The film explores Margaret's journey to find her own identity and artistic voice, separate from her husband Walter's influence. As she gains recognition for her art, she must navigate the complexities of fame and her own sense of self.
2. **Marital Relationships and Power Dynamics**: The movie portrays a tumultuous marriage between Margaret and Walter, with Walter exploiting Margaret's talent and taking credit for her work. This theme highlights the struggles women face in patriarchal societies and the importance of female empowerment.
3. **Artistic Expression and Authenticity**: Big Eyes delves into the world of art, showcasing Margaret's unique style and the controversy surrounding her work. The film raises questions about artistic ownership, authenticity, and the value placed on creative expression.
4. **Fame and Celebrity Culture**: As Margaret's artwork gains popularity, she becomes a celebrity in her own right. The movie explores the darker side of fame, including the pressures of maintaining a public image and the consequences of success.

Throughout the film, Tim Burton masterfully weaves these themes together, creating a narrative that is both captivating and thought-provoking.

overview: St. Agatha is set in the 1950s in small town Georgia. A pregnant con woman named Agatha is on the run and seeks refuge in a convent hidden in deafening isolation. What first starts out as the perfect place to have a child turns into a dark lair where silence is forced. Ghastly secrets are masked, and every bit of will power Agatha has is tested. She soon learns the sick and twisted truth of the convent and the odd people that lurk inside its halls. Agatha must now find a way to discover the unyielding strength needed to escape and save her baby before she’s caged behind these walls forever.
tagline: Atone for your sins.
title: St. Agatha
plot:
St. Agatha is a 2018 American horror film directed by Jeremy Hart and written by Jeremy Hart and David W. Egan. 

The movie revolves around a young woman named Sarah, who takes a job as a waitress at a remote restaurant in upstate New York, only to discover that the establishment has a dark history tied to the legend of St. Agatha. As Sarah delves deeper into the mystery, she begins to experience strange and terrifying occurrences that threaten her sanity and her life.

At its core, St. Agatha is a film about the dangers of curiosity and the power of female vulnerability in a male-dominated world. The movie explores themes of isolation, loneliness, and the struggle for empowerment, as Sarah navigates a patriarchal society that seeks to silence and control her. Through Sarah's character, the film highlights the ways in which women are often forced to confront their own vulnerabilities and fears in order to survive.

The movie also touches on the theme of trauma and its lasting impact on individuals and communities. The dark history of the restaurant and the legend of St. Agatha serve as a metaphor for the ways in which traumatic experiences can be passed down through generations, affecting not only the individual but also those around them.

Ultimately, St. Agatha is a film about the resilience of the human spirit and the power of female solidarity in the face of adversity. Despite being trapped in a desperate situation, Sarah finds ways to resist and subvert her oppressors, ultimately emerging stronger and more determined than ever before.

overview: A revered bounty hunter's latest gig is rather satisfying, as his bail-skipper is his ex-wife, who has no intention of getting nabbed without a fight.
tagline: It's a Job. It Isn't Personal. Well, Maybe a Little...
title: The Bounty Hunter
plot:
The Bounty Hunter is an American romantic action comedy of 2010 directed by Andy Tennant. Gerard Butler stars as Milo Boyd, a former New York police detective turned bounty hunter, and Jennifer Aniston as his former wife, the reporter Nicole Hurley, with Jason Sudeikis as her admiring colleague Stewart, Jeff Garlin as the bail bondsman Sid, Cathy Moriarty as the bookmaker Irene, Peter Greene as the corrupt officer Earl Mahler and Dorian Missick as Milo's friend and former partner Bobby.

Nicole, awaiting trial for assaulting a police officer, skips her court date to chase a tip about a suicide that may have been a murder, and the judge issues a warrant for her arrest. Her informant, Jimmy, is kidnapped before she can meet him. Milo is delighted when Sid offers him $5,000 to bring her in, and with unwitting help from Nicole's mother he tracks her to a New Jersey racetrack, throws her in the boot of his car and heads for Manhattan. They are pursued on several fronts: Irene's thugs want Milo's gambling debts, Earl Mahler, implicated in Nicole's story, wants her dead, and Stewart is trying to rescue her, until the thugs mistake him for Milo and abduct him.

After Earl tries and fails to shoot Nicole on the road, Milo learns that her investigation implicates his old partner, Bobby, and agrees to look into it. Clues lead them to a country club and then towards Earl's tattoo parlour in Queens. Lying low at the very inn where they honeymooned, the exes rediscover their feelings, but when Nicole overhears Milo saying he will still deliver her to jail, she handcuffs him to the bed and drives off. She frees Jimmy but is seized by Irene's men, and Milo rescues her at a strip club. At the police evidence warehouse, Earl, who has exploited Bobby's name to steal drugs and cash, shoots Bobby, but Milo and Nicole overpower him, and the wounded Bobby explains he had been waiting for Earl to make his move. Despite their reconciliation, Milo still hands Nicole over for the bounty, then punches an officer who had insulted him, landing in the neighbouring cell so that they can spend their anniversary together, declaring their love through the bars.

Released in the United States on 19 March 2010, the film was panned by critics, scoring 13% on Rotten Tomatoes, yet grossed about $136.3 million worldwide on a budget of $40-45 million.

overview: Molly Mahoney is the awkward and insecure manager of Mr. Magorium's Wonder Emporium—the strangest, most fantastic and most wonderful toy store in the world. After Mr. Magorium bequeaths the store to her, a dark and ominous change begins to take over the once-remarkable Emporium.
tagline: You have to believe it to see it.
title: Mr. Magorium's Wonder Emporium
plot:
Mr. Magorium's Wonder Emporium is a 2007 American family fantasy comedy written and directed by Zach Helm in his directorial debut. Dustin Hoffman stars as Edward Magorium, the eccentric 243-year-old owner of a magical toy store, with Natalie Portman as its manager Molly Mahoney, Jason Bateman as the accountant Henry Weston and Zach Mills as Eric Applebaum, a lonely young customer. Kermit the Frog makes a cameo.

Molly, a former child piano prodigy, is stuck: she dreams of becoming a concert pianist and composer but cannot finish her first concerto. At the Emporium she works with the bookbinder Bellini and Eric, who visits daily and acts like an employee. Magorium gives Molly a plain block of wood called the Congreve Cube, telling her it will lead her to a new life if she has faith in it. He then announces that he intends to "leave" and give the store to Molly, hiring Henry, a buttoned-up accountant, to sort out his finances. Henry refuses to believe that the store is magical. When Molly panics about running it, the Emporium throws a tantrum, turning its toys against everyone inside until Magorium calms it.

Realizing that Magorium means he is about to die, Molly rushes him to the hospital, where doctors find nothing wrong. She tries to show him the joys of life, but he assures her that he has lived fully. Using the stage directions of King Lear to show how simple death is, he encourages her and dies. Convinced she cannot run the shop, Molly puts it up for sale, and it loses its magic. Henry, now Eric's friend, meets Molly to sign the papers. When she admits her faith in the store, the block flies around the room, and Henry faints. He realizes that it was Molly who made it fly, and he tells her she can do anything if she believes in herself. Confident at last, Molly conjures and conducts her finished concerto, reviving the store. In a post-credits scene, Magorium paints The Son of Man on a wall.

The film was shot in Toronto in 2006 and released by 20th Century Fox and Walden Media on November 16, 2007. It underperformed, grossing under $70 million worldwide. Reviews were mixed. Rotten Tomatoes reported 40% approval, finding its colorful visuals and talented cast unable to overcome a bland story, and Rolling Stone named it the year's worst family film. Roger Ebert, however, gave it three stars and called it charming, especially for young viewers. Helm later disowned the film as a "Technicolor train-wreck".

overview: Bertram Pincus, a cranky, people-hating Manhattan dentist, develops the unwelcome ability to see dead people. Really annoying dead people. Even worse, they all want something from him, particularly Frank Herlihy, a smooth-talking ghost, who pesters him into a romantic scheme involving his widow Gwen. They are soon entangled in a hilarious predicament between the now and the hereafter!
tagline: He sees dead people... and they annoy him.
title: Ghost Town
plot:
Ghost Town is a 2008 romantic comedy film that explores the complexities of love, loss, and redemption. The story revolves around Dr. Bertram Pincus, a dentist who has lost his sense of purpose after being unable to save his wife from cancer.

The main theme of Ghost Town is the power of human connection and the importance of living in the present moment. Through Bertram's journey, the film highlights the idea that life is short and fragile, and that we must cherish every moment with loved ones before it's too late. The movie also explores the concept of grief and how it can both consume us and ultimately lead to healing.

The character of Dr. Pincus serves as a catalyst for exploring these themes, as he struggles to come to terms with his own mortality and the impermanence of life. His interactions with a ghost named Gwen, who is stuck between worlds, serve as a metaphor for the human experience and the interconnectedness of all things.

Ultimately, Ghost Town suggests that love and connection can transcend even death itself, and that it's never too late to find meaning and purpose in life. The film's themes are woven throughout its narrative, creating a poignant and thought-provoking exploration of what it means to be human.

original_title: Sweeney Todd: The Demon Barber of Fleet Street
overview: The infamous story of Benjamin Barker, a.k.a Sweeney Todd, who sets up a barber shop down in London which is the basis for a sinister partnership with his fellow tenant, Mrs. Lovett. Based on the hit Broadway musical.
tagline: Never Forget. Never Forgive.
title: Sweeney Todd: The Demon Barber of Fleet Street
plot:
Sweeney Todd: The Demon Barber of Fleet Street is a Gothic musical slasher film of 2007 directed by Tim Burton from a screenplay by John Logan, adapted from the stage musical by Stephen Sondheim and Hugh Wheeler. Johnny Depp stars as the vengeful barber, with Helena Bonham Carter as Mrs. Lovett, Alan Rickman as Judge Turpin, Timothy Spall as Beadle Bamford, Sacha Baron Cohen as Adolfo Pirelli, Jamie Campbell Bower as Anthony Hope, Jayne Wisener as Johanna, Ed Sanders as Toby and Laura Michelle Kelly as the beggar woman.

In 1846 the barber Benjamin Barker returns to London with the young sailor Anthony, sixteen years after the corrupt Judge Turpin had him falsely convicted and transported to Australia in order to seize his wife, Lucy. Calling himself Sweeney Todd, he reopens his shop on Fleet Street above the dismal pie shop of Mrs. Lovett, who tells him that Turpin assaulted Lucy, driving her to suicide, and took their daughter Johanna as his ward. Mrs. Lovett, secretly in love with Todd, returns his old razors. Anthony falls for Johanna on sight and is thrown out by Turpin's henchman, the Beadle. When the rival barber Pirelli recognises Todd and tries to blackmail him, Todd kills him, and Mrs. Lovett takes in Pirelli's young assistant, Toby.

Turpin, who means to marry Johanna, comes for a shave, but Anthony bursts in and the judge escapes, locking Johanna in an asylum. Enraged, Todd vows vengeance on the whole city, and he and Mrs. Lovett hit upon a gruesome scheme: he will murder his customers and drop them through a trapdoor into her bakehouse to be baked into pies. Business booms. Anthony rescues Johanna disguised as a wigmaker, while Toby grows suspicious and is locked in the basement, where he discovers the remains. Todd kills the Beadle and then a beggar woman who has wandered into his shop, before luring Turpin back, revealing his identity and cutting his throat. He spares Johanna without recognising her, then realises that the beggar woman was Lucy, alive all along, and that Mrs. Lovett had lied. Feigning forgiveness, he waltzes her into the oven. As he cradles Lucy's body, Toby emerges from the sewers and kills him with his own razor.

Shot at Pinewood Studios in 2007, the film was released in December and grossed about $152.5 million worldwide. It was widely acclaimed, with 86% on Rotten Tomatoes; it won Golden Globes for Best Musical or Comedy and for Depp, and the Academy Award for Best Art Direction, with Depp also Oscar-nominated.

overview: Sam Witwicky leaves the Autobots behind for a normal life. But when his mind is filled with cryptic symbols, the Decepticons target him and he is dragged back into the Transformers' war.
tagline: Revenge is coming.
title: Transformers: Revenge of the Fallen
plot:
Transformers: Revenge of the Fallen is a 2009 science fiction action film directed by Michael Bay and produced by Steven Spielberg, Don Murphy, and Tom DeSanto. The movie is the second installment in the live-action Transformers film series.

The story begins with Sam Witwicky (Shia LaBeouf), a young man who has just graduated from high school. He buys his first car, a Chevrolet Camaro, which turns out to be Bumblebee, an Autobot sent to Earth to protect him. The Autobots, led by Optimus Prime (Peter Cullen), are on a mission to find the AllSpark, a powerful energy source that can bring life to inanimate objects.

Meanwhile, the Decepticons, led by Megatron (Hugo Weaving), are searching for the AllSpark as well. They plan to use its power to destroy Earth and rule the universe. The Autobots and Decepticons engage in an epic battle on the planet of Cybertron, but they are interrupted when the AllSpark is stolen by the human scientist Dr. William Lennox (Josh Duhamel) and his team.

The movie then shifts to Sam's life on Earth, where he begins to uncover a conspiracy involving the government and the Decepticons. He also meets Mikaela Banes (Megan Fox), a beautiful and intelligent woman who becomes his love interest.

As the story unfolds, Sam discovers that the Decepticons are planning to use the AllSpark to destroy Earth. He teams up with Optimus Prime and the Autobots to stop them, but they soon realize that the Decepticons have set a trap for them. The Autobots are ambushed by the Decepticons on the planet of Cybertron, and Sam is forced to flee.

The movie's climax features an epic battle between the Autobots and Decepticons on Earth. Optimus Prime sacrifices himself to save humanity, but not before he gives Sam a special key that will help him unlock the secrets of the AllSpark.

In the end, Sam and Mikaela escape from the Decepticons, and Sam uses the key to activate the AllSpark, which ultimately destroys the Decepticon spaceship. The movie concludes with Sam reflecting on his experiences and realizing that he has become a part of something much bigger than himself.

Overall, Transformers: Revenge of the Fallen is an action-packed sci-fi adventure that explores themes of friendship, sacrifice, and self-discovery. While it received mixed reviews from critics, it was a commercial success and helped establish the Transformers franchise as a major player in the science fiction genre.

overview: Shaun Brumder is a local surfer kid from Orange County who dreams of going to Stanford to become a writer and to get away from his dysfunctional family household. Except Shaun runs into one complication after another, starting when his application is rejected after his dim-witted guidance counselor sends in the wrong form.
tagline: It's not just a place. It's a state of mind.
title: Orange County
plot:
Orange County is a 2002 American comedy film directed by Jake Kasdan. The movie follows the story of Shaun Brumder, a high school dropout who returns to his hometown in Orange County, California, after dropping out of college.

The main theme of Orange County revolves around the struggle for identity and self-discovery. Shaun's journey is marked by his desire to fit in with his peers and prove himself as a capable individual, despite being a non-traditional student. As he navigates through his relationships with his family, friends, and romantic interests, Shaun grapples with the idea of who he wants to be and where he belongs.

The film also explores themes of social class and status, particularly in the context of Orange County's affluent communities. Shaun's experiences highlight the superficiality and materialism that can define certain social circles, leading him to question what truly matters in life.

Furthermore, Orange County touches on the idea of redemption and second chances. Shaun's decision to return to school and pursue his education is motivated by a desire to make amends for past mistakes and prove himself as a responsible individual. Throughout the movie, he faces various challenges that test his resolve and force him to confront his flaws.

Overall, Orange County is a heartwarming and humorous exploration of identity, class, and redemption, set against the vibrant backdrop of California's Orange County.

overview: A parolee falls for a reclusive movie star while trying to evade a ruthless gangster.
tagline: Not every criminal wants to be one.
title: London Boulevard
plot:
London Boulevard is a 2010 crime drama film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the consequences of one's actions. The movie follows the story of Harry Fielding, a struggling writer who becomes embroiled in a world of crime and violence after befriending a notorious gangster, Richard Harrow.

At its core, London Boulevard explores the theme of redemption and the blurred lines between good and evil. Harry's journey is marked by his desire to escape his mundane life and find meaning through his writing, but he soon finds himself drawn into a world where morality is relative and survival is the ultimate goal.

The film also touches on the idea of toxic masculinity, as embodied by Richard Harrow, who uses violence and intimidation to assert his dominance. Through Harry's interactions with Harrow, the movie highlights the destructive nature of this toxic behavior and its impact on those around him.

Furthermore, London Boulevard examines the theme of loneliness and isolation, particularly in the context of urban life. The film's portrayal of a city where people are disconnected from one another and struggling to find meaning in their lives resonates with the audience.

Overall, London Boulevard is a gritty and thought-provoking film that challenges its viewers to confront the darker aspects of human nature and the consequences of our actions.

overview: Following a mysterious disappearance on a jump, a group of skydivers experiences paranormal occurrences that leave them fighting for their lives.
tagline: Jump. Pull. Pray. Die.
title: Hex
plot:
Hex is a 2022 American supernatural horror film directed by Chris Johnston and Andy Malchiodi, both making their feature directing debuts, from a screenplay by Hans Rodionoff, the writer of Deep Blue Sea 2 and Lost Boys: The Thirst. Set in the world of sport skydiving, it stars Kayla Adams, Matthew Holcomb, Chloe Berman, Bryan David Roberts, Eric Alperin, Brad Worch II and Schno Mozingo, with Cody Renee Cameron. Although it carries a 2020 copyright and its release was postponed from August, the film was released on video-on-demand and digital platforms by Lionsgate in late October 2022. It is rated R for language, some violent content and brief nudity.

The film opens with a montage of old illustrations of demons, skydivers performing a risky manoeuvre and blood being dripped onto an altimeter as it is assembled, ending with one of the parachutists falling to their death. Ten years later, Sarah (Adams), an avid skydiver like her late father, is the new member of a local skydiving club. Payson (Holcomb) is eager for her to join his team of Lisa (Berman), Wade (Roberts), Evan (Alperin) and Greg (Worch), because he wants to attempt The Hex, the dangerous and allegedly cursed formation jump that went wrong a decade earlier; the only ominous presence at the drop zone is Kris (Mozingo), a grizzled old parachute packer. The team pulls off the formation, but one of them never lands, vanishing in mid-air and even disappearing from the video of the jump. When the group jumps again the next day, another member suffers a heart attack on the way down, and further deaths follow, from a body found with every bone broken to an exploding apartment. Sarah, who seems to be the only one unaware that her father died performing The Hex along with the rest of his team, is drawn into a story of curses and deals with demons.

Reviews were negative. Jim Morazzini of Voices From the Balcony, in a review republished by Nerdly, gave it two out of five, calling it a waste of potential, "Point Break reaches its Final Destination"; he admired some impressive jump footage and the initially intriguing mystery, but found the script full of obvious twists and gaping plot holes, the deaths random and the gore light. Brian Costello of Common Sense Media described an interesting premise lost in flawed execution and clunky storytelling, with low-budget limitations increasingly evident, though he found its depiction of skydiving culture partly believable.

overview: Newlywed couple Ted and Tami-Lynn want to have a baby, but in order to qualify to be a parent, Ted will have to prove he's a person in a court of law.
tagline: Ted is coming, again.
title: Ted 2
plot:
Ted 2 is a 2015 American fantasy comedy directed by Seth MacFarlane, who co-wrote it with Alec Sulkin and Wellesley Wild. A sequel to Ted (2012), it stars MacFarlane as the voice of Ted, Mark Wahlberg as John Bennett, Amanda Seyfried as Samantha Jackson, Jessica Barth as Tami-Lynn, Giovanni Ribisi as Donny and Morgan Freeman as Patrick Meighan.

Ted, a living teddy bear, marries Tami-Lynn, while John is now divorced from Lori. A year later, the marriage is strained, and the couple decide that a baby could save it. Since Ted cannot father a child, he and John search for a sperm donor, and after several failed attempts John offers his own. When Tami-Lynn proves to be infertile because of past drug use, they try to adopt. The adoption process leads Massachusetts to declare that Ted is property rather than a person. He loses his job, his accounts and his marriage. John and Ted decide to sue, and a leading lawyer hands the case to his niece Sam, a novice attorney. She knows nothing about pop culture, but the three bond over their love of marijuana.

Meanwhile, Ted's old stalker Donny, now a janitor at Hasbro's headquarters, persuades an executive to back his plan to kidnap Ted and mass-produce living teddy bears. The court rules against Ted. The trio turn to Patrick Meighan, a renowned civil rights lawyer, and on the trip to New York, John and Sam fall in love. Meighan sympathizes but turns them down, saying Ted has contributed little to humanity. Angry and jealous of John's new romance, Ted storms off into New York Comic Con, where Donny, disguised as a Ninja Turtle, abducts him. John and Sam arrive just as Donny is about to cut Ted open. As they leave, Donny sends a model of the Starship Enterprise swinging toward Ted, and John pushes him aside and is struck. In the hospital, John appears to die but has merely been revived and is pranking them. News footage of Ted's grief and John's sacrifice persuades Meighan to take the case, and he wins by showing that Ted is self-aware and capable of empathy. Ted and Tami-Lynn remarry and adopt a son.

A dropped drug-smuggling storyline left no room for Mila Kunis's Lori. Filming began in Massachusetts in July 2014. Universal released the film on June 26, 2015. Its $33.5 million opening disappointed, but it grossed $217 million worldwide on a $68 million budget. Reviews were mixed to negative. Rotten Tomatoes reported 45% approval, saying enjoyment would depend on tolerance for its sophomoric, scatological humor.

overview: After an unprecedented global pandemic has turned the majority of humankind into violent infected beings, Morgan, a man gifted with the ability to speak the infected's new language, leads the last survivors on a hunt for patient zero and a cure.
title: Patient Zero
plot:
Patient Zero is a 2018 apocalyptic thriller film that delves into the theme of isolation and the blurred lines between humanity and savagery. The movie follows a lone survivor, Robert Neville, who finds himself immune to a deadly virus that has turned most of humanity into violent, zombie-like creatures.

As the story unfolds, the film explores the psychological effects of isolation on Neville's character, as he struggles to maintain his grip on sanity while navigating a desolate world devoid of human connection. The movie raises questions about what it means to be human and whether our relationships with others are essential to our survival.

The film also touches on the theme of loneliness, highlighting the devastating consequences of losing loved ones and being forced to confront the reality of one's own mortality. Neville's character is a poignant representation of this theme, as he grapples with the weight of his isolation and the moral implications of his actions in a world that has been ravaged by the virus.

Furthermore, Patient Zero critiques the notion of humanity's reliance on technology and societal structures to survive. In a post-apocalyptic world where these systems have failed, Neville is forced to rely on his wits and resourcefulness to stay alive, highlighting the importance of individual resilience in the face of catastrophic collapse.

Overall, Patient Zero presents a gripping narrative that explores the darker aspects of human nature, isolation, and the consequences of our actions in the face of unimaginable adversity.

overview: The Fantastic Mr. Fox bored with his current life, plans a heist against the three local farmers. The farmers, tired of sharing their chickens with the sly fox, seek revenge against him and his family.
tagline: Dig the life fantastic!
title: Fantastic Mr. Fox
plot:
Fantastic Mr. Fox is a 2009 stop-motion animated adventure comedy directed by Wes Anderson, who wrote the screenplay with Noah Baumbach from Roald Dahl's 1970 novel. George Clooney voices Mr. Fox, with Meryl Streep, Jason Schwartzman, Bill Murray, Willem Dafoe and Owen Wilson in the cast.

Caught in a trap while raiding a squab farm, Mr. Fox learns from his wife, Felicity, that she is pregnant and promises to find a safer line of work. Twelve fox-years later the couple and their son, Ash, live in a hole. Ignoring the warnings of his lawyer, Clive Badger, Mr. Fox moves the family into a tree near the operations of three notorious farmers, Walt Boggis, Nate Bunce and Frank Bean. Felicity's nephew Kristofferson comes to stay while his father is treated for double pneumonia. Missing his old life, Mr. Fox and his opossum friend Kylie steal poultry and cider from the three farms.
