The enraged farmers shoot off his tail and destroy his home, driving the Foxes underground, where they meet Badger and other animals made homeless by the farmers.

As the hungry animals start blaming the Foxes, Mr. Fox leads them in digging tunnels to all three farms and stealing the farmers' goods. In response the farmers and the fire chief flood the tunnels with Bean's cider, washing the animals into the sewers. Ash and Kristofferson sneak back to recover the tail, and Kristofferson is captured by Bean's wife. Bean's violent security guard, Rat, attacks Ash and Felicity, and after a fight with Mr. Fox he is electrocuted, revealing before he dies that Kristofferson is held in the attic of Bean Annex. Mr. Fox offers to surrender if the farmers free his nephew, and when they prepare an ambush, the animals counterattack, allowing Mr. Fox, Ash and Kylie to slip into the annex. Ash frees Kristofferson and impresses everyone by releasing a rabid beagle under fire. The animals settle into new homes in the sewers and soon raid a supermarket owned by the farmers, where Felicity announces another pregnancy.

Developed from 2004 at Revolution Studios with Henry Selick, the project moved to 20th Century Fox, and production began in 2007 at 3 Mills Studios in London. It opened the 53rd BFI London Film Festival in October 2009. Critics acclaimed its humor, animation and direction, with 93% on Rotten Tomatoes and 83 on Metacritic, but it earned only about $46.2 million against a $40 million budget. It was nominated for the Academy Awards for Best Animated Feature and Best Original Score.

overview: Just when you thought it was safe to go back to the beach, it appears that our large fishy friends have found a way to chomp on you when you're chilling out on the sand too!
tagline: Just When You Thought You Were Safe Out of the Water
title: Sand Sharks
plot:
Sand Sharks is an action-thriller film that revolves around a group of people who are stalked and killed by great white sharks in a beach town. The movie explores several themes, primarily centered around survival, human nature, and the consequences of playing with nature.

At its core, Sand Sharks delves into the idea of survival against all odds. The characters are faced with an impossible situation where they must fend off a relentless predator that seems to be always one step ahead. This scenario forces them to confront their own mortality and the limits of human endurance. As the body count rises, the survivors are pushed to their breaking points, leading to a thrilling and suspenseful ride.

The film also touches on the theme of human nature, specifically how people react in extreme situations. The characters' actions range from bravery to cowardice, revealing their true selves as they try to stay alive. This aspect of the movie adds an element of psychological tension, making it difficult for the audience to distinguish between good and evil.

Furthermore, Sand Sharks explores the consequences of playing with nature. The characters' reckless behavior in the water, such as surfing and swimming in areas known to be inhabited by sharks, ultimately leads to their downfall. This theme serves as a warning about the dangers of underestimating the power of nature and the importance of respecting its boundaries.

Overall, Sand Sharks is an action-packed thriller that combines elements of suspense, survival, and human psychology, making for an entertaining and thrilling ride.

overview: It's the ultimate buddy cop movie except for one thing: they're not cops.  When two struggling pals dress as police officers for a costume party, they become neighborhood sensations.  But when these newly-minted “heroes” get tangled in a real life web of mobsters and dirty detectives, they must put their fake badges on the line.
tagline: Fake Cops. Real Trouble.
title: Let's Be Cops
plot:
Let's Be Cops is a 2014 American action comedy film directed by Jason Stone and written by Jake Kasdan, Nicholas Stoller, and Jay Lavender. The movie stars Jake Johnson, Damon Wayans Jr., Nina Dobrev, and Rob Riggle.

The story follows two friends, Justin (Jake Johnson) and Ryan (Damon Wayans Jr.), who are struggling to find their place in the world. They work as sales representatives for a company that sells novelty items, but they're not very successful. One day, while browsing online, they stumble upon an advertisement for a costume party where people dress up as cops. The idea sparks their imagination, and they decide to take it to the next level by becoming actual police officers.

The two friends create fake IDs, uniforms, and badges, and start patrolling the streets of Los Angeles in their car. They soon attract the attention of Detective James Carter (Rob Riggle), a tough and no-nonsense cop who's not impressed with their antics. However, things take a turn when they meet Natalie (Nina Dobrev), a beautiful woman who's also into cosplay.

As Justin and Ryan continue to pretend to be cops, they start to get caught up in the thrill of it all. They begin to develop feelings for each other and for Natalie, but their fake identities put them at risk of being exposed. Meanwhile, Detective Carter becomes increasingly suspicious of their activities, and a cat-and-mouse game ensues.

As the story unfolds, Justin and Ryan's friendship is tested when they're forced to confront the consequences of their actions. They must decide whether to continue with their charade or come clean about who they really are. Along the way, they learn valuable lessons about trust, loyalty, and being true to oneself.

The movie takes a turn for the action-packed when Justin and Ryan find themselves in a series of intense situations, including a high-speed chase and a confrontation with some rough-looking thugs. In the end, they must use their wits and their fake cop skills to outsmart their enemies and save the day.

Let's Be Cops is a lighthearted, entertaining film that explores themes of identity, friendship, and self-discovery. The movie features plenty of humor, action, and heart, making it a fun watch for audiences of all ages.

overview: During the 17th century, a young woman is saved from execution and led to a priory to repent her sins but discovers a greater evil lies within.
tagline: Forgive us our sins
title: The Convent
plot:
The Convent is a 2018 South African drama film directed by Nia Diniz, produced by Templeheart Films, and released on Netflix.

The main themes of The Convent revolve around the struggles of women in patriarchal societies, particularly those who are marginalized or oppressed. The story follows a young woman named Mpho, who is forced to flee her home after being raped by her uncle, and finds herself at a convent where she hopes to escape her traumatic past.

Throughout the film, Diniz explores themes of trauma, survival, and resilience in the face of adversity. Mpho's journey is marked by moments of vulnerability, anger, and ultimately, empowerment as she navigates the complexities of her new environment.

The film also touches on issues of rape culture, patriarchal norms, and the societal expectations placed on women. The convent itself becomes a symbol of confinement and oppression, highlighting the ways in which institutions can perpetuate harm rather than healing.

Ultimately, The Convent is a powerful exploration of the human spirit's capacity for survival and transformation in the face of trauma and adversity.

overview: The true story of boxer Jim Braddock who, in the 1920s following his retirement, makes a surprise comeback in order to get him and his family out of a socially poor state.
tagline: One man's extraordinary fight to save the family he loved.
title: Cinderella Man
plot:
Cinderella Man is a 2005 biographical sports drama film directed by Ron Howard, produced by Brian Grazer and Eric Fellner, and distributed by Universal Pictures.

The main themes of Cinderella Man revolve around the underdog story of boxer James J. Braddock (played by Russell Crowe), who rose from poverty to become a heavyweight champion of the world during the Great Depression. Some of the key themes include:

1. **Perseverance and Resilience**: The film showcases Braddock's determination and grit in the face of adversity, as he overcomes numerous setbacks, including a devastating boxing injury that leaves him with a severely damaged hand.
2. **The American Dream**: Cinderella Man is an embodiment of the American Dream, where Braddock, a working-class man from New York City, achieves success through hard work and dedication, despite being given little chance of success by others.
3. **Class Struggle**: The film highlights the stark contrast between Braddock's humble beginnings and his eventual rise to fame, as well as the class divisions of the time, which are reflected in the character of Max Baer (played by Paul Giamatti), a wealthy and arrogant boxer who serves as a foil to Braddock.
4. **The Power of Redemption**: Through Braddock's journey, the film explores the idea of redemption, as he seeks to reclaim his dignity and self-respect after being humiliated in the ring and struggling to make ends meet.
5. **The Human Spirit**: The movie celebrates the human spirit's capacity for hope, courage, and determination in the face of adversity, as Braddock refuses to give up on himself or his dreams.

Overall, Cinderella Man is a powerful and inspiring film that explores themes of perseverance, resilience, and redemption, set against the backdrop of one of America's most tumultuous periods.

overview: Arthur Bishop thought he had put his murderous past behind him when his most formidable foe kidnaps the love of his life. Now he is forced to travel the globe to complete three impossible assassinations, and do what he does best, make them look like accidents.
tagline: Four continents. Three kills... Or the love of his life is dead.
title: Mechanic: Resurrection
plot:
Mechanic: Resurrection is a 2016 action thriller film directed by Dennis Gansel and starring Jason Statham as the titular character, Arthur Bishop. The movie follows Bishop's latest mission to rescue his mentor, Max (Tony Jaa), who has been kidnapped by a powerful crime lord named Gabriel (Michael Angarano).

The story begins with Bishop, a skilled assassin and mechanic, living in Bangkok, Thailand. He is approached by a wealthy businessman named Henry (Hugo Weaving) who asks for his help in rescuing Max, a former ally who has gone missing. Bishop agrees to take on the mission, but soon discovers that Gabriel, a ruthless crime lord, is behind Max's kidnapping.

As Bishop delves deeper into the world of high-stakes crime, he meets a young woman named Sarah (Hannah Hughes), Henry's daughter, who becomes his unlikely ally. Together, they embark on a perilous journey to rescue Max and take down Gabriel's operation.

Throughout the movie, Bishop faces off against Gabriel's henchmen in intense hand-to-hand combat sequences, showcasing his exceptional fighting skills. Along the way, he also encounters other characters, including a mysterious woman named Anna (Mia Goth), who seems to be hiding secrets of her own.

As the story unfolds, Bishop and Sarah navigate through the dark underbelly of Bangkok's crime scene, uncovering a complex web of corruption and deceit. They eventually track down Gabriel's operation to an abandoned warehouse on the outskirts of the city, where they engage in a fierce battle with Gabriel's men.

In the climactic final showdown, Bishop faces off against Gabriel, who reveals himself to be a former ally turned enemy. The two engage in a intense fight, with Bishop using his mechanical skills to outmaneuver and overpower Gabriel. In the end, Bishop emerges victorious, rescuing Max and bringing Gabriel's operation down.

Throughout the movie, Statham delivers his signature blend of action and humor, making Mechanic: Resurrection a thrilling ride for fans of the genre. The film's visuals are stunning, with breathtaking action sequences and impressive stunts that showcase Bishop's skills as a mechanic and assassin.

Overall, Mechanic: Resurrection is an adrenaline-fueled thrill ride that delivers on its promise of high-octane action and suspenseful storytelling. With Statham at the helm, the movie is a must-see for fans of the Mechanic franchise and action enthusiasts alike.

original_title: Mickey's Magical Christmas: Snowed in at the House of Mouse
overview: When a huge snowstorm leaves everyone stranded, Mickey and all of his guests at the House of Mouse, including Pooh, Belle, Snow White, Cinderella, Ariel and many more of his old and new friends, break out the cookies and hot chocolate to help Donald mend his tattered Christmas spirit.
title: Mickey's Magical Christmas: Snowed in at the House of Mouse
plot:
Mickey's Magical Christmas: Snowed In At The House Of Mouse is a direct-to-video animated film produced by Disney Television Animation, released in 2001. The movie takes place during the holiday season and revolves around Mickey Mouse and his friends at the House of Mouse.

The story begins with Mickey Mouse excitedly preparing for Christmas at the House of Mouse. However, on Christmas Eve, a severe snowstorm hits Toontown, causing the power to go out and trapping the guests inside the restaurant. As the night progresses, the group starts to get restless, and tensions rise as they realize that they won't be able to leave.

As the hours pass, Mickey tries to keep everyone's spirits high by telling Christmas stories and singing holiday songs. However, things take a turn when Pete, who has been trying to ruin Christmas for the gang all along, reveals his true intentions: he plans to steal Santa's bag of presents meant for Toontown.

Determined to stop Pete, Mickey rallies his friends, including Minnie Mouse, Pluto, and Goofy. Together, they devise a plan to outsmart Pete and save Christmas. Along the way, they learn valuable lessons about teamwork, friendship, and the true meaning of the holiday season.

As the night wears on, the group faces various obstacles, including a wild goose chase through the House of Mouse and a confrontation with Pete's accomplices. However, in the end, Mickey and his friends successfully thwart Pete's plans, and Christmas is saved.

The movie concludes with a heartwarming celebration of the holiday season, featuring festive music, decorations, and a special appearance by Santa Claus himself. The film ends on a high note, with Mickey and his friends enjoying a joyful Christmas Eve together, surrounded by the magic of the House of Mouse.

Throughout the movie, the characters' personalities shine through, adding to the humor and charm of the story. From Goofy's goofy antics to Pluto's loyal companionship, each character brings their unique voice to the film, making it a delightful holiday treat for audiences of all ages.

Overall, Mickey's Magical Christmas: Snowed In At The House Of Mouse is a fun, festive, and heartwarming animated film that captures the spirit of the holiday season. With its lovable characters, engaging storyline, and catchy music, this movie is sure to become a classic among Disney fans and families alike.

original_title: Fate/Grand Order -終局特異点 冠位時間神殿ソロモン-
overview: The Chaldea Organization must deal with the Grand Temple of Solomon, the King of Magic, which has come to destroy the world.
tagline: This is the final battle to take back our future.
title: Fate/Grand Order Final Singularity – Grand Temple of Time: Solomon
plot:
Fate/Grand Order Final Singularity – Grand Temple of Time: Solomon (Fate/Grand Order -終局特異点 冠位時間神殿ソロモン-) is a 2021 Japanese animated fantasy action film directed by Toshifumi Akai and animated by CloverWorks, with 3D computer graphics by Shirogumi, and distributed by Aniplex. It adapts the climactic chapter of the first part of the story of Fate/Grand Order, the TYPE-MOON mobile role-playing game written by Kinoko Nasu, who is credited with the original scenario. A sequel to the 2019–2020 television series Fate/Grand Order – Absolute Demonic Front: Babylonia, whose final episode announced it, the film was made by largely the same team, including character designer Tomoaki Takase and composers Keita Haga and Ryo Kawasaki. It was released in Japanese cinemas on 30 July 2021 and runs 94 minutes. The voice cast is led by Nobunaga Shimazaki as Ritsuka Fujimaru and Rie Takahashi as Mash Kyrielight, with Kenichi Suzumura as Romani Archaman, Maaya Sakamoto as Leonardo da Vinci, Ayako Kawasumi as Fou and Tomokazu Sugita as Solomon.

Having fought its way through all seven Singularities that threatened human history, the Chaldea Security Organization at last reaches the endpoint of the Grand Order: the Final Singularity, the Grand Temple of Time, a domain created by Solomon, the King of Magic, who intends to destroy the world. As the final operation looms, Romani Archaman weighs the choices he will soon have to make, Mash Kyrielight reflects on the limits of her own life, and the Master Ritsuka Fujimaru prepares to receive a new Mystic Code. The pair then launch their last mission into the temple, where dozens of Heroic Spirits they have met over the course of their journey arrive to join the battle against Solomon's forces, in a final struggle to reclaim humanity's future.

Kim Morrissy of Anime News Network gave the film a B, likening it to the Avengers: Endgame of the Fate franchise because its appeal hinges on cameos from dozens of Servants rarely seen in animated form. She admitted the plot was a load of nonsense she loved every minute of, praised the animation by the Babylonia team as among the best-looking in the franchise and the satisfying climax and ending, which neatly wraps up the first part of the story, but found the theatrical dialogue potentially cheesy and self-indulgent, the ensemble action scenes too short and the film likely to be off-putting to viewers who had not played the game.

overview: The film takes place one year after the events of Captain America: The First Avenger, in which Agent Carter, a member of the Strategic Scientific Reserve, is in search of the mysterious Zodiac.
tagline: In an all-new Captain America adventure.
title: Marvel One-Shot: Agent Carter
plot:
Marvel One-Shot: Agent Carter is a 2013 web series that serves as a spin-off to The Avengers. The story revolves around Peggy Carter, a skilled spy and agent of S.H.I.E.L.D., played by Hayley Atwell.

The main themes of the movie are:

1. **Female Empowerment**: The film showcases Peggy Carter's strength, intelligence, and determination in a male-dominated world. Her character is a powerful representation of women in espionage and a precursor to the modern female superheroes we see today.
2. **Sacrifice and Loyalty**: Agent Carter highlights the importance of loyalty and sacrifice in the face of adversity. Peggy's unwavering dedication to her country, S.H.I.E.L.D., and her friends puts her in harm's way, demonstrating the true meaning of these values.
3. **The Cost of War**: The movie explores the consequences of war on individuals and society. The story delves into the moral complexities of espionage and the blurred lines between right and wrong in a world where allegiances are constantly shifting.
4. **Identity and Self-Discovery**: As Peggy navigates her past and present, she grapples with her identity and sense of purpose. Her journey is a metaphor for finding one's place in the world and embracing one's true self.

The film's narrative is driven by Peggy's quest to uncover the truth about her past and the mysterious organization known as HYDRA. Along the way, she must confront her own demons and make difficult choices that will impact her future.

Overall, Marvel One-Shot: Agent Carter is a thrilling adventure that explores complex themes and features a strong, inspiring female protagonist at its core.

original_title: るろうに剣心 京都大火編
overview: Kenshin has settled into his new life with Kaoru and his other friends when he is approached with a request from the Meiji government. Makoto Shishio, a former assassin like Kenshin, was betrayed, set on fire and left for dead. He survived, and is now in Kyoto, plotting with his gathered warriors to overthrow the new government. Against Kaoru's wishes, Kenshin reluctantly agrees to go to Kyoto and help keep his country from falling back into civil war.
tagline: Fate Hangs On His Sword.
title: Rurouni Kenshin Part II: Kyoto Inferno
plot:
Rurouni Kenshin: Kyoto Inferno, released in North America as Rurouni Kenshin Part II: Kyoto Inferno, is a 2014 Japanese jidaigeki action film based on the Rurouni Kenshin manga and the second installment of the live-action series that began with Rurouni Kenshin (2012). Directed by Keishi Ōtomo, it stars Takeru Satoh as the wandering swordsman Himura Kenshin, with Emi Takei, Munetaka Aoki, Yū Aoi and Kaito Oyagi, and Tatsuya Fujiwara as the villain Shishio Makoto.

In a mine in Hyōgo Prefecture, police led by Saitō Hajime are ambushed and massacred by the men of Shishio, who had helped overthrow the Tokugawa shogunate before being betrayed. Kenshin, living at Kamiya Kaoru's dojo, at first refuses the government's request to stop Shishio, but agrees after the official Ōkubo Toshimichi is assassinated by Shishio's underling Seta Sōjirō. On the road, Kenshin meets Makimachi Misao, an aspiring ninja, and defends a village from Shishio's men, revealing his past as the assassin Hitokiri Battōsai. Brought before Shishio, he duels Sōjirō, who breaks Kenshin's reverse-blade sword.

In Kyoto, Kenshin stays at an inn run by Okina, a semi-retired ninja of the Oniwabanshū, who warns him that Shinomori Aoshi, who has already beaten Sanosuke in Tokyo, is determined to kill him. Kaoru, Yahiko and Sanosuke follow Kenshin to Kyoto. The swordsmith who made his blade has died, but his son Seikū gives Kenshin a twin of the old sword after Kenshin defeats Shishio's warrior Sawagejō Chō, who had kidnapped Seikū's baby. Learning that Shishio plans to burn Kyoto that night, the police, Kenshin, the ninja and his friends fight Shishio's forces, while Okina is defeated in a duel with his former pupil Aoshi. Kenshin realizes the attack on Kyoto is a diversion and that Shishio actually plans to set Tokyo ablaze. He pursues Sōjirō, who has kidnapped Kaoru, to Shishio's departing ship and battles Shishio until Kaoru is thrown overboard and he leaps into the sea after her. A mysterious man later finds Kenshin unconscious on a beach and carries him away.

Shot across Japan with more than 5,000 extras, the film was released by Warner Bros. Pictures Japan on August 1, 2014. It was the third highest-grossing film of 2014 in Japan, earning ¥5.22 billion, and critics praised its action and Kenji Tanigaki's fight choreography. The Legend Ends followed a month later.

overview: Kit, a troubled girl, is sent to the exclusive Blackwood boarding school, where she discovers that only four other female students have been admitted to learn the four pillars of knowledge under the ominous wing of the mysterious headmistress Madame Duret.
tagline: Welcome to Blackwood. Where lost girls find their way.
title: Down a Dark Hall
plot:
Down a Dark Hall is a psychological thriller that delves into the complexities of adolescent relationships and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy. The film follows two teenage girls, Pim (Hannah John-Kamen) and Amy (Sophie Skinner), who are sent to a mysterious boarding school called Blackwood House, rumored for its dark history.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the true horror lies not in the supernatural forces that seem to be at work, but rather in the toxic dynamics between the girls and the adults around them. The film expertly explores themes of trauma, mental health, and the struggles of growing up, particularly for young women who are often expected to conform to societal norms.

The movie also touches on the idea of female friendship and the ways in which these relationships can be both a source of support and a catalyst for pain. Pim and Amy's bond is complex and multifaceted, reflecting the messy and often fraught nature of female relationships.

Throughout the film, the director uses atmospheric tension and visual metaphors to convey the sense of unease and disorientation that pervades Blackwood House. The result is a thought-provoking and unsettling exploration of the darker aspects of adolescence, one that lingers long after the credits roll.

overview: On the first night of spring, the Super Monsters gather for food, fun and games in the park -- and get to meet their adorable new pets!
title: Super Monsters Furever Friends
plot:
Super Monsters Furever Friends is an animated film that revolves around the adventures of a group of monster friends who learn valuable lessons about friendship, love, and acceptance. The movie primarily focuses on the theme of family and the importance of embracing one's uniqueness.

The story centers around the main character, Leif, who struggles to find his place among his peers due to his differences. However, with the help of his monster friends, he learns to accept himself and finds a sense of belonging. The film showcases how these monsters come together to form an unbreakable bond, demonstrating that true friendship can conquer even the most daunting challenges.

The movie also explores the theme of love and acceptance, particularly in the context of Leif's journey to find his forever home with his monster family. Through his experiences, the film conveys a powerful message about the importance of embracing diversity and promoting inclusivity.

Overall, Super Monsters Furever Friends is a heartwarming tale that celebrates the beauty of individuality and the power of friendship in overcoming adversity.

overview: For one month every year, five highly competitive friends hit the ground running in a no-holds-barred game of tag they’ve been playing since the first grade. This year, the game coincides with the wedding of their only undefeated player, which should finally make him an easy target. But he knows they’re coming...and he’s ready.
tagline: Based on a true story. We’re not kidding.
title: Tag
plot:
Tag is a 2018 American comedy film directed by Jeff Tomsic and written by Rob McKittrick, Jim Strouse, and Brian Burns. The movie stars Ed Helms, Jake Johnson, Hannibal Buress, Leslie Mann, and Rashida Jones.

The story revolves around five friends - Jason (Ed Helms), Kevin (Jake Johnson), Randy (Hannibal Buress), Bob (Leslie Mann's husband, who is not in the film but his character is mentioned), and Marnie (Rashida Jones) - who have been friends since childhood. The movie takes place over a period of 30 years, from their high school days to their mid-40s.

The plot begins with Jason, Kevin, Randy, Bob, and Marnie as high school students, where they make a pact that if one of them dies before the others, the remaining friends will find out who is next. The group makes this promise on Halloween night in 1985, and it becomes a recurring theme throughout their lives.

As the years pass, the friends go their separate ways - Jason gets married to Marnie, Kevin stays single, Randy marries Bob's sister, and Bob has an affair with a woman who is not his wife. Despite their individual successes and failures, they always keep in touch and maintain their friendship.

The movie takes a dramatic turn when Randy dies suddenly at the age of 40. The remaining friends are shocked and devastated by his death, but they also realize that they have to find out who is next on the list. They start investigating Randy's life, looking for clues that might reveal who will be the next to die.

As they dig deeper, they uncover secrets about their friend's past, including a mysterious woman who was involved in Randy's life before he died. The friends also realize that Randy's death may not have been an accident, and they start to suspect foul play.

Throughout the movie, the friends face various challenges and obstacles as they try to unravel the mystery of Randy's death. Along the way, they also confront their own personal demons and learn more about each other's lives.

In the end, the friends finally discover who is next on the list - Jason. However, instead of killing themselves, Jason decides to take a different approach. He realizes that his life has been defined by this pact with his friends, and he wants to break free from it. The movie ends with Jason making a bold decision that will change the course of his life forever.

Overall, Tag is a heartwarming and hilarious comedy that explores the complexities of male friendship and the power of human connection. With its witty dialogue, relatable characters, and unexpected twists, the movie is sure to delight audiences of all ages.

overview: In a world where monster wrestling is a global sport and monsters are superstar athletes, teenage Winnie seeks to follow in her father’s footsteps by coaching a loveable underdog monster into a champion.
tagline: The biggest underdog story ever.
title: Rumble
plot:
Rumble is a 2021 American animated sports comedy film directed by Hamish Grieve, in his directorial debut, and written by Grieve and Matt Lieberman. Loosely based on Rob Harrell's 2013 graphic novel Monster on the Hill, it features the voices of Will Arnett, Geraldine Viswanathan and Terry Crews, alongside Becky Lynch, Roman Reigns, Ben Schwartz, Jimmy Tatro and Stephen A. Smith.

Monster wrestling is a global sport, and every town has its own giant monster champion. When Tentacular, the shark-like octopus who wrestles for the town of Stoker, wins the world title by beating King Gorge, he announces that he will now represent the town of Slitherpoole. Without a new wrestler, Stoker will lose its stadium and the income it brings. Wrestling enthusiast Winnie Coyle sets out to find one and discovers Rayburn Jr., son of the late world champion Rayburn Sr., fighting in an underground arena as "Steve the Stupendous". Her interference makes him win a bout he was meant to throw, angering the arena's boss, Lady Mayhem, who demands that he repay her losses. Winnie offers to train him for official matches so he can earn the money, and he reluctantly agrees.

Rayburn Jr. has little interest in learning to fight and wins his first bout simply by dodging. He admits that he left Stoker because he could not live up to his father's name. Discovering his love of salsa dancing, Winnie builds his training around dance moves, and he climbs the rankings. Tentacular and his agent then buy Stoker's stadium, planning to demolish it because it reminds Tentacular that he will always be compared with Rayburn Sr. Although Rayburn Jr. has paid off Lady Mayhem, he stays to help Winnie, reveals his identity and challenges Tentacular for the stadium. After being countered in the early rounds, he finds success with his dance moves, and following Winnie's advice he sticks Tentacular to a corner post with his own suckers. Both monsters are knocked out in a collision, but the crowd revives Rayburn Jr. by clapping a salsa rhythm, and he defeats Tentacular to become world champion and save the stadium.

Developed by Reel FX with Paramount Animation and Walden Media, the film was repeatedly delayed, partly by the COVID-19 pandemic, before premiering on December 15, 2021, as a Paramount+ exclusive. Reviews were mixed, with 47% on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 48.

overview: Agent Matt Graver teams up with operative Alejandro Gillick to prevent Mexican drug cartels from smuggling terrorists across the United States border.
tagline: No rules this time
title: Sicario: Day of the Soldado
plot:
Sicario: Day of the Soldado, also known as Sicario 2: Soldado, is a 2018 American action crime thriller directed by Stefano Sollima and written by Taylor Sheridan. A sequel to Sicario (2015), it sees Benicio del Toro, Josh Brolin, Jeffrey Donovan and Raoul Trujillo reprise their roles, with Isabela Merced, Manuel Garcia-Rulfo and Catherine Keener joining the cast.

After an ISIS suicide bombing kills fifteen people in a Kansas City grocery store, the government authorizes CIA officer Matt Graver to take extreme action against Mexican cartels suspected of smuggling the bombers across the border. Graver and the Department of Defense decide to ignite a war between the cartels, and he recruits operative Alejandro Gillick, using a private military contractor for deniability. Gillick assassinates a Matamoros cartel lawyer in Mexico City, while Graver's team kidnaps Isabel Reyes, daughter of rival Sonoran kingpin Carlos Reyes, in a false flag operation, then stages a DEA rescue in Texas. As they return her to Mexico, their corrupt police escort turns on them, and the Americans kill 25 Mexican police officers in the firefight. Isabel, suspecting the truth, flees into the desert, and Gillick follows her.

When investigators find that at least two of the bombers were domestic terrorists, the Secretary of Defense abandons the mission and orders Isabel and Gillick killed to hide American involvement. Gillick refuses and goes rogue to protect her, and the two pose as migrants and pay smugglers to cross into the U.S. At the border, Miguel, a young Mexican American recruited by the traffickers, recognizes Gillick from an earlier encounter, and the gang seizes them. As an initiation, Miguel is made to shoot the hooded Gillick in the head. Graver's team, having watched by satellite, wipes out the gang and, defying orders, takes Isabel to the U.S. to enter witness protection. Gillick, shot only through the cheek, survives and kills his pursuers. A year later, a heavily tattooed Miguel goes to meet his gang contact and finds Gillick waiting, ready to discuss his future as a sicario.

Sony Pictures Releasing distributed the film in North America from June 29, 2018, with Lionsgate handling most international markets; it is dedicated to the first film's composer, Jóhann Jóhannsson. It grossed $75.8 million worldwide. Critics found it less subversive than its predecessor but a stylish thriller, giving it 62% on Rotten Tomatoes and 61 on Metacritic.

overview: The story follows the adventures of Aang, a young successor to a long line of Avatars, who must put his childhood ways aside and stop the Fire Nation from enslaving the Water, Earth and Air nations.
tagline: Four nations, one destiny.
title: The Last Airbender
plot:
The Last Airbender is a 2010 American fantasy action-adventure film written and directed by M. Night Shyamalan, based on the first season of the animated series Avatar: The Last Airbender. Noah Ringer stars as Aang, with Nicola Peltz as Katara, Jackson Rathbone as Sokka, Dev Patel as Prince Zuko, Shaun Toub as Iroh, Aasif Mandvi as Commander Zhao and Cliff Curtis as Fire Lord Ozai.

For a century, the Fire Nation has waged war on the Air Nomads, the Water Tribes and the Earth Kingdom. In the Southern Water Tribe, the siblings Katara and Sokka break open an iceberg and free a twelve-year-old boy, Aang, and his flying bison Appa. The exiled Fire Nation prince Zuko sees the burst of light and arrives demanding the Avatar, the only person who can "bend" all four elements. Aang surrenders to protect the village but escapes. At the Southern Air Temple he learns he has been frozen for a hundred years and that the Fire Nation has wiped out his people, including his mentor Monk Gyatso. His grief sends him into the Avatar State, where he meets a Dragon Spirit. After freeing an occupied Earth Kingdom village, Aang admits he has mastered only airbending, and the group heads north so he can learn waterbending.

Aang is captured by Commander Zhao but rescued by the masked Blue Spirit, who turns out to be Zuko. Zuko survives Zhao's attempt on his life. At the Northern Water Tribe, Master Pakku teaches Aang and Katara, until the Fire Nation attacks. Zuko captures Aang, who returns to the Avatar State and receives the Dragon Spirit's advice to show the power of water. Katara freezes Zuko in ice. Zhao kills the Moon Spirit to rob the waterbenders of their power, but Iroh drives him away, and Princess Yue gives her life to restore the spirit. Zhao is drowned by waterbenders, and Aang raises the ocean into a towering wall that drives back the Fire Nation fleet. Fire Lord Ozai orders his daughter Azula to stop the Avatar before Sozin's Comet returns.

Filmed in Greenland and Pennsylvania in 2009, the film drew protests over the casting of white actors as characters from Asian- and Native-influenced cultures. Paramount released it on July 1, 2010. It grossed about $319.7 million worldwide but was almost universally panned for its script, acting, effects and 3D conversion. Rotten Tomatoes reported just 5% approval, the lowest for any Nickelodeon Movies production. Roger Ebert gave it half a star. It won five Golden Raspberry Awards, including Worst Picture and Worst Director.

overview: Carrie White, a shy and troubled teenage girl who is tormented by her high school peers and her fanatically religious mother, begins to use her powers of telekinesis to exact revenge upon them.
tagline: If you've got a taste for terror… take Carrie to the prom!
title: Carrie
plot:
Carrie is a 1976 American supernatural horror film directed by Brian De Palma, based on the 1974 novel of the same name by Stephen King.

The story begins with Margaret White (Piper Laurie), a devout and isolated mother who has been ostracized by her community due to her extreme Christian fundamentalism. She lives with her daughter Carrie (Sissy Spacek) in a small farmhouse on the outskirts of town, where she subjects Carrie to a strict and abusive upbringing.

As Carrie grows older, she begins to experience strange and terrifying events, including telekinetic powers that she struggles to control. Despite her mother's attempts to suppress her emotions and desires, Carrie becomes increasingly isolated and withdrawn, feeling like an outcast among her peers.

At school, Carrie is bullied by a group of girls led by Chris Hargensen (Nancy Allen), who take great pleasure in tormenting her. However, when Chris and her friends play a cruel prank on Carrie during the school's annual prom, something snaps inside Carrie. She unleashes her telekinetic powers, causing chaos and destruction throughout the school.

As the events of the prom unfold, it becomes clear that Carrie is not just a victim of bullying, but also a symbol of female empowerment and rebellion against the patriarchal society that has oppressed her for so long. Her powers grow stronger with each passing moment, and she begins to exact revenge on those who have wronged her.

In the climactic final scene, Carrie's telekinetic abilities reach new heights as she destroys the school and kills many of her tormentors. However, in a shocking twist, it is revealed that Carrie's mother has been hiding a dark secret: Margaret White was once a prom queen herself, but her own desires and ambitions were crushed by her father.

As the film ends, Carrie stands alone, her powers still raging out of control. It is unclear whether she will be able to find peace or continue down a path of destruction and chaos. The final shot of the film shows Carrie walking away from the carnage, a symbol of both vulnerability and resilience in the face of adversity.

Throughout the film, De Palma's direction and King's novel provide a commentary on themes such as female empowerment, isolation, and the dangers of patriarchal societies that suppress women's desires and ambitions. The film's use of suspense, tension, and graphic violence has become iconic in horror cinema, and its influence can still be seen in many modern films and TV shows.

Overall, Carrie is a powerful and thought-provoking film that explores the complexities of female identity and the dangers of unchecked power. Its enduring popularity is a testament to its ability to captivate audiences with its suspenseful plot and memorable characters.

overview: On the night of the discovery of a duplicate Earth in the Solar system, an ambitious young student and an accomplished composer cross paths in a tragic accident.
title: Another Earth
plot:
Another Earth is a 2011 science fiction film directed by Mike Cahill and written by Brit Marling and Zal Batmanglij. The movie premiered at Sundance Film Festival in 2011.

The main themes of Another Earth include:

1. **Existentialism**: The film explores the idea that we are not alone in the universe, but this realization raises more questions about our place in the cosmos and the meaning of life.
2. **Identity**: The protagonist, Rhoda (Brit Marling), struggles to find her identity and sense of purpose after discovering a duplicate Earth orbiting the Sun. This duplicate Earth serves as a symbol for the multiple versions of ourselves that we can be.
3. **Human Connection**: The movie highlights the importance of human relationships and connections in our lives. Rhoda's journey is motivated by her desire to find her doppelganger, which represents a longing for connection and understanding with someone who shares her experiences.
4. **Science vs. Faith**: Another Earth raises questions about the role of science and faith in our understanding of the universe. The duplicate Earth serves as a metaphor for the unknown and the unknowable aspects of existence.
5. **Self-Discovery**: Throughout the film, Rhoda undergoes a journey of self-discovery, confronting her past mistakes and fears to find a new sense of purpose and belonging.

The movie's themes are woven throughout its narrative, which follows Rhoda as she navigates her relationships with her doppelganger (Justine) and her own life. The film's exploration of these themes adds depth and complexity to the story, making it more than just a simple science fiction tale.

Overall, Another Earth is a thought-provoking film that challenges viewers to consider their place in the universe and the importance of human connection in our lives.

original_title: Scooby-Doo! and the Loch Ness Monster
overview: While the gang travel to Scotland to visit Daphne's cousin and witness the Highland Games, they find themselves terrorized by the legendary Loch Ness Monster.
title: Scooby-Doo! and the Loch Ness Monster
plot:
Scooby-Doo! and the Loch Ness Monster is a 2004 animated mystery comedy film based on the popular Scooby-Doo franchise. The movie follows the Mystery Inc. gang as they travel to Scotland, where they become embroiled in a mystery surrounding the legendary Loch Ness Monster.

The main themes of the movie include:

1. Friendship and teamwork: The Mystery Inc. gang works together to solve the mystery, using their unique skills and strengths to overcome obstacles and uncover clues.
2. Skepticism vs. superstition: The film pokes fun at the idea of supernatural creatures like the Loch Ness Monster, while also acknowledging the power of human imagination and the importance of considering alternative explanations for mysterious events.
3. Cultural exchange and appreciation: The movie features a Scottish setting and incorporates elements of Scottish culture, highlighting the gang's curiosity and enthusiasm for learning about new places and traditions.
4. Mystery and suspense: The film's central plot revolves around the mystery of the Loch Ness Monster, keeping viewers engaged and guessing until the very end.

The story begins with the Mystery Inc. gang arriving in Scotland, where they meet a local woman named Morven, who claims to have seen the Loch Ness Monster. As they investigate, they uncover a series of clues that suggest the monster may be real, but also begin to suspect that there may be a more human explanation for the sightings.

Throughout the movie, the gang encounters various obstacles and challenges as they try to solve the mystery, including treacherous terrain, suspicious locals, and even a rival treasure hunter. Along the way, they learn valuable lessons about teamwork, perseverance, and the importance of considering multiple perspectives.

In the end, the Mystery Inc. gang uncovers the truth behind the Loch Ness Monster, revealing a surprising twist that challenges their initial assumptions. The movie concludes with the gang reflecting on what they've learned and how it has brought them closer together as friends.

Overall, Scooby-Doo! and the Loch Ness Monster is a fun and entertaining mystery comedy that explores themes of friendship, skepticism, and cultural exchange, all set against the iconic backdrop of Scotland's famous loch.

overview: When a master thief is sabotaged during a bank heist and left for dead, he seeks revenge on his former crew one target at a time. Now, with the cops and the mob closing in, he's in the race of his life to reclaim an untold fortune in cryptocurrency from those who double-crossed him.
tagline: Be careful who you betray.
title: Blowback
plot:
Blowback is a 2022 American action crime thriller film directed by Tibor Takács from a screenplay credited to Matthew Eason, Robert Giardina and Robert Edward Thomas. Produced by Premiere Entertainment Group and distributed by Saban Films, it stars Cam Gigandet as a thief seeking revenge on the crew that betrayed him, with Randy Couture, Michele Plaia, Louis Mandylor, William McNamara, Benjamin Abiola, Rafael Cabrera, Chris Maher and Texas Battle in supporting roles. Set in Las Vegas, the film was released in June 2022. It is rated R for violence, drug use and language and runs 93 minutes.

Nick (Gigandet), a rideshare driver, has a teenage daughter (Melissa Diaz) who is gravely ill in hospital, and whose only chance of survival is an experimental treatment that his insurance and meagre earnings cannot cover. Through a contact at a bank, he learns of a valuable delivery and plans an inside job. He reconnects with his former girlfriend Veronica (Plaia), whose boyfriend Jack (Couture), the main investor in her gym and a hardened criminal, connects him with a crew of thieves; with his tech-savvy friend Xander (Abiola) also on board, the group is told to stick to the plan and that nobody will get hurt. The robbery goes largely as planned, but afterwards Jack's men shoot Nick, leave him for dead and take the stolen case, which holds hard drives containing millions of dollars in cryptocurrency. Patched up by a disgraced, drug-addicted doctor (McNamara) living in an RV, Nick sets out to recover the fortune and take revenge on his former crew one target at a time, enlisting the help of the mobster who owns the case, while Detective Cooper (Mandylor) leads a police investigation that keeps closing in on the trail of violence.

Reviews were generally negative. Roger Moore of Movie Nation found it a routine, bloody and slow-footed cops-and-robbers tale whose cryptocurrency angle threatened to date it instantly; he thought the leads were not bad but that the script was fatally flawed, particularly in handing Nick a "gangster ex machina" who solves his problems for him. Peter Gray of The AU Review called it a generic, disposable heist film that hit every expected beat yet had an odd watchability, largely thanks to Gigandet's sympathetic performance. Mark Dujsik of Mark Reviews Movies wrote that it consisted almost entirely of plot, with characters too thin even to count as archetypes.

overview: When history’s greatest aquatic predator returns, the armada of modern warships sent to destroy it has no chance at all.
tagline: Too big to fail.
title: Megalodon Rising
plot:
Megalodon Rising is a 2021 American action and science fiction creature film directed by Brian Nowak and produced by The Asylum as a sequel to its 2018 film Megalodon, once again trading on the popularity of the studio blockbuster The Meg. Tom Sizemore receives top billing as Commander Moore, although he appears only briefly in his office, while the lead role of Captain Emily Lynch, sister of the commander from the first film, is played by Wynter Eddins. The cast also includes O'Shay Neal as Lieutenant Commander Ahearn, Freda Yifan Jing as Dr. Lee, Zhan Wang as Captain Ping, Lisa Lee as Tuan and Chris Grant Wenchell as Samperio.

After a Chinese warship enters American waters while relaying classified US government information to a satellite, it is attacked and sunk by a megalodon. Nearby, an American warship commanded by Lynch is on patrol; Lynch is troubled because her sister faces a court-martial for allegedly sinking her own ship on purpose, and her claim that a giant shark was responsible has been dismissed as a lie. The crew recovers Dr. Lee, a scientist who survived the sinking in a life raft, and another Chinese warship under Captain Ping demands her return, threatening to treat a refusal as an act of war, with the crewmember Tuan acting as interpreter.

Tensions rise when three megalodons attack the Chinese ship and then the American vessel, leading Ping to suspect the Americans can control the sharks. When gunner Samperio kills one of the creatures, the others feed on it, allowing the ships to escape. Lynch contacts Moore, and the sharks head for a crowded beach in San Diego, where troops are sent to defend the coast; Dr. Lee and the radio operator Wilco lure them away by imitating the satellite signal. Returning to sea, the sharks sink the Chinese reinforcements one by one. The Americans rescue the Chinese survivors, kill a second shark with their guns, and Lynch makes peace with Ping before the two crews kill the last one together, although Wilco dies. Lynch publicly announces the attacks and the new alliance with China, but a final sonar reading reveals two more objects in the ocean.

Because of COVID-19 restrictions, the film used very few extras, and the sharks and many warship shots were created with CGI. German critics dismissed its effects, dialogue and characters, finding little to recommend beyond the sharks themselves.

overview: When Sara, a young design student from Iowa, arrives for college in Los Angeles, she is eager to fit in and get to know the big city. Her wealthy roommate, Rebecca, is more than eager to take Sara under her wing and show her the ropes. The two become close, but when Sara begins to branch out and make more friends on campus, Rebecca becomes resentful. Alarmed, Sara moves in with her new boyfriend, causing Rebecca's behavior to take a violent turn.
tagline: 2,000 colleges. 8 million roommates. Which one will you get?
title: The Roommate
plot:
The Roommate is a psychological thriller that delves into the darker aspects of human relationships and the blurred lines between friendship and obsession. The film follows Jules (Leighton Meester) as she moves in with her new roommate, Rebecca (Minka Kelly), who seems perfect at first but slowly reveals her true nature.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Rebecca's behavior is a manifestation of her own insecurities and emotional trauma, which she attempts to alleviate by manipulating those around her. The film expertly explores the theme of toxic relationships, where one person's need for control and validation can lead to devastating consequences.

The Roommate also touches on the idea of identity and how people present themselves to others. Rebecca's carefully crafted facade is slowly stripped away, revealing a complex web of emotions and insecurities that threaten to destroy her relationships with those around her.

Throughout the film, the tension builds as Jules becomes increasingly entangled in Rebecca's web of deceit, forcing her to confront the darker aspects of their relationship. The Roommate ultimately becomes a cautionary tale about the dangers of getting too close to someone who may not be what they seem, and the devastating consequences that can result from such an association.

The film's exploration of these themes is both thought-provoking and unsettling, making for a gripping and suspenseful viewing experience.

original_title: バースデー・ワンダーランド
overview: The story follows Akane, a girl with no self-confidence. On the day before her birthday, she meets a mysterious alchemist, Hippocrates, and his student, Pipo, who both tell her they're on a mission to save the world. Together, they set out from the basement for "Wonderland," and Akane finds herself labelled Wonderland's savior.
tagline: Today is your special day, but you are special every day.
title: The Wonderland
plot:
The Wonderland, released in Japan and the United Kingdom as Birthday Wonderland, is a 2019 Japanese animated coming-of-age fantasy adventure film directed by Keiichi Hara from a screenplay by Miho Maruo. It adapts Sachiko Kashiwaba's 1988 children's story Chikashitsu Kara no Fushigi na Tabi (Strange Journey from the Basement), with character designs by the illustrator Ilya Kuvshinov. Distributed by Warner Bros. Japan, it opened on 26 April 2019, as the last Japanese film released in the Heisei era, and was screened in competition at the Annecy International Animation Film Festival that June. The voice cast includes Mayu Matsuoka as Akane, Anne Watanabe as Chii, Kumiko Aso as Midori, Nao Tōyama as Pipo, Keiji Fujiwara as Zan Gu and Masachika Ichimura as Hippocrates.

Akane is a girl with no self-confidence. On the day before her birthday, her mother Midori sends her to collect her present from her aunt Chii, an outgoing antiques dealer whose boldness contrasts with Akane's timidity. At the shop they meet the mysterious alchemist Hippocrates and his tiny apprentice Pipo, who say they are on a mission to save their world. Through a passage from the basement they travel to Wonderland, a kingdom threatened by drought, where Akane is hailed as the Goddess of the Green Wind, the only one who can save it by helping the ailing crown prince of the rain kings perform the ceremony that renews the realm's water once every 600 years. A talisman that pulls her forward whenever she turns negative drags the reluctant Akane along. On the road the travellers clash with the menacing iron man Zan Gu and his sorcerer's apprentice, who are plotting to destroy the entrance to the great well, and Hippocrates is turned into a fly. In the capital, Akane learns that Zan Gu is in fact the prince himself, transformed after he grew afraid of his heavy responsibilities. Finding the courage to reach him, she embraces him, restoring his human form, and helps him perform the ceremony, which brings the water back to the kingdom. Returning home, where only hours have passed, Akane celebrates her birthday with new self-assurance.

Critics praised the visuals but found the story uneven. Matt Schley of The Japan Times gave it three out of five stars, judging that it pushes the Miyazaki buttons successfully on the surface but lacks a deeper emotional core, and Allan Hunter of Screen Daily felt that its overly busy story plays like a string of set pieces rather than building dramatic momentum.

overview: A loving father finds a clown suit for his son's birthday party, only to realize the suit is part of an evil curse that turns its wearer into a killer.
tagline: The kids aren't alright.
title: Clown
plot:
Clown is a 2014 American horror film directed by Jon Watts and written by Geoffrey Thurlow. The movie follows a young boy named Samson (played by Dylan Minnette) who, after being bullied at school, discovers that his father's old clown costume has been stolen.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the clown is not just any ordinary clown, but a malevolent entity with a twisted and sadistic personality. The main themes of Clown include:

1. **Childhood trauma and bullying**: Samson's experiences as a bullied child are expertly woven throughout the narrative, making his eventual descent into madness all the more believable and disturbing.
2. **The dangers of obsession**: The clown's fixation on Samson is a metaphor for the destructive power of obsession, highlighting how an all-consuming desire can lead to chaos and destruction.
3. **The blurring of reality and fantasy**: As the story progresses, it becomes increasingly difficult to distinguish between what's real and what's just Samson's imagination. This theme adds to the sense of unease and uncertainty that permeates the film.
4. **The consequences of revenge**: The clown's actions are motivated by a desire for revenge against those who have wronged him in the past, serving as a cautionary tale about the destructive nature of seeking vengeance.

Throughout the movie, Watts expertly builds tension and suspense, creating a sense of unease that culminates in a shocking and disturbing climax. The film's themes are thought-provoking and unsettling, making Clown a standout horror film of its era.

overview: Left heartbroken after Romeo begins to pursue her cousin Juliet, Rosaline schemes to foil the famous romance and win back her guy in this comedic twist of Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet.
tagline: The love story you know, the ex you don’t.
title: Rosaline
plot:
Rosaline is an American romantic comedy of 2022 directed by Karen Maine and written by Scott Neustadter and Michael H. Weber, adapted from Rebecca Serle's young adult novel When You Were Mine (2012), itself a riff on Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet. Kaitlyn Dever stars as Rosaline, Romeo's spurned love, with Isabela Merced as Juliet, Kyle Allen as Romeo, Sean Teale as the suitor Dario Penza, Minnie Driver as the Nurse, Bradley Whitford as Rosaline's father and Christopher McDonald as Lord Capulet.

Rosaline, a free-spirited member of the house of Capulet, has been secretly seeing Romeo, a Montague, and plans to meet him at the Capulet masquerade. Instead, an outing with Dario, a suitor chosen by her father, leaves them stranded on a boat in a storm, and she rudely rebuffs him. At the ball, Romeo meets and falls for her cousin Juliet. Discovering his new romance, Rosaline sets out to sabotage it, telling Juliet that Romeo courts many women, dragging her to a seedy tavern to meet other men and stealing Romeo's letters. Juliet sends Romeo away, but realises her cousin's deception when she sees Rosaline's necklace engraved with her and Romeo's names. Rosaline then persuades her friend Count Paris, who wants to hide his homosexuality, to court Juliet, and the Capulets eagerly approve.

Learning that Romeo plans to elope with Juliet, Rosaline reluctantly accepts Dario's escort to break into the Montague estate at night; Dario fights off the guards, but they arrive too late to stop the secret wedding. Rosaline's feelings for Dario soften just as he announces he is rejoining the navy. When Tybalt intercepts the letters Rosaline returns to Juliet, he duels Romeo and is killed, and the two families declare war. Rosaline apologises to Dario and asks him to smuggle the lovers away on his boat, but Juliet has already taken a potion to feign death. In the tomb, Rosaline finds Romeo alive, since Dario has told him of the ruse, and has him pretend to be dead too, then scolds the feuding families into reconciling. Rosaline and Dario see the couple off by boat and share a kiss, while a mid-credits scene shows Romeo and Juliet struggling to find anything in common.

After a premiere at the El Capitan Theatre on 6 October 2022, Rosaline was released on Hulu in the United States and on Disney+ abroad on 14 October. Critics praised Dever's performance, giving it 75% on Rotten Tomatoes.

overview: Responding to an urgent call for help, a police officer becomes trapped by the evil spirits of a cursed house.
title: La Casa
plot:
La Casa (The House) is a 2020 Chilean horror film directed by Jorge Olguín, the Chilean filmmaker who has devoted more of his career to horror and fantasy than any other in his country, known for films such as Ángel Negro (2000) and Caleuche: el llamado del mar (2012). It was his sixth feature. The film stars Gabriel Cañas as Corporal Arriagada, a carabinero, with Camila Carreño, Carol Campos, Carlos Cortez and Felipe Silva Rodríguez in the cast. It runs about 73 minutes and opened in Chilean cinemas on 30 January 2020.

The film is inspired by the urban legend surrounding the Casona Dubois in the Santiago district of Quinta Normal, now a cultural centre, where most of it was shot. According to the legend, a French engineer and his wife who settled there in the early twentieth century turned to witchcraft to conceive a child; the baby was born deformed, the father killed it and the mother took her own life, and the house has been considered cursed ever since. Title cards at the start inform the audience of this history. The story is set in 1986, during the military dictatorship. In the middle of the night Arriagada receives an urgent call: neighbours report someone inside the old mansion, crying for help. Arriagada, who that same day has committed an atrocity of his own by beating a woman labelled a subversive to death, goes to investigate, calling for reinforcements that will take time to arrive. Once inside he cannot find his way out, and the violent spirits of the family begin to torment him, including a bloodied woman who appears and vanishes, until a final twist ties the haunting to his own guilt and to the repression of the regime. Olguín shot the film quickly as an apparent single real-time take, following Cañas through the dark, labyrinthine house lit largely by his flashlight, with only a handful of actors inside the mansion.

Olguín described the film as "a great lie to tell a great truth." Reception was mixed. Patricia Reyes of La Tercera highlighted its sound design and its blend of the political context with horror, and Edgardo Viereck Salinas of Cine y Literatura considered it the director's best work, a powerful portrait of guilt under Pinochet. Reid Ramsey of Cinematary praised Cañas's physically demanding performance and the practical effects but found the scares repetitive and the concept better suited to a short film.

overview: A documentary on Al Gore's campaign to make the issue of global warming a recognized problem worldwide.
tagline: By far the most terrifying film you will ever see.
title: An Inconvenient Truth
plot:
An Inconvenient Truth is an American documentary of 2006 directed by Davis Guggenheim that follows former United States vice president Al Gore's campaign to educate the public about global warming. Built around the illustrated lecture Gore estimates he has given more than a thousand times around the world, it was produced by Laurie David, who was inspired after seeing his presentation at a town hall meeting with Lawrence Bender.

Gore, who began giving the talk in 1989 with flip charts and now uses a computer slide show, opens with his familiar joke that he "used to be the next president of the United States." He admits he feels he has so far failed to get his message across. The lecture combines detailed graphs, charts and striking images, beginning with photographs of Earth taken from space, such as Earthrise and The Blue Marble, which he credits with helping to spark the modern environmental movement. Interwoven are personal episodes that shaped his concerns: his studies at Harvard under the early climate scientist Roger Revelle, the death of his sister from lung cancer, his young son's near-fatal car accident and his defeat in the 2000 presidential election, which he calls a hard blow that sharpened his sense of mission. A clip from the animated series Futurama provides a comic explanation of the greenhouse effect.

Gore presents the scientific consensus on climate change and argues that it is a moral rather than a political issue. He shows Antarctic ice-core data indicating that carbon dioxide levels are higher than at any point in the past 650,000 years, and documents retreating glaciers around the world. He warns that the collapse of the ice sheets of Greenland or West Antarctica could raise sea levels by about 20 feet, flooding coastlines and creating some 100 million refugees, and that meltwater from Greenland could disrupt the ocean currents that keep northern Europe warm. Segments rebut critics who call warming unproven or trivial, as Gore urges deep cuts in emissions.

After premiering at the 2006 Sundance Film Festival, the film opened in New York and Los Angeles on 24 May 2006 and grossed about $50 million worldwide, among the top-grossing documentaries in the United States. Rated 93% on Rotten Tomatoes, it won two Oscars, for Best Documentary Feature and for Melissa Etheridge's song "I Need to Wake Up". In 2007 Gore shared the Nobel Peace Prize with the IPCC.

overview: Lucas is a young man who lives with his religious aunt Lourdes in a quiet country town. He helps his aunt by holding religious meetings with the ladies of the area, in the living room, playing biblical songs on the keyboard. This quiet life will end as soon as the charitable aunt communicates the arrival of another nephew, Mario, just out of jail. The clash of reality between the cousins ends up causing unusual situations, and an unexpected attraction among the boys.
title: Cousins
plot:
Cousins (Portuguese: Primos) is a 2019 Brazilian romantic comedy-drama written by Thiago Cazado and co-directed by Cazado and Mauro Carvalho. It was Cazado's second feature after About Us, and he also plays one of the two leads, Mario Hantz, opposite Paulo Sousa as Lucas Hantz. The cast also includes Juliana Zancanaro as Aunt Lourdes, Duda Esteves as Julia and Denis Camargo as Emilio. The film was produced by MACA Entretenimento and runs 83 minutes.

Lucas is a reserved young man who lives with his charitable, deeply religious Aunt Lourdes in a quiet country town. He helps her by playing hymns on his keyboard at the religious meetings she holds in the living room with the local ladies, and he gives music lessons to an eccentric young woman whose increasingly inappropriate advances he has to fend off. His tranquil routine is upended when Lourdes announces the arrival of another nephew he barely knows, Mario, a distant cousin who has just spent a couple of weeks in jail over a mix-up and cannot return home because his abusive father has rejected him. Shortly before Mario arrives for what is meant to be a brief stay, Lourdes leaves on a trip, so the two young men are left alone and Lucas must share his bedroom with the newcomer. The contrast between the uninhibited, scrappy ex-prisoner and his repressed, closeted cousin produces comic situations, while playful flirting gradually builds into sexual tension and then a passionate romance. The story also mocks the hypocrisy of the town's devout churchgoers and homophobes, and the aunt turns out to have a few surprises of her own.

Cazado said he wanted to make a love story that defied moral standards but in a light way, something fun with a happy ending that would encourage audiences to believe they could love whom they want and be accepted by their families. The film was released in Brazil in 2019 and distributed on home video and on demand in the United Kingdom by TLA Releasing from December 2019. English-language reviewers were generally warm. Culture Fix praised the charming central performances, the uplifting tone and a satire of judgmental religion it likened to John Waters, while Derek Winnert gave it four stars, calling it sweet and good-natured and highlighting the chemistry between Cazado and Sousa as well as Zancanaro's performance as the drinking, smoking, swearing aunt. Some Brazilian critics, including Cinema com Rapadura, were harsher, describing it as a weak fable about overcoming prejudice.

overview: Noah spends the perfect first night with the girl of his dreams Avery but gets relegated to the friend zone. He spends the next three years wondering what went wrong - until he gets the unexpected chance to travel back in time and alter that night, and his fate, over and over again.
tagline: All he needs is a second chance... to be her first choice.
title: When We First Met
plot:
When We First Met is a romantic comedy-drama film that explores the complexities of love, relationships, and the human experience. The movie delves into the theme of nostalgia, revisiting past memories and experiences to understand how they have shaped us into who we are today.

The film also touches on the idea of regret and what could have been. The protagonist's journey is a poignant exploration of the "what ifs" that haunt us after a lost love. As he navigates his way through life, he grapples with the notion of whether it's possible to recapture the past or if it's forever lost in the sands of time.

Furthermore, When We First Met examines the concept of identity and how our experiences, both joyful and painful, contribute to who we are. The film's protagonist is on a quest to understand himself and his place in the world, which leads him down a path of self-discovery and introspection.

The movie also explores the idea of human connection and the power of relationships in shaping us. Through its portrayal of complex characters and their intricate web of emotions, When We First Met highlights the beauty and fragility of love and human connections.

Overall, When We First Met is a thoughtful and poignant exploration of the human experience, delving into themes that are both universally relatable and deeply personal.

overview: Bumbling supervillain Megamind finally defeats his nemesis, the superhero Metro Man. But without a hero, he loses all purpose and must find new meaning to his life.
tagline: His brain is off the chain.
title: Megamind
plot:
Megamind is a 2010 American animated superhero comedy film produced by DreamWorks Animation. The movie follows the story of Megamind, a supervillain who was created by the scientist Dr. Minion.

The film begins with the introduction of Metro Man, a powerful superhero who saves the city of Metro City from various villains and disasters. However, when Metro Man is killed by his arch-nemesis, Titan, Megamind sees an opportunity to become the greatest hero the world has ever known. He decides to take on the mantle of Metro Man and becomes a supervillain.

Megamind's plan is to kill Metro City's mayor, Roxanne Ritchi, who he believes will be the perfect target for his evil plans. However, things don't go as planned when Megamind discovers that Roxanne is not only alive but also intelligent and resourceful. Despite this, Megamind continues with his plan, using his advanced technology to create a massive robot to destroy the city.

As the story unfolds, we see glimpses of Megamind's troubled past, where he was created by Dr. Minion as part of an experiment to create the perfect supervillain. However, things didn't go as planned, and Megamind ended up being rejected by his creator. This rejection led to a deep-seated insecurity in Megamind, which drives him to seek validation through his evil deeds.

Meanwhile, Roxanne Ritchi is introduced as a brilliant and feisty journalist who is determined to uncover the truth behind Metro Man's death. She teams up with Hal Stewart, a bumbling but lovable cop who becomes her partner in solving the mystery of Metro Man's demise.

As Megamind continues his plan to destroy the city, Roxanne and Hal begin to close in on him. However, just as they think they have finally caught him, Megamind reveals that he has been playing a cat-and-mouse game with them all along. In a shocking twist, it is revealed that Titan, Metro Man's arch-nemesis, was actually the one who killed Metro Man.

In the end, Megamind and Roxanne team up to take down Titan, who has become increasingly unstable due to his own ego and desire for power. The movie culminates in an epic battle between Megamind, Roxanne, Hal, and Titan, with Megamind ultimately emerging victorious.

Throughout the film, we see a transformation in Megamind from a self-centered villain to a hero who has finally found redemption. With Roxanne by his side, Megamind learns to let go of his insecurities and find purpose beyond being a supervillain. The movie ends on a heartwarming note, with Megamind and Roxanne sharing a romantic moment as the city celebrates their victory over Titan.

Overall, Megamind is a hilarious and action-packed animated film that explores themes of identity, redemption, and the power of friendship. With its witty humor, lovable characters, and engaging storyline, it's no wonder why this movie has become a beloved classic among animation fans.

overview: Terminal Island, New York: 2020. Overcrowding in the US penal system has reached a breaking point. Prisons have been turned over to a monolithic Weyland Corporation, which sees jails full of thugs as an opportunity for televised sport. Adrenalized inmates, a global audience hungry for violence and a spectacular, enclosed arena come together to form the 'Death Race', the biggest, most brutal event.
tagline: Get ready for a killer race.
title: Death Race
plot:
Death Race is a 2008 science fiction action film directed by Paul W.S. Anderson, starring Jason Statham, Joan Allen, and Ian McShane.

In the year 2012, the United States has been transformed into a dystopian society where corporations have replaced governments. The tyrannical President John Spilner rules with an iron fist, and the poor are forced to live in poverty-stricken areas called "The Slums." To maintain control, Spilner creates a deadly game show called "Death Race," where prisoners are forced to compete in a high-stakes, televised event.

The main character, Jensen Ames (played by Jason Statham), is an ex-con who is sentenced to Death Race after being framed for a crime he didn't commit. In prison, Ames befriends the current champion of Death Race, Frankenstein (played by Joan Allen's character's husband, played by Ian McShane). However, when Ames is released from prison, he discovers that his wife has been killed in a brutal attack.

Ames' desire for revenge leads him to participate in Death Race, where he becomes the new favorite to win. With the help of his mechanic friend, Doc (played by John Leguizamo), Ames builds a customized car called the "Tyrant," which gives him an edge over the other competitors.

As the game progresses, Ames forms alliances with other prisoners and begins to uncover the dark secrets behind Death Race. He also discovers that President Spilner is using the show as a means to distract the population from his corrupt regime.

Throughout the film, Ames faces numerous challenges and obstacles, including treacherous terrain, deadly traps, and ruthless opponents. However, he remains determined to win and take down President Spilner.

In the climactic final showdown, Ames faces off against Frankenstein in a high-speed battle on the Death Race track. With his Tyrant car, Ames outmaneuvers Frankenstein and emerges victorious, killing her in the process.

With his victory, Ames is hailed as a hero by the people, and he becomes a symbol of resistance against President Spilner's regime. However, Ames' newfound fame comes with a price, as he realizes that he has become a pawn in a larger game.

The film ends with Ames driving away from the Death Race track, ready to take on his next challenge and continue his fight for justice.

overview: When a willful young man tries to venture beyond his sequestered Pennsylvania hamlet, his actions set off a chain of chilling incidents that will alter the community forever.
tagline: There is no turning back
title: The Village
plot:
The Village is a psychological horror-thriller film directed by M. Night Shyamalan, released in 2004 by Touchstone Pictures and Scott Rudin Productions.

The story takes place in the late 19th century in a small, isolated village surrounded by a dense forest in Pennsylvania. The villagers live in fear of the "wild" that exists outside their community, which is said to be inhabited by monstrous creatures. The villagers believe that if they venture too far from their village, they will be attacked and killed by these creatures.

The film follows the story of Lucy (Bryce Dallas Howard), a young woman who lives in the village with her brother, Seth (Joel Edgerton). Lucy is a curious and independent individual who longs to explore the world beyond her village. She becomes fascinated with a mysterious figure named Edward (Joaquin Phoenix) who lives on the other side of the forest.

As Lucy spends more time with Edward, she begins to question the villagers' beliefs about the "wild" and its inhabitants. She discovers that the creatures are not as monstrous as they seem, but rather, they are human beings who have been isolated from society for generations.

However, their isolation has led to a twisted and violent culture, where they live in fear of each other and the outside world. Lucy's relationship with Edward deepens, and she begins to see him as an outsider who is not afraid to challenge the villagers' way of life.

As tensions rise within the village, Lucy must decide whether to conform to the villagers' expectations or to follow her heart and explore the truth about the "wild." The film builds towards a climactic confrontation between Lucy and the villagers, which ultimately leads to a shocking revelation about Edward's true identity.

Throughout the film, Shyamalan uses suspenseful storytelling and atmospheric tension to create a sense of unease and uncertainty. The cinematography is stunning, capturing the eerie beauty of the forest and the isolation of the village.

The Village received mixed reviews from critics but has since become a cult classic, praised for its originality and thought-provoking themes. The film's exploration of fear, conformity, and the human condition continues to resonate with audiences today.

Overall, The Village is a gripping and unsettling thriller that challenges viewers to question their assumptions about the world around them. With its atmospheric tension, suspenseful plot, and thought-provoking themes, it is a must-see for fans of psychological horror and suspense.

overview: It's not easy being a teen like Duncan. His mom wants him to pay more attention to his homework, while his dad - a 120-foot-tall monster known as a Kaiju - wants him to become the next King of All Monsters. When these worlds collide, Duncan must use his human wits and his Kaiju powers - including super strength, agility and the ability to breathe fire - to protect his family and friends from a giant monster rampage.
tagline: Forged in Darkness, Born in Flames
title: Firebreather
plot:
Firebreather is an American computer-animated superhero television film of 2010 based on the Image Comics series created by Phil Hester and Andy Kuhn. Directed by Peter Chung from a screenplay by James Krieg, it premiered on Cartoon Network on 24 November 2010. Jesse Head voices the teenage hero Duncan Rosenblatt, with Dana Delany as his mother Margaret, Kevin Michael Richardson as his monstrous father Belloc, Amy Davidson as Jenna, Tia Texada as Isabel, Dante Basco as Kenny and Reed Diamond as Agent "Blitz" Barnes.

On the last day of the war between humans and the giant monsters called Kaiju, their dragon-like king Belloc attacks a city, but when a woman named Margaret confronts him, the two fall in love and he withdraws. Their son, Duncan, is born with Kaiju features and powers. Sixteen years later, Margaret and Duncan move to a new town, where he fears his appearance will make him a target. He falls for the popular Jenna, makes an enemy of her former boyfriend Troy, and befriends the outcasts Kenny and Isabel, a Kaiju-obsessed girl who develops a crush on him. Blitz Barnes, an agent of a monster-defence agency posing as a gym teacher, discovers that Duncan can breathe fire.

At a party, Duncan grows closer to Jenna, but Belloc arrives and carries him off to his desert lair, presenting him to the other Kaiju as his heir and hurling him into a lava pit, from which Duncan emerges transformed. Back at school, Isabel has made him a celebrity by claiming he saved everyone from Belloc.
