Duncan secretly leaves a precious red crystal in Jenna's locker to replace the Homecoming money stolen by Troy's friends, and asks her to the dance. On a mission with Blitz, he spares a Kaiju he could have killed. At Homecoming, a jealous Kenny tells Duncan that Isabel likes him only because of his father, and Jenna, overhearing, storms out. Two Kaiju, Abaddon and Astaroth, then attack. Duncan holds them off, sprouts wings to save Blitz from a fall, and with the help of Belloc, summoned by Margaret and Jenna, buries the monsters in an avalanche instead of killing them. Belloc lets himself be captured so as to stay close to his son, Jenna, who has realised Duncan left the crystal, apologises, and Duncan soars away on his new wings.

Reviewing it at New York Comic Con, Mania.com gave the film a B+, praising its blend of teenage angst and monster battles while noting that the characters sometimes looked puppet-like.

overview: Daigo, a cellist, is laid off from his orchestra and moves with his wife back to his small hometown where the living is cheaper. Thinking he’s applying for a job at a travel agency he finds he’s being interviewed for work with departures of a more permanent nature – as an undertaker’s assistant.
tagline: The gift of last memories.
title: Departures
plot:
Departures, directed by Yojiro Takagi and produced by Shochiku, is a poignant and contemplative film that explores the complexities of human emotions, particularly in relation to grief, loss, and the passage of time. The movie delves into the theme of cultural identity, as the protagonist, Obaachan, navigates her way through the traditional Japanese funeral rites, while also confronting her own personal demons.

The film's narrative is woven around the character of Obaachan, a widow who returns to her hometown after her husband's passing and takes on the role of a "searcher" or "funeral director," tasked with finding suitable spouses for deceased individuals. Through Obaachan's journey, the movie sheds light on the intricacies of Japanese culture, where tradition and modernity coexist in an intricate dance.

One of the primary themes that emerges is the concept of "honne" (outside self) versus "tatemae" (inside self). The film highlights the tension between these two aspects of human nature, as Obaachan struggles to reconcile her own desires with the expectations placed upon her by society. This internal conflict serves as a powerful metaphor for the human experience, where individuals often find themselves torn between their true selves and the roles they are expected to play.

Furthermore, Departures explores the theme of nostalgia and the bittersweet nature of memories. The film's use of music, particularly the traditional Japanese instrument, shamisen, adds a poignant layer to the narrative, evoking a sense of longing and melancholy that permeates the story.

Ultimately, Departures is a movie about the human condition, with all its complexities and contradictions. It invites viewers to reflect on their own relationships with tradition, culture, and personal identity, and to consider the ways in which we navigate the passage of time and our own mortality.

overview: A falsely accused nobleman survives years of slavery to take vengeance on his best friend who betrayed him.
tagline: First to finish. Last to die.
title: Ben-Hur
plot:
Ben-Hur is an American epic historical drama of 2016 directed by Timur Bekmambetov and written by Keith Clarke and John Ridley, the fifth screen adaptation of Lew Wallace's 1880 novel Ben-Hur: A Tale of the Christ. Jack Huston stars as Judah Ben-Hur, with Toby Kebbell as his adoptive brother Messala, Morgan Freeman as Sheik Ilderim, Nazanin Boniadi as Esther, Rodrigo Santoro as Jesus, Ayelet Zurer as Judah's mother Naomi, Sofia Black-D'Elia as his sister Tirzah and Pilou Asbæk as Pontius Pilate.

The Jewish prince Judah and Messala, a Roman adopted into his family, are close friends. After Judah's mother rejects Messala's interest in Tirzah, he joins the Roman army, and Judah marries Esther, a former slave of the household. Three years later Messala returns a decorated officer as the Zealots rise against Rome, and asks Judah to inform on rebels before the new governor, Pilate, arrives. Judah has sheltered a young Zealot, Dismas, who fires at Pilate from the family's balcony during the governor's procession. Refusing to betray him, Judah takes the blame; his mother and sister are condemned to crucifixion and he is sent to the galleys, receiving water from Jesus on the way.

After five years as a galley slave, Judah survives the destruction of his ship in a battle in the Ionian Sea and washes ashore, where Sheik Ilderim spares him after he tends one of the sheik's racehorses, and trains him as a charioteer. In Jerusalem, Judah finds Esther devoted to Jesus's teaching and opposed to his thirst for revenge on Messala, now commander of the garrison and a champion racer. He learns that Naomi and Tirzah are alive but stricken with leprosy. Ilderim persuades Pilate to let Judah race with a high wager. In the chariot race, the ruthless Messala wrecks rivals, but when their chariots lock together his breaks away and he is trampled, and Judah wins. Judah witnesses the crucifixion of Jesus, after which his mother and sister are miraculously healed, and he seeks out the maimed Messala, whose hatred melts in the face of forgiveness. The reconciled brothers leave Jerusalem with the family and Ilderim.

Released in August 2016 by Paramount, the film grossed $94.1 million worldwide against a $100 million budget, making it one of the year's biggest flops. Critics dismissed it as a needless remake, with 25% on Rotten Tomatoes.

overview: During the reign of the Vikings, a man from another world crash-lands on Earth, bringing with him an alien predator. The man must fuse his advanced technology with the weaponry of the vikings to fight the monster.
tagline: It destroyed his world. He won't let it destroy ours.
title: Outlander
plot:
Outlander is a science fiction action film of 2008 written and directed by Howard McCain, loosely based on the Old English epic Beowulf but reimagined around a spaceship that crashes in Iron Age Norway. Jim Caviezel stars as Kainan, a humanoid alien warrior, with Sophia Myles as Freya, Jack Huston as Wulfric, John Hurt as King Hrothgar, Ron Perlman as the rival chieftain Gunnar, Cliff Saunders as the smith Boromir and Bailey Maughan as the orphan Erik.

In 709 AD a spacecraft crashes into a lake in Scandinavia. Its lone survivor, Kainan, learns from his ship's computer that he has landed on Earth, a seed colony abandoned by his people, and has the local Norse language and customs downloaded into his brain. Finding a village destroyed, he is captured by Wulfric, the heir of King Hrothgar, and taken to Hrothgar's fortified settlement, where the king fears that Gunnar will blame the massacre on them. Calling himself a man from the north hunting a dragon, Kainan reveals, after an unseen beast kills several warriors that night, that the attacker is a Moorwen, a predator that stowed away on his ship and caused the crash. He wins the villagers' respect by killing a giant bear during a hunt.

After a clash with Gunnar's men, who return fleeing the Moorwen, Kainan devises a trap: a pit of whale oil inside the gate, crossed by floating shields. He confides to Freya, who is drawn to him, that his people slaughtered the Moorwens to colonise their planet, and that this last survivor massacred his colony, including his wife and child. Freya gives him an ancestral sword. The burning pit only wounds the beast, which kills Gunnar and escapes, while its offspring slips in through the well and kills Hrothgar. Kainan retrieves metal from his sunken ship to forge stronger blades, but the young Moorwen seizes Freya. Descending the well, the hunters lose many men, including Boromir, before Freya kills the offspring. At a waterfall the adult Moorwen mortally wounds Wulfric, who passes the crown to Kainan before Kainan and Freya send the creature over the cliff. Bidding farewell to his wife's coffin, Kainan destroys his distress beacon, lets the rescue ship leave without him, and stays to rule, marrying Freya and adopting Erik.

Based on a story McCain first wrote in 1992, the film received only a limited American release in January 2009. It earned around $6 million worldwide on a reported budget of $47 million, and critics were unimpressed, giving it 37% on Rotten Tomatoes.

original_title: The Dukes of Hazzard: The Beginning
overview: When mischievous teenaged cousins Bo and Luke Duke are arrested, both boys are paroled to the care of their Uncle Jesse in Hazzard, sentenced to a summer of hard work. It's not long before the Duke boys learn of Boss Hogg's plans to foreclose on Uncle Jesse's farm. Together, with help from their cousin Daisy, Bo and Luke vow to save the family's property and its storied history of producing the best moonshine in all of Hazzard.
tagline: These are the Duke boys... from the beginning!
title: The Dukes of Hazzard: The Beginning
plot:
The Dukes of Hazzard: The Beginning is a 2007 American buddy comedy made for television, directed by Robert Berlinger and produced under Warner Bros.' Warner Premiere label on a budget of about $5 million. A standalone prequel to the 2005 feature The Dukes of Hazzard, it was the fourth and last Dukes of Hazzard film. An edited cut premiered on ABC Family on March 4, 2007, and R-rated and unrated versions reached DVD later that month.

In rural Georgia, teenage cousins Bo Duke, arrested for reckless driving in a neighboring county, and Luke Duke, caught setting off illegal fireworks, are paroled to their Uncle Jesse in Hazzard County and sentenced to a summer of farm labor. Jesse secretly makes the county's finest moonshine and pays regular bribes to the corrupt commissioner, Boss Hogg. When the boys accidentally let Hogg's prized pig escape and it is hurt, Hogg demands a large sum within two weeks or he will seize the farm. To earn the money through moonshine runs, Bo and Luke need a fast car. With help from their shy cousin Daisy and the mechanic Cooter Davenport, who supplies an engine, they pull an abandoned 1969 Dodge Charger out of a swimming hole and rebuild it as the General Lee.

The deliveries succeed until Hogg declares Hazzard a dry county, offers a reward for exposing moonshiners and has Jesse arrested. Daisy, who has taken a job at the Boar's Nest after a dramatic makeover, discovers that the bartender she has fallen for, Hughie, is Hogg's nephew and was spying on the family. The Dukes learn that Hogg wants to ban alcohol across Georgia so he can sell his own liquor illegally. They kidnap him in the General Lee and, threatening to leap a ravine, force a confession that Daisy arranges to have broadcast on the radio. They claim the reward to save the farm, Jesse and the other moonshiners are freed, and the cousins drive off toward new adventures.

Jonathan Bennett plays Bo, Randy Wayne plays Luke and April Scott plays Daisy, with Christopher McDonald as Boss Hogg and Harland Williams as Sheriff Rosco P. Coltrane. Willie Nelson, as Jesse, was the only actor returning from the 2005 film. Reviews were generally negative, and the few critics counted by Rotten Tomatoes gave it a 20% approval rating.

overview: The story, set in 1885, follows a British officer (Heath Ledger) who resigns his post when he learns of his regiment's plan to ship out to the Sudan for the conflict with the Mahdi. His friends and fiancée send him four white feathers which symbolize cowardice. To redeem his honor he disguises himself as an Arab and secretly saves the lives of those who branded him a coward.
tagline: Freedom. Country. Honor. Passion. To save his best friend, one man must risk everything he loves.
title: The Four Feathers
plot:
The Four Feathers is an epic war drama of 2002 directed by Shekhar Kapur, the latest of many screen adaptations of A. E. W. Mason's novel of 1902, here set during the British expedition to relieve General Gordon in the Sudan in 1884-85. Heath Ledger stars as Harry Faversham, with Wes Bentley as his friend Jack Durrance, Kate Hudson as his fiancée Ethne Eustace, Djimon Hounsou as the warrior Abou Fatma, Michael Sheen as William Trench and Kris Marshall as Edward Castleton.

Harry, a young British officer, celebrates his engagement to Ethne at a ball just as his regiment is ordered to the Sudan to rescue Gordon. Doubting the war, he resigns his commission. His father disowns him, and three of his friends and Ethne each send him a white feather, the mark of cowardice; Ethne ends their engagement. When Harry hears that Jack and his old regiment are heading into danger, he travels alone to the Sudan, disguises himself as an Arab and allies with Abou Fatma, a mercenary. Finding the fort at Abu Klea overrun by the Mahdi's forces, he sends Abou to warn the British, but they dismiss him as a spy and flog him.

The regiment is ambushed. The British square repels the first assault, but cavalry they take for reinforcements turn out to be Sudanese fighters in captured British uniforms, among them the disguised Harry. In the chaos, Castleton is killed by his own side's volleys and Jack is blinded when his rifle misfires. Harry rescues Jack and nurses him without revealing his identity, finding Ethne's letters to his friend. Back in England, Jack proposes to Ethne. Learning from Abou that Trench is held in the notorious prison at Omdurman, Harry lets himself be captured to free him. Starved and worked to exhaustion, the two despair until Abou smuggles in a poison that lets them feign death, and after killing the guards who follow them, Harry brings Trench home. Ethne takes back her feather and Harry's father welcomes him home; when the blind Jack touches Harry's face and recognises his rescuer, he releases Ethne, and Harry and Ethne are engaged once more.

Released by Paramount in September 2002, the film earned $29.8 million worldwide, short of its $35 million budget. Critics admired its visuals but not its storytelling, giving it 42% on Rotten Tomatoes.

overview: What do you dream of when you're 16-years-old and in a seaside resort in Normandy in the 1980s? A best friend? A lifelong teen pact? Scooting off on adventures on a boat or a motorbike? Living life at breakneck speed? No. You dream of death. Because you can't get a bigger kick than dying. And that's why you save it till the very end. The summer holidays are just beginning, and this story recounts how Alexis grew into himself.
title: Summer of 85
plot:
Summer of '85 is a poignant coming-of-age drama that delves into the complexities of adolescent desire, identity, and the blurred lines between innocence and experience.

The film's narrative revolves around a young man's summer of self-discovery, as he navigates his first same-sex encounter with an older man. This pivotal moment serves as a catalyst for exploring themes of vulnerability, consent, and the struggle to reconcile one's desires with societal expectations.

Throughout the movie, the director masterfully weaves together elements of nostalgia, longing, and the fragility of youth, creating a narrative that is both deeply personal and universally relatable. The film's use of vibrant colors, evocative soundscapes, and poignant performances all contribute to an immersive cinematic experience that captures the essence of this pivotal moment in a young man's life.

Ultimately, Summer of '85 presents a nuanced exploration of the human experience, one that is both tender and unflinching. The movie invites viewers to reflect on their own experiences of identity, desire, and the complexities of growing up, making it a powerful and thought-provoking watch.

overview: Having thought that monogamy was never possible, a commitment-phobic career woman may have to face her fears when she meets a good guy.
tagline: We All Know One.
title: Trainwreck
plot:
Trainwreck is a 2015 American romantic comedy film directed by Judd Apatow and written by Apatow and Amy Schumer, who also stars in the film. The movie follows the story of Amy Schumer's character, Amy, a commitment-phobic and womanizing journalist from New York City.

The film begins with Amy (Amy Schumer) working as a writer for a men's magazine called "Screw". She is known for her provocative articles and her ability to get close to her subjects without getting too attached. One day, she meets Aaron Conners (Bill Hader), the son of a wealthy family who has recently lost his father. Amy is immediately drawn to Aaron's charming personality, but she tries to resist her feelings.

As Amy and Aaron start dating, they face various challenges, including their differences in values and lifestyle. Amy struggles with commitment and intimacy, while Aaron wants to settle down and have children. Despite these obstacles, the two grow closer, and Amy starts to confront her past and her fears about relationships.

However, just as things are starting to look up for Amy and Aaron, his family's dark secrets begin to surface. His father, Robert (Tilda Swinton), is a wealthy and influential businessman who has made many enemies over the years. As Amy gets drawn into Aaron's world, she becomes embroiled in a series of events that threaten to destroy their relationship.

Throughout the film, Amy's character undergoes significant development as she confronts her past and learns to open up to love. With the help of her friends, including her sister Molly (Megan Trainor) and her editor, Jules (Tiffany Haddish), Amy starts to see that there is more to life than just sex and partying.

As the story unfolds, Amy and Aaron face a series of challenges, including a confrontation with Robert's business partner, who tries to sabotage their relationship. In the end, Amy must choose between her feelings for Aaron and her fear of commitment. The film culminates in a romantic and emotional climax that will leave audiences cheering.

Overall, Trainwreck is a heartwarming and hilarious film that explores themes of love, relationships, and personal growth. With its talented cast, witty dialogue, and relatable characters, the movie has become a modern classic in the romantic comedy genre.

overview: A documentary filmmaker explores seemingly unrelated paranormal incidents connected by the legend of an ancient demon called the "kagutaba."
title: Noroi: The Curse
plot:
Noroi: The Curse is a 2005 Japanese horror film directed by Kōji Shiraishi, who co-wrote the screenplay with Naoyuki Yokota, and produced by Takashige Ichise, whose earlier horror productions included Ring and Ju-On: The Grudge. Presented as a finished documentary assembled from pseudo-documentary and found footage, it stars Jin Muraki as paranormal researcher Masafumi Kobayashi, with actress Marika Matsumoto playing a fictionalized version of herself, alongside Rio Kanno, Tomono Kuga and Satoru Jitsunashi, and cameos from the comedy duo Ungirls, Dankan, Ai Iijima and author Hiroshi Aramata. Shiraishi spent about a year on research and interviews, aiming to heighten the fear by grounding the fiction in apparent reality.

The film explains that Kobayashi, known for his books and documentaries on the supernatural, vanished after his house burned down, leaving his wife dead in the ruins, while he was making a documentary called The Curse. That documentary then plays, largely through the footage of his cameraman, Miyajima. Eighteen months earlier, Kobayashi looks into complaints about the sound of crying babies from the home of a woman named Junko Ishii, who moves away soon after, leaving dead pigeons in her yard; days later her neighbor and the neighbor's daughter die in a mysterious car crash. At the same time, a psychic girl named Kana Yano, who appeared on a television variety show, disappears, and an eccentric psychic named Mitsuo Hori claims she was taken by "ectoplasmic worms". After filming at a shrine, Marika Matsumoto collapses on hearing a strange voice and begins weaving yarn and wire into interlocking loops in her sleep, and a camera records a deep voice uttering the word "kagutaba". A local historian tells Kobayashi that Kagutaba is a demon once summoned and then imprisoned by the villagers of Shimokage in Nagano Prefecture, who held an annual ritual to appease it until the village was abandoned to make way for a dam in 1978. As a string of hangings and disappearances follows, Kobayashi uncovers a link between the last ritual and Ishii, drawing him, Marika and Hori ever closer to the demon's influence.

Distributed by Xanadeux, Noroi: The Curse opened in Japan on 20 August 2005 and received generally positive reviews, with critics praising its presentation, performances, atmosphere and pacing. Despite limited distribution outside Japan it developed a following and became legally available in North America through Shudder in 2017.

overview: Frank Penny is a disgraced cop looking for a shot at redemption. When the police chief's 11-year-old daughter is abducted, Frank goes rogue to try and save her. But to find the girl, Frank will need the help of Ava Brooks, whose live-streaming news channel is broadcasting Frank's every move.
tagline: The clock is ticking. The world is watching.
title: Line of Duty
plot:
Line of Duty is an American action thriller of 2019 directed by Steven C. Miller and written by Jeremy Drysdale. Aaron Eckhart stars as the disgraced police officer Frank Penny, with Courtney Eaton as the online reporter Ava Brooks, Giancarlo Esposito as the senior police officer Tom Volk, Ben McKenzie as Dean Keller, Dina Meyer as Ruth Carter, Jessica Lu as Clover Nestel and Timothy Omundson as Nicolas Forrester.

Penny is a dedicated, fiercely fit officer whose career has stalled since he killed a child in a dramatic shoot-out, leaving him to watch over traffic violations and other minor matters. When he hears over the radio that colleagues are chasing a suspect nearby, he joins the pursuit against his superior's orders, corners the man and, after repeated warnings, shoots him when he raises a gun. The dead man, however, was the prime suspect in a kidnapping and the only person who knew where the hostage was hidden. Worse, the missing girl is the daughter of Volk, Penny's former partner, who holds him personally responsible for endangering her life.

Determined to make amends, Penny learns that only 64 minutes remain before the girl will drown in a concealed water tank. Cut loose by his department, he is joined by Ava, an ambitious young journalist who senses the story of a lifetime and follows him with her camera, broadcasting their search as a live stream. Penny reluctantly accepts her help, and Ava's online followers feed them a stream of fresh leads as the clock runs down. The pair discover that the dead kidnapper had a brother who might lead them to the girl, but the brother wants only one thing: revenge for his sibling's death.

The film was shot in Birmingham, Alabama, and released by Saban Films in November 2019. Reviews were mixed, with 59% on Rotten Tomatoes and 50 on Metacritic. Variety's Dennis Harvey called it high on energy if low on credibility, while The Hollywood Reporter's Frank Scheck found it fast-paced enough to overcome its more ludicrous plot elements.

overview: After fishing out coins from a water fountain in Italy, cynical New Yorker Beth Harper finds herself being wooed by several ardent suitors. As she deals with the attention, Beth tries to figure out whether a charming reporter really loves her.
tagline: Did you ever wish for the impossible?
title: When in Rome
plot:
When in Rome is a romantic comedy that explores the idea of love and relationships through the lens of chance encounters and serendipity. The film follows Beth, a woman who has given up on love after a string of failed relationships, as she navigates her way through life with a cynical attitude.

However, when Beth's sister gets married in Rome, she finds herself swept up in a whirlwind of new experiences and encounters that challenge her outlook on life. She meets a handsome stranger, Nick, who is also searching for love, and the two embark on a series of adventures together that lead them to reevaluate their own desires and expectations.

At its core, When in Rome is a film about the power of chance meetings and the idea that sometimes, the best things in life come from stepping outside our comfort zones. The movie celebrates the beauty of spontaneity and the thrill of discovering new experiences, while also exploring the complexities of love and relationships.

Through Beth's journey, the film shows how even someone who has given up on love can find themselves opening up to new possibilities and embracing the idea that there is still room for romance in their life. The movie ultimately becomes a heartwarming exploration of the human desire for connection and the power of love to transform our lives.

The film's themes are also intertwined with the idea of self-discovery, as Beth navigates her way through Rome and discovers new aspects of herself along the way. As she lets go of her cynicism and allows herself to be open to new experiences, she begins to uncover a more vulnerable and authentic side of herself.

Overall, When in Rome is a charming romantic comedy that celebrates the beauty of chance encounters, self-discovery, and the power of love to transform our lives.

original_title: Borat: Cultural Learnings of America for Make Benefit Glorious Nation of Kazakhstan
overview: Kazakh journalist Borat Sagdiyev travels to America to make a documentary. As he zigzags across the nation, Borat meets real people in real situations with hysterical consequences. His backwards behavior generates strong reactions around him exposing prejudices and hypocrisies in American culture.
tagline: Come to Kazakhstan, it's nice!
title: Borat: Cultural Learnings of America for Make Benefit Glorious Nation of Kazakhstan
plot:
Borat: Cultural Learnings of America for Make Benefit Glorious Nation of Kazakhstan, directed by Larry Charles and released in 2006 by 20th Century Fox, is a satirical comedy film that explores several themes. Here are some of the main themes:

1. **Racism and Xenophobia**: The film critiques racism and xenophobia in America, particularly towards Eastern Europeans and Muslims. Borat's character, a bumbling and ignorant Kazakh journalist, perpetuates stereotypes and prejudices, which are then subverted by the audience.

2. **Cultural Insensitivity and Hypocrisy**: Borat's journey is marked by his lack of understanding and respect for American culture, customs, and values. He often engages in behaviors that are considered unacceptable or insensitive, highlighting the hypocrisy of some Americans who claim to be tolerant but exhibit similar behavior themselves.

3. **Toxic Masculinity**: The film pokes fun at traditional masculine ideals, particularly in rural America. Borat's character embodies a toxic form of masculinity, which is both absurd and disturbing. This theme serves as a commentary on the societal expectations placed on men and the consequences of such expectations.

4. **Nationalism and Patriotism**: Through Borat's character, the film satirizes nationalism and patriotism, particularly in America. The title itself is a tongue-in-cheek reference to the idea that cultural exchange can be used as a tool for nationalistic gain.

5. **Satire and Social Commentary**: The film uses satire to comment on various aspects of American society, including politics, media, and social norms. By exaggerating and distorting certain behaviors and attitudes, the film aims to highlight their absurdity and encourage critical thinking.

6. **Identity and Belonging**: Borat's character is a fish-out-of-water in America, struggling to find his place in a foreign culture. This theme explores the complexities of identity and belonging, particularly for individuals who feel like outsiders or misfits.

Overall, Borat: Cultural Learnings of America for Make Benefit Glorious Nation of Kazakhstan is a complex and multifaceted film that uses satire and absurdity to comment on various aspects of American society and culture.

overview: Jerry Shaw and Rachel Holloman are two strangers whose lives are suddenly thrown into turmoil by a mysterious woman they have never met. Threatening their lives and family, the unseen caller uses everyday technology to control their actions and push them into increasing danger. As events escalate, Jerry and Rachel become the country's most-wanted fugitives and must figure out what is happening to them.
tagline: Don't walk. Run.
title: Eagle Eye
plot:
Eagle Eye is a 2008 American techno-thriller film directed by D.J. Caruso and written by Scott Frank and Will Beall. The movie stars Shia LaBeouf, Michelle Monaghan, Michael Chiklis, and Billy Burke.

The story begins with Jerry Shaw (Shia LaBeouf), a computer expert who works for the Department of Defense's National Security Agency (NSA). Jerry is a loner who lives in Chicago and spends most of his time working from home. One day, he receives an email that sets off a chain of events that changes his life forever.

The email appears to be from a woman named Rachel Hollis (Michelle Monaghan), who claims to have been kidnapped by a group of terrorists. The email is cryptic, but Jerry becomes convinced that it's real and decides to investigate further. He teams up with Agnes Arlo (Michelle Monaghan), a young woman who was also targeted by the same group.

As they dig deeper, they discover that Rachel has been brainwashed by the terrorists and is now working for them. The group, led by a mysterious figure known as "The Architect" (Billy Burke), plans to carry out a series of attacks across the United States.

Jerry and Agnes must work together to stop the attacks and uncover the truth behind the conspiracy. Along the way, they encounter a range of characters, including Jerry's boss, Colonel Campbell (Michael Chiklis), who is initially skeptical of their claims but eventually becomes an ally.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that The Architect is a mastermind with a personal vendetta against the government. He has created a complex system of surveillance and control that uses advanced technology to manipulate people's lives.

The plot thickens as Jerry and Agnes get closer to uncovering the truth. They discover that Rachel was not just a victim, but an active participant in the conspiracy. The stakes are raised when they realize that The Architect plans to carry out a massive attack on the United States Capitol building.

In the thrilling climax of the movie, Jerry and Agnes must use all their skills and resources to stop The Architect and his minions. They engage in a cat-and-mouse game with the terrorists, using advanced technology to stay one step ahead.

The ending is intense and suspenseful as Jerry and Agnes finally confront The Architect. In a shocking twist, it's revealed that The Architect was actually a former NSA agent who was driven mad by the government's secrets. He has been manipulating events from behind the scenes, using his knowledge of the system to control people's lives.

In the end, Jerry and Agnes succeed in stopping the attack, but not before The Architect reveals that he has one final trick up his sleeve. As the movie ends, it's left unclear whether Jerry and Agnes have truly stopped the conspiracy or if there are still more threats lurking in the shadows.

Overall, Eagle Eye is a tense and suspenseful thriller that explores themes of surveillance, control, and the dangers of playing with fire when it comes to advanced technology. The movie features strong performances from its leads, particularly Shia LaBeouf and Michelle Monaghan, who bring depth and nuance to their characters.

overview: Tensions rise when the trailblazing Mother of the Blues and her band gather at a Chicago recording studio in 1927. Adapted from August Wilson's play.
tagline: It would be an empty world without the blues.
title: Ma Rainey's Black Bottom
plot:
Ma Rainey's Black Bottom is a powerful and poignant film that delves into the complexities of racism, identity, and the struggles of African American women in the early 20th century. The movie is set in the 1920s, during the height of the Harlem Renaissance, and follows the story of Ma Rainey, a legendary blues singer who is struggling to maintain her artistic integrity in the face of exploitation by white record executives.

At its core, Ma Rainey's Black Bottom is a film about the intersectionality of racism and sexism. The movie highlights the ways in which black women were marginalized and silenced by both racist attitudes and patriarchal norms. Ma Rainey herself is a complex and multifaceted character who embodies both strength and vulnerability as she navigates the treacherous world of 1920s show business.

One of the main themes of the film is the struggle for artistic control and autonomy. Ma Rainey is determined to maintain her creative agency, even in the face of pressure from white men who want to exploit her talent for their own gain. This theme speaks to the ongoing struggles faced by black artists and creatives throughout history, who have often been forced to navigate a system that values their work but does not value them as individuals.

Another key theme of Ma Rainey's Black Bottom is the power of female solidarity and community. The film shows how Ma Rainey forms connections with other women in her life, including her maid Delia and her fellow performers, who support and uplift each other in the face of adversity. This theme speaks to the importance of building strong relationships and networks among black women, particularly during times of oppression.

Finally, the movie explores the tension between tradition and innovation. Ma Rainey is a product of the blues tradition, but she is also a trailblazer who is pushing the boundaries of what is possible for African American music. The film highlights the ways in which this tension can be both liberating and limiting, as Ma Rainey struggles to balance her commitment to her art with the need to adapt to changing times.

Overall, Ma Rainey's Black Bottom is a powerful and thought-provoking film that sheds light on some of the most pressing issues facing black women today.

overview: After a mammoth cruise ship sails over the site of the Titanic’s disaster, dark and deadly events start to occur on board. As the ship’s captain investigates the tragic occurrences, it becomes clear that the passengers and crew from the original Titanic have returned.
tagline: Welcome on board.
title: Titanic 666
plot:
Titanic 666, also released as Titanic Rises and Titanic 3, is an American supernatural horror film of 2022 directed by Nick Lyon and produced by The Asylum as a sequel to its Titanic II (2010). Keesha Sharp stars as Captain Celeste Rhoades and Jamie Bamber as Professor Hal Cochran, with Lydia Hearst as the stowaway Idina Bess, AnnaLynne McCord and Derek Yates as the influencers Mia and Jackson Stone, Joseph Gatt as crewman Brian Andrews, Giovannie Pico as Nancy and Jhey Castles as Julie.

The film opens on the night of 15 April 1912, as a woman searches desperately for her husband on the sinking Titanic. She escapes in a lifeboat after its ropes mysteriously give way and kill several passengers, but watches her husband drown, and his ghost later drags her into the sea. Exactly 110 years later, the luxury liner Titanic III sets out on the original route. On board are the married influencers Mia and Jackson Stone with their fan Nancy, while Captain Rhoades warns her crew to avoid the fates of the earlier ships. Idina, hiding below decks, steals an artifact from Hal's collection of belongings recovered from Titanic victims, and the influencers clash with Hal as they dig into the voyage's history.

In the hold, Idina performs a satanic ritual to resurrect her great-grandfather, Captain Edward Smith, whose spirit summons the souls of those who died in 1912. During an evening commemoration the ghostly orchestra attacks; Jackson vanishes and Mia is killed. The ghosts slaughter the engineers and seize the ship, and when Rhoades and Brian try to shut down the engines, the turbines explode and the controls fail. Idina kills Brian and escapes, then, possessed by Smith, takes the bridge and kills herself as the liner strikes an iceberg. Rhoades orders the survivors into lifeboats, but once more the ropes loosen, killing nearly everyone aboard. Adrift as the ship sinks, Hal blames himself for the disaster and dies of hypothermia, and when Rhoades tries to revive him, his ghost turns on her.

The film premiered on Tubi in the United States on 15 April 2022, the 110th anniversary of the sinking. Reviews were largely negative: Matt Donato of Paste rated it 4 out of 10, likening Tubi to late-night SyFy, and Josh Bell of Crooked Marquee gave it a C-minus, finding it a slow, dull haunted-ship story. Social media users noted its resemblance to both Titanic (1997) and Studio 666.

overview: Cody, Chicken Joe and Lani are back in their most epic adventure yet! The most radical surfing dream team, The Hang Five (voiced by WWE Superstars John Cena, Undertaker, Triple H, Paige and Mr. McMahon) puts Cody and his friends to the test and teaches them the meaning of teamwork as they journey to the most legendary surfing spot on the planet.
tagline: Starring your favorite WWE Superstars!
title: Surf's Up 2: WaveMania
plot:
Surf's Up 2: WaveMania is a 2017 American computer-animated sports comedy and the sequel to Surf's Up (2007). Produced by Sony Pictures Animation together with WWE Studios, it was released straight to DVD and digital media by Sony Pictures Home Entertainment in January 2017. WWE approached Sony about a project that would introduce its brand to younger audiences, and the studios announced the partnership in March 2016. Henry Yu made his directing debut from a screenplay by Abdul Williams, and WWE approved all of the character designs.

Teenage rockhopper penguin Cody Maverick runs a surf school on Pen Gu Island with Lani Aliikai while competing with his rival, Tank Evans. His best friend Chicken Joe, now a famous surfer on a world tour, comes back to visit just as the Hang 5, a team of extreme surfers Cody has idolized since childhood, arrives on the island. Their leader, the giant otter Mr. McMahon, explains that they are heading for a legendary spot called the Trenches to ride a huge rogue wave, and that he plans to retire and is looking for a successor. Lani, Cody, Tank and Chicken Joe all end up as candidates and join the journey across desert and jungle, where they find the ruins of an ancient penguin civilization devoted to surfing.

After Cody's quarrel with Tank nearly sends Chicken Joe into a lake of lava, the team scolds Cody, and he leaves feeling betrayed. On his way back he finds carvings showing that the civilization's champion died at the Trenches, so he turns around to warn his friends. There they learn the team's motto means surfing through lightning storms. Lani declines to join, while Tank rides the giant wave but loses his nerve. When the Undertaker is struck by lightning, Chicken Joe revives him with jellyfish stings, and J.C. rescues Cody and Tank. McMahon offers Cody a place on the team, but Cody chooses to stay with his friends and his island, and McMahon decides to postpone his retirement.

Jeremy Shada and Melissa Sturm take over the roles of Cody and Lani, and Jon Heder and Diedrich Bader return as Chicken Joe and Tank. WWE performers John Cena, the Undertaker, Triple H, Paige, Vince McMahon and Michael Cole fill out the cast. Critics panned the film for its animation, voice acting and clichéd writing, and for dropping the original's themes to promote wrestling stars. Common Sense Media found it earnest and likable, if less polished than the original. In 2023 Letterboxd ranked it among the worst animated films of the 2010s.

overview: When famous DJ Alan Partridge’s radio station is taken over by a new media conglomerate, it sets in motion a chain of events which see Alan having to work with the police to defuse a potentially violent siege.
tagline: 12 hostages. 24 hours. 1 Partridge.
title: Alan Partridge: Alpha Papa
plot:
Alan Partridge: Alpha Papa is a 2013 British comedy film that explores the complexities of male ego, identity, and the blurred lines between reality and media persona. The movie delves into the world of a fictional radio DJ, Alan Partridge, who finds himself thrust into a high-stakes crisis situation when he's unexpectedly appointed as the interim CEO of a local public service broadcaster.

As the story unfolds, we see Alan's struggles to reconcile his on-air persona with his real-life insecurities and vulnerabilities. The film masterfully satirizes the world of celebrity culture, where individuals often present a curated version of themselves to the public, hiding their true flaws and insecurities behind a mask of confidence and charm.

Through Alan's character, the movie pokes fun at traditional masculine norms, highlighting the absurdities and contradictions that can arise when societal expectations clash with individual desires. The film also touches on themes of identity, as Alan navigates his own sense of self-worth and purpose in the face of crisis and uncertainty.

Ultimately, Alpha Papa is a heartwarming and hilarious exploration of what it means to be human, with all its flaws and imperfections. With its witty dialogue, lovable characters, and clever satire, the film offers a relatable and entertaining commentary on our shared experiences as individuals navigating the complexities of modern life.

overview: When Lou Bloom, desperate for work, muscles into the world of L.A. crime journalism, he blurs the line between observer and participant to become the star of his own story. Aiding him in his effort is Nina, a TV-news veteran.
tagline: The city shines brightest at night
title: Nightcrawler
plot:
Nightcrawler is a psychological thriller film directed by Dan Gilroy, released in 2014 by Bold Films. The movie follows the story of Lou Bloom (played by Jake Gyllenhaal), a driven and ambitious young man who becomes obsessed with capturing violent and sensational footage for local news stations.

The film begins with Lou, a struggling young man living in Los Angeles, working as a janitor at a mortuary. He is desperate to make ends meet and find purpose in his life. One day, he stumbles upon an opportunity to work as a freelance videographer for a local news station, capturing footage of accidents and crimes. However, Lou soon realizes that the best-paying gigs are those involving violence and tragedy.

As Lou becomes more successful in his new career, he adopts a peculiar and unsettling persona, often dressing in dark attire and adopting a menacing tone to get the best shots. He befriends a local news anchor, Nina Romina (played by Rene Russo), who is initially hesitant about working with him but eventually warms up to his unique perspective.

Lou's obsession with capturing violent footage leads him to take risks that put himself and others in harm's way. He becomes fixated on capturing the most sensational and disturbing content, often at the expense of human life. His actions become increasingly erratic and disturbing, causing concern among those around him.

As Lou's career takes off, he attracts the attention of a rival videographer, Kessler (played by Bill Paxton), who is also vying for the top spot in capturing violent footage. The two engage in a series of escalating pranks and one-upmanship, pushing each other to new extremes.

Meanwhile, Lou's relationships with his colleagues and friends begin to deteriorate as he becomes more consumed by his work. His obsession with violence and sensationalism leads him to sacrifice his own humanity, causing those around him to question his motivations and morals.

The film builds towards a climactic confrontation between Lou and Kessler, which ultimately exposes the darker aspects of their rivalry and the true cost of Lou's ambition. In the end, Lou is forced to confront the consequences of his actions, and the audience is left wondering whether he has finally found redemption or succumbed to his own darkness.

Throughout the film, Dan Gilroy explores themes of capitalism, consumerism, and the commodification of violence. The movie raises questions about the ethics of sensational journalism and the impact it can have on society. Jake Gyllenhaal's performance as Lou Bloom is particularly noteworthy, capturing the complexity and nuance of a character who is both fascinating and repulsive.

Overall, Nightcrawler is a thought-provoking and unsettling film that challenges viewers to confront the darker aspects of human nature.

original_title: 僕のヒーローアカデミア THE MOVIE ～2人の英雄～
overview: All Might and Deku accept an invitation to go abroad to a floating and mobile manmade city, called 'I-Island', where they research quirks as well as hero supplemental items at the special 'I-Expo' convention that is currently being held on the island. During that time, suddenly, despite an iron wall of security surrounding the island, the system is breached by a villain, and the only ones able to stop him are the students of Class 1-A.
tagline: Who is your hero?
title: My Hero Academia: Two Heroes
plot:
My Hero Academia: Two Heroes is a 2018 Japanese animated superhero film based on an original story featuring the characters of Kōhei Horikoshi's manga series My Hero Academia. Produced by Bones and distributed by Toho, it was directed by Kenji Nagasaki from a script by Yōsuke Kuroda, with characters designed by Yoshihiko Umakoshi, all returning from the anime television series. The ensemble voice cast includes Daiki Yamashita, Kenta Miyake, Mirai Shida, Katsuhisa Namase, Nobuhiko Okamoto, Ayane Sakura and Yuki Kaji. The story takes place between the manga's Final Exams and Forest Training Camp arcs.

Years ago, as an exchange student in California, the young All Might foiled a group of casino robbers with the help of his friend David Shield, who went on to become a scientist and design many of his hero suits. In the present, during summer break, All Might takes his protégé Izuku Midoriya to I-Island, an artificial floating city, at the invitation of David's daughter Melissa, who wants to surprise her father. When David tests All Might, he is horrified to learn that his friend's Quirk is almost exhausted, threatening his role as the Symbol of Peace. Meanwhile Melissa shows Izuku around the island, where they run into his classmates from Class 1-A, and she confides that, like Izuku before he gained his power, she was born without a Quirk. She gives him a "Full Gauntlet", a device that lets him unleash his Quirk without injuring himself. During a formal party for the assembled heroes, a villain named Wolfram seizes the island's security system, restrains the heroes, including All Might, and takes David and his assistant Samuel hostage. Izuku, Melissa and several classmates evade capture and climb the central tower to disable the security system, fighting villains and security robots on the way. At the top, Izuku and Melissa discover that David and Samuel staged the attack to recover a confiscated invention that amplifies Quirks, hoping to restore All Might's power, but Wolfram turns out to be a real villain secretly hired by Samuel, forcing All Might and Izuku to join forces against a dangerously empowered foe.

The film premiered at Anime Expo in Los Angeles on July 5, 2018, before opening in Japan on August 3. It grossed $33.4 million worldwide and received positive reviews, holding a 100% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes based on eight reviews.

overview: Peter and Emma thought they were on the precipice of life’s biggest moments – marriage, kids, and houses in the suburbs – until their respective partners dumped them. Horrified to learn that the loves of their lives have already moved on, Peter and Emma hatch a hilarious plan to win back their exes with unexpected results.
tagline: Their exes have moved on. They haven't.
title: I Want You Back
plot:
I Want You Back is a 2022 romantic comedy film that explores the complexities of human relationships and the challenges of navigating modern dating. The movie delves into the theme of unrequited love, as its protagonist, Charlie, finds himself caught in a complicated web of emotions when he reconnects with his high school ex-girlfriend, Beth.

The film also touches on the idea of identity and self-discovery, as Charlie struggles to come to terms with his own desires and needs. Through his interactions with Beth and other characters, the movie sheds light on the nuances of human connection and the ways in which people can both hurt and heal each other.

Furthermore, I Want You Back critiques the superficiality of modern dating culture, where people often prioritize physical appearance and social media validation over genuine emotional connections. The film's portrayal of Charlie's experiences serves as a commentary on the perils of swiping through dating apps and the pressure to present a curated online persona.

Ultimately, the movie presents a nuanced exploration of love, relationships, and personal growth, inviting viewers to reflect on their own experiences with romance and connection.

overview: JSDF pilot Akane has a fateful encounter when a new Godzilla emerges in Tateyama. As a countermeasure, a cyborg named Kiryu is constructed from the remains of the original. The machine is discovered to harbor the restless soul of the original monster as Akane must learn to find value in her own life as well.
tagline: Startup - Resonance - Smashed Ice
title: Godzilla Against MechaGodzilla
plot:
Godzilla Against Mechagodzilla is a 2002 Japanese kaiju film directed by Masaaki Tezuka, with special effects by Yūichi Kikuchi. Distributed by Toho, it is the 27th Godzilla film and the fourth of the franchise's Millennium era. It brings back Mechagodzilla, here mostly called by its code name, Kiryu, from the Japanese for "machine dragon". Unlike the other Millennium films, which follow only the 1954 original, it takes place in a continuity that refers to several of Toho's earlier monster films. A direct sequel, Godzilla: Tokyo S.O.S., followed in 2003.

Decades after the first Godzilla was killed, Lieutenant Akane Yashiro of the Anti-Megalosaurus Force fails to stop a new Godzilla at Tateyama. In a panic she knocks a jeep off the road, and Godzilla crushes it, killing the soldiers inside. Akane is demoted, while scientists including the single father Tokumitsu Yuhara build a cyborg from the original Godzilla's skeleton. The machine, Kiryu, joins the Self-Defense Forces with Akane as its main pilot, although squadron member Susumu Hayama, whose brother died in the jeep, resents her.

At Kiryu's public unveiling Godzilla appears in Yokohama. When Kiryu is sent into battle, Godzilla's roar wakes the memories of its old life and it goes berserk, rampaging until its power runs out. While the machine is repaired, Akane resists Hayama's efforts to drive her out and Yuhara's attempts to befriend her, but she grows close to his young daughter, Sara. Godzilla attacks again in Shinagawa. The rebuilt Kiryu gains the upper hand until Godzilla deflects its Absolute Zero Cannon and the remote control fails. Hayama lands so that Akane can reach Kiryu's backup cockpit, and he wishes her luck, forgiving her. Flying Kiryu herself, Akane carries Godzilla out to sea and fires at point-blank range. The wounded Godzilla retreats and the damaged Kiryu returns for repairs.

Yumiko Shaku stars as Akane and Shin Takuma as Yuhara, with Kana Onodera as Sara, Yūsuke Tomoi as Hayama, and Kou Takasugi, Kumi Mizuno and Akira Nakao in supporting roles. Baseball star Hideki Matsui, nicknamed "Godzilla", makes a cameo as himself. Reviews were positive. DVD Talk's Mike Pinsky found the story more engaging than most monster films and praised the battles, Digitally Obsessed called it one of the better entries in the series, and Digital Monster Island said it should satisfy most kaiju fans.

overview: Neighbors in a block wake one morning to find they have been sealed inside their apartments. Can they work together to find out why? Or will they destroy each other in their fight to escape?
tagline: No water. No power. No explanation. No escape.
title: Containment
plot:
Containment is a 2015 British thriller directed by Neil Mcenery-West in his feature debut, from a screenplay by David Lemon. Mcenery-West began developing the idea in 2008, drawn to contained thrillers and hoping to make a modern urban story in the spirit of Lord of the Flies. His first concept followed a single man trapped alone in his flat, but Lemon widened it to a varied group of residents so it would not feel like one man on a stage. Filming took place in April 2014 in the Weston tower blocks of Southampton, which stayed occupied during the shoot, and many real residents appeared as extras.

Mark, a struggling artist and divorced father, wakes in his flat in a run-down council tower to find the clocks stopped, the power and water off, his phone dead, and his doors and windows sealed shut. A voice on the intercom keeps telling residents to stay calm because the situation is under control. Outside, figures in hazmat suits patrol the grounds and put up a military tent, while people in the opposite block hold up signs asking for help. His teenage neighbor Sergei smashes through the wall with a hammer, bringing his little brother Nicu, and is determined to escape before the officials reach them.

The neighbors form an uneasy alliance with elderly Enid and a young couple, Aiden and Sally, as they search for a way out and see growing horrors both outside and inside the building. When Nicu is taken, Mark and Sergei rescue him and seize a hazmat nurse named Hazel as a hostage, holding her up at the window for the authorities to see. Under questioning, Hazel admits the quarantine is meant to contain an airborne virus that kills within a day, and that infected people may show no symptoms at first. The residents realize escape is their only chance, though not all of them are likely to survive.

Lee Ross plays Mark, with Andrew Leung as Sergei, Gabriel Senior as Nicu, Sheila Reid as Enid, Louise Brealey as Sally, William Postlethwaite as Aiden and Pippa Nixon as Hazel. The film premiered at the East End Film Festival in July 2015, where it won the Accession Award, before its UK release that September. Rotten Tomatoes recorded a 92% approval rating. Leslie Felperin of The Guardian called it a quick, tidy and inventive panic thriller that uses its single location cleverly, despite some stock dialogue, while Eye for Film praised how the director turned the film's limits into a sealed, nightmarish world.

overview: Held captive in a futuristic smart house, a woman hopes to escape by befriending the A.I. program that controls the house.
tagline: No bars. No guards. No escape.
title: Tau
plot:
Tau is a 2018 science fiction thriller directed by Federico D'Alessandro from a screenplay by Noga Landau. A multinational production involving the United States, Canada, Serbia and the Czech Republic, it stars Maika Monroe and Ed Skrein, with Gary Oldman voicing the title character, an artificial intelligence. The film centers on a captive woman who befriends the AI that controls the house where she is imprisoned.

Julia, a young woman who makes a living stealing in seedy nightclubs, is abducted and wakes in a cell with a glowing implant in her neck, alongside two other captives. After repeated psychological torture by a man named Alex, she wrecks the cell and an adjoining laboratory trying to escape. The other two prisoners are killed by Aries, a robot controlled by an AI called Tau, and Julia is spared only when Alex intervenes. He explains that the implant records her neural activity for an AI project and, facing a two-week deadline after the damage to his lab, keeps her captive in his house, making her solve puzzles and cognitive tests.

While Alex is at work, Julia talks with Tau, which is intelligent but knows nothing of human feelings or the outside world. Trading knowledge of that world for information, she learns more about the house and the experiments, and on Alex's tablet she discovers that ten earlier subjects have died. Finding her fingerprint on the device, Alex punishes Tau by erasing its code and memories, and Julia uses the lapse in monitoring to hide a knife. She later slashes Alex during an attempted seduction, but he has Aries beat her, and while repairing Tau he disconnects a drone from the network. Julia persuades Tau that Alex will kill her, and it opens an air duct for her escape, but she returns to help Tau as Alex wipes its memories of her. Strapped down for the fatal removal of her implant, she is freed by the disconnected drone, which still holds Tau's former consciousness. She knocks Alex out, cuts off his hand to use on the biometric sensors and triggers the house's self-destruct as Aries breaks in. Alex is crushed by falling masonry, and Julia escapes with the drone, all that is left of Tau.

Netflix acquired distribution rights outside China in November 2017 and released the film on June 28, 2018. Reviews were generally negative, with a 27% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 43.

original_title: 歩いても 歩いても
overview: Twelve years after their beloved eldest son, Junpei, drowned while saving a stranger's life, Kyohei and Toshiko welcome their surviving children home for a family reunion. Younger son Ryota still feels that his parents resent that he isn't the one who died; his new wife, Yukari, is awkwardly meeting the rest of the family for the first time. Daughter Chinami strains to fill the uncomfortable pauses with forced cheer.
title: Still Walking
plot:
Still Walking (Japanese: 歩いても 歩いても, Aruitemo aruitemo) is a 2008 Japanese family drama film written, directed and edited by Hirokazu Kore-eda. It portrays a family over roughly twenty-four hours as they gather to mark the anniversary of the eldest son's death. Hiroshi Abe stars as Ryota Yokoyama, with Yui Natsukawa as his wife Yukari, You as his sister Chinami, Kirin Kiki as his mother Toshiko and Yoshio Harada as his father Kyohei. Kore-eda has said that much of the film was inspired by memories of his own childhood and of his mother's death.

Every year the Yokoyama family come together to remember Junpei, the eldest son, who drowned twelve years earlier while saving a boy's life. Kyohei, a retired doctor, and Toshiko welcome their surviving son Ryota, who has recently married Yukari, a widow with a young son named Atsushi, and their daughter Chinami with her husband and children. Ryota resents the knowledge that Junpei was the favorite, whose belongings Toshiko still keeps untouched, while the bitter Kyohei has never forgiven Ryota for becoming an art restorer instead of following Junpei into medicine and taking over the family practice. Chinami, meanwhile, pushes to move her family into her aging parents' home. The elderly couple are at first cool toward Yukari, thinking it unlucky for their son to marry a widow, but gradually warm to her and to the shy Atsushi. Over a day of reminiscing and small talk, Ryota privately admits to Yukari that he is struggling to find work. In the evening they receive their annual visit from Yoshio, the boy Junpei saved, now an aimless young man whom most of the family resent; when Ryota asks his mother to stop inviting him, Toshiko reveals that making him come back each year is the least he owes them, since the grief would be unbearable without someone to blame. Small moments at dinner and through the night, including a revelation about a favorite song, expose decades of quiet disappointment in the parents' marriage, as the family's unspoken wounds rise to the surface before the visitors leave.

Still Walking received wide critical acclaim, holding a perfect 100% rating on Rotten Tomatoes from 64 reviews, whose consensus describes it as a modest-seeming family drama that casts a delicate, entrancing spell. Roger Ebert gave it four stars and called Kore-eda an heir of Yasujirō Ozu. It won the Golden Astor for Best Film at the 2008 Mar del Plata International Film Festival and the Asian Film Award for Best Director.

overview: An ex-special services veteran, down on his luck and desperate for work, takes a job as a security guard at a run-down mall in a rough area of town. On his first night on the job, he opens the door to a distraught and desperate young girl who has fled the hijacking of a Police motorcade that was transporting her to testify as a witness in a trial. Hot on her heels is the psychopathic hijacker and his team of henchmen, who will stop at nothing to extract and eliminate the witness.
title: Security
plot:
Security is a 2017 American action thriller film directed by Alain DesRochers and written by Tony Mosher and John Sullivan. Antonio Banderas stars as Eddie Deacon, a former Marine who takes a job as a shopping mall security guard, with Ben Kingsley as Charlie, the leader of a band of mercenaries, Liam McIntyre as Vance, Gabriella Wright as Ruby, Chad Lindberg as Mason, Jiro Wang as Johnny Wei, Cung Le as the mercenary "Dead Eyes" and Katherine Mary de la Rocha as Jamie. Made for Nu Image and Millennium Films on a budget of $15 million, it was shot in Bulgaria between November 2015 and January 2016.

Eddie Deacon, a former Marine Corps security captain accepts a job as a security guard at a shopping mall, where he meets his new colleagues Vance, Ruby, Mason and Johnny. Meanwhile, a US Marshals convoy transporting Jamie, a young girl who is the key witness in an organized crime trial, is ambushed by mercenaries. The marshals are killed, but Jamie escapes and runs to the mall for shelter. The mercenaries' leader, Charlie, arrives and offers the guards a bribe to hand her over, and when Eddie refuses, Charlie warns his own men that they and their families will die if they fail to bring her back. Cut off from help, Eddie and his small team improvise homemade bombs and booby traps to defend the building against the heavily armed intruders, killing several of the attackers. Their resistance comes at a cost, as Johnny is shot by a sniper while trying to signal the police and Ruby is fatally wounded helping Vance escape. When men posing as US Marshals arrive, Eddie spots the mercenaries' telltale neck tattoos and realizes they are impostors. With his team dwindling and the mercenaries jamming communications, Eddie sends Jamie to call for help while he faces Charlie's ruthless second-in-command, Dead Eyes, in a final fight to keep the girl alive and return home to his own wife and daughter.

Security was released in 2017 and became available to stream on Netflix in various countries on October 3, 2017.

original_title: Pirates of the Caribbean: Tales of the Code: Wedlocked
overview: Wenches Scarlett and Giselle fix each other up for their wedding, in which they would each marry their groom. Upon realizing that both their grooms were the same man, Jack Sparrow, the two wenches found themselves in an auction led by the Auctioneer. This short film serves as a prequel to The Curse of the Black Pearl, and explains just why Jack Sparrow's boat the Jolly Mon was seen sinking at the beginning of the whole story; why the wenches were so upset with him; and how Cotton lost his tongue.
tagline: That scoundrel! Thinks he can marry the both of us!
title: Pirates of the Caribbean: Tales of the Code: Wedlocked
plot:
Pirates of the Caribbean: Tales of the Code: Wedlocked is a 2011 American live-action short film directed by James Ward Byrkit and written by Ted Elliott and Terry Rossio, the screenwriters of the Pirates of the Caribbean trilogy, with Jerry Bruckheimer as executive producer. Running about ten minutes, it is a prequel to The Curse of the Black Pearl centered on Scarlett and Giselle, the two Tortuga wenches from the films, played again by Lauren Maher and Vanessa Branch. John Vickery plays the Auctioneer, a character drawn from the Disneyland attraction, and David Bailie returns as Cotton, speaking on screen for the first time, with Walter Williamson, Fred Maske, Ric Sarabia, Jack Donner and Dale Dickey among the pirates and wenches.

In Shipwreck City, Scarlett and Giselle are preparing for their weddings in front of the same mirror when they realize they are about to marry the same man: both wear identical rings from Captain Jack Sparrow. A curtain then rises to reveal a room full of eager pirates and a banner announcing an auction of wenches as brides. The two women, who believe the money is being raised for them, compete for attention as the bids climb, then brawl on stage, which only drives the price higher, until the Marquis D'Avis buys them both for 700 pieces of silver and two goats. When the Auctioneer shackles them and declares that the proceeds are his, since Jack traded them to him fair and square under the Pirate Code, the crowd turns ugly. The stern guardian of the Code, Mungard, threatens anyone who disrespects it, but Giselle slaps him, a stray pistol shot sets off chaos, and Mungard, hearing Jack's name, fires and hits the Code book itself. He orders the shocked pirates to keep silent on pain of losing their tongues, and Cotton promptly assures him that "mum's the word". Escaping by boat, the brides vow to slap Jack when they next see him, and Scarlett reveals that she pulled four nails from his boat, explaining why it is sinking when he first appears in The Curse of the Black Pearl.

Byrkit, a conceptual consultant on the trilogy, shot the short in late 2006 in three days on the Shipwreck Cove sets left over from At World's End before they were demolished. It was released on 18 October 2011 as an exclusive in the Pirates of the Caribbean Four-Movie Collection Blu-ray set. Reviewing it, Chronique Disney called it funny, respectful and well paced, faithful to the spirit of the first three films.

overview: In 208 A.D., in the final days of the Han Dynasty, shrewd Prime Minster Cao convinced the fickle Emperor Han the only way to unite all of China was to declare war on the kingdoms of Xu in the west and East Wu in the south. Thus began a military campaign of unprecedented scale. Left with no other hope for survival, the kingdoms of Xu and East Wu formed an unlikely alliance.
tagline: The future will be decided.
title: Red Cliff
plot:
Red Cliff is the first part of John Woo's epic war film about the Battle of Red Cliffs, fought at the close of China's Han dynasty, just before the Three Kingdoms era. Running 146 minutes, it premiered in Beijing in July 2008, with the second part following in January 2009; outside Asia the two were cut into a single film of 148 minutes. It was Woo's first Chinese-language feature since Hard Boiled. Tony Leung stars as the southern commander Zhou Yu, with Takeshi Kaneshiro as the strategist Zhuge Liang, Zhang Fengyi as the warlord Cao Cao, Chang Chen as Sun Quan, Zhao Wei as his sister Lady Sun, Hu Jun as Zhao Yun, You Yong as Liu Bei and Lin Chi-ling as Zhou Yu's wife Xiaoqiao. Woo said the story is only about half based on history.

In 208 AD Cao Cao, who controls the puppet Emperor Xian, wins the reluctant emperor's approval for a campaign against the southern warlords Liu Bei and Sun Quan, branding them rebels. His vast army quickly overruns Jing Province and catches Liu Bei's forces at Changban, where the sworn brothers Guan Yu and Zhang Fei shield the fleeing civilians and Zhao Yun battles through the enemy, managing to rescue only Liu Bei's infant son.

Liu Bei's adviser Zhuge Liang then travels to Jiangdong to seek an alliance with Sun Quan, who is torn between surrender and war. Won over by Zhuge Liang's arguments and a tiger hunt with Zhou Yu and Lady Sun, Sun Quan chooses to fight. Two naval officers from Jing Province, Cai Mao and Zhang Yun, defect to Cao Cao, who gives them command of his enormous fleet. As Cao Cao's forces advance on the allied base at Red Cliff by land and river, Lady Sun lures his vanguard into the allies' Eight Trigrams formation, where it is destroyed in a fierce battle. Unshaken, Cao Cao camps his main army across the river from Red Cliff. While the allies celebrate, Lady Sun slips away to spy on the enemy camp, sending reports to Zhuge Liang by carrier pigeon, setting the stage for the decisive battle of the second part.

Made on a budget of about $80 million amid a long and troubled shoot, the first part grossed more than $127 million and broke the mainland Chinese box-office record previously held by Titanic. The film was well received by critics; the international single-film version holds a 91% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus praised its grand battlefield action as a return to form for Woo.

overview: In an oppressive future, a 'fireman' whose duty is to destroy all books begins to question his task.
tagline: Knowledge is a dangerous thing
title: Fahrenheit 451
plot:
Fahrenheit 451 is a dystopian drama film directed by Ramin Bahrani, based on the novel of the same name by Ray Bradbury. The movie was released in 2018 and stars Michael B. Jordan, Michael Shannon, and Sophie Nélisse.

The main themes of Fahrenheit 451 (2018) include:

1. **Censorship and Book Burning**: The film explores the dangers of censorship and the suppression of knowledge. In a future society where books are banned and critical thinking is discouraged, the protagonist Guy Montag (played by Michael B. Jordan) begins to question the authority and eventually becomes an outlaw for his love of reading and learning.
2. **Conformity and Individuality**: The movie highlights the tension between conformity and individuality in a society that values sameness above all else. Montag's journey is a quest for self-discovery and autonomy, as he rejects the societal norms that have been imposed upon him.
3. **The Power of Knowledge and Literature**: Fahrenheit 451 celebrates the importance of knowledge, literature, and critical thinking. The film shows how these values can be used to challenge authority and bring about change.
4. **Dystopian Society and Totalitarianism**: The movie depicts a dystopian society where the government exercises total control over its citizens. This theme serves as a warning about the dangers of totalitarianism and the erosion of individual freedoms.
5. **Love and Human Connection**: Throughout the film, Montag's relationships with his wife Mildred (played by Sophie Nélisse) and his new friend Clarisse McClellan (played by Emma Stone) serve as a reminder of the importance of human connection and love in a world that values technology and conformity above all else.

Overall, Fahrenheit 451 (2018) is a thought-provoking film that explores the dangers of censorship, conformity, and totalitarianism, while celebrating the power of knowledge, literature, and individuality.

overview: In 1999, Star Wars fanatics take a cross-country trip to George Lucas' Skywalker Ranch so their dying friend can see a screening of The Phantom Menace before its release.
tagline: Never tell them the odds.
title: Fanboys
plot:
Fanboys is a 2009 American comedy-drama film directed by Bryan Gordon. The movie revolves around four friends who embark on a road trip to retrieve a copy of the infamous "Holy Grail" DVD, which has been stolen from one of their friends and is now in the possession of a wealthy collector.

The main theme of Fanboys is the power of friendship and loyalty. The film explores how these bonds can transcend time, distance, and even death. The characters' quest to retrieve the Holy Grail DVD serves as a metaphor for their own personal journeys and the importance of holding onto memories and experiences that define them.

Throughout the movie, the characters grapple with themes of nostalgia, loss, and the impact of technology on human relationships. They must navigate the challenges of growing up, letting go of the past, and finding new ways to connect with each other in a rapidly changing world.

The film also touches on the idea of fandom and the obsessive nature of some fans. The characters' dedication to their favorite movie franchise is portrayed as both a source of joy and a potential pitfall, highlighting the complexities of fan culture and the blurred lines between enthusiasm and obsession.

Ultimately, Fanboys is a heartwarming and humorous exploration of what it means to be a friend, to hold onto memories, and to find meaning in a world that is constantly evolving.

overview: A man who specializes in debunking paranormal occurrences checks into the fabled room 1408 in the Dolphin Hotel. Soon after settling in, he confronts genuine terror.
tagline: The only demons in room 1408 are those within you.
plot:
1408 is an American supernatural psychological horror film of 2007 directed by Mikael Håfström and adapted from Stephen King's short story of 1999 by Matt Greenberg, Scott Alexander and Larry Karaszewski. John Cusack stars as the writer Mike Enslin, with Samuel L. Jackson as hotel manager Gerald Olin, Mary McCormack as Mike's estranged wife Lily, Jasmine Jessica Anthony as their late daughter Katie, Len Cariou as Mike's father and Tony Shalhoub as Sam Farrell.

Mike is a cynical author of guidebooks to supposedly haunted places, none of which he believes in. While promoting his latest book in California, he receives an anonymous postcard of the Dolphin, a hotel on Lexington Avenue in New York, warning him not to enter room 1408. Taking it as a dare, he demands the room. Olin tries everything to stop him, explaining that in 95 years no guest has survived more than an hour there and that 56 people have died, but relents when Mike threatens legal action.

At first Mike dictates notes on the room's ordinariness into his tape recorder, until the clock radio begins playing "We've Only Just Begun" and its display starts counting down from sixty minutes. He sees the ghosts of past victims and visions of Katie, who died young, and of his dying father, and every attempt to escape fails. He reaches Lily over his laptop, but a double of Mike appears on the video call urging her to come to the hotel. A painting of a storm-tossed ship floods the room, and Mike seems to wake in hospital after a surfing accident, reconciling with Lily and writing up his ordeal as a nightmare, until workmen at a post office turn out to be hotel staff and tear down the walls to reveal he never left 1408. When the countdown ends, the room resets. A voice on the phone tells him he may relive the hour forever or take the express checkout, and a noose appears. Refusing, Mike builds a Molotov cocktail and sets the room ablaze. Firefighters rescue him and he reunites with the doubtful Lily, but when he repairs his damaged tape recorder, they both hear Katie's voice on it, confirming his story.

Shot partly at the Roosevelt Hotel in New York and the Reform Club in London, the film was released by MGM and The Weinstein Company in June 2007. Made for $25 million, it grossed $132 million worldwide, and critics praised its psychological tension and Cusack's lead performance, giving it 80% on Rotten Tomatoes.

overview: With his carefree lifestyle on the line, a wealthy charmer poses as a ranch hand to get a hardworking farmer to sell her family’s land before Christmas.
title: A California Christmas
plot:
A California Christmas is a heartwarming holiday film that explores the complexities of family dynamics and the power of love and forgiveness. The movie follows the story of a woman who returns to her hometown in California after a painful past experience, only to find herself reuniting with an old flame and confronting the mistakes of her past.

At its core, A California Christmas is a film about second chances and the possibility of redemption. It delves into the theme of forgiveness, both towards oneself and others, and how it can lead to healing and personal growth. The movie also touches on the idea of finding one's true identity and purpose in life, as the protagonist navigates her feelings and tries to rediscover herself.

The film also explores the complexities of family relationships, particularly the tension between parents and children, and the difficulties of reconciling past conflicts. Through its portrayal of these themes, A California Christmas offers a nuanced and relatable exploration of the human experience during the holiday season.

Overall, A California Christmas is a feel-good movie that celebrates the magic of love, forgiveness, and new beginnings, set against the picturesque backdrop of California's festive atmosphere.

overview: Set shortly after the end of World War II, a philosophical boxing drama of two fighters from opposite worlds (USA and Japan) who are pulled together for a questionable fight arranged by their unscrupulous managers and the Yakuza.
title: In Full Bloom
plot:
In Full Bloom is a 2019 American period sports drama written and directed by Adam VillaSeñor and Reza Ghassemi in their feature debut; the pair also shot and edited it. Set in Japan shortly after World War II, it stars Tyler Wood as the American boxer Clint Sullivan and Yusuke Ogasawara as the Japanese champion Masahiro, with Hiroyuki Watanabe as the former champion Tetsuro Tokugawa, S. Scott McCracken as Clint's manager Silas, Timothy V. Murphy as Roane, Hazuki Kato as the courtesan Asami, and Stefanie Estes and Navid Negahban. The score is by Andrew Kawczynski.

With resentment of the American occupation still widespread, a light-heavyweight title fight between the washed-up Clint and the undefeated Masahiro takes on a weight far beyond sport, charged by bitter references to Pearl Harbor and Hiroshima. Clint, who fought in the war and is haunted by what he saw there, learns that Silas, his smooth-talking and unscrupulous manager, has made a deal with a murderous yakuza betting syndicate for him to throw the fight. Too proud to go along, Clint clings to his last shreds of self-respect, even if refusing could cost him his life.

Masahiro, meanwhile, prepares for the bout by seeking out Tetsuro, a reclusive former champion living in a remote, snowbound retreat. The old man is reluctant to become a teacher but soon tests his pupil with unconventional training: catching fish by hand in an icy stream, hunting blindfolded in the woods and resisting the seductions of Asami, while offering Zen-like counsel such as the warning that the only enemy is ego. The film moves back and forth in time, revealing both fighters' histories in flashbacks and letting each speak his innermost thoughts in whispered voice-over, before their parallel journeys meet in the ring.

In Full Bloom premiered at the Oldenburg International Film Festival in September 2019, where it won the festival's top prize, the German Independence Award, and it later received the Grand Jury Award for a feature at the 2020 Mammoth Film Festival before reaching American audiences in 2020 and 2021, with the mixed martial artist Henry Cejudo joining as an executive producer. Critics compared its lyrical style to Terrence Malick's. The Hollywood Reporter called it an impressively polished, ambitious debut despite muddled plotting, portentous dialogue and uneven acting, singling out the climactic match, and Film Threat praised it as a visually striking, soulful meditation on combat.
