However, when he discovers that his brother, Chris (O'Shea Jackson Jr.), has been arrested by the LAPD, Nate sees an opportunity to use his skills to get his brother out of trouble.

Nate teams up with Big Nick O'Brien (Pablo Schreiber), a ruthless and cunning thief who is being pursued by the FBI. The two men plan to rob a Federal Reserve Bank in downtown Los Angeles, but things quickly go awry when they discover that the bank's security system has been upgraded, making it much more difficult to breach.

As Nate and Big Nick work together to find a way into the bank, they are joined by Chris, who is initially hesitant to get involved in his brother's plans. However, as the situation becomes more desperate, Chris agrees to help his brother, and the three men come up with a plan to infiltrate the bank.

The heist itself is intense and suspenseful, with the three men using their skills and cunning to evade the FBI and the LAPD. However, things take a turn for the worse when Big Nick's true intentions are revealed, and Nate and Chris must work together to survive.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Big Nick has been playing both sides against each other, working with the FBI to bring down his rivals while also using them to further his own interests. In the end, only one man will walk away from the heist alive, and the true nature of Big Nick's betrayal is revealed.

The movie features a talented ensemble cast, including 50 Cent as Berra, a young and ambitious thief who becomes embroiled in the heist. The film also features a strong supporting cast, including Oleg Taktarov as Viktor, a ruthless Russian mobster who is involved in Big Nick's plans.

Overall, Den of Thieves is a tense and suspenseful thriller that keeps viewers on the edge of their seats from start to finish. With its talented cast, intricate plot, and intense action sequences, it's no wonder this movie has become a fan favorite among crime thriller enthusiasts.

overview: A disgraced parole officer is indebted to a local gang leader and forced to pull off a series of dangerous drug heists within twelve hours in order to pay the $2 million dollars he owes, rescue his kidnapped pregnant wife, and settle a score with the city's corrupt police chief, who is working with the gang leader and double-crossed him years ago.
tagline: Only the savage survive.
title: A Day to Die
plot:
A Day to Die is a 2022 American heist action thriller directed, co-written and co-produced by Wes Miller. It stars Kevin Dillon as Connor Connolly, Leon as the drug kingpin Tyrone Pettis, Frank Grillo as Brice Mason and Bruce Willis as the corrupt police official Alston, with Gianni Capaldi, Brooke Butler and Vernon Davis. It was one of the low-budget films Willis made in 2021, shortly before he retired from acting following the disclosure of his cognitive decline.

The film opens with a hostage rescue carried out by Connor, Mason and their elite team on the orders of police captain Alston, an operation that goes badly wrong and leads to the team's breakup. Eighteen months later, Connor is a disgraced but dedicated parole officer, while Alston has risen to police chief. After Connor is forced into killing one of Pettis's young enforcers, a death that leaves him in the kingpin's debt, Pettis kidnaps his pregnant wife Candice and gives him twelve hours to pull off a series of dangerous drug heists and deliver the two million dollars he supposedly owes. Desperate, Connor reunites his old crew, including his brother Tim, Mason, Dwayne and Steve. Pettis is secretly in an uneasy alliance with Alston, financing his political rise in return for protection, and the drug house he sends the team to rob belongs to his main rival. After the heists and a confrontation in which Candice is rescued, Connor and Pettis reach a mutual understanding and stage one final heist to disrupt Alston's criminal operations. Alston is caught on camera shooting a subordinate who was catching on to his schemes and is arrested, while Connor, Pettis and Candice flee the country.

Principal photography began in March 2021 in Jackson, Mississippi, the first feature shot in the city that year, and wrapped after six weeks in April, with final scenes filmed at Hawkins Field Airport. Vertical Entertainment acquired the rights in May 2021 and released it in select theaters and on video on demand on 4 March 2022. Against a five-million-dollar budget, it grossed under 100,000 dollars abroad. Critics found it generic. Decider advised viewers to skip it, faulting a choppy, confusing opening, awkward CGI blood and a muddled plot with a finale borrowed from Heat, while praising Leon's performance and Grillo's gravitas and noting that many of Willis's lines are delivered over the phone. Some action-focused outlets called it a serviceable, bullet-riddled time-waster with a strong final battle.

overview: When a China-run oil refinery is attacked in Mosul, Iraq, a Chinese private security contractor is called in to extract the oil workers. He learns, however, that the attackers’ real plan is to steal a fortune in oil, and teams up with an American former Marine to stop them.
title: Project X-Traction
plot:
Project X-Traction, released in most markets as Hidden Strike, is an action-adventure film directed and edited by Scott Waugh from a screenplay by Arash Amel, starring Jackie Chan, John Cena, Ma Chunrui and Pilou Asbæk. The project began as a pairing of Chan with Sylvester Stallone, who withdrew and was replaced by Cena. It was shot in 2018, with Chinese locations standing in for the Middle East, and Cena spent months living in Yinchuan to work on it. Before its final title, it was known variously as Ex-Baghdad, Project X, Project X-Traction and SNAFU.

In Iraq, repeated attacks by mercenaries under former special forces soldier Owen Paddock force the closure of an oil refinery owned by the Chinese firm Unicorp. Security contractor "Dragon" Luo Feng leads a convoy of eleven buses carrying its civilian staff, among them chief engineer Professor Chang, her son and his own estranged daughter Mei, along the Highway of Death toward the Green Zone. Former US Marine Chris Van Horne, who needs money to repair a well in a rural village, reluctantly joins his mercenary brother Henry in the attack. Using a jet-engined truck to raise a sandstorm, the mercenaries seize two buses and take Professor Chang and her son hostage, as Owen plans to force her to restart the refinery and steal its oil.

Disgusted, Chris turns on Owen, who murders Henry. After fighting off French mercenaries together, Feng and Chris become allies, and Feng repairs his bond with Mei. Owen threatens the village to recover the notebook of restart codes that Chris had taken by accident, and Chris hands it over to protect the villagers. When Owen sends the oil away in a convoy of fuel trucks, the heroes storm the refinery, wreck the convoy with the jet truck and drive Owen's vehicle off a cliff. Later they fix the village well, and Chris accepts Feng's invitation to join him on a new mission.

Released in July 2023, theatrically in the United Arab Emirates and some other markets and on Netflix elsewhere, it grossed under $1 million in cinemas against an $80 million budget. On Netflix it became the most-watched film worldwide in its opening weekend, with 56.8 million views in 28 days. Critics were largely negative, with 24% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and complaints about weak chemistry between the leads, although some reviewers enjoyed it as light popcorn entertainment.

overview: When a nuclear missile was fired at Washington in 1945, Captain America managed to detonate it in the upper atmosphere. But then he fell miles into the icy depths of the North Atlantic, where he remained lost for over sixty years. But now, with the world facing the very same evil, Captain America must rise again as our last hope for survival.
tagline: Saving the world, one enemy at a time.
title: Ultimate Avengers: The Movie
plot:
Ultimate Avengers: The Movie is a 2006 animated superhero film produced by Marvel Animation. The movie brings together some of Marvel's most iconic heroes, including Iron Man, Captain America, Thor, Hulk, Black Widow, and Hawkeye.

The main themes of Ultimate Avengers: The Movie revolve around the concept of unity, sacrifice, and the responsibility that comes with great power. Here are some key takeaways:

1. **Unity in the face of adversity**: The movie highlights the importance of teamwork and cooperation among superheroes when faced with a common threat. Despite their differences, the heroes put aside their personal agendas to work together and save the world from the villainous Loki.
2. **Sacrifice for the greater good**: Many characters in the movie are forced to make sacrifices for the sake of others, demonstrating that true heroism involves putting the needs of others before one's own interests. This theme is particularly evident in Captain America's selfless actions and Iron Man's willingness to put himself in harm's way to protect his teammates.
3. **The responsibility that comes with power**: The movie explores the consequences of wielding great power and the importance of accountability. Characters like Thor, who struggles with his newfound abilities, and Hulk, who grapples with his rage-filled nature, serve as cautionary tales about the dangers of unchecked power.
4. **Redemption and forgiveness**: Throughout the movie, characters are given opportunities to make amends for past mistakes or wrongdoing. This theme is particularly relevant in Captain America's storyline, where he seeks redemption for his past actions during the Cold War.

Overall, Ultimate Avengers: The Movie offers a compelling exploration of these themes, showcasing the complexities and nuances of Marvel's iconic heroes as they navigate their relationships with each other and confront the challenges of being superheroes.

overview: During a stopover in Germany in the middle of a carefree road trip through Europe, two American girls find themselves alone at night when their car breaks down in the woods. Searching for help at a nearby villa, they are wooed into the clutches of a deranged retired surgeon who explains his mad scientific vision to his captives' utter horror. They are to be the subjects of his sick lifetime fantasy: to be the first to connect people, one to the next, and in doing so bring to life "the human centipede."
tagline: Their flesh is his fantasy
title: The Human Centipede (First Sequence)
plot:
The Human Centipede (First Sequence) is a 2009 Dutch horror film directed by Tom Six, produced by Six Entertainment, and written by Tom Six. The film's plot revolves around the twisted and disturbing story of three individuals who become connected in a horrific manner.

The movie begins with Dr. Josef Heiter (played by Dieter Laser), a deranged surgeon who has been conducting inhumane experiments on his patients. His latest obsession is to create a human centipede, where three people are surgically connected mouth-to-anus, creating a single, grotesque entity.

The story takes a turn when Lindsay (played by Ashley C. Williams), Jenny (played by Ashlynn Yennie), and Katsuro (played by Sogo Ishii) become the unwitting victims of Heiter's twisted experiment. The three strangers are kidnapped and taken to Heiter's mansion, where they are subjected to various forms of physical and psychological torture.

Heiter's plan is to create a human centipede by connecting Lindsay's mouth to Jenny's anus, and then attaching Katsuro's anus to Jenny's mouth. This would create a single, functioning entity with three mouths and one anus. The idea behind this experiment is to study the digestive system of humans and understand how it functions.

As the story progresses, the three victims are forced to endure unimaginable pain, humiliation, and psychological trauma. They are subjected to various forms of physical abuse, including being forced to eat feces and vomit on each other. The situation becomes increasingly desperate as they try to find a way to escape from Heiter's clutches.

Throughout the film, the audience is left with a sense of unease and discomfort as they witness the graphic and disturbing scenes unfold. The special effects used in the film are particularly noteworthy, as they bring the twisted and grotesque concept of the human centipede to life.

The ending of the film is both shocking and disturbing, leaving the audience with a lasting impression of the horrors that Heiter has inflicted upon his victims. Without giving away too many spoilers, it's safe to say that the ending is both gruesome and thought-provoking, leaving the viewer questioning the morality and ethics of Heiter's actions.

Overall, The Human Centipede (First Sequence) is a disturbing and unsettling film that explores themes of torture, psychological trauma, and the boundaries of human decency. While it may not be to everyone's taste, the film is undeniably a work of art that will leave even the most seasoned horror fans with a lasting sense of unease.

overview: A former mob enforcer who is released from prison after serving 22 years for a crime he didn't commit sets out on a path for revenge against the people who wronged him.
tagline: Revenge Is Coming
title: A Score to Settle
plot:
A Score to Settle is a 2019 American crime thriller film directed by Kevin Goetz and Angela Bettis. The movie follows two brothers, Mike (played by Luke Mitchell) and Tom (played by James Badge Dale), who are on the run from the law after being wrongly accused of murdering their father.

The main themes of A Score to Settle include:

1. **Redemption**: Throughout the film, both brothers strive for redemption, trying to clear their names and make amends for a mistake they didn't commit.
2. **Brotherly Love**: The bond between Mike and Tom is tested as they navigate their situation together, showing that despite their differences, they are willing to do whatever it takes to protect each other.
3. **Guilt and Guilt Tripping**: As the brothers try to escape their predicament, they must confront their own guilt and learn to let go of the past. This theme is particularly evident in Tom's character development as he grapples with his role in their father's death.
4. **The Power of Truth**: The film highlights the importance of seeking truth and justice, even when it's difficult or uncomfortable. Mike and Tom's determination to uncover the real events surrounding their father's murder drives the plot forward.

Overall, A Score to Settle explores complex themes that delve into the human condition, making for a gripping and thought-provoking watch.

overview: A 16-year-old girl and her extended family are left reeling after her calculating grandmother unveils an array of secrets on her deathbed.
tagline: Growing up. One mistake at a time.
title: Summer '03
plot:
Summer '03 is a 2018 American coming-of-age comedy-drama written and directed by Becca Gleason in her feature debut. Joey King stars as sixteen-year-old Jamie Winkle, with Jack Kilmer as Luke, Andrea Savage as her mother Shira, Paul Scheer as her father Ned, June Squibb as her grandmother Dotty, and Erin Darke, Kelly Lamor Wilson, Stephen Ruffin and Logan Medina in supporting roles. The cinematography is by Ben Hardwicke, the editing by Josie Azzam and the music by Nathan Matthew David.

In the summer of 2003, Jamie's family is thrown into turmoil when her manipulative, anti-Semitic grandmother Dotty, on her deathbed, summons each relative in turn and hands out insults, outrageous advice and long-buried secrets before dying contentedly. The revelations set off a chain of chaos. Jamie's father learns that he never knew his biological father and abandons the family to track him down, returning days later with an ailing German man who insults Jamie's Jewish mother. Jamie's younger cousin Dylan (Medina), told by Dotty to seek out a gay conversion camp, steals his parents' car and nearly gets himself killed. Dotty's most pointed instruction to Jamie concerns sex, a subject her more experienced friend Emily (Wilson) is happy to explain. Searching for meaning during a summer of bad choices, Jamie neglects her devoted friend March (Ruffin), who is in love with her, and begins a secret fling with Luke, a seminary student eager to sample worldly pleasures before his ordination who says he chose the priesthood for its job security. Grounded by her clueless parents and torn between guilt and desire, Jamie finally confronts the family's hypocrisy in a frank monologue at Dotty's funeral, pointing out that her grandmother disliked her mother simply for being Jewish.

Principal photography began in Atlanta, Georgia, on 19 September 2017. The film premiered at South by Southwest on 10 March 2018 and was released by Blue Fox Entertainment on 28 September 2018. Reviews were mixed, with 63% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus praised Gleason's earnest direction despite the clichés, and a Metacritic score of 45. RogerEbert.com called it possibly King's finest showcase, admiring Squibb's deadpan matriarch, Kilmer's sympathetic performance and the film's tender, honest approach to teenage sexuality, while other critics found the plot scattered and underdeveloped.

original_title: Beavis and Butt-Head Do the Universe
overview: In 1998, Beavis and Butt-Head are sentenced to Space Camp by a “creative” judge. Their obsession with a docking simulator (huh huh) leads to a trip on the Space Shuttle, with predictably disastrous results. After going through a black hole, they re-emerge in our time, where they look for love, misuse iPhones, and are hunted by the Deep State. Spoiler: They don’t score.
tagline: The dumbest science fiction movie ever made.
title: Beavis and Butt-Head Do the Universe
plot:
Beavis and Butt-Head Do the Universe is a 2022 American adult animated science fiction comedy film directed by Mike Judge, who also created the original series. The movie follows the misadventures of Beavis and Butt-Head as they travel through space and time.

The main themes of the movie include:

1. **Existentialism**: The film explores existentialist ideas about the meaninglessness of life and the search for purpose. Beavis and Butt-Head's journey is a metaphor for their own aimless existence, as they struggle to find direction and significance in an indifferent universe.
2. **Nihilism**: The movie critiques nihilistic ideologies that reject traditional values and morality. Beavis and Butt-Head's actions are often driven by self-interest and a desire for pleasure, highlighting the absurdity of their worldview.
3. **Pop Culture Satire**: As with much of Mike Judge's work, the film is a satire of modern pop culture, particularly music videos and social media. The movie pokes fun at the superficiality and vacuity of contemporary society.
4. **Friendship and Loyalty**: Despite their absurd behavior, Beavis and Butt-Head are ultimately depicted as loyal friends who stick together through thick and thin. Their relationship is a commentary on the importance of human connection in an often-meaningless world.

Throughout the movie, Judge uses humor, irony, and absurdity to explore these themes, often subverting audience expectations and challenging conventional notions of what it means to be alive.

overview: The life story of Elvis Presley as seen through the complicated relationship with his enigmatic manager, Colonel Tom Parker.
tagline: The Man. The Legend. The King of Rock & Roll.
title: Elvis
plot:
Elvis is a 2022 musical epic biographical drama film directed and co-produced by Baz Luhrmann, who wrote the screenplay with Sam Bromell, Craig Pearce and Jeremy Doner. It chronicles the life of the American singer and actor Elvis Presley through his long association with his manager, Colonel Tom Parker. Austin Butler stars as Presley and Tom Hanks as Parker, with Olivia DeJonge, Helen Thomson, Richard Roxburgh, David Wenham, Kodi Smit-McPhee and Luke Bracey in supporting roles. Announced in 2014, the project stalled in development until Hanks joined in 2019, and filming wrapped in March 2021.

Raised largely by his devoted mother Gladys, the young Elvis grows up poor in Tupelo, Mississippi, and after the family moves to Memphis he is drawn to the African-American music of Beale Street. Parker, a former carnival huckster managing country singer Hank Snow, hears "That's All Right" and recognizes Elvis's crossover appeal, then witnesses the frenzy his performance provokes at the Louisiana Hayride and persuades him to hand over control of his career. Elvis rises meteorically, moving to RCA Records and lifting his family out of poverty, but his suggestive dancing alarms segregationist politicians, and Parker steers him into the Army to avoid legal trouble. Elvis is devastated by his mother's death, meets the young Priscilla Beaulieu while serving in West Germany and, after his discharge, turns to films and marries her. Shaken by the assassinations of Martin Luther King Jr. and Robert F. Kennedy in 1968, he defies Parker's plans for a wholesome Christmas special and, working with director Steve Binder, delivers a triumphant comeback ending with "If I Can Dream". Elvis then conquers Las Vegas, but Parker, burdened by gambling debts, blocks his wish for a world tour and traps him in a long casino residency. As exhaustion and prescription drug addiction take their toll and Priscilla leaves with their daughter Lisa Marie, Elvis learns the truth about Parker's stateless past, yet remains bound to his manager until his death in 1977.

Elvis premiered at the Cannes Film Festival on 25 May 2022 and was released by Warner Bros. Pictures in June. It grossed $288.7 million worldwide against an $85 million budget, received generally positive reviews, with Rotten Tomatoes' consensus praising Luhrmann's dazzling style and Butler's outstanding performance, and earned eight Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture and Best Actor.

overview: Cecilia and her son embark on a journey. On the third day, she is found wandering alone, not remembering what happened during this time. She is desperately looking for her son and finds herself wrapped in a brutal hunt, carried out by a religious fanatic, whom she faces off against. To her, he's a lunatic. To him, Cecilia is the enemy.
tagline: Hell is coming.
title: On the Third Day
plot:
On the Third Day (Spanish: Al 3er día) is a 2020 Argentine horror thriller directed by Daniel de la Vega from a screenplay by Alberto Fasce and Gonzalo Ventura, produced by Del Toro Films and Furia Films. It stars Mariana "Moro" Anghileri as Cecilia and Gerardo Romano as Enrique, with Diego Cremonesi as Fernando, Lautaro Delgado Tymruk, Osvaldo Santoro as Ventura, Osmar Núñez, Octavio Belmonte as Martín, Verónica Intile, Arturo Bonín and Rodolfo Ranni. Luciano Onetti composed the music. It runs about 85 to 88 minutes and carried the tagline "Hell is coming."

Cecilia, a young divorced mother, sets off into the night by car with her small son Martín, apparently eager to leave everything behind. On the way they have a serious, strange accident. Three days later Cecilia is found wandering alone and disoriented and cannot remember anything that happened in the meantime. Desperate to find her son, she struggles to make herself heard by the police and doctors while being pursued by the stubborn veteran detective Ventura and by her abusive ex-husband Fernando, confiding only in a kind doctor. In a parallel storyline, the film follows Enrique, a priest whom Cecilia encountered on her interrupted journey and who appears to be on a violent mission of his own, carrying an axe in his pick-up truck. As further disappearances and murders lead back to Cecilia and Martín, she is drawn into a brutal hunt led by the religious fanatic and must confront him. To her, he is a lunatic; to him, she is the enemy. Mirrors recur throughout the film, opening onto Cecilia's memories through hallucinations and double images, and the mystery is only fully revealed in the final act, which turns towards the supernatural.

The film premiered in Argentina on CineAR TV and the streaming platform CineAR Play in February 2021 and was later screened at the Fantasia International Film Festival. Reviews were divided. Adolfo C. Martínez of La Nación rated it good, praising de la Vega's handling of suspense and a cast in which Anghileri, Romano, Núñez and Santoro were impeccable. Santiago García of LeerCine found the plot predictable, the scares ineffective and Romano miscast. Signal Horizon, reviewing it at Fantasia, admired Anghileri's strong central performance but called the film a confused pastiche of giallo, possession and torture horror with weak computer effects and makeup.

overview: A family is forced to live in silence while hiding from creatures that hunt by sound.
tagline: If they hear you, they hunt you.
title: A Quiet Place
plot:
A Quiet Place is a 2018 American horror-thriller film directed by John Krasinski, who also co-wrote the screenplay with Bryan Woods and Scott Beck. The film stars Emily Blunt, John Krasinski, Millicent Simmonds, and Noah Jupe.

The story takes place in a post-apocalyptic world where creatures that hunt by sound have wiped out much of humanity. The film follows the Abbott family - Lee (John Krasinski), Evelyn (Emily Blunt), and their children Regan (Millicent Simmonds) and Marcus (Noah Jupe) - who live in a rural area, trying to survive in silence.

The creatures, which are blind but have an acute sense of hearing, can detect even the slightest sound. The family must navigate their daily lives without making any noise, using sign language and creative methods to communicate with each other. They also use a system of taps on the wall to signal danger or important events.

The story begins with Evelyn giving birth to Regan in a hospital, where she is forced to make a difficult decision to save her baby's life by sacrificing her own hearing. The family then moves to their rural home, where they try to live in silence and avoid attracting the creatures' attention.

As the story progresses, the family faces various challenges, including a neighbor who becomes infected with the creatures after being attacked, and Evelyn's growing concern about Regan's ability to communicate with her family without making noise. The tension builds as the family tries to protect themselves from the creatures, while also dealing with their own personal struggles.

One of the most striking aspects of the film is its use of sound design, which creates a sense of unease and tension throughout. The creatures' movements are often accompanied by eerie sounds, such as rustling leaves or snapping twigs, which make it impossible for the audience to look away.

The climax of the film takes place in an abandoned church, where Evelyn and Regan must navigate through the darkness to find a way out. Along the way, they encounter the creatures, who are attracted by Regan's tapping on the wall. The scene is intense and suspenseful, with the audience holding its breath as Evelyn tries to protect her daughter.

In the end, Evelyn manages to save Regan, but not without great personal cost. The film ends with a sense of hope and renewal, as Evelyn and Regan begin to rebuild their lives in silence.

Overall, A Quiet Place is a masterclass in tension and suspense, with a unique premise that is both terrifying and thought-provoking. The film's use of sound design and its exploration of themes such as family and sacrifice make it a standout in the horror genre.

overview: A saga of class relations and changing times in an Edwardian England on the brink of modernity, the film centers on liberal Margaret Schlegel, who, along with her sister Helen, becomes involved with two couples: wealthy, conservative industrialist Henry Wilcox and his wife Ruth, and the downwardly mobile working-class Leonard Bast and his mistress Jackie.
title: Howards End
plot:
Howards End is a thought-provoking period drama that explores the complexities of social class, relationships, and personal growth in early 20th-century England. The film delves into the lives of two families from different walks of life, the Schlegels and the Wilcoxes, and their interconnected experiences.

At its core, Howards End is a nuanced exploration of the human condition, examining the tensions between individuality and conformity, as well as the struggle for social mobility and self-discovery. The film's protagonist, Helen Schlegel, embodies the spirit of independence and intellectual curiosity, which serves as a catalyst for her relationships with both the aristocratic and working-class characters.

The movie also delves into the theme of class divisions and the rigid social hierarchies of the time, highlighting the constraints placed on individuals by their social status. The character of Leonard Bast, a poor but proud tenant farmer, serves as a poignant example of the struggles faced by those living outside the upper echelons of society.

Furthermore, Howards End is a rich tapestry of relationships, exploring the complexities of love, friendship, and family dynamics. The film's portrayal of the intricate web of connections between its characters adds depth and nuance to the narrative, underscoring the idea that personal relationships can transcend social boundaries.

Ultimately, Howards End is a powerful exploration of the human experience, one that invites viewers to reflect on their own values, loyalties, and sense of belonging. The film's thoughtful pacing and rich characterizations make it a thought-provoking and emotionally resonant viewing experience.

overview: As the plague decimates medieval Europe, rumours circulate of a village immune from the plague. There is talk of a necromancer who leads the village and is able to raise the dead. A fearsome knight joined by a cohort of soldiers and a young monk are charged by the church to investigate. Their journey is filled with danger, but it's upon entering the village that their true horror begins.
tagline: In an age of darkness one man will face the ultimate battle against evil.
title: Black Death
plot:
Black Death is a 2010 historical horror film directed by James Wan and starring Jamie Campbell Bower, Carice van Houten, and Charlie Hunnam.

The movie is set in 14th-century England during the time of the Black Death pandemic. The main theme of the film revolves around the fear of the unknown and the breakdown of societal norms as people succumb to the deadly plague. As the disease spreads rapidly, the characters are forced to confront their own mortality and the collapse of traditional values.

The film explores the idea of chaos and anarchy that ensues when the rules of society no longer apply. The characters must navigate a world where the normal constraints of behavior and morality are thrown out the window, leading to a descent into madness and violence.

At its core, Black Death is a movie about the human condition in the face of unimaginable horror and suffering. It delves into the psychological effects of living through one of humanity's darkest periods, highlighting the fear, desperation, and despair that can grip individuals when faced with an existential threat.

The film also touches on themes of faith, superstition, and the role of religion in times of crisis. As the characters struggle to understand the cause of the plague, they turn to their faith for answers, leading to a exploration of the tensions between spirituality and scientific inquiry.

Overall, Black Death is a visceral and unsettling movie that plunges viewers into the midst of a medieval nightmare, forcing them to confront the darkest aspects of human nature in the face of unimaginable terror.

overview: After 29-year-old Adaline recovers from a nearly lethal accident, she inexplicably stops growing older. As the years stretch on and on, Adaline keeps her secret to herself  until she meets a man who changes her life.
tagline: Love is timeless.
title: The Age of Adaline
plot:
The Age of Adaline is a 2015 American romantic drama film directed by Lee Toland Krieger, written by J. Mills Goodloe and Kelly Marcel, and produced by Lakeshore Entertainment.

The movie begins with Adaline Bowman (played by Blake Lively), a beautiful young woman who lives in the United States during World War II. On her 29th birthday, while walking home from work, she is hit by a car and suffers severe injuries that leave her clinically dead for 129 years. When Adaline awakens, she finds herself in the present day, but with no memory of her past life.

As Adaline tries to adjust to her new life, she meets Ellis Jones (played by Michiel Huisman), a charming and handsome man who becomes infatuated with her. However, their budding relationship is complicated by Adaline's mysterious past and her inability to remember anything before the car accident.

Throughout the film, Adaline struggles to come to terms with her immortality and the weight of living for centuries without aging. She has witnessed historical events unfold, including wars, assassinations, and social movements, but she is unable to form lasting connections with people due to her inability to remember their faces or their lives.

As Adaline navigates her new life, she meets William "Ellis" Jones (played by Michiel Huisman), a man who becomes her love interest. Despite the danger of revealing her true nature, Adaline finds herself falling for Ellis, but she is hesitant to open up to him due to her fear of losing him.

As their relationship deepens, Adaline must confront the consequences of her immortality and the secrets she has kept hidden for so long. She also begins to realize that her past is not just a series of random events, but a complex web of relationships and experiences that have shaped her into the person she is today.

The film's climax revolves around Adaline's decision to reveal her true nature to Ellis, who ultimately accepts her for who she is. The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Adaline finally able to form a lasting connection with someone and find a sense of belonging in the world.

Overall, The Age of Adaline is a beautifully crafted film that explores themes of love, loss, and identity. With its stunning visuals, engaging storyline, and memorable performances, it's no wonder this movie has captured the hearts of audiences worldwide.

overview: It’s just weeks before Christmas when Ellie gets a call to return home to help her father on the family’s poinsettia farm. The family business is on the line to deliver tens of thousands of plants for the town’s annual parade. The problem is — the poinsettias have yet to turn red! As Ellie searches for the solution, she is reminded of where her heart truly lies as she falls in love with both her roots and a local botanist.
title: Poinsettias for Christmas
plot:
Poinsettias for Christmas is a 2018 Canadian-American romantic holiday television film directed by Christie Will Wolf and made for Lifetime, with Johnson Production Group and Annuit Coeptis Entertainment among its production companies. It stars Bethany Joy Lenz as Ellie Palmer, Marcus Rosner as Sean and John Schneider as Ellie's father, with Sharon Lawrence, Lauren London and Rhonda Dent in the supporting cast. It runs 87 minutes and is set in a small town in Maryland.

Ellie is a career-driven city planner who enjoys a busy urban life. Just weeks before Christmas, she is called home to help on her family's poinsettia farm because her father has hurt his back and cannot keep up during the busiest season of the year. The family business must deliver tens of thousands of plants for the town's annual Christmas parade, but on arrival Ellie discovers that the real problem is worse: the poinsettias are still green and have yet to turn red. Her parents admit that this is why they really needed her, since she has always had a special touch with the plants. Ellie initially clashes with Sean, a handsome botanist who now works on the farm, spends much of his time with her family and spills dirt on her cashmere coat when they first meet, and she blames him for the problem. As the two try new fertilizer, adjust the watering and argue over the thermostat, they grow closer. Complications come from Patty, Ellie's childhood rival and now a local lifestyle personality with her own show, who is dating Sean and offers to buy the farm. Ellie eventually realizes that the town's new development is to blame: the city lights at night are preventing the plants from changing color. The poinsettias turn red in time, but Ellie must still decide whether her future lies in the city or back home with her roots and the man she has fallen for.

The film premiered on Lifetime during the 2018 holiday season. Reviewers found it light and predictable but pleasant. Very Merry Movies called it an enjoyable, quick-paced film that was not too schmaltzy and that far exceeded its title, praising Lenz while regretting that the rivalry with Patty was shallow and that the story had too little Christmas in it, likening it to an HGTV episode crossed with a Hallmark movie. Patrick Serrano of Lifetime Uncorked gave it a rating of two Christmas trees, poking fun at its montages and formula.

overview: When a madman dubbed 'Scorpio' terrorizes San Francisco, hard-nosed cop, Harry Callahan – famous for his take-no-prisoners approach to law enforcement – is tasked with hunting down the psychopath. Harry eventually collars Scorpio in the process of rescuing a kidnap victim, only to see him walk on technicalities. Now, the maverick detective is determined to nail the maniac himself.
tagline: Detective Harry Callahan. He doesn't break murder cases. He smashes them.
title: Dirty Harry
plot:
Dirty Harry is a 1971 American action thriller film directed by Don Siegel and starring Clint Eastwood as the iconic character Inspector Harry Callahan.

The main themes of Dirty Harry include:

1. **Tough on Crime**: The film's portrayal of a tough, no-nonsense law enforcement officer who operates outside the boundaries of traditional police procedure resonated with audiences in the early 1970s. This theme was particularly relevant during the height of the Vietnam War and the social unrest of the time.

2. **Personal Justice**: Harry Callahan is driven by a personal sense of justice, which often puts him at odds with his superiors and the law. This theme explores the idea that individual justice can be more effective than bureaucratic or institutionalized justice.

3. **The American Dream**: The film's protagonist, Harry Callahan, represents the quintessential American hero: tough, resourceful, and unapologetic. The movie taps into the American Dream of self-reliance and individual freedom, even if it means operating outside the law.

4. **Social Commentary**: Beneath its action-packed surface, Dirty Harry contains social commentary on issues like police corruption, racial tensions, and the breakdown of social norms in urban America during the 1970s.

5. **Moral Ambiguity**: The film's portrayal of a complex, morally ambiguous character in Inspector Callahan raises questions about the nature of justice and the morality of taking the law into one's own hands.

Overall, Dirty Harry is a classic example of an action movie that explores themes of personal justice, social commentary, and moral ambiguity, all set against the backdrop of 1970s America.

overview: The youngest of King Triton’s daughters, and the most defiant, Ariel longs to find out more about the world beyond the sea, and while visiting the surface, falls for the dashing Prince Eric. With mermaids forbidden to interact with humans, Ariel makes a deal with the evil sea witch, Ursula, which gives her a chance to experience life on land, but ultimately places her life – and her father’s crown – in jeopardy.
title: The Little Mermaid
plot:
The Little Mermaid is an American musical fantasy film of 2023, Disney's live-action remake of its animated film of 1989, which was loosely based on Hans Christian Andersen's fairy tale. Directed by Rob Marshall from a screenplay by David Magee, it stars Halle Bailey as the mermaid Ariel and Jonah Hauer-King as Prince Eric, with Melissa McCarthy as the sea witch Ursula, Javier Bardem as King Triton, Noma Dumezweni as Queen Selina, Art Malik as Grimsby and the voices of Daveed Diggs as Sebastian, Jacob Tremblay as Flounder and Awkwafina as Scuttle.

In the undersea kingdom of Atlantica, in the Caribbean, Ariel collects human objects in a secret grotto, though her father Triton forbids merfolk to visit the surface because a human killed her mother. One night she swims up to watch fireworks from a ship carrying Eric, prince of a nearby island. When a storm wrecks the ship, she saves him, brings him to shore and sings to him, vanishing before he fully wakes. Learning from the crab Sebastian that she rescued a human, Triton smashes her collection. Ursula, Triton's banished sister, then offers Ariel a deal: three days as a human in exchange for her voice. If she wins true love's kiss she stays human; if not, she returns to the sea and her soul belongs to Ursula.

Found on the shore and taken to the palace, Ariel bonds with Eric, who has been seeking the girl who saved him, over his collection of treasures from his travels, and they tour the island together. Sebastian discovers that Ursula's spell makes Ariel forget she needs the kiss, and he, Flounder and Scuttle nearly bring the couple together before Ursula's eels intervene. Ursula then takes human form as Vanessa and uses Ariel's voice to bewitch Eric, who announces their engagement. Alerted by Scuttle, Ariel breaks the shell holding her voice, freeing Eric, but the sun sets before they can kiss. To save his daughter, Triton gives himself up to Ursula, who seizes his trident, grows to enormous size and raises a storm and sunken ships. Ariel steers a wreck to impale her on its broken bowsprit, Triton is restored, and he transforms Ariel into a human so she can be with Eric, the couple setting off on travels together with both families' blessing.

Released in May 2023, the film grossed $569.6 million worldwide. Reviews were mixed to positive, with 67% on Rotten Tomatoes, and Bailey was widely praised.

overview: A mysterious video has been linked to a number of deaths, and when an inquisitive journalist finds the tape and views it herself, she sets in motion a chain of events that puts her own life in danger.
tagline: One curse, one cure, one week to find it
title: Ringu
plot:
Ring (Ringu) is a 1998 Japanese supernatural psychological horror film directed by Hideo Nakata and written by Hiroshi Takahashi, adapted from Koji Suzuki's 1991 novel. Nanako Matsushima, Miki Nakatani and Hiroyuki Sanada star in the story of a reporter racing to unravel a cursed videotape that kills its viewers seven days after they watch it. Released in North America as Ringu, it was shot back to back with the sequel Spiral and the two films opened together in Japan.

At a sleepover, schoolgirl Tomoko tells her friend Masami about a legend of a videotape that dooms its viewers to die a week after a mysterious phone call, then admits that she and her friends watched such a tape a week earlier. Moments later the television switches itself on and Tomoko is killed by an unseen presence. Her aunt, journalist Reiko Asakawa, learns that the three friends who watched with her all died at the same moment. At a resort cabin in Izu where the group stayed, Reiko finds an unlabeled tape of disjointed images and screeching sounds ending with a shot of a well. After watching it she sees an apparition and receives a phone call carrying the same sounds.

Reiko turns to her psychic ex-husband, Ryūji Takayama, who studies a copy and finds a message in the dialect of Ōshima island. Before they leave, Reiko catches their son, Yōichi, watching the tape. On Ōshima they learn of Shizuko Yamamura, a psychic who became notorious after a public demonstration arranged by her lover, researcher Dr. Heihachiro Ikuma, before her suicide, and a vision reveals that her young daughter, Sadako, psychically killed a journalist who mocked her mother. Returning to the Izu cabin, they discover a sealed well beneath it and learn through another vision that Ikuma trapped Sadako inside it. Concluding that her rage gave birth to the curse, they drain the well and recover her remains. When Reiko survives her deadline, they believe the curse is lifted, but the next day Sadako crawls out of Ryūji's television and kills him. Reiko realizes that she was spared because she copied the tape and showed it to someone else, and she drives to her father's house to make him watch it and save Yōichi.

Distributed by Toho, Ring became the highest-grossing horror film in Japan, earning about ¥1.7 billion there. Critics praised its atmosphere and themes, giving it 98% on Rotten Tomatoes. It spawned a franchise and English-language remakes beginning with The Ring (2002) and helped spark a wave of Japanese horror.

overview: Following the passing of his father, Aaron Hammond returns to his hometown to help his devastated mother and to confront his past demons. Sifting through his father’s belongings, Aaron comes upon a mysterious item that is far more than it seems.
title: The Final Wish
plot:
The Final Wish is a 2018 American supernatural horror film directed by Timothy Woodward Jr. and written by Jeffrey Reddick, William Halfon and Jonathan Doyle, with Reddick also serving as co-producer. Michael Welch stars as Aaron Hammond, a young man who unwittingly unleashes a wish-granting evil, and Lin Shaye plays his grieving mother, Kate, with Melissa Bolona, Spencer Locke and Tony Todd in supporting roles.

The film opens with a girl coming home from a date to find her mother hacked in half and her blood-soaked father holding a samurai sword. Years later, after his father's death, Aaron, a struggling law school graduate, returns to his small hometown, where his relationship with his mother remains strained. Sorting through his father's collection of antiques, he finds a recently acquired urn and tries to sell it online for $3,000 to cover his overdue rent. Without realizing it, he has freed a malevolent spirit trapped inside, and the careless wishes he blurts out begin to come true in terrible ways. Wishing that Kate could forget his father and move on, he leaves her stripped of her memories and lost in confusion, and later finds her dancing in the barn with his father's corpse. His best friend, Jeremy, vanishes, and Aaron learns from Jeremy's mother that he died in a car accident a year earlier.

With his friend Lisa, Aaron consults an antiques dealer, who suggests the urn may be a dybbuk box, an object from Jewish folklore said to hold evil spirits. They trace its previous owner, William, the man who killed his wife in the opening scene and later cut out his own tongue; visiting him in an asylum, they learn in writing that a seventh wish will cost Aaron his soul. The djinn begins to taunt him, and Aaron finds his mother hanged in the barn. When the local sheriff warns him away from Lisa, Aaron wishes that the man would stop hurting her, only for the spirit to twist the wish into a deadly confrontation in which the sheriff is shot and Lisa is accidentally killed. With his final wish, Aaron chooses to undo his own life, and he awakens with his soul trapped in a mirror. At a yard sale, Kate, now alive and preparing to move, hands the urn to Lisa, who invites her to visit in Chicago, hinting that the curse will continue.

The Final Wish premiered at the Screamfest Horror Film Festival on October 17, 2018, and was distributed by Cinedigm. It holds a 67% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes from a small number of reviews.

overview: Set against the backdrop of San Francisco’s Chinatown, this cross-cultural biopic chronicles Bruce Lee’s emergence as a martial-arts superstar after his legendary secret showdown with fellow martial artist Wong Jack Man.
tagline: The Fight That Created The Legend
title: Birth of the Dragon
plot:
Birth of the Dragon is a 2016 martial arts film directed by George Nolfi, not 2017, and produced by Blumhouse Productions, but released in 2016. The movie is based on the true story of the infamous fight between Wong Jack Man (Bruce Lee) and Wong Jack Man's rival, Ah Sahm (Yuen Biao), which took place in San Francisco's Chinatown in 1964.

The main themes of Birth of the Dragon include:

1. Cultural Identity: The film explores the clash between traditional Chinese culture and modern American society, as embodied by the two protagonists. Wong Jack Man represents a traditional Chinese martial artist who has come to America seeking fame and fortune, while Ah Sahm is a more modern and adaptable fighter.
2. Friendship and Loyalty: The movie highlights the complex friendship between Wong Jack Man and Ah Sahm, which is tested when they engage in their legendary fight. The film also explores the loyalty that both characters have for their respective families and communities.
3. Racism and Xenophobia: Birth of the Dragon touches on the racist attitudes prevalent in 1960s America, particularly towards Chinese immigrants. The film portrays how these prejudices can lead to violence and conflict between different groups.
4. Identity and Belonging: Both Wong Jack Man and Ah Sahm struggle with their identities and sense of belonging. Wong Jack Man is torn between his traditional Chinese roots and his desire for success in the American martial arts scene, while Ah Sahm must navigate his own identity as a Chinese-American fighter.

Overall, Birth of the Dragon is a gripping and thought-provoking film that explores themes of cultural identity, friendship, loyalty, racism, and belonging.

overview: Max, a macho, solitary Rottweiler police dog is ordered to go undercover as a primped show dog in a prestigious Dog Show, along with his human partner, to avert a disaster from happening.
tagline: Unleashed and undercover
title: Show Dogs
plot:
Show Dogs is a 2018 buddy cop comedy directed by Raja Gosnell from a screenplay by Max Botkin and Marc Hyman, mixing live action with talking animals. Filming began on November 28, 2016, at Pinewood Studio Wales in Great Britain, with further scenes shot on location in Las Vegas. The film was released in the United States on May 18, 2018, and reached DVD and Blu-ray that August.

Max, a tough Rottweiler serving as a police dog, tries to rescue Ling-Li, a baby giant panda that an animal smuggling ring is preparing to sell. In doing so he accidentally ruins an FBI sting run by his human partner, Frank, who blames the dog for letting the criminals escape. Forced to cooperate despite their mutual dislike, the two go undercover as a show dog and his handler at the prestigious Canini Invitational dog show in Las Vegas, hoping to unmask the smugglers from inside the competition.

Ludacris voices Max and Will Arnett plays Frank, with Natasha Lyonne as Mattie and Omar Chaparro as Señor Gabriel. The voice cast also includes Stanley Tucci as the Papillon Philippe, Jordin Sparks as Daisy, an Australian Shepherd, Gabriel Iglesias as the Pug Sprinkles, Shaquille O'Neal as the Komondor Karma, RuPaul as Persephone and Alan Cumming as Dante.

Reviews were negative. Rotten Tomatoes gave it a 16% approval rating and Metacritic a score of 31, although CinemaScore audiences awarded an A−. Christy Lemire gave it half a star, Peter Hartlaub gave it none, and Mark Kermode later named it the worst film of 2018, while The Hollywood Reporter was more forgiving of its self-aware script. Shortly after release, critics and parents' groups objected to a subplot in which Max must let a judge touch his genitals and is told to go to his "happy place", arguing that it normalized child grooming. Botkin said the script had been heavily rewritten by other writers, and the distributor Global Road Entertainment apologized, removed two scenes and sent a revised cut to theaters for the second weekend. The British Board of Film Classification considered the scene non-sexual and the US concerns a misinterpretation. Made for $5.5 million, the film grossed $40 million worldwide.

overview: For Pablo Escobar family is everything. When young surfer Nick falls for Escobar's niece, Maria, he finds his life on the line when he's pulled into the dangerous world of the family business.
tagline: Welcome to the family
title: Escobar: Paradise Lost
plot:
Escobar: Paradise Lost is a 2014 biographical crime drama film directed by Daniel Muñoz and produced by Nexus Factory. The movie tells the story of Pablo Escobar, the infamous Colombian drug lord who was responsible for the deaths of thousands of people.

The film begins with Pablo Escobar (played by Wagner Moura) as a young man growing up in Medellín, Colombia. He is portrayed as a charismatic and ambitious individual who becomes involved in the local crime syndicates at an early age. As he rises through the ranks, Escobar's ambition and desire for wealth and power drive him to become one of the most powerful men in Colombia.

The plot follows Escobar's rise to power, his involvement in the cocaine trade, and his eventual downfall. The film depicts Escobar's ruthless tactics, including the use of violence and intimidation to eliminate his enemies and maintain control over his empire. At the same time, it also shows his softer side, particularly his relationship with his wife, María (played by Deborah Young), and his love for his children.

As Escobar's power grows, so does his ego, and he becomes increasingly paranoid and isolated. He is eventually forced to flee Colombia after a failed assassination attempt on his life. The film depicts his subsequent attempts to evade capture and maintain his lifestyle, including the use of fake identities and safe houses.

Meanwhile, the Colombian government and law enforcement agencies are determined to bring Escobar down. The film shows the cat-and-mouse game between Escobar's henchmen and the authorities, as well as the personal toll it takes on those involved in the pursuit.

The movie culminates with Escobar's eventual capture by Colombian police at his private ranch in Medellín. In a dramatic and intense confrontation, Escobar is killed in a shootout with the authorities. The film ends with a sense of closure for María and their children, who are finally able to move on from the trauma and pain caused by Escobar's actions.

Throughout the film, the cinematography and direction create a visceral and immersive experience, drawing the viewer into the world of Pablo Escobar and his empire. The performances by the cast, particularly Wagner Moura as Escobar, are also noteworthy, capturing the complexity and nuance of this infamous figure.

Overall, Escobar: Paradise Lost is a gripping and intense biographical drama that explores the life and times of one of the most notorious figures in modern history.

overview: When one school teacher gets the other fired, he is challenged to an after-school fight.
tagline: After school. Parking lot. It's on.
title: Fist Fight
plot:
Fist Fight is a 2017 American comedy film directed by Thomas McCarthy and starring Ice Cube and Charlie Day.

The movie follows two high school teachers, Andy Campbell (Ice Cube) and Ron Strickland (Charlie Day), who engage in a physical altercation after being forced to participate in a mandatory staff meeting. The fight escalates into a series of events that disrupt the entire school, leading to chaos and hilarity.

Some of the main themes present in Fist Fight include:

1. **The struggle for authority**: Both Andy and Ron are struggling with their own personal demons and feel disrespected by their school's administration. They take matters into their own hands, leading to a series of confrontations that challenge their authority.
2. **Mentorship and fatherhood**: As the story progresses, it becomes clear that both characters have a deep desire to be seen as positive influences in their students' lives. The fight serves as a catalyst for them to re-evaluate their priorities and find ways to connect with their students on a more meaningful level.
3. **The absurdity of bureaucracy**: The film pokes fun at the red tape and petty politics that often plague schools. The characters' frustration with the system is palpable, and their actions serve as a commentary on the frustrations many teachers face in their daily lives.
4. **Redemption and personal growth**: Through their experiences, both Andy and Ron are forced to confront their own flaws and weaknesses. They learn to put aside their differences and work together to resolve the situation, ultimately emerging with a newfound sense of respect for each other and themselves.

Overall, Fist Fight is a comedy that uses humor to explore themes of authority, mentorship, and personal growth in a relatable and entertaining way.

overview: Nicolas Bannister, a rugged and solitary veteran living in a near-future Miami flooded by rising seas, is an expert in a dangerous occupation: he offers clients the chance to relive any memory they desire. His life changes when he meets a mysterious young woman named Mae. What begins as a simple matter of lost and found becomes a passionate love affair. But when a different client's memories implicate Mae in a series of violent crimes, Bannister must delve through the dark world of the past to uncover the truth about the woman he fell for.
tagline: Don't look back.
title: Reminiscence
plot:
Reminiscence is a 2021 science fiction film directed by Lisa Joy and written by Joy and Nathaniel Malathat. The movie stars Hugh Jackman, Rebecca Ferguson, and Cliff Curtis.

The main themes of Reminiscence revolve around the concept of memory, identity, and humanity in a world where virtual reality (VR) has become indistinguishable from reality. The story follows Nick Bannion (Hugh Jackman), a "memory detective" who uses VR to experience and manipulate memories for his clients.

One of the primary themes is the exploration of what it means to be human in a world where technology can alter or even replace our experiences. As Nick delves deeper into the mysteries of memory, he begins to question the nature of reality and his own identity. The film raises questions about the consequences of relying on technology to manipulate and control memories, and whether this can lead to a loss of authenticity and connection with others.

Another significant theme is the power dynamics at play in relationships, particularly between Nick and his partner, Dr. Lydia Mercer (Rebecca Ferguson). Their relationship is complex and multifaceted, with both characters struggling to navigate their own desires, needs, and boundaries. The film explores the tension between control and surrender, as well as the blurred lines between love and obsession.

The movie also touches on the idea of nostalgia and the human desire to hold onto memories, even if they are painful or traumatic. Nick's work as a memory detective allows him to experience and manipulate memories, but it also forces him to confront his own past and the traumas he has experienced.

Ultimately, Reminiscence is a thought-provoking exploration of what it means to be human in a world where technology is rapidly changing our experiences and relationships. The film raises important questions about identity, memory, and connection, leaving the audience to ponder the implications of these themes long after the credits roll.

overview: Three people, three extraordinary stories. All lived out within a hundred London streets.
tagline: Anybody can take a wrong turn.
title: 100 Streets
plot:
100 Streets is a 2016 British ensemble drama directed by Jim O'Hanlon from a screenplay by first-time feature writer Leon F. Butler, who also produced and raised its roughly £3 million budget from private investors. Idris Elba, who also served as a producer, stars alongside Gemma Arterton, Franz Drameh, Ken Stott, Charlie Creed-Miles, Kierston Wareing, Tom Cullen and Jo Martin. The production companies included CrossDay Productions and Green Door Pictures and the music is by Paul Saunderson. The title comes from Cicely Fox Smith's poem "The Oldest Thing in London".

The film weaves together three stories unfolding at the same time within about one square mile of London, each centered on a man forced to face the consequences of his past actions as he struggles toward a better life. In wealthy Chelsea, Max (Elba), a celebrated former England rugby captain, is in a bitter trial separation from his wife Emily (Arterton), an actress who gave up her career, after his infidelity came to light. As she tries to return to the stage and drifts into a romance with her old flame Jake (Cullen), Max sinks into heavy drinking and cocaine use. On a council estate south of the river, Kingsley (Drameh), a teenager with a gift for words and performance, has slipped into drug dealing and gang violence, to the dismay of his weary single mother (Martin), until a chance encounter with the aging actor Terence (Stott) offers him a way out through the theatre. Between these two worlds, the gentle cab driver George (Creed-Miles) and his patient wife Kathy (Wareing) hope to adopt a child and start a family, but their plans are thrown into turmoil when George is involved in a fatal road accident. As the stories progress, chance meetings and coincidences increasingly connect the characters, showing how circumstance and choice shape their fates.

The film premiered at the Los Angeles Film Festival in June 2016, opened in British cinemas through Vertigo on 11 November 2016, and reached American theaters and video-on-demand via Samuel Goldwyn Films on 13 January 2017. Critical reception was lukewarm, with 41% on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 44, the consensus finding its talented cast stranded in a well-meaning but contrived drama. Variety likened it to a gentler London version of Crash, praising Drameh's promising performance, Arterton and Blaubach's bright cinematography but calling the script banal, while The Guardian also considered it a misfire.

overview: In 1984, a group of LGBT activists decide to raise money to support the National Union of Mineworkers during their lengthy strike. There is only one problem: the Union seems embarrassed to receive their support.
tagline: Based on the inspirational true story.
title: Pride
plot:
Pride is a 2014 historical comedy-drama written by Stephen Beresford and directed by Matthew Warchus. Based on a true story, it follows the lesbian and gay activists who raised money for mining families during the 1984 miners' strike, the start of the Lesbians and Gays Support the Miners campaign. It premiered in the Directors' Fortnight at Cannes, where it won the Queer Palm, and opened in British cinemas on 12 September 2014.

Watching news coverage of the strike, London activist Mark Ashton notices that the police have shifted their harassment from gay people to the miners. After a bucket collection at the Pride march, he founds LGSM, joined by the closeted 20-year-old student Joe and by Jonathan and Gethin, whose bookshop Gay's the Word becomes its base. Frustrated by the lack of response, the group takes its donations directly to the Welsh village of Onllwyn. Local spokesman Dai Donovan gives a moving speech of thanks in a gay bar, and although Maureen leads a walkout when LGSM first visits, Hefina and the outspoken newcomer Siân James help win the village round, especially after Jonathan's legal knowledge frees detained miners.

Maureen leaks the story to a tabloid, and the activists answer by staging the "Pits and Perverts" benefit concert headlined by Bronski Beat. But a hastily brought-forward union vote rejects further help, Mark is shaken by a former lover's hint that he has AIDS, Gethin is badly beaten, and Joe is outed to his parents. When the strike ends in March 1985, Joe leaves home and Mark rejoins the group, and at the 1985 Pride march LGSM is joined by hundreds of miners. An epilogue recounts the union's support for gay rights within the Labour Party and Mark's death from AIDS at 26.

Ben Schnetzer plays Mark, Bill Nighy plays Cliff, Paddy Considine plays Dai and Imelda Staunton plays Hefina, with Dominic West, Andrew Scott, George MacKay and Joseph Gilgun. Critics were highly positive, with 92% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and comparisons to The Full Monty and Billy Elliot, and the film earned more than £3.2 million in the UK in its first four weekends. It was nominated for the Golden Globe for Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy and for three BAFTAs, and a stage musical version premiered in Cardiff in 2026.

overview: Three friends discover a mysterious machine that takes pictures 24 hours into the future and conspire to use it for personal gain, until disturbing and dangerous images begin to develop.
tagline: Once you see the future, you can't look away.
title: Time Lapse
plot:
Time Lapse is a 2014 American independent science fiction thriller directed by Bradley D. King in his directorial debut and starring Danielle Panabaker, Matt O'Leary and George Finn. It follows three friends who find a machine that photographs events 24 hours in the future, trapping them in increasingly complex causal loops.

Finn, a blocked painter who manages an apartment complex, lives there with his girlfriend, Callie, and his best friend, Jasper. Checking on an elderly tenant, Mr. Bezzerides, who has not paid his rent, they find a machine in his apartment that takes a Polaroid of their living room window every evening at eight, a day ahead of time, and then discover his charred body in his storage unit. Jasper, a gambler, wants to use the photos to win bets, and the next picture shows that they do, as well as a new painting by Finn, which he copies to overcome his block. Believing from the old man's notes that they must make every photo come true, they hide his death. When a photo shows Callie kissing Jasper, the staged kiss stirs Finn's jealousy, and soon Jasper's violent bookie, Ivan, learns of the machine and forces them to pose with gambling results for him.

After a photo showing a crude skull on the canvas, Jasper convinces Ivan that the next picture shows his death, then stabs Ivan's enforcer, Marcus, and kills Ivan. Mr. Bezzerides's colleague Dr. Heidecker arrives with a photo he mailed her before his death, showing blood on the window and a painting of a coil, and explains that he died from gas released by a coil he knocked over, not from defying time. Jasper shoots her, then locks Finn in the storage unit so that a photo of Callie and Jasper having sex can come true. Finn escapes, and in the ensuing fight Callie kills Jasper. Finn then learns that the camera also takes a photo at 8 a.m., which Callie has secretly used to send herself messages and manipulate events to win him back, and that the sex photo dated from a drunken night a month earlier. When Finn rejects her and moves to destroy the machine, Callie shoots him, producing the blood in Heidecker's photo. She posts a note on the window hoping to reset events, but it falls away, the timeline proving fixed.

The film premiered at the Brussels International Fantastic Film Festival in April 2014. Reviews were positive, with a 78% rating on Rotten Tomatoes; The Hollywood Reporter said it made the most of a simple brain-teasing premise.

overview: Cube Zero is the third film in the trilogy yet this time instead of a film about people trapped in a deadly cube trying to get out we see it from the eyes of someone who is controlling the cube and the torture of the victims inside. When the nerd can’t stand to see a woman suffer he himself enters the cube to try and save her.
tagline: Every nightmare has a beginning.
title: Cube Zero
plot:
Cube Zero is a thought-provoking sci-fi thriller that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the consequences of playing with forces beyond one's control.

At its core, Cube Zero explores the theme of existential crisis, where characters are forced to confront their own mortality and the meaninglessness of their existence. The movie takes place in a mysterious, labyrinthine structure known as "The Cube," where a group of individuals are trapped and subjected to a series of gruesome and surreal challenges.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that The Cube is not just a physical prison but also a psychological one, designed to break down its inhabitants and expose their deepest fears and insecurities. The movie masterfully crafts an atmosphere of tension and unease, where characters are forced to confront their own demons and question the nature of reality.

Throughout the film, the main theme of survival is expertly woven, as characters must rely on each other to stay alive in a desperate bid for escape. However, this theme is not just about physical survival but also about emotional and psychological resilience. The movie raises questions about the human condition, highlighting our capacity for cruelty, compassion, and self-sacrifice.

Ultimately, Cube Zero is a gripping and unsettling film that challenges its viewers to confront the darker aspects of human nature and the consequences of playing with forces beyond one's control.

overview: After a series of brutal slayings, a teen and her friends take on an evil force that's plagued their notorious town for centuries.
tagline: Face the evil.
title: Fear Street: 1994
plot:
Fear Street: 1994 is a 2021 American supernatural horror film directed by Leigh Janiak and written by Phil Graziadei. The movie is based on the first book in R.L. Stine's popular Fear Street series.

The story takes place in Shadyside, Ohio, where three high school students - Sam (Mia Goth), Deena (Jordana Brewster), and Margot (Zoey Deutch) - are struggling to cope with their respective traumas. Sam is haunted by a dark presence from her past, while Deena is dealing with the aftermath of a tragic accident that took the life of her best friend. Margot, on the other hand, is trying to navigate her complicated relationships with her friends and family.

The three girls meet at a local diner, where they share their stories and form an unlikely bond. They soon discover that Shadyside has a dark history, particularly when it comes to the infamous "Shadyside Slasher" who terrorized the town in 1994.

As the story unfolds, Sam begins to experience strange and terrifying occurrences that seem to be connected to the Shadyside Slasher. She becomes convinced that the killer is still active and is targeting her specifically. Deena and Margot try to help Sam uncover the truth behind the murders, but they soon realize that the lines between reality and myth are blurred.

Throughout the movie, Janiak expertly weaves together elements of horror, mystery, and coming-of-age drama. The film's pacing is relentless, with a steady stream of jump scares and creepy atmosphere that will keep viewers on the edge of their seats.

As the story reaches its climax, Sam discovers that the Shadyside Slasher was not just a random killer, but a symbol of the town's dark secrets and the trauma that has been buried for decades. The film's final act is both shocking and thought-provoking, leaving viewers to ponder the true nature of evil and the power of female friendship.

Overall, Fear Street: 1994 is a chilling and atmospheric horror film that pays homage to the classic slasher movies of the 1980s while still managing to feel fresh and modern. With its talented cast, clever plot twists, and eerie atmosphere, this movie is sure to delight fans of the genre.

overview: Monstrous creatures leap from a magical storybook and unleash mayhem and mischief for Auntie Opal and her tween niece Nina in this spooky short film.
title: Erax
plot:
Chocolat is a 2000 romantic drama film that explores the complexities of human nature and the transformative power of desire. The story revolves around Vianne Rocher, a young widow who opens a chocolate shop in a small French village, bringing with her a sense of liberation and temptation.

At its core, Chocolat is a tale of self-discovery and the struggle for individuality in a society that often values conformity. Vianne's arrival sparks a chain reaction of events that challenge the moral fabric of the community, forcing its residents to confront their own desires and inhibitions.

The film delves into the theme of temptation, not just as a physical desire, but also as a metaphor for the human condition. The chocolate shop becomes a symbol of indulgence and pleasure, representing the allure of the forbidden and the thrill of the unknown. Through Vianne's character, the film explores the idea that our desires can be both liberating and destructive, depending on how we choose to navigate them.

Furthermore, Chocolat touches on the theme of community and social hierarchy. The village is portrayed as a tight-knit, conservative society where tradition and conformity are deeply ingrained. Vianne's arrival disrupts this status quo, forcing the residents to confront their own prejudices and biases. As they grapple with their desires and inhibitions, they are also forced to reevaluate their relationships with one another.

Ultimately, Chocolat is a film about the human condition, with all its complexities and contradictions. It invites us to reflect on our own desires, values, and relationships, encouraging us to embrace our individuality and find the courage to follow our hearts.

overview: Seminary student Michael Kovak reluctantly attends exorcism school at the Vatican. While he’s in Rome, Michael meets an unorthodox priest who introduces him to the darker side of his faith, uncovering the devil’s reach even to one of the holiest places on Earth.
tagline: You can only defeat it when you believe.
title: The Rite
plot:
The Rite is a supernatural horror film directed by Mikael Håfström and released in 2011 by New Line Cinema.

The movie follows Michael Kovak (played by Anthony Hopkins), a former priest who has lost his faith after the death of his son. He is now working as an exorcist, but he's struggling to find purpose in his life. Kovak is assigned to train a young priest named Michael Kovak Jr. (played by Colin O'Donoghue), who is eager to become an exorcist.

Kovak takes the younger man under his wing and teaches him the ways of exorcism, but he also warns him about the dangers of demonic possession. As Kovak Jr. begins his training, he starts experiencing strange occurrences that make him question his own faith and sanity.

The story takes a dark turn when Kovak Jr. is sent to Rome to complete his training at the Vatican's Pontifical Academy of Sciences. There, he meets Father Lucas (played by Ciarán Hinds), a seasoned exorcist who becomes his mentor. However, it soon becomes clear that something is amiss in the academy, and Kovak Jr. begins to suspect that one of his fellow students may be possessed by a demon.

As the story unfolds, Kovak Jr. discovers that he has a personal connection to the demonic entity, which makes him more susceptible to its influence. The demon, known as "The Rite," is an ancient evil that feeds on human fear and suffering. It's a powerful and malevolent force that will stop at nothing to claim its next victim.

As Kovak Jr. delves deeper into the mystery of the demonic possession, he must confront his own demons (no pun intended) and face the darkness within himself. With the help of Father Lucas, he embarks on a perilous journey to uncover the truth behind The Rite and find a way to defeat it.

The movie builds up to a thrilling climax as Kovak Jr. faces off against the demon in a desperate bid to save his own soul and those of others. In the end, Kovak Jr. emerges victorious, but not without scars. He has learned a valuable lesson about the power of faith and the importance of confronting one's fears head-on.

Throughout the movie, Anthony Hopkins delivers a standout performance as the seasoned exorcist Michael Kovak. His character serves as a mentor and guide for Kovak Jr., while also providing a sense of gravitas and authority to the story. The supporting cast, including Colin O'Donoghue and Ciarán Hinds, deliver solid performances that add depth and complexity to the narrative.

Overall, The Rite is a tense and suspenseful horror film that explores themes of faith, doubt, and redemption. With its well-crafted plot and strong performances, it's a must-see for fans of supernatural thrillers.

overview: Craig and his cousin Day Day have finally moved out of their parents' houses and into their own crib, working nights at a local mall as security guards. When their house is robbed on Christmas Eve they set out to track down the culprit.
tagline: The party's back in the 'hood!
title: Friday After Next
plot:
Friday After Next is a 2002 American stoner comedy film directed by Fred Durst and written by Fred Durst, David Zuckerman, and Chris "Ludacris" Bridges. The movie stars Ice Cube, Mike Epps, and Faizon Love.

The main themes of Friday After Next revolve around the struggles of growing up, friendship, and finding one's identity. The film takes place during a snowstorm on Christmas Eve in Atlanta, Georgia, where three friends - Big Worm (Mike Epps), B-Dawg (Faizon Love), and Big Worm's cousin, Big Worm Jr. (Ice Cube) - try to survive the harsh winter conditions while dealing with their personal issues.

Throughout the movie, the characters face various challenges, including family problems, relationships, and finding a sense of purpose. The film also explores themes of loyalty, friendship, and the importance of supporting one another through thick and thin.

The movie's plot is driven by Big Worm Jr.'s attempts to save his family's Christmas celebration from being ruined by a snowstorm, which serves as a metaphor for the challenges that come with growing up and finding one's place in the world. Ultimately, the film concludes on a heartwarming note, highlighting the power of friendship and the importance of holding onto what truly matters.

Overall, Friday After Next is a lighthearted, entertaining film that explores themes of identity, loyalty, and the struggles of growing up, all set against the backdrop of a hilarious snowstorm.

overview: A detective from Hong Kong teams up with an American gambler to battle against a notorious Chinese criminal.
tagline: Ready. Set. Panic.
title: Skiptrace
plot:
Skiptrace is a 2016 buddy cop action comedy film directed by Renny Harlin and based on a story by Jackie Chan, who also produced it and stars as Hong Kong detective Bennie Chan. Johnny Knoxville co-stars as the American gambler Connor Watts, with Fan Bingbing as Samantha Bai, Eric Tsang as Yung Bai, Winston Chao as Victor Wong and Eve Torres as Dasha. First announced in 2013 as a Sino-American co-production, the film originally cast Seann William Scott as Connor before Knoxville replaced him in 2014. Filming began in China in September 2014; during the shoot, cinematographer Chan Kwok-hung drowned.

In Hong Kong in 2007, detective Bennie Chan is hunting the notorious crime boss known as the Matador, whom he believes to be businessman Victor Wong. During the pursuit, Chan's partner Yung Bai is captured and apparently sacrifices himself, leaving Chan his watch. Nine years later, when Yung's daughter Samantha falls foul of Wong's syndicate, Chan sets out to find Connor Watts, an American conman banned from casinos at home who witnessed the murder of a woman named Esther Yee in Wong's casino in Macau. Before Chan can reach him, Connor is seized by the henchmen of Dima, a Russian kingpin whose daughter Natalya he has made pregnant, and Chan has to fight his way through the Russians to rescue him.
