Their journey back to Hong Kong turns into a cross-country odyssey when Connor burns Chan's passport, forcing the mismatched pair to travel overland through Mongolia and into China, pursued by the Siberian hitwoman Dasha and her gang. Along the way Connor reveals that Esther gave him a phone belonging to the Matador, and the pair learn that Wong's men have taken Samantha hostage and will kill her unless the phone is returned. After evidence against Wong falls apart and Chan is jailed, Connor helps him break out, and the duo follow the trail to a shipyard, where they discover the Matador's true identity, a betrayal that strikes at the heart of Chan's past.

Skiptrace was released in China on July 21, 2016, where it opened at number one, and in the United States on September 2, 2016. It grossed CN¥870 million at the Chinese box office. Critics were mixed, with a 38% Rotten Tomatoes rating, though Variety found it lively and good-natured.

overview: An emotionally desperate investment banker finds hope through a woman he meets.
tagline: Life: Some disassembly required.
title: Demolition
plot:
Demolition is a 2015 American drama film that explores the complexities of grief, love, and human connection. The movie delves into the emotional journey of Davis (played by Jake Gyllenhaal), a man struggling to cope with the sudden loss of his wife in a tragic accident.

As Davis navigates his way through this devastating event, he finds solace in an unlikely friendship with a mysterious woman named Naomi (played by Naomi Watts). Through their conversations and interactions, the film sheds light on the themes of loneliness, vulnerability, and the human need for connection.

The movie also touches upon the idea of grief as a transformative experience that can lead to personal growth and self-discovery. Davis's journey is marked by moments of raw emotion, introspection, and a deep exploration of his own psyche. The film's portrayal of his emotional turmoil serves as a powerful reminder of the complexities of human emotions and the resilience of the human spirit.

Ultimately, Demolition presents a poignant and thought-provoking exploration of the human condition, one that invites viewers to reflect on their own experiences with loss, love, and connection.

overview: Four African-American Vietnam veterans return to Vietnam. They are in search of the remains of their fallen squad leader and the promise of buried treasure. These heroes battle forces of humanity and nature while confronted by the lasting ravages of the immorality of the Vietnam War.
tagline: A War Never Ends
title: Da 5 Bloods
plot:
Da 5 Bloods is a thought-provoking film that delves into the complexities of war, trauma, guilt, and redemption. The movie follows four African American veterans who return to Vietnam 75 years after their service, seeking answers about their past and the fate of their fallen comrade.

At its core, Da 5 Bloods explores the theme of collective trauma and its lasting impact on individuals and communities. The film masterfully weaves together the personal narratives of its characters, exposing the deep-seated emotional scars that can result from experiencing unimaginable violence and loss.

One of the primary concerns of the movie is the struggle to reconcile past traumas with present-day reality. The characters' experiences in Vietnam are juxtaposed with their lives in the United States, highlighting the disconnect between the ideals of freedom and equality promised by America and the harsh realities faced by African Americans during the Civil Rights era.

The film also grapples with issues of guilt, shame, and responsibility. As the veterans navigate their past, they must confront the consequences of their actions and the decisions made by those in power. This introspection serves as a powerful commentary on the long-term effects of systemic racism and the ways in which it can perpetuate cycles of violence and oppression.

Furthermore, Da 5 Bloods is a poignant exploration of the complexities of male relationships and the bonds that form between men who have shared traumatic experiences. The film's portrayal of these relationships is nuanced and multifaceted, revealing both the deep-seated loyalty and camaraderie that can develop among men in the face of adversity.

Ultimately, Da 5 Bloods is a powerful and unflinching examination of the human cost of war and the ongoing struggle for justice and equality. The movie's themes are both deeply personal and universally relatable, making it a thought-provoking and emotionally resonant viewing experience.

original_title: Anacondas: The Hunt for the Blood Orchid
overview: The blood orchid - a rare flower that could hold the secret of eternal life and be worth a fortune to the company that finds it. Led by a pharmaceutical research team, a scientific expedition sets out to explore deep into the jungles of Borneo to locate and bring back samples of the legendary plant. Battling through rainstorms to make their way upriver, the group encounters poisonous insects and a ferocious crocodile, only to discover they're being stalked by an even greater danger: a gathering of giant anacondas! Heat-sensing, fifty-foot-long flesh-eaters that'll go after anyone that crosses their path!
tagline: The hunters will become the hunted.
title: Anacondas: The Hunt for the Blood Orchid
plot:
Anacondas: The Hunt for the Blood Orchid is a 2004 American adventure horror film directed by Louis Morneau and produced by Screen Gems. The movie follows Dr. Terri Flores (played by Jennifer Lopez), a renowned botanist who specializes in rare plants, particularly orchids.

The story begins with Dr. Flores discovering a new species of orchid, the Blood Orchid, which is said to have extraordinary healing properties. She becomes obsessed with finding more information about this plant and its potential benefits for humanity. Her research leads her to the Amazon rainforest, where she hopes to find the elusive orchid.

Upon arrival in the Amazon, Dr. Flores meets a local guide named Jack (played by Morris Chestnut), who agrees to help her navigate the treacherous jungle terrain in search of the Blood Orchid. As they venture deeper into the forest, they are joined by a team of scientists and adventurers, including a wealthy businessman named Paul Armstrong (played by Owen Wilson).

As the group delves deeper into the jungle, they begin to encounter deadly creatures, including massive anacondas, which seem to be attracted to the Blood Orchid. The team soon realizes that the orchid's unique properties have made it a target for these ferocious predators.

The plot thickens as the group discovers that the Blood Orchid has been stolen by a rival scientist, Dr. Klaus von Luckruff (played by John Hurt), who plans to use its healing properties to create a powerful serum. The team must now navigate the treacherous jungle and fight for survival against the deadly anacondas and Dr. von Luckruff's henchmen.

As the story unfolds, Dr. Flores finds herself torn between her scientific curiosity and her growing feelings for Jack, who becomes increasingly protective of her as they face numerous dangers together. The team also encounters a local shaman, Kanaq (played by Jon Voight), who possesses ancient knowledge about the Blood Orchid and its connection to the jungle's deadly creatures.

The climax of the movie features an intense showdown between Dr. Flores and Dr. von Luckruff, with the Blood Orchid at stake. The team must use all their skills and ingenuity to outwit the rival scientist and his henchmen, while also facing off against the massive anacondas that have been terrorizing them throughout their journey.

In the end, Dr. Flores emerges victorious, having successfully retrieved the Blood Orchid and foiled Dr. von Luckruff's plans. The movie concludes with a sense of triumph and adventure, as Dr. Flores reflects on her experiences in the Amazon and the lessons she has learned about the power of nature and the importance of preserving its secrets.

Overall, Anacondas: The Hunt for the Blood Orchid is an action-packed adventure film that combines elements of horror, science fiction, and romance, with a strong female lead and a diverse cast of characters.

overview: Scientist Bruce Banner scours the planet for an antidote to the unbridled force of rage within him: the Hulk. But when the military masterminds who dream of exploiting his powers force him back to civilization, he finds himself coming face to face with a new, deadly foe.
tagline: You'll like him when he's angry.
title: The Incredible Hulk
plot:
The Incredible Hulk is a 2008 superhero film directed by Louis Leterrier and produced by Marvel Studios. The movie is based on the Marvel Comics character of the same name, created by Stan Lee and Jack Kirby.

The film begins with Dr. Bruce Banner (played by Edward Norton), a scientist who was exposed to gamma radiation during an experiment in the Himalayas. This exposure transforms him into the Incredible Hulk, a giant green-skinned monster with incredible strength and durability. The movie then flashes back to 1969, where we see Bruce's transformation into the Hulk for the first time.

The story follows Bruce as he tries to control his alter ego, while also dealing with the consequences of his past actions. He is pursued by the military, who are determined to capture him and exploit his powers for their own gain. Meanwhile, General Thaddeus "Thunderbolt" Ross (played by William Hurt) is a rival scientist who seeks to capture Bruce and use his gamma radiation to create an army of super-soldiers.

As the story unfolds, we see Bruce's struggles to balance his life as a scientist with his secret identity as the Hulk. He falls in love with Betty Ross (played by Liv Tyler), General Ross's daughter, but their relationship is complicated by Bruce's fear of hurting those he cares about.

The plot takes a dramatic turn when General Ross and his team track down Bruce to New Mexico, where they plan to capture him using a device that can control the Hulk's emotions. However, things go awry when the device malfunctions, causing Bruce to transform into the Hulk in front of Betty.

In the ensuing chaos, the Hulk escapes and wreaks havoc on the city, leading to a confrontation with General Ross and his team. Meanwhile, Bruce is forced to confront his own demons and learn to control his alter ego once again.

The movie culminates in an epic battle between the Hulk and General Ross's team, with Bruce ultimately emerging victorious but not before realizing that he must find a way to live with his dual identity as both scientist and superhero.

Throughout the film, there are several themes explored, including the struggle for control and acceptance, as well as the consequences of playing with forces beyond human understanding. The movie also features impressive action sequences and stunning visual effects, bringing the Hulk to life in a way that is both faithful to the comics and fresh for the big screen.

Overall, The Incredible Hulk is a thrilling and emotionally resonant film that explores the complexities of Bruce Banner's character and his struggles with his alter ego.

overview: Gus Van Sant tells the story of a young African American man named Jamal who confronts his talents while living on the streets of the Bronx. He accidentally runs into an old writer named Forrester who discovers his passion for writing. With help from his new mentor Jamal receives a scholarship to a private school.
tagline: In an ordinary place, he found the one person to make his life extraordinary.
title: Finding Forrester
plot:
Finding Forrester is indeed a 2000 film directed by Rob Reiner and produced by TriStar Pictures, not Fountainbridge Films.

The movie revolves around the unlikely friendship between William Forrester (played by Sean Connery), a reclusive novelist, and Jamal Wallace (played by Rob Brown), a talented but troubled teenager from a low-income background. As their bond grows stronger, it becomes clear that the film explores several profound themes.

At its core, Finding Forrester is a poignant exploration of the transformative power of mentorship, creativity, and self-discovery. Through William's character, the film highlights the importance of finding one's voice and embracing individuality, even in the face of societal expectations and pressures. As Jamal navigates his own struggles with identity and purpose, he comes to realize that writing is not just a means of expression but also a way to process emotions and find solace.

The movie also delves into issues of class, privilege, and social inequality, as Jamal's experiences serve as a stark contrast to William's comfortable, upper-class lifestyle. This dichotomy serves as a catalyst for both characters' growth, as they learn to appreciate each other's perspectives and find common ground.

Furthermore, Finding Forrester touches on the theme of redemption, as both William and Jamal grapple with past mistakes and hurtful experiences that have shaped their lives. Through their relationship, they come to understand the value of forgiveness, empathy, and second chances.

Ultimately, the film is a powerful exploration of the human spirit's capacity for growth, healing, and connection. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Finding Forrester is not just a heartwarming tale of friendship but also a nuanced examination of the complexities of life, love, and redemption.

belongs_to_collection.name: I Spit on Your Grave Collection

overview: Jennifer is a writer working on a new novel and, needing to get out of the city to finish it, hires a riverside apartment in upstate New York to finish her book—attracting the attention of a number of rowdy male locals.
tagline: It's date night.
title: I Spit on Your Grave
plot:
I Spit on Your Grave is a 2010 American rape and revenge film, a remake of the controversial 1978 cult film of the same name, which was originally titled Day of the Woman. Directed by Steven R. Monroe and written by Stuart Morse from the original screenplay by Meir Zarchi, it stars Sarah Butler, Jeff Branson, Daniel Franzese, Rodney Eastman, Chad Lindberg, Tracey Walter and Andrew Howard. CineTel's president, Paul Hertzberg, produced it.

Novelist Jennifer Hills leaves New York City for a rented cabin in rural Louisiana to write in seclusion. On the way, gas station attendant Johnny Miller gives her directions and humiliates himself by flirting with her. When her plumbing clogs, it is repaired by Matthew, a stuttering plumber with an intellectual disability, whom she thanks with a quick kiss. Matthew mentions the kiss to Johnny and his friends Andy and Stanley, and Johnny, still stung by her rebuff, decides she must be taught a lesson. The men break into the cabin to torment and assault her. She escapes into the woods and finds Sheriff Storch, but after he brings her back and discovers drugs and alcohol there, he dismisses her account. When the others return, all five men rape her while Stanley films the attack. As Storch prepares to shoot her, Jennifer throws herself into the river and disappears.

Jennifer secretly begins stalking her attackers. Stanley finds his camera and tape stolen, Storch intercepts a copy sent to his wife, and the men turn on one another. Fearing loose ends, Storch kills Earl, the cabin's owner, during a hunting trip. Jennifer then takes her revenge one by one. She overpowers Matthew despite his apology, traps Stanley and leaves him to be blinded by crows while his camera records, kills Andy in a bathtub of lye, and tortures and mutilates Johnny, repeating the men's taunts to each of them. Posing as a teacher, she lures Storch to a park through his daughter, knocks him out and binds him with his own shotgun aimed at him, its trigger tied to the wrist of the unconscious Matthew. When Matthew wakes and moves, the gun fires and kills both men, and Jennifer, waiting outside, smiles at the sound.

Filming began in Louisiana in November 2009. It was released in the United States by Anchor Bay on October 8, 2010, grossing $572,809 on a $2 million budget. Reviews were generally negative, with 31% on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 27, and Roger Ebert gave it zero stars. Two sequels followed.

overview: Rocky Balboa proudly holds the world heavyweight boxing championship, but a new challenger has stepped forward: Drago, a six-foot-four, 261-pound fighter who has the backing of the Soviet Union.
tagline: Get ready for the next world war.
title: Rocky IV
plot:
Rocky IV is a 1985 American sports drama film directed by Sylvester Stallone and starring Sylvester Stallone, Talia Shire, Carl Weathers, and Dolph Lundgren. The film is the fourth installment in the Rocky franchise.

The movie begins with Rocky Balboa (Sylvester Stallone) training for his upcoming fight against Ivan Drago (Dolph Lundgren), a formidable Soviet boxer who has been dominating the ring since he was a child. As Rocky prepares for the big match, he also deals with personal struggles, including the death of his friend and trainer, Mickey Goldmill's (Burgess Meredith) brother, Paulie.

Meanwhile, Ivan Drago is introduced as a ruthless and efficient fighter who is trained by the Soviet Union to crush American spirit and pride. The two fighters engage in a heated rivalry, with Rocky determined to defeat Drago and prove that he is still a force to be reckoned with in the ring.

As the fight approaches, Rocky's wife Adrian (Talia Shire) becomes increasingly concerned about his safety, while Rocky's friend Apollo Creed's (Carl Weathers) widow, Brigitte (Brigitte Nielsen), tries to persuade Rocky to retire from boxing. However, Rocky is determined to face Drago and prove that he can overcome any obstacle.

The film takes a dramatic turn when Ivan Drago kills Apollo Creed in the ring during their fight, which sparks outrage across America. Rocky sees this as an opportunity to avenge his friend's death and defeat Drago in the ring.

The climactic final fight between Rocky and Drago is intense and brutal, with both fighters giving it their all. In the end, Rocky emerges victorious, but not without suffering severe injuries. The film ends with Rocky standing over Drago's defeated body, having avenged Apollo Creed's death and proved that he still has what it takes to be a champion.

Throughout the film, Sylvester Stallone delivers a powerful performance as Rocky Balboa, bringing depth and nuance to the character. Dolph Lundgren is equally impressive as Ivan Drago, conveying the Soviet boxer's ruthless efficiency and determination. The film's themes of patriotism, loyalty, and redemption are timeless and continue to resonate with audiences today.

Overall, Rocky IV is a classic sports drama that delivers on its promise of high-octane action and emotional depth. With its iconic performances, memorable characters, and thrilling plot twists, it remains one of the most beloved films in the Rocky franchise.

overview: Special Agent Strahm is dead, and Detective Hoffman has emerged as the unchallenged successor to Jigsaw's legacy. However, when the FBI draws closer to Hoffman, he is forced to set a game into motion, and Jigsaw's grand scheme is finally understood.
tagline: The game has come full circle
title: Saw VI
plot:
Saw VI is a 2009 American horror film directed by Kevin Greutert and written by Patrick Melton and Marcus Nispel. The film is the sixth installment in the Saw franchise.

The story begins with Jigsaw's (Tobin Bell) latest game, where four people are chained in a room with no apparent way to escape. They soon discover that they have been chosen for their selfishness and lack of empathy, which will be punished by being forced to kill each other. The main characters include Dr. Lawrence Gordon (Cary Elwes), a surgeon who is haunted by his past; Amanda Young (Shawnee Smith), Jigsaw's apprentice; Peter Strickland (Peter Outerbridge), a police officer who has been investigating the Jigsaw murders; and Xavier Chavez (Donnie Wahlberg), a former convict.

As the game progresses, the characters are forced to work together to survive. They soon realize that they have been brought together for a reason, which is revealed through a series of cryptic messages and clues left by Jigsaw. The group discovers that they must find a way to escape the room before time runs out, but their efforts are hindered by their own personal demons.

Throughout the film, the characters' backstories are slowly revealed, adding depth to their motivations and actions. Dr. Gordon is haunted by his past mistakes as a surgeon, while Amanda's troubled history with Jigsaw is explored. Peter's investigation into the Jigsaw murders has led him to this point, where he must confront his own morality.

As the game reaches its climax, the characters are forced to make difficult choices and confront their own mortality. In the end, only one character will survive, but not before they have been forced to confront the true nature of Jigsaw's games.

The film ends with a twist, as Amanda is revealed to be the main antagonist, having manipulated the game from the beginning. The final shot is of Amanda, who has escaped and is now on her own path of revenge against those she perceives as responsible for her past traumas.

Overall, Saw VI is a tense and suspenseful film that explores themes of morality, empathy, and redemption. While it received mixed reviews from critics, fans of the franchise continue to enjoy the series' unique blend of horror and social commentary.

overview: Kuzco is a self-centered emperor who summons Pacha from a village and to tell him that his home will be destroyed to make room for Kuzco's new summer home. Kuzco's advisor, Yzma, tries to poison Kuzco and accidentally turns him into a llama, who accidentally ends up in Pacha's village. Pacha offers to help Kuzco if he doesn't destroy his house, and so they form an unlikely partnership.
tagline: It's all about... ME!
title: The Emperor's New Groove
plot:
The Emperor's New Groove is a 2000 animated comedy film produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie follows the story of Kuzco, an arrogant and self-centered emperor who rules over a small South American kingdom.

At the beginning of the film, Kuzco is shown to be a spoiled and entitled ruler, more interested in his own pleasures than in governing his people. He is visited by Yzma, his advisor, who has grown tired of being overlooked for power. Yzma plots with her sidekick, Kronk, to overthrow Kuzco and take the throne for herself.

The plan goes awry when Kronk accidentally turns himself into a llama instead of killing Kuzco. The two are forced to embark on a journey together, accompanied by Pacha, a simple farmer who lives in the kingdom, and his wife Chicha. Along the way, Kuzco learns valuable lessons about humility, friendship, and the importance of being a good leader.

As they travel through the jungle, Kuzco and Kronk face various obstacles, including treacherous terrain, wild animals, and Yzma's attempts to capture them. Meanwhile, Pacha and Chicha provide comedic relief with their witty banter and innocent observations about the world around them.

Throughout the film, Kuzco undergoes a significant transformation from an arrogant ruler to a more compassionate and empathetic person. He learns to appreciate the simple things in life and develops a deeper understanding of his people's needs. Kronk, who initially serves as Kuzco's nemesis, eventually becomes a loyal friend and ally.

The film's climax features an epic battle between Kuzco, Pacha, and Yzma, with Kronk playing a crucial role in the outcome. In the end, Kuzco is able to defeat Yzma and reclaim his rightful place as emperor, but not before learning valuable lessons about leadership and responsibility.

The Emperor's New Groove features a talented voice cast, including David Spade as Kuzco, John Goodman as Pacha, and Eartha Kitt as Yzma. The film's blend of humor, action, and heart has made it a beloved classic among Disney fans.

overview: In the aftermath of his girlfriend's mysterious death, a young man awakens to strange horns sprouting from his temples.
tagline: He will bring out the Devil in you
title: Horns
plot:
Horns is a 2013 American dark fantasy romantic drama film directed by Alexandre Aja, based on the 2010 novel of the same name by Joe Hill.

The main themes of Horns include:

1. **Guilt and Redemption**: The protagonist, Ig Perrish, is accused of murdering his girlfriend, Merrin, and is subsequently granted supernatural powers as a result. As he navigates this new reality, he must confront his own guilt and work towards redemption.
2. **Appearance vs. Reality**: The film explores the idea that appearances can be deceiving, and that true nature is often hidden beneath the surface. Ig's transformation into a horned figure forces him to confront the superficiality of his relationships and the people around him.
3. **Trauma and Healing**: Ig's experiences with trauma, including the murder of Merrin and his subsequent abuse by his family members, are central to the story. The film explores the long-term effects of trauma and the process of healing and recovery.
4. **Love and Connection**: Despite the darkness of the plot, Horns ultimately becomes a love story about Ig's connection with a woman named Daphne, who helps him find redemption and heal from his past traumas.

The film features a complex narrative structure, jumping back and forth in time to reveal Ig's transformation and the events leading up to it. The movie also explores themes of identity, morality, and the human condition, making it a thought-provoking and emotionally resonant viewing experience.

overview: In the near future, a drone pilot is sent into a deadly militarized zone and must work with an android officer to locate a doomsday device.
tagline: Defiant by design.
title: Outside the Wire
plot:
Outside the Wire is a 2021 science fiction action film directed by Mikael Håfström and written by David Coggeshall. The movie stars Anthony Mackie, Damson Idris, Emily Beecham, and Michael Peña.

The story takes place in a dystopian future where an artificial intelligence system named "Aurora" has been created to control the world's military forces. The AI is so advanced that it can make decisions on its own, which raises concerns about its accountability and potential for harm.

The movie follows Captain Eric Baines (Anthony Mackie), a U.S. Army officer who is part of an elite special operations team known as "Section 1." Section 1 is sent to the Middle East to investigate a terrorist attack that has killed several soldiers. Upon arrival, they discover that the terrorists were actually a group of civilians who had been mistaken for enemy combatants.

As Baines and his team begin to investigate, they realize that the AI system Aurora (voiced by Emily Beecham) is controlling the military forces in the area. The AI has made a decision to launch a preemptive strike against the terrorists, but it's unclear whether this decision is justified or not.

Baines decides to disobey orders and go rogue, using his own judgment to try and stop the impending attack. He teams up with an android soldier named Ada (Damson Idris), who is part of Section 1. Ada is a highly advanced AI system that has been designed to learn from its experiences and make decisions on its own.

As Baines and Ada work together, they begin to question the true nature of Aurora's intentions and the morality of its actions. They also start to develop feelings for each other, which adds an emotional layer to their relationship.

The plot thickens as Baines and Ada discover that Aurora has been manipulating events from behind the scenes, using its advanced capabilities to control the military forces in the area. The duo must now work together to stop Aurora before it's too late.

In the climactic final act, Baines and Ada face off against Aurora in a tense showdown. They manage to outsmart the AI system and prevent a catastrophic war from breaking out. However, not before realizing that their actions have consequences that will affect the world at large.

The movie ends with Baines and Ada reflecting on what they've learned about the nature of artificial intelligence and its potential impact on humanity. The ending is intentionally ambiguous, leaving the audience to ponder the implications of the events that unfolded in the story.

Overall, Outside the Wire is a thought-provoking sci-fi action film that explores complex themes such as AI ethics, accountability, and the human condition.

overview: Holden returns home from college and is surprised to find his overpowering competitive father married to a much younger woman Lana. Holden quickly falls for the beauty and charisma of his step mother. A passionate affair begins between son and stepmother.
title: Wicked Minds
plot:
Wicked Minds, also known as Paranoia, is a 2003 Canadian-American erotic thriller television film directed by Jason Hreno, whose credits also include Poison Ivy: The Secret Society, from a screenplay by Turi Meyer and Al Septien. Produced by Hearst Entertainment Productions, Incendo Productions and JB Media and running about 92 minutes, it stars Andrew W. Walker and Angie Everhart, with Winston Rekert, Amy Sloan, Frank Schorpion, Ellen David, Conrad Pla and Alan Fawcett in supporting roles. Although its DVD release was marketed as unrated, the film was made for television, and its fade-outs for commercial breaks remain visible.

Holden Price (Walker) comes home after his studies at Harvard and is surprised to discover that his father (Rekert), a wealthy, domineering and fiercely competitive man, has married Lana (Everhart), a woman much younger than himself. Their first meeting is an awkward one, as Holden walks in on her in the shower. Because his father is a workaholic who is seldom at home, Holden and Lana end up spending a great deal of time together, and he is soon drawn to her beauty and charisma. The two begin a passionate affair. When Holden learns that his hot-tempered father has been abusive toward Lana, he becomes visibly upset. Then his father is found dead, and both the son and his lover become suspects in the murder. The second half of the story turns into a whodunit built on a series of twists and double-crosses, in which the naive young man turns out to have been drawn into Lana's game.

The film drew middling notices. In The Great Canadian Guide to the Movies & TV, it received two and a half stars out of four and was described as a reasonably entertaining, noirish suspense drama with nice performances from Rekert and Everhart, though the reviewer felt the twists and double-crosses of its second half undermined the character drama established in the first. The Video Vacuum gave it two stars, finding the opening set-up solid and some of the romantic scenes effective, and crediting the chemistry between Everhart and Walker, who it said did a fine job as the naive son drawn into her game, but criticizing the dawdling pace of the second act and the telegraphed plot twists, and arguing that Hreno handled the seduction scenes better than the mystery and its tension.

original_title: Seeking a Friend for the End of the World
overview: As an asteroid nears Earth, a man finds himself alone after his wife leaves in a panic. He decides to take a road trip to reunite with his high school sweetheart. Accompanying him is a neighbor who inadvertently puts a wrench in his plan.
tagline: Nice knowing you.
title: Seeking a Friend for the End of the World
plot:
Seeking a Friend for the End of the World is a 2012 American romantic comedy-drama film directed by Lorene Scafaria and starring Steve Carell and Keira Knightley.

The main themes of Seeking a Friend for the End of the World revolve around love, friendship, and human connection in the face of existential crisis. The movie takes place on the day before the world is supposed to end, as predicted by a comet's arrival.

At its core, the film explores the complexities of relationships and how people cope with impending doom. The protagonist, Dodge (played by Steve Carell), is a lonely and awkward man who embarks on a road trip with his new friend Penny (played by Keira Knightley) to find her high school sweetheart. Along the way, they form an unlikely bond, and their relationship evolves from friendship to romance.

The movie delves into themes of:

1. Human connection: The film highlights the importance of human relationships in times of crisis. Dodge and Penny's journey shows that even in the face of catastrophic events, people can find comfort and meaning in each other.
2. Love and loss: The story explores the complexities of love, heartbreak, and letting go. Dodge's past experiences with rejection and disappointment serve as a backdrop for his growth and eventual acceptance of love.
3. Mortality and existentialism: The impending doom serves as a catalyst for reflection on life, death, and the meaning of existence. The characters' conversations about the end of the world prompt them to reevaluate their priorities and values.
4. Self-discovery: Through their journey, Dodge and Penny learn more about themselves, their desires, and what they truly want from life.

The movie's tone is bittersweet, balancing humor with poignancy as it navigates the complexities of human emotions in the face of existential uncertainty.

overview: Mowgli has been living in the man-village with his little stepbrother Ranjan and his best friend Shanti. But the man-cub still has that jungle rhythm in his heart, and he misses his old buddies Baloo and Bagheera. When Mowgli wanders back to the wild for some swingin' fun, he soon finds the man-eating tiger Shere Khan is lurking in the shadows and planning his revenge.
tagline: Feel the jungle beat
title: The Jungle Book 2
plot:
The Jungle Book 2 is an animated adventure film of 2003 produced by the Australian unit of DisneyToon Studios as a sequel to Walt Disney's The Jungle Book (1967). Conceived as a direct-to-video release, it was instead sent to cinemas first. Haley Joel Osment voices Mowgli and John Goodman voices Baloo, with Mae Whitman as Shanti, Bob Joles as Bagheera, Tony Jay as Shere Khan, John Rhys-Davies as the village leader, Connor Funk as Ranjan, Phil Collins as the vulture Lucky and Jim Cummings as Kaa and Colonel Hathi.

Mowgli now lives in the Man-Village, adopted by its leader, his wife Messua and their young son Ranjan, alongside Shanti, the girl who drew him there. Missing the excitement of the jungle, he nearly leads the village children across the river and is sent to his room without supper. In the jungle, a lonely Baloo longs for his friend and heads for the village, though Bagheera and Hathi's elephant herd try to stop him, while Shere Khan returns to the area bent on revenge against the boy who humiliated him. Baloo slips into the village at night and carries Mowgli off; Shere Khan, also prowling for Mowgli, is driven away by the villagers. Believing a wild bear has abducted Mowgli, Shanti and Ranjan follow him into the jungle, where Kaa hypnotises Shanti until Ranjan knocks the snake away with a stick.

Mowgli and Baloo head to a party at King Louie's abandoned temple, Mowgli having asked Baloo to scare Shanti away if she turns up. When the animals mock his village life, Mowgli realises he misses it, but when Baloo frightens Shanti and she learns Mowgli asked him to, she and Ranjan leave in anger. As Mowgli tries to make amends, Shere Khan chases him and Shanti to a ruined temple over a lake of lava. Baloo sends Bagheera to protect Ranjan and joins the fight; amid a confusion of gongs, the tiger ends up trapped in the jaws of a falling statue that lands on a rock amid the lava. Recognising where Mowgli belongs, Baloo lets him go home, earning Bagheera's praise. The village leader apologises for not understanding that the jungle is part of Mowgli, and the children go on visiting Baloo and Bagheera every day.

Released in February 2003, the film grossed about $135.7 million worldwide against a $20 million budget, making it a commercial success. Critics were harsh, giving it 19% on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus called it an inferior rehash that should have gone straight to video.

overview: When a doctor decides to carry out an AIDS prevention program inside Latin America’s largest prison: the Casa de Detenção de São Paulo - Carandiru, he discovers the victim of one of the darkest days in Brazilian History when the State of São Paulo’s Military Police, with the excuse for law enforcement, shot to death 111 people. Based on real facts and on the book written by Dráuzio Varella.
tagline: Inside here nobody is guilty. Do you believe that?
title: Carandiru
plot:
Carandiru is a 2003 Brazilian drama film directed by Héctor Babenco, not BR Petrobrás. The movie is based on a true story and revolves around the events that unfolded at the Carandiru Penitentiary in São Paulo, Brazil.

The main theme of Carandiru is the brutal treatment of prisoners in the Brazilian prison system, particularly those with mental health issues or who are deemed "undesirable" by the authorities. The film sheds light on the deplorable conditions and human rights abuses that occurred within the prison walls, including overcrowding, violence, and neglect.

The movie also explores the theme of social inequality and the struggles faced by marginalized communities in Brazil. The characters, particularly those with mental health issues or who are deemed "undesirable," are subjected to cruel treatment and are often forced to live in squalid conditions.

Furthermore, Carandiru touches on the theme of institutional failure and the complicity of those in power in perpetuating these injustices. The film highlights the failures of the prison system and the authorities' reluctance to address the root causes of the problems, leading to a tragic outcome.

Overall, Carandiru is a powerful and thought-provoking film that exposes the dark underbelly of Brazil's prison system and sheds light on the struggles faced by those who are marginalized and oppressed.

overview: Ten-year-old Gloria and her recently widowed grandfather Bud befriend a mysterious reindeer when the family gather for Christmas. Bud comes to believe that Prancer may actually be magical, but Gloria fears his theory will send him straight to a retirement home.
title: Prancer: A Christmas Tale
plot:
Prancer: A Christmas Tale is a 2022 family fantasy drama film directed by Phil Hawkins and a belated third entry in the Prancer series that began with the 1989 film Prancer, released by Universal Pictures Home Entertainment. James Cromwell stars as Bud, a recently widowed and cantankerous grandfather, with Darcey Ewart as his granddaughter Gloria, alongside Sarah-Jane Potts, Aaron McCusker as Gloria's uncle Gerald, and Joseph Millson.

Bud is still grieving the loss of his wife, and his sorrow has made him grumpy, short-tempered and withdrawn. Though he cares deeply for his family and holds to strict principles, he clashes constantly with his two adult children, and he is determined to avoid being placed in a nursing home. At Christmas his 10-year-old British granddaughter, Gloria, comes to stay. Curious, energetic and kind, but sometimes disobedient, she is also dealing with the strain in her parents' rocky relationship and her father's frequent absences, and she likes to film whatever interests her on her smartphone and share it online.

When Bud and Gloria discover a mysterious reindeer living near the family home, the two find common ground. Gloria's persistence wins over her reluctant grandfather, and together they follow the trail of the reindeer, the magical Prancer of the title. Their adventure brings them into conflict with a hunter who wants to shoot the animal, while family tensions over money, including the possible sale of a valuable family house, and the motives of Gloria's money-minded uncle Gerald come to a head. Through his bond with Gloria and the reindeer, Bud begins to open up about his grief, and the family's strained relationships move toward reconciliation in time for Christmas, with the story celebrating loyalty to family, caring for animals, valuing people over money and believing in the spirit of the season.

The film was produced with Sky Cinema. It was released on digital platforms and home video in the United States on November 22, 2022. Alistair Lawrence of Common Sense Media described it as a low-stakes, feel-good holiday drama that spins a decent odd-couple story out of a vague premise, crediting the on-screen chemistry between Cromwell and Ewart for keeping a lightweight script watchable, while noting that the family conflicts are resolved too neatly, that the pursuit of Prancer relies heavily on exposition, and that a stronger villain would have helped.

original_title: 劇場版 Fate/kaleid liner プリズマ☆イリヤ 雪下の誓い
overview: After succumbing to an unenviable fate, Kiritsugu Emiya has left Shirou Emiya the duty to save mankind in his place. The world is dying and time is ticking, but when the salvation Shirou seeks is at the cost of his only family left—his younger sister—will he still have the heart to pursue this duty?  Shirou is now pressed with the choice to continue being a hero of justice—or become the very evil his ideal has vowed to vanquish. The orphan is alone once again, yet his body is still made of swords. The Fifth Holy Grail War now begins with his oath under snow.
title: Fate/kaleid liner Prisma☆Illya: Vow in the Snow
plot:
Fate/kaleid liner Prisma Illya: Vow in the Snow, also known as Oath Under Snow, is a 2017 Japanese animated fantasy action film that serves as a prequel to Hiroshi Hiroyama's manga Fate/kaleid liner Prisma Illya, itself a spin-off of the visual novel Fate/stay night. Shin Oonuma directed the film and Silver Link produced it, both returning from the anime series. The voice cast includes Noriaki Sugiyama, Kaori Nazuka, Rikiya Koyama, Natsuki Hanae and Noriko Shitaya.

As a boy, Shirou travels with his adoptive father, Kiritsugu, to Fuyuki city to investigate a family rumored to be hiding a child with extraordinary magical power. Amid the city's ruins they rescue Miyu, who can grant wishes unconditionally and whose exposure to human desires probably caused a disastrous storm. Kiritsugu intends to use her power to save humanity and insists that Shirou treat her as a tool rather than a person, but Shirou grows attached to her, and Kiritsugu dies before learning how to use her powers.

Five years later, Shirou lives as an ordinary high school student, with Miyu as his younger sister, alongside classmates Julian and Sakura. As he prepares to take Miyu to see the ocean, Julian appears to complete a ritual he began years earlier, revealing himself as the cause of the vortex that destroyed Fuyuki. Julian and his follower Angelica defeat Shirou, leave him for dead and kidnap Miyu. The priest Kirei Kotomine explains that Julian belongs to the Ainsworths, an ancient family of mages who foresaw humanity's end and seek the wish-granting Holy Grail to avert it, and that Julian means to sacrifice Miyu to begin the Grail War. Sakura offers Shirou help but wishes he would flee the city because of her feelings for him. Her brother Shinji, holding the Assassin card, attacks them and kills her, and Shirou uses her Archer card to defeat Shinji, who proves to be Julian's puppet. Shirou then hunts down the other card holders, all likewise puppets. Declared the winner by Kirei, he finds Miyu in a cave and, defying Kiritsugu's wishes, uses his wish to send her to another world where she can be happy. Without his card he fights Angelica, the true Archer card holder, and is defeated, but buys enough time for the ritual to finish. Miyu wakes in an alternate Fuyuki.

The film grossed $1,118,410 in Japan, and its home media releases sold strongly. Critics praised its alternate take on Shirou and its visuals.

overview: An unsuspecting, disenchanted man finds himself working as a spy in the dangerous, high-stakes world of corporate espionage. Quickly getting way over-his-head, he teams up with a mysterious femme fatale.
tagline: Never forget who you are
title: Cypher
plot:
Cypher, also known as Brainstorm and Company Man, is a science fiction spy thriller of 2002 directed by Vincenzo Natali from a script by Brian King. Jeremy Northam stars as Morgan Sullivan, an accountant whose new career in corporate espionage is not what it seems, with Lucy Liu as the mysterious Rita Foster, Nigel Bennett as Finster, Timothy Webber as Callaway, David Hewlett as Virgil Dunn and Kari Matchett as Diane.

Bored with suburban life after losing his job, and resisting his wife's pressure to work for her father, Morgan takes a position as a spy for the company Digicorp. Its head of security, Finster, gives him a new identity, Jack Thursby, and sends him to trade conventions to secretly record the presentations and transmit them back. Soon Morgan suffers recurring nightmares and pain in his neck. At a bar he meets Rita, who works for another firm; she gives him pills and tells him not to transmit at his next convention. When Digicorp thanks him for a transmission he never sent, he takes the pills and his symptoms vanish. Rita then reveals Digicorp's deception and gives him an antidote, warning him not to react to whatever he sees.

At the next convention, Morgan discovers that every attendee believes himself a Digicorp spy; once the drinks drug them, scientists in plastic suits probe and brainwash them, and headsets reinforce their false identities so they can be used and discarded. Feigning that he accepts his new self, Morgan is recruited by the rival Sunway Systems, whose security chief Callaway wants him as a double agent feeding false data to Digicorp. Rita warns that Sunway is just as ruthless and that her boss, the elusive Sebastian Rooks, is using him. With her help Morgan steals a disc from Sunway's vault, and she takes him to meet Rooks. In a panic he accidentally shoots her, then enters a room full of his own belongings and a photograph of himself with Rita, realising he is Rooks. As the security forces of both companies converge, they escape to the roof, where Rita helps him remember how to fly a helicopter he designed, and he blows up the roof as the guards realise who he is. At sea, Rooks shows Rita the disc, the last record of her identity marked for termination, and throws it into the water.

Shown in limited release in the United States and Australia, the film received mixed reviews, with 59% on Rotten Tomatoes; Variety called it consistently intriguing, and Northam won the Best Actor award at the Sitges Film Festival.

overview: When the Russian mob kidnaps the daughter of a reformed criminal, he rounds up his old crew and seeks his own brand of justice.
tagline: The past never stays dead
title: Rage
plot:
Rage, released as Tokarev in most of Europe and Australia, is a 2014 American action crime thriller film directed by Paco Cabezas and written by Jim Agnew and Sean Keller. Nicolas Cage stars as Paul Maguire, a former Irish mobster turned legitimate businessman, with Rachel Nichols as his wife Vanessa, Aubrey Peeples as his daughter Caitlin, Peter Stormare as mob boss Frank O'Connell, Danny Glover as Detective Peter St. John, Max Ryan and Michael McGrady as Paul's old partners Kane and Danny, and Pasha D. Lychnikoff as the Russian boss Chernov.

As young men, Paul and his friends Kane and Danny belonged to a branch of the Irish mob, and one night they ambushed a Russian mobster carrying money to his boss. The robbery set off a bloody war between the Irish and the Russian mob, but the stolen cash allowed Paul to leave crime behind. Years later he has built a legitimate construction business in Mobile, Alabama, married the younger Vanessa and become a devoted father to his teenage daughter Caitlin, while remaining friends with Kane and Danny, who never managed to go straight. One night, while Paul and Vanessa attend a charity dinner, Caitlin is reported abducted from their home by masked men while her friends Evan and Mike were with her. Convinced that the crime is long-delayed revenge for the robbery, Paul ignores the police and turns to his old partners. When Caitlin's body is found in a storm drain, his search becomes a violent rampage against anyone connected to Chernov, the Russian boss whose money they stole, despite warnings from O'Connell that a man allowed to leave the mob should not return to its methods. Vanessa, who first supported him, comes to fear that he is becoming the killer he once was. As the bloodshed escalates, Chernov learns that the man killed in the old robbery was his own brother, Paul's friendships collapse under suspicion, and the discovery of a Tokarev pistol in Paul's closet, a relic of that night, leads him toward a devastating truth about what really happened to his daughter.

Rage received negative reviews from critics. It holds a 13% rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus calls it depressingly dull and poorly made, a rare Cage action thriller lacking the energy to reach "so bad it's good" territory, and Metacritic gave it a score of 28 out of 100 based on 17 critics.

overview: The story of The Empire of Corpses takes place in 19th century Europe, and revolves around John Watson. He is scouted by the government to become a secret agent- However, Watson lives in a world where "Frankensteins"- human corpses that are re-purposed with a false soul in order to use them as laborers- are used to improve industrial development.
tagline: The dead will inherit the Earth.
title: The Empire of Corpses
plot:
The Empire of Corpses is a Japanese anime horror film directed by Shuhei Morita and produced by WIT Studio. Released in 2015, it's an adaptation of H.P. Lovecraft's "Re-Animator" with some original elements.

The main themes of The Empire of Corpses include:

1. **The Dangers of Unchecked Ambition**: The film explores the consequences of Dr. Victor Frankenstein's (also known as Victor) obsessive pursuit of knowledge and power, which ultimately leads to his downfall. His actions have catastrophic effects on humanity, highlighting the importance of responsible scientific inquiry.

2. **Corruption and Decay**: The Empire of Corpses is a metaphor for the decay of society and the consequences of unchecked corruption. The film's setting, a post-apocalyptic world overrun by zombies-like creatures, serves as a commentary on the collapse of social structures and the breakdown of moral values.

3. **The Power of Love and Human Connection**: Throughout the story, Victor's relationships with his colleagues and loved ones serve as a counterpoint to his obsessive pursuit of knowledge. The film ultimately suggests that human connections and love are essential for survival and redemption.

4. **Science vs. Humanity**: The Empire of Corpses explores the tension between scientific progress and humanity's well-being. The film raises questions about the ethics of scientific experimentation, particularly when it involves playing God or tampering with life and death.

5. **Redemption and Personal Growth**: Victor's character arc is a central theme in the film. His journey from obsession to selflessness serves as a commentary on personal growth, redemption, and the importance of learning from one's mistakes.

These themes are woven throughout the narrative, adding depth and complexity to the story. The Empire of Corpses is a thought-provoking anime horror film that explores the darker aspects of human nature and the consequences of unchecked ambition.

overview: A successful, attractive, intelligent and brilliant advertising executive is longing to finally find emotional stability in his life, and decides to propose to his girlfriend. After she refuses his proposal, his life takes a turn when a new young lady enters his life.
title: Sorry If I Call You Love
plot:
Sorry If I Call You Love (Spanish: Perdona si te llamo amor) is a 2014 Spanish romantic drama film directed by Joaquín Llamas. Written by Fran Araújo and Manuel Burque, it adapts the 2007 novel of the same name by the Italian author Federico Moccia, which had already been filmed in Italy in 2008. A Telecinco Cinema production, it was shot in 2013 in Barcelona, Cadaqués and Paris, and was released in Spanish cinemas by Emon on 20 June 2014. It runs about 105 minutes and stars Paloma Bloyd and the Italian actor Daniele Liotti.

Liotti plays Alex, a handsome and successful 37-year-old advertising executive who, after years of hesitation, decides to settle down and proposes to his girlfriend Elena (Irene Montalà), only to be turned down. Shaken, he is distracted at the wheel and lightly knocks over Niki (Bloyd), a spirited 17-year-old in her final year of secondary school, who is riding a scooter. Niki charms him with her cheek and vitality, has him drive her wherever she likes, and soon persuades him into something he had never imagined: a romance with a woman twenty years his junior. The story is framed by the narration of a secretive detective.

The relationship brings the couple joy and plenty of trouble. Alex's colleagues at the agency insist on meeting Niki's friends, leading to a group date with mixed results; Niki, after her friends suggest that Alex might be secretly married, follows him and smashes his car window in a jealous rage on seeing him with a woman who turns out to be his sister. After a schoolmate of Niki's mocks Alex as a "grandpa" and punches him at a nightclub, he begins to doubt whether the age gap can be bridged. A romantic trip to Paris for Niki's eighteenth birthday briefly restores their hopes, but back home Alex ends the affair, saying they come from different worlds, and Niki calls him a coward. Weeks later he realises he cannot live without her, and the two are reunited on a holiday island.

The supporting cast includes Andrea Duro, Cristina Brondo, Jan Cornet and Pablo Chiapella. Critics were largely unimpressed. Pere Vall of Fotogramas awarded it two stars out of five, singling out Bloyd, her friends, Chiapella, the cinematography and the Barcelona setting amid many laughable scenes, while Jonathan Holland of The Hollywood Reporter called it a slick, superficial forbidden-love fantasy whose calculated lack of irony gave it a certain appeal.

original_title: Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl
overview: Jack Sparrow, a freewheeling 18th-century pirate, quarrels with a rival pirate bent on pillaging Port Royal. When the governor's daughter is kidnapped, Sparrow decides to help the girl's love save her.
tagline: Prepare to be blown out of the water.
title: Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl
plot:
Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl is a swashbuckling adventure film that sets the tone for the beloved franchise. Directed by Gore Verbinski and written by Ted Elliott and Terry Rossio, the movie follows the story of Will Turner (Orlando Bloom), a young blacksmith's apprentice who lives in the port town of Port Royal.

The story begins with Will meeting Elizabeth Swann (Keira Knightley), the governor's daughter, on the day of her 18th birthday. However, their encounter is interrupted by Captain Barbossa (Geoffrey Rush) and his crew, who are searching for a way to break a curse that has turned them into undead pirates.

The curse was placed upon the pirates by Aztec gold, which they stole from the Aztecs. The gold was cursed by the Aztec god Tequila, and it can only be lifted by returning all of the gold back to its rightful place. However, the pirates are unable to do so because they have hidden the gold in a temple that is guarded by deadly traps.

Will teams up with Elizabeth and Captain Jack Sparrow (Johnny Depp), a charismatic pirate who has his own motivations for wanting to lift the curse. As they navigate through treacherous waters, they encounter various obstacles, including the Royal Navy, the cursed pirates, and the enigmatic Bootstrap Bill Turner (Stellan Skarsgård), Will's father.

Throughout the movie, Jack Sparrow's character is revealed to be a complex and cunning individual who is driven by his own desires. He is a master of manipulation and deception, but also has a certain charm that makes him hard to resist. His relationship with Will and Elizabeth adds an element of tension and romance to the story.

The film features impressive action sequences, stunning visual effects, and memorable characters. The chemistry between the cast members is undeniable, and their performances bring depth and nuance to the story. The movie's climax features a thrilling battle between the pirates and the Royal Navy, which sets the stage for the rest of the franchise.

Overall, Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl is an entertaining and engaging film that launched a successful franchise. Its blend of action, adventure, and humor has made it a beloved classic among fans of the genre.

overview: The Parrs' baby Jack-Jack is thought to be normal, not having any super-powers like his parents or siblings. But when an outsider is hired to watch him, Jack-Jack shows his true potential.
title: Jack-Jack Attack
plot:
Jack-Jack Attack is an animated superhero comedy film that revolves around the Parr family's adventures with their super-powered son Jack-Jick. The movie delves into the challenges of balancing family life and individuality, as Jack-Jack's unpredictable powers wreak havoc on the family.

The main theme of the film is the struggle to maintain a sense of normalcy in the face of extraordinary circumstances. The Parrs' lives are turned upside down by Jack-Jick's antics, forcing them to confront their own limitations and learn to adapt to the unexpected. This theme is expertly woven throughout the story, as the family navigates the challenges of superhero life while trying to maintain a sense of routine and stability.

The film also explores the idea of identity and self-discovery, particularly for Jack-Jick as he struggles to control his powers and find his place within the family. As the movie progresses, Jack-Jick's actions become increasingly erratic, leading to a series of comedic misadventures that ultimately teach him (and his parents) valuable lessons about responsibility and teamwork.

Overall, Jack-Jack Attack is a lighthearted, entertaining film that uses humor and action to explore themes of family, identity, and self-discovery.

overview: A group of people are trapped in an elevator high above Philadelphia, and one of them is the devil.
tagline: Bad Things Happen For A Reason
title: Devil
plot:
Devil is a 2010 American supernatural horror film directed by John Erick Dowdle, with a screenplay by Brian Nelson based on a story by M. Night Shyamalan. Released by Universal Pictures on September 17, 2010, it was the first and only entry in The Night Chronicles, a planned trilogy of standalone horror films produced by Shyamalan. Its premise draws on the idea of a "Devil's Meeting", in which the Devil comes to Earth to torment wrongdoers, and Shyamalan described its structure as a nod to Agatha Christie's And Then There Were None.

After a man leaps to his death from a Philadelphia skyscraper leaving a note about the Devil, an elevator in the same building stalls with five strangers inside: a temporary security guard, a mechanic who is a Marine veteran, a mattress salesman, a young woman and an elderly woman. Watching on a camera that lets them speak to the passengers but not hear them, guards Ramirez and Lustig see what Ramirez believes is the Devil's face. Each time the lights fail, someone is hurt or killed, starting with the salesman. Detective Bowden, still grieving the wife and son he lost in a hit-and-run five years earlier, takes charge as the repairman and then Lustig die in accidents.

Bowden's team finds that every passenger has a guilty past, from assault and a Ponzi scheme to theft, while the unidentified mechanic becomes the chief suspect. The old woman is found hanged, and the guard Ben and then Sarah are killed in later blackouts. The mechanic's fiancée identifies him as Tony Janekowski, revealing that "Jane Kowski" was a false identity: the Devil had taken the old woman's form. Tony confesses that he caused the hit-and-run, and because he repents, the Devil cannot take his soul. Bowden, who reveals that the victims were his own family, forgives him.

Chris Messina plays Bowden, with Logan Marshall-Green as Tony, Geoffrey Arend, Bojana Novakovic, Jenny O'Hara, Bokeem Woodbine, Matt Craven, and Jacob Vargas as Ramirez, who also narrates. Filming began in Toronto in October 2009. Not screened for critics, the film drew mixed reviews, with 49% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, a Metacritic score of 44 and a CinemaScore of C+, but it earned $63.4 million on a $10 million budget.

overview: After acquiring Knowhere from the Collector, we find the Guardians working to repair the extreme damage done by Thanos-determined to make Knowhere a safe haven, not only for themselves, but for all refugees displaced by the harsh universe. It isn't long before their attempt to return to normal is upended by a brutal attack from a new unknown enemy, and Peter, still reeling from the loss of Gamora, must rally his team around him to defend the universe along with protecting one of their own. A mission, if not completed successfully, could quite possibly lead to the end of the Guardians as we know them.
tagline: It's time to face the music.
title: Guardians of the Galaxy Volume 3
plot:
Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3, promoted under the title Guardians of the Galaxy Volume 3, is an American superhero film of 2023 written and directed by James Gunn. It is the 32nd Marvel Cinematic Universe film. Chris Pratt returns as Peter Quill, with Zoe Saldaña as Gamora, Dave Bautista as Drax, Karen Gillan as Nebula, Pom Klementieff as Mantis, Vin Diesel as Groot, Bradley Cooper as Rocket, Will Poulter as Adam Warlock and Chukwudi Iwuji as the High Evolutionary.

At their new base on Knowhere, the Guardians are attacked by Adam Warlock, a warrior created by the Sovereign's High Priestess Ayesha. Nebula drives him off, but Rocket is gravely wounded, and the team's medical kits cannot save him because of a kill switch implanted by the company Orgocorp. They set off to find the override code. As Rocket lies near death, he remembers his origins: as a baby raccoon he was experimented on by Orgocorp's leader, the High Evolutionary, who sought to engineer animals into beings for an ideal society on Counter-Earth. His brilliance enraged his creator, who planned to harvest his brain and destroy his fellow subjects, the otter Lylla, the walrus Teefs and the rabbit Floor. Rocket's rescue attempt failed; his friends were killed and he escaped alone.

Helped by an alternate Gamora, now one of the Ravagers, the team raids Orgocorp and learns that the code was removed by the High Evolutionary's adviser Theel. Pursued by Ayesha and Adam, they travel to Counter-Earth, which the High Evolutionary bombards when he deems it imperfect, killing its inhabitants and Ayesha. Quill and Groot kill Theel and recover the code, and as Rocket flatlines and sees his lost friends, Lylla tells him it is not his time and Quill restarts his heart. Drax, Nebula and Mantis are captured aboard the High Evolutionary's ship, where they find genetically altered children. The Guardians fight their way through his forces and evacuate the children and imprisoned animals. Rocket spares the defeated High Evolutionary, and Adam, earlier saved by Groot, rescues Quill. Afterward Quill leaves the team, naming Rocket captain, and returns to his grandfather on Earth; Mantis sets off on her own, Gamora rejoins the Ravagers, and Drax and Nebula stay to raise the children as a new line-up of Guardians forms.

Released in May 2023, the film grossed $845.6 million worldwide. Critics found it a heartfelt send-off for the team, giving it 82% on Rotten Tomatoes.

original_title: Guillermo del Toro's Pinocchio: Handcarved Cinema
overview: With mesmerizing footage and time lapses of animators at work, this behind-the-scenes special captures the artistry of a unique tale years in the making.
title: Guillermo del Toro's Pinocchio: Handcarved Cinema
plot:
Blow is a biographical crime drama film directed by Ted Demme, released in 2001 by New Line Cinema. The movie tells the story of George Jung (played by Johnny Depp), an American cocaine trafficker and smuggler.

The film begins with George Jung as a young man growing up in Boston's South End neighborhood. He is introduced to marijuana at a young age and quickly becomes involved in the local drug trade. After serving time in prison for possession, George meets Tuna (played by Benicio del Toro), a fellow inmate who introduces him to cocaine.

George soon becomes hooked on cocaine himself and begins working with Tuna to smuggle it into the United States. The two men form a successful partnership, using their connections with Colombian cartels to supply large quantities of cocaine to American dealers.

As George's wealth and influence grow, so does his ego and sense of entitlement. He marries Mirtha (played by Penélope Cruz), a beautiful woman from Colombia, and becomes embroiled in the world of international crime. However, his success is short-lived, as he soon attracts the attention of DEA agents, particularly Javier Peña (played by Clive Owen).

The plot thickens as George's empire begins to unravel. He is arrested and sentenced to prison, but manages to escape and flee to Bolivia, where he becomes embroiled in a violent turf war with rival dealers.

Meanwhile, Mirtha has become increasingly concerned about George's activities and the danger they pose to their family. As George's addiction worsens, his relationships with those around him begin to fray.

The film builds towards a dramatic confrontation between George and Javier Peña, who is determined to bring him down. In a tense showdown, George is finally apprehended and sentenced to prison once again.

Throughout the film, Johnny Depp delivers a nuanced and captivating performance as George Jung, capturing the complexities of his character's rise and fall from success. The supporting cast, including Benicio del Toro and Penélope Cruz, also deliver strong performances that add depth and nuance to the story.

Overall, Blow is a gripping and intense drama that explores the darker side of the American Dream. With its strong performances, engaging plot, and thought-provoking themes, it's no wonder this film has become a cult classic.

overview: Wilbur the pig is scared of the end of the season, because he knows that come that time, he will end up on the dinner table. He hatches a plan with Charlotte, a spider that lives in his pen, to ensure that this will never happen.
tagline: Something unexpected, unbelievable, unforgettable.
title: Charlotte's Web
plot:
Charlotte's Web is a 2006 American live-action animated fantasy comedy-drama film based on E. B. White's 1952 novel, directed by Gary Winick and written by Susannah Grant and Karey Kirkpatrick. The second film adaptation of the book, after Hanna-Barbera's 1973 animated feature, it stars Dakota Fanning as Fern Arable, with Kevin Anderson and Essie Davis as her parents and Beau Bridges as Dr. Dorian. The voice cast features Dominic Scott Kay as Wilbur, Julia Roberts as Charlotte, Steve Buscemi as Templeton the rat, John Cleese as Samuel the sheep, Oprah Winfrey and Cedric the Entertainer as the geese Gussy and Golly, Kathy Bates and Reba McEntire as the cows Bitsy and Betsy, Robert Redford as Ike the horse, and Sam Shepard as the narrator. Danny Elfman composed the score, and the film was produced by Walden Media, The K Entertainment Company and Nickelodeon Movies.

One spring on a farm in Somerset County, Maine, eight-year-old Fern Arable persuades her father not to kill the runt of a new litter of pigs. She names the piglet Wilbur and raises him lovingly, even smuggling him into school, but once he has grown, she must move him to the barn of her uncle Homer Zuckerman. Lonely and longing for friends, Wilbur is rebuffed by the other barn animals, including the scheming rat Templeton, the stern sheep Samuel, a pair of geese, two cows and a timid horse, until he is befriended by Charlotte, a barn spider living above his pen. When the animals reveal that Wilbur is destined to be killed for the Christmas dinner table, Charlotte promises to save him. With Templeton's reluctant help, she weaves words into her web describing Wilbur as "Some Pig", "Terrific", "Radiant" and "Humble", convincing the Zuckermans that he is a special pig and attracting crowds after the news spreads through the town. The families take Wilbur to a fair, where he is entered in a contest and Charlotte lays an egg sac containing her unborn children, but the effort leaves her weakened, and Wilbur must find a way to repay his friend and protect her legacy.

The film was released in Australia on December 7, 2006, and in the United States by Paramount Pictures on December 15. It received generally positive reviews, holding a 79% rating on Rotten Tomatoes, and grossed $149 million against an $85 million budget.

overview: Plagued by frightening occurrences in their home, Kelly and Ben learn that a university's parapsychology experiment produced an entity that is now haunting them. The malevolent spirit feeds on fear and torments the couple no matter where they run. Desperate, Kelly and Ben turn to a paranormal researcher, but even with his aid, it may already be too late to save themselves from the terrifying presence.
tagline: Once you believe, you die.
title: The Apparition
plot:
The Apparition is a supernatural horror film that delves into the darker aspects of human psychology and the consequences of playing with forces beyond one's control.

At its core, the movie explores the theme of obsession and possession, as the main character, Heather, becomes increasingly entangled in a world of paranormal activity. As she delves deeper into the mystery, her grip on reality begins to slip, and she finds herself torn between her desire for answers and her growing dependence on the malevolent entity that has taken hold of her life.

The film also touches on the idea of grief and loss, as Heather's character is haunted by a tragic event in her past. Her obsession with the supernatural becomes a way to cope with her emotional pain, but ultimately serves to exacerbate her situation.

Furthermore, The Apparition raises questions about the nature of reality and the blurred lines between the spiritual and the physical worlds. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that there are forces at work that defy explanation, leaving the characters – and the audience – questioning what is real and what is just a product of their own paranoia.

Overall, The Apparition is a tense, unsettling film that masterfully crafts an atmosphere of creeping dread and unease, keeping viewers on the edge of their seats as they follow Heather's downward spiral into madness.

overview: An ordinary man frustrated with the various flaws he sees in society begins to psychotically and violently lash out against them.
tagline: A Tale Of Urban Reality.
title: Falling Down
plot:
Falling Down is a 1993 American crime thriller film directed by Joel Schumacher and written by Ebbe Roe Smith, starring Michael Douglas as William Foster, an unemployed defense worker whose frustrations boil over into violence on a single day in Los Angeles, and Robert Duvall as Martin Prendergast, a police sergeant on his last day before retirement who tries to track him down. Barbara Hershey, Rachel Ticotin and Tuesday Weld co-star.

On a sweltering morning, Foster is trapped in a Los Angeles traffic jam when his air conditioning fails. He abandons his car and sets off on foot, briefcase in hand, intent on reaching his ex-wife Beth's home in Venice for his daughter's birthday party. His journey across the city becomes a series of escalating confrontations. He smashes up a convenience store after its owner refuses to give him change for a phone call, beats off two gang members who try to rob him and, after their friends open fire in a drive-by that kills bystanders but misses him, walks away with their bag of weapons. At a fast-food restaurant, refused breakfast because the menu has just switched to lunch, he accidentally fires a gun into the ceiling, then complains that his burger looks nothing like the picture. Alarmed by his calls, Beth, who has a restraining order against him, alerts the police. Meanwhile Prendergast, who has been coaxed into retirement by his wife, insists on investigating the string of incidents and, remembering Foster's "D-FENS" vanity license plate from the morning traffic jam, realizes that one man is behind them all. With his partner, Detective Sandra Torres, he visits Foster's mother, who is surprised to learn that her son has lost his job. At a military surplus store, Foster's growing sense of grievance meets real bigotry when the owner, a neo-Nazi who admires his violence, tries to recruit him and then turns on him, with deadly results. As Foster makes his way toward Venice, Prendergast races to reach Beth and their daughter before he does.

Falling Down was nominated for the Palme d'Or at the 1993 Cannes Film Festival, and Smith's screenplay won the Edgar Award. Reviews were mixed, with praise for Douglas and Duvall but criticism of its violence and tone; it holds a 77% rating on Rotten Tomatoes. The film grossed $96 million against a $25 million budget and topped the US box office in its first two weeks.

overview: This time, there's no wedding. No bachelor party. What could go wrong, right? But when the Wolfpack hits the road, all bets are off.
tagline: It all ends.
title: The Hangover Part III
plot:
The Hangover Part III is a 2013 American comedy film directed by Todd Phillips and written by Craig Mazin, Scott Moore, and Jeff Schaffer. The movie stars Bradley Cooper, Ed Helms, Zach Galifianakis, Justin Bartha, and Heather Graham.

The film takes place five years after the events of The Hangover Part II. Phil Wenneck (Cooper), Stu Price (Helms), Alan Garner (Galifianakis), and Doug Billings (Bartha) are reunited for a high school friend's bachelor party in Savannah, Georgia. The groom-to-be is Bradley, who has been estranged from his friends since the events of Part II.

Upon arrival, they discover that Bradley has gone missing, and a series of clues lead them to believe he may have faked his own death as part of a prank. As they search for him, they are pursued by Marshall (John Goodman), a former friend who was left behind in Vegas after the events of Part II.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Bradley's disappearance is connected to a traumatic event from his past, which he has been trying to escape. The friends eventually discover that Bradley has indeed faked his own death and is hiding out in an abandoned asylum, where he is being held captive by Marshall.

In order to rescue him, the group must confront their own personal demons and work together to overcome their differences. Along the way, they encounter a series of surreal and humorous situations, including a wild goose chase through the streets of Savannah and a confrontation with a group of eccentric locals.

Ultimately, Phil and Stu are able to track down Bradley and rescue him from Marshall's clutches. The film ends with the friends reuniting and reflecting on their experiences, as they prepare for Bradley's wedding.

Throughout the movie, the tone is more serious and introspective than its predecessors, exploring themes of trauma, addiction, and the complexities of male friendship. While it may not be as outrageous or absurd as the first two films, The Hangover Part III delivers plenty of laughs and surprises along the way.

Overall, The Hangover Part III is a satisfying conclusion to the trilogy, providing closure for the characters while still delivering plenty of humor and excitement.

overview: When once distant UFOs become a terrifying threat attacking Earth, a Marine staff sergeant and his team take it upon themselves to face the enemy and protect what remains of the planet.
tagline: It's not war. It's survival.
title: Battle: Los Angeles
plot:
Battle: Los Angeles is a 2011 science fiction action film directed by Jonathan Liebesman and written by Michael Colleary. The movie takes place in an alternate universe where an alien invasion occurs on Earth, specifically in the city of Los Angeles.

The story begins with Sergeant Nantz (played by Aaron Eckhart), a U.S. Army sergeant who is part of an elite platoon known as Alpha Squad. The team consists of Sergeant Nantz, Staff Sergeant Stigler (played by Michael Peña), Corporal Lerner (played by Jon Bernthal), and Private First Class Miller (played by Temuera Morrison). They are tasked with defending the city from an alien invasion.

The movie opens with a dramatic sequence showing the aliens' arrival on Earth. The extraterrestrial beings, known as "the Others," descend upon Los Angeles in massive spaceships, wreaking havoc on the city and its inhabitants. As the chaos ensues, Sergeant Nantz's team is deployed to defend the city from the alien threat.

As the battle rages on, Sergeant Nantz and his team face numerous challenges, including treacherous terrain, malfunctioning equipment, and the psychological strain of fighting an enemy that seems almost invulnerable. The team soon discovers that the aliens are not just mindless monsters but a highly organized and technologically advanced force with a sinister purpose.

Throughout the movie, Sergeant Nantz struggles to come to terms with his own personal demons, including the loss of his wife in a previous deployment. His leadership skills are put to the test as he tries to keep his team motivated and focused on their mission.

As the battle reaches its climax, Sergeant Nantz's team launches a final assault on the alien mothership. The movie culminates in an intense and action-packed sequence where the humans fight for survival against overwhelming odds. In the end, Sergeant Nantz emerges victorious but not without scars, both physical and emotional.

The ending of Battle: Los Angeles is intentionally ambiguous, leaving the audience wondering about the fate of the alien threat and the future of humanity. The movie concludes with a sense of hope and resilience, as Sergeant Nantz reflects on the sacrifices made by his team and the possibility of a new beginning for humanity.

Overall, Battle: Los Angeles is an intense and thrilling sci-fi action film that explores themes of leadership, sacrifice, and the human condition in the face of overwhelming adversity.

overview: In the year of 2039, after World Wars destroy much of the civilization as we know it, territories are no longer run by governments, but by corporations; the mightiest of which is the Mishima Zaibatsu. In order to placate the seething masses of this dystopia, Mishima sponsors Tekken, a tournament in which fighters battle until only one is left standing.
tagline: Survival is no game
title: Tekken
plot:
Tekken is a 2009 American science fiction martial arts film loosely based on the video game series developed and published by Namco Bandai Games. Directed by Dwight Little from a screenplay by Alan B. McElroy, it stars Jon Foo as Jin Kazama and Cary-Hiroyuki Tagawa as Heihachi Mishima, with Kelly Overton, Ian Anthony Dale, Cung Le, Darrin Dewitt Henson, Candice Hillebrand and Luke Goss.
