As tempers fray and another crew member is lost in a sandstorm, Elliott, who claims to be an aircraft designer, proposes a radical solution: rebuilding the wrecked plane into a new aircraft that can fly them to safety. Frank at first dismisses the idea, but after one of the men walks off in protest, he agrees. For weeks they labor under brutal conditions, battling heat, dust storms, shortages of water and bitter quarrels, and they christen their creation Phoenix, after the legendary bird. Their efforts are threatened by a band of smugglers camped nearby, by Elliott's increasingly arrogant demands to be acknowledged as their leader, and finally by the discovery that his design experience is limited to model aircraft. With their supplies running out, the survivors must decide whether to trust Elliott's design and stake their lives on a single attempt to get the Phoenix into the air.

Released in the United States by 20th Century Fox on December 17, 2004, the film was a box-office bomb, grossing about $35 million worldwide amid competition from other holiday releases. Reviews were generally mixed, with critics comparing it unfavorably to the original while praising its visuals and action; it holds a 31% Rotten Tomatoes rating.

overview: A young Los Angeles couple Tara and Sam fall head over heels into a new romance, entwining their lives—until their intimacy transforms into something terrifying.
tagline: How well do you know the one you love?
title: Tentacles
plot:
Tentacles is a 2021 American romantic horror film directed by Clara Aranovich from a screenplay by Alexandra Pechman, with a story credit shared with Nick Antosca, both of whom had worked on the anthology series Channel Zero. Produced by Blumhouse Television, it was released on Hulu on 12 February 2021 as the Valentine's Day instalment of Into the Dark, the monthly holiday-themed horror anthology series, and was the series' first new feature since July 2020, following a hiatus caused by the COVID-19 pandemic; it was filmed under pandemic restrictions. Dana Drori and Casey Deidrick star, with Kasey Elise in a supporting role. It runs about 84 minutes.

Sam (Deidrick), a commercial photographer in Los Angeles, meets Tara (Drori), a mysterious drifter who lives in vacant houses and seems to have plenty of money from uncertain sources, at an open house. The two share an instant, intensely physical connection, and Tara is soon living in the run-down family home Sam inherited from his parents, renovating it in exchange for a place to stay. As they fall ever deeper in love and race through the milestones of a relationship towards marriage, Sam's business partner and longtime best friend Esther (Elise) worries that they are moving far too quickly, but he ignores her. Tara then reveals that an ex-boyfriend is stalking her, break-ins follow, and Sam's health begins to deteriorate for reasons no one can diagnose, with piercing earaches and moments of disorientation. In its final act the film reveals that Sam, not Tara, is the one in danger, and their consuming romance turns into a tale of transformation and aquatic body horror.

Critics found the film underpowered. Matt Donato of /Film gave it 5 out of 10, writing that its first forty minutes hazily build a relationship between thinly written characters, that Aranovich's attempts at style, such as a fast-motion sex montage and distorted camera views, were not enough, and that its tentacled horror arrives only after the viewer's attention has waned, though he did not fault the performers. Drew Koenig of Tell-Tale TV credited the film with subverting the familiar story of a woman endangered by an untrustworthy man by revealing Sam as the victim of a different kind of toxic love, but felt that Tara's characterisation and the final twist muddied its romantic metaphor and that, while decently paced, it lacked teeth.

overview: In a world divided into factions based on personality types, Tris learns that she's been classified as Divergent and won't fit in. When she discovers a plot to destroy Divergents, Tris and the mysterious Four must find out what makes Divergents dangerous before it's too late.
tagline: What makes you different makes you dangerous.
title: Divergent
plot:
In a post-apocalyptic Chicago, society is divided into five factions, each representing a different virtue: Abnegation (selflessness), Amity (peacefulness), Candor (honesty), Dauntless (bravery), and Erudite (intelligence). The story follows Beatrice "Tris" Prior, a young girl who lives with her family in Abnegation.

On the day of the Choosing Ceremony, where teenagers choose which faction to join, Tris decides to leave Abnegation to join Dauntless. This decision is motivated by her desire for excitement and adventure, as well as her feelings of restlessness within the confines of her faction. Tris's parents, Andrew and Natalie Prior, are proud of their daughter's choice, but also worried about the risks involved.

As Tris begins her initiation into Dauntless, she meets her instructor, Four (Tobias Eaton), a skilled and mysterious fighter who becomes her mentor. Tris struggles to keep up with the rigorous training and prove herself to her peers, while also navigating the complexities of her relationships with Four and her fellow initiates.

However, Tris soon discovers that she is Divergent, meaning she doesn't fit into any one faction's values or traits. This makes her a target for the Erudite, who seek to eliminate those who don't conform to their ideology. Tris also uncovers a plot by the Erudite to overthrow the government and take control of society.

As Tris delves deeper into the mystery, she must use her wits and bravery to stay one step ahead of the Erudite. Along the way, she forms close bonds with her fellow initiates, including Christina and Will, who become her allies in the fight against the Erudite.

The story takes a dramatic turn when Tris discovers that Four is actually Tobias Eaton, a former Dauntless initiate who was thought to have died in a training accident. The two share a complicated past, and their relationship becomes increasingly complex as they navigate their feelings for each other.

In the climactic final confrontation, Tris faces off against the Erudite leader, Jeanine Matthews, who will stop at nothing to achieve her goals. With the help of Four and her fellow initiates, Tris must use all her skills and cunning to defeat the Erudite and save Dauntless from destruction.

In the end, Tris emerges victorious, but not without scars. She realizes that being Divergent is not a weakness, but a strength, and that she has found her true place in society as a member of Dauntless. The film concludes with Tris and Four standing together, ready to face whatever challenges come their way.

Overall, Divergent is a thrilling and action-packed adaptation of Veronica Roth's bestselling novel, with a strong female protagonist at its center. The film explores themes of identity, loyalty, and the importance of embracing one's individuality in a society that values conformity above all else.

overview: Struggling to make ends meet, former special ops soldiers reunite for a high-stakes heist: stealing $75 million from a South American drug lord.
tagline: You can’t go this far without crossing every line
title: Triple Frontier
plot:
Triple Frontier is a 2019 American action-adventure film directed by J.C. Chandor and written by Mark Boal, J.C. Chandor, and Matt Boling. The movie stars Oscar Isaac, Ben Affleck, Charlie Hunnam, Garrett Hedlund, and Pedro Pascal.

The story follows three former US Special Forces operatives - Chris Mullin (Oscar Isaac), Billy Marks (Ben Affleck), and Mike Kinney (Charlie Hunnam) - who have retired from their military careers. The trio reunites for a high school friend's 40th birthday party in New York City, where they are approached by Santiago "Pope" Garcia (Gael García Bernal), a former comrade-in-arms.

Santiago reveals that his younger brother, Francisco, has been kidnapped by the notorious Bolivian cartel leader, Dina (Catalina Sandino Moreno). The kidnappers demand $75 million in exchange for Francisco's safe return. Pope asks his old friends to help him rescue his brother and retrieve the ransom money.

The team devises a plan to infiltrate Bolivia and gather intelligence on the cartel's operations. They assemble a group of local fighters, including a Bolivian woman named Ana (Natalia Beristáin), who becomes an ally in their mission.

As they prepare for the rescue operation, the team faces personal demons and conflicts that threaten to derail their mission. Chris struggles with his past mistakes, Billy grapples with feelings of guilt over his role in a previous military operation gone wrong, and Mike tries to reconcile his loyalty to his friends with his growing sense of morality.

The team launches a daring rescue mission, navigating treacherous terrain and avoiding cartel henchmen. Along the way, they encounter Ana, who becomes an integral part of their plan. The group faces numerous challenges, including treacherous mountain paths, rival factions within the cartel, and personal betrayals.

As the stakes escalate, the team's bond is tested, and they are forced to confront their own mortality. In a tense showdown, they face off against Dina's henchmen in a violent confrontation that leaves several characters gravely injured or killed.

In the aftermath of the rescue mission, the team reflects on the true cost of their actions. Chris comes to terms with his past mistakes, Billy finds redemption through his sacrifice, and Mike learns to prioritize his humanity over his loyalty to his friends.

The movie concludes with a poignant moment of closure for Pope, who finally gets to see his brother safe and sound. The film ends on a hopeful note, suggesting that even in the face of adversity, friendship and loyalty can be powerful forces for redemption and healing.

Overall, Triple Frontier is an action-packed thrill ride with a strong ensemble cast and a gripping narrative that explores themes of loyalty, sacrifice, and redemption.

original_title: STAND BY ME ドラえもん2
overview: He and her beloved Shizuka are finally married! Nobita's childhood dream was supposed to come true on his wedding day, but for some reason, Nobita doesn't show up... One of the most popular episodes from the original story transcends time and space, and leads to Nobita's future. Doraemon and Nobita's great adventure begins in order to fulfill his grandmother's wish to see his bride at first sight. This is a story of tears and bonds, set in the past, present and future.
title: Stand by Me Doraemon 2
plot:
Stand by Me Doraemon 2 is a heartwarming and nostalgic film that explores the complexities of childhood friendships and the importance of holding onto memories from one's past. The movie delves into the theme of nostalgia, as the main characters reminisce about their adventures with Doraemon in the summer of 1965.

The story also touches on the idea of growing up and letting go. As the characters face new challenges and responsibilities, they must come to terms with the fact that their carefree childhood days are slowly fading away. This theme is beautifully captured through the character of Nobita, who struggles to balance his desire for adventure with the need to take responsibility for his actions.

Furthermore, the film highlights the significance of friendship and loyalty in overcoming adversity. The bond between Nobita and his friends is put to the test as they navigate the challenges of adolescence, but ultimately, their relationships are strengthened by their shared experiences.

The movie also explores the theme of time travel and its consequences. Doraemon's ability to travel through time serves as a metaphor for the complexities of growing up and the importance of learning from one's past mistakes. The film encourages viewers to appreciate the present moment and not take anything for granted, while also acknowledging the value of nostalgia and the lessons learned from past experiences.

Overall, Stand by Me Doraemon 2 is a poignant and uplifting film that celebrates the beauty of childhood friendships and the importance of holding onto memories from one's past.

overview: Female adventurer Parker joins a crew of male trophy hunters in a remote wilderness park. Their goal: slaughter genetically recreated dinosaurs for sport using rifles, arrows, and grenades. After their guide is killed by raptors, the team tries to escape the park – but the hunters quickly become the hunted. Even worse, the park’s manager suspects Parker of being a spy and sends a hit squad after her. This battle’s about to become primitive!
tagline: This time it's mankind that's going extinct.
title: Jurassic Hunt
plot:
Jurassic Hunt is a 2021 American low-budget science fiction action film directed by Hank Braxtan, a filmmaker known for monster films such as Unnatural and Snake Outta Compton. Released by Lionsgate and Grindstone Entertainment Group, it went straight to digital and home video in August 2021. Courtney Loggins stars as Parker, with Ruben Pla, Tarkan Dospil, Joston Theney, Antuone Torbert and Dan Sinclair in the supporting cast. The film runs 83 minutes.

The story is set in a remote wilderness preserve that offers a big-game safari experience in which wealthy thrill-seekers pay for the privilege of hunting genetically recreated dinosaurs with rifles, arrows and grenades. Parker, the only woman in a new group of otherwise male trophy hunters that includes Torres (Pla) and Valentine (Dospil), is not what she seems: she is an undercover activist, and a vegan, trying to gather evidence to expose the operation. Lindon, the ambitious and ruthless tycoon who runs the park, is determined to keep it secret from the outside world. Soon after the party sets out, their guide is killed by raptors, and the hunters find themselves picked off one by one by the animals they came to kill, in encounters with a pterodactyl, a stampeding Tyrannosaurus and wave after wave of baby raptors. As the survivors try to escape the park, Lindon, who suspects Parker of being a spy, makes no effort to rescue them, appearing instead to cheer on the dinosaurs, and sends a hit squad after her.

Reviewers found the film cheap but not without entertainment value. Writing for Free Kittens Movie Guide, D. M. Anderson said the computer-generated effects were on a par with a student project and the film looked hastily slapped together, with laughable lapses in logic and continuity, yet found it surprisingly entertaining and sometimes genuinely funny without heavy-handed self-awareness, singling out Torbert's mercenary Blackhawk, whose monologue about the power of killing is cut short by a pterodactyl. Jim McLennan of Film Blitz gave it a C, saying it had surpassed his low expectations; he felt the dinosaur effects passed muster on their own but not when interacting with the actors, criticised its pixelated digital blood and thin characters, but enjoyed the scene in which a hunter faces a horde of baby raptors.

overview: Reuben Feffer is a guy who's spent his entire life playing it safe. Polly Prince is irresistible as a free-spirit who lives for the thrill of the moment. When these two comically mismatched souls collide, Reuben's world is turned upside down, as he makes an uproarious attempt to change his life from middle-of-the-road to totally-out-there.
tagline: For the most cautious man on Earth, life is about to get interesting.
title: Along Came Polly
plot:
Along Came Polly is a 2004 American romantic comedy film directed by John Hamburg and written by Hamburg and Larry Levin. The movie stars Ben Stiller, Jennifer Aniston, Philip Baker Hall, and Debra Messing.

The story begins with Reuben Feffer (Ben Stiller), a risk-averse and uptight insurance salesman who has been in a long-term relationship with his girlfriend, Polly Prince (Jennifer Aniston). However, their relationship is stagnant, and Reuben feels suffocated by the predictability of it all. He meets a free-spirited woman named Sandy (Debra Messing) at a singles bar, but she's not interested in him.

Reuben's life takes an unexpected turn when he meets Polly's cousin, Polly Prince (Jennifer Aniston), who is also his coworker and friend. Reuben has had feelings for Polly since high school, but she never reciprocated them. When Polly gets engaged to a man named Ray (Philip Baker Hall), Reuben sees this as an opportunity to finally be with her.

However, things take a turn when Reuben's life insurance policy is canceled due to his lack of risk-taking behavior. He then decides to go skydiving for the first time, which becomes a pivotal moment in his life. This experience makes him realize that he needs to take more risks and live life on his own terms.

As Reuben navigates his newfound sense of freedom, he starts to reevaluate his relationship with Polly. He realizes that he's been playing it safe all these years, and it's time for him to be more spontaneous and open-minded. Meanwhile, Polly is struggling with her engagement and feeling suffocated by the idea of settling down.

The plot thickens when Reuben and Polly start to reconnect, but their relationship is put to the test as they face various challenges together. Along the way, Reuben learns valuable lessons about love, risk-taking, and being true to oneself.

In the end, Reuben must decide whether he's willing to take a chance on Polly and their relationship. The movie culminates in a heartwarming and humorous climax that showcases the growth and development of both characters.

Throughout the film, Ben Stiller delivers a standout performance as the lovable but awkward Reuben Feffer. Jennifer Aniston shines as the charming and free-spirited Polly Prince, bringing depth and nuance to her character. The supporting cast adds to the humor and charm of the movie, making Along Came Polly a delightful and entertaining romantic comedy that explores themes of love, risk-taking, and self-discovery.

overview: When a covert mission to rescue a kidnapped CIA operative uncovers a chilling plot, an elite, highly trained U.S. SEAL team speeds to hotspots around the globe, racing against the clock to stop a deadly terrorist attack.
tagline: The only easy day was yesterday.
title: Act of Valor
plot:
Act of Valor is a 2012 American action thriller film directed by Mike McCoy and Scott Waugh, written by Aaron Guzikowski, and produced by Tom Cruise, Doug Liman, and Don Grubbs.

The movie follows the story of two Navy SEALs, Lieutenant Alex Shaw (played by Taylor Kitsch) and Petty Officer Michael "Bible" Stone (played by Alexander Skarsgård), who are part of an elite counter-terrorism unit. The film's narrative is presented in a unique way, as it is framed as a documentary-style film, with the characters' voicesover explaining their actions.

The story begins with Lieutenant Shaw and Petty Officer Stone on a mission to rescue a group of hostages being held by a Mexican cartel leader, Carlos Rueda (played by Efrain Funes). The two SEALs are sent to infiltrate the cartel's hideout in Mexico, where they encounter various obstacles and dangers.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Lieutenant Shaw is on a personal mission to rescue his father, who was kidnapped by the cartel. Petty Officer Stone, on the other hand, is initially hesitant to join the mission, but eventually agrees to help his fellow SEAL.

Throughout the film, the two characters face numerous challenges, including intense firefights with the cartel members and navigating treacherous terrain. Along the way, they also encounter a local Mexican woman, Elena (played by Teresa Perez), who becomes an ally in their mission.

As the story reaches its climax, Lieutenant Shaw and Petty Officer Stone launch a final assault on the cartel's hideout, resulting in a intense and action-packed confrontation with Carlos Rueda. In the end, the two SEALs successfully complete their mission, rescuing the hostages and killing the cartel leader.

Throughout the film, the action sequences are fast-paced and intense, showcasing the skills and training of the Navy SEALs. The movie also explores themes of loyalty, duty, and sacrifice, as Lieutenant Shaw and Petty Officer Stone put themselves in harm's way to complete their mission.

Overall, Act of Valor is an action-packed thrill ride that showcases the bravery and skill of the Navy SEALs. While some critics have argued that the film's narrative is predictable and lacks depth, it remains a thrilling and entertaining watch for fans of action movies.

original_title: Beverly Hills Chihuahua 3: Viva la Fiesta!
overview: When Papi, Chloe, the pups, Uncle Pedro, and their owners move to a hotel, the smallest pup Rosa feels like she doesn't fit in, and Papi wants to make her feel better by showing her how special she is.
tagline: Family Always Matters
title: Beverly Hills Chihuahua 3: Viva la Fiesta!
plot:
Beverly Hills Chihuahua 3: Viva la Fiesta! is an American family comedy of 2012 directed by Lev L. Spiro, the third and last entry in Disney's Beverly Hills Chihuahua series, released straight to home video. George Lopez and Odette Annable voice the chihuahua couple Papi and Chloe, with Kay Panabaker as their daughter Rosa, Logan Grove as Papi Jr., Ernie Hudson as Pedro, Jake Busey as Oscar, Lacey Chabert as Charlotte, Tom Kenny as Sebastian and Miguel Ferrer as Delgado. Marcus Coloma and Erin Cahill play the dogs' owners Sam and Rachel, with Cedric Yarbrough as hotel manager Mr. Hollis.

Two years after their wedding, Sam and Rachel take jobs at the luxurious Langham Hotel as landscaper and sous-chef, moving in with Papi, Chloe, their puppies and Pedro. Mr. Hollis, worried about competition from the rival Montague hotel, wants Chloe to make appearances for the Langham, and the puppies are enrolled in the hotel's Doggy Day School, run by Jenny and her dog Oscar, which leaves Papi disappointed that he will no longer teach them himself. Rachel suffers under the arrogant Chef Didier, who has her washing dishes, while Sam is saddled with the lazy assistant Lester. Rosa, the runt of the litter, is teased by a big dog for wearing swimming aids, and her siblings take revenge on her behalf.

In an overgrown garden, Papi befriends Arnie, a mute stray, and begins to suspect that Jenny and Oscar are hiding something, though Arnie's attempt to warn him with a carving at first confuses him. Feeling small and wanting to grow up, Rosa asks for a quinceañera, the Mexican coming-of-age celebration Papi once took part in, and he promises to throw her one, helped by his old friend Sebastian. As Papi juggles the party preparations with his growing suspicions, Rosa saves Charlotte, a VIP guest's dog who cannot swim, after she falls into the pool. Papi, Pedro and Arnie enlist the police dog Delgado to help expose Jenny, who ends up stuck in a puddle of peanut butter, while Delgado appears with the rival hotelier Montague. Chloe apologises to Papi for doubting him, and Rosa's quinceañera goes ahead with her siblings in matching outfits. Jenny and Oscar are arrested, Papi becomes the new teacher at the day school, and Hollis adopts Arnie.

Disney released the film on Blu-ray and DVD in September 2012. Zachary Gordon and Chantily Spalan did not return as Papi Jr. and Rosa, and it was Kay Panabaker's final film before she retired from acting to study zoology.

overview: In the year 2455, Old Earth is now a contaminated planet abandoned for centuries -- a brown world of violent storms, toxic landmasses and poisonous seas. Yet humans have returned to the deadly place that they once fled, not to live, but to research the ancient, rusting artifacts of the long-gone civilizations. But it's not the harmful environment that could prove fatal to the intrepid, young explorers who have just landed on Old Earth. For them, it's Friday the 13th, and Jason lives!
tagline: Evil has an upgrade.
title: Jason X
plot:
Jason X is a 2001 American science fiction slasher film directed by James Isaac and written by Todd Farmer, the tenth installment in the Friday the 13th franchise. It stars Lexa Doig, Lisa Ryder and Chuck Campbell, with Kane Hodder in his fourth and final appearance as the killer Jason Voorhees, and director David Cronenberg in a supporting role for which he rewrote his own dialogue. Farmer settled on a space slasher concept modeled on Alien, in which Jason is transformed by future technology into a cyborg. The film was shot in Toronto from March to May 2000, with a score by Harry Manfredini.

In 2008, the mass murderer Jason Voorhees is captured by the US government and held at the Crystal Lake Research Facility. By 2010, after many failed attempts to execute him, facility head Rowan LaFontaine proposes freezing him in cryogenic stasis, but military scientists who want to study his regenerative powers intervene, and Jason breaks free and slaughters them. Rowan lures him into a cryogenic pod, but he stabs her, and both are frozen solid. More than four centuries later, Earth is a polluted wasteland abandoned for a new planet, Earth II. Professor Brandon Lowe brings his students, his intern and the android KM-14 on a field trip to the ruins and discovers the frozen pair, taking them aboard their spaceship, the Grendel. Rowan is revived, but her warnings are ignored as the debt-ridden Lowe sees a profit in selling Jason to a collector. Soon Jason thaws and begins killing the crew one by one, then the squad of soldiers led by Sergeant Brodski who try to stop him, and a collision destroys a nearby space station. The survivors fight back with the help of KM-14, upgraded into a formidable combat android, and appear to destroy Jason, only for the ship's medical nanites to rebuild him as a nearly unstoppable cyborg. As the crippled ship falls apart, the remaining survivors resort to desperate measures, including a holographic recreation of Camp Crystal Lake, to escape their pursuer.

Jason X premiered in Spain on November 15, 2001, and was released in the United States on April 26, 2002. It underperformed at the box office, grossing about $17 million against a budget of $11–14 million, and received negative reviews, holding a 27% rating on Rotten Tomatoes.

overview: In a broken city rife with injustice, ex-cop Billy Taggart seeks redemption and revenge after being double-crossed and then framed by its most powerful figure, the mayor. Billy's relentless pursuit of justice, matched only by his streetwise toughness, makes him an unstoppable force - and the mayor's worst nightmare.
tagline: Proof Can Be a Powerful Weapon.
title: Broken City
plot:
Broken City is a 2013 American neo-noir crime thriller film directed by Allen Hughes and starring Mark Wahlberg, Russell Crowe, and Catherine Zeta-Jones.

The main themes of Broken City include:

1. Corruption and Power: The movie explores the corrupting influence of power and money on individuals, particularly in the context of politics and law enforcement. The protagonist, Billy Rosewood (Mark Wahlberg), is a detective who becomes embroiled in a web of corruption and deceit when he is hired by a wealthy politician, Mayor Reilly (Russell Crowe), to investigate his wife's infidelity.

2. Loyalty and Betrayal: Throughout the movie, characters are forced to confront their own loyalties and allegiances as they navigate the complex web of relationships and alliances that define the story. Billy Rosewood is torn between his duty as a detective and his growing feelings for Reilly's wife, Kate (Catherine Zeta-Jones), who becomes embroiled in her husband's corruption.

3. Identity and Self-Discovery: As the story unfolds, Billy Rosewood begins to question his own identity and sense of purpose. He is forced to confront the fact that he has become complicit in Reilly's corruption, and must decide whether to continue down a path of moral compromise or take a stand against it.

4. The Corrupting Influence of Wealth: The movie critiques the corrupting influence of wealth and power on individuals and institutions. Mayor Reilly's wealth and influence have made him ruthless and willing to do whatever it takes to maintain his position, even if it means compromising his own values and principles.

Overall, Broken City is a gripping thriller that explores complex themes of corruption, loyalty, identity, and the corrupting influence of power.

overview: When U.S. Rangers and an elite Delta Force team attempt to kidnap two underlings of a Somali warlord, their Black Hawk helicopters are shot down, and the Americans suffer heavy casualties, facing intense fighting from the militia on the ground.
tagline: Leave No Man Behind.
title: Black Hawk Down
plot:
Black Hawk Down is a 2001 war film directed by Ridley Scott, produced by Jerry Bruckheimer Films, and based on the book "Black Hawk Down: A Story of Modern War" by Mark Bowden. The film tells the true story of the Battle of Mogadishu, which took place during the Somali Civil War in October 1993.

The movie begins with a prologue that sets the stage for the events of the film. It shows the aftermath of the battle and introduces the main characters, including Delta Force operative Norm "Hoot" Gibson (played by Josh Hartnett), Sergeant First Class Mike Steele (played by Tom Sizemore), and Lieutenant Colonel Mike Steele's son, also named Mike (played by Ewan McGregor).

The story then flashes back to October 3, 1993, when a U.S. military operation aimed at capturing two top Somali warlords, Mohamed Farrah Aidid and Hassan Abdullah Hersi Gabane, goes awry. A team of U.S. soldiers from the 1st Battalion, 75th Ranger Regiment, led by Lieutenant Colonel Mike Steele, is sent to capture Aidid's bodyguards.

The operation begins with a helicopter assault, but things quickly go wrong when the Black Hawk helicopters are ambushed by Somali militiamen. The pilots, including Staff Sergeant Gary "Falcon" Gordon (played by Eric Bana), struggle to escape the city, but their aircraft are severely damaged and begin to take fire from the ground.

As the situation spirals out of control, the U.S. soldiers are forced to abandon ship and make a desperate bid for safety on foot. The movie's intense action sequences follow the soldiers as they navigate through the treacherous streets of Mogadishu, fighting off waves of Somali militiamen and trying to reach the relative safety of their extraction point.

The film's climax features an epic battle between the U.S. soldiers and the Somali militiamen, with both sides suffering heavy casualties. The movie ends with a poignant scene showing the aftermath of the battle, as the surviving soldiers are left to mourn their fallen comrades and grapple with the trauma they have experienced.

Throughout the film, Ridley Scott's direction brings a sense of realism and intensity to the action sequences, while also conveying the emotional toll that the battle takes on the soldiers. The cast delivers strong performances, particularly Josh Hartnett and Tom Sizemore, who bring depth and nuance to their characters.

Overall, Black Hawk Down is a gripping and intense war film that brings the true story of the Battle of Mogadishu to life with stunning action sequences and powerful performances.

overview: Two soldiers from opposite sites get stuck between the front lines in the same trench. The UN is asked to free them and both sides agree on a ceasefire, but will they stick to it?
production_companies: The Centre du Cinema et de l'Audiovisuel de la Communauté Française de Belgique
Direction du Développement et de la Coopération (DDC), Département Fédéral des Affaires Etrangères
tagline: A lot can happen between the lines
title: No Man's Land
plot:
No Man's Land (Serbo-Croatian: Ničija zemlja) is a 2001 war film set during the Bosnian War, written and directed by Danis Tanović in his feature debut. Described as a parable, it was a co-production between companies in Bosnia and Herzegovina, Slovenia, Italy, France, Belgium and the United Kingdom. Branko Đurić stars as Čiki, a Bosniak soldier, and Rene Bitorajac as Nino, a Bosnian Serb, with Filip Šovagović as Cera, Georges Siatidis as Sergeant Marchand, Simon Callow as Colonel Soft and Katrin Cartlidge as the journalist Jane Livingstone.

At the height of the war, two wounded soldiers from opposing sides, Čiki and Nino, find themselves trapped together in a trench in the no man's land between the front lines, where they must wait for darkness. At first they trade insults and threats, but gradually they begin to find some common ground. The situation becomes even more precarious when Cera, another wounded Bosniak soldier, regains consciousness and discovers that Bosnian Serb troops have placed a land mine beneath his body, set to explode if he moves. Sergeant Marchand, a French officer with the United Nations Protection Force, tries to help the three men despite orders from his superiors to stay out of it, since UNPROFOR's mandate is to protect humanitarian convoys and remain neutral. Only when a British reporter arrives and media pressure mounts does the UN high command spring into action to try to save the soldiers. As the day wears on, the exhausted and frightened Čiki and Nino continue to quarrel, their hostility escalating even after help arrives, while a mine expert struggles with the device beneath Cera. The film builds toward a bleak conclusion that exposes the absurdity of the conflict and the hollowness of the international response, in which saving face proves more important than saving lives.

No Man's Land won the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film and the Golden Globe for Best Foreign Language Film, as well as the award for best screenplay at the 2001 Cannes Film Festival and from the European Film Academy. It received widespread acclaim, holding a 93% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus calls it bleak and darkly humorous in illustrating the absurdity of war, and a Metacritic score of 84. It earned about $4.9 million worldwide.

overview: The "black sheep" son of a wealthy family meets a young psychiatric patient who's been raised in isolation her entire life. He takes the naive young woman home for his brother's wedding an improbable romance blooms, as she impresses everyone with her genuine, simple charms.
tagline: She's stepping out into the world.
title: Barefoot
plot:
Barefoot is a 2014 American romantic comedy film directed by Andrew Fleming and written by Stephen Zotnowski. It is technically a remake of the 2005 German film Barfuss by Til Schweiger, although that film was itself based on Zotnowski's original screenplay. Evan Rachel Wood stars as Daisy Kensington, a young psychiatric patient raised in isolation, and Scott Speedman as Jay Wheeler, the black sheep of a wealthy family, with Treat Williams and Kate Burton as Jay's parents and J. K. Simmons as Dr. Bertleman. The film was produced by WhiteFlame Productions.

Jay, a ne'er-do-well working as a janitor at a Los Angeles psychiatric hospital as part of his probation, intervenes one night when a fellow janitor tries to assault a patient, Daisy, by pretending to be a doctor. Daisy, who was admitted to the hospital after being raised in isolation and has gone barefoot all her life, follows Jay when he leaves. Rather than return her, he takes her with him to his brother's wedding in New Orleans, hoping to convince his family that he has turned his life around, when in reality he needs money to pay off a loan shark. Daisy impresses his family, but she tells Jay that she was hospitalized for killing her mother, and when Jay's suspicious father presses her with questions, she suffers a panic attack. After admitting the truth to his parents, Jay sets out with Daisy in his father's vintage RV. Pursued by the authorities, the pair enjoy an unlikely road trip, outwitting a police officer along the way, and grow closer. When Daisy overhears Jay telling Dr. Bertleman that he will bring her back, she flees and crashes the RV. Jay learns that it was her mother, not Daisy, who heard voices, and that Daisy blames herself for her mother's death. Daisy is returned to the hospital and Jay is arrested. Released on bail, Jay finds his apartment ransacked by the loan shark and realizes that he wants to be with Daisy, devising a desperate plan to get back inside the hospital to see her.

Barefoot premiered at the Santa Barbara International Film Festival on February 2, 2014, and received a limited theatrical release by Roadside Attractions, alongside a video-on-demand release, on February 21, grossing only $15,071 in theaters. Critics gave it negative reviews, with a 19% Rotten Tomatoes rating and a Metacritic score of 22.

overview: An oddball group of cops, criminals, tourists, and teens converge in a Georgia forest where a 500-pound black bear goes on a murderous rampage after unintentionally ingesting cocaine.
tagline: Get in line.
title: Cocaine Bear
plot:
Cocaine Bear is a dark comedy film that delves into the consequences of addiction and the exploitation of nature for human gain. The movie follows the story of a bear that ingests a large amount of cocaine, leading to a series of chaotic events.

At its core, Cocaine Bear explores the theme of the destructive power of addiction. The bear's transformation from a gentle creature to a violent force is a powerful metaphor for the devastating effects of substance abuse on individuals and society as a whole. The film also critiques the exploitation of nature for human purposes, highlighting the consequences of treating animals as mere commodities.

Furthermore, Cocaine Bear touches on themes of class struggle and social inequality. The movie portrays a world where the wealthy and powerful exploit the natural resources and creatures for their own gain, while the poor and marginalized are left to suffer the consequences. This commentary on class struggle is often humorous and satirical, but also serves as a scathing critique of societal ills.

Ultimately, Cocaine Bear is a film that uses humor and absurdity to comment on some very serious issues. It's a wild ride that will keep you laughing and on the edge of your seat, while also making you think about the consequences of our actions on the world around us.

overview: Two competing lawyers join forces to sue a prestigious law firm for AIDS discrimination. As their unlikely friendship develops their courage overcomes the prejudice and corruption of their powerful adversaries.
tagline: No one would take on his case... until one man was willing to take on the system.
title: Philadelphia
plot:
Philadelphia is a drama film released in 1993, directed by Jonathan Demme and produced by TriStar Pictures. The movie stars Tom Hanks as Andrew Beckett, a young lawyer who is fired from his job at a prestigious law firm due to his AIDS diagnosis.

The story begins with Andrew Beckett (Tom Hanks), a successful and ambitious lawyer working for the law firm of Joseph Miller & Keefe. However, when he contracts HIV through a blood transfusion during a surgery, his life takes a drastic turn. Despite being aware of his condition, Andrew is fired from his job due to the stigma surrounding AIDS at that time.

Andrew seeks help from his friend and colleague, Joe Miller (Denzel Washington), who is also a lawyer at the firm. However, when Joe tries to support Andrew, he is met with resistance from their boss, Alvin "Al" Courtenay (Martin Landau). Courtenay refuses to acknowledge Andrew's condition and instead accuses him of being "unfit for work."

Andrew decides to take on his former employer in a lawsuit, claiming wrongful termination due to his AIDS diagnosis. He hires a new lawyer, Joe Miller, who agrees to take on the case despite the risks involved.

As the trial progresses, it becomes clear that Courtenay's actions were motivated by fear and prejudice against people with HIV/AIDS. The court ultimately rules in Andrew's favor, awarding him $1.4 million in damages.

Throughout the film, Tom Hanks delivers a powerful performance as Andrew Beckett, conveying the emotional toll of being ostracized due to his condition. Denzel Washington also shines as Joe Miller, who becomes a source of support and strength for Andrew during this difficult time.

The movie tackles themes of prejudice, discrimination, and the importance of human rights. The film's portrayal of the AIDS epidemic in the 1990s is both poignant and thought-provoking, highlighting the need for greater understanding and acceptance of people living with HIV/AIDS.

In the end, Andrew Beckett emerges victorious, but not without scars. The film concludes on a hopeful note, as Andrew begins to rebuild his life and find a new sense of purpose. The movie's powerful message about the importance of empathy and compassion resonates long after the credits roll.

Overall, Philadelphia is a masterful drama that explores themes of prejudice, identity, and the human condition. With outstanding performances from Tom Hanks and Denzel Washington, this film remains a powerful and thought-provoking classic of American cinema.

overview: Straitlaced Princeton University admissions officer, Portia Nathan is caught off-guard when she makes a recruiting visit to an alternative high school overseen by her former college classmate, the freewheeling John Pressman. Pressman has surmised that Jeremiah, his gifted yet very unconventional student, might well be the son that Portia secretly gave up for adoption many years ago.
tagline: Let someone in.
title: Admission
plot:
Admission is a 2013 American romantic drama film that explores the complexities of human relationships, identity, and the search for meaning. The movie delves into the theme of nostalgia, as the protagonist, Portia Nathan, played by Tina Fey, grapples with her past and the choices she made in life.

The film also touches on the idea of regret and the what-ifs that haunt us. Portia's complicated relationship with her daughter, Lily, serves as a catalyst for her introspection, forcing her to confront the decisions she made about her own life and career. This introspection leads to a deeper understanding of herself and her place in the world.

Furthermore, Admission explores the theme of identity and how it evolves over time. Portia's journey is marked by self-discovery, as she navigates her relationships with others and comes to terms with who she is today. The film suggests that our identities are not fixed entities but rather fluid and dynamic, shaped by our experiences and choices.

The movie also examines the complexities of mother-daughter relationships, highlighting the tensions and conflicts that can arise between generations. Portia's relationship with Lily is fraught with emotion, as they struggle to connect and understand each other.

Ultimately, Admission presents a nuanced exploration of human emotions, relationships, and the search for meaning in life. The film invites viewers to reflect on their own experiences and choices, encouraging them to consider the complexities of identity, regret, and the power of human connection.

overview: 27 years after overcoming the malevolent supernatural entity Pennywise, the former members of the Losers' Club, who have grown up and moved away from Derry, are brought back together by a devastating phone call.
tagline: You'll Float Again
title: It Chapter Two
plot:
It Chapter Two is a 2019 American horror film directed by Andy Muschietti, based on the novel of the same name by Stephen King. The film serves as a sequel to the 2017 film It and concludes the story of the Losers' Club.

The movie takes place 27 years after the events of the first film. The Losers' Club, now in their mid-40s, has been reunited for Pennywise's (Bill Skarsgård) return to Derry, Maine. The group consists of Bill Denbrough (James McAvoy), Beverly Marsh (Jessica Chastain), Ben Hanscom (Jay Ryan), Richie Tozier (Bill Hader), Mike Hanlon (Isaiah Mustafa), and Eddie Kaspbrak (James Ransone).

As Pennywise returns, the Losers' Club must face their personal demons and confront the evil entity once again. The group is forced to return to Derry, where they are met with a mixture of nostalgia and terror. They soon realize that Pennywise has been awakened by a mysterious ritual performed by a group of children who have been possessed by his spirit.

The Losers' Club must work together to stop Pennywise's return and save the town of Derry from destruction. Along the way, they are forced to confront their own personal traumas and the consequences of their past actions. The film features a mix of horror, drama, and coming-of-age themes, as the characters navigate their complex relationships with each other.

One of the standout aspects of It Chapter Two is its exploration of the Losers' Club's adult lives. The film delves into the personal struggles and triumphs of each character, adding depth to the story and making it more relatable to audiences. The film also features a number of memorable performances, including Jessica Chastain's portrayal of Beverly Marsh, which earned her an Academy Award nomination.

Overall, It Chapter Two is a satisfying conclusion to the Losers' Club's story, offering a mix of horror, drama, and emotional depth. While it may not be as tightly wound as its predecessor, the film delivers on its promise of a thrilling and emotionally resonant conclusion to the series.

original_title: Scary Stories to Tell in the Dark
overview: Mill Valley, Pennsylvania, Halloween night, 1968. After playing a joke on a school bully, Stella and her friends decide to sneak into a supposedly haunted house that once belonged to the powerful Bellows family, unleashing dark forces that they will be unable to control.
tagline: Stories taken from true urban legends
title: Scary Stories to Tell in the Dark
plot:
Scary Stories to Tell in the Dark is a 2019 supernatural horror film directed by André Øvredal and based on Alvin Schwartz's children's book series. Dan and Kevin Hageman wrote the screenplay from a story by Guillermo del Toro, Patrick Melton and Marcus Dunstan, and del Toro also produced. CBS Films acquired the rights in 2013, del Toro came aboard in 2016 and Øvredal was hired in late 2017. A co-production of the United States, Canada and Mexico, it was shot in Ontario between August and November 2018 and released by Lionsgate on August 9, 2019. Del Toro explained that he avoided an anthology format because such films are only as good as their weakest segment.

On Halloween night in 1968, in the fictional town of Mill Valley, Pennsylvania, teenagers Stella, Auggie and Chuck and the newcomer Ramón explore the supposedly haunted Bellows house. They find a book of horror stories by Sarah Bellows, an outcast girl blamed for the deaths of local children who reportedly killed herself in 1898, and Stella takes it home. New stories begin writing themselves in blood, and each comes true. The bully Tommy is turned into the scarecrow Harold, and Auggie is dragged away by a corpse searching for its missing toe. Chuck's sister Ruth survives a swelling that bursts with spiders but is left traumatized.

Investigating, the friends learn that Sarah actually hanged herself in a hospital where her brother, a doctor, had subjected her to electroshock to make her confess, and that the children had really died because the family's paper mill poisoned the water with mercury. Chuck is absorbed by the Pale Lady, and after Police Chief Turner arrests Stella and Ramón, exposing Ramón as a draft dodger, the Jangly Man kills Turner. Back at the Bellows house, Stella relives Sarah's abuse and promises to tell the truth if she stops the killings, then writes the true story in her own blood, and the monsters vanish. Ramón leaves for Vietnam, while Stella searches for a way to bring Chuck and Auggie back.

The cast includes Zoe Colletti, Michael Garza, Gabriel Rush, Austin Zajur, Natalie Ganzhorn, Austin Abrams, Dean Norris, Gil Bellows and Lorraine Toussaint, with Javier Botet also joining the cast. Reviews were generally positive, with 78% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, praise for its faithful re-creations of the books' scares and some complaints about filler. It grossed $104.5 million worldwide, and a sequel is in development.

overview: The modern-day story focuses on two beautiful young vampires who are living the good nightlife in New York until love enters the picture and each has to make a choice that will jeopardize their immortality.
tagline: Dating Sucks
title: Vamps
plot:
Vamps is a 2012 American comedy horror film written and directed by Amy Heckerling. Alicia Silverstone and Krysten Ritter lead a cast that includes Dan Stevens, Richard Lewis, Wallace Shawn, Justin Kirk, Kristen Johnston, Malcolm McDowell and Sigourney Weaver. The story follows two vampires who try to keep up with trends and stay youthful while living without human blood and dealing with the malevolent vampire who created them.

Goody and Stacy are vampires enjoying life in New York City. Goody was turned in 1841 by the vampire Cisserus, and after leaving the man she loved in the 1960s she struggled with her existence until Cisserus turned Stacy in 1992. Goody taught Stacy to live on rat blood and use her new powers, while Stacy helps Goody stay young and fashionable. Goody hides her true age, fearing that Stacy will see her as old. At a vampire support meeting she learns that if their maker, or "stem", Cisserus is killed, they will revert to their human ages. Working as an exterminator at a hospital, Goody meets her former boyfriend Danny for the first time since the 1960s. They reconnect while she pretends to be her own daughter, but Danny discovers the truth when he sees her bite a man to stop a stroke, and she explains that she left so that he could build a life with someone who could grow old with him.

When the government uses the Patriot Act to hunt vampires, Goody devises a plan to alter the records of every vampire in the New York area during a solar eclipse, and the vampires celebrate its success with a party, though Cisserus massacres a restaurant full of people. Stacy begins dating Joey, a college student who turns out to be the son of the vampire hunter Dr. Van Helsing. After seeing Stacy climb down his building before dawn, Joey accepts what she is. Stacy then becomes pregnant and learns that the baby can survive only if she becomes human again, which requires killing Cisserus. With Joey and Van Helsing, the two women kill him. Stacy, now forty, looks much the same, but Goody ages rapidly. Revealing her true age, she visits Times Square with Stacy and Joey to reminisce and crumbles to dust as the sun rises. Years later, Van Helsing plays with Stacy and Joey's daughter, named after Goody, and is amused to see that she has fangs.

The film received a limited theatrical release on November 2, 2012, followed by Blu-ray and DVD editions. Reviews were mixed, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting a 56% approval rating from 18 critics.

overview: Deep inside the mountain of Dovre, something gigantic awakens after being trapped for a thousand years. Destroying everything in its path, the creature is fast approaching the capital of Norway. But how do you stop something you thought only existed in Norwegian folklore?
tagline: Mountains will move.
title: Troll
plot:
Troll is a 2022 Norwegian epic monster film directed by Roar Uthaug and written by Espen Auken, starring Ine Marie Wilmann, Kim Falck, Mads Sjøgård Pettersen and Gard B. Eidsvold. It follows a ragtag group who must stop an ancient giant troll awakened inside a Norwegian mountain before it wreaks havoc across the country. Uthaug developed the project with Motion Blur as his film Tomb Raider was nearing completion, drawing on a folklore-inspired idea he had been considering for more than twenty years. Principal photography took place from August to November 2021, with locations including Dovre, Lom, Askim and Ulsteinvik, and the score was written by Johannes Ringen.

As a child, Nora Tidemann listens to her father Tobias tell stories about trolls and how they shaped the mountains. Years later, a tunneling operation through the mountains of Dovre triggers an eruption that kills workers and protesters. Nora, now a paleontologist, is recruited by the government along with other experts, and while most blame a methane pocket, she and the prime minister's adviser Andreas notice that the area is marked by enormous impressions resembling footprints. When a second incident destroys a house near Lesja, Nora, Andreas and Captain Kris Holm of the Norwegian special forces seek help from Tobias, who lost his professorship for believing that myths had a basis in fact. In the mountains, they accidentally awaken a troll some 50 metres tall that had been camouflaged against the mountainside, capturing the first video proof of its existence. Military attacks only irritate the creature, Tobias is killed while trying to communicate with it, and an attempt to repel it with church bells, based on old legends, instead sends it on a destructive rampage. As the troll heads for Oslo and the government prepares a drastic nuclear option, Nora and Andreas follow Tobias's notes to the Royal Palace, where they uncover a long-buried secret about the fate of Norway's trolls, transforming Nora's understanding of the creature and what drives it.

Netflix released Troll on 1 December 2022. It received generally positive reviews, holding a 90% rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus says that its rich mythology and exciting action make up for a familiar monster-movie formula, and a Metacritic score of 62. A sequel, Troll 2, was released in 2025.

overview: An ex-fireman with PTSD goes on the run when accused of a crime he doesn't even remember committing, leading him down a rabbit hole of conspiracy to the highest degree.
tagline: You Can't Outrun Your Self.
title: Indemnity
plot:
Indemnity is a 2021 South African action thriller film written and directed by Travis Taute in his feature debut. Produced by Benjamin Overmeyer and Bradley Joshua for Gambit Films, in association with M-Net Films and the National Film and Video Foundation, it stars Jarrid Geduld as a traumatised Cape Town firefighter on the run, with Gail Mabalane, André Jacobs, Nicole Fortuin, Abduragman Adams and Louw Venter. Shot by Zenn van Zyl with music by Kyle Shepherd, and in Afrikaans and English, the film premiered at the Fantasia International Film Festival in August 2021, where it was nominated for the Cheval Noir award, and was released in the United States by Magnet Releasing on 11 February 2022. It runs 124 minutes.

A prologue shows firefighter Theo Abrams (Geduld) and his colleagues battling a catastrophic blaze in a Cape Flats township, where he defies protocol to rescue a baby from a burning home, with tragic consequences that later return to him in flashbacks. Months afterwards he is suspended from his job, suffering from severe post-traumatic stress disorder and dulling it with alcohol rather than through his mandatory therapy sessions. His relationship with his wife Angela (Fortuin), a journalist, is strained, and she has warned him, after a tip from a mysterious informant, that he is in danger. One morning, after an argument, Theo wakes up to find her strangled beside him, with no memory of what happened and the evidence pointing to him. Disbelieved by police detective Rene Williamson (Mabalane) and pursued by deputy police chief Alan Shard, who is determined to catch him before he retires, he escapes when a police van crashes and, while on the run, investigates a conspiracy linked to the shadowy defence contractor M-Tech, which appears to be targeting a list of seemingly unconnected people.

Reviews were generally favourable about the action and less so about the script. Variety praised the sharp fight choreography and stunt work, including an extended hotel-room escape, and Geduld's charismatic performance in moments of panic and rage, but found the dialogue flat and declarative, likened the plot to The Fugitive, The Bourne Identity and The Manchurian Candidate, and felt the late turn into light science fiction strained the budget. Noel Murray of the Los Angeles Times wrote that the weight of exposition dragged down a strong premise, while the German critic Christopher Diekhaus singled out Geduld's intensely physical performance.

overview: Every culture has one – the horrible monster fueling young children's nightmares. But for Tim, the Boogeyman still lives in his memories as a creature that devoured his father 16 years earlier. Is the Boogeyman real? Or did Tim make him up to explain why his father abandoned his family?
tagline: You thought it was just a story.
title: Boogeyman
plot:
Boogeyman is a supernatural horror film that delves into the darker aspects of human psychology and the consequences of unresolved trauma. The movie follows a young man, Eric Balfour, who returns to his childhood home after his mother's death, only to discover that it holds a dark secret: the Boogeyman, a malevolent entity that preys on people with deep-seated fears.

At its core, Boogeyman explores the theme of repressed emotions and the destructive power of unresolved trauma. The film suggests that when we fail to confront our deepest fears and anxieties, they can manifest in terrifying ways, often targeting those who are most vulnerable. This idea is expertly woven throughout the narrative, as Eric's own dark past begins to unravel, revealing a complex web of psychological scars.

The movie also touches on the theme of guilt and responsibility, particularly in relation to Eric's mother's death. As he navigates his way through the haunted house, he must confront the possibility that his own actions may have contributed to her demise. This sense of culpability adds a layer of tension to the story, as Eric struggles to come to terms with his past and find a way to move forward.

Furthermore, Boogeyman can be seen as a commentary on the fragility of the human psyche. The film's portrayal of the Boogeyman as a manifestation of collective fears suggests that our deepest anxieties are not unique to ourselves, but rather shared experiences that can be triggered by external stimuli. This idea is both unsettling and thought-provoking, highlighting the ways in which our individual traumas can be linked to broader societal concerns.

Overall, Boogeyman is a gripping horror film that masterfully explores the darker corners of human psychology, revealing the devastating consequences of unresolved trauma and the destructive power of repressed emotions.

overview: Thunder, an abandoned young cat seeking shelter from a storm, stumbles into the strangest house imaginable, owned by an old magician and inhabited by a dazzling array of automatons and gizmos. Not everyone welcomes the new addition to the troupe as Jack Rabbit and Maggie Mouse plot to evict Thunder. The situation gets worse when the magician lands in hospital and his scheming nephew sees his chance to cash in by selling the mansion. Our young hero is determined to earn his place and so he enlists the help of some wacky magician's assistants to protect his magical new home.
tagline: One lost little cat. One magical adventure.
title: The House of Magic
plot:
The House of Magic, released in the United States as Thunder and the House of Magic (French: Le Manoir magique), is a 2013 animated fantasy comedy film directed by Ben Stassen and Jeremy Degruson, the latter making his directorial debut. The voice cast includes Brianne Siddall, Joey Camen, Elisa Gabrielli, Robin Atkin Downes and Shanelle Workman. The story follows an abandoned young cat who takes refuge in the home of an elderly retired magician filled with robots and gadgets.

Left behind by his owners when they move away from their home in Boston, a tabby kitten searches for shelter and finds his way into an old house the neighbors believe is haunted. Inside he meets its owner, Mr. Lawrence, a kindly old magician, along with his animals and automatons, among them a mouse named Maggie, her grumpy rabbit friend Jack and Edison, a robot with a light bulb for a head. Jack chases the kitten to throw him out, but Lawrence adopts him and names him Thunder after his fear of lightning. Jealous and afraid of being replaced, Jack and Maggie try everything to drive Thunder away.

Thunder joins Lawrence's rabbit-out-of-a-hat routine at a children's hospital magic show, but on the way home Lawrence is injured and hospitalized with a broken leg. His materialistic nephew Daniel, a real estate agent, tricks him into giving him power of attorney and plans to sell the house. Jack and Maggie convince the automatons that Thunder caused the accident, but because Daniel is severely allergic to cats, they agree to keep the kitten to help scare off buyers, though they lock him in a birdcage. A Chihuahua belonging to one prospective buyer frees Thunder, and visiting the hospital, Thunder learns that Lawrence never blamed him. The household drives several more buyers away by convincing them the house is haunted. When Lawrence returns with the help of children he met in the hospital and finds Daniel swinging a wrecking ball at the house, he sees his nephew's true nature. Thunder saves the automatons, rescuing Maggie and winning her friendship. Thunder is accepted into the family, and once Lawrence recovers, the kitten stars in his magic shows alongside Jack and Maggie.

The film grossed about $64.2 million, nearly all of it outside North America. It earned 73% on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus said that its visual splendor compensated young viewers for its lack of narrative depth, and a Metacritic score of 47. A spin-off series, Presto! School of Magic, was announced in 2017.

original_title: จันดารา ปฐมบท
overview: Set in the 1930s, the story recounts the growing pains of Jan, whose mother dies while giving birth to him and who’s intensely hated by his sadistic and debauched father. Jan grows up with his stepmother, and he struggles to reconcile his guilt and longing with different women in his life.
tagline: A tragedy of lust, love and revenge…
title: Jan Dara: The Beginning
plot:
Jan Dara: The Beginning is a 2011 Thai drama film directed by Ananda Everingham, not 2012. I'll provide you with the details.

The movie is based on the novel "Jan Dara" by Thak Hong Jai and tells the story of two brothers, Jan (played by Poj Arnon) and Dara (played by Yannin Sookkhem), who are extremely close in age and share a deep bond. The film begins with the introduction of the two brothers, showcasing their unique relationship and the love they have for each other.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Jan is the favored son, while Dara is often overlooked by their parents. This disparity leads to feelings of resentment and jealousy in Dara's heart. The situation worsens when their father, a wealthy businessman, decides to marry a woman named Nong (played by Urassaya Sperbund), who is much younger than him.

The arrival of Nong brings about significant changes in the household, including the introduction of her son, Jai (played by Poj Arnon's real-life brother, Pongpat Arnon). Jan and Dara are forced to navigate their complicated relationships with each other and their new family members. As they grow older, their bond becomes increasingly strained due to the pressures of their father's expectations and the changing dynamics within the household.

Throughout the film, the director explores themes of love, loyalty, and identity. The characters' struggles to find their place in the world are deeply rooted in their relationships with each other. Jan Dara: The Beginning is a poignant portrayal of sibling love, family dynamics, and the complexities of growing up.

The movie received critical acclaim for its nuanced storytelling, strong performances, and thoughtful exploration of complex themes. It has become a beloved Thai drama that continues to resonate with audiences worldwide.

overview: After sparing a girl's life during a massacre, an elite Triad assassin is targeted by an onslaught of murderous gangsters.
tagline: In search of salvation, he'll make the city rain blood.
title: The Night Comes for Us
plot:
The Night Comes for Us is a 2018 Indonesian action thriller film directed by Timo Tjahjanto. The movie follows an ex-con, Jaka (played by Iko Uwais), who tries to go straight after being released from prison but gets pulled back into his old life when he's forced to confront his past.

The main themes of the movie include:

1. Redemption: Jaka's journey is a classic tale of redemption, as he tries to leave his violent past behind and start anew. However, the film shows that this is not an easy task, and Jaka's past continues to haunt him throughout the story.
2. Loyalty and Family: The movie highlights the importance of loyalty and family in Indonesian culture. Jaka's relationships with his brother and sister are central to the plot, and he will stop at nothing to protect them.
3. Violence and Trauma: The film is known for its intense and brutal fight scenes, which serve as a metaphor for the trauma and violence that Jaka has experienced in his past. The movie shows how these experiences have shaped him into the person he is today.
4. Corruption and Injustice: The plot revolves around corruption and injustice within the Indonesian prison system, highlighting the struggles of those who are trapped in a cycle of poverty and violence.

The Night Comes for Us received critical acclaim for its intense action sequences, stunning cinematography, and thought-provoking themes.

overview: A dangerous CIA renegade resurfaces after a decade on the run. When the safe house he's remanded to is attacked by mercenaries, a rookie operative escapes with him. Now, the unlikely allies must stay alive long enough to uncover who wants them dead.
tagline: No one is safe
title: Safe House
plot:
Safe House is a 2012 American action thriller film directed by Daniel Espinosa and starring Denzel Washington and Ryan Reynolds.

The movie follows the story of Matt Weston (Ryan Reynolds), a young CIA agent who is assigned to protect David Callum (Denzel Washington), a seasoned operative who has been hiding in witness protection. However, their safe house is compromised, and they must go on the run to evade a ruthless assassin named Varga (Samuel L. Jackson).

The main themes of Safe House include:

1. **Loyalty and Trust**: The film explores the complex relationship between Matt and David, who are forced to rely on each other for survival. As they navigate their way through treacherous situations, they must confront their own trust issues and learn to put aside their differences.
2. **Identity and Belonging**: David's character is a classic example of an outsider who has been forced to reinvent himself. Throughout the film, he struggles with his past and his sense of identity, which serves as a metaphor for the human desire to belong and find one's place in the world.
3. **Redemption and Sacrifice**: As Matt and David work together to evade their pursuers, they are forced to confront their own personal demons and make difficult choices that will ultimately lead to redemption or sacrifice.
4. **The Cost of Protection**: The film highlights the high cost of protection and the sacrifices that come with it. David's character has been living in witness protection for years, but at what cost? He is forced to leave behind his life, his family, and his sense of identity.

Overall, Safe House is a gripping action thriller that explores complex themes of loyalty, trust, identity, redemption, and sacrifice.

overview: A socially awkward woman with a fondness for arts and crafts, horses, and supernatural crime shows finds her increasingly lucid dreams trickling into her waking life.
title: Horse Girl
plot:
Horse Girl is a 2020 American drama film directed by Chris and Sean Duplass. The movie follows the story of a teenage girl named Bina, who becomes obsessed with a horse that she believes has supernatural healing powers.

The main theme of Horse Girl revolves around the complexities of adolescence and the struggles of growing up. Bina's obsession with the horse serves as a metaphor for her own emotional turmoil and her desire to escape the mundanity of her life. As she delves deeper into the world of equine mysticism, she begins to question the boundaries between reality and fantasy.

The film also explores themes of mental health, particularly anxiety and depression, which are deeply intertwined with Bina's experiences. Her fixation on the horse becomes a coping mechanism for her emotional pain, but it also leads to further isolation and disconnection from those around her.

Furthermore, Horse Girl touches on the idea of female empowerment and the search for identity. Bina's journey is marked by a desire to break free from societal expectations and forge her own path in life. Her relationship with the horse serves as a symbol of her independence and self-discovery.

Overall, Horse Girl is a poignant exploration of the challenges faced by teenagers navigating the complexities of adolescence, mental health, and identity.

original_title: The Land Before Time VII: The Stone of Cold Fire
overview: Littlefoot and his pals set off in search of a "stone of cold fire" that fell from the night sky. Since he's the only one who has seen it though, nobody really believes him. Petrie's uncle Pterano offers support only because he thinks the stone has secret powers and wants it for himself but conceals this from the rest. The young dinos must figure out the truth, before Pterano gets the power.
title: The Land Before Time VII: The Stone of Cold Fire
plot:
The Land Before Time VII: The Stone of Cold Fire is an animated adventure film that explores several significant themes. At its core, the movie delves into the complexities of friendship and loyalty, as the main characters navigate the challenges of growing up and facing new responsibilities.

One of the primary themes present in the film is the struggle for independence. As the young dinosaurs transition from childhood to adulthood, they must confront their own limitations and learn to rely on themselves. This journey is fraught with self-doubt, fear, and uncertainty, as the characters grapple with the idea of leaving behind the comfort and security of their youth.

The movie also touches upon the theme of sacrifice and the importance of putting the needs of others before one's own desires. The main character, Littlefoot, must make difficult choices that test his courage and loyalty to his friends, ultimately leading him to discover the value of selflessness and the power of friendship in overcoming adversity.

Furthermore, The Stone of Cold Fire explores the idea of identity and self-discovery. As the characters face new challenges and experiences, they are forced to re-evaluate their sense of purpose and belonging within their community. This theme is particularly relevant for Littlefoot, who must come to terms with his own destiny and the weight of responsibility that comes with being a leader.

Throughout the film, these themes are woven together to create a narrative that is both entertaining and emotionally resonant. The movie's use of stunning animation and engaging storytelling brings the prehistoric world to life, immersing audiences in a richly detailed and immersive environment that is both captivating and heartwarming.

overview: Based on the original animated series Ben 10.  Ben becomes targeted by an evil Mechamorph Warrior, named "Retaliator," who mistakenly blames Ben for something he did not do and attempts to destroy all aliens.
title: Ben 10: Destroy All Aliens
plot:
Ben 10: Destroy All Aliens is an animated science fiction comedy film that revolves around the story of Ben Tennyson, a teenager who discovers a device called the Omnitrix, which allows him to transform into different alien creatures. The movie takes place when an alien invasion threatens Earth, and Ben must use his newfound powers to save humanity.

The main theme of the movie is the struggle between individuality and conformity. Ben's unique abilities as an alien-human hybrid make him an outcast among humans, but also give him a sense of purpose and belonging among his alien friends. As he navigates this complex identity crisis, Ben must confront the idea that being different can be both a strength and a weakness.

Another significant theme in the movie is the importance of teamwork and cooperation. Ben's relationships with his grandfather Max, his cousin Gwen, and his new alien allies are crucial to their success against the alien invasion. Through their interactions, the film highlights the value of diverse perspectives and skills coming together to achieve a common goal.

The movie also explores the idea of responsibility and power. As Ben gains more control over the Omnitrix, he must learn to wield its immense power responsibly, balancing his desire for adventure with the need to protect humanity. This theme is particularly relevant in today's world, where individuals are increasingly faced with complex decisions that require careful consideration.

Overall, Ben 10: Destroy All Aliens is a fun and action-packed film that explores themes of identity, teamwork, and responsibility through its engaging storyline and lovable characters.

overview: Many thousands of years in the future, Earth’s cities roam the globe on huge wheels, devouring each other in a struggle for ever diminishing resources. On one of these massive traction cities, the old London, Tom Natsworthy has an unexpected encounter with a mysterious young woman from the wastelands who will change the course of his life forever.
tagline: Some scars never heal
title: Mortal Engines
plot:
Mortal Engines is a 2018 science fantasy adventure film directed by Christian Rivers and written by Fran Walsh, Philippa Boyens, and Peter Jackson. The movie is set in a post-apocalyptic world where cities are on wheels and roam the land, preying on smaller towns to sustain themselves.

In the year 2256, London is one of the largest and most powerful mobile cities, known as Cogtopolis. The city is ruled by the tyrannical Mayor, who controls its citizens through a complex system of gears and machinery. The story follows Hester Shaw (Hera Hilmar), a young woman with a prosthetic leg, who seeks revenge against the man responsible for her father's death.

Hester's father was killed by the leader of the city, Thaddeus Valentine (Robert Sheehan), who is also the inventor of the "mangler" - a machine that can crush and devour smaller cities. Hester sets out on a perilous journey to find Valentine, accompanied by her friend Anubis (Jorge Lendeborg Jr.), a skilled engineer.

As they travel across the land, they encounter other mobile cities, including New London, which is ruled by the ruthless Mayor of London, and the nomadic tribes that live outside the city walls. The group also meets Shangdu, a Chinese city that has been destroyed by Valentine's mangler.

The story takes a dramatic turn when Hester and Anubis discover that Valentine is planning to destroy all the smaller cities in order to create a new world order. They must use their skills and ingenuity to stop him and save the world from destruction.

Throughout the movie, the action unfolds at a breakneck pace, with thrilling chases and battles between the mobile cities. The special effects are impressive, bringing the post-apocalyptic world to life in stunning detail.

One of the standout aspects of Mortal Engines is its unique world-building. The concept of mobile cities roaming the land is both fascinating and terrifying, and the movie does an excellent job of exploring the consequences of such a society. The characters are also well-developed, with Hester being a particularly compelling protagonist.

The ending of the movie sets up a potential sequel, as Hester and Anubis face off against Valentine in a final showdown. However, the conclusion is bittersweet, leaving some questions unanswered and setting the stage for further adventures in this richly imagined world.

Overall, Mortal Engines is an exciting and visually stunning film that will appeal to fans of science fiction and adventure movies. With its unique world-building and compelling characters, it's a must-see for anyone looking for a thrilling ride.

overview: When a poor college student who cracks an online poker game goes bust, he arranges a face-to-face with the man he thinks cheated him, a sly offshore entrepreneur.
tagline: The house always wins.
title: Runner Runner
plot:
Runner Runner is a 2013 American crime thriller film directed by Brad Furman and written by Brian Koppelman and David Levien, starring Justin Timberlake, Ben Affleck, Gemma Arterton and Anthony Mackie. Set in the world of online gambling, it follows a Princeton graduate student who is drawn into the operations of a powerful but corrupt gambling tycoon in Costa Rica. Principal photography took place in 2012 in Puerto Rico and at Princeton.

Richie Furst, a former Wall Street professional, is ineligible for financial aid at Princeton, so he pays for his master's degree by steering fellow students to online gambling sites in return for a cut. When the dean threatens to expel him, Richie tries to win his tuition at online poker, only to lose everything to a player he can prove statistically was cheating. He flies to Costa Rica to confront Ivan Block, the man who runs the world's largest empire of online gambling websites. Impressed when Richie's evidence exposes coders who rigged the software, Ivan fires them and offers Richie a lucrative job helping run the business. Richie is soon living a life of luxury and grows close to Rebecca Shafran, Ivan's former lover, but the job quickly turns dark: he is sent to blackmail a business affiliate and to bribe a local official, who has him beaten when the payment proves too small. Meanwhile, FBI agent Shavers, who has no legal authority in Costa Rica and uses ruthless methods, pressures Richie to help bring Ivan down, at one point having drugs planted in his luggage. Richie's friend Andrew Cronin, who works on the software, suspects that Ivan is running a Ponzi scheme with his players' money. When Ivan brings Richie's father, a heavy gambler, to Costa Rica by buying up his debts, and Cronin is found badly beaten, Richie realizes that he is being set up as the fall guy for Ivan's crimes and must find a way to outmaneuver both the tycoon and the FBI.

Runner Runner was released in the United States on October 4, 2013. It received generally negative reviews from critics and grossed about $62 million worldwide.

overview: Journalist Fred Flarsky reunites with his childhood crush, Charlotte Field, now one of the most influential women in the world. As she prepares to make a run for the Presidency, Charlotte hires Fred as her speechwriter — much to the dismay of her trusted advisers.
tagline: Unlikely but not impossible.
title: Long Shot
plot:
Long Shot is a 2019 American romantic comedy film directed by Jonathan Levine and written by Dan Sterling. The movie stars Seth Rogen, Charlize Theron, O'Shea Jackson Jr., Bob Odenkirk, and June Diane Raphael.

The story begins with Fred Flarsky (Seth Rogen), a charismatic but unemployed journalist who has been living in his parents' basement since the 1990s. He is still close to his childhood friend Charlotte Field (Charlize Theron), who is now a successful and ambitious Secretary of State under President Andrew Dixon (Bob Odenkirk).

Years later, Fred receives an invitation from Charlotte to attend her inauguration as the new Secretary of State.
