During the event, they reconnect, and it becomes clear that their friendship has evolved into something more. However, their social differences and past traumas make a romantic relationship complicated.

As they spend more time together, Fred is drawn back into his old life, including his job at a tabloid newspaper and his relationships with his eccentric family members. Meanwhile, Charlotte's team is working to pass the "Global Health Security Act," which aims to strengthen international cooperation on pandemics.

Despite their growing feelings for each other, Fred struggles to balance his desire for romance with his own sense of identity and purpose. He also faces challenges from his friends and family, who are skeptical about his relationship with Charlotte due to her high-profile position and his lack of ambition.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Charlotte's past is marked by trauma and a complicated relationship with her father, who was a politician. Her desire for power and control stems from a need to prove herself and overcome her insecurities.

Throughout the film, Fred and Charlotte navigate their feelings for each other while also confronting their personal demons. They must decide whether their love can overcome their differences and help them grow as individuals.

The movie culminates with a dramatic speech by Charlotte at the United Nations, where she advocates for global cooperation on pandemics. Meanwhile, Fred's past comes back to haunt him in unexpected ways, forcing him to confront his own insecurities and doubts.

Ultimately, Fred and Charlotte find a way to reconcile their differences and make their relationship work. The film ends with a heartwarming moment of intimacy between the two leads, as they finally find happiness together.

Overall, Long Shot is a charming and witty romantic comedy that explores themes of identity, power, and love. With strong performances from its leads, the movie delivers a satisfying and entertaining ride for audiences.

overview: A cheap, powerful drug emerges during a recession, igniting a moral panic fueled by racism.  Explore the complex history of crack in the 1980s.
title: Crack: Cocaine, Corruption & Conspiracy
plot:
Crack: Cocaine, Corruption & Conspiracy is a 2021 American documentary film directed by Stanley Nelson and produced by his company Firelight Films for Netflix, which released it on 11 January 2021. Running 89 minutes, it examines the crack epidemic that swept American inner cities in the 1980s and how the government and the media responded to it, turning a drug crisis into a moral panic fuelled by racism. Nelson, a Harlem native who lived through the epidemic, combines archival footage, hip-hop music of the era and interviews with former dealers and users, journalists, historians and experts, among them the Columbia University neuroscientist Carl Hart, the writer Nelson George, the activist and former user Felipe Luciano, and the former dealers Samson Styles, "Freeway" Ricky Ross and Corey Pegues.

The film begins with the rise of powder cocaine as an expensive party drug associated with money, power and glamour, popularised by Richard Pryor's 1980 freebasing accident and by Scarface (1983). As supply boomed and prices fell, by 1984 cocaine was reaching working-class neighbourhoods as crack, a smokable form that gave a short, intense high for the price of a child's allowance. Former dealers describe the trade as a gold rush in neighbourhoods where legitimate work paid little, while turf wars turned streets into battlegrounds and addiction tore families apart, hitting women and mothers especially hard. Pegues recounts being stopped by police with 300 vials and released because dealers were paying off officers. The documentary then turns to the Reagan administration's war on drugs and Nancy Reagan's "Just Say No" campaign, the media's exaggerated coverage of so-called crack babies, and the portrayal of users as overwhelmingly Black when, as the film notes, about two-thirds were white, and it traces the punitive sentencing and militarised policing that swelled the prison population under successive presidents.

Owen Gleiberman of Variety called the film eye-opening, praising Nelson's flair for making history more interesting than the myths it dismantles and its account of how government and media turned crack against the communities it victimised. The New York Times described it as a brisk look back at the crisis, while some critics felt it covered too much ground too quickly to explore every issue in depth.

overview: Jess Bhamra, the daughter of a strict Indian couple in London, is not permitted to play organized soccer, even though she is 18. When Jess is playing for fun one day, her impressive skills are seen by Jules Paxton, who then convinces Jess to play for her semi-pro team. Jess uses elaborate excuses to hide her matches from her family while also dealing with her romantic feelings for her coach, Joe.
tagline: Sometimes, to follow your dreams... you've got to bend the rules!
title: Bend It Like Beckham
plot:
Bend It Like Beckham is a 2002 British sports comedy-drama film directed by Gurinder Chadha and produced by Deepak Nayar and Gurinder Chadha.

The main themes of Bend It Like Beckham include:

1. Cultural Identity: The movie explores the theme of cultural identity, particularly in the context of the Indian diaspora in the UK. The protagonist, Jesminder "Jess" Bhamra, struggles to balance her traditional Punjabi upbringing with her desire to fit in with British culture.

2. Family and Tradition: The film highlights the importance of family and tradition in the lives of its characters. Jess's parents, particularly her mother, are portrayed as strict and traditional, while Jess's father is more laid-back and supportive.

3. Self-Discovery: Throughout the movie, Jess navigates her own identity and finds her place in the world. She discovers a passion for football (soccer) and eventually joins a local team, which becomes a source of empowerment and self-expression.

4. Female Empowerment: The film celebrates female empowerment and independence, particularly through Jess's journey from being a shy and uncertain teenager to becoming a confident and talented footballer.

5. Community and Belonging: Bend It Like Beckham emphasizes the importance of community and belonging. Jess finds her place in the world by joining a local football team and forming friendships with her teammates, who accept her for who she is.

The movie features a talented cast, including Parminder Nagra, Keira Knightley, Jonathan Rhys Meyers, Anupam Kher, and Archie Panjabi. The film's success can be attributed to its engaging storyline, memorable characters, and the way it tackles complex themes with humor and sensitivity.

overview: In Los Angeles at the turn of the 1970s, drug-fueled detective Larry "Doc" Sportello investigates the disappearance of an ex-girlfriend.
tagline: Under the paving stones, the beach!
title: Inherent Vice
plot:
Inherent Vice is a 2014 American neo-noir crime comedy film directed by Paul Thomas Anderson, based on the novel of the same name by Thomas Pynchon.

The main themes of Inherent Vice include:

1. **Paranoia and Conspiracy**: The film explores the paranoid world of its protagonist, Doc Sportello (played by Joaquin Phoenix), a laid-back private investigator who becomes embroiled in a complex web of conspiracy involving organized crime, government agencies, and mysterious figures.
2. **The Dark Side of 1970s California**: Inherent Vice is set in the late 1960s and early 1970s, a time of great social change and upheaval in America. The film critiques the excesses and superficiality of the counterculture movement, as well as the darker aspects of American history, such as racism and government corruption.
3. **The Search for Identity**: Doc Sportello's journey is also one of self-discovery, as he navigates a world that seems to be constantly shifting and morphing around him. His search for identity and meaning is reflected in his relationships with others, including his ex-girlfriend Shasta Fay Hepworth (played by Katherine Waterston) and his friend Mickey Wolfmann (played by Eric Roberts).
4. **The Power of Obsession**: The film explores the destructive power of obsession, as embodied by characters like Doc's nemesis, Bigfoot Bjornsen (played by Josh Brolin), who will stop at nothing to achieve his goals.
5. **The Fragmentation of Reality**: Inherent Vice is known for its surreal and dreamlike quality, which reflects the fragmented nature of reality in a world where truth and illusion are constantly blurred.

Overall, Inherent Vice is a complex and thought-provoking film that explores themes of paranoia, conspiracy, identity, obsession, and the fragmentation of reality.

overview: A genetically created Anaconda, cut in half, regenerates itself into two aggressive giant snakes, due to the Blood Orchid.
tagline: Bigger, Faster, Hungrier
title: Anacondas: Trail of Blood
plot:
Anacondas: Trail of Blood is a 2009 American horror film directed by Don E. FauntLeRoy and starring Morris Chestnut, Matt Bushell, and Kari Wuhrer.

The main themes of Anacondas: Trail of Blood revolve around the dangers of playing with nature and the consequences of scientific hubris. The movie takes place in the Amazon rainforest, where a team of scientists and adventurers embark on an expedition to study the legendary anaconda. However, their actions inadvertently awaken the giant reptiles, which begin to wreak havoc on the local population.

Throughout the film, the characters face numerous challenges as they try to survive the deadly attacks of the anacondas. The movie serves as a cautionary tale about the importance of respecting and preserving the natural world. The scientists' reckless behavior and disregard for the environment ultimately lead to their downfall, highlighting the dangers of tampering with nature.

The film also explores themes of colonialism and the exploitation of indigenous cultures. The local population is portrayed as being in harmony with the natural world, while the outsiders bring destruction and chaos. This dichotomy serves as a commentary on the historical legacy of colonialism and the impact it has had on indigenous communities.

Overall, Anacondas: Trail of Blood is a horror film that uses the anaconda as a metaphor for the dangers of playing with nature and the consequences of human actions. The movie's themes are rooted in a cautionary tale about respecting the natural world and preserving the balance of ecosystems.

overview: A hiking trip into the wild turns into a desperate bid for survival for five friends on the run from a mysterious shooter.
title: Prey
plot:
Prey is a 2021 German film directed by Thomas Sieben, who wrote the screenplay with Sonja Ewers. It stars David Kross, Hanno Koffler and Maria Ehrich and was released by Netflix on September 10, 2021.

Five friends, Roman, his brother Albert, Peter, Vincent and Stefan, are on a canoeing trip through the forest when they stop for a campfire and hear gunshots in the distance, which they assume mark the start of hunting season. Albert finds a toy unicorn on a hike and pockets it. When another shot wounds Vincent in the hand and further bullets shred their car's tire and windows, they realize a sharpshooter is hunting them. They flee into the trees toward a road, and Albert sprains his ankle in a hole. Calling for help to a woman by a lake, they watch her raise a rifle and kill Stefan: she is the hunter. At a forest information center, a clerk tries to call the emergency services for them, but the gunwoman, Eva, kills both the clerk and Vincent through the window.

Only Peter, Roman and Albert remain. Eva lets them walk away once, and in an abandoned settlement with children's playgrounds Roman finds a laptop video revealing that Eva's baby was once shot by accident, a loss that has driven her to hunt unarmed men. Tensions within the group surface when Peter presses Albert about Lisa, Roman's girlfriend. Peter is soon shot down and executed as he pleads for his life, and Eva wounds Albert but lets Roman drag him away.

Using Albert's fingerprint to unlock his phone, Roman discovers nude photographs of Lisa and realizes his brother has betrayed him. Albert apologizes, but Roman strikes him and hides him in a cave that holds the bodies of other men Eva has shot. Roman climbs out with the unicorn toy and sneaks up behind her; she shoots him in the foot, but when he shows her the toy and she reaches for it, he wrestles away her rifle and throws it aside. Disarmed, Eva throws herself from a cliff, leaving Roman to sit down in exhausted relief.

Kross plays Roman and Koffler plays Albert, with Ehrich as the hunter Eva, Robert Finster as Peter, Yung Ngo as Vincent, Klaus Steinbacher as Stefan, Livia Matthes as Lisa and Nellie Thalbach as Jenny.

overview: Legendary rock band Foo Fighters move into an Encino mansion steeped in grisly rock and roll history to record their much anticipated 10th album. Once in the house, Dave Grohl finds himself grappling with supernatural forces that threaten both the completion of the album and the lives of the band.
tagline: He gives new meaning to a killer track.
title: Studio 666
plot:
Studio 666 is a 2022 American comedy horror film directed by B. J. McDonnell from a screenplay by Jeff Buhler and Rebecca Hughes, based on a story by Dave Grohl. Grohl and his Foo Fighters bandmates Taylor Hawkins, Nate Mendel, Pat Smear, Chris Shiflett and Rami Jaffee play fictionalized versions of themselves, making it the band's first non-documentary film. Grohl drew on the band's experience of recording their tenth album, and the film was shot in secret in the same house where they had made Medicine at Midnight. Production was halted near the end by the COVID-19 pandemic and resumed months later in Los Angeles, where a planned six days of shooting stretched to three weeks under safety rules.

In 1993, in Encino, Dream Widow frontman Greg Nole attacks his bandmates with a hammer, killing the drummer Skye Willow, and then hangs himself. In 2019 the Foo Fighters, pushed by their manager Jeremy Shill to beat writer's block and deliver a new album, move into the same mansion. Grohl is enthralled by the house, and after the band's technician Krug is electrocuted, he finds a basement full of satanic objects and becomes possessed by Nole's demonic spirit while listening to an old demo tape. Driven by the demon, he forces the band to keep recording while secretly killing a delivery man and then Shiflett.

With help from their neighbor Samantha, the others discover the history of the house and the cause of Grohl's possession, and learn that they need a book to exorcise him. Grohl kills Jaffee and Samantha with a chainsaw and Hawkins with a cymbal once he finishes the song, before Mendel and Smear free him, and the spirits of Dream Widow drag the demon back to hell. Jeremy and the property developer Barb Weems then reveal that they planned everything, and Mendel and Smear die in the ensuing violence. Told that the album is a hit and his solo career has begun, Grohl abandons his fight with Jeremy and, a year later, prepares a solo concert with marks of possession around his eyes.

Whitney Cummings plays Samantha, Will Forte the delivery man Darren, Jeff Garlin the manager and Leslie Grossman Barb, with Jenna Ortega as Skye, Kerry King as Krug and small roles for Lionel Richie and John Carpenter. Released by Open Road Films and Briarcliff Entertainment on February 25, 2022, it earned only $1.54 million in its opening weekend. Reviews were mixed, with 56% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, and it was Hawkins's final film.

original_title: 吸血鬼ハンターD ブラッドラスト
overview: D has been hired to track down Meier Link, a notoriously powerful vampire who has abducted a woman, Charlotte Elbourne. D's orders are strict - find Charlotte, at any cost. For the first time, D faces serious competition. The Markus Brothers, a family of Vampire Hunters, were hired for the same bounty. D Must intercept Meier and conquer hostile forces on all sides in a deadly race against time.
title: Vampire Hunter D: Bloodlust
plot:
Vampire Hunter D: Bloodlust is a 2000 anime film directed by Toshiya Shinohara, produced by Madhouse, and based on the novel "The Book of Vampire Hunting" by Hideyuki Kikuchi.

The main themes of Vampire Hunter D: Bloodlust include:

1. **Existentialism**: The film explores the concept of existence and the nature of humanity through the character of D, a vampire hunter who is also an immortal being. D's existence is marked by loneliness and isolation, yet he continues to hunt vampires, suggesting that his purpose in life is to find meaning in a seemingly meaningless world.
2. **Morality and Ethics**: The film raises questions about morality and ethics in the face of immortality. D's actions are guided by a strict code of honor, which leads him to confront difficult moral dilemmas. This theme is further complicated by the presence of vampires, who embody both beauty and terror.
3. **Loneliness and Isolation**: D's character is defined by his loneliness and isolation. He has lived for centuries, watching civilizations rise and fall, and yet he remains a solitary figure. This theme is echoed in the film's depiction of the vampire characters, who are also isolated and disconnected from humanity.
4. **Beauty and Ugliness**: The film explores the tension between beauty and ugliness, as embodied by the vampire characters. D's own appearance is that of an old man, while the vampires are depicted as beautiful and alluring. This theme highlights the complexity of human (and vampire) nature.
5. **The Human Condition**: Ultimately, the film grapples with fundamental questions about the human condition. What does it mean to be human? How do we define ourselves in a world filled with monsters and mysteries?

Overall, Vampire Hunter D: Bloodlust is a thought-provoking film that explores complex themes through its unique blend of action, horror, and fantasy elements.

overview: Edee, in the aftermath of an unfathomable event, finds herself unable to stay connected to the world she once knew and in the face of that uncertainty, retreats to the magnificent, but unforgiving, wilds of the Rockies. After a local hunter brings her back from the brink of death, she must find a way to live again.
tagline: A story of humanity, in the face of uncertainty
title: Land
plot:
Land is a 2021 psychological drama directed by Robin Wright in her feature directorial debut, from a screenplay by Jesse Chatham and Erin Dignam. Wright also stars, alongside Demián Bichir and Kim Dickens. Jessica Lange had been set for the lead before dropping out over scheduling conflicts. The film was shot over 29 days in October 2019 in the Rockies west of Calgary, Alberta, where rapid weather changes let the crew capture the four seasons of the story's two years in one month, with town scenes filmed in Didsbury.

After a traumatic experience that leaves her wanting to avoid people, Edee Holzer leaves the city for a small, remote cabin in Wyoming, determined to live alone with no phone, car or other link to the outside world. She struggles to chop wood and catch fish, and when a black bear wrecks her cabin and devours her supplies, she reaches a breaking point. Unable to shoot a deer, she nearly turns the rifle on herself, stopping only when she remembers her sister Emma begging her not to. Hurt during a blizzard, she is found and nursed back to health by Miguel, a local hunter, and his nurse friend Alawa.

Respecting Edee's wish for solitude, Miguel teaches her to trap, hunt and grow food so that she can survive on her own, and a quiet friendship develops. He tells her that his wife and daughter died in a car accident eight years earlier, while she admits only that she once had a family. When Miguel goes away and leaves his dog in her care, Edee looks at old photographs of her husband and son. After months without him, she walks into town for the first time and, with Alawa's help, finds Miguel bedridden and dying of cancer. He confesses that he was driving drunk the night his family died, and Edee tells him that her husband Adam and son Drew were killed in a random shooting at a concert hall. Thanking him for giving her life back, she leaves with the phone he gave her and calls Emma for the first time since coming to Wyoming.

Land premiered at the Sundance Film Festival on January 31, 2021, and was released by Focus Features on February 12, 2021, grossing $3.1 million worldwide. Critics were generally positive, with 69% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 61, though some felt its beautiful landscapes could not hide a hollow center.

overview: No one thought Donna would go very far. But when she sets her sights on becoming a first-class international flight attendant, Donna throws caution to the wind and takes off in pursuit of her dream. The ride is anything but smooth, however, and Donna's laugh-packed journey of a lifetime is rocked by more turbulence than she bargained for.
tagline: Prepare for her arrival.
title: View from the Top
plot:
View from the Top is a 2003 romantic comedy-drama film that explores the complexities of female empowerment, self-discovery, and the challenges of navigating one's identity in a male-dominated industry. The movie follows the story of Christina "Christy" Marshall (played by Gwyneth Paltrow), a young woman who lands a job as a flight attendant on a major airline.

As Christy navigates her new role, she faces numerous obstacles and setbacks, including sexism, objectification, and personal struggles. However, through her experiences, she begins to discover her own strength, resilience, and determination. The film takes the audience on a journey of self-discovery, as Christy learns to assert herself, set boundaries, and find her place in the world.

One of the main themes of View from the Top is the struggle for female empowerment in a patriarchal society. The movie highlights the ways in which women are often objectified, marginalized, and excluded from positions of power. However, it also offers a message of hope and resilience, suggesting that with determination and hard work, women can overcome these obstacles and achieve their goals.

The film also explores themes of identity, self-discovery, and personal growth. Christy's journey is marked by moments of introspection, self-doubt, and transformation, as she grapples with her own desires, values, and sense of purpose. Through her experiences, the movie suggests that true fulfillment and happiness can only be achieved when one is true to oneself.

Overall, View from the Top is a thought-provoking and engaging film that offers a nuanced exploration of female empowerment, self-discovery, and personal growth.

original_title: LEGO Monkie Kid: A Hero Is Born
overview: Monkey King comes to life as a young boy named MK, obsessed with the legends of old, discovers Monkey King's magical staff. After witnessing Red Son and Princess Iron Fan release the Demon Bull King from his prison under the mountain, MK accidentally grabs Monkey King’s magical staff and escapes, sending him on a journey to return the staff to Monkey King in order for him to save the day.
tagline: Awaken the hero in you
title: LEGO Monkie Kid: A Hero Is Born
plot:
LEGO Monkie Kid: A Hero Is Born is an animated adventure film that delves into the world of ancient Chinese mythology and the legend of the Monkey King, Sun Wukong. At its core, the movie explores themes of identity, belonging, and self-discovery.

The story follows a young boy named Jade, who discovers he has the ability to transform into the legendary Monkey King, Sun Wukong. As Jade navigates his newfound powers and responsibilities, he must confront the challenges of being an outsider and finding his place in the world. The film's portrayal of Jade's journey is reminiscent of classic coming-of-age tales, where the protagonist struggles to reconcile their true nature with societal expectations.

The movie also touches on the theme of friendship and loyalty, as Jade forms strong bonds with a group of allies who help him master his powers and overcome formidable foes. Through these relationships, the film highlights the importance of embracing one's uniqueness and finding support in those who accept you for who you are.

Furthermore, LEGO Monkie Kid: A Hero Is Born incorporates elements of Chinese culture and mythology, weaving them into a narrative that is both entertaining and educational. The film's use of vibrant animation and imaginative storytelling brings ancient legends to life, making it an engaging experience for audiences of all ages.

Overall, the main themes of LEGO Monkie Kid: A Hero Is Born revolve around self-discovery, identity, friendship, and the power of embracing one's individuality.

overview: Three friends, whose lives have been drifting apart, reunite for the funeral of a fourth childhood friend. When looking through their childhood belongings, they discover a trunk which contained details on a quest their friend was attempting. It revealed that he was hot on the trail of the $200,000 that went missing with airplane hijacker D.B. Cooper in 1971. They decide to continue his journey, but do not understand the dangers they will soon encounter.
tagline: The call of the wild, the thrill of adventure. The mistake of a lifetime.
title: Without a Paddle
plot:
Without a Paddle is a 2004 American comedy film directed by Steven Paul. The movie follows three friends, played by Seth Green, Matthew Lillard, and Dax Shepard, who embark on a disastrous canoeing trip down the Mississippi River.

The main theme of Without a Paddle revolves around the idea of male friendship and the challenges that come with it. The film explores the complexities of male relationships, particularly those between friends who have grown up together. As the three friends navigate their way through the treacherous waters of the Mississippi, they are forced to confront their own personal demons and learn to rely on each other in order to survive.

Throughout the movie, the characters' personalities and quirks are put to the test as they face various obstacles, including wild animals, harsh weather conditions, and their own ineptitude. The film's humor is largely based on the absurdity of these situations and the characters' reactions to them.

Ultimately, Without a Paddle is a heartwarming comedy that celebrates the power of male friendship and the importance of learning to let go of one's ego in order to truly connect with others.

overview: After one of his class papers is stolen and turned into a movie, a young student and his best friend exact a hilarious, slapstick revenge on the Hollywood hot shot who has taken credit!
tagline: Two friends are about to cut one Hollywood big shot down to size.
title: Big Fat Liar
plot:
Big Fat Liar is a 2002 American comedy film that revolves around the story of Jason Shepherd, a teenager who discovers that his best friend, Kevin, has been impersonating him in order to get into trouble and gain attention. As Jason navigates this situation, he learns valuable lessons about friendship, loyalty, and being true to oneself.

The main theme of Big Fat Liar is the importance of authenticity and staying true to one's identity. Jason's journey is a metaphor for the challenges of adolescence, where teenagers often struggle to find their place in the world and define themselves. Through his experiences, Jason comes to realize that it's essential to be genuine and authentic, rather than trying to fit into someone else's mold.

The film also explores the theme of friendship and loyalty, highlighting the complexities and nuances of relationships between friends. Kevin's actions serve as a catalyst for Jason's growth, forcing him to confront the consequences of his own behavior and reevaluate his priorities.

Furthermore, Big Fat Liar touches on the idea of identity theft and the consequences of deception. The film uses humor and satire to comment on the absurdity of modern life, where people often present a false image to the world. Jason's situation serves as a commentary on the ease with which people can be manipulated and deceived, highlighting the importance of being mindful of one's actions and their impact on others.

Overall, Big Fat Liar is a lighthearted comedy that explores themes of identity, friendship, and authenticity in a way that is relatable to teenagers and adults alike.

overview: Freddy Lupin, heir to a proud family line of werewolves, is in for a shock when on his 14th birthday his first 'warfing' goes awry, turning him into a ferocious poodle.  The pack elders give Freddy until the next moonrise to prove he has the heart of a wolf, or risk being cast out forever.  With the help of an unlikely ally in a streetwise stray named Batty, Freddy must prove he's 100% Wolf.
tagline: Every pack needs a leader!
title: 100% Wolf
plot:
100% Wolf is a 2020 Australian animated adventure fantasy comedy film directed by Alexs Stadermann and produced by Alexia Gates-Foale and Barbara Stephen, adapted from Jayne Lyons' 2009 novel of the same name. It features the voices of Jai Courtney, Samara Weaving, Magda Szubanski, Rhys Darby, Ilai Swindells, Akmal Saleh, Rupert Degas and Jane Lynch. Produced by Flying Bark Productions, it tells the story of a boy from a family of werewolves whose first transformation turns him into a poodle instead of a wolf.

Freddy Lupin is the young heir to a pack of werewolves who secretly protect their town and have little love for dogs. One night, when he tries to follow his family on patrol using a magical moonstone, he loses the stone to an ice cream man named Foxwell Cripp, and his father Flashheart apparently dies after falling from a cliff while trying to save Cripp. Freddy's uncle Hotspur becomes the new pack leader. Six years later, Freddy undergoes his first transformation, and despite the encouragement of the family's loyal housekeeper Mrs. Mutton, he is humiliated when he turns into a poodle. Scorned by the pack, he is given until moonrise the next day to prove he is a true wolf or face banishment. Freddy sets out to recover the moonstone from Cripp, who has become obsessed with proving that werewolves exist, and befriends Batty, a mixed-breed stray known as "Houndini" for her talent for escaping dog catchers. They retrieve the stone but are caught and taken to the Coldfax Dog Pound, which is secretly run by Hotspur, where they meet a Scottish Terrier named Hamish, a Blue Heeler named Bruno and a Chihuahua named Twitchy. Hotspur takes the moonstone and leaves his nephew behind. Thrown into a pit with a dreaded creature known as the Beast, Freddy discovers that it is his long-lost father, imprisoned in wolf form by his jealous brother. With the help of his new canine friends and Mrs. Mutton, Freddy must free his father, escape the pound and stop Hotspur's sinister scheme to turn the town's dogs into wigs.

100% Wolf was released by Studio 100 Film on May 29, 2020. It received mixed reviews from critics, holding a 69% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes based on 16 reviews. A sequel, 200% Wolf, was released in August 2024.

overview: Grace is a religious woman who lives in an old house kept dark because her two children, Anne and Nicholas, have a rare sensitivity to light. When the family begins to suspect the house is haunted, Grace fights to protect her children at any cost in the face of strange events and disturbing visions.
tagline: Sooner or later they’ll find you.
title: The Others
plot:
The Others is a Gothic psychological horror film of 2001 written, directed and scored by Alejandro Amenábar, set on the island of Jersey in 1945. Nicole Kidman stars as Grace Stewart, a mother living in an isolated manor with her two children, with Fionnula Flanagan as the housekeeper Bertha Mills, Christopher Eccleston as Charles, Alakina Mann and James Bentley as the children Anne and Nicholas, Eric Sykes as the gardener Edmund Tuttle and Elaine Cassidy as the mute maid Lydia.

Grace lives in a remote house on Jersey, recently freed from German occupation. Because Anne and Nicholas suffer from an extreme sensitivity to light, she keeps the house in constant gloom behind heavy curtains. Grace hires three servants who arrive seeking work, learning that they served in the house years before. Anne insists that she has seen a boy called Victor, his parents and a blind old woman. Grace dismisses this as fantasy until she hears footsteps and voices herself and orders a search for intruders. In a storeroom she finds a nineteenth-century album of photographs of the dead, and Mrs Mills mentions that many people left the house during a tuberculosis outbreak in 1891.

Torn between her fears and her Catholic faith, Grace becomes convinced the house is haunted when a piano plays by itself, and sets out to fetch a priest, while Mrs Mills has Tuttle cover a set of gravestones with leaves. In the woods she instead finds Charles, whom she believed killed in the war and brings him home, but he soon departs again for the front, though she insists the war is over. Grace sees an old woman in Anne's communion dress speaking with her daughter's voice and attacks her, only to find she has struck Anne. When every curtain in the house vanishes, exposing the children to daylight, Grace throws out the servants, but the children discover their names on the hidden graves, and Grace finds a post-mortem photograph of the three, who all died in 1891. At a séance, Grace learns the truth: the blind woman is a medium contacted by Victor's living family, and Grace, in despair after Charles's death, smothered her children and then shot herself. She, the children and the servants are the ghosts. Victor's family moves out, the children enjoy sunlight for the first time, and Grace declares that the house is theirs and they will never leave.

The film grossed $210 million worldwide on a $17 million budget. It won eight Goya Awards, including Best Film, a first for a film with no Spanish dialogue.

original_title: Rogue One: A Star Wars Story
overview: A rogue band of resistance fighters unite for a mission to steal the Death Star plans and bring a new hope to the galaxy.
tagline: A Rebellion Built on Hope
title: Rogue One: A Star Wars Story
plot:
Rogue One: A Star Wars Story is a 2016 science fiction film directed by Gareth Edwards and written by Chris Weitz, Tony Gilroy, and John Knoll. The film is set just before the events of the original Star Wars film (Episode IV: A New Hope) and follows a group of rebels as they attempt to steal the plans for the Death Star.

The story begins with Jyn Erso (Felicity Jones), the daughter of Galen Erso (Mads Mikkelsen), a brilliant engineer who designed the Death Star. Jyn was raised by her mother, Shaak Ti (Deborah Ann Woll), a former Jedi, and her father's past is shrouded in mystery.

As Jyn grows older, she becomes increasingly disillusioned with her life on the planet Eadu, where she lives with her mother. She discovers that her father has been working for the Galactic Empire, designing the Death Star, and she begins to question his motives.

Jyn soon meets Cassian Andor (Diego Luna), a rebel spy who is tasked with infiltrating the Imperial facility on Scarif, where the Death Star plans are stored. The two form an alliance and embark on a perilous mission to steal the plans.

Along the way, they encounter K-2SO (Alan Tudyk), a reprogrammed Imperial droid who becomes their unlikely ally. They also meet Chirrut Îmwe (Donnie Yen), a blind Jedi monk who possesses a deep connection to the Force.

As the team navigates the treacherous landscape of Scarif, they face numerous challenges and obstacles, including Imperial stormtroopers, deadly traps, and treacherous terrain. Meanwhile, Jyn's personal demons come to the forefront as she grapples with her complicated past and her feelings towards her father.

The film builds towards a climactic showdown between the rebels and the Empire, culminating in a tense battle on Scarif. In the end, Jyn and her team successfully steal the Death Star plans, but not without great cost. The film concludes with Jyn's sacrifice, as she gives her life to ensure the plans are delivered to the Rebel Alliance.

Throughout the film, there are nods to classic Star Wars moments, including a memorable scene in which Jyn and Cassian escape from Imperial forces on a speeder bike. The film also explores themes of redemption, loyalty, and the power of sacrifice.

Overall, Rogue One: A Star Wars Story is a gripping and action-packed adventure that expands our understanding of the Star Wars universe. While it may not be as iconic as some of its predecessors, it offers a compelling narrative that sets the stage for the events of A New Hope.

overview: In 2257, a taxi driver is unintentionally given the task of saving a young girl who is part of the key that will ensure the survival of humanity.
tagline: There is no future without it.
title: The Fifth Element
plot:
The Fifth Element is a 1997 science fiction film directed by Luc Besson, produced by Gaumont and Columbia Pictures.

In the year 2258, the Earth is on the brink of destruction due to an ancient evil known as the Great Evil. To save humanity, the priest who created the world's first atomic bomb, Zorg (Gary Oldman), steals a powerful artifact called the "Eclipse" that can destroy the planet. The only way to stop him is for a chosen one, known as the Fifth Element, to be born.

The story begins with Korben Dallas (Bruce Willis), a taxi driver who lives in the sprawling metropolis of New York City. On his 18th birthday, Korben meets Leeloo (Milla Jovovich), a mysterious and beautiful woman who is revealed to be the Fifth Element. Unbeknownst to Korben, he has been chosen by fate to protect her.

As they embark on their journey together, they are pursued by Zorg's minions and the villainous Ruby Rhod (Chris Tucker), a TV personality who serves as a spokesperson for Zorg. The duo soon discovers that Leeloo is not just any ordinary woman but possesses unique abilities that make her the key to saving humanity.

Their quest takes them to the Moon, where they meet Father Vito Cornelius (Ian Holm), a priest who created the world's first atomic bomb and has been searching for the Fifth Element. He reveals that Leeloo is the chosen one and that Korben must protect her at all costs.

As they journey through space, Korben and Leeloo face numerous challenges, including Zorg's army of robots and Ruby Rhod's attempts to capture them. Along the way, Korben learns more about himself and his connection to Leeloo, who is revealed to be a being from another planet with the power to destroy or create.

The film's climax features an epic battle between Korben, Leeloo, and Zorg on the Moon. In the end, Korben sacrifices himself to save Leeloo, but not before she uses her powers to destroy the Eclipse and save humanity.

In a surprising twist, it is revealed that Korben was actually the reincarnation of Father Vito Cornelius, making him the chosen one all along. The film ends with Leeloo standing alone on the Moon, ready to face whatever challenges come her way.

The Fifth Element is a visually stunning film with a unique blend of science fiction and action elements. The movie's themes of fate, destiny, and self-discovery are woven throughout the narrative, making it a thought-provoking and entertaining ride for audiences.

overview: The adventures of a father and his young daughter, in their search for a long lost book that will help reunite a missing, close relative.
tagline: Every story ever written is just waiting to become real.
title: Inkheart
plot:
Inkheart is a 2008 fantasy adventure film directed by Iain Softley, based on the novel of the same name by Cornelia Funke.

The main themes of Inkheart include:

1. **The Power of Stories**: The movie explores the idea that stories have the power to shape our lives and transport us to other worlds. The protagonist, Meggie, discovers that her father, Mo, has the ability to bring characters from books into the real world through a magical process called "Inkheart".
2. **Identity and Self-Discovery**: As Meggie navigates this new reality, she must also confront her own identity and sense of self. She struggles to come to terms with her father's past and his connection to the world of stories.
3. **The Importance of Family**: The movie highlights the importance of family bonds and relationships. Mo's relationship with Meggie is central to the story, and he must make sacrifices to protect her from the dangers of the book world.
4. **Good vs. Evil**: The film features a classic battle between good and evil, as Mo and his allies try to outwit the villainous Capricorn, who seeks to exploit the power of stories for his own gain.

The story begins with Meggie's father, Mo (played by Brendan Fraser), being forced to return to the world of stories when he is kidnapped by Capricorn. In order to rescue him, Mo must use his ability to bring characters from books into the real world. However, this process has unintended consequences, and Meggie finds herself caught up in a world of fantasy and adventure.

As the story unfolds, Meggie discovers that she has inherited her father's ability and must learn to control it. Along the way, she meets a cast of characters from the book world, including Fenoglio (played by Robert De Niro), a writer who becomes her ally, and Basta (played by Paul Bettany), a ruthless villain.

Ultimately, Mo and his allies must work together to defeat Capricorn and restore balance to both the real world and the world of stories. The movie features stunning visuals, memorable characters, and a thrilling plot that explores the power of stories and the importance of family bonds.

overview: The Shadow Mountains, 1983. Red and Mandy lead a loving and peaceful existence; but when their pine-scented haven is savagely destroyed, Red is catapulted into a phantasmagoric journey filled with bloody vengeance and laced with fire.
title: Mandy
plot:
Mandy is a 2018 American psychological horror film written and directed by Panos Cosmatos. The film stars Nicolas Cage, Andrea Riseborough, and Linus Roache.

The story begins with Red Miller (Nicolas Cage), a lumberjack living in the Pacific Northwest with his girlfriend, Mandy Bloom (Andrea Riseborough). They are happy together, but their idyllic life is disrupted when Red's past comes back to haunt him. A former friend and fellow lumberjack, Jeremiah Sand (Linus Roache), arrives at their cabin, seeking refuge from a traumatic event in his own life.

Jeremiah's presence sets off a chain of events that ultimately leads to the downfall of Red and Mandy's relationship. It is revealed that Jeremiah was involved in a heinous crime with Red, which has left a deep scar on both men. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Jeremiah's true intentions are sinister, and he is seeking revenge against Red.

The film takes a dark and surreal turn as Jeremiah's actions escalate, leading to a series of gruesome and disturbing events. Mandy, who is initially oblivious to the danger lurking around her, begins to experience strange and terrifying visions. As the situation spirals out of control, Red becomes increasingly unhinged, descending into madness.

Throughout the film, Cosmatos employs a distinctive visual style, blending elements of folk horror, heavy metal music, and psychedelic art. The cinematography is striking, with vivid colors and unsettling imagery that adds to the overall sense of unease and dread.

As the plot reaches its climax, Red's world begins to disintegrate, and he is forced to confront his own demons. In a shocking and disturbing finale, Red's actions become increasingly erratic, leading to a confrontation with Jeremiah that will leave only one man standing.

Mandy is a film that defies easy interpretation, but at its core, it is a story about the destructive power of trauma and the devastating consequences of unchecked anger. The film's use of heavy metal music and its surreal, dreamlike atmosphere add to the sense of unease and tension, creating a viewing experience that is both captivating and unsettling.

Overall, Mandy is a bold and unflinching exploration of the human psyche, with a performance from Nicolas Cage that is both mesmerizing and terrifying. The film's unique blend of horror and drama makes it a must-see for fans of the genre, but be warned: Mandy is not for the faint of heart.

overview: A crew of rugged firefighters meet their match when attempting to rescue three rambunctious kids.
production_companies: Canadian Film or Video Production Tax Credit (CPTC)
tagline: 0% Contained
title: Playing with Fire
plot:
"Playing with Fire" is a 2019 American comedy film directed by Jon M. Chu and starring Ice Cube, Keegan-Michael Key, and Gabrielle Union.

The movie follows Joe Carman (Ice Cube), a firefighter who must care for three rambunctious foster children while his wife is away on business. As Joe navigates the challenges of parenting, he learns valuable lessons about responsibility, love, and acceptance.

Some of the main themes in "Playing with Fire" include:

1. **The importance of family**: The movie highlights the significance of having a supportive family unit, whether biological or foster-based. Joe's journey shows that family is not just about blood ties but also about creating a loving environment for those who need it.
2. **Embracing diversity and inclusivity**: The film celebrates the diversity of its characters, showcasing a blended family with children from different racial and ethnic backgrounds. This theme promotes acceptance, understanding, and empathy towards people from diverse backgrounds.
3. **Overcoming personal limitations**: Joe's character is initially portrayed as someone who struggles to connect with his own children due to his tough exterior. However, as he cares for the foster kids, he learns to open up and become a more patient and loving father figure. This theme encourages viewers to confront their own emotional vulnerabilities and limitations.
4. **The power of love and connection**: Throughout the movie, Joe forms strong bonds with the children in his care, teaching them valuable life lessons and showing them love and acceptance. The film demonstrates that love can conquer even the toughest challenges and help people grow as individuals.

Overall, "Playing with Fire" is a heartwarming comedy-drama that explores themes of family, diversity, personal growth, and the transformative power of love.

overview: After the death of her mother, Sara moves to the South Side of Chicago to live with her father and gets transferred to a majority-black school. Her life takes a turn for the better when befriends Chenille and her brother Derek, who helps her with her dancing skills.
tagline: The Only Person You Need To Be Is Yourself.
title: Save the Last Dance
plot:
Save the Last Dance is a 2001 American romantic drama film that explores the complexities of social class, identity, and the struggle for self-discovery. The movie delves into the world of two young women from different backgrounds who find themselves drawn to each other despite their vastly different lifestyles.

The film's narrative revolves around Sara Johnson, a white ballet dancer from a wealthy family in Chicago, who is forced to re-evaluate her life when her mother passes away. She finds solace in hip-hop dance and meets Derek Reynolds, a black teenager from the wrong side of the tracks, at a local club. As they spend more time together, Sara begins to confront the societal expectations placed upon her and the limitations imposed by her privileged upbringing.

Through their relationship, the film sheds light on the tensions between cultural identity and social status. The contrast between Sara's world of elegance and refinement and Derek's gritty reality serves as a backdrop for exploring themes of class struggle, racism, and the search for authenticity. As Sara becomes more immersed in Derek's world, she begins to question her own values and the privileges that have defined her life.

The movie also touches on the theme of self-discovery, as both characters navigate their identities and grapple with the expectations placed upon them by others. Through their relationship, they learn to let go of their preconceptions and find a sense of belonging in each other's worlds.

Ultimately, Save the Last Dance is a poignant exploration of the human experience, one that challenges its viewers to confront the complexities of social class, identity, and the power of love to transcend boundaries.

overview: With the aid of a fellow Auschwitz survivor and a hand-written letter, an elderly man with dementia goes in search of the person responsible for the death of his family.
tagline: Dark truths will come to light.
title: Remember
plot:
Remember is a 2015 Canadian-German drama thriller directed by Atom Egoyan and written by Benjamin August, a first-time screenwriter who wanted to create a lead role for an older actor. Producer Robert Lantos saw Egoyan as the ideal director, and Egoyan considered the project timely because the last Holocaust survivors and perpetrators were still alive and trials were under way in Germany. Shooting began in July 2014 in Sault Ste. Marie and northern Ontario.

In a New York nursing home, Zev Guttman, an 89-year-old Auschwitz survivor with dementia, keeps waking up looking for his wife, Ruth, who died two weeks earlier. His friend Max Rosenbaum, another survivor who is physically incapacitated, reminds him of his promise: to find and kill Otto Wallisch, the camp Blockführer who murdered both their families and is believed to have entered the United States under the name Rudy Kurlander. Four men by that name have been identified, and Zev and Max are the last people able to recognize him. Guided by Max's detailed letter and travel arrangements, Zev slips away, buys a pistol in Cleveland and sets off to visit each candidate in turn.

The first Kurlander turns out to have fought in North Africa, and the second, in Ontario, was himself imprisoned at Auschwitz as a gay man. In Idaho, Zev learns that the third has died; the man's son, a neo-Nazi state trooper, turns violent on discovering that Zev is Jewish, and Zev kills his dog and then him. After a fall in Reno, Zev reaches the fourth Kurlander's home near Lake Tahoe and recognizes his voice. Threatening the man's granddaughter, he demands the truth, and the old man reveals that he is Kunibert Sturm and that Zev himself is Otto Wallisch: both had been Blockführers and afterward tattooed each other with numbers to pass as Jewish survivors. Zev shoots Sturm, declares "I remember" and kills himself, and back in New York Max reveals that he recognized Zev as Wallisch on his arrival and that the two men had killed his family.

Christopher Plummer plays Zev and Martin Landau plays Max, with Bruno Ganz, Heinz Lieven and Jürgen Prochnow as Kurlanders, Dean Norris as the trooper and Henry Czerny as Zev's son. The film screened in competition at the Venice Film Festival and was released by A24 in the United States in March 2016. Critics were mostly positive, especially about Plummer's performance, with 69% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, and August won the Canadian Screen Award for Best Original Screenplay.

overview: When Duchess Margaret unexpectedly inherits the throne & hits a rough patch with Kevin, it’s up to Stacy to save the day before a new lookalike — party girl Fiona — foils their plans.
title: The Princess Switch: Switched Again
plot:
The Princess Switch: Switched Again is a 2020 American Christmas romantic comedy film directed by Mike Rohl and produced by Brad Krevoy, the second installment in The Princess Switch trilogy. Vanessa Hudgens plays three look-alike roles: Stacy, now Princess of Belgravia; Margaret Delacourt, who is about to become Queen of Montenaro; and Margaret's scheming cousin, Lady Fiona Pembroke. Sam Palladio plays Stacy's husband, Prince Edward, Nick Sagar plays Stacy's best friend Kevin, Suanne Braun plays Margaret's assistant Mrs. Donatelli, Mia Lloyd plays Kevin's daughter Olivia and Lachlan Nieboer plays Count Antonio Rossi.

Two years after the events of the first film, Margaret unexpectedly inherits the throne of Montenaro after the king's death and his son's abdication. Overwhelmed by her new responsibilities, she has ended her relationship with Kevin, who now runs his Chicago bakery with his daughter Olivia. Stopping in Chicago on her way to the Christmas coronation, Stacy finds Kevin miserable and persuades him to come to Montenaro, even as her own marriage to Edward is strained by her devotion to royal duty. Kevin and Margaret reunite while decorating the palace for Christmas, but she remains preoccupied with royal affairs, and her charming chief of staff, Count Antonio, courts her and plants doubts in Kevin's mind about whether a commoner could ever be worthy of a queen. Meanwhile Margaret's cousin Fiona, an immature and greedy aristocrat who has squandered her family's fortune, hatches a plan to impersonate Margaret, be crowned queen and loot the royal treasury, with the help of her servants Reggie and Mindy. To give Margaret and Kevin time together, Stacy and Margaret switch places once more, and while the couple spend an afternoon at a Christmas park, Fiona's accomplices kidnap Stacy, believing her to be Margaret, and Fiona takes her place at the palace. With three identical women now in play, Margaret and Edward race to rescue Stacy and unmask the impostor before the coronation, while Antonio pursues schemes of his own.

The film was released on Netflix on November 19, 2020, and received mixed reviews, holding a 56% rating on Rotten Tomatoes; Variety's Dennis Harvey wrote that what it was really selling was Yuletide. The trilogy concluded with The Princess Switch 3: Romancing the Star.

overview: Hong Kong, 1962: Chow Mo-Wan and Su Li-Zhen move into neighboring apartments on the same day. Their encounters are formal and polite—until a discovery about their spouses creates an intimate bond between them.
tagline: Feel the heat, keep the feeling burning, let the sensation explode.
title: In the Mood for Love
plot:
In the Mood for Love is a 2000 Hong Kong drama film directed by Wong Kar-wai, produced by Paradis Films, and released by Central Pictures. The movie stars Maggie Cheung and Tony Leung as the two main characters.

The story takes place in 1960s Hong Kong during the Sino-Japanese War. We are introduced to two neighbors, Mrs. Carman (Maggie Cheung) and Mr. Ewing (Tony Leung), who live in a high-rise apartment building. They lead seemingly ordinary lives, but their relationships with each other and those around them are complex.

Mrs. Carman is married to a wealthy businessman, Mr. Carman (Charles Ng), who is often away from home due to his work. She appears to be content with her life, but we sense that she may be unhappy in her marriage. On the other hand, Mr. Ewing is separated from his wife, Mrs. Ewing (Anita Yuen), and is struggling to cope with their divorce.

The story begins when Mrs. Carman and Mr. Ewing start an affair, which they keep hidden from their spouses. They begin a secret relationship, exchanging love letters and meeting in secret. As time passes, their feelings for each other deepen, but they struggle to reconcile their desires with the societal norms of the time.

Throughout the film, Wong Kar-wai masterfully weaves together themes of love, desire, and repression. The cinematography is stunning, capturing the vibrant colors and textures of 1960s Hong Kong. The score by Takao Taniguchi perfectly complements the mood of each scene, adding to the overall sense of longing and melancholy.

As the story unfolds, we see Mrs. Carman and Mr. Ewing's relationship become more intense, but also more complicated. They must navigate their feelings for each other while maintaining the illusion that they are still married to someone else. The tension builds as they struggle to keep their secret hidden from their spouses and the world around them.

The film's climax is both poignant and heartbreaking. Mrs. Carman and Mr. Ewing finally confess their love for each other, but it comes too late. They realize that their relationship has been doomed from the start, and that they must part ways. The ending is bittersweet, leaving the audience with a sense of sadness and longing.

In the Mood for Love is a beautifully crafted film that explores the complexities of human relationships and desire. Wong Kar-wai's direction is masterful, capturing the mood and atmosphere of 1960s Hong Kong with precision and sensitivity. The performances by Maggie Cheung and Tony Leung are outstanding, bringing depth and nuance to their characters.

Overall, In the Mood for Love is a timeless classic that will continue to captivate audiences with its poignant story and stunning visuals.

overview: 14-year-old Joe is the only child of Jeanette and Jerry — a housewife and a golf pro — in a small town in 1960s Montana. Nearby, an uncontrolled forest fire rages close to the Canadian border, and when Jerry loses his job (and his sense of purpose) he decides to join the cause of fighting the fire, leaving his wife and son to fend for themselves.
title: Wildlife
plot:
Wildlife is a 2018 American drama film directed by Paul Dano, based on the novel of the same name by Richard Ford.

The movie explores the complex and often tumultuous relationship between a father, Charlie (played by Jake Gyllenhaal), and his son, Jamie (played by Ed Harris in flashbacks, but played by Ashton Sanders as an adult). The story delves into themes of masculinity, identity, and the struggles of growing up.

As the narrative unfolds, it becomes clear that Charlie's own troubled past has a profound impact on his relationship with Jamie. The film masterfully weaves together the threads of their complicated bond, revealing the ways in which they both grapple with feelings of inadequacy, loneliness, and disconnection.

One of the primary themes of Wildlife is the exploration of toxic masculinity, as embodied by Charlie's character. His struggles to reconcile his own desires and expectations with those of his son serve as a catalyst for the story's emotional depth. The film raises important questions about the societal pressures that can shape men's identities and relationships, highlighting the need for vulnerability and empathy in order to truly connect with others.

The movie also touches on the theme of identity formation, particularly in the context of Jamie's coming-of-age journey. As he navigates adolescence, Jamie must confront his own desires, values, and sense of self, all while struggling to understand his father's complex and often contradictory nature.

Ultimately, Wildlife is a poignant exploration of the human condition, one that probes the intricacies of family relationships, masculinity, and the search for meaning in life. Through its nuanced portrayal of Charlie and Jamie's bond, the film offers a powerful and moving examination of the complexities of love, loss, and redemption.

overview: The chilling true story of a newly married FBI poster boy assigned to an Appalachian mountain town in Kentucky. There he is drawn into an illicit affair with an impoverished local woman who becomes his star informant. She sees in him her means of escape; instead, it's a ticket to disaster for both of them.
tagline: The devil always comes as everything you wanted
title: Above Suspicion
plot:
Above Suspicion is a 2019 American thriller film directed by Richard Shepard. The movie revolves around a complex web of deceit and corruption, where the lines between right and wrong are constantly blurred.

At its core, Above Suspicion explores the theme of toxic masculinity and the dangers of unchecked power and privilege. The protagonist, a charismatic and confident individual, is driven by his own ego and sense of entitlement, which ultimately leads him down a path of destruction and chaos.

The film also delves into the consequences of playing with fire when it comes to power and relationships. As the protagonist's actions become increasingly reckless and manipulative, those around him are drawn into his orbit, often against their will. This serves as a cautionary tale about the dangers of being seduced by power and the importance of accountability.

Furthermore, Above Suspicion touches on the theme of gaslighting and emotional manipulation, highlighting how these tactics can be used to control and exploit others. The film's portrayal of a complex and toxic dynamic between characters serves as a commentary on the ways in which power imbalances can lead to abuse and exploitation.

Overall, Above Suspicion is a gripping thriller that explores the darker aspects of human nature, revealing the devastating consequences of unchecked ambition and the importance of empathy and accountability.

overview: Animal pals Alex, Marty, Melman, and Gloria are still trying to make it back to New York's Central Park Zoo. They are forced to take a detour to Europe to find the penguins and chimps who broke the bank at a Monte Carlo casino. When French animal-control officer Capitaine Chantel DuBois picks up their scent, Alex and company are forced to hide out in a traveling circus.
tagline: They Have One Shot to Get Back Home.
title: Madagascar 3: Europe's Most Wanted
plot:
Madagascar 3: Europe's Most Wanted is a 2012 animated musical comedy film produced by DreamWorks Animation. The movie serves as the third installment in the Madagascar film series.

The story begins with Alex the lion (voiced by Ben Stiller), Marty the zebra (voiced by Chris Rock), Gloria the hippopotamus (voiced by Jada Pinkett Smith), and Melman the giraffe (voiced by David Schwimmer) living on a traveling circus, led by Stefano the lion tamer. However, their lives are turned upside down when they discover that the circus is in danger of being shut down due to financial difficulties.

The group decides to embark on a journey to Europe, where they hope to find a new home for the circus and save it from extinction. Along the way, they meet a new character, Vitaly (voiced by Sacha Baron Cohen), a Russian circus performer who becomes an ally to the group.

Upon arriving in Europe, the group discovers that Vitaly is being pursued by Interpol agents, led by Captain Chantel DuBois (voiced by Frances McDormand). The agents believe that Vitaly is wanted for his involvement in a jewel heist. However, it is revealed that Vitaly is actually innocent and has been framed.

As the group navigates through Europe, they face various challenges and obstacles, including being pursued by the Interpol agents and dealing with their own personal struggles. Meanwhile, Alex begins to question his identity as a lion and his role in the circus.

The movie takes a dramatic turn when the group discovers that Vitaly's real target is a valuable diamond necklace worth millions of dollars. The group decides to help Vitaly clear his name and find the real thief.

In the end, the group successfully outsmarts the Interpol agents and retrieves the stolen necklace. However, in the process, they also discover that the true mastermind behind the heist is none other than Stefano, who had been seeking revenge against the circus for abandoning him.

The movie concludes with the group returning to New York City, where they are welcomed back as heroes. Alex finally finds his place in the circus and comes to terms with his identity as a lion. The movie ends on a high note, with the group performing a musical number together, celebrating their newfound freedom and happiness.

Overall, Madagascar 3: Europe's Most Wanted is a heartwarming and entertaining film that explores themes of identity, friendship, and redemption. With its catchy musical numbers and lovable characters, it is sure to delight audiences of all ages.

overview: When a mysterious cyber-attack cripples civilization, a group of old college friends and lovers retreat to a remote country cabin, where they must cope with an uncertain future while navigating the minefield of their shared past.
title: Goodbye World
plot:
Goodbye World is a 2013 American apocalyptic comedy drama film directed, co-written and co-produced by Denis Henry Hennelly. The ensemble cast includes Kerry Bishé, Caroline Dhavernas, Adrian Grenier, Gaby Hoffmann, Ben McKenzie, Scott Mescudi and Mark Webber, with Mckenna Grace making her film debut. The story follows a group of old college friends who gather at an off-the-grid home in the woods north of San Francisco as society collapses around them.

The film opens with James reciting a quotation from Henry David Thoreau and explaining that, foreseeing society's collapse, he moved his free-spirited wife Lily and young daughter Hannah off the grid. A montage introduces his old college friends on the eve of the catastrophe: the radical activist Benji, who is sleeping with one of his students, Ariel; James's former business partner Nick and his wife Becky; Laura, a former senator's aide whose career was ruined by a public sex scandal; and Lev, a computer hacker on the verge of suicide. Simultaneously, they and countless others receive a mysterious text message reading "Goodbye World", and the nation's infrastructure begins to fail. The friends converge on James and Lily's home in Mendocino County as riots break out across the country. Laura admits that Homeland Security had contacted her about Lev, suspected of involvement in a computer virus, while in town bikers gouge locals for supplies. A televised presidential message reveals that the country is under martial law, and two National Guardsmen ask to use the house as a base, but James sends them away. Isolated together, the friends reopen old wounds: Becky clashes with the others over her libertarian beliefs, James and Nick feud over an old lawsuit, and Nick and Lily confront their feelings for each other. After Ariel is expelled, she tells the neighbors and the Guardsmen about James's stockpile of food and medicine, and the menacing guardsman Damon threatens violence unless the supplies are handed over. Lev confesses his role in creating the virus, and the friends must decide how far they will go to protect themselves and whether they can build a community in the ruins.

Goodbye World premiered at the Los Angeles Film Festival on June 15, 2013, and was released in a limited release and through video on demand by Samuel Goldwyn Films and Phase 4 Films on April 4, 2014. It received negative reviews, with 24% of 25 critics positive on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 36.

overview: An epic love story centered around an older man who reads aloud to a woman with Alzheimer's. From a faded notebook, the old man's words bring to life the story about a couple who is separated by World War II, and is then passionately reunited, seven years later, after they have taken different paths.
tagline: Behind every great love is a great story.
title: The Notebook
plot:
The Notebook is a classic romantic drama film directed by Nick Cassavetes, released in 2004 by New Line Cinema. The movie is based on the novel of the same name by Nicholas Sparks.

The story begins in the summer of 1946, when two young lovers, Noah Calhoun (played by Ryan Gosling) and Allie Hamilton (played by Rachel McAdams), meet at a social gathering in Seabrook, South Carolina. Noah, a poor but passionate young man, falls deeply in love with Allie, a beautiful and charming debutante, on their first encounter. Despite their different backgrounds, they share a deep connection, and their romance blossoms.

As the summer progresses, Noah and Allie spend more time together, and their feelings for each other grow stronger. However, their social differences and the disapproval of Allie's parents threaten to tear them apart. Allie's mother, Mrs. Hamilton (played by Gena Rowlands), is particularly opposed to Noah's humble background and wants her daughter to marry a wealthy man.

Despite these obstacles, Noah and Allie continue to see each other in secret, and their love for each other only deepens. However, when Allie's parents force her to leave Seabrook and return to her life in Charleston, she is torn between her love for Noah and the expectations of her family.

The movie then jumps forward in time, to 1946, where an older Noah (played by James Garner) reads their story to an older Allie (played by Gena Rowlands), who is suffering from Alzheimer's disease. As Noah reads their story, we see flashbacks of their young love and the sacrifices they made for each other.

The plot development is a beautiful portrayal of true love, which transcends time, social class, and even illness. The movie shows how Noah's unwavering devotion to Allie keeps her memory alive, even as she struggles with Alzheimer's disease.

In the end, the story concludes with an elderly Noah, who has spent his life waiting for Allie to remember him, finally finding peace in knowing that their love will endure forever. The Notebook is a timeless tale of love, loss, and the power of true devotion, which continues to captivate audiences to this day.

The movie received widespread critical acclaim, with many praising the performances of Gosling and McAdams, as well as the beautiful cinematography and the poignant script by Jeremy Leven. The Notebook has become a modern classic, widely regarded as one of the greatest romantic films of all time.

original_title: The Lion Guard: Return of the Roar
overview: Set in the African savannah, the film follows Kion as he assembles the members of the 'Lion Guard'. Throughout the film, the diverse team of young animals will learn how to utilize each of their unique abilities to solve problems and accomplish tasks to maintain balance within the Circle of Life, while also introducing viewers to the vast array of animals that populate the prodigious African landscape.
tagline: A new hero finds his roar!
title: The Lion Guard: Return of the Roar
plot:
The Lion Guard: Return of the Roar is a 2015 American animated television film produced by Disney Television Animation, with animation services from Mercury Filmworks, which serves as the pilot for the series The Lion Guard. Directed by Howy Parkins and written by Ford Riley, who developed the series, it continues the story of Disney's 1994 film The Lion King and is set during the time span of The Lion King II: Simba's Pride. It premiered on Disney Channel in the United States and Canada on 22 November 2015, ahead of the series launch in January 2016, and was released on DVD in February 2016.

The film centres on Kion (Max Charles), the fun-loving younger son of King Simba (Rob Lowe) and Queen Nala (Gabrielle Union), who is happy that his sister Kiara (Eden Riegel) is the one destined to rule. While chasing a ball into the forbidden Outlands with his friend Bunga, a fearless honey badger (Joshua Rush), Kion lets loose a tremendous roar that drives off the hyenas of Janja's clan. Simba and Rafiki reveal that this is the Roar of the Elders, a power once held by Simba's uncle Scar, who lost it by using it for evil and destroying his Lion Guard. As the second-born, Kion must now lead a new Guard of the fiercest, bravest, fastest, strongest and keenest of sight.

Kion chooses his friends: Bunga as the bravest, the cheetah Fuli (Diamond White) as the fastest, the hippo Beshte (Dusan Brown) as the strongest and the egret Ono (Atticus Shaffer) as the keenest of sight. Simba is dismayed that his son has not picked lions, insisting the Guard is no game. Doubting himself and fearing he might turn out like Scar, Kion receives advice from the spirit of his grandfather Mufasa (James Earl Jones), who tells him to trust his instincts. Meanwhile, alerted by the vulture Mzingo, Janja plots to strike before the new Guard can form, and the hyenas start a stampede in a gazelle herd. Kion defies his father, bestows the Mark of the Guard on his friends, and leads them into battle; together they rout the hyenas, Bunga saves Kiara from a stampede, and Kion's roar drives Janja back to the Outlands, after which Simba accepts the new Lion Guard.

Ernie Sabella voices Pumbaa, alongside Kevin Schon as Timon, Jeff Bennett as Zazu and Khary Payton as Rafiki, while Sarah Hyland and Madison Pettis voice Kiara's friends Tiifu and Zuri. The film introduces the motto "Zuka Zama" as the Guard's counterpart to "Hakuna Matata".

overview: Heidi, is an eight-year-old Swiss orphan who is given by her aunt to her mountain-dwelling grandfather. She is then stolen back by her aunt from her grandfather to live in the wealthy Sesemann household in Frankfurt, Germany as a companion to Klara, a sheltered, disabled girl in a wheelchair. Heidi is unhappy but makes the best of the situation, always longing for her grandfather.
title: Heidi
plot:
Heidi is a 2015 Swiss-German family adventure film directed by the Zurich-born filmmaker Alain Gsponer from a screenplay by Petra Biondina Volpe, adapted from Johanna Spyri's 1881 novel, one of the best-selling Swiss books of all time. Anuk Steffen plays the title role, with Bruno Ganz as her grandfather, the Alpöhi, Quirin Agrippi as the goatherd Peter, Isabelle Ottmann as Klara Sesemann, Katharina Schüttler as the governess Fräulein Rottenmeier, Hannelore Hoger as Klara's grandmother, Maxim Mehmet as her father, Anna Schinz as Aunt Dete, and Peter Lohmeyer and Jella Haase as the household's butler and maid.

After living for some years with her Aunt Dete, the orphaned Heidi is brought up into the Swiss Alps and left with her grandfather, a gruff recluse feared by the villagers below, who is far from pleased to have his solitude disturbed. The curious, cheerful girl soon wins him over, and she befriends Peter, a slightly older boy who herds goats, growing up happily in the mountains while longing to attend the village school.

Dete unexpectedly returns and tricks Heidi into leaving with her for Frankfurt, where she is to be a companion to Klara, the daughter of a wealthy family, who cannot walk and uses a wheelchair. With Klara's loving father often away on business, the household is run by the strict Fräulein Rottenmeier. Heidi struggles with reading and polite manners, but the two girls become close friends, and Klara's kindly grandmother encourages Heidi to learn to read. Heidi's homesickness grows until she begins sleepwalking at night, and the servants take her for a ghost. On the doctor's advice, she is sent home, leaving Klara hurt. Back in the Alps, her grandfather lets her go to school and takes a winter home in the village. When Klara later visits, a jealous Peter pushes her wheelchair off a cliff, but in the mountain air she gradually regains the use of her legs and surprises her father by walking, and Klara's grandmother gives Heidi a notebook to encourage her dream of becoming a writer.

Filmed mainly in the Grisons region of Switzerland, including Bergün and Rheinwald, the film opened in Germany on 10 December 2015 and became a major European hit, grossing nearly 39 million dollars worldwide. The Hollywood Reporter called it a familiar but crowd-pleasing adaptation, praising Ganz and its contrasts between city and country while noting that the plot drags in later reels, and the few reviews collected by Rotten Tomatoes were all positive.

overview: 2020: A year so [insert adjective of choice here], even the creators of Black Mirror couldn't make it up… but that doesn't mean they don't have a little something to add. This comedy event that tells the story of the dreadful year that was — and perhaps still is? The documentary-style special weaves together some of the world's most (fictitious) renowned voices with real-life archival footage.
tagline: "What a shit show!"
title: Death to 2020
plot:
Death to 2020 is a satirical mockumentary film that critiques modern society and politics. The movie takes a humorous approach to tackle various issues, including social media obsession, celebrity culture, and the superficiality of contemporary life.

The main theme of Death to 2020 revolves around the idea of how people have become increasingly obsessed with their online personas and social media presence. The film portrays a world where everyone is more concerned with presenting a perfect image on social media than with genuine human connections or meaningful relationships.

Another significant theme explored in the movie is the absurdity of celebrity culture and the way it has become an integral part of our lives. The film pokes fun at the notion that celebrities are somehow more interesting or relevant to our lives than actual people, highlighting the superficial nature of fame and its effects on society.

The movie also touches upon the theme of nostalgia and how we often romanticize past eras, particularly the 1980s and 1990s. The film's protagonist, a young woman named Sophie, is obsessed with the music and fashion of these decades, and her fixation serves as a commentary on the way we often idealize the past and struggle to adapt to the present.

Overall, Death to 2020 uses humor and satire to critique modern society and encourage viewers to think critically about their relationships with technology, celebrity culture, and each other.

overview: Three bad girls (a down-and-out stripper, a drug-running killer and a corporate powerbroker) arrive at a remote desert hideaway to extort and steal $200 million in diamonds from a ruthless underworld kingpin.
tagline: Prepare to get slapped...
title: Bitch Slap
plot:
Bitch Slap is a 2009 American action comedy film directed by Stephanie Allyn Graham and written by Graham and Brian Shaw. The movie follows two women, Amber (Kate Upton) and Vanessa (Ashlynn Yennie), who are both involved in the world of underground fighting.

The main themes of Bitch Slap include:

1. Female Empowerment: The film showcases strong female characters who are not afraid to take risks and fight for what they want. Amber and Vanessa are complex and multi-dimensional characters who defy traditional feminine norms.
2. Toxic Masculinity: The movie pokes fun at toxic masculinity, highlighting the absurdity of a world where men are expected to be tough and aggressive all the time. The film's portrayal of male characters is often humorous and satirical.
3. Empowerment through Violence: Bitch Slap explores the idea that violence can be a form of empowerment for women. Amber and Vanessa use their fighting skills to take control of their lives and assert their independence.
4. Subversion of Traditional Genres: The film blends action, comedy, and drama genres in a way that challenges traditional audience expectations. This subversion adds to the movie's irreverent and humorous tone.

Overall, Bitch Slap is a darkly comedic film that uses humor and satire to explore themes of female empowerment, toxic masculinity, and the complexities of human relationships.

overview: Two children, Ignacio and Enrique, know love, the movies and fear in a religious school at the beginning of the 1960s. Father Manolo, director of the school and its professor of literature, is witness to and part of these discoveries. The three are followed through the next few decades, their reunion marking life and death.
production_companies: Preparatory Action of the European Union
title: Bad Education
plot:
