Bad Education is a thought-provoking film that delves into the complexities of human nature, morality, and the blurred lines between good and evil. The movie tells the story of a charismatic and manipulative teacher who becomes embroiled in a web of deceit and corruption.

At its core, Bad Education explores the theme of toxic masculinity, where traditional masculine norms are subverted by the protagonist's unapologetic and calculating nature. This character's actions are driven by a desire for power, control, and validation, which ultimately leads to his downfall.

The film also examines the consequences of unchecked ambition and the dangers of idolizing charismatic leaders who prioritize their own interests over the well-being of others. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the protagonist's actions have devastating effects on those around him, including his students, colleagues, and even his own family.

Furthermore, Bad Education critiques the societal pressures that can lead individuals to compromise their values and morals in pursuit of success or recognition. The film suggests that this relentless pursuit of status and prestige can ultimately destroy one's sense of self and relationships with others.

Overall, Bad Education is a gripping drama that raises important questions about the nature of humanity, morality, and the consequences of our actions.

overview: Set in France during the mid-1970s, Vanessa, a former dancer, and her husband Roland, an American writer, travel the country together. They seem to be growing apart, but when they linger in one quiet, seaside town they begin to draw close to some of its more vibrant inhabitants, such as a local bar/café-keeper and a hotel owner.
tagline: When we die on the inside, the outside is left wandering dangerously by the sea.
title: By the Sea
plot:
By the Sea is a 2015 drama film directed by Angelina Jolie, which explores the complexities of marriage and relationships through the eyes of a couple struggling to reconnect with each other. The movie delves into the darker aspects of love, revealing the cracks that can form over time when two people are no longer on the same page.

The film's narrative is woven around the story of a couple, played by Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt, who embark on a journey of self-discovery and healing in a seaside town. As they navigate their troubled relationship, they must confront the emotional baggage that has been weighing them down for years.

Through the lens of this fictional tale, By the Sea sheds light on the fragility of human connections and the devastating consequences of unresolved conflicts. The movie masterfully captures the sense of desperation and longing that can arise when two people feel lost and disconnected from each other.

Ultimately, By the Sea is a poignant exploration of the human experience, one that probes the depths of love, loss, and redemption. It invites viewers to reflect on the complexities of relationships and the importance of communication in maintaining emotional intimacy.

overview: Aging wrestler Randy "The Ram" Robinson is long past his prime but still ready and rarin' to go on the pro-wrestling circuit. After a particularly brutal beating, however, Randy hangs up his tights, pursues a serious relationship with a long-in-the-tooth stripper, and tries to reconnect with his estranged daughter. But he can't resist the lure of the ring and readies himself for a comeback.
tagline: Love. Pain. Glory.
title: The Wrestler
plot:
The Wrestler is a 2008 American sports drama directed by Darren Aronofsky and written by Robert Siegel. Mickey Rourke stars as an aging professional wrestler who keeps fighting despite failing health and fading fame, driven by money troubles and a wish to relive his 1980s glory, with Marisa Tomei as a stripper he hopes to romance and Evan Rachel Wood as his estranged daughter.

Robin Ramzinski, known in the ring as Randy "The Ram" Robinson, was a wrestling star in the 1980s. Twenty years later he wrestles on weekends for small New Jersey promotions, lives in a trailer park and works part time at a supermarket under a manager who belittles him. A regular at a strip club, he befriends a dancer, Pam, who performs as Cassidy. After a local win he agrees to a 20th-anniversary rematch with his most famous opponent, the Ayatollah, hoping to regain stardom, and steps up his training and steroid use. After a brutal hardcore match he suffers a heart attack and has bypass surgery, and his doctor warns that his heart can no longer take wrestling. Randy reluctantly retires and takes a full-time job at the deli counter.

Encouraged by Cassidy, he seeks out his daughter, Stephanie, whom he abandoned as a child. She rejects him at first, but after he apologizes they reconnect on a boardwalk he used to take her to and plan dinner. Cassidy, a single mother, refuses his romantic advances, citing her rule against dating customers, and after a quarrel with her Randy goes on a night of drinking, drugs and sex, then sleeps through his dinner with Stephanie. When he shows up to apologize, she cuts him out of her life for good. Recognized by a customer at the deli, Randy cuts his hand on the slicer, quits in a rage and recommits to the rematch. Cassidy, who has left her job, begs him not to wrestle, but he tells her he belongs in the ring with the fans. During the match, as his chest pains worsen, the Ayatollah urges him to end it quickly, but Randy climbs the top rope, sees that Cassidy has gone, smiles at the crowd chanting his name and leaps into his signature "Ram Jam" as the screen fades to black.

The film premiered at the 65th Venice International Film Festival, where it won the Golden Lion,. It grossed $44.7 million on a $6 million budget and was universally acclaimed, with 99% on Rotten Tomatoes. The role revived Rourke's career, earning him a Golden Globe, a BAFTA and an Academy Award nomination, and Tomei was also nominated for an Oscar.

overview: Ten years ago, over forty people were brutally torn to pieces in Louisiana’s Honey Island Swamp. Over the past decade, lone survivor Andrew’s claims that local legend Victor Crowley was responsible for the horrific massacre have been met with great controversy. But when a twist of fate puts him back at the scene of the tragedy, Crowley is mistakenly resurrected and Andrew must face the bloodthirsty ghost from his past.
tagline: Return to his Swamp
title: Victor Crowley
plot:
Victor Crowley, also known as Hatchet IV, is a 2017 American supernatural slasher film written and directed by Adam Green, the sequel to Hatchet III and the fourth installment in the Hatchet series. Kane Hodder returns as the title killer, alongside Parry Shen, Laura Ortiz, Dave Sheridan, Katie Booth and Brian Quinn. Green had become reluctant to continue the franchise until George A. Romero persuaded him to make the film. He wrote the script under the title Arwen's Fancy Dinner, and the film was shot in secret over eleven days under the working title Arwen's Revenge, with a full day lost when a set collapsed.

Ten years after the Honey Island Swamp massacre, its survivor Andrew Yong is offered an interview for a true crime television series on the condition that it be filmed in the swamp itself. Haunted by his ordeal, Andrew refuses until his publicist Kathleen secures him a million-dollar fee. On the chartered flight, he discovers that the interview will be conducted by his ex-wife Sabrina and her crew. Meanwhile, in the swamp, aspiring filmmaker Chloe, her boyfriend Alex and her best friend Rose are shooting a trailer for a movie based on the Crowley massacre with the help of Dillon, an eccentric local tour guide and actor. While researching online, Rose looks up videos of people attempting to recite the voodoo curse that originally brought Crowley back to life. When the plane suffers an engine explosion and crashes into the swamp, killing several on board, Rose and Dillon go to help the survivors, finding one of the crew trapped in the partially submerged wreckage as the water rises. At that moment, Rose's phone automatically plays a video of the curse being read aloud, inadvertently resurrecting Victor Crowley. Crowley begins slaughtering everyone in his path, and the trapped survivors, including Andrew, must find a way to escape the wreckage and outlast Crowley before he claims them all.

Victor Crowley premiered by surprise in Los Angeles on August 22, 2017, at an event billed as a tenth-anniversary screening of the original Hatchet, and was then shown at one-night "Victor Crowley Road Show" events across the United States from October 5, 2017, before its home release in February 2018. Reviews were generally mixed, though it holds a 67% rating on Rotten Tomatoes.

overview: A young lion prince is cast out of his pride by his cruel uncle, who claims he killed his father. While the uncle rules with an iron paw, the prince grows up beyond the Savannah, living by a philosophy: No worries for the rest of your days. But when his past comes to haunt him, the young prince must decide his fate: Will he remain an outcast or face his demons and become what he needs to be?
tagline: Life's greatest adventure is finding your place in the Circle of Life.
title: The Lion King
plot:
The Lion King is a timeless classic that has captivated audiences for generations. Released in 1994, this animated masterpiece tells the story of Simba, a young lion cub who must assume his rightful place as king of the Pride Lands.

The film begins with the birth of Simba, son of King Mufasa and Queen Sarabi. Mufasa teaches Simba about the responsibilities of being a king and the circle of life, which connects all living things in the animal kingdom. However, Mufasa's brother Scar, who was next in line for the throne, grows jealous of his brother's position and plots to overthrow him.

Tragedy strikes when Scar's plan succeeds, and Mufasa is killed in a tragic accident. Simba, believing himself responsible for his father's death, runs away from the Pride Lands and abandons his royal heritage. With the help of new friends Timon and Pumbaa, a meerkat and warthog duo who teach him their carefree "Hakuna Matata" lifestyle, Simba grows up in exile.

Years pass, and Simba's childhood friend Nala, now a strong and determined lioness, finds Simba and informs him of the suffering of the Pride Lands under Scar's tyrannical rule. She convinces Simba to return home and reclaim his rightful place as king. With newfound courage and determination, Simba faces his destiny and confronts Scar in an epic battle.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Scar's actions were motivated by a deep-seated jealousy and resentment towards Mufasa. Through Simba's journey, we see the importance of facing one's fears, embracing responsibility, and honoring one's heritage.

The Lion King features stunning animation, memorable characters, and an unforgettable soundtrack, with iconic songs like "Circle of Life," "Hakuna Matata," and "Can You Feel the Love Tonight." The film's themes of identity, community, and redemption continue to resonate with audiences today.

Overall, The Lion King is a masterpiece of storytelling that has become an integral part of popular culture. Its timeless tale of self-discovery and leadership continues to inspire new generations of viewers.

overview: An American businessman with a stake in a pharmaceutical company that's about to go public finds his life is thrown into turmoil by an incident in Mexico.
tagline: An American corporation, the Mexican cartel, chances are this won't end well.
title: Gringo
plot:
Gringo is a 2018 American crime comedy film directed by Nicolas Winding Refn. The movie follows the story of Billy Bob Thornton's character, Jack, an American who gets caught up in a Mexican cartel's money laundering scheme.

The main theme of Gringo revolves around the destructive nature of greed and the consequences that come with it. The film portrays how Jack's desire for wealth and material possessions leads him down a path of chaos and destruction, not only for himself but also for those around him. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the true cost of Jack's actions is far greater than he ever could have imagined.

The movie also explores the theme of identity and how people can become lost in their own desires and ambitions. Jack's character, in particular, struggles with his sense of self-worth and purpose, which ultimately leads him to make decisions that put himself and others at risk.

Furthermore, Gringo touches on the issue of cultural differences and the complexities of navigating foreign cultures. The film's portrayal of the Mexican cartel's world is both fascinating and terrifying, highlighting the dangers of underestimating or misjudging other people's customs and values.

Overall, Gringo is a darkly comedic exploration of the human condition, delving into themes that are both thought-provoking and unsettling.

overview: 11-year-old Nicolas lives with his mother in a seaside housing estate. The only place that ever sees any activity is the hospital. It is there that all the boys from the village are forced to undergo strange medical trials that attempt to disrupt the phases of evolution.
title: Evolution
plot:
Evolution (French: Évolution) is a 2015 French science fiction horror thriller film directed and co-written by Lucile Hadžihalilović. Set in an isolated seaside village, it stars Max Brebant as Nicolas, a boy who begins to question the strange world around him, with Roxane Duran as Stella, a nurse, Julie-Marie Parmentier as Nicolas's mother, Mathieu Goldfeld as his friend Victor and Nissim Renard as Frank. The film was shown in the Vanguard section of the 2015 Toronto International Film Festival.

Nicolas, a sickly boy living by the sea with his mother, is swimming one day when he glimpses the body of a dead boy on the seabed with a red starfish at his waist. His mother dives down and retrieves the starfish but insists there is no body, yet that night Nicolas sees her bring the corpse back as the other mothers gather around it. After an angry outburst, he is taken to a hospital, where a doctor makes an incision above his stomach and he finds himself in a ward with other boys who have undergone the same procedure, while the nurses watch videos of caesarean sections. Back home, Nicolas grows suspicious, and sneaking out at night with Victor he witnesses the village women writhing together naked on the shore; later he notices what look like suckers on his mother's back. At the hospital an ultrasound reveals the heartbeat of a fetus inside him, to his mother's apparent joy. Victor dies during an operation in which a creature is removed from his body, though the boys are told he is recovering. Nicolas, who refuses to eat what his mother brings him and accuses her of not being his real mother, finds a confidante in Stella, a young nurse who gives him crayons and paper. His drawings of things never seen in the village, such as a car, a bicycle and a giraffe, suggest that he and the other boys may have been brought there from elsewhere. As Stella reveals her own secret to him, Nicolas faces a choice about whether he can ever escape the island.

Evolution received generally positive reviews from critics. It holds an 82% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus calls it creepy, provocative and aesthetically absorbing and a satisfying step forward for its director, and a Metacritic score of 77, indicating generally favorable reviews.

overview: During the 1980s, a failed stand-up comedian is driven insane and turns to a life of crime and chaos in Gotham City while becoming an infamous psychopathic crime figure.
tagline: Put on a happy face.
title: Joker
plot:
Joker is a psychological thriller film directed by Todd Phillips, released in 2019. The movie stars Joaquin Phoenix as Arthur Fleck, a struggling comedian and clown-for-hire who descends into madness.

The film begins with Arthur's childhood, where he is shown to be an outcast among his peers due to his physical disability and mental health issues. As the years pass, Arthur becomes increasingly isolated and disillusioned with society, feeling like an outsider in a world that seems to value superficiality over genuine human connection.

As an adult, Arthur works as a clown-for-hire at children's birthday parties, where he is met with ridicule and disdain by the very people he is trying to entertain. He also struggles to make ends meet, working multiple jobs while living in poverty. Despite his efforts, Arthur feels like he is invisible and ignored by society.

Arthur's life takes a turn for the worse when his mother passes away, leaving him feeling abandoned and alone. He begins to question the nature of reality and the world around him, becoming increasingly paranoid and detached from reality.

As Arthur's mental health deteriorates, he becomes obsessed with the idea that he is the only one who truly understands the suffering of others. He starts to see himself as a symbol of resistance against a society that has wronged him and others like him.

The film builds towards a tragic confrontation between Arthur and the wealthy elite, who are shown to be callous and indifferent to the struggles of those on the margins. In a shocking and disturbing climax, Arthur's transformation into the Joker is complete, and he unleashes his wrath upon the world.

Throughout the film, Joaquin Phoenix delivers a tour-de-force performance as Arthur Fleck/Joker, bringing depth and nuance to a character that could have easily been reduced to a cartoonish villain. The film's themes of isolation, loneliness, and the breakdown of social norms are timely and thought-provoking, making Joker a haunting and unforgettable cinematic experience.

Village Roadshow Pictures did not produce this movie, it was actually Warner Bros. Pictures

overview: Based on a true story of serial killer a model citizen, loving father and husband and serial killer John Wayne Gacy, a man with over 30 dead men and boys entombed in the crawl space underneath his house which he shared with his family.
tagline: Friend. Neighbor. Killer.
title: Gacy
plot:
Gacy, also known as The Crawl Space, is a 2003 American crime horror film written and directed by Clive Saunders, with David Birke as co-writer. Released direct to video, it dramatizes the crimes of John Wayne Gacy, the serial killer who raped, tortured and murdered at least thirty-three men and boys in the Chicago area during the 1970s. Mark Holton plays Gacy in his first leading role.

A prologue set in 1953 shows the young Gacy being belittled and kicked by his father, who tells him he will never be brave enough. In 1976 the adult Gacy has a family lunch interrupted by a neighbor complaining about a stench from his crawl space, and then by Steve, an employee who has gone unpaid for two weeks. Advised by a friend to use lime against the smell, Gacy continues to lead a double life. He abducts a man, confides his troubles to him in his garage and lets him go and invites a new hire to wrestle in his yard, and when Steve mocks him with a homophobic slur, Gacy is enraged. Steve and two other men beat and rob Gacy, and soon afterward Gacy's wife, Kara, sees him bring a handcuffed Steve into the garage at night, then finds clothes scattered there and catches Gacy emerging from the crawl space.

Gacy throws a Fourth of July costume party at which he is praised as an asset to the community and offers a job to a young man, Tom Kovak. He hires an exterminator for the maggots and cockroaches under the house and tells police that Steve left for Costa Rica or Puerto Rico. After Kara finds handcuffs and gay magazines in the garage, she leaves with their two daughters, leaving him with his mother. Tom, troubled at home, rents Gacy's spare room. Gacy chloroforms a male prostitute, holds him in chains overnight and leaves him in a park, pours concrete into the crawl space to mask the smell, and drowns a man in his bathtub after agreeing to buy his car. When a video about Gacy's business turns into pornography, Tom becomes terrified and tries to leave, but Gacy handcuffs him and begins strangling him. Tom escapes and goes to the police, who search the house, find dozens of watches and driver's licenses, arrest Gacy and exhume the bodies. The film closes with Gacy's defiant last words before his execution.

Critics were negative: the film holds 17% on Rotten Tomatoes from six reviews. LA Weekly called it unconvincing and unenlightening, faulting its dime-store psychology, and DVD Talk gave it half a star out of five.

overview: During the reign of King Zhou, an official enters his bedchamber, and is devoured by the monstrous tails of Daji, his concubine. Outside their city, several warriors within a metal wagon discuss their strategies to free the Invisible People and their Chief, when Jiang Ziya appears to them. He tells them that when King Zhou was younger, he let himself become possessed by the Black Dragon for his quest for power.
title: League of Gods
plot:
League of Gods is a 2016 Chinese fantasy film directed by Tsui Hark and produced by China Star Entertainment. The movie is based on ancient Chinese mythology, specifically the legend of the Eight Immortals.

The main theme of League of Gods revolves around the struggle between good and evil, as embodied by the two main characters: Zhuge Liang, a wise and powerful strategist, and Guan Yu, a chivalrous and loyal warrior. The film explores the complexities of human nature, highlighting the gray areas between right and wrong.

Throughout the story, the characters are forced to confront their own demons and make difficult choices that challenge their moral compass. The movie delves into themes of loyalty, honor, and the consequences of one's actions, raising questions about the true meaning of heroism and the nature of good and evil.

The film also touches on the idea of the cyclical nature of time, as the characters navigate a complex web of cause and effect that spans centuries. The movie's use of mythology and historical figures adds depth to the narrative, allowing for explorations of universal themes that transcend time and culture.

Ultimately, League of Gods is a thought-provoking film that invites viewers to ponder the complexities of human nature and the consequences of our choices.

overview: Tessa Young is a dedicated student, dutiful daughter and loyal girlfriend to her high school sweetheart. Entering her first semester of college, Tessa's guarded world opens up when she meets Hardin Scott, a mysterious and brooding rebel who makes her question all she thought she knew about herself -- and what she wants out of life.
tagline: After your first, life is never the same.
title: After
plot:
After is a 2019 American romantic drama directed by Jenny Gage, who wrote the screenplay with Susan McMartin, Tamara Chestna and Tom Betterton, adapted from Anna Todd's 2014 novel, which began as fan fiction posted on Wattpad. The first entry in the After film series, it stars Josephine Langford and Hero Fiennes Tiffin, with Selma Blair, Shane Paul McGhie, Dylan Arnold, Jennifer Beals and Peter Gallagher in supporting roles.

Tessa Young starts college, moving into her dorm with the help of her mother, Carol, and her boyfriend, Noah, and meets her roommate, Steph, and Steph's friend Hardin Scott. At a party with Steph's circle, a game of truth or dare reveals that Tessa is a virgin, and she refuses a dare to kiss Hardin and later rebuffs his advances. Her classmate Landon tells her that he and Hardin are about to become stepbrothers. Hardin asks Tessa to start over, takes her swimming at a lake and kisses her, but when she wants to tell Noah, Hardin says he does not date. After a bonfire party where Hardin fights with another student who kissed Tessa during a game, Landon asks her to check on Hardin, who has wrecked his house in a drunken rage. She comforts him and stays the night, and Noah, realizing where she has been, leaves heartbroken.

Tessa and Hardin begin dating despite her mother's threat to cut her off financially. Hardin finds them an apartment, and at his father's wedding reception he tells her that his father was a drunk and that his mother was assaulted by men his father had provoked. That night Tessa loses her virginity to him. Troubled by texts Hardin receives from Molly, Tessa follows him to a diner, where Molly shows her a video from the first party revealing that Hardin pursued her on a dare, planning to make her fall in love with him and then break her heart. Hardin insists his feelings changed, but Tessa leaves him, reconciles with her mother and Noah, cuts ties with Steph's group and interviews for an internship at Vance Publishing. At the end of the semester her lecturer gives her an essay in which Hardin confesses his love, and she goes to meet him at the lake.

The film premiered at The Grove in Los Angeles on April 8, 2019, and Aviron Pictures released it in the United States on April 12. Critics panned its screenplay and its glamorization of an abusive relationship, giving it 18% on Rotten Tomatoes, but it grossed $69.7 million worldwide on a $14 million budget, and After We Collided followed in 2020.

overview: Julia moves in with her fiancé, David, but his ex-wife and her own haunting past join forces to rock her quiet suburban existence.
tagline: When love ends, madness begins.
title: Unforgettable
plot:
Unforgettable is a psychological thriller film that revolves around the complex and intricate relationship between two women, Amy Dunne (played by Rosamund Pike) and Tessa Stowell (played by Carrie Preston). The movie delves into themes of obsession, revenge, and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy.

At its core, Unforgettable is a story about the destructive power of obsession. Amy's fixation on Tessa stems from a traumatic event in her past, which she believes Tessa was responsible for. As the narrative unfolds, it becomes clear that nothing is as it seems, and the truth behind the events is slowly revealed.

The film expertly explores the theme of revenge, highlighting the devastating consequences of allowing obsession to consume one's life. Amy's relentless pursuit of Tessa serves as a catalyst for her own downfall, while also raising questions about the morality of seeking revenge in such a manner.

One of the most striking aspects of Unforgettable is its portrayal of the fragility of human memory and perception. The film masterfully manipulates the audience's perceptions, making it difficult to distinguish between reality and fantasy. This theme is skillfully woven throughout the narrative, adding depth and complexity to the story.

Ultimately, Unforgettable is a thought-provoking thriller that delves into the darker aspects of human nature. It raises important questions about the consequences of allowing obsession to consume us and the devastating impact it can have on those around us.

overview: When her husband abruptly ends their marriage, empty nester Kate embarks on a solo second honeymoon in Africa, finding purpose and potential romance.
tagline: A romance off the beaten path
title: Holiday in the Wild
plot:
Holiday in the Wild is a 2019 romantic comedy film that follows the story of a woman named Sandy, who embarks on a disastrous African safari adventure with her friends. As she navigates through the challenges of the wilderness and confronts her own personal demons, Sandy discovers new things about herself and finds love in unexpected places.

The main theme of Holiday in the Wild is self-discovery and empowerment. Through Sandy's journey, the film explores the idea that one must take risks and step out of their comfort zone to truly find themselves and discover what they want from life. The movie also touches on themes of friendship, love, and finding one's purpose.

The film features a strong female lead character who is flawed but relatable, making her journey all the more endearing and inspiring. As Sandy navigates through the challenges of the wilderness, she learns to let go of her past mistakes and find forgiveness, both for herself and others. The movie ultimately ends on a hopeful note, suggesting that it's never too late to start anew and pursue one's dreams.

Overall, Holiday in the Wild is a heartwarming and entertaining film that explores themes of self-discovery, empowerment, and the power of human connection.

overview: Members of the Granite Mountain Hotshots battle deadly wildfires to save an Arizona town.
tagline: It’s not what stands in front of you, it’s who stands beside you
title: Only the Brave
plot:
Only the Brave is a 2017 American biographical drama film directed by Joseph Kosinski and written by Ken Nolan, Andrew Niccol, and Christopher McQuarrie. The film is based on the true story of the Granite Mountain Hotshots, an elite team of firefighters from Prescott, Arizona.

The movie begins with a flashback to 2008, where we see the formation of the Granite Mountain Hotshots, led by Brendan McDonough (Josh Brolin), a young and ambitious firefighter. The team is handpicked by their leader, Eric Marsh (Anders Holm), who has a vision for a elite firefighting unit that can tackle the most challenging blazes in Arizona.

As the story unfolds, we see the team come together, consisting of 20 firefighters from different backgrounds, all united by their passion for fighting fires. The team is trained to be self-sufficient and work together seamlessly, with each member having a specific role. They are equipped with state-of-the-art gear and a customized truck that becomes their mobile command center.

The film takes us through the team's rigorous training, where they learn to navigate treacherous terrain, build complex shelters, and develop strategies for tackling massive fires. We see the camaraderie and banter among the team members, as well as their personal struggles and relationships outside of work.

As the summer of 2013 approaches, the Granite Mountain Hotshots are deployed to fight a devastating wildfire in Yarnell Canyon, Arizona. The fire is intense and unpredictable, with flames reaching up to 100 feet high. The team is tasked with creating a firebreak to contain the blaze, but they soon realize that the fire is moving faster than expected.

The film's climax is one of the most intense and emotional scenes in recent memory. As the fire closes in on the team, they make a desperate last stand, using everything at their disposal to try and escape. The scene is both heart-wrenching and awe-inspiring, as we witness the bravery and sacrifice of the Granite Mountain Hotshots.

The movie ends with a somber tone, as we reflect on the tragic loss of life that occurred during the Yarnell Canyon fire. Brendan McDonough's voiceover provides context for the events leading up to the tragedy, while also highlighting the team's unwavering dedication to their craft and each other.

Throughout the film, the cinematography is breathtaking, capturing the vast expanse of Arizona's desert landscapes and the intensity of the wildfires. The performances by Josh Brolin, Miles Teller, and Jeff Bridges are outstanding, bringing depth and nuance to the characters.

Overall, Only the Brave is a powerful tribute to the bravery and sacrifice of the Granite Mountain Hotshots. The film is both an emotional rollercoaster and a testament to the human spirit's capacity for courage and resilience in the face of adversity.

overview: A self-destructive punk rocker struggles with sobriety while trying to recapture the creative inspiration that led her band to success.
title: Her Smell
plot:
Her Smell is a 2019 American drama film that delves into the complexities of toxic relationships and the destructive nature of unchecked emotions. The movie follows the story of Annie, a punk rock singer who struggles with addiction, mental health issues, and her tumultuous relationships.

At its core, Her Smell explores the theme of emotional intensity and how it can both fuel creativity and destroy lives. Annie's music is a manifestation of her inner turmoil, and as she navigates her personal struggles, her art becomes increasingly raw and provocative. However, this intensity also leads to a cycle of self-destruction, causing harm to those around her.

The film also touches on the theme of toxic masculinity, particularly in Annie's relationships with men. Her partners are often portrayed as emotionally unavailable or even abusive, which exacerbates her feelings of isolation and desperation. This dynamic highlights the ways in which societal expectations can perpetuate unhealthy relationships and stifle women's emotional expression.

Furthermore, Her Smell examines the tension between creative expression and personal responsibility. Annie's addiction and mental health issues are deeply intertwined with her artistic pursuits, raising questions about the costs of pursuing one's passion at any cost. The film suggests that while creativity can be a powerful outlet for emotions, it must also be balanced with self-awareness and accountability.

Ultimately, Her Smell is a nuanced exploration of the darker aspects of human emotion, revealing the devastating consequences of unchecked intensity and the importance of seeking help and support in times of need.

overview: The story of Alana Kane and Gary Valentine running around and falling in love in the San Fernando Valley, 1973.
title: Licorice Pizza
plot:
Licorice Pizza is a 2021 American coming-of-age comedy-drama film written and directed by Paul Thomas Anderson. The movie takes place in the early 1970s, specifically in the San Fernando Valley region of Los Angeles.

The story revolves around Gary Valentine (played by Cooper Hoffman), a charismatic but awkward teenager who runs his family's struggling pizza parlor, Gary's Pizza. Gary is a bit of an outsider among his peers and struggles to find his place in the world. He becomes infatuated with Alana Haines (played by Alana Haim), a beautiful and popular high school student who is also the daughter of a wealthy businessman.

As Gary navigates his relationships, he befriends Alana's brother, Mason (played by Sean Penn), a charismatic but troubled musician who becomes a mentor to Gary. Through Mason, Gary gains insight into the world of rock music and begins to develop his own sense of identity.

Meanwhile, Gary also catches the eye of Alana's mother, Susan (played by Maya Rudolph), who is struggling to balance her career ambitions with her family life. As Gary and Alana grow closer, they must navigate the complexities of their social differences and confront the challenges of growing up in a rapidly changing world.

Throughout the film, Anderson explores themes of identity, class, and the struggles of adolescence. The movie features a talented ensemble cast, including Benny Safdie as Gary's friend and confidant, and Tom Waits as Alana's father, who is struggling to come to terms with his own mortality.

The title "Licorice Pizza" refers to the iconic San Fernando Valley pizza parlor that serves as the backdrop for much of the film. The movie's use of period-specific music, fashion, and cultural references adds to its nostalgic charm and helps to transport viewers back to the early 1970s.

Ultimately, Licorice Pizza is a poignant and humorous exploration of the complexities of growing up in America during a time of great social change. Through Gary's journey, Anderson offers a nuanced and empathetic portrayal of adolescence, capturing the struggles, triumphs, and awkwardness that define this pivotal stage of life.

overview: A prestigious Stockholm museum's chief art curator finds himself in times of both professional and personal crisis as he attempts to set up a controversial new exhibit.
title: The Square
plot:
The Square is a thought-provoking drama that delves into the complexities of modern art, morality, and the human condition. At its core, the film explores the tension between authenticity and pretension, as embodied by the enigmatic curator Adrian (played by Claes Bang). As the story unfolds, we witness Adrian's carefully constructed world begin to unravel, revealing a web of deceit and hypocrisy that threatens to destroy his reputation and relationships.

Through Adrian's character, the film critiques the art world's obsession with superficiality and the commodification of creativity. The Square is a scathing commentary on the ways in which people will stop at nothing to maintain their status and power, even if it means sacrificing their integrity and authenticity. As the narrative progresses, we see Adrian's carefully crafted persona begin to crumble, exposing the emptiness and desperation that lies beneath.

The film also explores themes of identity, class, and privilege, highlighting the ways in which these factors can shape our perceptions and relationships. The character of Beatrice (played by Elisabeth Moss), a socialite with a seemingly perfect life, serves as a foil to Adrian's more troubled existence, forcing him to confront his own insecurities and biases.

Ultimately, The Square is a nuanced exploration of the human condition, one that challenges us to confront our own flaws and vulnerabilities. Through its thought-provoking narrative and complex characters, the film invites us to question our assumptions about art, morality, and the people who create and consume them.

original_title: 劇場版ポケットモンスター みんなの物語
overview: A young athlete whose running days might be behind her, a compulsive liar, a shy researcher, a bitter old woman, and a little girl with a big secret—the only thing they have in common is the annual Wind Festival in Fula City.  The festival celebrates the Legendary Pokémon Lugia, who brings the wind that powers this seaside city. When a series of threats endangers not just the festival, but all the people and Pokémon of Fula City, it’ll take more than just Satoshi and Pikachu to save the day! Can everyone put aside their differences and work together—or will it all end in destruction?
tagline: Our hopes. Our dreams. Our stories.
title: Pokémon the Movie: The Power of Us
plot:
Pokémon the Movie: The Power of Us is a 2018 Japanese animated science fantasy film produced by OLM, Inc., and directed by Masamitsu Hidaka. The movie is based on the popular Pokémon franchise created by Satoshi Tajiri.

The story begins with Ash Ketchum, a young trainer from Pallet Town, who has been traveling through various regions with his Pikachu to become a Pokémon Master. However, this time around, Ash's journey takes an unexpected turn when he receives an invitation from Professor Kukui, a renowned Pokémon researcher, to attend the prestigious Aether Foundation's annual gathering in Alola.

Upon arrival, Ash meets Lillie, a young and talented Pokémon researcher who is also attending the event. As they spend more time together, Ash and Lillie develop strong feelings for each other, but their budding romance is put to the test when they discover that the Aether Foundation's true intentions are far from pure.

The foundation, led by Professor Kukui, has been secretly experimenting on Pokémon using a device called the "Aether Crystal," which can harness and control the power of Pokémon. The goal is to use this technology to create an army of powerful Pokémon that will help humans gain dominance over the natural world.

Ash and Lillie soon realize that they must stop the Aether Foundation's sinister plans, but they are faced with a daunting task. The foundation has already begun to deploy its army of controlled Pokémon, and it seems like an insurmountable challenge.

As Ash and Lillie embark on their mission, they are joined by other familiar faces from the Pokémon world, including Pikachu, Greninja, and Mew. Together, they use their unique skills and bond with each other to take down the Aether Foundation's forces and put a stop to its nefarious plans.

Throughout the movie, Ash and Lillie's relationship is put to the test as they navigate their feelings for each other amidst the chaos of battle. In the end, they successfully defeat the Aether Foundation and destroy the device that was controlling the Pokémon.

The Power of Us concludes with a heartwarming moment between Ash and Lillie, who finally confess their love for each other. The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Ash and Lillie looking forward to a bright future together, surrounded by their friends and the Pokémon they have come to care about.

Overall, Pokémon the Movie: The Power of Us is an exciting adventure that explores themes of friendship, love, and the importance of protecting the natural world. With its engaging storyline, lovable characters, and stunning animation, this movie is a must-see for fans of the Pokémon franchise.

overview: Troubled teen Will Hawkins has a run-in with the law that puts him at an important crossroad: go to juvenile detention or attend a Christian summer camp. At first a fish-out-of-water, Will opens his heart, discovers love with a camp regular, and sense of belonging in the last place he expected to find it.
title: A Week Away
plot:
A Week Away is a 2021 American musical drama film directed by Marc Webb and written by Marc Silverstein, Sean Anders, John Whittington, and Dan Fogelman. The movie stars Daniel Radcliffe, Abigail Breslin, and Jeremy Allen White.

The main themes of A Week Away revolve around the story of Luke (played by Daniel Radcliffe), a young musician who embarks on a journey to find his estranged father's ashes in Ireland. Along the way, he meets a free-spirited woman named Leanne (played by Abigail Breslin) and her friends, who challenge his views on life and love.

Throughout the film, several themes emerge:

1. **Self-discovery**: Luke's journey is also one of self-discovery as he navigates his past, present, and future. He learns to let go of his emotional baggage and find a new sense of purpose.
2. **Love and relationships**: The movie explores the complexities of love, friendship, and family relationships. Leanne and Luke's connection serves as a catalyst for personal growth and healing.
3. **Healing and forgiveness**: As Luke confronts his past and the circumstances surrounding his father's death, he begins to heal and find closure. Forgiveness is also a key theme, as Luke learns to forgive himself and others.
4. **Music and creativity**: Music plays a significant role in the film, serving as a means of expression, comfort, and connection. The movie highlights the therapeutic benefits of music and the importance of pursuing one's passions.

Overall, A Week Away is a heartwarming story about finding oneself, healing from past wounds, and embracing love and relationships.

overview: November 1944. On the flooded isle of Walcheren, Zeeland, thousands of Allied soldiers are battling the German army. Three young lives become inextricably connected. A Dutch boy fighting for the Germans, an English glider pilot and a girl from Zeeland connected to the resistance against her will, are forced to make crucial choices that impact both their own freedom and the freedom of others.

overview: An ambitious reporter probes the reasons behind the sudden split of a 1950s comedy team.
tagline: Your best friend could be your worst enemy.
title: Where the Truth Lies
plot:
Where the Truth Lies is a 2005 American comedy-drama film directed by Ken Kwapis. The movie follows the story of Cliff Spink (played by Matt Dillon), a charismatic and confident radio DJ who recounts his past experiences to a young journalist, Alex Hitchens (played by Kevin Costner).

The main theme of Where the Truth Lies is the power of storytelling and the blurred lines between reality and fiction. Cliff's tales are so captivating that they become an integral part of his identity, and he struggles to distinguish between what actually happened and what he has created over time.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Cliff's stories are not just mere fabrications but also a way for him to cope with the pain of his past. His experiences have left emotional scars, and through his storytelling, he attempts to make sense of them and find redemption.

The film explores the idea that our perceptions of ourselves and others can be influenced by the stories we tell and the ones we hear. It highlights the complexities of human relationships and the ways in which our narratives shape our understanding of ourselves and the world around us.

Ultimately, Where the Truth Lies is a poignant exploration of the human condition, delving into themes of identity, vulnerability, and the search for truth amidst the complexities of life.

overview: Lilo, Stitch, Jumba, and Pleakley have finally caught all of Jumba's genetic experiments and found the one true place where each of them belongs. Stitch, Jumba and Pleakley are offered positions in the Galactic Alliance, turning them down so they can stay on Earth with Lilo, but Lilo realizes her alien friends have places where they belong – and it's finally time to say "aloha".
tagline: Here comes trouble!
title: Leroy & Stitch
plot:
Leroy & Stitch is a 2006 animated science fiction comedy film produced by Walt Disney Television Animation. The movie revolves around the story of Leroy, an alien who crash-lands on Earth and meets Stitch, a genetically engineered experiment designed to destroy everything in his path.

The main themes of Leroy & Stitch can be broken down into several key elements:

1. **Family and Belonging**: Throughout the film, Leroy struggles to find his place in the world and form meaningful connections with others. He eventually finds acceptance and love from Nani, a young girl who takes him under her wing, and becomes part of her ohana (family). This theme highlights the importance of finding one's family and belonging.

2. **Redemption and Personal Growth**: Stitch, initially designed to cause chaos and destruction, undergoes significant character development as he learns about the value of friendship, loyalty, and compassion. His transformation serves as a metaphor for personal growth and redemption, demonstrating that individuals can change and become better versions of themselves.

3. **The Power of Love and Acceptance**: The film showcases the transformative power of love and acceptance. Nani's unwavering kindness and dedication to Leroy help him overcome his initial fears and insecurities, while Stitch's own experiences with love and acceptance lead to a profound shift in his behavior.

4. **Cultural Exchange and Understanding**: The movie celebrates the diversity of cultures and traditions, as seen through the characters' interactions and experiences. The film promotes cross-cultural understanding and appreciation, highlighting the importance of embracing differences and finding common ground.

5. **The Importance of Home and Belonging**: Leroy's journey is also a metaphor for finding one's home and sense of belonging. As he navigates his new surroundings, he comes to realize that home is not just a physical place but also a sense of connection and community.

Overall, Leroy & Stitch explores themes of family, redemption, love, acceptance, cultural exchange, and the importance of finding one's place in the world, making it a heartwarming and engaging animated film.

overview: Jimmy is a young man who was born without an immune system and has lived his life within a plastic bubble in his bedroom... who pines for the sweet caresses of girl-next-door Chloe. But when Chloe decides to marry her high school boyfriend, Jimmy – bubble suit and all – treks cross-country to stop her.
tagline: Life is an adventure. Don't blow it.
title: Bubble Boy
plot:
Bubble Boy is a 2001 American comedy film directed by Blair Treu. The movie follows the story of Jimmy Livingston (played by Jake Gyllenhaal), a young man who has been living in a plastic bubble since birth due to a rare immune disorder that makes him extremely susceptible to infection.

The main theme of Bubble Boy revolves around the struggle for independence and self-discovery. Jimmy's life is confined within his protective bubble, which serves as both a physical barrier and an emotional shield. As he navigates the world outside, he must confront the harsh realities of adulthood, including relationships, careers, and mortality.

Throughout the film, Jimmy's character undergoes significant development as he learns to let go of his dependence on his mother (played by Swoosie Kurtz) and take control of his life. The movie explores themes of identity, vulnerability, and the human need for connection and intimacy.

The film also touches on the idea of societal expectations and the pressure to conform to certain norms. Jimmy's unusual circumstances make him an outcast, and he must navigate a world that doesn't always understand or accept him. This theme is reflected in his relationships with others, particularly his love interest, Penny (played by Marley Shelton), who challenges his perceptions of himself and the world around him.

Ultimately, Bubble Boy is a heartwarming and humorous exploration of what it means to be human, with all its imperfections and vulnerabilities. The movie offers a poignant commentary on the importance of embracing our uniqueness and finding our place in the world.

overview: When a college student starts having a reoccurring nightmare, she begins to believe that it's a suppressed memory. Her search to find the answers forces her to confront her past traumas, while at the same time, helps her unlock a mystery that may bring a killer to justice.
tagline: Sometimes you have to risk everything to finally be free
title: Wildflower
plot:

The movie follows the story of Ali, a young woman who is struggling to survive on the streets. She meets a man named Joe, who becomes her love interest and helps her find stability in her life. However, their relationship is complicated by the fact that Joe has a wife and children.

overview: Years after the Racoon City catastrophe, survivors travel across the Nevada desert, hoping to make it to Alaska. Alice joins the caravan and their fight against hordes of zombies and the evil Umbrella Corp.
tagline: The Extinction Is Coming...
title: Resident Evil: Extinction
plot:
Resident Evil: Extinction is an action-horror film that delves into several thought-provoking themes. The movie primarily revolves around the struggle for survival in a post-apocalyptic world overrun by zombies and other monstrous creatures.

At its core, Resident Evil: Extinction explores the human condition, particularly the resilience and determination of its protagonist, Alice (played by Milla Jovovich). As she navigates this treacherous landscape, Alice must confront her own identity and purpose in a world that seems to have lost all sense of humanity. The film raises questions about what it means to be alive and how far one would go to survive in the face of unimaginable horrors.

The movie also touches on themes of loneliness and isolation. Alice's journey is marked by encounters with other survivors, but these interactions are often fleeting and fraught with danger. This highlights the difficulties of forming connections in a world that seems determined to destroy any sense of community or belonging.

Furthermore, Resident Evil: Extinction critiques the notion of a "utopia" or a perfect society. The film depicts a world where humanity has been reduced to mere survival mode, highlighting the darker aspects of human nature when faced with catastrophic circumstances. This serves as a commentary on our own world's propensity for violence and destruction in the face of adversity.

Ultimately, Resident Evil: Extinction presents a bleak yet thought-provoking vision of a world gone mad, where the lines between good and evil are constantly blurred. Through Alice's story, the film invites viewers to reflect on their own values and priorities in the face of unimaginable horrors.

overview: A group of Iraq War veterans goes on the run from U.S. military forces while they try to clear their names after being framed for a crime they didn't commit. Along the way, Col. Hannibal Smith, Capt. H.M. ‘Howling Mad’ Murdock , Sgt. Bosco ‘B.A.’ Baracus, and Lt. Templeton ‘Faceman’ Peck help out various people they encounter.
tagline: There Is No Plan B
title: The A-Team
plot:
The A-Team is a 2010 American action comedy based on the 1980s television series created by Frank Lupo and Stephen J. Cannell. Joe Carnahan directed and co-wrote it with Brian Bloom and Skip Woods, and Cannell and Tony Scott produced, with Ridley Scott as executive producer. In development since the mid-1990s, the project went through several writers and pauses before the cast assembled in 2009 and filming took place in Canada, including Vancouver. 20th Century Fox released it on June 11, 2010.

In Mexico, Army Ranger John "Hannibal" Smith escapes from corrupt police working for the renegade general Javier Tuco, rescues Templeton "Face" Peck with help from B.A. Baracus, and recruits the eccentric pilot H.M. "Howling Mad" Murdock from an Army hospital to fly them away in a medical helicopter. Eight years later in Iraq, a CIA operative named Lynch hands the team a black operation to recover U.S. Treasury printing plates and a large amount of cash leaving Baghdad. They succeed, but the cash and their commander, General Morrison, are apparently blown up by Brock Pike's private security firm Black Forest. With no proof the mission was authorized, the four are court-martialed and sent to separate prisons, and Face's former girlfriend Charissa Sosa, a Defense Criminal Investigative Service officer, is demoted.

Six months later Hannibal accepts Lynch's offer of reinstatement in return for the plates, breaks his men out of prison, and escapes a drone attack by flying a tank under parachutes out of a doomed cargo plane. They discover that Morrison faked his death and stole the plates with Pike and Lynch, who then double-crossed him. After an elaborate showdown on a container ship in the Port of Los Angeles, the pacifist B.A. kills Pike, and Lynch is tricked into confessing and arrested by Sosa. The team is taken into custody for escaping prison, but Sosa slips Face a handcuff key with a kiss, and they survive as soldiers of fortune.

Liam Neeson plays Hannibal, Bradley Cooper plays Face, Quinton Jackson plays B.A., Sharlto Copley plays Murdock and Jessica Biel plays Sosa, with Patrick Wilson. Original stars Dirk Benedict and Dwight Schultz make cameos. Reviews were mixed, praising the cast and action but faulting the script, with 48% approval on Rotten Tomatoes. Grossing $177 million on a $110 million budget, it underperformed, and plans for a sequel were dropped.

overview: The innocent Célène might be falling in love with popular surfer Tristan at her new school. But she has no idea that, in actuality, she’s the object of a cruel bet between Tristan and Instagram influencer Vanessa.
title: Dangerous Liaisons
plot:
Dangerous Liaisons (French: Les Liaisons dangereuses) is a 2022 French teen romantic drama directed by Rachel Suissa for Netflix, a modern adaptation of Pierre Choderlos de Laclos's 18th-century epistolary novel in which the letters of the original are replaced by Instagram posts and stories. Produced by Autopilot Entertainment, it stars Paola Locatelli as Célène and Simon Rérolle as Tristan, with Ella Pellegrini as Vanessa, Héloïse Janjaud as Célène's cousin Charlotte, Jin Xuan Mao as Tao and Alexis Michalik. The film runs 109 minutes.

The story opens on a dramatic night when both Tristan and Célène appear close to despair, with Tristan narrating that fame is power in the modern age, before flashing back to show how they got there. In Biarritz, Célène, a shy and studious seventeen-year-old who prefers literature to social media and is in a long-distance relationship, is starting at a new school, Victor Hugo High. There she meets Tristan, a champion surfer with 3.5 million Instagram followers, after he saves her dog from being run over by a driver livestreaming at the wheel. Tristan and Vanessa, the pampered child star of a film series who is afraid of becoming a has-been, present themselves online as a couple, but their relationship is a sham; the two cynics actually enjoy scheming to destroy other people's romances. Unaware that she is the object of a cruel bet between them, Célène falls for Tristan as he sets out to seduce her, manipulating those around her, including her friend Tao, a DJ and dealer, and her goofy cousin Charlotte. Preparations for the school musical, a costume party with spiked punch and a surfing lesson that ends in a romantic beach hut push the scheme forward, while Célène, who joins Instagram under a provocative handle, gradually discovers the power and cruelty of online fame.

Released on Netflix on 8 July 2022, the film drew mostly negative reviews. Decider's John Serba advised viewers to skip it, calling it a toothless social-media remake that pales beside the 1988 Stephen Frears film and Cruel Intentions, with a soft Tristan, an underwritten heroine and a drawn-out ending, though he praised Janjaud's spirited comic performance and the idea behind Vanessa's character. The New York Times and Firstpost likewise found its social-media update colorful but shallow and clichéd.

overview: Yuta Okkotsu is a nervous high school student who is suffering from a serious problem—his childhood friend Rika has turned into a curse and won't leave him alone. Since Rika is no ordinary curse, his plight is noticed by Satoru Gojo, a teacher at Jujutsu High, a school where fledgling exorcists learn how to combat curses. Gojo convinces Yuta to enroll, but can he learn enough in time to confront the curse that haunts him?
tagline: Fight what's within.
title: Jujutsu Kaisen 0
plot:
Jujutsu Kaisen 0 is a Japanese animated dark fantasy film of 2021, adapted from Gege Akutami's 2017 manga of the same name, a prologue to the Jujutsu Kaisen series. Directed by Sunghoo Park from a screenplay by Hiroshi Seko, it features the voices of Megumi Ogata as Yuta Okkotsu, Kana Hanazawa as Rika Orimoto, Mikako Komatsu as Maki Zen'in, Kōki Uchiyama as Toge Inumaki, Tomokazu Seki as Panda, Yuichi Nakamura as Satoru Gojo and Takahiro Sakurai as the antagonist Suguru Geto.

Yuta is a bullied high school student who is haunted by a Cursed Spirit; when it brutally kills his tormentors, the leaders of the jujutsu world want him executed as too dangerous. Satoru Gojo, a teacher at Tokyo Jujutsu High, saves him by enrolling him at the school in November 2016. Yuta explains that the spirit is Rika, his childhood friend, whom he promised to marry when they grew up. After she died in a freak accident, she became a fiercely protective curse that attacks anyone who threatens him. At the school he meets his classmates Maki, Toge and Panda and on his first mission with Maki he deliberately summons Rika for the first time to save them both.

During a mission with Toge, the two are attacked by a powerful curse sent by Suguru Geto, a former student and old friend of Gojo, who abandoned the school after killing more than a hundred innocent people. Geto tries to recruit Yuta in order to use Rika, but Yuta refuses when Geto insults his friends. Geto then declares war, announcing that he will unleash a thousand curses on the city to wipe out ordinary humans, whom he considers inferior to sorcerers. His real goal, however, is to distract Gojo while he kills Yuta and seizes Rika for his own collection of spirits. Gojo sends Toge and Panda back to protect Yuta, but Geto overpowers them all. Enraged at seeing his friends hurt, Yuta offers himself to Rika to unleash her full strength, and Geto is gravely wounded. Gojo finds his old friend and finishes him. Gojo then tells Yuta that it was Yuta who cursed Rika by refusing to accept her death, rather than the other way around. Released from the curse, Rika passes on peacefully as Yuta continues his training. In a post-credits scene, Yuta shares a meal in Kenya with Miguel, one of Geto's former allies, and Gojo joins them.

Released by Toho in December 2021, the film earned 13.75 billion yen in Japan, making it the highest-grossing film of 2021 there. Critics were enthusiastic, giving it 98% on Rotten Tomatoes.

overview: Uday Gupta, a medical college student wanted to specialise in Orthopaedic, but is stuck in an all-female class of Gynaecology. Will he change his department, or will the department change him?
tagline: Inki toh lag gayi ji
title: Doctor G
plot:
Doctor G is an Indian Hindi-language medical comedy-drama of 2022, the feature directing debut of Anubhuti Kashyap, produced by Vineet Jain for Junglee Pictures. Ayushmann Khurrana stars as Uday Gupta, a reluctant male trainee in gynaecology, with Rakul Preet Singh as his senior Dr Fatima Siddiqui, Shefali Shah as the strict head of department Dr Nandini Shrivastava, Sheeba Chaddha as his mother Shobha, Indraneil Sengupta as his cousin Dr Ashok Gupta and Ayesha Kaduskar as the schoolgirl Kavya.

Uday, freshly qualified in Bhopal, dreams of specialising in orthopaedics like his distant cousin Ashok, but his entrance rank is too low to do so in his city. Unwilling to leave his widowed mother, an aspiring social media chef, he settles for gynaecology at the Bhopal Institute of Medical Sciences, planning to retake the exam the next year. He starts badly: Nandini scolds him for joining ten days late, his all-female colleagues tease him, and he insists that patients will never trust a male gynaecologist, prompting Nandini to tell him to lose his male touch. Gradually he befriends his colleagues, especially Fatima, and falls for her, but after a kiss she reminds him she is about to marry her fiancé, Aarif.

When Uday examines a woman without a female attendant during a staff shortage, he faces a disciplinary complaint, but while under inquiry he delivers his first baby in a sudden labour, and the grateful family names the child after him. His colleagues' testimony clears him, though Nandini remains unconvinced. Meanwhile Ashok, a married doctor with two children, has made Kavya, the teenager he tutors, pregnant, and asks Uday to take her for an abortion. A dangerous placental condition makes the procedure risky, and Nandini insists the family be told. Kavya stays at Uday's home, and her view of Ashok makes Uday ashamed of how he once vented at his former girlfriend. Uday also clashes with his mother over her Tinder date before they reconcile. When Kavya is left in agony after an injection at a private clinic, Uday and Shobha rush her to hospital, where Nandini saves her life, and Ashok is arrested for statutory rape. Seeing how much Uday has changed, Nandini spares him punishment for lying about Kavya's age, and he hurries to Fatima's engagement to pledge lasting friendship.

Shot mainly in Bhopal and released in October 2022, the film drew generally positive reviews for its performances and its mix of humour and social message.

overview: Rachel is a girl, adopted by an upper middle class family, who rebelled at 17 and left her family and studies at a traditional college in Sao Paulo to become a call girl. Shortly after starting work, she decided to write a blog about her experiences. Since some clients thought she looked like a surfer she adopted the name "Surfistinha" which means little surfer girl.
tagline: The story of a family girl. Until take 2.
title: Confessions of a Brazilian Call Girl
plot:
Confessions of a Brazilian Call Girl is a 2011 drama film that delves into the life of a young woman who becomes involved in the sex trade, navigating the complexities of her own desires and the harsh realities of her profession. The movie explores themes of identity, empowerment, and the objectification of women.

At its core, the film is a powerful exploration of the human condition, shedding light on the darker corners of society where individuals are often forced to confront their own vulnerabilities and limitations. Through the protagonist's journey, the movie raises important questions about the nature of consent, the commodification of the body, and the struggle for autonomy in the face of societal expectations.

The film also touches on the theme of cultural identity, highlighting the tensions between traditional values and modern aspirations. The protagonist's experiences serve as a catalyst for self-discovery, forcing her to confront the contradictions between her own desires and the expectations placed upon her by society.

Ultimately, Confessions of a Brazilian Call Girl is a thought-provoking and unflinching portrayal of a complex issue, one that challenges viewers to consider the intricacies of human experience and the ways in which societal norms can both empower and oppress individuals.

overview: USSR, June 1985. After contact with the Salyut 7 space station is lost, cosmonauts Vladimir Dzhanibekov and Viktor Savinykh dock with the empty, frozen craft, and bring her back to life. Based on actual events.
title: Salyut-7
plot:
Salyut 7 (Russian: Салют-7) is a 2017 Russian space disaster drama directed by Klim Shipenko from an idea by space journalist Aleksey Samolyotov. Starring Vladimir Vdovichenkov and Pavel Derevyanko, it is inspired by the 1985 Soyuz T-13 mission, the first time a "dead" space station was docked with and brought back into service, although the characters' names were changed and events were dramatised.

In July 1984, during a spacewalk, cosmonaut Vladimir Fyodorov helps colleague Svetlana Lazareva after her glove is punctured and glimpses a strange blue glow; doctors decide he was hallucinating and ground him, to the relief of his wife Nina. In February 1985 the unmanned Salyut 7 stops responding to Mission Control. Western media warn of an uncontrolled crash, and Soviet officials learn that the US is preparing the shuttle Challenger, whose cargo bay is suspiciously sized to hold the station. Engineer Viktor Alyokhin, who helped build Salyut 7, is chosen for a two-man rescue flight, but no candidate pilot can dock with the tumbling station in the simulator, and flight director Valeriy Shubin turns to Fyodorov. In June 1985 Fyodorov matches the station's spin and docks on his second attempt. They find Salyut 7 without power and encased in ice from a burst water system. Mission Control urges them to deorbit it, warning that thawing could cause short circuits and fire, but they begin warming and repairing it. On a spacewalk Fyodorov sees that a meteoroid shower has crushed the cover of the sensor that orients the solar panels. Thawed water shorts the Soyuz's wiring and sets it ablaze; Alyokhin puts the fire out by depressurising the craft, which is gutted, and he is badly burned. With Challenger launched, the Soviet military prepares to destroy the station, and controllers realise there is only enough oxygen for one man to return. Fyodorov offers to sacrifice himself, but Alyokhin proposes knocking the damaged cover off with a hammer. The gamble works, power returns, and as Challenger arrives a French astronaut aboard salutes the cosmonauts, who then see the blue glow.

Vdovichenkov plays Fyodorov, based on Vladimir Dzhanibekov, and Derevyanko plays Alyokhin, based on Viktor Savinykh, with Aleksandr Samoylenko as Shubin and Mariya Mironova as Nina. Filmed largely suspended on wires in a pavilion near Saint Petersburg, it was released by Nashe Kino on October 12, 2017, grossed 783 million rubles on a 400 million budget, and won the Golden Eagle for Best Film.

overview: When the devil resurfaces with aims to take over the world in human form, Johnny Blaze reluctantly comes out of hiding to transform into the flame-spewing supernatural hero Ghost Rider -- and rescue a 10-year-old boy from an unsavory end.
tagline: He rides again.
title: Ghost Rider: Spirit of Vengeance
plot:
Ghost Rider: Spirit of Vengeance is a 2012 American supernatural action film directed by Neveldine/Taylor, but released as 2011 due to a distribution deal. The movie stars Nicolas Cage as Johnny Blaze, also known as the Ghost Rider.

The story begins with Johnny Blaze (Nicolas Cage), who has been living in hiding for years after his last encounter with Mephisto (Peter Fonda). However, when a young boy named Robbie (Fergus Rees) is kidnapped by the devil's minions, Blaze is forced back into action to rescue him.

Blaze soon discovers that the boy is being held captive by the devil himself, and that he has been chosen as part of an ancient ritual to bring about the apocalypse. The only way to stop this from happening is for Blaze to ride the Ghost Rider again and put an end to Mephisto's plans.

As Blaze embarks on his quest, he teams up with a mysterious woman named Stakelbeck (Ciarán Hinds), who claims to be working against Mephisto. However, it becomes clear that Stakelbeck has ulterior motives, and is actually working for the devil himself.

The plot thickens as Blaze delves deeper into the world of demonic magic, encountering a range of supernatural creatures along the way. He also begins to question his own sanity, as he struggles to maintain control over his Ghost Rider persona.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Mephisto's plan is to use Robbie as a vessel for an ancient evil entity known as the "Devil's Son". This entity has the power to bring about the apocalypse, and only Blaze can stop it.

The climax of the film features an epic showdown between Blaze and Mephisto, with the fate of the world hanging in the balance. In the end, Blaze is able to defeat Mephisto and save Robbie from becoming a vessel for the Devil's Son.

However, the film ends on a bleak note, as Blaze is left feeling empty and unfulfilled after his victory. He realizes that he has lost himself to the Ghost Rider persona, and that he needs to find a way to reconcile his dual identity.

Overall, Ghost Rider: Spirit of Vengeance is a dark and action-packed take on the Ghost Rider franchise. While it received mixed reviews from critics, fans of the series will appreciate the film's over-the-top action sequences and supernatural thrills.

overview: The story of the rise and fall of the first American-born drug lord in Mexico, this tale of power, money, greed and betrayal amongst rival members of the drug cartels finds American gangster Erik Vasquez scheming to become the top dog in the Mexican underworld, only to find himself making enemies out of both the powerful cartels and his own allies.
tagline: The story of America's most dangerous drug trafficker.
title: American Sicario
plot:
American Sicario is a 2021 American crime action film directed by Raja "RJ" Collins from a screenplay by Rich Ronat, presented as being based on a true story. Produced in association with VMI Worldwide and GFG Entertainment and distributed by Saban Films, it stars Philippe A. Haddad as an American-born drug lord in Mexico, with Danny Trejo, Cali Morales, Maurice Compte, Maya Stojan, Jaylen Moore, Johnny Rey Diaz, Dionysio Basco and David A. Lockhart in supporting roles. The film opened in select US theatres on 10 December 2021 and was released on demand and on digital platforms on 14 December. It is rated R for violence, pervasive language, drug use and sexual material.

The film charts the rise and fall of Erik Vasquez (Haddad), a burly Texas native who fled to Mexico to escape narcotics charges in Laredo and has since worked his way up the cartel food chain, building his own gang and smuggling drugs back across the border. He now has a pregnant wife, Gloria (Morales), and a father-in-law, Pedro (Trejo), who is staying with them for an extended visit. Pedro, a veteran who once dealt drugs and worked with the cartels himself before getting out, has firm ideas about how Erik should treat Gloria and her unborn child, and warns him that in their business nothing is more important than family and loyalty. Scheming to become the top figure in the Mexican underworld, Erik tries to outmanoeuvre his bosses, the Feliz brothers (Compte and Diaz), and also crosses paths with DEA agent Monica Wells (Stojan). His ambition and greed turn both the powerful cartels and his own allies against him, culminating in an attack on his mansion, while his clashes with Pedro test the bonds of family and loyalty.

Critics generally found the film derivative. Josh Lasser of The TV and Film Guy's Reviews considered the cartel storyline bland and populated by two-dimensional characters, but enjoyed the lighter, more comic family thread driven by Trejo's sly presence, regretting that it played second fiddle. John Strange of Selig Film News gave it two stars, calling the gunfights poorly staged and edited and saying Trejo was wasted on the material. Mae Trumata of The Upcoming was more positive, praising the high-contrast, neon-lit cinematography and editing, the mansion assault sequence and the well-drawn generational contrast between Erik and Pedro.

overview: "Barbie" stars as Clara in this animated retelling of the classic Christmas ballet, complete with Tchaikovsky soundtrack and ballet choreography.
title: Barbie in the Nutcracker
plot:
Barbie in the Nutcracker is a 2001 Canadian-American computer-animated fantasy film co-produced by Mainframe Entertainment and Mattel Entertainment and distributed by Artisan Home Entertainment. Loosely based on E. T. A. Hoffmann's 1816 story "The Nutcracker and the Mouse King" and set to music from Tchaikovsky's ballet, it was Barbie's first film since two 1987 television specials and her first CGI film. Kelly Sheridan voices Barbie, with Kirby Morrow and Tim Curry also in the cast.

Barbie tells a story to her little sister, Kelly, who is struggling with a ballet solo. In 1890s Germany, Clara lives with her stern grandfather, Drosselmeyer, and her little brother, Tommy. On Christmas Eve their aunt Elizabeth gives Clara a nutcracker, which Tommy breaks in a tussle. Clara mends it and falls asleep by the tree, and at midnight she wakes to see the Nutcracker come to life and fight the army of the wicked Mouse King, who shrinks her with magic. The Nutcracker, also under the Mouse King's spell, takes Clara to find the Sugarplum Princess, the only one who can undo their enchantments, and an owl gives Clara a locket that will send her home when opened.

Helped by snow fairies, they reach the Nutcracker's homeland, Parthenia, where they learn that its heir, Prince Eric, has vanished. Major Mint and Captain Candy rescue them from the Mouse King's soldiers and explain that the old king had made the Mouse temporary ruler until the careless prince grew responsible. Clara realizes that the Nutcracker is Eric, transformed when the Mouse decided to keep the throne. On the journey they free trapped flower fairies and defeat a rock giant. The Princess's island proves a trap, and the Mouse King's bat henchman, Pimm, carries off the Nutcracker, Mint and Candy, but Clara frees them at the Mouse King's castle. In the duel, the Mouse King's spell rebounds and shrinks him. Clara kisses the wounded Nutcracker, restoring Eric, and is revealed to be the Sugarplum Princess herself. As Eric is crowned, the Mouse King steals and opens the locket, sending Clara home. Her grandfather dismisses her tale, but Aunt Elizabeth arrives with a young man named Eric, who asks Clara to dance. Inspired, Kelly masters her solo.

Released on VHS on October 2, 2001, and on DVD later that month, the film sold more than 3.5 million units and generated $150 million in total sales including merchandise. The New York Times called it a diverting, inoffensively sweet tale for very small children.

overview: To end an apocalyptic war and save her daughter, a reluctant soldier embarks on a desperate mission to cross a frozen sea carrying a top-secret cargo.
tagline: Hope burns brightest in the cold.
title: Black Crab
plot:
Black Crab (Swedish: Svart krabba) is a 2022 Swedish action thriller directed by Adam Berg, who adapted Jerker Virdborg's 2002 novel of the same name with Pelle Rådström. Noomi Rapace stars as Caroline Edh, a speed skater conscripted into a small unit sent to skate across frozen sea behind enemy lines. Netflix released the film on 18 March 2022.

In a flashback, Edh and her young daughter, Vanja, are caught in an enemy attack on civilians. Years later Edh is a soldier summoned to a base where Colonel Raad briefs a hand-picked team: the inexperienced signals specialist Karimi, the seasoned Danish soldier Malik, the Norwegian sniper Granvik and their leader, Captain Forsberg. They must skate across the ice-covered Stockholm archipelago to deliver two canisters to the research base on Ödö, which could win the war. Edh calls it a suicide mission but agrees when she is told that Vanja has been found alive in a refugee camp. Joined by Lieutenant Nylund, the team sets off as the base comes under attack. Forsberg drowns after breaking through thin ice, an enemy helicopter destroys their shelter after Karimi uses the radio, and Karimi and Malik are fatally wounded in a shootout with an elderly couple who had stayed behind.

Opening the canisters, the survivors find vials marked with a biohazard warning, apparently a biological weapon, and the dying Malik warns that it would mean not the end of the war but the end of everything before taking his own life. Granvik is killed in an enemy attack, and Edh shoots Nylund when he deserts with the vials to destroy them. Collapsing on the ice, she wakes at the base with frostbite, is decorated and promoted, and then learns that the promise of her daughter was only a ruse to keep her going. With Nylund, who survived, she steals the vials back from the laboratory during an evacuation. Cornered by the commander, Nordh, she steps off a cliff holding the vials and an unpinned grenade, and in death she is reunited with Vanja underwater.

Jakob Oftebro, Erik Enge, Dar Salim, Ardalan Esmaili, Aliette Opheim, David Dencik, Susan Taslimi and Stella Marcimain Klintberg appear in supporting roles. Reviews were mixed, with 50% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a consensus calling it exciting in the moment but bleak and derivative. The Guardian admired Berg's suspenseful handling of the ice but found its pacifist message hollow, while IGN called Rapace powerful throughout.

overview: A young Brooklyn couple head upstate to disconnect from their phones and reconnect with themselves. Cut off from their devices, they miss the news that the planet is under attack.
tagline: Turning off their phones was the dumbest idea on the planet.
title: Save Yourselves!
plot:
Save Yourselves! is a 2020 American science fiction romantic comedy film that explores the complexities of relationships and human connection in the face of catastrophic change. The movie takes place on a spaceship where two couples, struggling with their own issues, must navigate the challenges of isolation and confinement.

At its core, Save Yourselves! delves into the theme of love and relationships in the most unexpected ways. As the characters' initial romantic connections begin to fray under the pressure of their situation, they are forced to confront the true nature of intimacy and connection. The film masterfully weaves together humor, pathos, and wit to examine the ways in which people respond to crisis and the importance of human vulnerability.

The movie also touches on the theme of identity and how it is shaped by our relationships with others. As the characters' sense of self becomes increasingly tied to their romantic partners, they must confront the possibility that their identities may be more fluid than they initially thought.
