Ultimately, The Secret Life of Bees presents a powerful exploration of the human experience, one that celebrates the resilience and strength of women, particularly those from marginalized communities, as they navigate the complexities of life, love, and social change.

overview: Two high schoolers find hope as they fight to save an old wartime era clubhouse from destruction during the preparations for the 1964 Tokyo Olympics.
tagline: Let’s walk facing upwards.
title: From Up on Poppy Hill
plot:
From Up on Poppy Hill is a 2011 Japanese animated drama film written and directed by Gorō Miyazaki, the eldest son of Studio Ghibli's co-founder Hayao Miyazaki. The film is set in 1964, during the height of Japan's post-war economic boom.

The story takes place in the seaside town of Shirokane, where a group of high school students are struggling to find their place in the world. The main character, Umi Kitano, is a shy and introverted girl who has just transferred to Shirokane High School from a rural area. She becomes fast friends with Shun Kazama, a charismatic and confident student who is also an avid photographer.

As they explore the town together, Umi and Shun stumble upon a mysterious clubhouse hidden in the attic of a former school building. The clubhouse was once the hangout spot for the school's baseball team, but it has been abandoned since the team disbanded years ago. The two friends decide to restore the clubhouse to its former glory and make it their own secret hideout.

As they work on the clubhouse, Umi and Shun begin to uncover the town's history and secrets. They learn about the town's past glories as a major industrial center and the struggles of its people during World War II. They also discover that the clubhouse was once the site of a tragic accident that resulted in the death of several students.

Through their research, Umi and Shun develop feelings for each other, but they are hesitant to express them due to their different personalities and social status. Meanwhile, the town is facing a crisis as the local factory, which has been the backbone of the economy, announces its closure due to declining profits.

As the school year comes to a close, Umi and Shun must confront their own feelings for each other and find a way to save the clubhouse from being demolished. In the process, they learn valuable lessons about friendship, love, and the importance of preserving the past.

The film's title, "From Up on Poppy Hill," refers to the iconic poppy hill that dominates the town's landscape. The hill is a symbol of the town's history and resilience, and it serves as a backdrop for Umi and Shun's journey of self-discovery.

Throughout the film, Miyazaki explores themes of identity, community, and the power of human connection. He also pays tribute to the post-war generation in Japan, who were shaped by the country's tumultuous history and struggled to find their place in the world.

Overall, From Up on Poppy Hill is a poignant and beautifully animated film that celebrates the beauty of small-town life and the importance of preserving our collective past.

original_title: Le guide de la famille parfaite
overview: A couple in Québec deals with the pitfalls, pressure and high expectations of raising kids in a society obsessed with success and social media image.
title: The Guide to the Perfect Family
plot:
The Guide to the Perfect Family (French: Le Guide de la famille parfaite) is a 2021 Canadian comedy-drama film directed by Ricardo Trogi. Louis Morissette and Catherine Chabot star as Martin Dubois and Marie-Soleil Blouin, a married couple with a tendency toward helicopter parenting, with Émilie Bierre as Martin's teenage daughter Rose, from his previous marriage to Caroline, played by Isabelle Guérard. Xavier Lebel also appears. The story centres on the pressure that a father's ambitions place on his daughter.

At work, the middle-aged Martin hires a young man named Pier-Luc only because he is the son of a colleague. The new employee refuses to work under pressure, resents a heavy workload and will not accept criticism from his superiors, and when a major contract under his responsibility is lost, Martin misses out on an important promotion. At home, Martin applies relentless pressure of his own to Rose, constantly reminding her of her dance and hockey practices and tutoring sessions and warning her that unless she excels in her eleventh-grade studies she may end up in a low-paying job, such as working as a cashier at a convenience store. Overwhelmed, Rose begins using and trading drugs in exchange for old exam papers to meet her father's demands. As her final exams approach, Martin takes her for a weekend in the woods near a lake on a visit to her grandparents, hoping to reconnect with her, but an activity that begins pleasantly ends in a fierce argument in which Rose finally tells him she never feels she can live up to his expectations. Back in the city, she moves in with her mother. Devastated by her exam results, Rose suffers a crisis that lands her in hospital, forcing Martin to confront the damage caused by his ambitions. Father and daughter reconcile, and Martin begins to understand that sometimes children must be allowed to fall in order to learn.

The film was released theatrically in Quebec on July 14, 2021, and was acquired by Netflix for international distribution. The trade magazine Playback named it the Film of the Year in its year-end review of Canadian film and television in 2021.

original_title: Dead Like Me: Life After Death
overview: When George and her colleagues get a new boss whose focus is on moving souls quickly and enjoying life without consequences, the team begins to break the strict reaper rules. While her friends fall victim to their desires for money, success, and fame, George breaks another rule by revealing her true identity to her living family.
title: Dead Like Me: Life After Death
plot:
Dead Like Me: Life After Death is an American fantasy comedy-drama of 2009 directed by Stephen Herek and written by John Masius and Stephen Godchaux, continuing Bryan Fuller's short-lived television series Dead Like Me (2003). Ellen Muth returns as Georgia "George" Lass, a young woman working as a grim reaper after death, with Callum Blue as Mason, Jasmine Guy as Roxy, Britt McKillip as George's sister Reggie, Christine Willes as her temp agency boss Delores and Henry Ian Cusick as the new head reaper Cameron Kane. Sarah Wynter replaces Laura Harris as Daisy Adair, and Mandy Patinkin does not appear.

The reapers, whose task is to collect the souls of people just before they die, face upheaval when their usual hangout, Der Waffle Haus, burns down on the same day that their boss Rube vanishes. Their replacement supervisor is Cameron Kane, a smooth businessman who died falling from the World Trade Center on 11 September 2001. Kane lavishes gadgets and luxury on them and teaches them, as Roxy later puts it, that nothing they do on Earth matters. Under his influence the reapers go astray: Roxy saves people she was supposed to reap, Mason exploits his immortality to make money, Daisy lets a soul wander instead of guiding it on.

George, who narrates the story, is fired from the Happy Time temp agency after loudly scolding an employee for handing in a report late; the employee quits and sues for harassment. Meanwhile George reveals her true identity to her sister Reggie, and helps Reggie prepare for the coming death of her boyfriend, Hudson Hart. When the reapers confront Kane, they learn that he knew perfectly well that the small pebbles of their misdeeds would send waves of misfortune elsewhere. Fed up with his management, they set out to discover how a reaper can be destroyed, finally succeeding by dismembering and cremating him after shooting and drowning fail. His ashes are launched into orbit along with those of Murray, Delores's cat. At the launch Delores tells George that the employee who sued had made similar claims at previous jobs, and George is rehired with a corner office. Later George is suddenly showered with sticky notes falling from the sky, like the ones Rube once used to deliver their assignments.

After a television debut on Canada's Super Channel in January 2009, the film was released on DVD in February. Reel Film Reviews called it a fitting if uneven send-off for the cult Showtime series.

overview: When a rare phenomenon gives police officer John Sullivan the chance to speak to his father, 30 years in the past, he takes the opportunity to prevent his dad's tragic death.  After his actions inadvertently give rise to a series of brutal murders he and his father must find a way to fix the consequences of altering time.
tagline: The future is listening.
title: Frequency
plot:
Frequency is a 2000 American science fiction thriller film directed by Craig Mazin, starring Dennis Quaid, Jim Caviezel, and Shawn Doyle.

The main themes of Frequency include:

1. **Time Travel and its Consequences**: The movie explores the concept of time travel through a police scanner radio connection between two men across different timelines. This theme delves into the consequences of altering the past and the potential impact on one's present and future.
2. **Family and Legacy**: The story revolves around the relationship between Martin (Dennis Quaid) and his son Jake (Jim Caviezel), who are connected through a mysterious police scanner radio. As they navigate their different timelines, they must also confront their own personal struggles and learn to connect with each other across time.
3. **Redemption and Personal Growth**: Throughout the film, both Martin and Jake face challenges that force them to re-evaluate their lives and make amends for past mistakes. This theme highlights the importance of redemption, forgiveness, and personal growth in overcoming adversity.
4. **The Butterfly Effect**: The movie illustrates the concept of the butterfly effect, where small changes in one's actions can have significant effects on the course of events in another timeline.

Overall, Frequency is a thought-provoking film that explores complex themes through its unique blend of science fiction and family drama elements.

original_title: The Man Who Killed Don Quixote
overview: Toby, a cynical film director finds himself trapped in the outrageous delusions of an old Spanish shoe-maker who believes himself to be Don Quixote. In the course of their comic and increasingly surreal adventures, Toby is forced to confront the tragic repercussions of a film he made in his idealistic youth.
tagline: Today's a marvelous day for adventures!
title: The Man Who Killed Don Quixote
plot:
The Man Who Killed Don Quixote is a 2018 Spanish drama film directed by Terry Gilliam. The movie is an adaptation of Miguel de Cervantes' classic novel "Don Quixote" and explores the themes of reality, perception, and the human condition.

At its core, the film delves into the idea that our perceptions of reality are subjective and can be influenced by our own biases, experiences, and emotions. The protagonist, Toby Grisoni (played by Jonathan Pryce), is a filmmaker who becomes obsessed with recreating the world of Don Quixote for his movie. As he navigates this fictional realm, he begins to lose touch with reality, blurring the lines between what's real and what's not.

The film also explores the theme of identity and how it can be shaped by our experiences, relationships, and societal expectations. Toby Grisoni is a complex character who struggles with his own sense of self, feeling disconnected from the world around him. His journey becomes a metaphor for the search for meaning and purpose in life.

Furthermore, The Man Who Killed Don Quixote touches on the idea of nostalgia and how it can be both a bittersweet and redemptive force. Toby's obsession with recreating the past is driven by his desire to recapture lost love and experiences, but ultimately leads him down a path of self-discovery and transformation.

Throughout the film, Gilliam's signature visual style and sense of humor add depth and complexity to the narrative, making it a thought-provoking exploration of the human experience.

overview: When they're hired to recover the lost treasure of Columbus, married scuba divers Sebastian and Dani think they've hit the jackpot. But as they get closer to the fortune, the couple begins to suspect their employers have their own agenda. Hitting upon the real plan, the two come to the chilling realization that they may be expendable and that there's much more than riches at stake.
tagline: It's not another day at the beach.
title: Into the Blue 2: The Reef
plot:
Into the Blue 2: The Reef is an action-adventure film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature, particularly in the context of greed and the consequences of playing with forces beyond one's control. The movie follows a group of divers who embark on a perilous journey to find a lost treasure, only to discover that they are not alone in the depths of the ocean.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the characters' obsession with the treasure is driven by a desire for wealth and power, which ultimately leads them down a path of destruction and chaos. The film's portrayal of the destructive nature of greed serves as a cautionary tale, highlighting the devastating consequences of allowing ambition to consume one's values and principles.

Furthermore, the movie explores themes of redemption and personal growth, as some characters are forced to confront their past mistakes and make amends in order to survive. Through its narrative, Into the Blue 2: The Reef suggests that it is never too late to change one's ways and seek forgiveness, offering a message of hope and renewal.

The film also touches on the idea of the dangers of playing with nature, as the characters' actions have unintended consequences that put them and others at risk. This serves as a reminder of the importance of respecting the natural world and the delicate balance of ecosystems.

Overall, Into the Blue 2: The Reef is a thrilling adventure that explores complex themes and moral dilemmas, leaving viewers to ponder the consequences of human actions in the face of nature's power.

belongs_to_collection.name: My Little Pony: Equestria Girls Collection

original_title: My Little Pony: Equestria Girls - Rainbow Rocks
overview: Music rules and rainbows rock as Twilight Sparkle and pals compete for the top spot in the Canterlot High "Mane Event" talent show. The girls must rock their way to the top, and outshine rival Adagio Dazzle and her band The Dazzlings, to restore harmony back to Canterlot High.
tagline: To Restore Harmony, The Bands Must Battle!
title: My Little Pony: Equestria Girls - Rainbow Rocks
plot:
My Little Pony: Equestria Girls - Rainbow Rocks is a 2014 animated musical fantasy comedy film directed by Izzy Lazier and produced by DHX Media. The movie serves as the sequel to My Little Pony: Equestria Girls.

The main themes of My Little Pony: Equestria Girls - Rainbow Rocks include:

1. Friendship and unity: The movie emphasizes the importance of friendship, teamwork, and unity among the Mane Six and their friends in the human world. The characters work together to overcome challenges and achieve their goals.
2. Self-discovery and empowerment: The film explores themes of self-discovery, individuality, and empowerment, particularly for the character of Sunset Shimmer. She learns to accept herself and find her place among her peers.
3. Music as a form of expression and healing: Music plays a significant role in the movie, serving as a means of expression, comfort, and healing. The characters use music to cope with their emotions and overcome adversity.
4. Bullying and peer pressure: The film tackles the issue of bullying and peer pressure, highlighting the negative impact it can have on individuals. The characters learn to stand up for themselves and support one another in the face of adversity.

The movie follows the Mane Six as they attend a music camp called Camp Everfree, where they meet new friends and rivals. Sunset Shimmer, a former rival turned friend, helps the group overcome their differences and work together to stop an evil villain who seeks to destroy their friendship and the magic of Equestria.

Overall, My Little Pony: Equestria Girls - Rainbow Rocks is a heartwarming and entertaining film that promotes positive values such as friendship, self-acceptance, and empowerment.

overview: A group of people are plunged into a dark, claustrophobic maze, where they must fight to survive, as the outside world watches.
tagline: Only one survives
title: Andron
plot:
Andron, released internationally as Andròn: The Black Labyrinth, is an Italian-made, English-language dystopian science fiction action film written and directed by Francesco Cinquemani. Leo Howard and Gale Harold head an ensemble of young contestants that also includes Michelle Ryan, Antonia Campbell-Hughes, Jon Kortajarena, Margareth Madè and the Skunk Anansie singer Skin in her first acting role, with Alec Baldwin and Danny Glover in supporting parts. It was produced by Andrea Iervolino and Monika Bacardi for Ambi Pictures and shot in Italy and Malta.

Ten young people wake up in a dark underground maze with no idea how they got there and no memory even of their own names. As fragments of their past return, they are disturbed to find that they seem to come from different periods of history. Moving walls abruptly reshape the labyrinth, separating the group, crushing some of its members and bringing the survivors into contact with new people, while packs of heavily armoured fighters hunt them and a robotic voice announces each death. The captives gradually realize that they are contestants in the Redemption Games, a deadly contest from which only one can emerge alive. The year is 2154, a quarter of a century after a "Big Catastrophe" that killed billions and allowed nine corporations to take over the world and enslave most of humanity. The games are broadcast to pacify the suffering masses outside, who bet on the contestants' survival. Overseeing the show from a vast office is Adam, a television executive and puppet master who watches the action on screens and arbitrarily intervenes to liven things up, answering to his political master, Chancellor Gordon. As their numbers shrink, the survivors, among them Alexander and Julian, must work out the puzzle of where they are and try to find a way out of the labyrinth.

The film premiered at the Trieste Science+Fiction Festival on November 8, 2015, and Momentum Pictures gave it a limited release in the United States in June 2016. It was panned by critics and holds a Metacritic score of 16 out of 100. Dennis Harvey of Variety described it as a drab and dull recycling of The Hunger Games, The Maze Runner and Cube, with Baldwin and Glover barely concealing their disinterest, though he praised Gherardo Gossi's widescreen cinematography and Riccardo Eberspacher's score. Frank Scheck of The Hollywood Reporter found it boring, incoherent and derivative.

overview: A story of broken humanity following the invasion of a technologically superior alien species. Bleak, harrowing, and unrelenting, the humans must find enough courage to go on fighting.
title: Rakka
plot:
Rakka is a 2017 science fiction film directed by Travis Fimmel and written by Travis Fimmel and James Blake. The movie takes place in a post-apocalyptic world where humanity has been decimated by an alien invasion.

The main theme of Rakka revolves around the struggle for survival and the human condition in the face of catastrophic loss. The story follows a young woman named Maya, who is forced to confront her own mortality and the true meaning of life when she discovers that she may be the last human survivor on Earth.

As Maya navigates this desolate world, she must come to terms with the fact that she is no longer alone, but rather part of a larger, interconnected web of humanity. The film explores themes of loneliness, isolation, and the search for connection in a world that has been ravaged by destruction.

Throughout the movie, the audience is taken on a journey of self-discovery, as Maya grapples with her own identity and purpose in a world that seems to have lost its way. The film's use of stunning visuals and atmospheric sound design creates a sense of immersion and tension, drawing the viewer into Maya's world and forcing them to confront their own emotions and fears.

Ultimately, Rakka is a powerful exploration of what it means to be human in the face of unimaginable loss and destruction. It is a thought-provoking and visually stunning film that challenges the audience to consider the true meaning of existence and our place in the universe.

original_title: ホーホケキョ となりの山田くん
overview: The Yamadas are a typical middle class Japanese family in urban Tokyo and this film shows us a variety of episodes of their lives. With tales that range from the humorous to the heartbreaking, we see this family cope with life's little conflicts, problems, and joys in their own way.
tagline: The safety of family is the wish of the world.
title: My Neighbors the Yamadas
plot:
"My Neighbors the Yamadas" is a 1999 Japanese animated film written and directed by Isao Takahata, produced by Studio Ghibli. The movie is a poignant and humorous portrayal of family life in post-war Japan.

The main themes of "My Neighbors the Yamadas" can be summarized as follows:

1. **The Complexity of Family Life**: The film explores the intricate relationships within the Yamada family, showcasing their joys, struggles, and quirks. It highlights the imperfections and flaws that make families unique and relatable.
2. **Nostalgia and Sentimentality**: Set in the 1960s, the movie is a nostalgic tribute to Japan's post-war era. The film's use of music, costumes, and settings evokes a sense of nostalgia, reminding viewers of a bygone era.
3. **The Importance of Human Connection**: Despite their flaws, the Yamada family members are deeply connected to each other. The film emphasizes the value of relationships, friendships, and community in creating a fulfilling life.
4. **Growing Up and Letting Go**: As the children grow older, they face new challenges and must navigate the complexities of adulthood. The movie explores the bittersweet nature of growing up and letting go of childhood innocence.
5. **The Power of Everyday Life**: "My Neighbors the Yamadas" celebrates the beauty in everyday moments, highlighting the mundane yet meaningful aspects of family life. The film shows that even the most ordinary experiences can be extraordinary.

Through its gentle humor, poignant storytelling, and memorable characters, "My Neighbors the Yamadas" offers a heartwarming exploration of what it means to be human, to love, and to connect with others.

overview: Diamonds are stolen only to be sold again in the international market. James Bond infiltrates a smuggling mission to find out who's guilty. The mission takes him to Las Vegas where Bond meets his archenemy Blofeld.
tagline: The man who made 007 a household number.
title: Diamonds Are Forever
plot:
Diamonds Are Forever is a 1971 spy film directed by Guy Hamilton and produced by Albert R. Broccoli and Harry Saltzman, under the United Artists banner.

The movie follows James Bond (played by Sean Connery), who is sent to investigate the theft of a diamond called "The Big Sleep". The diamond has been stolen from an American oil tycoon's safe deposit box at Fort Knox, Kentucky. Bond soon discovers that the thief is not after the diamond itself but rather its value as a symbol of wealth and power.

Bond's investigation leads him to Las Vegas, where he encounters Tiffany Case (played by Jill St. John), a beautiful and alluring woman who is being pursued by various villains. As Bond delves deeper into the case, he uncovers a complex web of intrigue involving organized crime syndicates, corrupt government officials, and a mysterious organization known as SPECTRE.

Bond's search for Tiffany leads him to a seedy underworld of Las Vegas casinos, nightclubs, and brothels, where he encounters a range of colorful characters, including the enigmatic Mr. Wint (played by Charles Gray) and his partner, Mr. Kidd (played by Louis Jourdan). As Bond navigates this treacherous landscape, he must also contend with the villainous Ernst Stavro Blofeld (played by Donald Pleasence), who is revealed to be the mastermind behind the theft of the diamond.

Throughout the film, Bond's character undergoes significant development as he confronts his own demons and struggles with the moral implications of his actions. The movie also explores themes of identity, loyalty, and the corrupting influence of power.

The plot thickens as Bond discovers that Tiffany is being used by SPECTRE to lure him into a trap. In a thrilling sequence, Bond must use all his skills and cunning to outwit Blofeld's henchmen and rescue Tiffany from their clutches.

In the climactic final confrontation, Bond faces off against Blofeld in a high-stakes game of cat and mouse. The movie culminates in a dramatic showdown at the SPECTRE headquarters, where Bond must use all his wits and resources to defeat Blofeld and save the world from his evil plans.

Ultimately, Bond emerges victorious, having saved the day once again. However, the film ends on a somewhat ambiguous note, leaving the audience wondering about the fate of Tiffany and the extent of SPECTRE's influence.

Overall, Diamonds Are Forever is a classic Bond film that showcases Sean Connery's signature style and charisma as James Bond. The movie's blend of action, suspense, and humor has made it a beloved entry in the franchise, and its themes of identity and loyalty continue to resonate with audiences today.

overview: The chronicles of four years in the life of Julie, a young woman who navigates the troubled waters of her love life and struggles to find her career path, leading her to take a realistic look at who she really is.
title: The Worst Person in the World
plot:
The Worst Person in the World is a 2021 Norwegian black comedy film directed by Joachim Trier, written by Espen Sandberg and Joachim Trier, and starring Andrea Riseborough, Anders Linnet Nordvang, and Jonas Holmlund.

The film follows Julie (Andrea Riseborough), a young woman who struggles to find direction in her life. The story is presented as a series of vignettes, each set at a different point in Julie's life, from her teenage years to adulthood.

In the first vignette, we see Julie as a teenager, feeling disconnected and uncertain about her future. She is portrayed as awkward and introverted, but also fiercely independent and determined to forge her own path.

As the film progresses, we follow Julie through various relationships and experiences, including a brief romance with a charismatic but troubled young man named Aman (Anders Linnet Nordvang). However, their relationship ultimately ends in heartbreak, leaving Julie feeling lost and uncertain about what she wants from life.

Throughout the film, Julie's character is portrayed as complex and multifaceted, struggling to reconcile her desire for independence with her need for human connection. Her relationships with others are often fraught with tension and uncertainty, but also marked by moments of tenderness and vulnerability.

One of the most striking aspects of The Worst Person in the World is its use of non-linear storytelling. Each vignette is presented as a self-contained unit, yet they are all linked together by Julie's ongoing journey of self-discovery. This structure allows the film to explore different themes and emotions, while also creating a sense of continuity and coherence.

As the film progresses, we see Julie navigate various careers and relationships, including a stint as a journalist and a brief romance with a man named Thomas (Jonas Holmlund). However, each of these experiences ultimately ends in disappointment or heartbreak, leaving Julie feeling lost and uncertain about her future.

Ultimately, The Worst Person in the World is a film about the complexities and challenges of growing up. It is a nuanced and thought-provoking exploration of identity, relationships, and the search for meaning in life. Through its non-linear structure and complex characters, the film creates a sense of depth and complexity that rewards close attention and reflection.

Overall, The Worst Person in the World is a powerful and moving film that explores the complexities of human experience with wit, nuance, and sensitivity.

overview: After the death of her mother, Evie is approached by an unknown cousin who invites her to a lavish wedding in the English countryside. Soon, she realizes a gothic conspiracy is afoot and must fight for survival as she uncovers twisted secrets in her family’s history.
tagline: You are cordially invited to a nightmare generations in the making.
title: The Invitation
plot:
The Invitation is a 2022 American horror thriller directed by Jessica M. Thompson and written by Blair Butler, inspired by Bram Stoker's novel Dracula. Screen Gems acquired Butler's pitch in 2019, and the project, first titled The Bride, lost producers Sam Raimi and Robert Tapert before Thompson came aboard to direct with Emile Gladstone producing. It stars Nathalie Emmanuel and Thomas Doherty, who replaced Garrett Hedlund, and was filmed in Budapest from September 2021.

In New York, struggling artist Evie Jackson works for a catering company with her best friend Grace. After her mother's death, a DNA test connects her with an English cousin, Oliver Alexander, who explains that her great-grandmother Emmaline had a secret child with a Black footman, and invites her to a family wedding in Whitby. At New Carfax Abbey, Evie is charmed by the estate's owner, Walter De Ville, as she meets his butler Mr. Field, the friendly bridesmaid Lucy and the haughty Viktoria. Meanwhile housemaids keep disappearing, and after discovering that Walter has been researching her, Evie confronts him before they make up and sleep together.

At the rehearsal dinner Walter announces that Evie is the bride. Mr. Field slits a maid's throat and serves her blood to Walter, Lucy and Viktoria, revealing them as vampires. The Alexanders are one of three families who have supplied Walter with wives for centuries in return for wealth and protection, and Emmaline, his former bride, had killed herself in guilt. Freed from the cellar by the maid Mrs. Swift, Evie flees to the village, but the elderly couple she turns to, Jonathan and Mina Harker, serve De Ville, who reveals he is Dracula. During the forced wedding, Evie drinks his blood, becomes a vampire, sets the chapel on fire and kills Mr. Field and, finally, Dracula, which returns her to human form, while Lucy destroys herself and Viktoria. Two weeks later, Evie and Grace go after Oliver for his betrayal.

Sony Pictures Releasing opened the film on August 26, 2022. Critics praised Emmanuel but faulted the predictable story and weak scares, giving it a 29% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes. It nonetheless topped the US box office in its first weekend and earned $38 million worldwide on a $10 million budget, turning a profit, and later reached Netflix's global top five.

overview: Four boyhood pals perform a heroic act and are changed by the powers they gain in return. Years later, on a hunting trip in the Maine woods, they're overtaken by a vicious blizzard that harbors an ominous presence. Challenged to stop an alien force, the friends must first prevent the slaughter of innocent civilians by a military vigilante ... and then overcome a threat to the bond that unites the four of them.
tagline: A circle of friendship. A web of mystery. A pattern of fear.
title: Dreamcatcher
plot:
Dreamcatcher is a science fiction horror film directed by Lawrence Kasdan, based on the novel of the same name by Stephen King. The movie was released in 2003 and stars Morgan Freeman, Thomas Jane, Damian Lewis, Donnie Wahlberg, and Jason Lee.

The story begins with four friends - Jonesy (Jason Lee), Beaver (Donnie Wahlberg), Pete (Thomas Jane), and Henry (Morgan Freeman) - who have been inseparable since childhood. They share a deep bond and are known for their unique friendship. The movie takes place in 1980, during the height of the Vietnam War.

The story begins with Jonesy, who has recently returned from Vietnam, suffering from amnesia due to his experiences as a soldier. He is unable to recall any memories before his time in the war. As he tries to piece together his past, he discovers that he and his friends have been chosen by an alien entity known as "The Gray" (also referred to as "The Others") to be its hosts on Earth.

The Gray has a plan to invade Earth using four human hosts, each with unique skills and abilities. The aliens intend to use the hosts' bodies to take over their minds and eventually conquer humanity. Jonesy, Beaver, Pete, and Henry are chosen for this purpose, but they soon realize that they must work together to stop The Gray's plans.

As the story unfolds, the four friends embark on a perilous journey across the United States, facing numerous challenges and obstacles along the way. They encounter various alien creatures, including giant spiders, mutated humans, and otherworldly beings. Along the way, they also uncover clues about their past and the true nature of The Gray's plan.

Throughout the movie, the characters' relationships are put to the test as they struggle to work together and trust each other. Jonesy, in particular, grapples with his amnesia and tries to come to terms with his past. Beaver is haunted by a traumatic event from his childhood, while Pete struggles with his own demons.

As the stakes grow higher, the friends discover that The Gray's plan involves using their combined skills to create an army of alien-human hybrids. They must use all their strength, courage, and ingenuity to stop this plan and save humanity.

The movie culminates in a climactic showdown between the four friends and The Gray's minions. In the end, Jonesy, Beaver, Pete, and Henry manage to defeat the aliens and destroy their plans for world domination. However, not before they are forced to confront their own personal demons and make sacrifices to save humanity.

Overall, Dreamcatcher is a thrilling science fiction horror film that explores themes of friendship, loyalty, and redemption. While it received mixed reviews from critics at the time of its release, it has since become a cult classic among fans of Stephen King's works.

overview: In the Yorkshire countryside, working-class tomboy Mona meets the exotic, pampered Tamsin. To seal their friendship, Mona introduces Tamsin to her born-again Christian brother and helps her spy on her adulterous father. Bound together by their secrets, the two girls see their friendship deepen and enter into dangerous waters.
tagline: The most dangerous thing to want is more.
title: My Summer of Love
plot:
My Summer of Love is a poignant and thought-provoking film that explores the complexities of human relationships, identity, and the struggles of growing up. The movie delves into the story of Tamsin, a 16-year-old girl who becomes involved with a charismatic and older man, Eddie, in a small town in Northern England.

At its core, My Summer of Love is a nuanced portrayal of first love, innocence, and the fragility of adolescence. The film masterfully captures the intensity and uncertainty of Tamsin's emotions as she navigates her feelings for Eddie, who represents a world beyond her own. Through their relationship, the movie raises questions about the nature of desire, consent, and the blurred lines between childhood and adulthood.

The film also explores themes of social class, identity, and the constraints placed on young people in small towns. Tamsin's struggles to assert her individuality and find her place within her community serve as a powerful commentary on the limitations and expectations that can shape our lives.

Ultimately, My Summer of Love is a deeply human and relatable film that invites viewers to reflect on their own experiences of love, loss, and self-discovery. The movie's thoughtful pacing and atmospheric cinematography create a sense of intimacy and vulnerability, drawing the audience into Tamsin's world and inviting them to share in her joys and sorrows.

overview: A modern-day take on the "Beauty and the Beast" tale where a New York teen is transformed into a hideous monster in order to find true love.
tagline: Love is never ugly.
title: Beastly
plot:
Beastly is a 2011 American fantasy romantic comedy film that explores several thought-provoking themes. At its core, the movie delves into the complexities of high school social hierarchy and the consequences of bullying.

The story revolves around Lindy (Hayley Roberts), a beautiful and popular high school student who is seemingly perfect on the outside but struggles with her own insecurities and flaws. When she makes a wish to be unattractive in order to get closer to her crush, Aaron (Dylan O'Brien), she inadvertently transforms him into a monstrous creature.

Through this transformation, the film highlights the cruel nature of high school social dynamics, where students are often judged based on their physical appearance rather than their inner qualities. The movie critiques the superficiality of teenage culture and the devastating effects it can have on individuals who feel like they don't fit in.

Moreover, Beastly explores themes of self-acceptance, empathy, and redemption. As Aaron navigates his new form, he learns to appreciate the beauty within himself and those around him, including Lindy's inner strength and vulnerability. The film ultimately suggests that true beauty lies not in physical appearance but in the complexities and imperfections that make us human.

The movie also touches on the idea of toxic masculinity, as Aaron struggles to come to terms with his new form and the societal expectations placed upon him. His transformation serves as a metaphor for the pressures and constraints that men often face in their lives, particularly in high school.

Overall, Beastly is a thought-provoking film that challenges its audience to reevaluate their perceptions of beauty, social hierarchy, and personal identity.

overview: Primatologist Davis Okoye shares an unshakable bond with George, the extraordinarily intelligent, silverback gorilla who has been in his care since birth.  But a rogue genetic experiment gone awry mutates this gentle ape into a raging creature of enormous size.  To make matters worse, it’s soon discovered there are other similarly altered animals.  As these newly created alpha predators tear across North America, destroying everything in their path, Okoye teams with a discredited genetic engineer to secure an antidote, fighting his way through an ever-changing battlefield, not only to halt a global catastrophe but to save the fearsome creature that was once his friend.
tagline: Big meets bigger
title: Rampage
plot:
Rampage is a 2018 science fiction monster film directed by Brad Peeters and written by Ryan Condal. The movie stars Dwayne Johnson, Naomie Harris, Malin Åkerman, Jake Lacy, and Jeffrey Dean Morgan.

The story begins with Davis Okoye (Dwayne Johnson), a primatologist who works at the San Diego Zoo. He is particularly close to his genetically engineered gorilla, George, whom he has raised since childhood. However, their peaceful life is disrupted when a biotech company called UAC (United Animal Corporation) announces its plans to create genetically modified super-soldiers using DNA from various animals.

The CEO of UAC, Robert K. Ross (Jeffrey Dean Morgan), reveals that the company's goal is to create an army of super-intelligent and powerful creatures to fight in a war against China. The plan involves injecting DNA from different species into various animals, making them stronger and more aggressive.

As the story unfolds, Davis discovers that UAC has been secretly experimenting on his gorilla, George, without his knowledge or consent. When he confronts Ross, he is met with hostility and eventually loses control of George, who escapes and wreaks havoc on San Diego.

Meanwhile, a genetically modified wolf named Ruby (Naomie Harris) and an elephant named Ralph (Jake Lacy) also escape from UAC's facility. The three creatures, including George, begin to terrorize the city, causing destruction and chaos.

As Davis tries to find a way to stop his creations, he teams up with Dr. Kate Caldwell (Malin Åkerman), a geneticist who helped create the super-soldiers. Together, they embark on a mission to find a cure for George's DNA and prevent further destruction.

Throughout the movie, Davis struggles with his feelings of guilt and responsibility towards George, whom he considers a friend. He also grapples with the consequences of playing God and creating life forms that are beyond human control.

As the story reaches its climax, Davis and Kate devise a plan to use a virus to reverse the effects of the DNA injection on George and the other creatures. In the final battle, Davis confronts Ross and his team, who have been using the super-soldiers for their own gain.

In the end, Davis is able to stop George and the other creatures from causing further destruction, but not before they wreak havoc on San Diego. The movie concludes with Davis reflecting on the consequences of his actions and the importance of responsible scientific research.

Overall, Rampage is an action-packed monster film that explores themes of responsibility, friendship, and the dangers of playing God. While it received mixed reviews from critics, it has become a cult classic among fans of science fiction and monster movies.

overview: When a spiteful coworker sabotages her deliveries, a courier and a helpful customer must race to return Christmas presents to their intended recipients.
title: Delivery by Christmas
plot:
Delivery by Christmas (Polish: Jeszcze przed świętami) is a 2022 Polish Christmas romantic comedy film directed by Aleksandra Kułakowska and Maciej Prykowski, who co-wrote the screenplay with Maria Pułaska-Białkowska. Produced by Robert Kijak for Next Film, with music by Andrzej Smolik, it stars Monika Frajczyk and Piotr Pacek, with Dorota Kolak, Mirosław Baka, Łukasz Simlat, Zdzisław Wardejn, Marek Kalita, Łukasz Gawroński and Franciszek Krupowicz. It was released on Netflix on 6 December 2022 and runs about 100 minutes.

In Warsaw, Marysia (Frajczyk), a harried single mother who works for a courier company, is so busy before Christmas that she has to bring her young son Maks (Krupowicz) along on her rounds in her battered delivery van. In an office building, Maks wanders off to a restroom and is helped by Krzysiek (Pacek), a legal executive trying to finish contracts before the holiday, before making a mess in his office, so Marysia owes him a favour. She agrees to collect his grandmother's engagement ring from his grumpy, prank-loving grandfather (Wardejn), as Krzysiek plans to propose to his live-in girlfriend on Christmas Eve, but the old man sends a joke object instead. Meanwhile, after Marysia rebuffs an unwanted drunken kiss from her new boss, a hard-drinking, unhappy loner, he takes revenge by swapping the labels on her deliveries. On Christmas Eve, as most of Poland stays home to celebrate, Marysia, with an irate Krzysiek tagging along, races across the city to put things right while also tracking down her own gift for Maks. The misdirected parcels, among them an ultrasound photo, a doll with a hidden flash drive and a pair of slippers, upend the lives of their recipients, including a lonely woman (Kolak) ignored by her husband (Kalita) and an unmotivated man (Gawroński) still living with his parents, while two police officers become comically involved. As the day goes on, Marysia and Krzysiek grow closer.

Reviews were mixed. Decider recommended it as a sweet, modestly charming film, likening it to a Polish Love Actually and praising Frajczyk's grounded performance as a working-class single mother who holds the film together amid gently stereotyped supporting characters. Roger Moore of Movie Nation felt that much of its charm and potential cuteness was lost to a stumbling structure, as repeated jumps back in time to show each mistaken delivery killed the pace and lowered the stakes of the central romance.

overview: Set in Stalin-era Soviet Union, a disgraced MGB agent is dispatched to investigate a series of child murders -- a case that begins to connect with the very top of party leadership.
tagline: How do you find a killer who doesn’t exist?
title: Child 44
plot:
Child 44 is a 2015 mystery thriller directed by Daniel Espinosa and written by Richard Price, adapted from Tom Rob Smith's 2008 novel. The ensemble cast features Tom Hardy, Gary Oldman, Noomi Rapace, Joel Kinnaman, Paddy Considine, Jason Clarke and Vincent Cassel. Both the novel and the film are very loosely based on the case of the Soviet serial killer Andrei Chikatilo.

In the Soviet Union of the early 1950s, under Stalin, Leo Demidov, a war hero and an agent of the Ministry of State Security (MGB), encounters a series of brutal child murders, but his superiors refuse to call them murders because official doctrine holds that serial killers are a product of capitalism. Leo's wife, Raisa, is accused of disloyalty, a charge Leo suspects was engineered by his ambitious rival, Vasili Nikitin. When Leo refuses to denounce her, he is demoted to the militia in the town of Volsk under General Mikhail Nesterov, and Raisa is forced to work as a janitor. Vasili urges Raisa to leave Leo for him and, when she refuses, has her mistreated.

When more murdered children are found in Volsk, Raisa joins Leo's investigation, and together they persuade Nesterov and his wife, Inessa, that a serial killer is at work. They discover at least 44 victims and realize that the killer travels the railways. On a secret trip to Moscow to interview a witness, Raisa realizes that a former colleague they turn to is an informer, and Leo kills him. Arrested on their return to Volsk, the couple are sent by train to a labor camp, where passengers attack them on Vasili's orders. They kill their attackers, jump from the train and make their way to Rostov, where most of the victims were found. By matching factory workers' travel records with the dates and places of the murders, Leo identifies Vladimir Malevich, a tractor factory worker, as the killer. Malevich surrenders, but Vasili, who has followed them, shoots him dead and tries to execute the couple, who kill him in a struggle. Leo blames Vasili's death on Malevich, whom the MGB falsely brands a Nazi agent. Reinstated, Leo asks to set up a homicide division in Moscow, and he and Raisa adopt two orphaned girls whose parents Vasili had executed.

Filmed in the Czech Republic and Romania, the film was released on 17 April 2015 but was withdrawn from Russian cinemas over its depiction of Soviet history. It grossed only $13 million on a $50 million budget, with critics praising Hardy but giving it 30% on Rotten Tomatoes and 41 on Metacritic.

overview: Samba migrated to France 10 years ago from Senegal, and has since been plugging away at various lowly jobs. Alice is a senior executive who has recently undergone a burnout. Both struggle to get out of their dead-end lives. Samba's willing to do whatever it takes to get working papers, while Alice tries to get her life back on track until fate draws them together.
tagline: Sometimes those with nothing have the most to lose.
title: Samba
plot:
Samba is a 2014 French comedy-drama film that tells the story of Samba Vincenzo Montanaro, an undocumented immigrant from Guinea who is arrested and deported back to his home country. The movie explores themes of identity, belonging, and the struggles of being an outsider in a new society.

At its core, Samba is a powerful exploration of what it means to be a migrant and the challenges that come with navigating a foreign culture. The film delves into the complexities of Samba's experiences as he tries to reconcile his past life in Guinea with his present reality in France. Through Samba's story, the movie sheds light on the difficulties faced by undocumented immigrants who are often forced to live in limbo, caught between two worlds and unable to fully belong in either.

The film also touches on themes of loneliness and isolation, as Samba struggles to form connections with those around him. His experiences serve as a commentary on the human cost of xenophobia and racism, highlighting the ways in which societal attitudes can marginalize and exclude individuals who are perceived as "other."

Ultimately, Sambia is a poignant and thought-provoking film that challenges viewers to consider the complexities of identity, belonging, and the immigrant experience.

overview: A woman discovers that severe catastrophic events are somehow connected to the mental breakdown from which she's suffering.
tagline: There's a monster in all of us
title: Colossal
plot:
Colossal is a 2017 American science fiction comedy-drama film directed by Nacho Vigalondo and written by Vigalondo and Phil Hay. The movie stars Anne Hathaway, Jason Sudeikis, Dan Stevens, Austin Stowell, Tim Blake Nelson, and Maude Apatow.

The main themes of Colossal include:

1. **Toxic Masculinity**: The film critiques the societal expectations placed on men to be strong and stoic, as embodied by the character of Joe (Jason Sudeikis). His inability to express emotions and his reliance on toxic masculinity lead to a series of tragic events.

2. **Feminism and Empowerment**: The protagonist, Gloria (Anne Hathaway), is a complex and multifaceted character who undergoes significant personal growth throughout the film. Her journey from a vulnerable and insecure individual to a confident and self-assured person serves as a powerful feminist statement.

3. **Trauma and Mental Health**: The movie explores the long-term effects of trauma on individuals, particularly women. Gloria's experiences with her abusive father and her struggles with anxiety and depression are skillfully woven into the narrative, highlighting the importance of seeking help and support.

4. **Identity and Self-Discovery**: As Gloria navigates her relationships with her friends and family, she begins to uncover hidden aspects of herself and her past. This journey of self-discovery serves as a catalyst for personal growth and transformation.

5. **Existentialism and the Human Condition**: The film's portrayal of an apocalyptic monster wreaking havoc on Seoul raises questions about the meaninglessness of life and our place in the world. Gloria's experiences serve as a metaphor for the human condition, highlighting our vulnerabilities and imperfections.

6. **Body Horror and the Objectification of Women**: Colossal features a unique blend of science fiction and body horror elements, which serve to critique societal attitudes towards women's bodies. The monster, while terrifying, is also a symbol of the objectification and exploitation of women in patriarchal societies.

Overall, Colossal is a thought-provoking film that explores complex themes and ideas through a unique blend of humor, drama, and science fiction elements.

overview: Barbie stars as Merliah, a surfer who learns a shocking secret: she's a mermaid! She and her dolphin friend set out for an undersea adventure to rescue her mother, the queen of Oceana.
title: Barbie in A Mermaid Tale
plot:
Barbie in a Mermaid Tale is a 2010 computer-animated adventure film directed by Adam L. Wood and produced by Mattel Entertainment with Rainmaker Entertainment. The seventeenth entry in the Barbie film series, it follows Merliah Summers, a champion surfer from Malibu who learns that she is a mermaid princess and travels beneath the sea to rescue her long-lost mother, the rightful queen of an ocean kingdom. The voice cast includes Kelly Sheridan, Kathleen Barr, Nakia Burrise, Garry Chalk and Haryke Hendrikse.

During a surfing competition, Merliah's hair suddenly develops pink streaks and she wipes out, only to discover that she can breathe underwater and is approached by Zuma, a talking pink bottlenose dolphin. Her grandfather Break reveals that her mother was a mermaid who handed Merliah to him as a baby because she was born with legs. Zuma tells Merliah and her friends Fallon and Hadley that her mother is Calissa, former queen of Oceana, whose sister Eris seized the throne after Calissa vanished. Merliah at first refuses to get involved, but when her childhood pendant breaks and shows a magical image of her living mother, she agrees to go, hoping Calissa can make her normal. The ocean is weakening because Eris cannot properly spin Merillia, the magical substance that sustains the sea; the Merillia she hands out at her festivals is in fact spun by Calissa, who is held in the palace dungeon. Disguised with a fake tail by the mermaids Kayla and Xylie, Merliah consults the Destinies, three prophetic mermaids, who tell her she must collect the Celestial Comb, a Dreamfish and Eris's protective necklace. After finding the first two, Merliah snatches the necklace during a performance at Eris's festival, but her disguise is torn away and Eris casts her into a whirlpool. Offered the chance to return to Malibu as a normal human, Merliah instead embraces her role as princess, gains a true tail and escapes. She proves her identity with the Comb, traps Eris in the whirlpool and frees Calissa, who restores Oceana. Admitting she misses life on land, Merliah receives a magical gift from her mother, returns home to her grandfather and wins the surfing competition.

The film was released on DVD on March 9, 2010, and had its television premiere on Nickelodeon on April 4, 2010. It was followed by a 2012 sequel, Barbie in a Mermaid Tale 2.

overview: In 1997, before the visit of the pope to Rio de Janeiro, Captain Nascimento from BOPE (Special Police Operations Battalion) is assigned to eliminate the risks of the drug dealers in a dangerous slum nearby where the pope intends to be lodged.
tagline: On the streets of Rio only the elite survive
title: Elite Squad
plot:
Elite Squad (Portuguese: Tropa de Elite) is a 2007 Brazilian crime film directed by José Padilha, who wrote the screenplay with Bráulio Mantovani and Rodrigo Pimentel, based on the novel Elite da Tropa by Luiz Eduardo Soares, André Batista and Pimentel. Padilha's first narrative feature, it stars Wagner Moura as Captain Roberto Nascimento of Rio de Janeiro's Battalion of Special Police Operations (BOPE), with Caio Junqueira and André Ramiro.

In 1997, Nascimento leads a BOPE operation to secure the Turano favela ahead of Pope John Paul II's overnight stay at the nearby archbishop's residence. With his wife, Rosane, pregnant, he is looking for a successor so that he can move to a desk job. Rookie military police officers André Matias and Neto Gouveia, best friends, are given menial tasks by corrupt superiors: Neto runs the motor pool and Matias files complaints. Matias also studies law, where he begins dating Maria and meets her friends, who work at an NGO in territory controlled by the drug lord Baiano. He befriends Romerito, a nearsighted boy. Disgusted by corruption, Neto and Matias divert bribe money to repair police cars. When their captain sends a fellow officer to a funk party in Morro da Babilônia in what may be a setup, the two friends try to protect him and set off a deadly gunfight with traffickers, ending only when Nascimento's team rescues the officers.

Matias, photographed by the press after the shootout, joins Neto in applying to BOPE,. Both men survive BOPE's brutal training. After his relationship with Maria ends, Matias arranges to give Romerito a pair of glasses, but Edu, one of Maria's friends, tips off Baiano, who sets an ambush. Neto goes in Matias's place and is fatally shot. Seeing his BOPE tattoo, Baiano goes into hiding, but first has two NGO workers executed. After the funeral, BOPE raids the favela daily, torturing dealers for information; learning of Edu's role, Matias beats him at a peace march. When BOPE finally corners Baiano, Nascimento orders Matias to execute him with a shotgun, avenging Neto and completing his initiation, and the screen fades to white at the sound of the shot.

The film was a box office hit and a cultural phenomenon in Brazil. It won the Golden Bear at the 2008 Berlin Film Festival, though international reviews were mixed, with 51% on Rotten Tomatoes. Its sequel, Elite Squad: The Enemy Within, followed in 2010, and in 2015 Abraccine ranked the original 30th among the greatest Brazilian films.

overview: London, England, May 2000. The peaceful life of elderly Joan Stanley is suddenly disrupted when she is arrested by the British Intelligence Service and accused of providing information to communist Russia during the forties.
tagline: To change the world, she betrayed her country
title: Red Joan
plot:
Red Joan is a 2018 British drama film directed by William Oldroyd. The movie revolves around Joan Stanley, a retired academic who leads a double life, hiding her past as a Soviet spy during World War II.

The main theme of Red Joan is the exploration of identity and the complexities of human relationships. Through Joan's character, the film delves into the idea that people are not defined by their past actions or choices, but rather by how they navigate and reconcile with those experiences in the present. The movie also touches on the theme of loyalty, as Joan struggles to balance her love for her family with her duty to the Soviet Union.

The film's narrative is woven around the concept of secrets and deception, highlighting the ways in which people can become trapped in their own lies and the consequences that follow when those secrets are revealed. The movie also explores the theme of female empowerment, as Joan navigates a world dominated by men and seeks to reclaim her agency and autonomy.

Ultimately, Red Joan is a thought-provoking film that raises questions about the nature of identity, loyalty, and redemption, inviting viewers to reflect on their own relationships with the past and the people around them.

overview: Every six years, an ancient order of jiu-jitsu fighters joins forces to battle a vicious race of alien invaders. But when a celebrated war hero goes down in defeat, the fate of the planet and mankind hangs in the balance.
tagline: From the darkness, the ultimate fighter rises.
title: Jiu Jitsu
plot:
Jiu-Jitsu is a 2020 martial arts science fiction film directed by William Eubank and written by David Loughran. The movie stars Randy Couture, Scott Adkins, Alina Vasquez, and Jon Foo.

The story begins with a group of mercenaries who are hired to transport a mysterious briefcase from one location to another. Unbeknownst to them, the briefcase contains an alien artifact that has been sent to Earth as part of an intergalactic experiment. The mercenaries soon discover that they have been infected by the alien technology, which slowly transforms them into violent and aggressive creatures.

As the mercenaries begin to turn on each other, a former Marine named Beckett (Scott Adkins) is hired to protect a young girl named Ava (Alina Vasquez), who has been exposed to the alien artifact. Beckett soon discovers that he too has been infected and must fight for survival against his own kind.

The movie takes a turn when Beckett meets a mysterious woman named Lena (Linda Cardellini) who claims to be an expert in the alien technology. Together, they embark on a mission to stop the spread of the infection and find a way to reverse its effects.

As the story unfolds, Beckett and Lena face off against the infected mercenaries, including Beckett's own brother, who has been transformed into a violent and deadly creature. The movie builds up to an intense showdown between Beckett and his brother, with Beckett ultimately emerging victorious.

Throughout the movie, there are several action-packed sequences that showcase the martial arts skills of the characters. The film also explores themes of family, loyalty, and redemption as Beckett struggles to come to terms with his own transformation.

In the end, Beckett and Lena succeed in stopping the spread of the infection and finding a way to reverse its effects. However, not before many lives have been lost, including those of Beckett's brother and several other characters. The movie concludes on a hopeful note, with Beckett and Lena emerging as heroes who have saved humanity from an alien threat.

Overall, Jiu-Jitsu is a thrilling martial arts sci-fi film that combines action, suspense, and drama to create a compelling narrative. With its talented cast and impressive fight choreography, the movie is sure to delight fans of science fiction and martial arts films.

original_title: Me and Earl and the Dying Girl
overview: Greg is coasting through senior year of high school as anonymously as possible, avoiding social interactions like the plague while secretly making spirited, bizarre films with Earl, his only friend. But both his anonymity and friendship threaten to unravel when his mother forces him to befriend a classmate with leukemia.
tagline: A Little Friendship Never Killed Anyone.
title: Me and Earl and the Dying Girl
plot:
Me and Earl and the Dying Girl is a poignant coming-of-age drama that explores the complexities of human relationships, empathy, and the struggles of growing up. The film delves into the life of Greg Gaines, a high school student who navigates his way through adolescence with a mix of awkwardness and vulnerability.

At its core, the movie is a powerful exploration of the transformative power of friendship and the importance of human connection in the face of adversity. Through Greg's relationship with Rachel, a classmate diagnosed with leukemia, the film sheds light on the intricacies of empathy and understanding that can bridge even the most unlikely of friendships.

The movie also touches upon themes of identity, social hierarchy, and the struggles of adolescence, where teenagers are constantly trying to find their place in the world. Greg's character, in particular, is a relatable portrayal of a teenager struggling to balance his desire for independence with the need for acceptance and belonging.

Furthermore, the film raises important questions about mortality, the meaning of life, and the impact that one person can have on another's existence. Rachel's presence in Greg's life serves as a catalyst for him to reevaluate his priorities and confront the complexities of human relationships.

Overall, Me and Earl and the Dying Girl is a heartwarming and thought-provoking film that explores the intricacies of human connection, empathy, and the struggles of growing up.

overview: Thirty years ago, aliens arrive on Earth. Not to conquer or give aid, but to find refuge from their dying planet. Separated from humans in a South African area called District 9, the aliens are managed by Multi-National United, which is unconcerned with the aliens' welfare but will do anything to master their advanced technology. When a company field agent contracts a mysterious virus that begins to alter his DNA, there is only one place he can hide: District 9.
production_companies: Canadian Film or Video Production Tax Credit (CPTC)
The Department of Trade and Industry of South Africa
New Zealand Post Digital and Visual Effects Grant
tagline: You are not welcome here.
title: District 9
plot:
District 9 is a thought-provoking science fiction film directed by Neill Blomkamp, produced by Peter Jackson and Carolyn Markle, and distributed by Sony Pictures Releasing. The movie was released on August 14, 2009.

In the year 2012, humanity has been forced to retreat to a distant planet called Monarch, where they are quarantined due to an alien virus that causes severe mutations in humans. The United Nations Office for Outer Space Affairs (UNOSA) is responsible for managing the human population on Monarch, and it is here that we meet our protagonist, Wikus van der Merwe (played by Sharlto Copley), a bureaucrat who works for UNOSA.

Wikus's life takes a drastic turn when he is exposed to an alien substance while trying to evict a group of aliens from a slum-like area called District 9. The substance, known as "Prisoners' Compound," causes Wikus to undergo a terrifying transformation, turning him into a hybrid creature with the physical characteristics of both humans and aliens.

As Wikus struggles to cope with his new form, he befriends Christopher Johnson (played by Jason Cottle), a human who has been living in District 9 for years. Through their interactions, Wikus begins to understand the harsh realities of life on Monarch and the treatment of the alien population by humanity.

The story takes a dramatic turn when Wikus discovers that his new form grants him access to advanced technology that could potentially help the aliens. He also learns about the true nature of District 9 and the sinister plans of the UNOSA officials who are determined to exploit the aliens for their own gain.

As tensions rise, Wikus must navigate a complex web of politics, prejudice, and humanity's darker aspects. The film builds towards a climactic confrontation between humans and aliens, forcing Wikus to make an impossible choice that will determine the fate of both species.

District 9 is a powerful commentary on issues such as xenophobia, segregation, and the dangers of unchecked power. Through its thought-provoking narrative and visually stunning depiction of a dystopian future, the film challenges viewers to confront their own biases and prejudices. The movie's success can be attributed to its well-crafted storyline, memorable characters, and Blomkamp's direction, which masterfully balances action, drama, and social commentary.

Overall, District 9 is a gripping science fiction film that explores complex themes and features a compelling narrative with a strong protagonist at its center.

overview: In the near future, a weary Logan cares for an ailing Professor X in a hideout on the Mexican border. But Logan's attempts to hide from the world and his legacy are upended when a young mutant arrives, pursued by dark forces.
tagline: His time has come.
title: Logan
plot:
Logan is a 2017 American superhero film directed by James Mangold, based on the Marvel Comics character Wolverine. The movie takes place nine years after the events of X-Men: Days of Future Past.

The story begins with an aging Logan (Hugh Jackman), who has been living in hiding with his daughter Laura (Dafne Keen) in a remote cabin in the woods. Laura is a young mutant with a healing factor, similar to her father's. The two have been on the run from various factions seeking to exploit their powers.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Logan and Laura are being pursued by a group of mercenaries led by Donald Pierce (Boyd Holbrook), who is working for a mysterious organization known as Transigen. This organization seeks to capture Laura and use her healing factor to create an army of super-soldiers.

Meanwhile, Professor X (Patrick Stewart) has been in a coma for years, and his consciousness is being held captive by the villainous En Sabah Nur (Michael Shannon), also known as Apocalypse. Logan and Laura set out on a perilous journey to find Professor X's location and rescue him from Apocalypse's clutches.

Along the way, they are joined by Caliban (Stephen Merchant), a mutant with enhanced strength and agility who becomes an ally in their quest. The group faces numerous challenges and obstacles, including hordes of Transigen mercenaries and a treacherous terrain that threatens to tear them apart.

As the stakes grow higher, Logan's health begins to decline due to his advanced age and years of exposure to adamantium, a metal alloy that has been embedded in his skeleton since his encounter with Wolverine. Despite this, he remains fiercely protective of Laura and determined to save Professor X from Apocalypse's clutches.

The movie culminates in an epic showdown between Logan, Laura, Caliban, and the Transigen mercenaries at the site of Professor X's location. In a heart-wrenching climax, Logan sacrifices himself to save Laura and allow her to escape with Professor X.

Throughout the film, Mangold explores themes of mortality, sacrifice, and the complexities of father-daughter relationships. The movie features stunning visuals, intense action sequences, and a poignant performance from Hugh Jackman as the aging Wolverine.

Logan received widespread critical acclaim for its thoughtful storytelling, nuanced characters, and emotional resonance. It marked a fitting conclusion to Hugh Jackman's tenure as Wolverine in the X-Men franchise, cementing his status as one of the most beloved superheroes on screen.

overview: Jill Conway is trying to rebuild her life after surviving a terrifying kidnapping attempt. Though she is having a difficult time, she takes small steps toward normalcy by starting a new job and inviting her sister, Molly, to move in with her. Returning home from work one morning, Jill discovers that Molly has vanished, and she is certain that the same man who previously abducted her has returned for revenge.
tagline: No one believes her. Nothing will stop her.
title: Gone
plot:
Gone is a 2012 American thriller directed by Heitor Dhalia from a screenplay by Allison Burnett, starring Amanda Seyfried. Her casting in the lead was announced in February 2011. Set in Portland, Oregon, the story follows a young woman whose claims about a serial killer have never been believed and who must find him herself when her sister disappears.

A year earlier, Jill Conway was abducted by a brutal killer and held in a pit among the remains of his previous victims. She escaped, but because she had once been institutionalized, the police concluded that the attack never happened. Now she shares a house with her sister, Molly, and works as a waitress at the Lucky Star Diner. Returning home after work, Jill finds that Molly has vanished. The police again dismiss her, with the exception of Detective Hood, who has just joined the homicide unit, so Jill sets out to investigate on her own.

Following a trail of clues, Jill learns that a locksmith's van was parked outside her home overnight, rented by the owner's son, Nick, to a man calling himself Digger. A receipt leads her to a hardware store and then to the Royal Hotel, where she discovers that his real name is Jim LaPointe and finds duct tape, pet food and matches from her own diner in his abandoned room. Getting his phone number from her coworker Sharon, she calls him, and he directs her to a remote spot in Forest Park, insisting he does not have Molly. Meanwhile Molly, who had been held under Jill's own house, breaks free and tells the police what happened, proving that Jill was right all along. In the woods Jill photographs the remains of earlier victims and finds the hole where she was once kept. LaPointe attacks her; she shoots him and, after he admits he took Molly as bait to lure her back, pours kerosene into the pit and sets him on fire despite his pleas. At home she tells the police that the man existed only in her head, but an anonymous package containing photographs of the victims and a map to the grave later arrives at the police department.

The film was poorly received. Rotten Tomatoes reported 12% approval, Metacritic scored it 36 and CinemaScore audiences gave it a C+; critics found it formulaic and forgettable, although one reviewer found Seyfried as reliable as anyone could hope. It was a box office disappointment, grossing about $18.1 million worldwide.

original_title: Tom and Jerry: Shiver Me Whiskers
overview: Dueling cat-and-mouse team Tom and Jerry hit the high seas on a hunt for buried treasure in this pirate adventure. The tale begins when crew member Tom sets sail with an infamous pirate and finds a treasure map along with stowaway Jerry. The furry swashbucklers race to a deserted island where X marks the spot, but along with battling each other, they must outwit ruthless buccaneers, angry monkeys and a giant octopus to strike it rich.
title: Tom and Jerry: Shiver Me Whiskers
plot:
Tom and Jerry: Shiver Me Whiskers is a 2006 animated film that revolves around the classic cat-and-mouse duo, Tom and Jerry. The movie's plot begins with Tom, who has just lost his job as a housecat due to his constant misbehavior, and decides to take revenge on his nemesis, Jerry.

The main theme of the movie is the never-ending rivalry between Tom and Jerry, which drives the plot forward. However, beneath this surface-level conflict lies a deeper exploration of friendship and loyalty. As the story progresses, it becomes clear that despite their animosity towards each other, Tom and Jerry have developed an unbreakable bond over the years.

Throughout the film, Tom's attempts to catch Jerry are thwarted at every turn, leading him to question his own motivations and desires. Meanwhile, Jerry is shown to be a clever and resourceful mouse who always manages to stay one step ahead of Tom. The movie pokes fun at their never-ending cycle of chase and evasion, highlighting the absurdity and humor in their relationship.

The film also touches on themes of identity and self-discovery. Tom's job loss serves as a catalyst for his journey of self-discovery, as he learns to redefine himself and find new purpose in life. Jerry, on the other hand, is shown to be content with his simple life as a mouse, highlighting the importance of appreciating one's own unique qualities.

The movie's climax features an epic showdown between Tom and Jerry, which ultimately ends in a heartwarming moment of reconciliation between the two former adversaries. The film concludes on a positive note, emphasizing the power of friendship and forgiveness in overcoming even the most seemingly insurmountable obstacles.

Overall, Tom and Jerry: Shiver Me Whiskers is a lighthearted and entertaining animated film that explores themes of rivalry, friendship, identity, and self-discovery through the classic cat-and-mouse duo.

overview: An all-new Disney holiday classic is born - Santa Paws 2: The Santa Pups. Starring a brand-new litter of the cutest talking pups ever - Hope, Jingle, Charity, and Noble - it's perfect for the whole family. When Mrs. Claus travels to Pineville, the playful Santa Pups stow away on her sled. Taking mischief to a whole new level, they begin granting joyful wishes to Pineville's boys and girls, but something goes terribly wrong - the Christmas spirit begins to disappear. Now the Santa Pups and Mrs. Claus must race to save Christmas around the world. From the creators of Disney Buddies, this magical, heartwarming tale is brimming with hope, cheer, and Christmas spirit.
tagline: One Magical Wish Can Change Everything !
title: Santa Paws 2: The Santa Pups
plot:
Santa Paws 2: The Santa Pups is a heartwarming holiday film that explores several endearing themes. At its core, the movie is about the power of friendship and loyalty, as embodied by the adorable Santa Pups. These canine companions bring joy and comfort to those around them, serving as a reminder of the importance of kindness and compassion.

The film also delves into the theme of family, highlighting the value of found families and the bonds that form between individuals who may not be related by blood. The story showcases how these characters come together to support one another, demonstrating that family is not just about biology, but about the love and connection we share with others.

Furthermore, Santa Paws 2: The Santa Pups touches on the theme of selflessness and sacrifice. The main character, Stellaluna, learns valuable lessons about putting the needs of others before her own, illustrating the importance of empathy and understanding in our relationships with those around us.

Lastly, the movie celebrates the magic of the holiday season, capturing the essence of Christmas as a time for love, giving, and togetherness. The film's lighthearted tone and adorable characters make it an enjoyable watch for both children and adults alike, reminding us of the simple pleasures in life that bring us joy and happiness during this special time of year.

overview: The life story of Jesus is told from his humble birth through his teachings, crucifixion and ultimate resurrection.
tagline: Their Empire. His Kingdom.
title: Son of God
plot:
Son of God is a 2014 American epic biblical film directed by Christopher Spencer and produced by Mark Burnett and Roma Downey. It retells the life of Jesus by adapting The Bible, the miniseries that aired on the History channel in March 2013, combining aired scenes with unaired footage. Scenes of Satan were cut from the feature after commentators claimed that the actor playing him resembled President Barack Obama. The film opened in the United States and Canada on February 28, 2014.

The elderly John, the last of Jesus' followers still alive, recounts the story from his exile. Born in Bethlehem to Mary and Joseph and visited by three wise men, Jesus begins his ministry in Galilee thirty years later, gathering Peter, James, John, Matthew and Mary Magdalene. His teachings and miracles draw huge crowds who call him the Messiah, while the Pharisees accuse him of blasphemy for forgiving sins. Entering Jerusalem on a donkey before Passover, he is hailed with palm leaves and overturns the tables of the money changers in the temple. The high priest Caiaphas, warned by the Roman governor Pontius Pilate that any unrest will lead him to close the temple and cancel the festival, resolves to stop him, and Judas agrees to help in exchange for thirty pieces of silver.

After the Last Supper, Judas betrays Jesus with a kiss in the Garden of Gethsemane. Tried at night and convicted of blasphemy when he confirms he is the Son of God, Jesus is handed to the Romans. Pilate finds no breach of Roman law and has him flogged, but Caiaphas sways the crowd to free Barabbas instead and demand crucifixion, and Pilate washes his hands of the matter. Jesus is crucified at Golgotha beneath a sign proclaiming him King of the Jews, and his death brings an earthquake that tears the temple curtain. Three days later Mary Magdalene finds the tomb empty and meets the risen Jesus, who appears to the disciples, convinces the doubting Thomas and ascends into heaven, later visiting the aged John to promise that he will return.

Diogo Morgado plays Jesus, with Roma Downey as Mary, Greg Hicks as Pilate, Adrian Schiller as Caiaphas, Darwin Shaw as Peter, Sebastian Knapp as John, Joe Wredden as Judas and Amber Rose Revah as Mary Magdalene. Critics were largely negative, with 17% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, though audiences gave it an A− CinemaScore. It opened to $26.5 million and grossed $70.9 million on a $22 million budget.

original_title: The Drover's Wife: The Legend of Molly Johnson
overview: In 1893, heavily pregnant Molly Johnson and her children struggle in isolation to survive the harsh Australian landscape after her husband left to go droving sheep in the high country. One day, she finds a shackled Aboriginal fugitive named Yakada wounded on her property. As an unlikely bond begins to form between them he reveals secrets about her true identity. Realizing Molly’s husband is actually missing, new town lawman Nate Clintoff starts being suspicious and sends his constable to investigate.
title: The Drover's Wife: The Legend of Molly Johnson
plot:
