The Drover's Wife: The Legend of Molly Johnson is a 2022 Australian Western drama film directed by Rachel Perkins. The movie is based on the 1929 novel "The Drover's Wife" by A.B. Facey, but it also incorporates elements from the life of Molly Johnson, an Aboriginal woman who was part of the famous Burke and Wills expedition in 1860.

The story begins with Molly (played by Jessica Mauboy), a young Aboriginal woman living on a station in Western Australia. She is married to Drover (played by Damon Herriman), a rugged and experienced stockman. The couple's life is marked by hardship, isolation, and the struggles of their community.

As the story unfolds, we see Molly's daily life, her relationships with her family and friends, and her deep connection to the land and its people. However, the arrival of Burke (played by Damon Herriman) and Wills (played by Kris McQuade), two British explorers on a journey across Australia, sets off a chain of events that will change Molly's life forever.

Burke and Wills are seeking to cross the continent from east to west, but their expedition is fraught with danger, and they face numerous challenges along the way. Molly becomes embroiled in their story, and her interactions with the explorers have significant consequences for both herself and those around her.

Throughout the film, Perkins explores themes of colonialism, racism, and the complex relationships between Aboriginal people and European settlers. The movie also delves into the personal struggles of its characters, particularly Molly, who must navigate the challenges of being a woman in a patriarchal society.

As the story reaches its climax, Molly finds herself at the center of a tragic event that will have far-reaching consequences for her community. The film's ending is both poignant and powerful, highlighting the resilience and strength of Aboriginal women in the face of adversity.

Overall, The Drover's Wife: The Legend of Molly Johnson is a powerful and moving film that sheds light on a significant period in Australian history. With its strong performances, stunning cinematography, and thought-provoking themes, it is a must-see for anyone interested in Westerns or Aboriginal culture.

original_title: La Nuit a dévoré le monde
overview: After waking up to find himself all alone in an apartment where a massive party was being held the night before, Sam is immediately forced to face a terrifying reality: the living dead have invaded the streets of Paris.
title: The Night Eats the World
plot:
The Night Eats the World (French: La nuit a dévoré le monde) is a 2018 French English-language zombie film directed by Dominique Rocher, who wrote it with Jérémie Guez and Guillaume Lemans, based on Pit Agarman's novel of the same name. Anders Danielsen Lie stars as Sam, a man caught alone in a Paris overrun by zombies, with Golshifteh Farahani and Denis Lavant in supporting roles.

Sam, a musician, goes to his ex-girlfriend Fanny's apartment during a party to collect some tapes. After being bumped by a guest, he gets a nosebleed and passes out in the office, sleeping through sounds of chaos outside. The next morning the apartment is trashed and bloodied, and in the stairwell he finds Fanny and others transformed into zombies who charge at him. The zombies, fast and utterly silent, react in swarms to any sight or sound. A shotgun blast through the floor reveals that a man downstairs killed his infected wife and then himself, and Sam takes the gun, seals the building's doors and explores the apartments one by one, gathering supplies. He keeps a zombified elderly man, Alfred, trapped in the lift and talks to him, and plays music on equipment he finds.

As time passes, Sam grows lonely and unstable. After nearly dying trying to catch a stray cat, he fires at it in anger. Winter brings cold and cuts the water supply, and he survives on rainwater and a makeshift fireplace. Noticing the streets have emptied, he pounds a drum kit and screams, drawing a horde that almost climbs onto the balcony. One night he fires through his bedroom door and wounds a woman, Sarah, who has survived by crossing rooftops with a grappling hook. She later urges him to leave, warning that he will otherwise die or go mad, but he then finds her dead from the gunshot, revealing that their conversations were hallucinations. Among her belongings is a camera with photos of her family and of Sam on the roof. Deciding to leave, he burns his tapes and locks Alfred in an apartment, but the smoke sets off a fire alarm and zombies storm the building. Sam fights his way to the roof, swings across to the next building and gazes over the endless Paris skyline, where he briefly hears what may be another survivor.

The film premiered at the Angers Film Festival on 13 January 2018 and was released in France on 7 March. It holds 87% on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus praised its atmosphere and character focus, and a Metacritic score of 50.

overview: Christmas Eve in New York, and the lonely divorced publisher, Rose Collins, needs a miracle to improve the health of her mother, interned in a hospital with Alzheimers. She feels sorry for another patient and meets his visitor. Meanwhile, Nina Vasquez breaks her engagement with her beloved fiancé Mike due to his suffocating jealousy, but misses him. Mike is stalked by a stranger, bartender Artie Venzuela. The poor Jules arranges to spend Christmas Eve in the hospital, where he spent the best Christmas of his life when he was a teenager. The lives of some of these characters cross with others along the night.
tagline: Miracles are closer than you think
title: Noel
plot:
Noel is a 2004 American Christmas drama directed by Chazz Palminteri and written by David Hubbard. Its ensemble cast includes Penélope Cruz, Susan Sarandon, Paul Walker, Alan Arkin and Daniel Sunjata, with Robin Williams in an uncredited role. The film follows several intersecting stories that unfold on Christmas Eve in New York City,.

Rose Collins, a divorced publisher, struggles to care for her mother, who has Alzheimer's disease. As she considers suicide on a riverbank, a former priest named Charlie Boyd saves her, and they spend the night together at her apartment. Charlie admits he has lost his faith, but the next morning he tells Rose that it has been restored by a telepathic conversation with her mother, who wants Rose to move on with her life. Furious, Rose throws him out.

A young couple, Nina Vasquez and Mike Riley, are close to breaking up because of Mike's growing jealousy, and when he attacks one of Nina's platonic friends, she leaves him. At her family's Christmas celebration she meets Rose, who has ended up at the house through a series of coincidences, and the two women go to a bar. Meanwhile, an elderly waiter, Artie Venizelos, searches for his late wife every Christmas and becomes convinced that Mike is her reincarnation, making advances toward him. When Artie collapses and is taken to the hospital, Mike learns from a colleague that Artie once committed manslaughter in a jealous rage and that his wife then died in a car crash that was a suicide. Mike takes this as a sign that he must conquer his own jealousy. A depressed young man, Jules Calvert, whose only happy memory is a Christmas party in a hospital when he was a teenager, lets a criminal break his hand in hope of reliving it, only to learn that the past cannot be recovered. Rose, ashamed of how she treated Charlie, returns to the hospital and finds that he has been in a coma for some time and has no visitors. Across the hall, her mother has finally started eating thanks to Dr. Baron, and Rose agrees to have dinner with him.

Noel premiered at the 2004 Toronto International Film Festival and was acquired by Convex Group, owner of the Flexplay disposable DVD technology, which gave it a "trimultaneous" release in cinemas, on self-expiring Flexplay discs and on TNT within the same month. Critics largely dismissed it as sentimental; it holds a 28% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, and Dave Kehr of The New York Times called it a heap of platitudes.

overview: Rocky and Bullwinkle have been living off the finances made from the reruns of their cartoon show. Boris and Natasha somehow manage to crossover into reality and team up with Fearless Leader, an evil criminal turned media mogul with some evil plans up his sleeve. Rocky and Bullwinkle must stop the three of them before they wreak havoc.
tagline: This summer it's not the same old bull.
title: The Adventures of Rocky & Bullwinkle
plot:
The Adventures of Rocky and Bullwinkle is a 2000 American adventure comedy that combines live action and animation, directed by Des McAnuff and written by Kenneth Lonergan, based on Jay Ward's animated series The Adventures of Rocky and Bullwinkle and Friends. The animated heroes share the screen with live actors playing the villains: Robert De Niro, who also co-produced, as Fearless Leader, Jason Alexander as Boris Badenov and Rene Russo as Natasha Fatale. Randy Quaid and Piper Perabo co-star, June Foray returns as the voice of Rocky, and Keith Scott voices Bullwinkle and the narrator.

Since their show was canceled in 1964, Rocky the Flying Squirrel and Bullwinkle J. Moose have lived gloomily in a deforested Frostbite Falls; Rocky can no longer fly, and their narrator lives with his mother. Their old enemies, out of power since the Cold War ended, tunnel into a Hollywood studio and trick executive Minnie Mogul into green-lighting a film, which brings them into the real world in live-action form. Six months later they run RBTV, "Really Bad Television", a New York cable network designed to brainwash Americans into electing Fearless Leader president. FBI director Cappy von Trapment sends rookie agent Karen Sympathy to recruit Rocky and Bullwinkle, and she summons them into reality.

Boris and Natasha pursue the heroes with the CDI, or "Computer-Degenerating Imagery", a device that can trap cartoon characters inside the Internet. Karen is jailed but escapes with help from a lovestruck guard, Ole. At Bullwinkle's alma mater, Wossamotta U, the villains stage an honorary degree ceremony to kill him, but Rocky regains his power of flight and saves his friend. A starstruck judge later dismisses charges against them, and the trio escapes in a rickety biplane. Rocky carries Karen to New York, where they are captured, as Fearless Leader begins brainwashing the nation. Bullwinkle crash-lands at the White House, where his natural stupidity makes him immune to the broadcasts, and Cappy e-mails him to the studio to disrupt Fearless Leader's address. The villains are captured, and Bullwinkle accidentally triggers the CDI, turning them back into cartoons and banishing them to the Internet. Rocky and Bullwinkle get their own network, and they return to a replanted Frostbite Falls.

The film earned $35.1 million worldwide and was considered a box office failure. Critics found it faithful to the cartoon but unfunny, giving it 42% on Rotten Tomatoes and 36 on Metacritic.

overview: A young tech worker takes a job at a powerful Internet corporation, quickly rises up the company's ranks, and soon finds herself in a perilous situation concerning privacy, surveillance and freedom. She comes to learn that her decisions and actions will determine the future of humanity.
tagline: Knowing is good. Knowing everything is better.
title: The Circle
plot:
The Circle is a 2017 American techno-thriller directed by James Ponsoldt, who wrote the screenplay with Dave Eggers from Eggers's 2013 novel. Emma Watson stars as Mae Holland, alongside Tom Hanks, John Boyega, Karen Gillan, Ellar Coltrane, Patton Oswalt, Glenne Headly and Bill Paxton. Fully financed by Image Nation Abu Dhabi with Walter Parkes and Laurie MacDonald, it premiered at the Tribeca Film Festival on April 26, 2017, and was released two days later by STXfilms and EuropaCorp. It was released after Paxton's death in February 2017 and was Headly's last film released before she died that June.

Through her friend Annie, call-center temp Mae lands a customer support job at the Circle, a powerful tech and social media company, hoping to help her parents, particularly her father, who has multiple sclerosis. CEO Eamon Bailey unveils SeeChange, tiny cameras that can be placed anywhere to stream live video, and Mae rises quickly as she embraces the company's culture of constant sharing. Ty Lafitte, the creator of its TrueYou network, confides that his invention has escaped his control. When Mae posts a photo of a deer-antler chandelier made by her old friend Mercer, online abuse forces him to cut her off.

After capsizing while kayaking alone at night, Mae is rescued by the Coast Guard thanks to SeeChange cameras, and the experience persuades her to become the first employee to go "completely transparent", broadcasting her life around the clock. The exposure damages her relationships with her parents and Annie. She proposes requiring a Circle account to vote, and later demonstrates a program that finds a fugitive child murderer within minutes. When the crowd asks it to find Mercer, Circle users and a drone chase him down a road until he crashes off a bridge and dies. Grieving but still convinced of connection, Mae returns to the company and, with Ty's help, exposes the private email accounts of Bailey and the chief operating officer, Tom Stenton, insisting that no one is exempt from transparency.

Critics were largely negative, with 15% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, a Metacritic score of 43 and a D+ CinemaScore; reviewers found it repetitive and its villainous company too obvious. It grossed $45.5 million worldwide against an $18 million budget, opening fifth in North America with $9 million, yet it still became Ponsoldt's highest-grossing feature.

overview: After his wife falls under the influence of a drug dealer, an everyday guy transforms himself into Crimson Bolt, a superhero with the best intentions, though he lacks for heroic skills.
tagline: Shut up, crime!
title: Super
plot:
Super is a 2010 American black comedy film directed by Adam Reed and written by Reed and Paul Scheer. The movie follows the story of Frank (played by Rainn Wilson), a mild-mannered office worker who becomes obsessed with saving the world from an alien invasion.

The main themes of Super include:

1. **Obsession vs. Sanity**: Frank's fixation on saving the world from aliens is portrayed as both admirable and disturbing, highlighting the blurred lines between heroism and madness.
2. **Identity Crisis**: As Frank transforms into his superhero alter ego, "Super," he struggles to reconcile his mundane office life with his newfound sense of purpose, leading to a crisis of identity.
3. **The Power of Imagination**: The film showcases the importance of imagination in shaping our perceptions of reality and ourselves. Super's fantasies about saving the world serve as a coping mechanism for Frank's feelings of inadequacy.
4. **Toxic Masculinity**: Frank's transformation into Super can be seen as a manifestation of toxic masculinity, where he seeks to prove himself through aggressive and violent means.
5. **The Absurdity of Heroism**: The movie pokes fun at traditional superhero tropes, highlighting the absurdity and illogic of saving the world from an alien invasion.

Overall, Super is a dark comedy that explores themes of identity, obsession, and the human desire for meaning and purpose.

original_title: Rise of the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: The Movie
overview: When a mysterious stranger arrives from the future with a dire warning, Leo is forced to rise and lead his brothers, Raph, Donnie, and Mikey in a fight to save the world from a terrifying alien species.
title: Rise of the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: The Movie
plot:
Rise of the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: The Movie is a 2022 animated action-comedy film produced by Nickelodeon Movies. The movie serves as a reboot of the TMNT franchise and offers a fresh take on the classic characters.

The story begins with four brothers, Leonardo (voiced by Brady Noon), Donatello (voiced by Omar Miller), Michelangelo (voiced by Kyle Mooney), and Raphael (voiced by Bowen Yang), who are living in New York City. The brothers are mutated turtles from the sewers of New York, trained in the art of ninjutsu by their sensei Splinter (voiced by Josh Brener).

The movie starts with the Turtles trying to live a normal life on land, but they struggle to fit in and find their place in society. However, their lives are disrupted when Shredder (voiced by John Cena), the leader of the Foot Clan, returns from the dead and seeks revenge against the Turtles.

Shredder is aided by his loyal ally, Baxter Stockman (voiced by Ryan Kiera Armstrong), a mad scientist who creates an army of robotic ninjas to take down the Turtles. The Turtles must band together to stop Shredder's evil plans and save their city from destruction.

Throughout the movie, the Turtles face various challenges as they try to balance their ninja training with their everyday lives. They also encounter new allies, including April O'Neil (voiced by Maddie Capaldi), a young journalist who becomes entangled in the Turtles' adventures.

As the story unfolds, the Turtles discover that Shredder's plan is not just about revenge, but also about harnessing the power of the "Ninja Code," an ancient energy source that could grant him immense power. The Turtles must use their skills and teamwork to stop Shredder and his minions before it's too late.

The movie features plenty of action-packed sequences, humor, and heart, making it a fun and entertaining ride for fans of the TMNT franchise. The animation is vibrant and colorful, bringing the characters and world to life in a way that will appeal to both old and new fans.

In the end, the Turtles successfully defeat Shredder and his robotic ninjas, saving their city from destruction. Along the way, they learn valuable lessons about teamwork, friendship, and being true to themselves. The movie concludes with the Turtles returning to their sewers, ready to face whatever adventures come their way next.

Overall, Rise of the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: The Movie is a fun and action-packed adventure that offers a fresh take on the classic TMNT characters. With its vibrant animation, humor, and heart, it's a must-see for fans of the franchise and anyone looking for a fun animated movie experience.

overview: Ryota Nonomiya is a successful businessman driven by money. He learns that his biological son was switched with another child after birth. He must make a life-changing decision and choose his true son or the boy he raised as his own.
tagline: At what point does a father truly become a father?
title: Like Father, Like Son
plot:
Like Father, Like Son is a Japanese drama film of 2013 from writer, director and editor Hirokazu Kore-eda, giving Masaharu Fukuyama his first part as a father. Machiko Ono plays his wife Midori, with Keita Ninomiya as their son Keita, Shōgen Hwang as Ryūsei, Yōko Maki and Lily Franky as Yukari and Yūdai Saiki, and Jun Fubuki, Isao Natsuyagi, Jun Kunimura and Kirin Kiki in supporting roles.

Ryōta Nonomiya is a successful architect so absorbed by his career that he neglects Midori and their son Keita. One day Midori tells him that the hospital where Keita was born urgently wants to see them. There they learn that their biological son, Ryūsei, was switched with Keita at birth, and once DNA tests confirm the mistake, they face an agonising choice: keep the boy they have raised or exchange him for the child who is theirs by blood. They meet the other family, the Saikis, a small-town couple who lack Ryōta's money and ambition but understand far better the bond between parents and children, and for the first time see photographs of Ryūsei. After a series of meetings, the families begin swapping the boys for weekend visits. Since the Saikis have two other children, Ryōta tactlessly proposes that he and Midori raise both boys, deeply offending them.

The couples sue the hospital, and in court a nurse confesses that she switched the babies on purpose: newly married and struggling with her stepchildren, she envied the Nonomiyas' happiness. The statute of limitations protects her from prosecution. The families finally agree to exchange the boys permanently, but all four parents grieve for the sons they have lost, and both children withdraw, until Ryūsei runs away back to the Saikis and Ryōta has to fetch him home. When the nurse sends money as an apology, Ryōta goes to return it and confront her, only for her stepson to step in to defend her. Slowly Ryōta and Midori begin to bond with Ryūsei. Then, looking through his camera, Ryōta finds a series of pictures Keita secretly took of him, mostly asleep, and breaks down in tears. Visiting the Saikis, he follows the fleeing Keita, apologises for failing him as a father, and the two reconcile before both families go into the house together.

The film premiered in competition at the Cannes Film Festival in May 2013, where it received a long standing ovation and won the Jury Prize. It topped the Japanese box office for two weeks and passed three billion yen, and critics praised it highly, with 87% on Rotten Tomatoes.

overview: The story of a teenager, Richard Wershe Jr., who became an undercover informant for the police during the 1980s and was ultimately arrested for drug-trafficking and sentenced to life in prison.
tagline: Hustler. Informant. Kingpin. Legend.
title: White Boy Rick
plot:
White Boy Rick is a biographical crime drama film that delves into the life of Richard Wershe Jr., a young man who became embroiled in a world of crime and violence at a tender age. The movie explores the themes of family dynamics, loyalty, and the corrupting influence of power.

At its core, White Boy Rick is a story about the devastating consequences of growing up too fast and being forced to navigate a treacherous landscape of crime and addiction. Richard's father, Wershe Sr., is a small-time crook who introduces his son to the world of narcotics trafficking, setting him on a path that will ultimately lead to chaos and destruction.

The film also examines the complex relationships within Richard's family, particularly between him and his father. Their bond is rooted in a deep-seated loyalty and trust, but it is also tainted by the harsh realities of their lifestyle. As Richard becomes more entrenched in the world of crime, he begins to question the morality of his actions and the true nature of his relationship with his father.

One of the most striking aspects of White Boy Rick is its portrayal of the cyclical nature of violence and addiction. Richard's involvement in crime leads him down a path of self-destruction, but it also serves as a means of survival and escape from the trauma of his childhood. The film suggests that this cycle can be difficult to break, even for those who seek to leave it behind.

Ultimately, White Boy Rick is a powerful exploration of the human condition, one that grapples with the complexities of family, loyalty, and redemption. Through Richard's story, the film sheds light on the darker aspects of American society, revealing a world where the lines between right and wrong are often blurred and the consequences of one's actions can be devastating.

overview: The Grand Budapest Hotel tells of a legendary concierge at a famous European hotel between the wars and his friendship with a young employee who becomes his trusted protégé. The story involves the theft and recovery of a priceless Renaissance painting, the battle for an enormous family fortune and the slow and then sudden upheavals that transformed Europe during the first half of the 20th century.
tagline: A murder case of Madam D. With enormous wealth and the most outrageous events surrounding her sudden death!
title: The Grand Budapest Hotel
plot:
The Grand Budapest Hotel is a 2014 American comedy-drama film written and directed by Wes Anderson. The film stars Ralph Fiennes, Tony Revolori, F. Murray Abraham, Willem Dafoe, Jude Law, Tilda Swinton, Adrien Brody, Edward Norton, Jeff Goldblum, and Saoirse Ronan.

The story begins in 1932, with Gustave H (Ralph Fiennes), a charming and flamboyant concierge at the famous Grand Budapest Hotel in the fictional Republic of Zubrowka. Gustave is known for his exceptional hospitality skills and his ability to make guests feel like royalty. He befriends Zero Moustafa (Tony Revolori), a young lobby boy who becomes his most trusted assistant.

The plot takes a dramatic turn when one of Gustave's wealthy elderly clients, Madame Celine (Tilda Swinton), dies under mysterious circumstances. Gustave is accused of murdering her and flees the country with a priceless painting, "Boy with Apple," which he had been entrusted to guard. Zero follows him on his journey, determined to clear his friend's name.

As they travel through Europe, they encounter a series of misadventures, including a run-in with the villainous Dmitri (Adrien Brody), who is also after the painting. Along the way, Gustave and Zero form an unlikely bond, with Zero learning valuable lessons about loyalty, friendship, and the importance of following one's heart.

The story takes a dramatic turn when Gustave and Zero are arrested by the authorities in the Republic of Zubrowka. They escape and continue their journey, eventually finding themselves in the midst of a war between the Republic of Zubrowka and its neighboring country, the Empire of Austria-Hungary.

As the war escalates, Gustave and Zero find themselves on the run once again, this time with the help of a group of rebels. They embark on a perilous journey to clear Gustave's name and recover the stolen painting.

The film's climax features an action-packed sequence in which Gustave and Zero infiltrate the Empire's headquarters, where they engage in a series of clever disguises and narrow escapes. In the end, Gustave is able to clear his name and recover the painting, but not before facing a series of challenges that test his courage and wit.

The film concludes with an elderly Zero visiting Gustave in his final days, where he recounts their adventures and shares stories about their friendship. The film ends on a poignant note, as Zero reflects on the lessons he learned from Gustave and the importance of holding onto memories and experiences.

Throughout the film, Wes Anderson's signature visual style and attention to detail are on full display, with intricate production design, vibrant colors, and a memorable soundtrack that adds to the film's whimsical charm. The Grand Budapest Hotel is a visually stunning and engaging film that explores themes of friendship, loyalty, and the power of storytelling.

overview: A former Secret Service agent grudgingly takes an assignment to protect a pop idol who's threatened by a crazed fan. At first, the safety-obsessed bodyguard and the self-indulgent diva totally clash. But before long, all that tension sparks fireworks of another sort, and the love-averse tough guy is torn between duty and romance.
tagline: Never let her out of your sight. Never let your guard down. Never fall in love.
title: The Bodyguard
plot:
The Bodyguard is a romantic thriller film released in 1992, directed by Mick Jackson and starring Whitney Houston and Kevin Costner. The movie follows the story of two individuals from different worlds who find love in the midst of danger.

The film begins with Rachel Marron (Whitney Houston), a famous pop singer, preparing for her concert tour. Unbeknownst to her, she has been receiving threatening letters and gifts from an unknown stalker. Desperate for protection, Rachel hires two bodyguards, Frank Farmer (Kevin Costner) and his partner, Sy Spector (Gary Kemp). 

Initially, the two men are skeptical of their new assignment but soon realize that they need to take Rachel's safety seriously. As they begin to work together, a strong bond develops between them, and it becomes clear that there is more to Frank than meets the eye.

As the tour progresses, Rachel starts to open up to Frank about her fears and insecurities. Meanwhile, she also begins to develop feelings for him, which complicates their professional relationship. The stalker's threats escalate, putting both Rachel and Frank in grave danger.

Throughout the film, the tension builds as Frank becomes increasingly protective of Rachel. He discovers that the stalker is none other than her former lover, Sy Spector, who has been seeking revenge against Rachel for leaving him. 

In a thrilling climax, Frank confronts Sy at Rachel's concert venue, and in the ensuing fight, Sy is killed. The film ends with Rachel and Frank sharing a romantic moment, as they finally acknowledge their feelings for each other.

The Bodyguard was a commercial success, grossing over $410 million worldwide. It also received positive reviews from critics, who praised the chemistry between Houston and Costner. The movie's soundtrack, featuring Whitney Houston's hit single "I Will Always Love You," became one of the best-selling albums of all time.

Overall, The Bodyguard is a classic romantic thriller that explores themes of love, danger, and protection. With its memorable performances, catchy soundtrack, and suspenseful plot, it remains a beloved film to this day.

original_title: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind
overview: Joel Barish, heartbroken that his girlfriend underwent a procedure to erase him from her memory, decides to do the same. However, as he watches his memories of her fade away, he realises that he still loves her, and may be too late to correct his mistake.
tagline: You can erase someone from your mind. Getting them out of your heart is another story.
title: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind
plot:
Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind is a 2004 American romantic drama film written by Charlie Kaufman and directed by Michel Gondry. The movie stars Jim Carrey and Kate Winslet as Joel Barish, a man who undergoes a procedure to erase his memories of his ex-girlfriend Clementine (played by Kirsten Dunst).

The story begins with Joel and Clementine in the midst of a tumultuous relationship. They are constantly arguing and fighting, but they also share moments of deep love and connection. After a particularly painful fight, Joel decides that he wants to erase all memories of Clementine from his mind.

Joel visits a company called Lacuna, Inc., which offers this memory-erasing procedure. The process involves a team of technicians who use a special device to extract the memories from Joel's brain and store them on a computer. However, as the procedure begins, it becomes clear that Joel is not ready to let go of his feelings for Clementine.

As the movie progresses, we see flashbacks of Joel and Clementine's relationship through a non-linear narrative structure. We witness their first meeting, their courtship, and their eventual breakup. Through these flashbacks, we see the highs and lows of their relationship, including moments of tenderness, passion, and heartbreak.

Meanwhile, Joel begins to experience strange side effects from the memory-erasing procedure. He starts to see fragmented images of Clementine in his mind, and he becomes increasingly obsessed with trying to hold on to these memories. As the procedure continues, Joel's perception of reality becomes distorted, and he begins to question whether he is truly erasing his memories or just suppressing them.

Throughout the movie, Kaufman explores themes of love, loss, and memory. He raises questions about the nature of relationships and how we process our emotions. The film also delves into the concept of nostalgia and how it can be both a bittersweet and a comforting experience.

As the story unfolds, Joel's memories of Clementine become more vivid and intense. He starts to see her in his dreams, and he becomes convinced that she is still alive. In a poignant and emotional climax, Joel realizes that he cannot erase his memories of Clementine, and he begins to accept that their relationship was worth fighting for.

The movie ends with Joel sitting alone in a park, watching as the Lacuna technicians work on erasing his memories of Clementine. However, just as they are about to complete the procedure, Joel's emotions overwhelm him, and he breaks down in tears. The camera pans out, showing Joel's face contorted in anguish, as the sound of Clementine's voice echoes in his mind.

In the final shot, we see a montage of fragmented images from Joel and Clementine's relationship, set to a haunting melody. These images are intercut with shots of Joel sitting alone, lost in thought. The movie ends on a hopeful note, suggesting that even though memories can be painful, they can also be a source of comfort and connection.

Overall, Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind is a beautifully crafted film that explores the complexities of love and memory. With its unique narrative structure and poignant performances, it has become a modern classic of American cinema.

overview: European mercenaries searching for black powder become embroiled in the defense of the Great Wall of China against a horde of monstrous creatures.
tagline: 1700 years to build. 5500 miles long. What were they trying to keep out?
title: The Great Wall
plot:
The Great Wall is a 2016 monster film directed by Zhang Yimou, his first English-language feature, from a screenplay by Carlo Bernard, Doug Miro and Tony Gilroy and a story by Max Brooks, Edward Zwick and Marshall Herskovitz. An American and Chinese co-production, it stars Matt Damon, Jing Tian, Pedro Pascal, Willem Dafoe and Andy Lau. Filming began in Qingdao in March 2015, and the film premiered in Beijing on December 6, 2016, before release in China on December 16 and in the United States through Universal Pictures in February 2017.

During the reign of Emperor Renzong, European mercenaries searching for gunpowder are attacked by a monster north of the Great Wall. Only the Irishman William Garin and the Spaniard Pero Tovar survive, cutting off its arm, and they are captured by the Nameless Order, the army that guards the Wall against the Tao Tei, alien creatures that arrived with a meteorite and attack every sixty years. When a horde storms the Wall a week early, the two mercenaries, freed by Ballard, an Englishman who came east twenty-five years before, fight brilliantly and win the Order's respect. After General Shao is killed, Commander Lin takes command, and Strategist Wang notices that the magnet Garin carries seems to subdue the beasts.

Garin helps capture a Tao Tei alive to prove the theory, but an imperial envoy takes it to the capital. The attacks prove to be a diversion while the creatures dig a tunnel through the Wall's base. Tovar and Ballard steal black powder and knock Garin out when he tries to stop them, and Garin is jailed until Lin frees him. When the captive creature awakens in the capital and summons the horde, Lin, Garin, Wang and the young soldier Peng race there in hot-air balloons. Peng and Wang die buying time, and Garin throws the magnet into the horde, opening a gap for Lin's explosive spear to kill the queen, after which the rest of the horde dies. Rather than accept gunpowder as a reward, Garin asks to take the captured Tovar home with him.

Damon and Pascal play the mercenaries. Reviews were mixed to poor, with 35% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, although some critics admired its inventive action and visual style. It grossed $334.9 million worldwide against a $150 million budget, including $170.9 million in China, but was expected to lose about $75 million and was considered a box-office bomb.

overview: Into the world of the Emperor Penguins, who find their soul mates through song, a penguin is born who cannot sing. But he can tap dance something fierce!
tagline: WARNING: May Cause Toe-Tapping.
title: Happy Feet
plot:
Happy Feet is a 2006 animated musical comedy-drama film produced by Kennedy Miller Productions, Village Roadshow Pictures, and Warner Bros. Feature Animation. The movie follows the story of Mumble, an Emperor Penguin who lives in Antarctica.

The film begins with Mumble, a young Emperor Penguin, born to parents Norma Jean and Memphis. However, Mumble is different from his peers as he has two left feet instead of the traditional right-left flipper arrangement. This makes it difficult for him to dance like other penguins, which is an essential part of their mating rituals.

As Mumble grows up, he struggles to find his place among his colony. He tries to fit in by mimicking the movements of the other penguins, but his clumsiness and lack of coordination make it impossible. The elders of the colony view Mumble's uniqueness as a curse, and they shun him.

One day, Mumble meets Gloria, an Adelie Penguin who is different from the rest of her colony due to her love for singing. Gloria becomes Mumble's friend and confidant, and together they explore the world beyond their colony. They discover that humans are polluting the ocean, causing a decline in fish populations, which affects the penguins' food supply.

Mumble decides to embark on a journey to find the source of the problem and save his colony. He sets out with Gloria and a group of penguin friends, including Ramón, a wise-cracking Rockhopper Penguin who becomes Mumble's mentor. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, including treacherous ice caves, fierce predators, and rival colonies.

As Mumble navigates this new world, he learns to accept himself and his uniqueness. He discovers that his two left feet are not a curse but a gift, allowing him to tap dance in a unique style that captivates the humans. The humans, led by a kind-hearted scientist named Adelie, work together with Mumble's colony to find a solution to the pollution problem.

The climax of the film features an epic dance battle between Mumble and his rival, Ramón, which showcases their respective tap dancing skills. In the end, Mumble's unique style wins over the humans, and they work together to clean up the ocean and restore the fish populations.

The movie concludes with Mumble returning home as a hero, celebrated by his colony for his bravery and creativity. He finds love with Gloria, and they start a family of their own. The film ends on a hopeful note, emphasizing the importance of self-acceptance, friendship, and working together to overcome challenges.

Overall, Happy Feet is a heartwarming story about embracing individuality and finding one's true purpose. The movie features stunning animation, catchy musical numbers, and lovable characters that make it a delight for audiences of all ages.

overview: Gonzo is challenged to spend one night in The Haunted Mansion on Halloween night.
tagline: Cue the light(ning)!
title: Muppets Haunted Mansion
plot:
Muppets Haunted Mansion is a 2021 American comedy horror film directed by Justin Simien and written by Jason Segel, Nicholas Stoller, and Lee Eisenberg. The movie takes place in the classic Disney theme park attraction, The Haunted Mansion.

The story begins with Dr. Terminus (played by Eddie Murphy), a ghostly con artist who has been haunting the mansion for decades. He is determined to scare away all the living visitors and make it his own personal playground. However, his plans are foiled when he discovers that a new family, the Muppets, have moved into the mansion.

The Muppets, consisting of Kermit the Frog (played by Matt Vogel), Miss Piggy (played by Eric Jacobson), Fozzie Bear (played by Peter Linz), and Gonzo (played by Dave Goelz), are initially excited to explore their new home. However, they soon realize that it's not as empty as they thought.

As the family tries to settle in, they begin to experience strange occurrences and ghostly encounters. Dr. Terminus sees an opportunity to scare them away and starts to manipulate events to make it seem like the mansion is haunted by malevolent spirits.

Meanwhile, Kermit becomes convinced that there's a real ghost haunting the mansion, which he believes is the spirit of his late friend, Rizzo the Rat (played by Steve Whitmire). As the story unfolds, the Muppets work together to uncover the truth behind Dr. Terminus' sinister plans and put an end to his schemes.

Throughout the movie, there are plenty of humorous moments, clever references to The Haunted Mansion attraction, and exciting ghostly encounters. The film also features a number of celebrity cameos, including Tiffany Haddish, Rosario Dawson, and Wanda Sykes.

As the Muppets delve deeper into the mystery, they discover that Dr. Terminus' plan is not just about scaring them away but also about using their energy to fuel his own ghostly powers. In a thrilling climax, Kermit and his friends must work together to outsmart Dr. Terminus and put an end to his evil plans.

In the end, the Muppets succeed in defeating Dr. Terminus and restoring peace to the mansion. The movie concludes with the family enjoying their new home and looking forward to many more adventures together.

Overall, Muppets Haunted Mansion is a fun and spooky comedy that brings a fresh take to the classic Disney theme park attraction. With its talented voice cast, clever writing, and exciting plot twists, it's sure to delight both fans of The Muppets and horror enthusiasts alike.

overview: Because of her past, 17-year-old Rio lives her days filling the emptiness in her heart with money--until one day, she meets a university professor named Kouki and falls in love.
title: My Rainy Days
plot:
My Rainy Days (Japanese: Tenshi no Koi, literally "Angel's Love") is a 2009 Japanese romantic drama written and directed by Yuri Kanchiku in her directorial debut, adapted from the cell phone novel of the same name. Model Nozomi Sasaki plays a seventeen-year-old schoolgirl in her first leading film role, with Shosuke Tanihara and Hikaru Yamamoto in the cast.

Rio Ozawa, a beautiful and calculating high school student, earns money with her friends Maki and Miho through compensated dating and extortion. After defending her naive classmate Tomoko from a bully, Naoko, Rio draws Tomoko into the clique and into the scheme, though Naoko is secretly Rio's lover. When a photo shop mixes up Rio's prints with those of another Ozawa, she meets Kouki, a withdrawn 35-year-old history professor, to swap them, and he suddenly faints. Visiting him in the hospital, Rio grows close to him, quits her schemes, ends things with Naoko and asks him to tutor her. When she scores 99 on a history test, Kouki agrees to a date, and he later kisses her. Rio does not know that he had surgery for a brain tumor three years earlier that did not remove it completely, and to spare her, he abruptly withdraws from her life.

Naoko returns to school and tries to stab Tomoko, but Rio shields her. On the roof, Naoko reveals that she was repeatedly raped by her mother's boyfriend and killed him, then jumps to her death after declaring her love for Rio. Rio confesses that she had ordered Naoko to bully Tomoko, and the two drift apart until Rio collapses from stress and they reconcile. Kouki's cousin Kaori gives Rio his new address, and Rio tells him that she was raped and had an abortion three years earlier, turning to prostitution to avoid being hurt again. Kouki faints once more, and Rio learns of the tumor. He admits that meeting her made him wish for more time, and he agrees to surgery despite the risk to his memory, telling her he loves her. After Rio graduates, she finds him on a rainy day; he does not seem to remember her but walks her to the station under his umbrella, then returns to shelter her again, and she embraces him.

The film premiered as a special screening at the 22nd Tokyo International Film Festival and opened in Japan on 7 November 2009. It grossed about $1.09 million across four countries. Reviews were generally positive; The Hollywood Reporter said it avoided conventional tearjerking pitfalls.

overview: A multi-part documentary about the making of the Jurassic Park trilogy. Each part walks through the making of part of one of the films, including the hurricane during the shooting of the first film, and how advances in CGI for Jurassic Park helped change the world of special effects forever. All interviews for these retrospective documentaries come with comments from Spielberg, Johnston, Neill, Dern, Goldblum, the effects crews, the child actors, and Peter Stormare. This documentary is broken into five parts: Dawn of a New Era (25 min) Making Prehistory (20 min), the Next Step in Evolution (15 min), and the Third Adventure (25 min), Finding the Lost World (28 min), and Something Survived (16 min).
title: Return to Jurassic Park
plot:
Return to Jurassic Park is a 2011 American documentary series directed by Laurent Bouzereau. Produced for Universal, it was created as the main new bonus feature of the Jurassic Park Ultimate Trilogy, the 2011 box set that brought Jurassic Park, The Lost World: Jurassic Park and Jurassic Park III to Blu-ray for the first time. Running about two hours in total, it is divided into six high-definition parts spread across the set's three discs, two devoted to each film: Dawn of a New Era, Making Prehistory and The Next Step in Evolution for the first film, Finding the Lost World and Something Survived for the second, and The Third Adventure for the third. The retrospective interviews feature Steven Spielberg, Jurassic Park III director Joe Johnston, actors Sam Neill, Laura Dern, Jeff Goldblum and Peter Stormare, former child stars Joseph Mazzello and Ariana Richards, and members of the effects crews.

Dawn of a New Era covers the making of the original film and the direction the filmmakers first intended to take before realising that computer-generated imagery was the way to go, along with recollections of working with Stan Winston's effects team, surviving a real hurricane during the shoot and working with Spielberg. Making Prehistory looks more closely at the filming, particularly the animatronic Tyrannosaurus and Velociraptors, the origins of the dinosaur sounds and the animatics, while The Next Step in Evolution discusses the computer-generated images and digital composites created by Industrial Light & Magic, the sound effects and the score, and Spielberg's input while he was in the middle of filming Schindler's List. Finding the Lost World explains that a sequel was always at the back of Spielberg's mind, and that once novelist Michael Crichton had published a follow-up novel the filmmakers chose its much darker direction. Something Survived focuses on the sequel's technical side, including its ending, which was essentially written into the story on a whim. The Third Adventure has cast and crew reminiscing about working with Johnston, shooting on location and on soundstages, the practical effects and the choice of the Spinosaurus as the new villain.

High-Def Digest's M. Enois Duarte considered the series exhaustive, singling out the effects segment as a great watch for fans and the final installment as really interesting, especially for admirers of the third film.

overview: Wallace and Gromit have run out of cheese, and this provides an excellent excuse for the duo to take their holiday to the moon, where, as everyone knows, there is ample cheese.
title: A Grand Day Out
plot:
A Grand Day Out is a stop-motion animated comedy film produced by Aardman Animations, released in 1989 (not 1990). The movie follows the adventures of Wallace and Gromit, two lovable characters created by Nick Park.

The main themes of A Grand Day Out include:

1. Friendship: The bond between Wallace and Gromit is at the heart of the story. Their friendship is put to the test as they embark on a journey to the moon in search of cheese.
2. Curiosity and Exploration: Wallace's insatiable curiosity and desire for adventure drive the plot of the film. He and Gromit's exploration of the moon leads to unexpected consequences.
3. Resourcefulness and Ingenuity: The duo's resourcefulness and ingenuity are showcased as they use their skills and creativity to overcome obstacles and achieve their goals.
4. Humor and Satire: A Grand Day Out is known for its witty humor, satire, and parody of British culture, particularly the stereotypical image of the eccentric inventor.

The film's plot follows Wallace and Gromit's journey from their home in Wigan to the moon, where they encounter a group of alien creatures who are also searching for cheese. The movie features plenty of comedic moments, clever wordplay, and heartwarming interactions between the two main characters.

Overall, A Grand Day Out is a charming and entertaining film that showcases the unique blend of humor, satire, and adventure that has become synonymous with Aardman Animations.

overview: His only friend called him 'the man from nowhere'... Taesik, a former special agent becomes a loner after losing his wife in a miserable accident and lives a bitter life running a pawnshop. He only has a few customers and a friend named Somi, a little girl next door. As Taesik spends more and more time with Somi, he gets attached to her. Then Somi is kidnapped by a gang, and as Taesik tries to save Somi by becoming deeply associated with the gang his mysterious past is revealed.
tagline: Nothing to lose, nothing to compromise.
title: The Man from Nowhere
plot:
The Man from Nowhere is a 2010 South Korean action thriller film directed by Lee Won-suk and produced by CJ Entertainment. 

The movie follows the story of Dong-goo (played by Joong-ho Bae), a former special forces operative who has retired to a quiet life in Seoul. However, his peaceful existence is disrupted when he meets a young girl named Soo-jin (played by Kim Hye-seon) and her mother, who are being bullied by a local gangster.

Dong-goo's past comes back to haunt him as the gangster, Sung-nyeon (played by Joong-sang Lee), is revealed to be his former comrade-in-arms. Sung-nyeon has become a ruthless crime lord and will stop at nothing to eliminate Dong-goo, who he sees as a threat to his power.

As Dong-goo tries to protect Soo-jin and her mother, he must also confront his own troubled past and the reasons why he retired from special forces. Along the way, he teams up with a local cop, Detective Park (played by Kim Sung-kyun), who helps him take down Sung-nyeon's gang.

The movie's plot is driven by Dong-goo's quest for revenge against Sung-nyeon, but it also explores themes of redemption and the consequences of violence. As Dong-goo navigates his way through the underworld of Seoul, he must confront the demons of his past and make difficult choices about how far he is willing to go to protect those he cares about.

Throughout the movie, Lee Won-suk's direction creates a tense and suspenseful atmosphere, with plenty of action sequences that showcase Joong-ho Bae's impressive physical abilities. The supporting cast adds depth and complexity to the story, particularly Kim Hye-seon as Soo-jin, who brings a sense of vulnerability and determination to her character.

The ending of The Man from Nowhere is both intense and emotionally resonant, as Dong-goo faces off against Sung-nyeon in a final showdown. While the outcome is far from certain, the movie's conclusion provides a sense of closure for Dong-goo's story, but also leaves room for interpretation about his future.

Overall, The Man from Nowhere is a gripping and thought-provoking thriller that explores themes of redemption, violence, and the human condition. With its tense action sequences, complex characters, and emotional depth, it is a must-see for fans of Korean cinema and action movies in general.

original_title: The School for Good and Evil
overview: Best friends Sophie and Agatha navigate an enchanted school for young heroes and villains — and find themselves on opposing sides of the battle between good and evil.
tagline: There are two sides to every story.
title: The School for Good and Evil
plot:
The School for Good and Evil is a 2022 American fantasy film directed by Paul Feig, who wrote the screenplay with David Magee, based on Soman Chainani's 2013 novel. Sophia Anne Caruso and Sofia Wylie star as Sophie and Agatha, two best friends from the village of Gavaldon who are carried off to a magical academy that trains the heroes and villains of fairy tales. The cast also includes Kerry Washington as Professor Clarissa Dovey, Dean of the School for Good; Charlize Theron as Lady Leonora Lesso, Dean of the School for Evil; Laurence Fishburne as the aged School Master; Michelle Yeoh as Professor Emma Anemone; and Jamie Flatters as Prince Tedros.

The school was founded by twin brothers Rhian and Rafal to train heroes, known as Evers, and villains, known as Nevers, until Rafal, tired of evil always losing, attacked his brother with blood magic and both apparently fell from a cliff. Years later, the fairy-tale-obsessed Sophie dreams of becoming a princess, while the sceptical Agatha is content with village life. When Sophie tries to run away and Agatha follows to stop her, a giant creature called a stymph snatches them both, but to their dismay Agatha is dropped at the School for Good and Sophie at the School for Evil. The School Master agrees to let Sophie switch only if she proves herself an Ever by winning true love's kiss, and she sets her sights on Tedros, the son of King Arthur. Both girls struggle in class, though Dovey sees in Agatha's empathy the makings of a true princess. Rafal secretly watches over Sophie, and Lesso sees in her a chance for Evil to win at last. Under Rafal's influence Sophie transforms in looks and personality and becomes a leader among the Nevers. When a trial is held to settle the scandal of an Ever and a Never together, Sophie fails to protect Tedros and Agatha saves him instead, leading the prince to reject Sophie and turn to Agatha. Persuaded that her friend is her enemy, Sophie accepts Rafal's blood magic, disables the deans, crashes the Evers' Ball and goads Tedros into an attack that breaks the rule that Good defends and Evil attacks and sets off a battle between the schools.

After years in development, the project moved to Netflix in 2017 and was filmed in Northern Ireland in 2021. Released by Netflix on October 19, 2022, it was the service's most-viewed film in its opening week, but critics found it derivative despite praising its cast and visuals; it holds a 37% Rotten Tomatoes rating.

overview: On the eve of her college graduation, Natalie's life diverges into two parallel realities: one in which she becomes pregnant and must navigate motherhood as a young adult in her Texas hometown, the other in which she moves to LA to pursue her career. In both journeys throughout her twenties, Natalie experiences life-changing love, devastating heartbreak and rediscovers herself.
tagline: Wherever life takes you, let love guide you.
title: Look Both Ways
plot:
Look Both Ways is a 2022 American romantic comedy-drama directed by Wanuri Kahiu and written by April Prosser. Lili Reinhart stars as Natalie Bennett, a college student whose life splits into two parallel realities, with Danny Ramirez as her friend Gabe, David Corenswet as Jake, Aisha Dee as Cara, Nia Long as the animator Lucy Galloway, and Luke Wilson and Andrea Savage as Natalie's parents.

In her senior year at the University of Texas, Natalie sleeps with her friend Gabe, and both agree not to make a big deal of it. On graduation night she feels ill, and her best friend Cara buys her pregnancy tests. From that moment the film follows two versions of her life side by side.

When the test is positive, Natalie moves back in with her disappointed parents, who are unimpressed by Gabe's ambitions as a musician but urge her to keep pursuing animation. After their daughter, Rosie, is born, Natalie refuses Gabe's offer to live together and encourages him to date, later regretting it when he becomes involved with Miranda. While visiting Cara in Los Angeles, Natalie rushes home after a worrying call, and learns that Gabe has proposed to Miranda. Pouring herself into her art, she achieves a breakthrough and appears on a panel at South by Southwest in Austin with Lucy, discussing a comic inspired by Rosie. After watching his band play, Natalie learns that Gabe has broken off his engagement because he loves her, and they talk seriously about their future.

When the test is negative, Natalie moves to Los Angeles with Cara and lands a job as Lucy's assistant, where she falls for her colleague Jake, an aspiring producer. Their relationship falters when he takes a year-long job in Nova Scotia. Lucy criticizes Natalie's portfolio as unoriginal and encourages her to find her own voice, so Natalie quits and returns home feeling like a failure. Then her short film is accepted at South by Southwest. In Austin she runs into Gabe, now married, and jokes about how different life would have been had her test been positive. Jake surprises her by attending her screening, and Lucy invites her to reconnect. In both realities, Natalie returns to the bathroom where she took the test and reassures herself that things worked out.

Netflix released the film on August 17, 2022. Reviews were mixed to positive, with 62% on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 49; Variety praised its sentiments about risk and fate while faulting its execution.

overview: The story of an ancient war that is reignited when a young farmhand unwittingly opens a gateway between our world and a fearsome race of giants. Unleashed on the Earth for the first time in centuries, the giants strive to reclaim the land they once lost, forcing the young man, Jack into the battle of his life to stop them. Fighting for a kingdom, its people, and the love of a brave princess, he comes face to face with the unstoppable warriors he thought only existed in legend–and gets the chance to become a legend himself.
tagline: Prepare for a giant adventure
title: Jack the Giant Slayer
plot:
Jack the Giant Slayer is a 2013 American fantasy adventure film directed by Bryan Singer and written by Darren Lemke, David Koepp, and Christopher McQuarrie. The movie is based on the classic fairy tale "Jack and the Beanstalk" but offers a unique twist on the original story.

The film begins in medieval England, where King Braemar (Ian McShane) is preparing for war against the giant Riddoch (Craig Parkinson). However, before the battle can begin, the king's son Jack (Nicholas Hoult) is kidnapped by the giant. The only way to rescue Jack is to climb up a magical beanstalk that grows in the castle gardens.

Jack sets out on his journey, accompanied by a young woman named Isabelle (Ewan McGregor), who claims to be a skilled warrior. As they ascend the beanstalk, they encounter various obstacles and creatures, including giant spiders and treacherous terrain.

Upon reaching the top of the beanstalk, Jack and Isabelle discover that Riddoch is not just a mindless beast but a complex character with his own motivations and backstory. The giant's true intention is to steal the magical golden harp, which has the power to heal any wound.

As Jack navigates the giant's lair, he also discovers that Riddoch was once a human king who was cursed by an evil sorcerer. The curse transformed him into a giant, and he has been searching for a way to break it ever since.

Meanwhile, back in England, King Braemar is facing his own struggles as he prepares for war against the giants. He must also contend with his own son's disappearance and the pressure from his advisors to launch an attack on the giants before they can be defeated.

As Jack and Isabelle continue their journey, they face numerous challenges and obstacles, including a treacherous path that leads them deeper into the giant's lair. Along the way, Jack also discovers that he has a special connection to the magical harp and that it holds the key to breaking Riddoch's curse.

In the end, Jack and Isabelle successfully defeat Riddoch and shatter the curse that has been cast upon him. The golden harp is recovered, and King Braemar is able to launch a successful attack on the giants. However, the movie ends with a twist: Jack returns home as a hero, but he also carries with him the knowledge of his own destiny and the secrets of the magical world.

Overall, Jack the Giant Slayer offers a unique take on the classic fairy tale, exploring themes of identity, redemption, and the power of music. The film features stunning visuals, impressive action sequences, and a talented cast, making it a must-see for fans of fantasy adventure movies.

overview: A pair of best friends set out to have a legendary week-long summer vacation with the help of cheap rosé and a group of eclectic friends.
tagline: It takes a match to light a fire.
title: Fire Island
plot:
Fire Island is a 2022 American romantic comedy film directed by Andrew Ahn and written by Joel Kim Booster, who also stars. Inspired by Jane Austen's Pride and Prejudice, it follows a group of gay friends on their annual vacation to the New York island of the title, where romance is complicated by class divisions. Booster plays Noah, modelled on Elizabeth Bennet, with Bowen Yang as his best friend Howie, Conrad Ricamora as the lawyer Will, James Scully as the doctor Charlie, Margaret Cho as the friends' "house mother" Erin, Matt Rogers as Luke, Tomás Matos as Keegan, Torian Miller as Max, Nick Adams as Cooper and Zane Phillips as Dex.

Noah and his friends take the ferry to Fire Island Pines for their yearly week at Erin's house, only to learn that she must sell it and that this will be their last summer together. They meet Charlie and his wealthy circle, including Will and Cooper, and Charlie and Howie are drawn to each other, so Noah makes it his mission to see Howie find romance. At a party at Charlie's house the friends feel looked down upon, and Noah overhears Will dismissing him. Noah flirts with Dex and invites him to a dinner partly because Will dislikes him, yet Noah and Will unexpectedly connect over books. A night of partying in Cherry Grove ends in a public confrontation, and Noah sees Charlie kissing his ex, Rhys. Noah and Will argue bitterly, and Howie, hurt, tells Noah that their experiences are not the same simply because both are gay and Asian. A letter from Will apologizes for his early remarks and explains that Dex once hurt someone close to him. As Charlie announces he is leaving with Rhys, Noah and Will grow closer, and when Dex posts a video of himself and Luke online without Luke's consent, Will helps Noah force him to remove it. Learning that Charlie still has feelings for Howie, Noah and his friends race after Howie as he leaves the island, and Noah and Will finally kiss and agree to give their relationship a try.

Produced and distributed by Searchlight Pictures, the film was released on Hulu on June 3, 2022. Reviews were positive, with a 94% Rotten Tomatoes rating and praise for its cast and fresh take on Austen, and it ranked among the most streamed films in the week of June 11.

overview: The dialogue-less film follows the major life stages of a castaway on a deserted tropical island populated by turtles, crabs and birds.
title: The Red Turtle
plot:
The Red Turtle is a beautifully crafted film that explores the human condition through the story of a shipwrecked sailor who finds himself stranded on a deserted island. The movie delves into the complexities of loneliness, survival, and the transformative power of nature.

As the sailor struggles to come to terms with his isolation, he begins to form a connection with the red turtle that inhabits the island. This unlikely friendship serves as a catalyst for the sailor's emotional journey, forcing him to confront his inner demons and re-evaluate his relationship with the world around him.

Throughout the film, the director weaves together themes of solitude, self-discovery, and the cyclical nature of time. The island, with its rugged landscape and serene atmosphere, becomes a character in its own right, serving as a symbol of the untamed power of nature that can both inspire and intimidate humanity.

As the sailor's story unfolds, it becomes clear that his journey is not just about survival, but also about finding meaning and purpose in a world that seems devoid of human connection. The film ultimately suggests that even in the most desolate of environments, there is always the potential for growth, transformation, and redemption.

The Red Turtle is a poignant and visually stunning film that invites viewers to reflect on their own relationship with the natural world and the complexities of the human experience.

overview: A father is imprisoned after committing a brutal revenge crime. During his confinement he must adapt to a new life of abuse, including injury and humiliation by guards and other prisoners.
title: Dark Blood
plot:
Dark Blood, originally released in Colombia as Perros ("Dogs"), is a Colombian-Argentine prison drama film directed by Harold Trompetero, who wrote the screenplay with Jeiver Pinto and Gerardo Pinzón, and produced by Mauricio Brunetti through Patagonia Films and Oasis Films. It stars John Leguizamo as Misael, with Álvaro Rodríguez, Adriana Barraza, Ramiro Meneses, Hernán Méndez and María Nela Sinisterra. After premiering at Bogotá's IndieBo independent film festival in 2016, it opened in Colombian cinemas in March 2017, and it later circulated internationally under its English title, Dark Blood, released in 2021; in the United Kingdom it was distributed on streaming by Alarm Pictures. It runs 83 minutes.

Misael (Leguizamo), an ordinary man, is locked up in the squalid jail of his small town after killing a man in a crime of passion, believing he was avenging the abuse of one of his children. After he strikes Cáceres (Rodríguez), the head of the guards, on arrival, the guard becomes fixated on him, and Misael is systematically beaten, tortured, humiliated and sexually abused by guards and fellow inmates. Blamed and forgotten by his loved ones, he is tormented above all by his separation from his family and his need for his son to understand why he did what he did. A lawyer (Barraza) takes up his case, and during a conjugal visit his wife (Sinisterra) confesses her infidelity and tells him he was wrong about the man he killed. In his loneliness Misael finds tenderness only in Sarna, a stray dog that lives in the prison and becomes his one faithful companion.

Trompetero, known mainly for popular comedies, said the project took more than seven years and was a cathartic, personal departure for him. It was filmed in an abandoned prison in Facatativá, near Bogotá, after research in prisons such as La Picota, and used former guerrilla and paramilitary fighters as extras. Oswaldo Osorio of the Cinéfagos blog at El Colombiano called it a strong, aggressive film of dirty realism that explores human misery through a forgotten man, praising the use of Sarna as a leitmotif. Carlos Giraldo of El Sabanero X rated it four out of five, calling it sordid, cruel and pessimistic and praising Barraza, but noted that some viewers considered its portrayal of the homosexual guard homophobic.

overview: Five puppies are shocked to find out that their parents, Buddy and Molly, have been abducted and face obstacles while trying to rescue them.
tagline: They Shoot. They Score. They TALK!
title: Air Buddies
plot:
Air Buddies is a heartwarming film that revolves around the adventures of a group of adorable and lovable golden retriever puppies. The movie explores several themes, primarily centered around family, friendship, and loyalty.

At its core, Air Buddies is a story about the unbreakable bond between humans and animals. The film showcases the special connection between the main characters, particularly the puppies, and their human caregivers. As the puppies navigate various challenges and obstacles, they demonstrate remarkable resilience, empathy, and affection towards those around them.

One of the primary themes of Air Buddies is the importance of family. The movie highlights the value of having a loving and supportive family unit, where everyone works together to overcome difficulties. The film also emphasizes the significance of adopting pets from shelters, as it promotes responsible pet ownership and the joy that comes with sharing one's life with a furry companion.

Another significant theme in Air Buddies is the concept of loyalty and friendship. The puppies form strong bonds with each other, and their relationships are built on trust, empathy, and mutual support. As they face various challenges, they demonstrate remarkable loyalty to one another, showcasing the power of canine camaraderie.

The film also touches upon themes of responsibility, hard work, and perseverance. The main characters learn valuable lessons about taking care of others, working together as a team, and overcoming obstacles through determination and effort.

Overall, Air Buddies is a delightful film that celebrates the beauty of human-animal relationships, the importance of family, and the power of loyalty and friendship.

overview: James Bond returns as the secret agent 007 to battle the evil organization SPECTRE. Bond must defeat Largo, who has stolen two atomic warheads for nuclear blackmail. But Bond has an ally in Largo's girlfriend, the willowy Domino, who falls for Bond and seeks revenge.
tagline: Sean Connery is James Bond 007
title: Never Say Never Again
plot:
Never Say Never Again is a James Bond film directed by Irvin Kershner, released in 1983 by Warner Bros. Pictures. The movie is an adaptation of Ian Fleming's novel Thunderball, with some significant changes and additions.

The story begins with James Bond (Sean Connery), a secret agent working for the British Secret Intelligence Service (MI6). Bond is sent to the Bahamas to investigate the theft of two nuclear warheads from a US Navy submarine. He soon discovers that the stolen warheads are being sold on the black market, and he must track down the buyer.

Bond's investigation leads him to Emilio Largo (Klaus Maria Brandauer), a wealthy and mysterious Italian businessman who is suspected of being involved in the theft. As Bond delves deeper into the case, he discovers that Largo is actually working for SPECTRE, a terrorist organization led by Ernst Stavro Blofeld.

Bond's mission becomes more complicated when he falls in love with Domino Derval (Karin Hahn), a beautiful and alluring woman who is also being pursued by Largo. As Bond navigates the complex web of intrigue, he must use his skills and cunning to stay one step ahead of Largo and SPECTRE.

The plot thickens as Bond discovers that Largo's true intention is to use the stolen warheads to hold the world hostage and gain control over the global economy. With the help of his ally, Felix Leiter (Jeroen Krabbé), a CIA agent, Bond must stop Largo and SPECTRE before it's too late.

The film features many memorable scenes, including a thrilling underwater chase sequence and a dramatic showdown between Bond and Largo at the villain's lair. The movie also explores themes of loyalty, duty, and the moral complexities of espionage.

In the end, Bond successfully foils Largo's plan, but not before he suffers a serious injury that leaves him hospitalized. As he recovers, Bond reflects on the personal costs of his work as a spy and the sacrifices he must make for the greater good.

Never Say Never Again received mixed reviews from critics at the time of its release, with some praising Connery's performance and others criticizing the film's tone and style. However, over the years, the movie has developed a cult following and is now widely regarded as one of the best Bond films.

overview: The Sea Inside is about Spaniard Ramón Sampedro, who fought a 30-year campaign to win the right to end his life with dignity. It is the story of Ramón’s relationships with two women: Julia a lawyer who supports his cause, and Rosa, a local woman who wants to convince him that life is worth living.
tagline: Sensitive Drama About a Polemic Theme
title: The Sea Inside
plot:
The Sea Inside is a Spanish drama film of 2004 co-written, directed, co-produced, scored and edited by Alejandro Amenábar, based on the true story of Ramón Sampedro, a man left quadriplegic by a diving accident who campaigned for decades for the right to end his life. Javier Bardem stars as Ramón, with Belén Rueda as the lawyer Julia, Lola Dueñas as Rosa, Mabel Rivera as his sister-in-law Manuela, Celso Bugallo as his brother José, Tamar Novas as his nephew Javier and Josep Maria Pou as Father Francisco.

Ramón, now in his fifties, has spent more than a quarter of a century paralysed from the neck down after a diving accident in his youth. Unable to take his own life and unwilling to involve his loved ones, who under Spanish law could be charged with murder or assisting a suicide, he fights in the courts for the right to die. Since his mother's death he has been cared for by Manuela. His elder brother José opposes his wish, while Manuela and her son Javier support him. Through Gené, who works for a right-to-die organisation, he meets Julia, a lawyer suffering from a degenerative illness who takes up his case. As he tells her about his past, he explains that he sees no dignity in living paralysed. Rosa, a local woman who has read about him, comes to persuade him that life is worth living; rebuffed, she apologises on her part-time radio show and keeps visiting with her children, and they become friends. Drawn to both women, Ramón insists he belongs to death.

Julia reads his memoir and urges him to publish it, and he dreams of flying from his bed to meet her on the beach, but she suffers a stroke and must relearn to walk, so they correspond by letter. A quadriplegic priest, Father Francisco, comes to argue for life, but since Ramón refuses to be carried downstairs, a church boy shuttles their arguments up and down until Manuela, angered, sends the priest away. Julia, whose illness will only worsen, tells Ramón she plans to die herself but wants to help him first. With Javier, Ramón designs a wheelchair so he can attend court, but his appeal is rejected. In the end each of his friends performs a small act toward his death, too slight for any one to be convicted, and Ramón films himself as he drinks a glass laced with cyanide.

The film won the Grand Jury Prize at the Venice Film Festival and the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film. Critics praised Bardem's transfixing performance, giving the film 85% on Rotten Tomatoes.

overview: Ramona is a little girl with a very big imagination and a nose for mischief. Her playful antics keep everyone in her loving family on their toes, including her older sister Beezus, who's just trying to survive her first year of high school. Through all the ups and downs of childhood, Ramona and Beezus learn that anything's possible when you believe in yourself and rely on each other.
tagline: A Little Sister Goes A Long Way.
title: Ramona and Beezus
plot:
Ramona and Beezus is a heartwarming film that explores the complexities of sibling relationships, family dynamics, and the struggles of growing up. The movie delves into the world of Ramona Quimby, a spirited and imaginative young girl who often finds herself in humorous misadventures.

At its core, Ramona and Beezus is a story about the unbreakable bond between sisters. The film showcases the unique dynamic between Ramona and her older sister Beezus, highlighting their contrasting personalities and the ways in which they support each other despite their differences. Through their interactions, the movie reveals the importance of empathy, understanding, and communication in sibling relationships.

The film also touches on themes of family love and acceptance. The Quimby household is portrayed as a loving but imperfect one, where parents are well-meaning but sometimes clueless. This portrayal adds to the humor and relatability of the story, making it easy for audiences to identify with the characters' struggles.

Furthermore, Ramona and Beezus explores the challenges of growing up and finding one's place in the world. Ramona's imagination and creativity are often at odds with the mundane realities of childhood, leading to comedic misunderstandings and unexpected adventures. The movie suggests that embracing one's individuality and pursuing passions can lead to personal growth and happiness.

Overall, Ramona and Beezus is a lighthearted yet poignant film that celebrates the beauty of sibling relationships, family love, and the joys of growing up.

overview: Tad is a celebrity archaeologist and adventurer just like his hero Max Mordon... in his dreams! In reality, Tad is a Chicago construction worker. One day, however, he is mistaken for a real professor and takes his place on a flight to Peru in search of the lost city of Paititi.
tagline: No whip, no gun... All fun!
title: Tad, the Lost Explorer
plot:
Tad, the Lost Explorer (Spanish: Las aventuras de Tadeo Jones) is a 2012 Spanish animated adventure comedy film directed by Enrique Gato. A spinoff of Gato's 2004 short film Tadeo Jones and its sequel, it was mainly adapted from the Spanish graphic novel Tadeo and the Secret of the Toactlum, with a screenplay by Javier Barreira, Gorka Magallón, Ignacio del Moral, Jordi Gasull and Neil Landau. The Spanish voice cast includes Óscar Barberán, Michelle Jenner, José Mota, Pep Anton Muñoz and Miguel Ángel Jenner.

Tadeo Jones is a Chicago bricklayer working on the city's subway who has dreamed since the age of five of becoming an archaeologist. Fired for daydreaming, and after his dog urinates on the foreman, he visits his friend Professor Humbert to ask about an old Coca-Cola bottle found at the site. Humbert has just been summoned to Peru by his colleague Professor Lavrof to bring his half of a stone key that will unlock Paititi, the legendary lost city of the Incas, but after taking the wrong pills at the airport he ends up in hospital. Tad takes his place and flies to Cusco with his dog Jeff, unaware that the sinister company Odysseus Inc. is watching. There he meets Freddy, a local hustler, and when Odysseus thugs kidnap him and demand the key, he is rescued by Freddy and by Lavrof's daughter Sara, with whom Tad falls in love. The joined key leads them to Machu Picchu, where they learn that Lavrof has been taken by Odysseus and its leader Kopponen. After a string of adventures they find Lavrof together with Max Mordon, a famous archaeologist whom Tad idolizes and who is Sara's fiancé. Holding the real map, the group heads into the jungle and finds an underground temple, but Max is revealed to be working with Odysseus. Kopponen and his henchmen are wiped out by a booby-trapped chamber, and Max, believing the Incan gold will grant him eternal life, smashes its protective glass only to be turned into one of the undead mummies forever and locked in Paititi's darkest dungeon. The chief mummy lets Tad, Sara and the professor go on condition that they keep the city's secrets.

The film premiered at the Annecy International Animation Film Festival on 5 June 2012 and was released in Spain by Paramount Pictures on 31 August 2012. Spanish critics were positive, though it was less well received in North America. It earned about €45 million on an €8 million budget and won three Goya Awards, including Best Animated Film.

overview: After he reunites with an old pal through Facebook, a mild-mannered accountant is lured into the world of international espionage.
tagline: Saving the world takes a little Hart and a big Johnson.
title: Central Intelligence
plot:
Central Intelligence is a 2016 American action comedy film directed by Rawson Marshall Thurber and produced by New Line Cinema.
