The movie begins with Bob Stone (played by Kevin Hart), an overweight and awkward high school student who dreams of becoming a spy. However, his life takes a drastic turn when he meets Calvin Joyner (played by Dwayne Johnson), the star athlete of their high school. Despite their vastly different personalities, they become close friends.

Years later, Bob receives a message from Calvin, informing him that he has been recruited by the CIA and is now working undercover as a spy. However, his cover is blown, and he is forced to go into hiding after being targeted by a group of assassins hired by a rogue agent named James King (played by Karl Urban).

Calvin returns Bob's call, and they reunite to take down James King, who has stolen a deadly virus that can kill millions. As they embark on their mission, they must navigate through various obstacles, including treacherous terrain, high-tech gadgets, and James King's henchmen.

Throughout the movie, Calvin tries to help Bob regain his confidence and learn how to be a spy, while also dealing with his own personal demons. Meanwhile, Bob struggles to keep up with Calvin's high-octane lifestyle, leading to some hilarious moments of culture shock.

As they delve deeper into their mission, Bob and Calvin discover that James King is working for a shadowy organization known as "The Syndicate." They must use all their skills and resources to infiltrate The Syndicate's headquarters and stop the virus from being released.

In the climactic final act, Bob and Calvin face off against James King in an intense showdown. With Calvin's spy training and Bob's... um, unique set of skills, they manage to defeat James King and save the world from the deadly virus.

The movie ends with Bob finally finding his place as a spy, thanks to Calvin's mentorship. The two friends share a heartwarming moment, and the film concludes on a high note, leaving the audience laughing and entertained.

Overall, Central Intelligence is a fun and action-packed comedy that showcases the chemistry between Kevin Hart and Dwayne Johnson. With its witty dialogue, impressive stunts, and hilarious moments, it's no wonder this movie became a box office hit.

overview: After blind man Walter Cooke (Eric Jacobus) prevents a local gang from shaking down his local grocer Gordon (Roger Yuan), Walter must reckon with the gang's boss Sal (Joe Bucaro). The stakes are high, but Walter's got an ace up his sleeve.
title: Blindsided: The Game
plot:
Blindsided: The Game is a 2018 American action comedy short film directed by Clayton J. Barber, who wrote it with its star, the martial artist and stunt performer Eric Jacobus. Running about 46 minutes, it expands the twelve-minute short Blindsided, released the previous year, into a longer story after Jacobus's production company secured funding to continue it. The cast includes Roger Yuan, Joe Bucaro III, David William No, Michelle Lee, Pete Antico, Khalid Ghajji, Nicholas Verdi, Justin Hall and the veteran stuntman and fight choreographer Luke LaFontaine. Jacobus oversaw the action, with Yuan, LaFontaine and No, who also served as a producer, contributing to the fight choreography, and the score is by Steffan Schmidt and Raymond Lane. The film was released free to stream on YouTube on 17 May 2018.

Walter Cooke (Jacobus) is a blind man living in a modern American city, an apple pie enthusiast with a knack for sensing danger. Underestimated and brushed aside by a local gang while shopping at his neighbourhood grocery, he comes to the aid of its owner Gordon (Yuan), his friend, who is deep in debt to the gangsters. Surprising both Gordon and the thugs with his physical abilities, Walter sends them packing in an alley fight in which he puts his white cane to good use. This is where the original short ended and where The Game picks up. Following the gangsters back to their boss, Sal (Bucaro), Walter and Gordon get further into trouble, and elements of Gordon's own past come to light in connection with the villains. The stakes rise, but Walter has an ace up his sleeve, and the confrontation eventually leads the pair to take on the toughs in their own warehouse, where Gordon must fight alongside Walter against an array of opponents armed with guns and blades. Walter himself remains something of an enigma, with hints of a deeper history left for possible future stories.

Reviewers from action-focused outlets welcomed it as a homage to the blind swordsman genre, especially Zatoichi and Blind Fury. Cinapse called it enjoyable, praising the basic character work that adds heart and comedy between the set pieces and Jacobus's physical and comedic talents, and recommended it to action devotees and fans of the sub-genre. Film Combat Syndicate praised its blend of slapstick and intense fight scenes and its warm portrayal of Walter and Gordon's friendship, while noting that the short format leaves Walter's background largely unexplored.

overview: When terrorists threaten nuclear catastrophe at Chernobyl, the world's only hope is to reactivate decommissioned Universal Soldier Luc Deveraux. Rearmed and reprogrammed, Deveraux must take on his nemesis from the original Universal Soldier and a next-generation "UniSol" that seems almost unstoppable.
tagline: Reanimated. Rearmed. The ultimate rematch
title: Universal Soldier: Regeneration
plot:
Universal Soldier: Regeneration is a 2009 American science fiction action film directed and co-edited by John Hyams and written by Victor Ostrovsky. The fifth installment in the Universal Soldier franchise, it serves as an alternative sequel to the original 1992 film, ignoring the events of Universal Soldier: The Return and the made-for-television sequels. Jean-Claude Van Damme and Dolph Lundgren star, with mixed martial artist Andrei Arlovski as NGU, a Next-Generation Universal Soldier, and fellow fighter Mike Pyle as Captain Kevin Burke. Corey Johnson also appears.

Terrorists of the Pasalan Liberation Front, led by Commander Topov, kidnap the two children of the Ukrainian Prime Minister, seize the crippled Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant and threaten to blow it up unless their imprisoned comrades are freed within 72 hours. Among them is the NGU, smuggled in by the rogue scientist Dr. Robert Colin. The NGU massacres the American and Ukrainian troops sent to the plant, and four revived UniSols deployed by Colin's former colleague Dr. Richard Porter are wiped out in turn. The military then retrieves former UniSol Luc Deveraux from therapy in Switzerland. When the prisoners are released and the terrorists shut down the bomb, Colin, unsatisfied, unleashes a cloned and upgraded Andrew Scott, Deveraux's old nemesis, who kills Topov and then Colin himself before restarting the bomb and hunting the children. Captain Burke reaches the hostages and leads them out, but the NGU kills him after a brutal fight. With thirty minutes left on the timer, the reconditioned Luc storms the plant and finds Scott cornering the children; after a punishing fight he kills Scott. The NGU then attacks, and with under two minutes remaining Luc jams the detonator into the back of the NGU's uniform as both leap from the reactor chamber, and the NGU is destroyed in the blast. American soldiers take charge of the children as Luc leaves, while Burke's body and the NGU's remains are taken away; in Langley, Virginia, Burke is shown stored in a cryogenic chamber as a new UniSol, alongside multiple clones of him.

Shot mostly in Bulgaria, with a former steel factory standing in for Chernobyl, the film premiered at Fantastic Fest in Austin on October 1, 2009. It was released directly on DVD and Blu-ray in the United States in February 2010 and theatrically in parts of the Middle East and Asia, grossing about $844,000 against a $9 million budget. Reviews were mixed; a sequel came in 2012.

overview: Nineteen-year-old Laura is stressed by her first year at college when money worries distract her from her studies and so, desperate for cash, she answers an online advertisement for intimate companionship that leads her down a dangerous path.
title: Student Services
plot:
Student Services (French: Mes chères études) is a 2010 French television drama written and directed by Emmanuelle Bercot, adapted from Laura D.'s autobiographical book Mes chères études (2008). Déborah François stars as a cash-strapped first-year university student who drifts into selling sex to pay for her studies. The film was first broadcast by Canal+ on January 18, 2010, and later had a theatrical release in Poland and Italy.

Laura, 19, is determined to succeed at university, but the money from her job at a call centre is not enough to live on. She faints during a lecture because she has not been eating properly, and her working-class parents cannot afford to give her more. When her electricity is cut off over unpaid bills, she searches online for extra work and finds an advertisement from Joe, a 57-year-old man offering a hundred euros an hour to a student willing to keep him company. Telling herself it will happen only once, she meets him in a hotel room three days later. She is nervous and ashamed, but the practised Joe smooths things over, telling her that it is all about fantasy and that nowadays everything, fantasy included, is for sale. His money pays her bills and even a small party, and the episode becomes the start of a downward spiral. Exhilarated by money that seems so easily earned, she tries to forget the experiences themselves and remember only the envelopes of cash, and she keeps meeting men she finds online, with Joe becoming a regular. From the second client onward she wants to stop, but she never grows used to what is demanded of her. Clients push past her limits and cheat her out of payment, among them an abusive photographer and a man who meets her in a car park, and eventually even Joe betrays her. Strained further by her relationships with her callous first love Manu and the indolent Benjamin, Laura finally breaks down.

François plays Laura, with Alain Cauchi as Joe, Benjamin Siksou as Manu, Mathieu Demy as Benjamin, Anna Sigalevitch as Fanny and Marc Chapiteau as the photographer. Produced by Les Films du Kiosque, it was shot mainly in the centre of Besançon. François later said one sex scene, in which she lay trapped beneath a very heavy naked actor, was especially hard to film. Critics praised her performance, with MaryAnn Johanson calling the film well-acted and far more sad than scandalous, but several found the screenplay unconvincing for its thin character development.

overview: A dangerous international spy is determined to give up his high stakes life to finally build a closer relationship with his estranged wife and daughter. But first, he must complete one last mission - even if it means juggling the two toughest assignments yet: hunting down the world's most ruthless terrorist and looking after his teenage daughter for the first time in ten years, while his wife is out of town.
title: 3 Days to Kill
plot:
3 Days to Kill is a 2014 action thriller film directed by McG and written by Luc Besson and Adi Hasak. Kevin Costner stars as Ethan Renner, a CIA agent dying of cancer who hopes to retire and rebuild his relationship with his estranged family, with Amber Heard as the elite agent Vivi Delay, Hailee Steinfeld as his sixteen-year-old daughter Zooey, Connie Nielsen as his ex-wife Christine, Richard Sammel as the German arms trafficker known as the Wolf, and Tómas Lemarquis as the Wolf's lieutenant, the Albino.

During an operation in a Belgrade hotel to capture the Albino, who is helping the Wolf sell a dirty bomb to terrorists, Renner becomes dizzy, wounds the Albino in the leg and blacks out, letting him escape. Vivi, assigned by the CIA Director to kill the Wolf, suspects Renner has unknowingly seen him. Renner is diagnosed with terminal glioblastoma that has spread to his lungs and is told he will not live to the following Christmas. Having kept his work secret from Christine and Zooey for decades at the cost of losing them, he returns to Paris to make amends, only to find an African family squatting in his apartment whom the police say he cannot evict until after winter. Christine lets him reconnect with Zooey and leaves her in his care while she travels on business. Vivi then offers him an experimental drug that could greatly extend his life in exchange for hunting down the Wolf, and he reluctantly agrees. Working through the gang's limousine driver and accountant, he pursues the Albino while battling hallucinations brought on by the drug whenever his heart rate rises, which he can only control with alcohol, and while handling Zooey's lies and school troubles. Gradually he wins back his daughter's trust. After killing the Albino in the subway, Renner discovers that the father of Zooey's boyfriend is the Wolf's business partner, and at a party there he protects his family and sends the Wolf plunging down an elevator shaft. Facing the injured Wolf, Renner cannot pull the trigger, citing his promise to his wife to quit, and Vivi kills the Wolf herself. Renner lives to spend Christmas at a beach house with his family and receives a gift of more of the medicine, as Vivi watches from a nearby hill.

Released in February 2014, the film grossed $53.3 million against a $28 million budget. Reviews were mixed, with a 27% Rotten Tomatoes rating and a consensus finding its action accomplished but its family conflict underdeveloped.

overview: In the aftermath of WWI, a young German who grieves the death of her fiancé in France meets a mysterious French man who visits the fiance’s grave to lay flowers.
title: Frantz
plot:
Frantz is a 2016 German drama film directed by Florian Henckel von Donnersmarck, not X Filme Creative Pool. The movie tells the story of an anonymous letter sent to a young man named Franz, who is struggling to come to terms with the loss of his brother during World War I.

The main theme of Frantz revolves around the complexities of grief, guilt, and redemption in the aftermath of war. As Franz navigates his relationships with the family of his deceased brother's killer, he begins to confront the dark secrets of his own past and the true nature of his brother's death. The film explores the emotional toll of war on individuals and families, as well as the difficulties of rebuilding relationships and finding closure in the face of trauma.

Through Franz's journey, the film delves into the themes of identity, belonging, and the search for meaning in a world torn apart by conflict. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the past is never truly buried, and that the consequences of war can be felt long after the fighting has stopped.

Ultimately, Frantz is a powerful exploration of the human cost of war and the enduring power of love, forgiveness, and redemption in the face of unimaginable tragedy.

overview: Scientists create a genetic clone of a serial killer in order to help catch the killer, teaming up with two cops.
tagline: A ruthless killer... to destroy him, they had to create him.
title: Replicant
plot:
Replicant is a 2001 American science fiction action film directed by Ringo Lam, starring Jean-Claude Van Damme in a dual role opposite Michael Rooker. It was the second collaboration between Van Damme and the Hong Kong director and the third time Van Damme played two characters in one film, after Double Impact and Maximum Risk. Shot in Bulgaria and Vancouver, it received a limited theatrical release in many European countries and went straight to DVD in the United States on September 18, 2001.

In Seattle, Detective Jake Riley has spent three years hunting Edward "the Torch" Garrotte, a serial killer who murders mothers and sets their bodies on fire. Days before Jake retires, Garrotte strikes again and then taunts him by phone during his retirement party, threatening his friends and family. A secret government agency recruits Jake as a consultant on an unusual project: from DNA found at a crime scene, it has grown a clone of Garrotte, a man with an adult body but a child's mind who shares his genetic memories and a telepathic link with him. Jake is to train this Replicant and use that link to track the killer down.

Jake treats the Replicant harshly, fearing that the killer's instincts will surface, while the clone looks to him for protection and slowly learns about the world. After a bomb meant for Jake, the Replicant meets Garrotte in a bar and later in a parking garage, where the killer tries to persuade his "brother" that Jake cannot be trusted. Flashbacks reveal that Garrotte, whose real name is Luc Savard, was abused by a mother who killed her husband and tried to burn down their home. Tracing him to a hospital where his mother has just died, Jake and the Replicant are attacked, and in a final fight in the furnace room the Replicant realizes he is not a killer. When Garrotte strikes the clone with a shovel, Jake shoots him. The Replicant pulls Jake to safety before an explosion and is presumed dead, but weeks later he leaves a music box in Jake's mailbox as thanks for his help, revealing that he survived.

Van Damme plays both Garrotte and the Replicant and Rooker plays Jake, with Catherine Dent as Jake's wife, Anne, and Marnie Alton. Critics were mixed: only 27% of the eleven reviews counted by Rotten Tomatoes were positive, but some reviewers called it one of Van Damme's best films since Bloodsport and praised its well-staged action and his physical agility.

original_title: Batman Unmasked: The Psychology of the Dark Knight
overview: Delve into the world of Batman and the vigilante justice that he brought to the city of Gotham. Batman is a man who, after experiencing great tragedy, devotes his life to an ideal--but what happens when one man takes on the evil underworld alone? Examine why Batman is who he is--and explore how a boy scarred by tragedy becomes a symbol of hope to everyone else.
title: Batman Unmasked: The Psychology of the Dark Knight
plot:
Batman Unmasked: The Psychology of the Dark Knight is a 2008 American television documentary written and directed by Steven C. Smith and produced by Prometheus Entertainment for the History channel, with narration by Robert Clotworthy. Running about 45 minutes, it was first broadcast on 16 July 2008, the same month Christopher Nolan's The Dark Knight reached cinemas, and it approaches the comic book hero not as a piece of pop entertainment but as a subject for psychological analysis.

The programme asks what drives a man who, after suffering a devastating tragedy, devotes his whole life to a single ideal, and what happens when one person takes it upon himself to fight a city's criminal underworld alone. It traces Bruce Wayne back to the formative trauma of witnessing his parents' murder as a child and examines how that loss shaped him, how he channels fear and grief into a disciplined double life, and how a boy scarred by violence turns himself into a symbol of hope for Gotham City. Along the way it weighs the appeal and the dangers of vigilante justice, and looks at the costumed villains of Batman's rogues' gallery as reflections of the hero's own psyche, including foes who had not appeared in the Nolan films.

The film is built mainly around interviews, illustrated with dynamic treatments of comic book panels and covers and with clips from Batman Begins and The Dark Knight. Contributors include the clinical psychologist Robin S. Rosenberg, who discusses the effect of the Waynes' murder on their son, alongside DC Comics figures Paul Levitz and Dan DiDio and the veteran Batman writers and editors Denny O'Neil and Len Wein. Christopher Nolan and Christian Bale also appear, speaking about their interpretation of the character.

The documentary was later included as a high-definition special feature on the second disc of Warner Home Video's Blu-ray release of The Dark Knight in December 2008, where it was described as a look into the psyche of Bruce Wayne through real-world psychotherapy, and it reappeared in later Dark Knight Trilogy box sets. It holds a favourable user rating on IMDb, where one reviewer called it a thorough, credible and engaging examination of the character.

overview: Evan Hansen, a high schooler with social anxiety, unintentionally gets caught up in a lie after the family of a classmate who committed suicide mistakes one of Hansen’s letters for their son’s suicide note.
tagline: An honest and original story for the outsider in all of us.
title: Dear Evan Hansen
plot:
Dear Evan Hansen is a thought-provoking film that delves into the complexities of human relationships, social media's impact on mental health, and the struggle to find one's identity. The movie follows the story of Evan Hansen, a high school student who struggles with anxiety and loneliness.

At its core, Dear Evan Hansen explores the theme of isolation in a world where everyone seems connected through social media. Evan's character is a poignant representation of this phenomenon, as he navigates the blurred lines between online personas and real-life relationships. The film highlights how our digital presence can both unite and isolate us, making it difficult to form genuine connections with others.

The movie also touches on the theme of mental health, particularly anxiety and depression. Evan's struggles are deeply relatable, and his character serves as a catalyst for exploring the importance of seeking help and support. The film encourages viewers to confront their own vulnerabilities and to prioritize self-care.

Furthermore, Dear Evan Hansen examines the theme of identity and how it is shaped by our relationships with others. Evan's character is on a journey of self-discovery, trying to find his place in the world and define himself outside of his online persona. The film suggests that true connection and belonging can only be achieved through authentic interactions with others.

Ultimately, Dear Evan Hansen is a powerful exploration of what it means to be human in a world where social media dominates our lives. It encourages viewers to look beyond the digital facade and to cultivate meaningful relationships that foster empathy, understanding, and acceptance.

overview: When LexCorp accidentally unleashes a murderous creature, Superman meets his greatest challenge as a champion. Based on the "The Death of Superman" storyline that appeared in DC Comics' publications in the 1990s.
tagline: Where were you the day Superman died?
title: Superman: Doomsday
plot:
Superman: Doomsday is a 2007 American animated superhero film adapted from the DC Comics storyline "The Death of Superman", and the first of the DC Universe Animated Original Movies. Although its style resembles the DC Animated Universe series of 1992 to 2006, the film used new character models and is only loosely connected to them. It screened at San Diego Comic-Con on July 26, 2007, and was released on DVD by Warner Home Video on September 18, 2007, with a special edition following the next year.

Superman and Lois Lane are in a relationship, though Lois resents that he keeps his identity secret. LexCorp workers unearth the ship of Doomsday, a genetically engineered super-soldier that slaughters every living thing it meets, and the monster rampages toward Metropolis. Superman defeats it in a brutal battle across the city but dies in Lois's arms. To hide LexCorp's role, Lex Luthor kills his assistant Mercy Graves. As the world mourns, Jimmy Olsen joins a tabloid, Perry White turns to drink, and Lois, now aware that Clark was Superman, seeks comfort from Martha Kent.

When Toyman takes children hostage with a giant mechanical spider, an apparently resurrected Superman rescues Lois and a girl. In fact, he is a clone created by Luthor, who keeps the real Superman's body in a tube, unaware that a robot from the Fortress of Solitude has found him alive and is healing him. After learning that Toyman killed a child, the clone kills the villain publicly and begins ruling Metropolis through fear, convincing Lois and Martha that he is an impostor. He removes a kryptonite pellet Luthor planted in his brain, destroys Luthor's lab of unawakened clones and hurls Luthor's panic room into the street. Still weakened, the real Superman returns in a solar suit with a kryptonite gun and, helped by Lois, defeats the clone, who asks him to protect the people before dying. Superman reveals his identity to Lois, while a badly injured Luthor survives.

Adam Baldwin voices Superman and his clone, with Anne Heche as Lois Lane, James Marsters as Lex Luthor, Swoosie Kurtz as Martha Kent, Ray Wise as Perry White, Adam Wylie as Jimmy Olsen and John DiMaggio as Toyman. Reviews were generally positive, especially for Marsters and Baldwin, though some faulted its brevity and changes to the comics. It earned $10 million in home media sales on a $3.5 million budget.

overview: Recently deceased, a white-sheeted ghost returns to his suburban home to console his bereft wife, only to find that in his spectral state he has become unstuck in time, forced to watch passively as the life he knew and the woman he loves slowly slip away.
title: A Ghost Story
plot:
A Ghost Story is an American supernatural drama of 2017 written and directed by David Lowery, following a man who dies and lingers as a ghost in the house he shared with his wife. Casey Affleck plays the husband, C, who spends most of the film beneath a white sheet, with Rooney Mara as his wife M and Will Oldham as a party guest credited as the Prognosticator.

M tells C, a musician, that as a child she moved often and used to hide little notes in every home she left. C resists her wish to move and on the night he finally gives in they are woken by a loud bang they cannot explain. Soon after, C is killed in a car crash . At the hospital M draws a sheet over his body and leaves; C rises as a ghost, still draped in the sheet and invisible to the living. Ignoring a doorway of light, he walks home. There he watches M grieve, eating a whole pie until she is sick, and slowly move on. In the house next door he notices another sheeted ghost which says it is waiting for someone but can no longer remember who. When M starts seeing another man, C makes books tumble from a shelf, one falling open at Virginia Woolf's story "A Haunted House". Before she moves out, M writes a note, tucks it into a crack in the woodwork and paints over it, and C tries to scratch it free.

Time slips past. A Spanish-speaking mother and her two children move in, and C drives them out by smashing a photograph and dishes. At a party held by later tenants, a man holds forth on the futility of creative effort since the universe will end. The house falls derelict and is bulldozed before C can reach the note; the neighbouring ghost decides that its loved ones are not coming and vanishes from beneath its sheet. A skyscraper rises on the site, and C leaps from its balcony into a futuristic city, only to land on the same spot in the nineteenth century, where pioneers begin building a home; its youngest child hides a note under a rock while humming C's song before the family is killed. Back in the house, C watches himself and M arrive, reliving their life until he causes the mysterious bang himself by slumping onto the piano. After his earlier ghostly self watches M leave for the last time, C finally prises out her note, reads it, and vanishes, his empty sheet dropping to the floor.

Premiering at the Sundance Film Festival and released by A24 in July 2017, the film earned just under $2 million worldwide but was widely acclaimed, with 91% on Rotten Tomatoes, winning three prizes at Deauville.

overview: Spanning over one thousand years, and three parallel stories, The Fountain is a story of love, death, spirituality, and the fragility of our existence in this world.
tagline: Death is the road to awe
title: The Fountain
plot:
The Fountain is a 2006 American epic romantic drama film directed by Darren Aronofsky, not Warner Bros. Pictures.

The main themes of The Fountain are:

1. **Love and Sacrifice**: The film explores the complexities of love and relationships through the story of three interconnected narratives: Tom's quest for immortality in the New World, Izabella's journey to find a cure for her daughter's illness, and the Aztec priest's search for the Tree of Life.
2. **Time and Mortality**: The Fountain delves into the human experience of time, mortality, and the passage of life. Tom's quest for immortality serves as a metaphor for the human desire to transcend death and find eternal love.
3. **Spirituality and Faith**: The film touches on themes of spirituality, faith, and the search for meaning in life. Izabella's journey is driven by her devotion to God and her desire to save her daughter, while Tom's quest is motivated by his own spiritual seeking.
4. **The Power of Human Connection**: Despite the vast distances and obstacles between the characters, The Fountain highlights the transformative power of human connection and love.

Throughout the film, Aronofsky weaves together these themes in a non-linear narrative that explores the interconnectedness of life, death, and the human experience.

[No information on Warner Bros. Pictures as the production company is available for this specific movie.]

overview: A young woman's desperate search for her abducted boyfriend draws her into the infamous Colonia Dignidad, a sect nobody ever escaped from.
tagline: There is no turning back
title: Colonia
plot:
Colonia is a 2015 German drama film directed by Florian Gallenberger, produced by Majestic Filmproduktion, and released in some countries under the title "The Colony". The movie tells the story of Lena, a young woman who lives in East Germany during the communist regime. She is forced to flee her home after her husband is arrested for being an opponent of the government.

The main themes of Colonia are:

1. Oppression and Resistance: The film explores the oppressive nature of the communist regime in East Germany, highlighting the struggles of its citizens who resist against the government's control.
2. Identity and Belonging: Lena's journey is a search for identity and belonging, as she tries to find her place in a world that seems determined to suppress her individuality.
3. Love and Sacrifice: The movie portrays the sacrifices made by those who love their country but disagree with its policies, highlighting the complexities of loyalty and devotion.
4. Escape and Freedom: Colonia is also a story about escape and freedom, as Lena tries to find a way to leave her oppressive past behind and start anew.

The film features a strong performance from Emma Watson, who plays the lead role of Lena. The movie received critical acclaim for its thought-provoking themes, atmospheric setting, and powerful performances.

Overall, Colonia is a gripping drama that explores the complexities of human experience under oppressive regimes, highlighting the resilience and determination of those who resist against injustice.

overview: The year is 2087, the setting is the moon. Pluto Nash, the high-flying successful owner of the hottest nightclub in the universe, finds himself in trouble when he refuses to sell his club to lunar gangster Mogan, who just happens to be helping the mysterious Rex Crater mastermind a plan to take over the entire moon.
tagline: The MAN on the Moon.
title: The Adventures of Pluto Nash
plot:
The Adventures of Pluto Nash is a 2002 American science fiction action comedy directed by Ron Underwood and starring Eddie Murphy in a dual role, with Randy Quaid, Rosario Dawson, Joe Pantoliano, Jay Mohr, Luis Guzmán, James Rebhorn, Peter Boyle, Pam Grier and John Cleese. Produced by Castle Rock Entertainment and Village Roadshow Pictures, it was released by Warner Bros. on August 16, 2002. Underwood later said he sensed during filming that it lacked wit, and after a negative online review of an unfinished cut in early 2001, the studio ordered reshoots that pushed the budget to $100 million and delayed its release.

In 2080, on Little America, a colony on the Moon, the former smuggler and ex-convict Pluto Nash buys a run-down club from his old friend Tony Francis to save him from the mobsters threatening his life, and with his android friend Bruno turns it into a hugely popular nightclub. Seven years later, he hires Dina Lake, the stranded daughter of an old friend, as a waitress so she can earn her fare back to Earth. When Pluto refuses to sell the club to the mysterious tycoon Rex Crater, Crater's henchmen Mogan and Kelp blow it up.

Pluto, Dina and Bruno escape, and with help from the retired detective Rowland they learn that Crater's associates are tied to human cloning. Pursued by assassins, they hijack a limousine driven by a holographic chauffeur named James, and are later rescued by Felix Laranga, a smuggler who idolizes Pluto. Infiltrating Crater's casino resort at Moon Beach, Pluto discovers that Crater is his own clone, grown from DNA taken from his appendix while he was in prison, who has sent his creators into orbit and built a criminal empire. Crater kills his bungling henchmen and then fights Pluto, who throws him through a window to his death. Club Pluto is rebuilt, with Dina performing as a singer.

Murphy plays both Pluto and Crater, Quaid plays Bruno and Dawson plays Dina, with Grier as Pluto's mother, Flura, and Cleese as James. The film was panned, earning 6% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 12, along with five Golden Raspberry nominations. Grossing only about $7.1 million worldwide, it is regarded as one of the biggest box office bombs of all time.

overview: A teenager and his mother find themselves besieged by threatening forces when they move into a new house.
tagline: You can't lock out what's already inside.
title: The Open House
plot:
The One and Only Ivan is a heartwarming film that explores the complexities of friendship, empathy, and the transformative power of art. At its core, the movie delves into the emotional journey of Ivan, a majestic gorilla who has been living in a mall for over 27 years, surrounded by the trappings of human civilization but devoid of genuine connection.

As Ivan navigates his mundane existence, he forms an unlikely bond with Stella, a beautiful elephant who becomes his confidante and friend. Through their conversations, Ivan begins to confront the harsh realities of his captivity and the emotional toll it takes on him. The film masterfully captures the nuances of Ivan's inner world, revealing a character who is both strong-willed and vulnerable.

The movie also sheds light on the importance of art as a means of self-expression and empowerment. Ivan's passion for painting becomes an outlet for his emotions, allowing him to convey the depth of his feelings in a way that transcends words. Through his artwork, Ivan is able to connect with Stella and, ultimately, find a sense of purpose and belonging.

One of the most striking aspects of The One and Only Ivan is its thought-provoking exploration of empathy and understanding. As Ivan navigates his relationships with Stella and Bob, a young boy who befriends him, the film encourages viewers to consider the experiences of those who are often overlooked or marginalized. By humanizing Ivan's character and highlighting the emotional resonance of his story, the movie inspires audiences to think critically about the ways in which we treat others and the importance of compassion in our daily lives.

Overall, The One and Only Ivan is a poignant film that celebrates the transformative power of friendship, art, and empathy. Through its beautifully crafted narrative, the movie reminds us of the inherent value and dignity of all living beings, encouraging viewers to approach the world with kindness, understanding, and a deep appreciation for the complexities of the human (and non-human) experience.

overview: Ghost pirates attack the cruise ship that Scooby and the gang are vacationing on.
title: Scooby-Doo! Pirates Ahoy!
plot:
Scooby-Doo! Pirates Ahoy! is a 2006 animated film that combines mystery-solving with pirate-themed adventure. The movie follows Shaggy, Scooby, Velma, Daphne, and Fred as they travel to the Caribbean on a pirate ship called the "Mystery Ship." 

The main themes of Scooby-Doo! Pirates Ahoy! include friendship, teamwork, and overcoming fears. Throughout the film, the gang faces various obstacles and challenges, but ultimately works together to solve the mystery behind the cursed treasure.

One notable theme is the exploration of Shaggy's fear of water and his reluctance to participate in pirate-themed activities. However, with the encouragement of Scooby and the rest of the gang, he eventually overcomes his fears and becomes more confident.

Another significant theme is the importance of loyalty and trust among friends. The gang relies on each other's unique skills and strengths to overcome challenges and solve the mystery, demonstrating their strong bond and commitment to one another.

Overall, Scooby-Doo! Pirates Ahoy! is a lighthearted, entertaining film that emphasizes the value of teamwork, friendship, and facing fears in order to achieve success.

overview: The owner of a seedy small-town Texas bar discovers that one of his employees is having an affair with his wife. A chaotic chain of misunderstandings, lies and mischief ensues after he devises a plot to have them murdered.
tagline: Breaking up is hard to do.
title: Blood Simple
plot:
Blood Simple is a neo-noir crime thriller that delves into the dark and twisted world of obsession, desire, and the destructive nature of human relationships.

At its core, the film explores the theme of toxic masculinity, as embodied by the complex and troubled character of Julian Marty (played by John Getz). Julian's possessiveness and jealousy are expertly woven throughout the narrative, ultimately leading to a downward spiral of violence and chaos. This toxic dynamic is mirrored in the relationships between the other characters, particularly the doomed romance between Abby (Frances McDormand) and Julian.

The film also examines the theme of obsession, as Abby becomes increasingly entangled in her own desires and the manipulations of those around her. Her character serves as a symbol of the destructive power of unchecked passion, which ultimately leads to her downfall.

Furthermore, Blood Simple critiques the societal norms that perpetuate these toxic behaviors, particularly the patriarchal expectations placed on women. The film's portrayal of Abby's vulnerability and agency is particularly noteworthy, as she navigates a world where her desires are constantly being manipulated and exploited by those around her.

Ultimately, Blood Simple presents a bleak and unsettling vision of human nature, one that is marked by violence, manipulation, and the destructive power of unchecked desire. The film's dark and atmospheric tone serves to underscore this theme, creating a sense of unease and tension that permeates every aspect of the narrative.

overview: Detective Amelia Van Helsing is on the desperate hunt for the killer responsible for a string of grisly murders targeting young women. Matters only worsen when all evidence leads to the seemingly untouchable Count Dracula. And when Van Helsing’s girlfriend vanishes, she is forced to question the very existence of monsters in a final showdown with the enigmatic count.
tagline: The classic tale as you've never seen.
title: Dracula: The Original Living Vampire
plot:
Dracula: The Original Living Vampire is a 2022 American horror film directed by Maximilian Elfeldt and produced by The Asylum. A loose reimagining of Bram Stoker's novel Dracula as a police investigation, it was conceived as a "mockbuster" of Morbius, released the same year. Jake Herbert, in his screen acting debut, plays Count Dracula, with Christine Prouty as Detective Amelia Van Helsing, India Lillie Davies as Mina Murray, Ryan Woodcock as Jonathan Harker, Stuart Packer as Captain Renfield and Michael Ironside as Dr. Jack Seward.

A series of grisly murders is claiming the lives of young women in the city, and Captain Renfield assigns Detective Amelia Van Helsing to find the killer. All of the victims have red hair and are found drained of blood, with puncture wounds on their necks. The coroner, Jonathan Harker, suggests that the culprit may be something supernatural, an idea the rational Amelia initially dismisses. Meanwhile, Amelia's girlfriend Mina Murray has been promoted at work and is tasked with finding a property for a charming client, Count Dracula. As her investigation progresses, Amelia comes to believe that a vampire is responsible and realizes that it is Dracula, but the evidence points to a man who seems untouchable and who then disappears. The count is searching for the reincarnation of his long-lost love and has become fixated on Mina, convinced that she is the one. When Mina vanishes, Amelia is forced to question everything she believes, accept that monsters exist and confront the enigmatic count in a final showdown to save her.

The film was shot mainly in Belgrade, Serbia, and many supporting roles, including several of the vampire's victims, were filled by Serbian actors and models. It premiered in the United States on 28 January 2022 and was released in Germany on video on demand that July. Reviews were negative. Moria Reviews noted that the film never makes clear when and where it is set, since horses and carriages are heard but never seen and electric lighting alternates with candles, and remarked on the bold choice of making Van Helsing and Mina a lesbian couple. Writing for Voices from the Balcony, Jim Morazzini gave it one and a half stars out of five, criticizing a script that cannot decide between groan-worthy one-liners and serious vampire horror and calling Herbert one of the dullest Draculas he had seen, neither menacing nor charismatic.

original_title: G.I. Joe: The Rise of Cobra
overview: From the Egyptian desert to deep below the polar ice caps, the elite G.I. JOE team uses the latest in next-generation spy and military equipment to fight the corrupt arms dealer Destro and the growing threat of the mysterious Cobra organization to prevent them from plunging the world into chaos.
tagline: When all else fails, they don't.
title: G.I. Joe: The Rise of Cobra
plot:
G.I. Joe: The Rise of Cobra is a 2009 action-adventure film directed by Stephen Sommers, based on the popular toy franchise of the same name. The movie follows the story of Duke, a member of the elite G.I. Joe team, as he uncovers a plot to steal the world's most powerful energy source, known as the "Nanite."

The film begins with Duke (Channing Tatum), a former Marine who joins the G.I. Joe team, led by the Duke's father figure, General Hawk (Dennis Quaid). The Joes are tasked with stopping the evil Cobra organization, led by the enigmatic and ruthless Cobra Commander (Joseph Gordon-Levitt).

Cobra plans to use the Nanite, a microscopic energy source that can be used to control the world's military forces. Duke soon discovers that he has a personal connection to the Nanite, as it is linked to his father's death.

As Duke delves deeper into the mystery, he teams up with his fellow Joes, including Snake Eyes (Ray Park), Scarlett (Rachel Nichols), and Heavy Duty (Adewale Akinnuoye-Agbaje). Together, they embark on a perilous mission to stop Cobra and retrieve the Nanite.

The team faces numerous challenges as they navigate through treacherous terrain, avoiding Cobra's deadly traps and henchmen. Along the way, Duke also uncovers more about his father's past and his connection to the Nanite.

As the stakes grow higher, Duke and the Joes launch a final assault on Cobra's secret base. In an epic battle, they face off against Cobra Commander and his minions, with Duke ultimately facing off against the villain in a one-on-one showdown.

In the end, Duke emerges victorious, having successfully stopped Cobra's plan to control the world. The movie concludes with Duke reflecting on his journey and the sacrifices he made to protect his country and his fellow Joes.

Throughout the film, Sommers incorporates plenty of action-packed sequences, showcasing the G.I. Joe team in their signature style. While the movie received mixed reviews from critics, it has since become a cult classic among fans of the franchise.

Overall, G.I. Joe: The Rise of Cobra is an entertaining and thrilling adventure that brings the beloved toy franchise to life on the big screen.

overview: In the near future, Uffizi and Luke travel to the remote reaches of war torn Romania to rescue Elizabeth and finish the vampire once and for all. Along the way, they encounter TV news journalist and a corps of rebels trying to fight the vampire uprising which plagues their country.
tagline: You can't fight it. You can't kill it.
title: Dracula III: Legacy
plot:
Dracula III: Legacy is a 2005 horror film directed by Patrick Lussier and the third installment in the series that began with Dracula 2000 and continued with Dracula II: Ascension. It stars Jason Scott Lee as the vampire-hunting priest Uffizi, Jason London as his companion Luke, Diane Neal as Elizabeth Blaine, Alexandra Wescourt as the reporter Julia Hughes and Roy Scheider as Cardinal Siqueros. Rutger Hauer plays Dracula, succeeding Gerard Butler and Stephen Billington in the role and continuing the series' idea that the vampire's appearance changes as he regenerates.

Five years after the previous film, Uffizi and Luke learn that Dracula has returned to his castle in the Carpathian Mountains, taking Elizabeth with him. Cardinal Siqueros, fearing that Uffizi has been tainted by Dracula, refuses to bless the mission, so Uffizi leaves the priesthood and sets out with Luke for Bucharest. Romania has been torn apart by civil war, and NATO peacekeepers patrol the streets. In an abandoned village the two men find a crashed helicopter carrying Julia, a television news reporter, and her cameraman, Tommy. Tommy is turned by vampires who are terrorizing the village, but Uffizi and Luke destroy them all.

Leaving Julia behind, the hunters walk into a trap set by rebels, only to find Julia already with them; she refuses to return to England with nothing but a story about vampires. When the undead attack the rebel camp during the night, Uffizi, Luke and Julia survive and continue to Dracula's castle. There they find Elizabeth almost completely given over to Dracula's way of life. Dracula mortally wounds Julia and tells Uffizi that he can only truly die through God's forgiveness. Uffizi fights the ancient vampire, bites him and drains his blood, then beheads him, declaring that he may consider himself forgiven. At Elizabeth's own request, Luke beheads her. Luke then leaves the castle, while Uffizi takes his seat on Dracula's throne beside a revived Julia, now a vampire, suggesting that he has become the new vampire king with Julia as his queen.

The film was released directly to DVD and VHS on July 12, 2005. Critical reaction was mixed, though warmer than for Dracula II. John Puccio of DVD Town said it was hardly scary but had mood, tone and atmosphere to spare, along with decent acting, qualities he felt the first two films lacked. Kevin Carr of 7M Pictures ranked it below Hellraiser but above the Crow sequels and noted there is always a market for vampire films.

overview: A young man is plunged into a life of subterfuge, deceit and mistaken identity in pursuit of a femme fatale whose heart is never quite within his grasp
tagline: This is not a love story – it's a story about love.
title: Original Sin
plot:
Original Sin is an American erotic romantic thriller of 2001 written and directed by Michael Cristofer, adapted from Cornell Woolrich's novel Waltz into Darkness (1947), which François Truffaut had earlier filmed as Mississippi Mermaid (1969). Antonio Banderas stars as Luis Vargas, a wealthy Cuban, and Angelina Jolie as Julia Russell, the mysterious woman who becomes his wife, with Thomas Jane as Walter Downs.

Set in Cuba under Spanish rule in the late nineteenth century, the story is told in flashbacks by a woman awaiting execution, who recounts her tale to a priest. Luis sends for an American mail-order bride from Delaware, Julia Russell. The woman who steps off the ship looks nothing like her photograph; she explains that she wanted a man who cared for more than a pretty face and sent a picture of a plainer woman. Luis confesses a deception of his own, having passed himself off as a modest clerk rather than a rich plantation owner. They marry within hours of her arrival, and Luis falls passionately in love. Julia's sister Emily writes anxious letters, and Luis makes Julia reply. He gives her full access to his accounts.

A private detective, Walter Downs, arrives from Wilmington, hired by Emily to find her sister, and Emily herself soon comes to Cuba, where she tells Luis that the woman he married is an impostor and that the real Julia may be dead. Julia vanishes with almost all of Luis's fortune. Searching for her with Downs, Luis finds her and learns that she is really Bonny Castle and that Downs is her lover and accomplice, Billy. Luis abandons his prosperous life to run away with her. Believing Billy dead after a confrontation in which Luis shoots him, the couple live in hiding, but one night Luis follows Bonny and discovers that Billy is alive and that she means to poison her husband that very night. When she returns, Luis tells her he knows, declares his love once more and drinks the poison anyway. Bonny flees with the dying Luis, and when Billy catches them at a train station and holds a knife to her throat, Luis wounds him and she finishes him off. Back in the present, after she has told her story, the guards find the priest kneeling in her cell in her clothes. Later, in Morocco, Bonny signals other players' cards to Luis at a gambling table.

Critics savaged the film as laughably melodramatic, giving it 12% on Rotten Tomatoes, and Jolie was nominated for the Golden Raspberry Award for Worst Actress for this and Lara Croft: Tomb Raider.

original_title: The Hobbit: The Desolation of Smaug
overview: The Dwarves, Bilbo and Gandalf have successfully escaped the Misty Mountains, and Bilbo has gained the One Ring. They all continue their journey to get their gold back from the Dragon, Smaug.
tagline: Beyond darkness... beyond desolation... lies the greatest danger of all.
title: The Hobbit: The Desolation of Smaug
plot:
The Hobbit: The Desolation of Smaug is a 2013 fantasy adventure film directed by Peter Jackson, based on the novel of the same name by J.R.R. Tolkien. The film is the second installment in The Hobbit trilogy and follows the journey of Bilbo Baggins (Martin Freeman) as he joins a group of dwarves led by Thorin Oakenshield (Richard Armitage) to reclaim their treasure from the dragon Smaug.

The film begins with Bilbo, who has grown accustomed to his comfortable life in the Shire, being recruited by the wizard Gandalf (Ian McKellen) and the master thief Bard (Luke Evans) to join a group of 13 dwarves on a quest to reclaim their treasure from the dragon Smaug. The dwarves are led by Thorin Oakenshield, who is determined to reclaim his family's treasure and restore their honor.

As they journey through the forest of Mirkwood, the company encounters various obstacles, including giant spiders, goblins, and trolls. They also meet Beorn (Mikael Persbrandt), a shape-shifting bear who provides them with shelter and assistance.

Upon reaching Lake-town, the dwarves are met by Bard, who is seeking to reclaim his town from Smaug's tyranny. The dwarves agree to help Bard in exchange for his promise to let them pass through the town unharmed. However, things take a turn when Smaug appears, and the company must flee.

The film then shifts focus to Bilbo, who finds himself separated from the rest of the group and must navigate the treacherous forest alone. He encounters the Woodland Realm's elf-lord Thranduil (Lee Pace), who is hostile towards humans and dwarves. However, Bilbo manages to charm Thranduil's daughter, Tauriel (Evangelina Lilly), and gains her assistance in finding his way back to the group.

Meanwhile, Thorin becomes increasingly obsessed with reclaiming his treasure, which leads to tension within the group. The company eventually reaches the Lonely Mountain, where they find that Smaug has taken over and is guarding the treasure hoard.

The film's climax features a confrontation between Bilbo and Smaug, who is revealed to be a powerful and intelligent dragon. Bilbo uses his wits and cunning to distract Smaug while Thorin and the dwarves prepare to attack. However, things take a turn when Bard shoots an arrow at Smaug, which kills him but also destroys the treasure hoard.

The film ends with the company mourning the loss of their treasure and the death of Smaug. Thorin becomes increasingly isolated and withdrawn, while Bilbo reflects on his experiences and the lessons he has learned about courage and friendship. The stage is set for the final installment of The Hobbit trilogy, The Battle of the Five Armies.

Overall, The Desolation of Smaug is a thrilling adventure film that explores themes of courage, loyalty, and the complexities of leadership. The film features stunning visuals, memorable characters, and a gripping storyline that sets the stage for the epic conclusion to The Hobbit trilogy.

overview: With dreams of diving abroad, Tsuneo gets a job assisting Josee, an artist whose imagination takes her far beyond her wheelchair. But when the tide turns against them, they push each other to places they never thought possible, and inspire a love fit for a storybook.
tagline: Together they can fly.
title: Josee, the Tiger and the Fish
plot:
Josee, the Tiger and the Fish is a 2020 Japanese drama film directed by Sion Sono, produced by Shochiku, and based on the manga of the same name by Akihiko Yoshida. The movie follows the story of Josee, a young woman who has been confined to her home since childhood due to a rare condition that prevents her from moving or speaking.

The film begins with Josee's life in isolation, where she spends most of her time playing with a stuffed tiger and watching fish swim in a tank. Her only companion is a man named Kōichi, who visits her every day to bring her food and talk to her through the window. Despite their limited interactions, Kōichi has become an integral part of Josee's life, and she begins to develop feelings for him.

One day, Kōichi decides to take matters into his own hands and convinces a young man named Tetsuya to help him bring Josee out of her shell. Tetsuya is initially hesitant but eventually agrees to assist Kōichi in helping Josee overcome her condition. As they work together, the three form an unlikely bond, with Josee slowly beginning to interact with the world outside her home.

However, their progress is hindered by the complexities of Josee's condition and the societal expectations placed upon her. The medical professionals who have been caring for Josee are skeptical of Tetsuya's involvement, and Kōichi struggles to balance his desire to help Josee with the need to protect her from the outside world.

As the story unfolds, the film explores themes of isolation, loneliness, and the human need for connection. Through Josee's character, the movie highlights the challenges faced by individuals with rare conditions and the importance of empathy and understanding in breaking down barriers.

The title "Josee, the Tiger and the Fish" is a metaphor for Josee's inner world, where she finds solace in her stuffed tiger and watches fish swim in her tank. The tiger represents her imagination and creativity, while the fish symbolize her longing for freedom and connection with the outside world.

Ultimately, the film builds towards a poignant and emotional conclusion as Josee begins to confront her condition and the limitations placed upon her. Through her journey, the movie offers a powerful exploration of the human spirit and the importance of finding ways to overcome adversity.

Overall, Josee, the Tiger and the Fish is a heartwarming and thought-provoking film that explores themes of isolation, loneliness, and the power of human connection. With its unique blend of drama and fantasy elements, the movie offers a captivating and emotional viewing experience.

overview: While diving in a remote French lake, a couple of YouTubers who specialise in underwater exploration videos discover a house submerged in the deep waters. What was initially a unique finding soon turns into a nightmare when they discover that the house was the scene of atrocious crimes. Trapped, with their oxygen reserves falling dangerously, they realise the worst is yet to come: they are not alone in the house.
production_companies: Tax Shelter du Gouvernement Fédéral Belge
tagline: Breathe while you still can.
title: The Deep House
plot:
The Deep House is a 2021 English-language French supernatural horror film written and directed by Julien Maury and Alexandre Bustillo. James Jagger and Camille Rowe star as Ben and Tina, a young engaged couple from New York who explore reputedly haunted places for their YouTube channel, with Éric Savin as Pierre Montégnac, Alexis Servaes and Anne Claessens as Monsieur and Madame Montégnac, and Carolina Massey as their daughter Sarah.

Travelling through Europe in search of haunted houses to record, Ben and Tina head to south-west France to dive to a sanatorium submerged in an artificial lake, but find the site packed with tourists. A local man, Pierre, offers to guide them instead to a secluded part of the lake in the forest of Chanteloup, which was flooded in 1984 to prevent recurring floods and where, he claims, a mansion lies perfectly preserved. Diving down, they find the house with its contents strangely intact, but soon hear voices and noises, their drone's motion tracker registers movement with no visible cause and their equipment begins to fail. Inside they discover photographs and news cuttings about missing children, satanic symbols and deep scratches by the front door, and behind a door blocked by a crucifix they find two chained corpses in torture masks hanging above a pentagram, beside a room of preserved human remains. When the window they entered through is suddenly bricked up, the couple search desperately for another way out. Ben unmasks the corpses, revealing the Montégnacs, the family who owned the house, and the bodies come to life and pursue them. Separated by a collapsing chimney, Ben finds a family tree showing that Pierre is the Montégnacs' son and lured them there on purpose, before the undead daughter Sarah possesses him. Through Ben and an old film reel, Sarah reveals that her father and Pierre abducted local children as satanic sacrifices before a vengeful mob killed the rest of the family. Tina breaks Ben's possession with a diving knife, but Sarah stabs him to death; Tina escapes up a shaft into the lake, only to run out of air and drown just below the surface. A post-credits scene shows Pierre with two new divers at the lake.

Filmed in Belgium and at lakes in the Occitanie region in 2020, the film was released in France on 30 June 2021 by Apollo Films and in the United States that November by Blumhouse and Epix. It holds a 74% Rotten Tomatoes rating.

overview: Two years after bringing peace to the galaxy, Steven Universe sees his past come back to haunt him in the form of a deranged Gem who wants to destroy the Earth.
tagline: The true kinda love.
title: Steven Universe: The Movie
plot:
Steven Universe: The Movie is a 2019 animated film based on the popular Cartoon Network series Steven Universe. The movie takes place after the events of the fourth season and follows Steven, Garnet, Amethyst, Pearl, and the Crystal Gems as they face a new threat to their home, Beach City.

The story begins with Steven feeling unfulfilled and restless, struggling to find his place in the world now that he has saved the Earth from various threats. He is also dealing with the emotional aftermath of the events of the previous season, particularly the loss of Connie's father, Greg Universe. Meanwhile, a new villain emerges in the form of White Diamond, an ancient and powerful being who seeks to reclaim her lost Crystal Gem.

White Diamond reveals that she was once a Crystal Gem herself but was separated from her fellow Gems during a catastrophic event known as the "Great War." She believes that Steven is the key to restoring her powers and reunifying the Crystal Gems. However, White Diamond's intentions are far from pure, and she plans to use Steven's connection to the Crystal Gems to gain control over the Earth.

As White Diamond's power grows, the Crystal Gems must band together to stop her. Along the way, they encounter new allies, including a group of rebels fighting against White Diamond's rule. The movie features plenty of action-packed sequences, emotional character moments, and heartfelt dialogue as the Crystal Gems work to save their home and themselves.

Throughout the movie, Steven grapples with his own identity and purpose. He struggles to come to terms with his role as a leader and a hero, feeling overwhelmed by the weight of responsibility. However, with the help of his friends and family, he learns to find his place in the world and discover new strengths within himself.

The movie's climax features an epic battle between White Diamond and the Crystal Gems, with Steven playing a crucial role in the fight. In the end, the Crystal Gems emerge victorious, but not without sacrifices. The movie concludes on a hopeful note, with Steven and his friends looking towards a brighter future and a new beginning.

Overall, Steven Universe: The Movie is a heartwarming and action-packed film that explores themes of identity, friendship, and the power of love. With its stunning animation, memorable characters, and emotional storytelling, it's a must-see for fans of the series and newcomers alike.

overview: When an aspiring young artist is forced to join her high school track team, she uses it as an opportunity to pursue the girl she's been harboring a long-time crush on. But she soon finds herself falling for an unexpected teammate and discovers what real love feels like.
tagline: Love is messy AF.
title: Crush
plot:
Crush is a 2022 American coming-of-age romantic comedy directed by Sammi Cohen in their feature debut and written by Kirsten King and Casey Rackham, who drew on their own experiences to tell an LGBTQ story centered on queer joy rather than on coming out. Rowan Blanchard stars as Paige Evans and Auliʻi Cravalho as AJ Campos, with Isabella Ferreira as AJ's twin sister, Gabby, Tyler Alvarez, Teala Dunn, Aasif Mandvi, Michelle Buteau and Megan Mullally.

Paige, an art-loving student at Miller High School, hopes to attend a summer program at her dream school, CalArts, but struggles with its application prompt asking her to describe her happiest moment, and considers writing about her longtime unrequited crush on the popular Gabby. Meanwhile, an anonymous artist known as KingPun has been covering the school with pun-filled graffiti, and because of her interest in art, Paige is widely suspected. To avoid suspension she agrees to join the track team and to help uncover the real culprit. Lacking athletic talent, she is placed in the 4×100 relay with Gabby and AJ, and AJ is assigned to train her.

Paige enlists AJ's help in her investigation, including at a house party she thinks KingPun will attend. During a stakeout at the school, Paige and Gabby share an awkward first kiss, and Paige's friend Dillon suggests that her crush may simply have faded as she grows closer to AJ. On a team trip to a meet, a game of seven minutes in heaven pairs Paige with AJ and they kiss, which AJ believes is a first for both of them. That night Paige turns down Gabby's attempt to kiss her. After Miller High finishes second in the relay, Gabby apologizes to Paige and inadvertently reveals their earlier kiss, leaving AJ heartbroken; AJ then reveals that she is KingPun. Paige tries to take the blame, only to learn that AJ has already confessed and been suspended. With Gabby's help, Paige makes amends at a school assembly with a large mural of the moments she and AJ have shared, which she also submits to CalArts. AJ's suspension is lifted, and the two reconcile with another kiss.

Filmed in the Syracuse area of New York in the summer of 2021 under the working title Love in Color, Crush was released on Hulu on April 29, 2022, and was the third most-streamed film in the United States that week. It holds 83% on Rotten Tomatoes and 56 on Metacritic, and Variety praised the diversity of its cast and the leads' chemistry.

overview: The children of the Avengers hone their powers and go head to head with the very enemy responsible for their parents' demise.
tagline: The children of heroes past are our only hope for the future!
title: Next Avengers: Heroes of Tomorrow
plot:
Next Avengers: Heroes of Tomorrow is a 2008 animated superhero film produced by Marvel Animation. The movie follows the story of a group of young superheroes, including Kate Bishop, Wiccan, Speed, and Patriot, as they team up to stop an alien invasion.

The main themes of Next Avengers: Heroes of Tomorrow include:

1. Coming-of-age: The movie explores the challenges and struggles faced by these young heroes as they navigate their newfound powers and responsibilities.
2. Teamwork and camaraderie: The film highlights the importance of teamwork, friendship, and trust among the young heroes as they work together to save the world from an alien threat.
3. Identity and self-discovery: Each character in the movie grapples with their own identity and sense of purpose, particularly Kate Bishop, who struggles to live up to her father's legacy.
4. Responsibility and duty: The film emphasizes the importance of taking responsibility for one's actions and fulfilling one's duties as a hero.

The movie also explores some deeper themes, such as:

1. The weight of legacy: Kate Bishop's struggle to live up to her father's reputation serves as a metaphor for the pressure that can come with having a famous or influential family member.
2. Balancing personal life and superhero responsibilities: Many of the characters in the movie face challenges in balancing their personal lives with their duties as superheroes.

Overall, Next Avengers: Heroes of Tomorrow is a fun and action-packed film that explores themes relevant to young adults and fans of the Marvel universe.

overview: After a teenager has a terrifying vision of him and his friends dying in a plane crash, he prevents the accident only to have Death hunt them down, one by one.
tagline: No accidents. No coincidences. No escapes.
title: Final Destination
plot:
Final Destination is a supernatural horror film directed by James Wong, released in 2000 by New Line Cinema.

The movie begins with Alex Browning (played by Devon Sawa), a high school student who survives a plane crash that kills everyone on board. As he's the only survivor, he starts to experience strange and unexplained events that seem to be connected to his near-death experience.

Alex soon discovers that he is having premonitions of people around him dying in gruesome and unexpected ways. He tries to warn his friends about these impending deaths, but they don't believe him. One by one, Alex's friends start to die in the most horrific ways possible, all seemingly connected to their own personal fears and anxieties.

As the death toll rises, Alex realizes that he is somehow responsible for these events, as if he has the ability to see into the future and prevent his friends from dying. He becomes obsessed with understanding the cause of these premonitions and tries to find a way to stop them.

The main antagonist of the film is Death itself, personified by a mysterious figure known only as "Death". Throughout the movie, Alex encounters various characters who are also aware of his ability to see into the future. These characters include Wendy (played by Ali Larter), a classmate who becomes Alex's love interest, and Clear River High School's principal, Mr. Smith (played by Jimmie E. Woods).

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Death is not just a random force of nature, but rather a malevolent entity that feeds on human fear and anxiety. The more people die, the stronger Death becomes.

In the climactic final act, Alex discovers that he can manipulate his premonitions to change the course of events. He uses this power to try and prevent Wendy from dying, but ultimately fails. In a shocking twist, it is revealed that Alex's ability to see into the future was not just a gift, but also a curse.

The movie ends with Alex realizing that he has become Death himself, trapped in a never-ending cycle of premonitions and death. The final shot of the film shows Alex standing alone, surrounded by the bodies of his dead friends, as the sound of a plane crashing echoes through the air.

Overall, Final Destination is a tense and suspenseful horror film that explores themes of fate, mortality, and the supernatural. With its clever plot twists and gruesome death scenes, it has become a cult classic among horror fans.

overview: A young girl is raised in a dysfunctional family constantly on the run from the FBI. Living in poverty, she comes of age guided by her drunkard, ingenious father who distracts her with magical stories to keep her mind off the family's dire state, and her selfish, nonconformist mother who has no intention of raising a family, along with her younger brother and sister, and her other older sister. Together, they fend for each other as they mature in an unorthodox journey that is their family life.
title: The Glass Castle
plot:
The Glass Castle is a 2017 American biographical drama directed by Destin Daniel Cretton, who wrote the screenplay with Andrew Lanham and Marti Noxon, based on Jeannette Walls's best-selling 2005 memoir about growing up in poverty with her unconventional parents. Lionsgate acquired the rights in 2012 with Jennifer Lawrence in talks to star, but Brie Larson took over the lead in 2015. Filming began on May 20, 2016, in Welch, West Virginia, and Lionsgate released the film on August 11, 2017.

Young Jeannette grows up on the move with her painter mother, Rose Mary, her brilliant but irresponsible, hard-drinking father, Rex, and her siblings Lori, Brian and later Maureen. After she is badly burned cooking alone, Rex sneaks her out of the hospital before social workers can intervene, and enchants her with plans to build the family a dream house of glass. On the run from the law and out of money, the family settles in a ramshackle house without utilities in Welch, near the children's grandmother Erma. Rex briefly beats his drinking by tying himself to his bed, but relapses, refuses to believe that Erma has sexually abused Brian, and fights violently with Rose Mary. The children promise to look after each other and escape. Lori leaves for New York, and after one of Rex's pool hustles leaves her fending off an attempted rape and he steals her savings, Jeannette follows.

By 1989 Jeannette is a gossip columnist for New York magazine engaged to David, a financial analyst, and lies to his clients about her family while her parents are homeless and squatting in the city. After Rex punches David and Jeannette learns that her parents had owned land worth nearly $1 million all along, she disowns her father. Unhappily married, she at first refuses to visit when Rex is dying, but eventually tells the truth about her upbringing and reconciles with him before his death. Divorced and working as a freelance writer, she later spends Thanksgiving with her family, remembering him.

Larson plays Jeannette, Woody Harrelson plays Rex, Naomi Watts plays Rose Mary, Sarah Snook plays Lori and Max Greenfield plays David. Critics praised the cast, especially Larson, but found the adaptation too forgiving of the parents, giving it 52% approval on Rotten Tomatoes. It grossed $22 million in North America.

overview: This remake of the beloved classic follows the raucous exploits of a blended family of 12, the Bakers, as they navigate a hectic home life while simultaneously managing their family business.
title: Cheaper by the Dozen
plot:
Cheaper by the Dozen is a 2022 American family comedy directed by Gail Lerner in her feature debut, from a screenplay by Kenya Barris and Jenifer Rice-Genzuk Henry, with Shawn Levy as an executive producer. A new take on the familiar story of a very large household, it stars Zach Braff and Gabrielle Union as Paul and Zoey Baker, parents of a blended multiracial family, with Erika Christensen and Timon Kyle Durrett as their former spouses.

Restaurateur Paul has two daughters, Ella and Harley, with his ex-wife, Kate, and the couple also took in their godson, Haresh, after his parents died. Zoey has two children, Deja and DJ, from her marriage to football player Dom Clayton, whose lifestyle led to their divorce. After meeting at Paul's restaurant, the pair turn it into an all-day breakfast spot, marry and have two sets of twins. When Paul's signature sauce lands on store shelves, he moves the family from Los Angeles to a large house in a gated community in Calabasas, where Zoey faces racial profiling from her neighbor Anne. Paul also takes in his nephew Seth while his sister is in rehab; Ella and Harley treat him as a delinquent, but he bonds with Haresh, who is bullied because of his race, and teaches him self-defense.

As Paul travels to scout new locations under pressure from investors to cut costs, Zoey fears he is repeating Dom's absences. Deja, sidelined on her new basketball team, sneaks out to see her boyfriend, Chris, Haresh and Seth are suspended for fighting bullies, and DJ changes his look to impress a girl. At DJ's birthday party, Deja reveals she has quit the team and that the children are miserable, and Dom announces he will seek custody of Deja and DJ. When the girls accuse Seth of a string of neighborhood break-ins, he storms off, but the family learns he is innocent, finds him and welcomes him as one of their own. Paul and Dom come to understand each other, Paul gives up the corporate deal to keep running the restaurant himself, and the family returns to Los Angeles, unveiling a new sauce bottle design that includes Seth.

The film premiered at the El Capitan Theatre on March 16, 2022, and was released on Disney+ on March 18. Reviews were mostly negative, with 35% on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 42; critics noted its modern twists but found few fresh laughs.

overview: When three high-school friends invent a time-machine, they decide to use it to go back in time and prevent other youngsters from making humiliating mistakes.
tagline: It's a short trip from zero... to hero.
title: Minutemen
plot:
Minutemen is a 2008 science fiction Disney Channel Original Movie directed by Lev L. Spiro, with a teleplay by John Killoran from a story by David Diamond and David Weissman. Jason Dolley stars as Virgil Fox, with Luke Benward, Nicholas Braun, Chelsea Staub, Steven R. McQueen and Kara Crane.

On their first day of high school, best friends Virgil, Derek and Stephanie try out different activities. When young genius Charlie disrupts football practice with a homemade rocket-powered vehicle, Virgil tries to help him, and both are publicly humiliated by the jocks. Three years on, Virgil and Charlie are outcasts, while Derek and Stephanie are popular and dating. Charlie designs a time machine, and with Virgil and another outcast, the engineering-minded Zeke, he builds it. On their first trip a street performer ends up keeping a winning lottery ticket meant for them.

The trio then decides to use the machine to undo classmates' humiliations, recruiting Jeannette, who has an unrequited crush on Charlie, to monitor their trips; she provides snowsuits against the freezing temperatures of the time stream. Students hail the anonymous heroes as the "Snowsuit Guys" rather than the "Minutemen" they prefer, while Vice Principal Tolkan sees them as troublemakers. Charlie, who hacked NASA's files to finish the machine, urges restraint, but Virgil uses it to save Stephanie from an injury and reveals his identity to her. At her request he helps Derek undo a loss at the state championship, rekindling those friendships while neglecting Charlie and Zeke, and when Stephanie catches Derek cheating, Virgil, now aware of his own feelings for her, hesitates to undo it. The FBI, which has been tracking them, interrogates the trio, and they split up over Virgil's selfishness. Government scientists tell Charlie that their trips have damaged space-time and created a black hole, and the three reunite to fix it. Sent back to their first day of high school, Virgil considers preventing his friendship with Charlie but learns that Charlie treasures that day and that Derek joined in the humiliation to make the team. The trio escapes the closing black hole, and back in the present nobody remembers their exploits. Virgil confronts Derek and tells Stephanie how he feels.

The film premiered on Disney Channel on January 25, 2008 and with 6.48 million viewers was the most watched program on American cable that week. Spiro received a Directors Guild of America nomination for his work.

overview: As the war between the vampires and the Lycans rages on, Selene, a former member of the Death Dealers (an elite vampire special forces unit that hunts werewolves), and Michael, the werewolf hybrid, work together in an effort to unlock the secrets of their respective bloodlines.
tagline: My God. Brother, what have you done?
title: Underworld: Evolution
plot:
Underworld: Evolution is a 2006 supernatural action film directed by Patrick Tatopoulos and written by Len Wiseman and Danny McBride. The movie serves as a sequel to the 2003 film Underworld, starring Kate Beckinsale as Selene, a vampire warrior.

The story begins with Selene (Kate Beckinsale) being resurrected from her death in the first film by a group of vampires who believe she is destined to fulfill an ancient prophecy. The prophecy states that Selene will be the one to bring about the end of the war between humans and vampires, as well as the destruction of both species.

As Selene awakens, she finds herself in a desolate wasteland, surrounded by a group of vampires who claim to have been sent by her maker, Kraven (Shane Brolly). They inform her that she has been chosen to fulfill the prophecy and that she must find the Lycan leader, Lucian (Scott Speedman), who is also destined for greatness.

Selene soon discovers that she is not alone in her quest. A group of humans, led by Alexander Corvinus (Tom Cruise), are also searching for Lucian, believing him to be the key to their survival. As Selene navigates this treacherous landscape, she must confront her own destiny and the true nature of her existence as a vampire.

Throughout the film, Selene encounters various characters who aid or hinder her progress. These include Michael Corvin (Scott Speedman), Alexander's son, who becomes embroiled in the conflict; Kraven, who seeks to use Selene for his own purposes; and the Lycan leader, Lucian, who is torn between his loyalty to his pack and his growing feelings for Selene.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the prophecy is more complex than initially thought. The true nature of the war between humans and vampires is revealed, as well as the motivations behind Alexander's actions.
