Ultimately, Selene must make a choice between her own existence and the fate of humanity, leading to a climactic showdown with Kraven and Lucian.

The film concludes with Selene emerging victorious but not without scars. She has come to terms with her destiny and is ready to face whatever challenges lie ahead. The ending sets the stage for potential future sequels, leaving audiences wondering what the future holds for this iconic vampire warrior.

Overall, Underworld: Evolution offers a thrilling and action-packed ride, exploring themes of identity, loyalty, and the blurred lines between good and evil.

overview: A retelling of the biblical book of Hosea set against the backdrop of the California Gold Rush of 1850.
tagline: Never look back. Never look forward.
title: Redeeming Love
plot:
Redeeming Love is a 2022 American Christian Western romance directed by D.J. Caruso, who wrote the screenplay with Francine Rivers from her 1991 novel, itself a retelling of the biblical story of Hosea set during the California Gold Rush. Produced by Pinnacle Peak Pictures, Mission Pictures International and Nthibah Pictures, it was filmed in Cape Town, South Africa, in February 2020. Delayed by the COVID-19 pandemic, it was released by Universal Pictures on January 21, 2022.

In the mining town of Pair-a-Dice, a young prostitute called Angel survives on hatred and self-loathing. Flashbacks reveal that she was born Sarah, the unwanted daughter of a wealthy man's mistress, Mae. After her father abandoned them, her mother was forced into prostitution and died, and the girl was sold to the pimp Duke, who renamed her Angel. Farmer Michael Hosea, who has prayed for a wife, falls in love with her at first sight and keeps returning to propose. When the brothel's enforcer nearly beats her to death, Michael pays her debt, marries her and nurses her back to health on his farm, loving her as his wife without demanding intimacy.

Angel slowly comes to love Michael, but believing she is barren because of a forced abortion, she runs away more than once. The second time, Michael's brother-in-law Paul demands sex in exchange for a ride, and Angel finds the brothel burned down and returns to selling herself until Michael brings her home. Convinced that Miriam, the eldest daughter of a family they have taken in, would make him a better wife, Angel leaves her wedding ring for Miriam and disappears. Working at a cafe, she falls back into Duke's hands, then exposes his trafficking of young girls in front of an audience, and an outraged mob lynches him. She devotes herself to rescuing girls, and three years later Paul, now married to Miriam, tells her Michael is still waiting. Angel returns, reveals that her real name is Sarah, and the couple later appear with a young son and another child on the way.

Abigail Cowen plays Angel, Tom Lewis plays Michael and Logan Marshall-Green plays Paul, with Famke Janssen as the madam Duchess, Nina Dobrev as Mae and Eric Dane as Duke. Critics were harsh, with 11% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, while audiences gave it a B+ CinemaScore. It grossed $9.46 million worldwide against a $30 million budget, and was nominated for a GMA Dove Award.

original_title: The Day the Earth Stood Still
overview: A representative of an alien race that went through drastic evolution to survive its own climate change, Klaatu comes to Earth to assess whether humanity can prevent the environmental damage they have inflicted on their own planet. When barred from speaking to the United Nations, he decides humankind shall be exterminated so the planet can survive.
tagline: 12.12.08 is the Day the Earth Stood Still
title: The Day the Earth Stood Still
plot:
The Day the Earth Stood Still is a 2008 American science fiction film directed by Scott Derrickson from a screenplay by David Scarpa, remaking the 1951 film of the same name, which was based on the 1940 short story "Farewell to the Master". This version replaces the original's Cold War fear of nuclear war with concern about humanity's damage to the environment. Keanu Reeves, who agreed because he saw the script as a reimagining, stars as the alien Klaatu and insisted that the line "Klaatu barada nikto" be included.

In 1928 a mountaineer in the Karakoram meets a glowing sphere and wakes with a scar on his hand. In the present day, an object speeding toward Earth turns out to be a giant spherical ship that lands in Central Park. Astrobiologist Helen Benson, recruited by NASA official Michael Granier, watches as the emerging alien is shot and a towering robot disables the troops until the wounded being commands it to stop. In the laboratory, the alien sheds its placenta-like suit and becomes Klaatu, resembling the 1928 climber. He tells Secretary of Defense Regina Jackson that an alliance of planetary civilizations has sent him to save Earth from humanity, then escapes interrogation and turns to Helen and her stepson, Jacob.

As smaller spheres collect animal species around the world, Klaatu meets Mr. Wu, an alien living on Earth who considers humans destructive but has come to love them. Helen takes Klaatu to Nobel laureate Professor Barnhardt, who argues that humanity, like Klaatu's own people, can change when faced with extinction. Meanwhile the captured robot, nicknamed GORT, dissolves into a swarm of self-replicating insect-like machines that devour every man-made object in their path. At the grave of Jacob's father, Klaatu witnesses the boy's grief and the love between him and Helen and decides to stop the swarm. He walks through it to touch the sphere, sacrificing himself, and the swarm halts, though all electronics on Earth shut down as the sphere departs.

Jennifer Connelly plays Helen, Jaden Smith plays Jacob, Kathy Bates plays Jackson, John Cleese plays Barnhardt and Jon Hamm plays Granier. Critics were largely negative, with 21% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, but the film opened at number one in North America and grossed $233.1 million worldwide on an $80 million budget. Smith won a Saturn Award for his performance.

overview: After a family moves into the Heelshire Mansion, their young son soon makes friends with a life-like doll called Brahms.
tagline: He's made a friend.
title: Brahms: The Boy II
plot:
Brahms: The Boy II is a 2018 American supernatural horror film directed by William Brent Bell and written by Christopher Bubley. It was released on February 2, 2018, not in 2020 as mentioned.

The movie serves as a sequel to the 2016 film Brahms: The Boy. The story follows Elizabeth Brenner (Linda Cardellini), who has moved away from the haunted house with her husband Steve (Auggie Maturo) and their young son Josh (Jacob Tremblay). However, they soon discover that the malevolent spirit of Brahms, a German dollmaker, is still present in the house.

As the family tries to rebuild their lives, strange occurrences start to happen again. The dollmaker's presence becomes more pronounced, and Elizabeth begins to experience terrifying visions and nightmares. She starts to suspect that Brahms has followed her and her family to their new home.

The movie takes a darker turn as Josh becomes increasingly possessed by Brahms' spirit. As the events escalate, Elizabeth realizes that she must find a way to stop Brahms once and for all before it's too late. The film builds up to a thrilling climax as Elizabeth confronts the evil dollmaker in a desperate bid to save her family.

Throughout the movie, the atmosphere is tense and foreboding, with a sense of dread that permeates every scene. The special effects are impressive, bringing Brahms to life in a way that's both terrifying and mesmerizing.

One of the standout aspects of the film is its exploration of themes such as grief, trauma, and the supernatural. Elizabeth's character is particularly well-developed, as she struggles to come to terms with her past and find a way to move on from the horrors she experienced in the first film.

Overall, Brahms: The Boy II is a chilling horror movie that will keep you on the edge of your seat. With its creepy atmosphere, impressive special effects, and well-developed characters, it's a must-see for fans of the supernatural genre.

overview: On a bleak future Earth, a soldier endures a radical genetic transformation to save humanity. But his wife fears he's becoming more creature than man.
tagline: Evolve or die
title: The Titan
plot:
The Titan is a 2018 science fiction thriller film directed by Lennart Ruff from a screenplay by Max Hurwitz, based on a story by Arash Amel. An international co-production between the United Kingdom, the United States, Germany and Spain, it stars Sam Worthington, Taylor Schilling and Tom Wilkinson, with Agyness Deyn and Nathalie Emmanuel in supporting roles. The story follows a military pilot who undergoes radical genetic modification to prepare humanity for life on Saturn's moon Titan.

In 2048, with an overpopulated Earth torn by violent conflicts, scientists led by Professor Martin Collingwood see Titan as a new home for humanity. U.S. Air Force pilot Rick Janssen volunteers for an experiment on fourteen test subjects meant to adapt human bodies to the moon's frigid methane seas and thin oxygen atmosphere, and moves to the Titan I research area with his wife Abigail, a medical researcher, and their son Lucas. Early results are promising: Rick can swim at great speed and stay underwater for 42 minutes. But as training intensifies, his hair falls out, his skin sheds, one volunteer dies of convulsions and the subjects' veins darken. Another volunteer, Zane, suffers breakdowns and kills his wife Rayenne, Abigail's friend, before being shot by military police. Stealing Rick's key card, Abigail finds autopsy reports revealing that the subjects' DNA is being combined with animal DNA to create a new species, Homo titaniens, and Collingwood admits he does not know what the survivors will become. Rick and Tally, the only other surviving subject, complete their transformation, and Rick loses the ability to speak. After Tally kills her husband and is shot, Rick kills several military police officers and flees, and Abigail finds him before both are arrested. Ordered to give Rick a solution that would erase his memories, Abigail secretly substitutes saline, and she and Lucas escape with Dr. Freya Upton, a dissenting assistant of Collingwood's. Soldiers refuse Collingwood's order to fire on them, and the colonel arrests him. Abigail and Freya later continue the research at the Titan II facility by more ethical methods, while Rick is seen flying over a methane lake on Titan.

Netflix released The Titan in several countries on March 30, 2018, and it opened in British cinemas that April. Shot in Gran Canaria, it received generally negative reviews, holding a 23% Rotten Tomatoes rating with a consensus calling it bland and uninspired.

overview: A reformed sociopath heads to a remote island after the death of his brother. Soon after his arrival, the island falls under siege from a deadly gang of mercenaries, and when he discovers their role in his brother’s demise, he sets out on a relentless quest for vengeance.
tagline: Killer instincts die hard.
title: Dangerous
plot:
Dangerous is a 2021 action thriller directed by David Hackl, his fifth feature, starring Scott Eastwood, Tyrese Gibson, Famke Janssen, Kevin Durand and Mel Gibson. It was produced by Kevin DeWalt, Ben DeWalt and Doug Falconer through Minds Eye Entertainment and Falconer Pictures, and was Falconer's last film as a producer before his sudden death in July 2021. Shooting took place in Canada, including Kamloops and the Okanagan, between November and December 2020, during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Dylan Forrester, a former assassin with psychopathic tendencies, has been keeping his instincts in check with mood-stabilizing medication under the supervision of Dr. Alderwood. When his brother Sean dies suddenly, Dylan breaks his parole to travel to Guardian Island, which belongs to his family, hoping to make peace with his mother, Linda, who fears what he is and urges him to leave. Agent Shaughnessy is hunting him, convinced he is too dangerous to be free. On the island, Sheriff McCoy discovers that Dylan is a fugitive and locks him in a bunker.

A fixer named Cole then arrives with a team of mercenaries and kills the sheriff. Freed by a hotel employee named Jo, Dylan returns to protect his family, taking out several of Cole's men. He suspects that Sean had been hiding something, and the survivors discover a secret passage that leads to a Japanese World War II submarine loaded with Yamashita's gold. Sean had partnered with Cole in buying the island to find the treasure. In a shootout around the submarine, Dylan and an ally named Massey turn one of its deck guns on the mercenaries before Cole kills Massey and takes Linda hostage. Dylan dumps the gold Cole wanted into the water, Shaughnessy arrives and is wounded, and Dylan finally stabs Cole to death and rescues his mother. Leaving with some of the gold, he says goodbye to Dr. Alderwood by phone and throws his medication into the ocean.

Eastwood plays Dylan, Durand plays Cole, Janssen plays Shaughnessy, Tyrese Gibson plays Sheriff McCoy and Mel Gibson plays Dr. Alderwood. Lionsgate released the film in American and Canadian theaters and on demand on 5 November 2021. Reviews were negative, with 30% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 27, and it received two Golden Raspberry nominations and two Canadian Screen Award nominations. It later reached streaming top-ten charts in 17 countries.

original_title: The Flintstones & WWE: Stone Age SmackDown!
overview: The WWE comes to town in the new animated film teaming the Flintstones with Bedrock-ready versions of John Cena, Daniel Bryan and more.
title: The Flintstones & WWE: Stone Age SmackDown!
plot:
The Flintstones & WWE: Stone Age SmackDown! is a 2015 American direct-to-video animated film directed by Spike Brandt and Tony Cervone. The second co-production between Warner Bros. Animation and WWE Studios, it places Fred Flintstone, Barney Rubble and the rest of Bedrock alongside Stone Age versions of WWE wrestlers. Jeff Bergman voices Fred, Kevin Michael Richardson Barney, Tress MacNeille Wilma and Grey Griffin Betty, while John Cena, CM Punk, Rey Mysterio, Mark Henry, Brie and Nikki Bella, Vince McMahon and The Undertaker voice their animated counterparts.

Fred has promised his wife, Wilma, a vacation, but his boss, Mr. Slate, refuses him time off and money, having just hired a relative, John Cenastone. At a fair run by the Lodge of Water Buffaloes, Fred tries to raise cash by having Hoppy, the pet hopparoo of his friend Barney, box challengers. Hoppy wins repeatedly until the thug CM Punkrock humiliates him, and an outraged Barney defeats Punkrock, who storms off with his partner, Marble Henry. Seeing a chance to make money from wrestling, Fred teams up with a seafood seller, Mr. McMagma, to stage a show at an abandoned circus. Cenastone recruits the masked clerk Rey Mysteriopal and The Undertaker, a gloomy gravedigger, and Fred pushes a reluctant Barney into the ring against The Undertaker. Barney is about to win when Wilma and Betty arrive to scold their husbands, but the trouble passes because Fred has made enough money.

Inspired by McMagma, Fred wants more and rents Bedrock Stadium for a rematch between Barney and Punkrock, also booking Henry and the Boulder Twins. Barney refuses to take part, and Fred goes ahead without him. When Fred admits Barney will not appear, the other wrestlers walk out, disappointed that he has neglected his friend, and Fred is left to face Punkrock and his allies alone, taking a beating. Moved by Fred's sacrifice, Barney joins the fight with the other wrestlers, Wilma and Betty intimidate the Boulder Twins and young Bamm-Bamm easily defeats Henry. After the victory, Fred quits wrestling, sells the idea to McMagma and takes everyone on vacation.

Warner Home Video released the film on March 10, 2015. It was the first new Flintstones production in more than thirteen years, and Russi Taylor's last film. IndieWire wrote that it recaptured the heyday of Hanna-Barbera so meticulously that it left viewers yearning for more Flintstones cartoons.

overview: Nine years later, Jesse travels across Europe giving readings from a book he wrote about the night he spent in Vienna with Celine. After his reading in Paris, Celine finds him, and they spend part of the day together before Jesse has to again leave for a flight. They are both in relationships now, and Jesse has a son, but as their strong feelings for each other start to return, both confess a longing for more.
tagline: What if you had a second chance with the one that got away?
title: Before Sunset
plot:
Before Sunset is a 2004 American romantic drama directed by Richard Linklater, who wrote the screenplay with its stars Ethan Hawke and Julie Delpy from a story by Linklater and Kim Krizan. The sequel to Before Sunrise (1995) and the second part of the Before trilogy, it was the first release from Warner Independent Pictures. After plans for a larger-budget sequel failed to find funding, the four collaborators drew on years of draft scripts, and Linklater compiled the final screenplay from monologues and scenes that Hawke and Delpy sent him. It was shot entirely in Paris and unfolds in real time.

Nine years after spending one night with Céline in Vienna, Jesse is a successful author whose novel, This Time, is based on that encounter. At the end of a reading at the Shakespeare and Company bookstore in Paris, during his European book tour, he sees Céline, who now lives in the city. With barely an hour before he has to leave for the airport, they walk through Paris, through cafes and gardens and aboard a tourist boat on the Seine. They explain why their planned reunion in Vienna never happened: Céline's grandmother had died, while Jesse, after first pretending otherwise, admits that he did come back.

As they talk about work, politics and their pasts, it emerges that Jesse is in an unhappy marriage with a young son, Hank, while Céline, who works for an environmental organization, is with a photojournalist but struggles to sustain relationships. Both confess that their night together left them dissatisfied with love ever since, and Jesse admits that he wrote the book hoping to find her again. Jesse's car takes Céline home, and he talks his way into her apartment, where she plays him a waltz on her guitar that she wrote about their night in Vienna. As Nina Simone's "Just in Time" plays and Céline dances, both understand that he is going to miss his flight.

Hawke and Delpy reprise their roles, and Delpy also contributed original music to the soundtrack. The film premiered at the Berlin International Film Festival in February 2004 and opened in the United States on July 2, 2004, grossing about $16 million worldwide. It was widely acclaimed, with 94% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 91, and its screenplay was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay.

belongs_to_collection.name: Family Guy Trilogy Collection: Laugh It Up, Fuzzball!

original_title: Family Guy Presents: It's a Trap!
overview: With the Griffins stuck again at home during a blackout, Peter tells the story of “Star Wars Episode VI: Return of the Jedi.”
tagline: Clear some Space for the third chapter of the funniest trilogy in the Galaxy!
title: Family Guy Presents: It's a Trap!
plot:
Family Guy Presents: It's a Trap! is an animated science fiction comedy film that parodies Star Wars: Episode V - The Empire Strikes Back. The movie follows Peter Griffin and his friends as they try to rescue Stewie, who has been kidnapped by the evil Emperor Palpatine.

The main theme of Family Guy Presents: It's a Trap! revolves around the idea of obsession and the dangers of allowing one's desires to consume them. Stewie's kidnapping serves as a catalyst for Peter's journey, which is driven by his desperation to rescue his son and prove himself as a hero. However, as Peter navigates through various challenges and obstacles, he begins to realize that his motivations are not entirely pure.

The film also explores the theme of family dynamics and the complexities of relationships within a dysfunctional family. Peter's actions are often driven by his desire to be loved and accepted by his family, particularly Stewie, who is perceived as the perfect child. Through Peter's journey, the movie highlights the flaws and imperfections of its characters, showcasing how their individual quirks and flaws can both unite and drive them apart.

Furthermore, Family Guy Presents: It's a Trap! pokes fun at the conventions of science fiction and adventure films, using satire to comment on the genre's tropes and clichés. The movie's over-the-top action sequences, melodramatic plot twists, and absurd humor all serve as a commentary on the excesses and absurdities of the Star Wars franchise.

Overall, Family Guy Presents: It's a Trap! is a lighthearted, comedic take on science fiction and adventure films, using satire to explore themes of obsession, family dynamics, and the complexities of relationships.

overview: Fed up with all the attention going to Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck quits Hollywood, teams up with recently-fired stuntman Damien Drake Jr. and embarks on a round-the-world adventure, along with Bugs and The VP of Warner Bros. Their mission? Find Damien's father, and the missing blue diamond... and stay one step ahead of The Acme Corp., who wants the diamond for their own purposes.
production_companies: Lonely Film Productions GmbH & Co. KG.
tagline: Real life has never been so animated.
title: Looney Tunes: Back in Action
plot:
Looney Tunes: Back in Action is a 2003 live-action/animated comedy film directed by Joe Dante and produced by Warner Bros. Pictures. The movie brings together the beloved Looney Tunes characters with real-world celebrities, blending live-action and animation.

The story begins with James "Jim" Davis (played by Brendan Fraser), an action movie star who is struggling to find his next big role. Jim's life takes a turn when he meets Bugs Bunny (voiced by Billy West) and Daffy Duck (voiced by Jeff Bergman), the iconic cartoon characters, in a Las Vegas nightclub.

The two are on a mission to stop the villainous Marvin Acme (played by Steve Martin), who has stolen the world's most valuable diamond, the "Acme Diamond." Marvin plans to use the diamond to fund his latest scheme: creating an army of robotic Acme brand products that will take over the world.

Jim is recruited by Bugs and Daffy to help them on their mission. Along the way, they are joined by Lola Bunny (voiced by Rosie O'Donnell), a basketball player who becomes Jim's love interest. The group embarks on a series of wacky misadventures as they try to outsmart Marvin and his robotic minions.

Throughout the movie, the Looney Tunes characters interact with the real-world celebrities in hilarious ways. Jim often finds himself caught up in the zany antics of Bugs and Daffy, while Lola Bunny provides a more grounded perspective on the situation.

As the story unfolds, Jim begins to realize that he has been living a shallow life as an action movie star. He starts to develop feelings for Lola and learns to appreciate the value of friendship and teamwork. In the end, Jim and his new friends successfully stop Marvin's plan, saving the world from the robotic Acme products.

The movie features plenty of references to classic Looney Tunes cartoons, with many memorable moments and gags that will delight fans of the franchise. The film also pokes fun at action movie conventions and the absurdity of Hollywood blockbusters.

Overall, Looney Tunes: Back in Action is a lighthearted, entertaining film that brings together the best of both worlds: live-action comedy and beloved cartoon characters. While it may not be a masterpiece, it's a fun and silly ride that will leave audiences smiling.

overview: The untold true story set in the winter of 1925 that takes you across the treacherous terrain of the Alaskan tundra for an exhilarating and uplifting adventure that will test the strength, courage and determination of one man, Leonhard Seppala, and his lead sled dog, Togo.
tagline: The untold true story.
title: Togo
plot:
Togo is a 2019 American biographical drama film directed by Ross Katz and produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The film is based on the true story of Leonhard Seppala, a Finnish-Swedish sled dog breeder who played a crucial role in saving the life of a young boy during a diphtheria outbreak in Nome, Alaska.

The film begins with Leonhard Seppala (played by Willem Dafoe), a struggling sled dog breeder living on his farm in Nome. He is married to Rose (played by Anne Hathaway), and they have two children together. The story takes a dramatic turn when the town of Nome is hit by a diphtheria outbreak, which claims the lives of many residents.

The situation becomes dire as the town's medical supplies are running low, and the only way to transport medicine from Bluff, Alaska (about 674 miles away) is through sled dogs. The US Army sends a team led by Captain Balto (played by Paul Giamatti), who is tasked with delivering the diphtheria serum to Nome.

Leonhard Seppala, determined to save his community, decides to take on the challenge of leading the sled dog team himself. He chooses his most experienced and strongest dogs, including Togo (played by a combination of two dogs: Buck and Tundra), to make the perilous journey.

As the team sets out, they face numerous challenges, including treacherous terrain, harsh weather conditions, and the risk of losing their dogs in the process. Despite these obstacles, Seppala's determination and expertise as a sled dog breeder keep the team moving forward.

Meanwhile, Captain Balto is struggling with his own doubts about leading the mission. He is haunted by a past failure to deliver supplies during a previous expedition, which led to the death of several people in Nome.

As the journey progresses, Seppala's team faces numerous setbacks, including a near-fatal accident that leaves Togo injured. However, Seppala refuses to give up and continues to push his dogs forward, driven by his love for his community and his determination to save lives.

In the end, Seppala's team successfully delivers the diphtheria serum to Nome, saving countless lives in the process. The film ends with a poignant moment of reflection, as Seppala looks back on the journey and realizes that it was not just about delivering supplies but also about the bond between humans and animals.

Throughout the film, Willem Dafoe delivers a powerful performance as Leonhard Seppala, capturing the complexity and depth of his character. The chemistry between him and Anne Hathaway is undeniable, adding an emotional layer to the story. Paul Giamatti's portrayal of Captain Balto is equally impressive, conveying the weight of responsibility and the personal stakes involved in leading the mission.

Overall, Togo is a heartwarming and inspiring film that celebrates the human spirit and the unbreakable bond between humans and animals.

overview: Majestic mountains, a still lake and venomous betrayals engulf a female married couple attempting to celebrate their one-year anniversary.
tagline: There's a demon inside.
title: What Keeps You Alive
plot:
What Keeps You Alive is a 2018 Canadian psychological horror film written and directed by Colin Minihan, starring Hannah Emily Anderson and Brittany Allen. Early drafts centered on a husband and wife before the leads became a same-sex couple. The film was shot in Muskoka, Ontario, and Allen also composed its score, her first credit as a composer. It premiered at the SXSW Film Festival on March 10, 2018, and IFC Midnight released it in Los Angeles and New York and on video on demand on August 24, 2018.

Jackie and her wife, Jules, celebrate their first anniversary at a remote lakeside cabin owned by Jackie's family. Jules grows uneasy when Jackie's childhood friend Sarah calls her "Megan", a name Jackie says she dropped because the new one suits her better, and when Jules learns from Sarah and her husband, Daniel, that a girl named Jenny drowned in the lake when they were young. Jackie tearfully claims she has always blamed herself, and the couple seem reconciled, until Jackie shoves Jules off a cliff and goes back to rehearse a grief-stricken call to the police.

Jules survives and, watching Jackie search the woods, realizes that her wife's sobbing is an act. She tries to escape across the lake but is caught, and Jackie admits that she never loved her and plans to collect her life insurance. When Jules tries to alert Sarah during a dinner, Jackie murders Daniel and Sarah, confessing to Sarah that she killed Jenny too, and forces Jules to help hide the bodies. She explains that she has simply always lacked feeling or conscience, and Jules finds a hidden box of necklaces that Jackie gave to earlier wives. Jules escapes another trip to the cliff with a tranquilizer dart, but after a final fight Jackie throws her over the edge again and calls the police. When the diabetic Jackie takes her insulin, a video left by Jules reveals that it has been replaced with hydrogen peroxide, and Jackie collapses in the woods and dies of a stroke, while at the foot of the cliff Jules draws breath.

Anderson plays Jackie and Allen plays Jules, with Martha MacIsaac as Sarah and Joey Klein as Daniel. Reviews were positive, with 80% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 66. IndieWire praised the leads and the film's update of the Final Girl trope, while Newsweek felt it reduced its villain to a simple psychopath.

overview: Rose, a desperate mother takes her adopted daughter, Sharon, to the town of Silent Hill in an attempt to cure her of her ailment. After a violent car crash, Sharon disappears and Rose begins a desperate search to get her back. She descends into the center of the twisted reality of a town's terrible secret. Pursued by grotesquely deformed creatures and townspeople stuck in permanent purgatory, Rose begins to uncover the truth behind the apocalyptic disaster that burned the town 30 years earlier.
tagline: Once you enter Silent Hill, there is no turning back.
title: Silent Hill
plot:
Silent Hill is a psychological horror film directed by Christophe Gans, released in 2006. The movie stars Sean Bean as Harry Mason, Radha Mitchell as Maria Sullivan, and Laurie Holden as Heather Mason.

The story begins with a car accident on a foggy night in the town of Silent Hill. Harry Mason (Sean Bean) finds himself injured and separated from his daughter, Heather (Laurie Holden), who is being pursued by a group of cult-like figures. As Harry searches for his daughter, he discovers that she has been taken to an abandoned hospital.

Upon arriving at the hospital, Harry meets Maria Sullivan (Radha Mitchell), a nurse who claims to be searching for her own daughter, Alessa Gillespie (Abigail Spencer). Maria reveals that Alessa was a patient at the hospital and had been subjected to inhumane experiments by a cult-like group known as the Order of the Blackened Sun.

As Harry and Maria delve deeper into the mystery, they uncover a dark history about Silent Hill. The town has a reputation for being cursed, and many people who have entered it have never returned. They soon discover that Alessa was chosen to be the vessel for a supernatural entity known as Pyramid Head, a symbol of punishment and execution.

Throughout the film, Harry and Maria navigate through the fog-shrouded streets of Silent Hill, encountering various monsters and hallucinations that seem to be manifestations of their own guilt and trauma. They also uncover clues about Alessa's past and the true nature of the cult.

As they progress, Harry begins to experience strange visions and nightmares, hinting at his own dark past. Maria, on the other hand, seems to be hiding secrets about her daughter's disappearance. The tension builds as they get closer to the truth, but also face numerous challenges and obstacles that test their resolve.

The climax of the film takes place in a church, where Harry confronts Alessa, now possessed by Pyramid Head. In a shocking twist, it is revealed that Alessa was not just a victim but an active participant in her own torture. The cult had been using her as a vessel to summon the entity, and she had become trapped in this cycle of pain.

In the end, Harry manages to escape Silent Hill with Maria's help, but not before facing his own demons and confronting the darkness within himself. The film ends on a hopeful note, suggesting that Harry has found redemption and is ready to move forward.

Silent Hill received mixed reviews from critics but has since become a cult classic, praised for its atmospheric tension, eerie visuals, and thought-provoking themes.

overview: After suffering a family tragedy, Mack Phillips spirals into a deep depression causing him to question his innermost beliefs. Facing a crisis of faith, he receives a mysterious letter urging him to an abandoned shack deep in the Oregon wilderness. Despite his doubts, Mack journeys to the shack and encounters an enigmatic trio of strangers led by a woman named Papa. Through this meeting, Mack finds important truths that will transform his understanding of his tragedy and change his life forever.
tagline: You're never as alone as you think.
title: The Shack
plot:
The Shack is a 2017 American drama film directed by Charlie McDowell and written by John Fusco. The movie is based on the 2007 novel of the same name by William P. Young.

The story begins with Mackenzie "Mack" Phillips (played by Sam Worthington), a former pastor who has lost his faith after a traumatic event in his childhood. When his wife, Helen (played by Octavia Spencer), is diagnosed with cancer, Mack's world is turned upside down. He becomes obsessed with finding the Shack, a mysterious place where he believes God resides.

Mack's search for the Shack leads him to a remote cabin in the woods, where he encounters three figures: Papa (played by Max von Sydow), Sarayu (played by Younghoe Koo), and Jesus (played by Tim Roth). These figures claim to be the embodiment of God, love, and redemption.

As Mack spends more time with these figures, he begins to confront his past traumas and the pain that has driven him away from faith. Papa, the figure representing God's fatherly love, teaches Mack about the importance of forgiveness and letting go of anger. Sarayu, the figure representing God's motherly love, shows Mack the beauty of unconditional love and acceptance.

Jesus, the figure representing the Son of God, reveals to Mack that he has been searching for him all along. Jesus tells Mack that his wife is dying because she has been carrying a heavy burden of guilt and shame, which only Mack can help her overcome.

As Mack spends more time with Jesus, he begins to understand the true nature of God's love and redemption. He realizes that God is not a distant figure, but a loving presence that is always with him.

However, as Mack's journey progresses, he also faces challenges from his own past. His father, who was abusive and neglectful, appears in the form of Big Daddy (played by Greg Kinnear), a figure representing the darkness and pain that Mack has tried to escape.

In the end, Mack must confront his inner demons and make a choice between his old life and his new one. He chooses to forgive his father and let go of his anger, which allows him to heal and find peace.

The movie ends with Mack returning home to his wife, who is now at peace. Mack realizes that he has been given a second chance at life and love, and he is determined to make the most of it.

Overall, The Shack is a powerful and emotional film that explores themes of faith, forgiveness, and redemption. While some critics have questioned the movie's depiction of God and its portrayal of trauma, the film remains a thought-provoking and moving exploration of the human condition.

overview: The story of the Arthurian legend, based on the 'Sarmatian hypothesis' which contends that the legend has a historical nucleus in the Sarmatian heavy cavalry troops stationed in Britain, and that the Roman-British military commander, Lucius Artorius Castus is the historical person behind the legend.
tagline: Rule Your Fate.
title: King Arthur
plot:
King Arthur is an epic historical adventure film of 2004 directed by Antoine Fuqua and written by David Franzoni, which recasts the legendary king as a Roman officer in fifth-century Britain rather than a medieval knight. Clive Owen stars as Arthur, with Ioan Gruffudd as Lancelot, Keira Knightley as Guinevere, Mads Mikkelsen as Tristan, Ray Winstone as Bors, Stephen Dillane as Merlin, Stellan Skarsgård as the Saxon leader Cerdic and Til Schweiger as his son Cynric.

As the declining Roman Empire withdraws from Britain, the native Woads, led by Merlin, wage an insurgency. Arthur, the half-British commander Artorius Castus, and his Sarmatian knights have completed fifteen years of compulsory service for Rome and are ready to go home. Instead Bishop Germanus orders one last mission: to rescue an important Roman family living north of Hadrian's Wall before an invading Saxon army under Cerdic and Cynric arrives, whose son Alecto may one day be pope. Arthur and his surviving knights, Lancelot, Tristan, Galahad, Bors, Gawain and Dagonet, reluctantly agree.

At the estate they find that the patriarch Marius, who refuses to leave, has enslaved the local people. Arthur frees two tortured Woad prisoners, Guinevere and her young brother, and forces Marius to leave. As the convoy flees through the mountains with the Saxons in pursuit, Marius attempts a revolt and is killed by Guinevere. Learning from Alecto that Germanus and the bishops had his beloved mentor Pelagius executed for heresy, Arthur grows disillusioned with Rome, while Guinevere and Merlin remind him of his bond with Britain through his Celtic mother. On a frozen lake Arthur's men confront Cynric's troops, and Dagonet gives his life breaking the ice with his axe to halt them. The knights deliver Alecto and his mother safely to the Wall and receive their discharge, but Arthur resolves to stay and fight with his mother's people. After a night with Guinevere, he confronts Cerdic under a flag of truce, and his knights return to fight beside him. At the Battle of Badon Hill, Lancelot kills Cynric but is mortally wounded, Cerdic kills Tristan and Arthur slays Cerdic, breaking the Saxon assault. Arthur marries Guinevere, Merlin proclaims him king of the Britons.

Released in July 2004, the film grossed $203.6 million worldwide against a $120 million budget. Critics were largely unimpressed, giving it 30% on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus called it a dreary, generic action movie.

overview: A semi-biographical account of Yip Man, the first martial arts master to teach the Chinese martial art of Wing Chun. The film focuses on events surrounding Ip that took place in the city of Foshan between the 1930s to 1940s during the Second Sino-Japanese War. Directed by Wilson Yip, the film stars Donnie Yen in the lead role, and features fight choreography by Sammo Hung.
production_companies: Beijing ShengShi HuaRei Film Investment & Management Co.
New Film Studio of Beijing Starlight International Media Co. Ltd.
tagline: The celebrated Kung Fu master of Bruce Lee.
title: Ip Man
plot:
Ip Man (2008) is a biographical martial arts film directed by Wilson Yip, starring Donnie Yen as the titular character, Ip Man.

The main themes of Ip Man (2008) include:

1. Perseverance and Resilience: The film showcases Ip Man's unwavering dedication to his craft and his ability to overcome adversity, including the Japanese invasion of China during World War II.
2. Loyalty and Family: Ip Man's relationships with his family, particularly his wife Cheung Wing-sing (played by Lynn Hung) and his son Ip Ching (played by Sammo Hung), are central to the film. His loyalty to them is tested when he is forced to flee China and settle in Hong Kong.
3. Identity and Belonging: As a Chinese martial artist living in Hong Kong, Ip Man struggles with his identity and sense of belonging. The film explores his efforts to balance his cultural heritage with his new life in the British colony.
4. Honor and Integrity: Ip Man's commitment to his art and his values is unwavering, even when faced with temptation or pressure from others. This theme is reflected in his relationships with his students and his rivalries with other martial artists.

The film's plot development revolves around Ip Man's experiences as a Wing Chun master, including his training under Grandmaster Yip Man (played by Siu Tin-yuen) and his subsequent teaching of the art to Bruce Lee. The story also explores Ip Man's involvement in the Chinese resistance movement during World War II and his eventual departure from China.

The ending of the film shows Ip Man settling into his new life in Hong Kong, where he establishes a martial arts school and trains a young Bruce Lee. While the film is based on real events, it takes some creative liberties to enhance the storytelling and character development.

overview: In post-apocalyptic England, an American volunteer and a British survivor team up to fight off a brood of fire-breathing dragons seeking to return to global dominance after centuries of rest underground. The Brit -- leading a clan of survivors to hunt down the King of the Dragons -- has much at stake: His mother was killed by a dragon, but his love is still alive.
tagline: Fight Fire With Fire
title: Reign of Fire
plot:
Reign of Fire is a post-apocalyptic horror film directed by Rob Bowman, produced by The Zanuck Company, and released in 2002.

The main themes of Reign of Fire include:

1. **Survival vs Humanity**: The movie explores the struggle between human survivors and the dragon-infested world they inhabit. As the dragons threaten to destroy what's left of humanity, the characters must confront their own morality and decide whether to prioritize survival or hold on to their humanity.
2. **Leadership and Power Struggle**: The story revolves around Quinn (Matthew McConaughey), a former blacksmith who becomes one of the leaders in the fight against the dragons. His leadership is challenged by Van Zan (Christian Bale), a ruthless and cunning fighter, leading to a power struggle that threatens the fragile human settlements.
3. **Loss and Grief**: The film explores the emotional toll of losing loved ones to the dragon attacks. Quinn's character, in particular, grapples with his past and the loss of his family, which drives his actions throughout the movie.
4. **Redemption and Sacrifice**: As the story unfolds, characters are forced to confront their own demons and make difficult choices that require sacrifice. This theme is particularly evident in Quinn's journey as he seeks redemption for past mistakes.

The plot development follows Quinn, a blacksmith who must navigate a world overrun by dragons, while also confronting his personal demons and leading a group of survivors against the dragon threat. As the story progresses, alliances are formed and broken, and characters face difficult choices that test their humanity.

The ending is intense and action-packed, with Quinn facing off against Van Zan in a final confrontation. Ultimately, Quinn emerges victorious but not without scars, both physical and emotional. The movie concludes on a hopeful note, suggesting that even in the darkest of times, there is always a chance for redemption and a new beginning.

Overall, Reign of Fire is a gripping post-apocalyptic thriller that explores themes of survival, leadership, loss, and redemption in a world ravaged by dragons.

overview: Christine Collins is overjoyed when her kidnapped son is brought back home. But when Christine suspects that the boy returned to her isn't her child, the police captain has her committed to an asylum.
tagline: To find her son, she did what no one else dared.
title: Changeling
plot:
Changeling is a 2008 American drama film directed by Clint Eastwood, produced by Clint Eastwood and Brian Grazer, and written by J. Michael Straczynski.

The main themes of Changeling revolve around the dark underbelly of Los Angeles during the Great Depression, corruption, and the struggle for justice. The story is based on a true event in 1928, where a woman named Christine Collins (played by Angelina Jolie) discovers that her missing son has been replaced with an imposter.

The film explores themes of:

1. **Identity**: The movie delves into the theme of identity, particularly for women and children, during a time when they were often marginalized and vulnerable to exploitation.
2. **Corruption**: The story highlights the corruption within the Los Angeles Police Department (LAPD) and the city's power structures, which led to the disappearance and replacement of Christine's son.
3. **Justice**: The film showcases the struggle for justice and the importance of seeking truth in the face of overwhelming odds.
4. **Motherhood**: Christine's love and devotion to her son serve as a catalyst for her actions, highlighting the depth of a mother's love and the lengths she will go to protect her child.

The movie also features a strong performance by Angelina Jolie, who brings depth and nuance to the character of Christine Collins. The film received critical acclaim, with many praising Eastwood's direction and Jolie's portrayal of the titular character.

Overall, Changeling is a powerful and thought-provoking drama that explores themes of identity, corruption, justice, and motherhood in the context of a true historical event.

overview: Living with her tyrannical stepfather in a new home with her pregnant mother, 10-year-old Ofelia feels alone until she explores a decaying labyrinth guarded by a mysterious faun who claims to know her destiny. If she wishes to return to her real father, Ofelia must complete three terrifying tasks.
tagline: What happens when make-believe believes it's real?
title: Pan's Labyrinth
plot:
Pan's Labyrinth (El laberinto del fauno) is a Spanish-language dark fantasy film of 2006 written, produced and directed by Guillermo del Toro, set in Francoist Spain in 1944. Ivana Baquero stars as Ofelia, a girl drawn into a mythical world, with Sergi López as her brutal stepfather Captain Vidal, Maribel Verdú as the housekeeper Mercedes, Doug Jones as both the Faun and the child-eating Pale Man and Ariadna Gil as Ofelia's mother Carmen.

A fable tells of Princess Moanna, daughter of the king of the underworld, who visited the human world, lost her memory in the sunlight and died as a mortal; her father built labyrinths across the world as portals for her spirit's return. Ofelia travels with her pregnant, ailing mother to a rural outpost commanded by Vidal, a fanatical Francoist officer hunting the Maquis resistance. An insect she takes for a fairy leads her to an ancient stone labyrinth, where a faun tells her she is the reincarnated princess and gives her a book revealing three tasks she must perform to return to her kingdom. Meanwhile Mercedes secretly aids her brother Pedro and the guerrillas.

Ofelia retrieves a key from the belly of a giant toad, and the faun gives her a mandrake root to keep beneath her mother's bed, easing her illness. In the second task she takes a dagger from the lair of the Pale Man but, ignoring the faun's warning, eats two grapes; the monster wakes and devours two fairies, and the furious faun abandons her. Vidal's cruelty escalates as he murders two farmers and tortures a captured guerrilla, whom Ferreiro mercifully kills before Vidal shoots the doctor. When Carmen burns the mandrake, she dies giving birth to Vidal's son. Exposed as a spy, Mercedes slashes Vidal's face and escapes. The faun returns with a final task: bring her baby brother into the labyrinth. There he asks for a drop of the infant's blood, but Ofelia refuses to harm him. Vidal, who cannot see the faun, takes the baby and shoots her. At the labyrinth's entrance he is surrounded by the Maquis; Mercedes tells him his son will never know his name, and Pedro kills him. As Ofelia dies, her blood falls onto an altar, and she awakens in a golden throne room, where her father the king tells her she passed the last test by shedding her own blood rather than an innocent's, and she takes her place beside him and her mother.

Premiering at Cannes in May 2006, the film grossed $83 million worldwide and won three Academy Awards and three BAFTAs. It scored 98 on Metacritic.

overview: Two melancholic Hong Kong policemen fall in love: one with a mysterious underworld figure, the other with a beautiful and ethereal server at a late-night restaurant he frequents.
tagline: What a difference a day makes.
title: Chungking Express
plot:
Chungking Express is a 1994 American independent film written and directed by Wong Kar-wai. The movie stars Takeshi Kaneshiro, Tony Leung Chiu-wai, Faye Wong, and Charlie Yeung.

The story takes place in Hong Kong and revolves around two police officers, Inspector Chan (Tony Leung) and Detective Jing (Takeshi Kaneshiro), who work at the Chungking Express police station. The film is divided into three main storylines that intersect with each other throughout the movie.

Inspector Chan is a middle-aged officer who has been divorced for several years. He is struggling to find meaning in his life, and his marriage has become stale. His only solace is his relationship with his colleague, Detective Jing, whom he has had feelings for since they were both young officers. However, their professional relationship remains platonic.

The first storyline follows Inspector Chan's search for a missing woman named Su Li-zhen (Faye Wong), who was last seen at the Chungking Express station. As Chan searches for her, he becomes increasingly obsessed with finding her and reconnecting with his lost love.

Meanwhile, Detective Jing is dealing with his own personal struggles. He has recently been dumped by his girlfriend, and he is struggling to come to terms with his new single status. Jing's life takes a turn when he meets a young woman named Jiazhen (Charlie Yeung), who becomes the object of his affections.

The second storyline follows Detective Jing's relationship with Jiazhen, which blossoms into romance. However, their love is complicated by Jing's past and his inability to open up to Jiazhen about his feelings.

Throughout the movie, Wong Kar-wai uses vibrant colors, stunning cinematography, and a memorable soundtrack to capture the mood and atmosphere of 1990s Hong Kong. The film's title, "Chungking Express," refers to the iconic train station in Kowloon, which serves as a symbol of connection and separation for the characters.

As the storylines converge, Inspector Chan finally finds Su Li-zhen, but their reunion is bittersweet. Jing, on the other hand, must confront his feelings about Jiazhen and decide whether he is ready to commit to her.

The movie ends with Inspector Chan and Detective Jing reflecting on their experiences and the connections they have made with others. The film's final shot features a montage of the characters' storylines, set to the iconic song "Chungking Express" by The Wannadies.

Overall, Chungking Express is a poignant and visually stunning film that explores themes of love, loss, and connection in 1990s Hong Kong. Wong Kar-wai's direction and the performances of the cast bring depth and nuance to the story, making it a timeless classic of independent cinema.

original_title: Straight Outta Nowhere: Scooby-Doo! Meets Courage the Cowardly Dog
overview: With Mystery, Inc. on the tail of a strange object in Nowhere, Kansas, the strange hometown of Eustice, Muriel, and Courage, the gang soon find themselves contending with a giant cicada monster and her winged warriors.
tagline: Ooga! Booga! Booga!
title: Straight Outta Nowhere: Scooby-Doo! Meets Courage the Cowardly Dog
plot:
Straight Outta Nowhere: Scooby-Doo! Meets Courage the Cowardly Dog is a 2021 animated film that brings together two beloved cartoon franchises, Scooby-Doo and Courage the Cowardly Dog. The movie follows the adventures of Shaggy Rogers (voiced by Robbie Daymond) and Scooby-Doo (voiced by Scott Innes), who are on their way to a music festival in Nowhere, Kansas.

Upon arrival, they meet Eustace Bagge (voiced by Jason Alexander), Courage's owner, and his family. However, things take a dark turn when the town is plagued by supernatural occurrences, including ghostly apparitions, monsters, and unexplained events. The Scooby-Doo gang soon discovers that these events are connected to an ancient curse that has been awakened in Nowhere.

As the mystery unfolds, Shaggy and Scooby team up with Courage (voiced by Eric Bauza) to uncover the truth behind the curse. Along the way, they encounter a range of bizarre characters, including a ghostly cowboy, a possessed preacher, and a mysterious woman who seems to be connected to the curse.

Throughout their investigation, Shaggy and Scooby use their signature skills to gather clues and solve puzzles, while Courage provides his own unique brand of cowardice to help them navigate the supernatural threats. Meanwhile, Eustace's family is torn apart by the events unfolding in Nowhere, leading to a heartwarming moment of connection between Shaggy and Muriel Bagge (voiced by Grey DeLisle).

As the mystery deepens, the Scooby-Doo gang discovers that the curse is connected to an ancient ritual that was performed by the town's founders. They must work together to break the curse and restore peace to Nowhere before it's too late.

The film features a mix of humor, action, and heart, blending the signature styles of both franchises. The animation is vibrant and colorful, with plenty of nods to the original Scooby-Doo and Courage the Cowardly Dog series. The voice cast delivers solid performances, bringing the characters to life in a way that feels true to their respective franchises.

Overall, Straight Outta Nowhere: Scooby-Doo! Meets Courage the Cowardly Dog is a fun and entertaining film that brings together two beloved cartoon franchises in a unique and exciting way. With its blend of humor, action, and heart, it's sure to delight fans of both Scooby-Doo and Courage the Cowardly Dog.

overview: When Chef Carl Casper suddenly quits his job at a prominent Los Angeles restaurant after refusing to compromise his creative integrity for its controlling owner, he is left to figure out what's next. Finding himself in Miami, he teams up with his ex-wife, his friend and his son to launch a food truck. Taking to the road, Chef Carl goes back to his roots to reignite his passion for the kitchen -- and zest for life and love.
tagline: Starting from scratch never tasted so good.
title: Chef
plot:
Chef is a 2014 road comedy-drama film written, produced and directed by Jon Favreau, who stars as Carl Casper, a celebrity chef who starts a food truck business with his friends and young son. The ensemble cast includes Sofía Vergara, John Leguizamo, Scarlett Johansson, Oliver Platt, Bobby Cannavale, Amy Sedaris, Emjay Anthony and Dustin Hoffman, with Robert Downey Jr. in a cameo. Favreau wrote the script after a run of big-budget films, wanting to go "back to basics" with a movie about cooking, with chef Roy Choi as co-producer.

Carl, born in Miami, is head chef at Gauloises, an upscale restaurant in Brentwood, Los Angeles, where he frequently clashes with the owner, Riva, who insists on a safe, traditional menu. At home, his relationships with his wealthy ex-wife Inez and their tech-savvy young son Percy are strained. When the influential critic and blogger Ramsey Michel comes to dine, Riva forces Carl to abandon his bold new menu at the last minute, and the result is a scathing review. Carl's angry public reply on Twitter makes him an online sensation, and he invites the critic back for a rematch. When Riva again demands the standard menu, Carl quits on the spot; Ramsey, served the same dishes, publicly mocks him, and Carl's furious confrontation at the restaurant goes viral, leaving him humiliated and unable to find work. Reluctantly joining Inez and Percy on a trip to Miami, he rediscovers his love of Cuban cooking, and Inez's other ex-husband, Marvin, offers him a rundown food truck. Father and son bond as they restore it, and Carl's former line cook Martin turns down a promotion at Gauloises to join them. Driving back to Los Angeles, they serve Cuban sandwiches while Percy builds a social media following. By the time they arrive, Carl has rebuilt his career and his bond with Percy. Ramsey visits the truck and explains that, as an early admirer, he had been disappointed by a meal so far below Carl's talent; impressed by his renewed passion, he offers to back a new restaurant with full creative freedom. Six months later the restaurant is thriving, and Carl and Inez celebrate their remarriage there.

Filmed in July 2013 in Los Angeles, Miami, Austin and New Orleans, Chef premiered at South by Southwest on March 7, 2014, and was released by Open Road Films that May. Well received by critics, with an 87% Rotten Tomatoes rating, it grossed $49.8 million on an $11 million budget.

overview: A newly married couple who, in the process of starting a family, learn many of life's important lessons from their trouble-loving retriever, Marley. Packed with plenty of laughs to lighten the load, the film explores the highs and lows of marriage, maturity and confronting one's own mortality, as seen through the lens of family life with a dog.
tagline: Heel the love.
title: Marley & Me
plot:
Marley & Me is a 2008 American comedy-drama film directed by David Frankel from a screenplay by Scott Frank and Don Roos, based on John Grogan's 2005 memoir of the same name. Owen Wilson and Jennifer Aniston star as John and Jenny Grogan, journalists whose family life is shaped over many years by their unruly yellow Labrador retriever, Marley, and the cast also includes Eric Dane, Kathleen Turner and Alan Arkin.

After moving from Michigan to South Florida, the newlyweds take reporting jobs at rival newspapers: Jenny quickly lands front-page stories at The Palm Beach Post, while John is stuck writing obituaries and short news items at the South Florida Sun-Sentinel. Sensing Jenny is thinking about motherhood, John's colleague Sebastian Tunney suggests a dog to test their readiness, and they adopt a puppy John names after Bob Marley. Marley grows to around 100 pounds and proves impossible to control, getting thrown out of obedience school. When editor Arnie Klein offers John a twice-weekly column on any subject he likes, John writes about Marley's misadventures, and the column becomes so popular that it helps double the paper's circulation. Jenny suffers a miscarriage early in her first pregnancy, and the couple return from a belated honeymoon in Ireland to find that Marley has wrecked the house under an overwhelmed sitter. Jenny later gives birth to two sons, Patrick and Conor, and decides to stay at home while John takes on a daily column. The family moves to a larger house in Boca Raton, but the exhausted Jenny grows short-tempered with both Marley and John and demands that the dog be rehomed, before quickly realizing he is an essential member of the family. After their daughter Colleen is born and John turns 40, envy of Sebastian's new job at The New York Times leads him to take a reporting post at The Philadelphia Inquirer, and the family moves to a farm in rural Pennsylvania, though John soon realizes he is a better columnist than reporter. Their contentment is shaken when the aging Marley suffers a near-fatal intestinal illness; he recovers, but after a second attack, too old for surgery, he is put down with John at his side and buried beneath a tree in the yard.

Released by 20th Century Fox on December 25, 2008, the film set a Christmas Day box office record of $14.75 million and grossed $247.8 million against a $60 million budget. Reviews were mixed, with a 64% Rotten Tomatoes rating. A prequel, Marley & Me: The Puppy Years, followed in 2011.

overview: The Peanuts gang is nervous about going to a new school, so Lucy starts her own. She soon learns that teaching is tougher than she thought—and that change can be a good thing.
tagline: A tribute to teachers!
title: Snoopy Presents: Lucy's School
plot:
Snoopy Presents: Lucy's School, also known simply as Lucy's School, is a 2022 animated television special based on Charles M. Schulz's Peanuts comic strip. Directed by Raymond S. Persi and written by Craig Schulz, Bryan Schulz and Cornelius Uliano, it is the 49th Peanuts animated special and the fourth made for Apple TV+. It follows Lucy van Pelt, who opens a school of her own because she is anxious about starting at a new one. The voice cast includes Isabella Leo as Lucy, Etienne Kellici as Charlie Brown, Wyatt White as Linus, Terry McGurrin as Snoopy, Rob Tinkler as Woodstock.

As summer vacation draws to a close, Charlie Brown and his friends learn that they will be attending a newly built school in the autumn. While most of the children are curious, Lucy is unsettled by the thought of unfamiliar teachers, older students, lockers and being separated from her friends. Masking her fear by criticizing the new school, she announces that she will run a school of her own, enlists the others as pupils and sets up a classroom. Certain that teaching will be easy, she poses as an expert on every subject, but her lessons soon fall into disorder as Linus, Franklin and Marcie question her answers, the students ask things she cannot answer and refuse to behave as she wishes, and Snoopy and Woodstock add to the distractions. Once her pupils lose faith in the school, Lucy admits she does not know how to teach them, and Linus helps her see that she started it because she was frightened of the coming change. The others confess that they are nervous too and assure her they will face the new school together, and Lucy gains a new appreciation of the preparation, patience and encouragement teachers must give. On the first day of term the children meet their new teacher, Miss Halverson, who welcomes them and eases their worries, and Lucy walks into the classroom with her friends, ready to accept the change. The special closes with a tribute to teachers and their influence on students.

Apple TV+ released the special worldwide on August 12, 2022, alongside new episodes of The Snoopy Show. It was produced for Peanuts Worldwide and WildBrain. Common Sense Media gave it four out of five stars, praising its handling of back-to-school anxiety. It won Best Animation Program at the 2023 Leo Awards and earned a Children's and Family Emmy nomination.

overview: An orphaned boy raised by underground creatures called Boxtrolls comes up from the sewers and out of his box to save his family and the town from the evil exterminator, Archibald Snatcher.
tagline: When troubles strikes friends stack together
title: The Boxtrolls
plot:
The Boxtrolls is a stop-motion animated fantasy comedy film directed by Graham Annable and Anthony Stacchi, produced by Laika Entertainment, and released in 2014. The story is loosely based on the children's book series "Here Be Monsters!" by Alan Snow.

In the fictional town of Cheesebridge, a group of small, mischievous creatures known as the Boxtrolls live beneath the streets. These trolls are scavengers who feed on human trash and are feared by the townspeople. The main character, Eggs (voiced by Charlie Tahan), is a young orphan boy who lives in an orphanage run by the evil Lord Eggman (voiced by Jeremy Suarez). Eggs' life changes when he discovers that he is actually a Box Troll himself.

As Eggs navigates his new identity, he meets a human girl named Eve (voiced by Isla Fisher) who has been kidnapped by Lord Eggman. The two form an unlikely friendship and embark on a journey to rescue Eve from the clutches of the evil lord. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, including treacherous terrain, ferocious creatures, and rival gangs of Boxtrolls.

Throughout their adventure, Eggs learns about his true identity as a Box Troll and the history of his people. He also discovers that Lord Eggman is actually a former human who was transformed into a troll by a magical curse. The lord's ultimate goal is to capture all the remaining humans in Cheesebridge and use them to create an army of super-strong trolls.

As Eggs and Eve near their destination, they face off against Lord Eggman and his minions in an epic battle. In the end, Eggs and Eve successfully rescue Eve from the clutches of the evil lord, and Eggs finds a new sense of belonging among his fellow Boxtrolls.

The film features stunning stop-motion animation, witty humor, and a heartwarming story about acceptance and friendship. The characters are well-developed and relatable, with Eggs being a particularly endearing protagonist. The film's themes of identity, community, and the power of human connection make it a delightful and entertaining watch for audiences of all ages.

Overall, The Boxtrolls is a charming and imaginative film that will delight both children and adults with its unique blend of humor, adventure, and heart.

original_title: 劇場版 NARUTO 大活劇! 雪姫忍法帖だってばよ!!
overview: Naruto is thrilled when he is sent on a mission to protect his favorite actress, Yukie Fujikaze, on the set of her new movie, The Adventures of Princess Gale. But when the crew ventures out to film in the icy, foreboding Land of Snow, Yukie mysteriously flees! Naruto and his squad set off to find her... unaware that three Snow Ninja lie in wait, with a sinister purpose that will force Yukie to face her hidden past!
title: Naruto: Ninja Clash in the Land of Snow
plot:
Naruto the Movie: Ninja Clash in the Land of Snow is a 2004 Japanese animated martial arts fantasy adventure film based on Masashi Kishimoto's manga and the Naruto anime series, set after the series' 101st episode. Most of the television voice cast returns, with Junko Takeuchi voicing the hero, Naruto Uzumaki, alongside Chie Nakamura, Noriaki Sugiyama and Kazuhiko Inoue.

Naruto, Sasuke Uchiha and Sakura Haruno watch a film starring Yukie Fujikaze, which their teacher Kakashi Hatake has assigned as preparation for their next mission: protecting Yukie, famous as the heroine Princess Gale, during production of her next film. Yukie is in fact Koyuki Kazahana, princess of an island called the Land of Snow, whose father, Sosetsu, was murdered in a coup by her uncle Doto Kazahana. During filming, Doto's henchmen, clad in chakra armor, attack, and Team 7 holds them off for a time.

Doto eventually captures Koyuki, killing her bodyguards, who had revealed themselves in an attempt to restore her to the throne. Naruto boards Doto's ship to rescue her but is caught and fitted with a device that drains his chakra. Doto takes a crystal necklace Koyuki received from her father as a child, believing it to be the key to a treasure Sosetsu hid. Sasuke, Sakura and Kakashi infiltrate the fortress as Naruto and Koyuki escape, but Doto seizes the necklace and flees with the princess. While Naruto pursues him, Kakashi defeats the henchman Nadare Roga, and Sasuke and Sakura defeat Fubuki Kakuyoku and Mizore Fuyukuma. Doto finds the hidden treasure, a heat generator that can transform the island into a Land of Spring. Overpowered at first, Naruto is helped by Sasuke's Chidori, which weakens Doto's armor, and then unleashes a new Seven Colored Chakra Rasengan that kills Doto and activates a mirror that transforms the land. Koyuki reclaims her throne and tells Team 7 that her acting career will continue. Later, Sasuke and Sakura give Naruto a signed photo of the princess kissing him in the hospital, and the team prepares for a new adventure.

The film opened in Japan on August 21, 2004, and was released on DVD in April 2005. In 2007 it had one-day theatrical screenings in the United States, Canada and Australia and aired on Cartoon Network. Reviews were positive; Helen McCarthy called it a good introduction to the series' themes of persistence and self-belief and praised its frozen landscapes.

overview: A young man meets and instantly falls in love with an engaged woman.
tagline: Love... it's a balancing act
title: Playing It Cool
plot:
Playing It Cool is a 2014 American romantic comedy film directed by Michael Showalter and written by Paul Wernick and Rhett Reese. The movie stars Jason Sudeikis, Anna Faris, and Chris Pratt.

The story revolves around Jake (played by Jason Sudeikis), a charming but slightly arrogant baseball player who is dating a beautiful woman named Molly (played by Anna Faris). However, Jake's life takes an unexpected turn when he meets a free-spirited woman named Charlotte (played by Michelle Monaghan) on a plane.

Despite their instant attraction, Jake and Charlotte engage in a game of cat-and-mouse, with each trying to outdo the other in a series of escalating pranks and one-upmanship. As they spend more time together, Jake finds himself falling for Charlotte's charms, but he struggles to balance his feelings with his commitment to Molly.

Meanwhile, Molly is dealing with her own issues - she's struggling to come to terms with the fact that Jake has been lying about his relationship status, and she's starting to realize that she may have fallen in love with him. As the story unfolds, Jake must confront his own emotions and make a choice between his feelings for Charlotte and his commitment to Molly.

Throughout the movie, the characters engage in witty banter and clever pranks, adding to the comedic tone of the film. However, as the plot thickens, the stakes become higher, and the characters are forced to confront their true feelings.

In the end, Jake must make a difficult decision - will he choose the comfort and security of his relationship with Molly, or will he take a chance on love with Charlotte? The movie culminates in a heartwarming and humorous conclusion that leaves the audience rooting for the lovable but flawed protagonist.

Overall, Playing It Cool is a charming and witty romantic comedy that explores themes of love, relationships, and self-discovery. With its talented cast and clever script, the movie is sure to delight audiences looking for a lighthearted and entertaining film experience.

overview: In Glasgow, Scotland, while a mysterious pandemic begins to spread around the world, Susan, a brilliant epidemiologist, falls in love with Michael, a skillful cook.
tagline: Without love there is nothing
title: Perfect Sense
plot:
Perfect Sense is a 2011 British drama film directed by David Mackenzie. The movie follows Dr. Fiona Allen (Eva Green), an ear, nose and throat specialist who begins to lose her sense of smell due to a mysterious illness.

The main themes of Perfect Sense include:

1. **Loss of Identity**: As Fiona loses her sense of smell, she struggles to maintain her identity and sense of self. Her relationships with others begin to deteriorate, and she starts to question her own existence.
2. **Emotional Connection**: The film explores the importance of emotional connection in our lives. Fiona's loss of smell affects not only her physical senses but also her emotional well-being, highlighting the interconnectedness of our experiences.
3. **Love and Relationships**: Perfect Sense delves into the complexities of love and relationships. Fiona's struggles to maintain intimacy with her partner, James (Ewan McGregor), serve as a catalyst for exploring the fragility of human connections.
4. **Mortality and Impermanence**: The film touches on the theme of mortality, as Fiona's condition forces her to confront the impermanence of life and the inevitability of loss.
5. **The Human Experience**: Perfect Sense is a poignant exploration of the human experience, highlighting the complexities and nuances of our emotions, relationships, and existence.

Through its thought-provoking narrative, the film encourages viewers to reflect on their own experiences and connections with others, making it a deeply moving and introspective watch.

overview: High school student Shun Takahata is bored. Bored with the day-to-day monotony of school and life, he prays for change, for something exciting. Suddenly, he and his classmates are forced to play deadly children's games and facing terrifying creatures from a talking Daruma doll to a sharp-clawed lucky cat.
tagline: Oh my God, please return my tedious everyday.
title: As the Gods Will
plot:
As the Gods Will (Japanese: Kami-sama no Iu Tōri) is a 2014 Japanese supernatural horror film directed by Takashi Miike and based on the first story arc of the manga by Muneyuki Kaneshiro and Akeji Fujimura. Sota Fukushi plays Shun Takahata, with Ryūnosuke Kamiki as Takeru Amaya, Hirona Yamazaki as Ichika Akimoto and Mio Yūki as Shoko Takase, and Lily Franky as a homeless man who is God.

Shun, a high school student bored with his ordinary life, is suddenly forced along with his class into a deadly version of the children's game daruma-san ga koronda. A Daruma doll at the front of the classroom kills anyone it sees moving, while a button on its back can end the game. Everyone in the class except Shun dies. Reunited with his childhood friend Ichika, Shun reaches the gym, where students must throw a giant bell into a hoop on the collar of a huge beckoning-cat doll or die. Shun and Ichika devise a trick that works with Amaya's help, but Amaya then kills the students who did not help, saying the unworthy do not deserve to live. As he and Shun fight, the cat knocks everyone out with sleeping gas.

Shun wakes in a giant cube floating over Tokyo with other students, including Takase. In a round of kagome kagome, blindfolded players must guess which of four floating kokeshi dolls stands behind them, and Shun wins by tricking his doll into revealing itself. Reunited with Amaya and Ichika, he faces a giant polar bear that demands truthful answers and has the group vote out suspected liars; Ichika, Takase and Amaya all admit liking Shun, and after deaths including Takase's, Shun realizes the bear itself is lying. In the final game, a hide-and-seek game with a can, hosted by matryoshka dolls, Amaya is the demon and captures every other player, but Shun chains him long enough to kick the can. The dolls declare that everyone survives and hand out ice cream, but the sticks are a lottery, and everyone except Shun and Amaya draws death. Standing atop the cube as crowds chant "God's children", Shun insists there is no god, but the dolls name each game host as a god, "and God", as a man appears behind him and Shun turns to face him.

The film premiered at the Rome Film Festival on October 18, 2014, opened in Japan on November 15 and earned $1.5 million there in its first weekend. Western critics gave mixed reviews, praising its effects but faulting its plot. After the 2021 release of Squid Game, the series was accused of copying the film, which its creator denied.

overview: One day, Koyomi Araragi encounters the horrifying vampire, Kiss-shot Acerola-orion Heart-under-blade A.K.A. the "King of Apparitions." He saves the fatally wounded Kiss-shot by offering his blood at the expense of his own life as a human. Now Koyomi has to face the vampire hunters to retrieve Kiss-shot’s limbs which were taken by these hunters...
title: Kizumonogatari Part 1: Tekketsu
plot:
Kizumonogatari Part 1: Tekketsu is a thought-provoking film that delves into the complexities of human relationships, identity, and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy. The movie follows the story of Araragi Koyomi, a high school student who becomes entangled in a world of vampires and supernatural creatures.

At its core, Kizumonogatari Part 1: Tekketsu explores the theme of existential crisis, as Koyomi navigates his own identity and sense of purpose. The film raises questions about what it means to be human, and whether one's existence is defined by their relationships with others or by their own inner struggles.

The movie also touches on the idea of trauma and its lasting impact on individuals. Koyomi's experiences with the vampire Kiss-Shot Acerola-Orion Heart-Under-Blade serve as a catalyst for his introspection, forcing him to confront the darker aspects of his own psyche.

Furthermore, Kizumonogatari Part 1: Tekketsu examines the concept of love and its many forms. The film presents a nuanced portrayal of relationships, highlighting both the beauty and the pain that can accompany them. Through Koyomi's interactions with various characters, including Miki Saeki and Shinobu Oshino, the movie illustrates the complexities of human connection and the ways in which it can shape our understanding of ourselves.

Ultimately, Kizumonogatari Part 1: Tekketsu is a film that defies easy categorization, instead embracing its own ambiguity and complexity. It invites viewers to ponder the nature of reality, identity, and relationships, leaving a lasting impression long after the credits roll.

overview: Agents of the Korean National Intelligence Service (KNIS), Pyung-ho at Int’l Dept. and Jung-do at Domestic Dept. are both independently hunting a North Korean mole within the agency. During this investigation, they come face to face with an unbearable truth and must deal with an unthinkable plot to assassinate the South Korean president.
tagline: Two rivals, a hidden truth.
title: Hunt
plot:
Hunt (Korean: 헌트) is a 2022 South Korean spy action thriller directed by Lee Jung-jae in his feature directorial debut. Lee and Jung Woo-sung star as two intelligence chiefs who come to suspect each other while hunting a mole inside their agency, with Jeon Hye-jin, Heo Sung-tae and Go Youn-jung, in her film debut, in the supporting cast. It premiered in the Midnight Screenings section of the 2022 Cannes Film Festival on 19 May, where it received a seven-minute standing ovation, and Megabox released it in South Korea on 10 August 2022.

In the 1980s, under the military dictatorship of President Chun Doo-hwan, Park Pyong-ho, head of the foreign unit of the Agency for National Security Planning, and Kim Jung-do, head of its domestic unit, are guarding the president in Washington, D.C., when a team of assassins strikes. Jung-do shoots the last gunman as he holds Pyong-ho hostage, and the two men blame each other. Afterward, the agency's director reveals that a North Korean mole code-named Donglim is working inside the agency and plotting to kill the president, and both chiefs are ordered to find him.

A botched operation in Japan to bring over a defecting North Korean physicist, and the betrayal of a failed military mission to the North, push the rivals to investigate each other. Each uncovers the other's secret. Jung-do leads a conspiracy to assassinate the president in revenge for the Gwangju massacre and was behind the Washington attack, while Pyong-ho is Donglim. Learning that the North now plans to invade and intends to eliminate him, Pyong-ho is rescued by Jung-do and drawn into the assassination plot in Bangkok, but fearing that the killing will trigger the invasion, he turns against the attack on the motorcade. A bomb set by a North Korean agent fails to kill the president, and Jung-do dies in the blast. Later, Pyong-ho is ambushed and killed while offering the young woman Yoo-jeong an escape to America, after it is revealed that she really is a North Korean agent.

After the Cannes screening, Lee re-edited the film and changed key lines to make the 1980s political background clearer to foreign audiences, presenting the new version at the Toronto International Film Festival.
