Critics were dismissive, giving it 13% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and noting how closely its plot resembles the 1997 Kurt Russell thriller Breakdown. When it reached Netflix on October 1, 2022, however, it became the service's most-watched film in the United States and ranked in its top ten in many other countries.

overview: A young girl named Mija risks everything to prevent a powerful, multi-national company from kidnapping her best friend - a massive animal named Okja.
title: Okja
plot:
Okja is a 2017 South Korean-American science fiction film directed by Bong Joon-ho, written by Bong Joon-ho and Han Jin Won, and produced by Plan B Entertainment. The film stars An Seo Hyun, Byun Hee-bong, Steven Yeun, Paul Dano, Lily Collins, and Jake Gyllenhaal.

The story begins in a small village in South Korea, where a young girl named Mija (An Seo Hyun) lives with her father, Mr. Park (Byun Hee-bong), who is a kind-hearted farmer. The family's life is disrupted when a multinational corporation called Mirae Life Science, led by Lucy Mirando (Jake Gyllenhaal), arrives in the village to harvest a genetically engineered super-pig named Okja.

Okja is a massive, intelligent, and friendly creature that has been created using advanced biotechnology. Mija forms a deep bond with Okja, and as she grows older, she becomes determined to save her beloved companion from being exploited by Mirae Life Science for their own gain.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Mirae Life Science plans to use Okja's DNA to create a new breed of super-pigs, which will be used for food production. Mija and her father embark on a perilous journey across the globe to stop the corporation and rescue Okja from their clutches.

Along the way, they meet a group of animal rights activists, led by Johnny Wilcox (Steven Yeun), who are fighting against Mirae Life Science's sinister plans. The group faces numerous challenges and obstacles as they try to reach Okja before it's too late.

As Mija and her allies close in on their target, the stakes become increasingly high. The corporation will stop at nothing to achieve its goals, and Mija must use all her wit and determination to outsmart them and save Okja.

The film's climax features an epic showdown between Mija and Lucy Mirando, with the fate of Okja hanging precariously in the balance. In the end, Mija emerges victorious, but not without scars. The film concludes on a hopeful note, with Mija reflecting on the lessons she has learned about the importance of compassion, empathy, and standing up for what is right.

Throughout the film, Bong Joon-ho explores themes of corporate greed, animal rights, and the ethics of scientific experimentation. Okja is a powerful commentary on the consequences of playing God with nature and the importance of treating all living beings with kindness and respect.

Overall, Okja is a visually stunning and emotionally resonant film that will keep you on the edge of your seat from start to finish. With its talented cast, engaging storyline, and thought-provoking themes, it's a must-see for anyone who loves science fiction, adventure, or just great storytelling in general.

overview: Upon discovering her husband's infidelity, Sandy leaves the suburbs and moves into the city. There, she befriends Aram, a guy whose wife only married him so she could get a green card. Sandy hires Aram to be her nanny, and  it isn't long until Aram and Sandy find out they get along wonderfully and start to date. But is their relationship real or is it, in fact, just a rebound for both of them?
tagline: She's still got it. He's just getting it.
title: The Rebound
plot:
The Rebound is a 2009 American romantic comedy film written and directed by Bart Freundlich. Catherine Zeta-Jones stars as Sandy, a newly divorced mother of two, and Justin Bartha as Aram Finklestein, the younger man who becomes her children's nanny and then her partner. The cast also includes Kelly Gould, Marcel Simoneau, Art Garfunkel, Joanna Gleason and Lynn Whitfield. It was the last role of the actress Alice Playten before her death in 2011.

Sandy, a housewife, discovers that her husband has been unfaithful and, after a quick divorce, moves to New York City with her son and daughter to start over. Living above a coffee house, she befriends its barista Aram, an aimless 25-year-old college graduate recently separated from a French wife who married him for a green card. Aram takes a job at a women's centre, and during a self-defence class in which he plays the attacker, Sandy unleashes what is described as an "ocean of anger" on him. The next day she apologizes at the coffee shop and asks him to babysit her children. He soon becomes the family's full-time nanny, bonding with the children, and an attraction grows between him and Sandy, leading to an awkward first sexual encounter that the children find out about. The two nevertheless begin dating and, two months later, seem well suited to each other. When Sandy suspects she is pregnant, Aram is overjoyed, but a doctor finds that the pregnancy is ectopic and will end in a miscarriage. Leaving the doctor's office, they quarrel, and Sandy insists it is ridiculous to think that two people fifteen years apart could ever be happy together. After their break-up Aram sets out to travel the world, while Sandy is promoted to anchor at the sports news job where she works. Five years later they meet by chance in a Chinese restaurant. Aram, still single, has adopted a young boy from Bangladesh, and Sandy, celebrating another promotion with her children and a colleague, invites them to join her table. As their children begin to get to know one another, Sandy and Aram hold hands beneath the table, suggesting that their romance will be rekindled.

The Rebound opened in cinemas in several countries in late 2009, but its planned American release was cancelled when its distributor shut down, and it went straight to DVD in the United States in February 2012. Reviews were generally negative, with a 42% Rotten Tomatoes score, and the film grossed about $21.8 million worldwide.

overview: When a threat no one could have expected bears down on the Marvel Universe, this ragtag, untrained band of teens have no choice but to rise together and prove to the world that sometimes the difference between a 'hero' and 'misfit' is just in the name.
title: Marvel Rising: Secret Warriors
plot:
Marvel Rising: Secret Warriors is an animated superhero film that explores several key themes. At its core, the movie delves into the idea of identity and self-discovery, particularly for young characters navigating their roles in a world of superheroes.

The story follows a group of teenage heroes who are part of the Secret Warriors, a team of young agents working under the supervision of S.H.I.E.L.D. The film showcases the struggles these characters face as they try to balance their personal lives with their responsibilities as superheroes. This theme is particularly evident in the character of Kate Bishop, who grapples with her own identity and sense of purpose.

The movie also touches on the concept of mentorship and the importance of guidance in helping young heroes find their place in the world. The relationship between Kate and her mentor, Madame Masque, serves as a powerful example of this theme.

Furthermore, Marvel Rising: Secret Warriors explores the idea of teamwork and collaboration, highlighting the value of diverse perspectives and skills in achieving common goals. The film showcases the Secret Warriors' ability to work together, support one another, and learn from each other's strengths and weaknesses.

Lastly, the movie touches on the theme of responsibility and the consequences of power. As the characters navigate their roles as superheroes, they must confront the weight of their responsibilities and make difficult choices that impact not only themselves but also those around them.

Overall, Marvel Rising: Secret Warriors is a story about growth, self-discovery, and the importance of relationships and teamwork in helping young heroes find their place in the world.

overview: A horrifying story of a shaman’s inheritance in the Isan region of Thailand. But the goddess that appears to have taken possession of a family member turns out not to be as benevolent as it first appears.
tagline: A story about shamanism in Thailand.
title: The Medium
plot:
The Medium is a supernatural folk horror film of 2021 shot as a mock documentary in the Isan language, directed by Banjong Pisanthanakun and co-written and produced by the Korean filmmaker Na Hong-jin. Sawanee Utoomma stars as Nim, a village shaman, with Narilya Gulmongkolpech as her niece Mink, Sirani Yankittikan as Mink's mother Noi and Boonsong Nakphoo as the shaman Santi.

A documentary crew travels to Isan in north-eastern Thailand to film Nim, a medium who says she is possessed by Ba Yan, a local goddess. Nim inherited the role after her sister Noi refused it and became a Christian. At the funeral of Noi's husband Wiroj, Nim explains that misfortune has dogged his family's men: his father, a factory owner, killed himself after an insurance fraud, and his son Mac supposedly died in a road accident. Noi now lives with her daughter Mink and Manit's family. Mink begins to behave strangely, shifting between personalities and hearing voices, and she loses her job over her behaviour at work. Nim suspects Ba Yan has chosen Mink as her next host, but Noi forbids a ceremony. Nim then learns that Mac actually hanged himself after an incestuous relationship with Mink and fears his ghost is haunting her.

After Mink attempts suicide, Noi, believing Ba Yan is punishing her through her daughter, secretly hires another medium to pass the goddess to Mink. The rite fails and Mink runs away, to be found a month later delirious in her grandfather's ruined factory. Ba Yan's statue is found beheaded, and the more powerful shaman Santi declares that Mink is possessed by countless evil spirits, the legacy of her paternal ancestors' crimes. As Santi prepares a great exorcism, Mink terrorises the household, even killing and eating the family dog. Nim dies in her sleep the day before the ritual. At the ruined factory, Noi offers herself as a vessel to draw out the spirits, while at home Mink is sealed in her room. Lured by what sounds like her son crying, Manit's wife opens the door and is stabbed, and the ritual collapses as the spirits seize the participants. Mink arrives at the factory and, when Noi tries to cast out the spirits, calls her mother before burning her alive. A mid-credits scene shows Nim, before her death, doubting that Ba Yan was ever inside her.

The film won the best feature award at the Bucheon International Fantastic Film Festival, topped the South Korean box office in July 2021 and was Thailand's Oscar submission. It holds 81% on Rotten Tomatoes.

original_title: Curious George: A Very Monkey Christmas
overview: George and The Man In The Yellow Hat are having a merry time counting down to Christmas. But neither can decide what to give each other. Will they find the answers before Christmas morning?
title: Curious George: A Very Monkey Christmas
plot:
Curious George: A Very Monkey Christmas is a 2009 American animated holiday television film based on the Curious George children's books by Margret and H. A. Rey and the PBS Kids animated series they inspired. Produced by Universal Animation Studios with Imagine Entertainment, it was directed by Scott Heming, Cathy Malkasian and Jeff McGrath from a script by Joe Fallon. Universal released it on DVD on 13 October 2009, and it was broadcast on PBS that November. The special runs just under an hour, and its visual style sits between the more lavish 2006 theatrical feature and the simpler look of the television series.

With Christmas approaching, the little monkey George and his friend Ted, the Man with the Yellow Hat, count down the days, decorate and look for ways to make the time fly, but each secretly faces the same problem: neither knows what to give the other. George draws a Christmas list full of seemingly random shapes that Ted cannot decipher, nor can the doorman or Chef Pisghetti when Ted shows it to them, so Ted asks George to surprise him instead. George decides to make his friend a present but cannot settle on what. Meanwhile, Betsy struggles to write a new carol for her Aunt Margaret, since every Christmas subject seems to have its song already.

The preparations bring a series of gentle mishaps. A trip to the country to buy a tree ends with George climbing to the top of one and toppling a whole row; a snowplough built by Professor Wiseman, which George hopes will be the perfect gift, goes awry; and a small fire brings a fire engine. At Betsy's Christmas Eve performance, her new song turns out to be about George himself. In a dream inspired by Dickens's A Christmas Carol, the clockmaker shows Ted imagined lives in which other friends give George a perfect existence, and he realises that his friend wanted the toys in a shop window. On Christmas morning, George presents Ted with a roll of wrapping paper illustrated with the story of their Christmas.

Frank Welker voices George and Jeff Bennett the Man with the Yellow Hat, with Rino Romano narrating and Grey DeLisle, Jim Cummings, E. G. Daily, Rob Paulsen and Rolonda Watts among the supporting cast. Animated Views found the special slight but highly pleasing, praising its old-fashioned, storybook animation and amusing dialogue, while Common Sense Media judged it suitable for children aged three and up.

overview: Determined to ensure Superman's ultimate sacrifice was not in vain, Bruce Wayne aligns forces with Diana Prince with plans to recruit a team of metahumans to protect the world from an approaching threat of catastrophic proportions.
title: Zack Snyder's Justice League
plot:
Zack Snyder's Justice League is a 2021 superhero film directed by Zack Snyder, based on the DC Comics team of the same name. The movie follows the story of five superheroes who must come together to save the world from an ancient evil.

The film begins with Bruce Wayne (Ben Affleck), aka Batman, who has been training himself physically and mentally after the events of Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice. He is approached by the Justice League's leader, Diana Prince (Gal Gadot), also known as Wonder Woman, who informs him that an ancient being known as Steppenwolf has returned to Earth with a plan to harvest three powerful artifacts.

Meanwhile, Arthur Curry (Jason Momoa), aka Aquaman, is introduced as he tries to find his place in the world and understand his connection to the underwater kingdom of Atlantis. He eventually joins forces with Batman and Wonder Woman to stop Steppenwolf's plans.

The team also includes Barry Allen (Ezra Miller), aka The Flash, who has been struggling to control his powers after the events of Justice League. They are joined by Cyborg (Ray Fisher), a half-human, half-robot who is still learning to control his abilities.

As Steppenwolf's plan unfolds, the team must work together to stop him and save the world from destruction. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles and challenges that test their skills and teamwork.

Throughout the film, Snyder explores themes of unity, sacrifice, and the power of friendship. The movie also delves into the characters' backstories and emotional struggles, adding depth to the story.

One notable aspect of the film is its visual style, which features a mix of practical and CGI effects. Snyder's direction creates a sense of grandeur and spectacle, bringing the Justice League to life in a way that feels both epic and intimate.

Overall, Zack Snyder's Justice League is a thrilling adventure that brings together some of DC Comics' most iconic superheroes. While it may not be perfect, the film offers a unique take on the characters and their relationships, making it a must-see for fans of the franchise.

overview: A juror on the inside and a woman on the outside manipulate a court trial involving a major gun manufacturer.
tagline: Trials are too important to be decided by juries.
title: Runaway Jury
plot:
Runaway Jury is a thought-provoking film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the corrupting influence of power. The movie revolves around the theme of manipulation, where characters use their charm and wit to influence others for personal gain.

At its core, Runaway Jury explores the idea of a system that can be easily manipulated by those who are skilled at it. The film highlights how the justice system can be exploited by those with the right connections and resources, leading to a miscarriage of justice. This theme is expertly woven throughout the narrative, as the protagonist, Nicholas Easter (played by Dustin Hoffman), navigates the complex web of corruption that surrounds the jury selection process.

The movie also touches on the theme of free will versus determinism, as characters are forced to make choices that ultimately lead them down a path of destruction. The film's portrayal of a system that is rigged against the innocent and vulnerable adds to the sense of unease and tension, leaving the audience questioning the very fabric of justice.

Furthermore, Runaway Jury explores the theme of obsession, as Nicholas Easter becomes increasingly fixated on exposing the corruption within the system. His single-minded pursuit drives him to take risks that put himself and others in harm's way, highlighting the dangers of unchecked ambition.

Overall, Runaway Jury is a gripping thriller that exposes the darker aspects of human nature and the corrupting influence of power. The film's thought-provoking themes and intricate plot make it a compelling watch, leaving audiences on the edge of their seats until the very end.

overview: Widower Cedric Brown hires Nanny McPhee to care for his seven rambunctious children, who have chased away all previous nannies. Taunted by Simon and his siblings, Nanny McPhee uses mystical powers to instill discipline. And when the children's great-aunt and benefactor, Lady Adelaide Stitch, threatens to separate the kids, the family pulls together under the guidance of Nanny McPhee.
tagline: You'll learn to love her. Warts and all.
title: Nanny McPhee
plot:
Nanny McPhee is a 2005 British fantasy comedy film directed by Chris Noonan and produced by Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer. The movie is based on the 1981 children's book "The Nanny Farm" by Christianna Brand.

The story begins with the introduction of the Grimstone family, consisting of Mr. and Mrs. Grimstone (played by Richard Griffiths and Corin Redgrave) and their five mischievous children: Thomas (Lucas Raine), Kate (Lara Pulver), Simon (Josh Flitter), Rachel (Scarlett Byrne), and Edgar (Nathan Bailey). The family is in disarray, with the children constantly causing chaos and mayhem.

When Mr. Grimstone dies suddenly, his will stipulates that the family must find a new nanny to care for their children within 30 days or face the consequences of being turned into donkeys. Desperate and unable to find anyone suitable, Mrs. Grimstone reluctantly accepts the help of Nanny McPhee (played by Emma Thompson), a magical and no-nonsense nanny with a mysterious past.

Nanny McPhee arrives at the Grimstone estate and quickly sets about restoring order and discipline to the household. She uses her magical powers to make the children behave, but also teaches them valuable lessons about responsibility, kindness, and empathy. As the days pass, the children begin to transform from spoiled brats into well-behaved and caring individuals.

However, Nanny McPhee's methods are not without controversy. The family soon discovers that she has a hidden agenda, which involves using her magic to make them confront their own flaws and weaknesses. Thomas, who is initially resistant to change, must come to terms with his own selfishness and learn to care for others. Kate, who is struggling with her own identity crisis, finds solace in Nanny McPhee's guidance.

As the 30-day deadline approaches, the Grimstone family faces a series of challenges that test their newfound relationships and Nanny McPhee's magical abilities. In the end, they successfully complete the tasks set by Mr. Grimstone's will, and Nanny McPhee is rewarded with a special gift: the ability to remain in the family's lives as a trusted friend and advisor.

The movie ends on a heartwarming note, with the Grimstone children having transformed into kind and caring individuals, thanks to Nanny McPhee's guidance. The film concludes that even the most difficult challenges can be overcome with love, discipline, and a little bit of magic.

Overall, Nanny McPhee is a delightful and entertaining film that explores themes of family, responsibility, and personal growth. With its talented cast, witty dialogue, and magical storyline, it has become a beloved classic among both children and adults alike.

overview: High school classmates, who once dubbed themselves the “cursed class,” reconnect at Christmas for their 15-year reunion. Over the course of their time reconnecting, the classmates challenge each other to remember who they were, who they are, and who they want to be.
title: Christmas Class Reunion
plot:
Christmas Class Reunion is a 2022 Canadian Christmas romantic comedy-drama television film directed by Jonathan A. Rosenbaum from a screenplay by Erin Rodman, produced by Lighthouse Pictures for Hallmark Channel. Adapted from Paul E. Wootten's book of the same name, it stars Aimee Teegarden as Elle and Tanner Novlan as Devin, with Dejan Loyola, Maya Ford, Stephanie Bennett, Marshall Williams, Dylan Archambault, Yasmeen Kelders as Devin's daughter Skylar and Andy Thompson. The film runs 84 minutes; it marked Novlan's first Hallmark role, after he had become known for playing John Finnegan on the soap opera The Bold and the Beautiful.

Elle, a former class valedictorian who has become a powerhouse in the tech industry, is the class president of a group of high school classmates who once dubbed themselves the "cursed class" after a run of disasters stretching back to their senior winter formal and continuing through their previous reunions. Determined to break the bad luck, she meticulously plans their fifteen-year reunion at Christmas, only to find that much of it depends on Devin, the former class clown and vice-president, whose events company is supplying the equipment and who had not intended to attend. When fire and water damage leaves them scrambling for a new venue, the two opposites work together to find another location, and Elle comes to appreciate the spontaneous approach to life of Devin, a single father devoted to his teenage daughter and his business. At the same time her career unravels when the CEO of her company, whom she cannot reach, is reported to be under FBI investigation. Elle had also hoped to reconnect with her high school crush, Kam, but spending time with him shows her that what she wanted at seventeen is not what she needs now. Alongside them, classmates including Sam, a successful broadcaster who still feels invisible, and a pair of high school sweethearts going through a rough patch challenge one another to remember who they were, who they are and who they want to be.

The film premiered on Hallmark Channel on 10 December 2022 as part of its Countdown to Christmas season. Alonso Duralde of TheWrap ranked it 33rd of the network's 43 new holiday films of 2022, crediting a valiant attempt at a different kind of storytelling and an appealing cast but finding it undermined by contrivances and illogical character choices. Kristen of TV Tweetie called it predictable and ho-hum, though she liked Novlan.

overview: From his rise as a business mogul to his plummet into international notoriety, this true crime documentary examines the bizarre story of Carlos Ghosn.
title: Fugitive: The Curious Case of Carlos Ghosn
plot:
Death Sentence is a 2007 American action thriller film directed by Peter Howitt and starring Kevin Costner, Lynn Collins, and John Gielgud. The movie follows the story of Nick Halsey (played by Kevin Costner), a widowed father who seeks revenge against the men responsible for his son's death.

The film begins with Nick Halsey, a former Army Ranger, living in rural Ohio with his wife, Laura (Lynn Collins), and their teenage son, Steve (Forest Whitaker). The family is struggling to cope with the loss of their daughter, who died in a car accident several years ago. Nick's life is marked by grief and anger, which he tries to keep under control.

However, when a group of thugs, led by a man named Victor Vex (John Malkovich), break into his home and kill Steve, Nick's world is shattered once again. The men are revealed to be the same gang that had been terrorizing the neighborhood for months, and they have been targeting families with young sons.

Nick becomes consumed by a desire for revenge against Victor and his gang. He begins to track them down, using his military skills to gather intelligence and plan his attacks. As he delves deeper into the world of organized crime, Nick's obsession with revenge grows, causing him to lose sight of what is truly important in life.

As the story unfolds, Nick's actions become increasingly violent and erratic. He starts to see himself as a vigilante, taking the law into his own hands. However, this newfound sense of purpose also puts a strain on his relationship with Laura, who tries to hold him back from descending into madness.

The film builds towards a tense showdown between Nick and Victor's gang. In a thrilling climax, Nick confronts the men responsible for Steve's death, leading to a violent and bloody confrontation. The ending is both satisfying and haunting, leaving the audience wondering if Nick has finally found closure or if his quest for revenge will consume him completely.

Throughout the film, Kevin Costner delivers a powerful performance as the complex and troubled Nick Halsey. His character's journey from grief to rage to redemption is both compelling and heartbreaking. The supporting cast, including Lynn Collins and John Malkovich, add depth and nuance to the story.

Overall, Death Sentence is a gripping and intense thriller that explores themes of grief, anger, and redemption. While it may not be an entirely original or subtle film, its strong performances and tense action sequences make for a compelling watch.

overview: Based on a true story, in which Richmond High School head basketball coach Ken Carter made headlines in 1999 for benching his undefeated team due to poor academic results.
tagline: It begins on the street. It ends here.
title: Coach Carter
plot:
Coach Carter is a biographical sports drama film released in 2005, directed by Thomas Carter and starring Samuel L. Jackson as Ken Carter, a high school basketball coach.

The movie is based on the true story of Ken Carter, who coached the Richmond High School basketball team in Richmond, California, in 1999-2000. The film begins with Coach Carter, a former NBA player, taking over as the new head coach of the Richmond High School basketball team. He is determined to teach his players not only about basketball but also about life and responsibility.

Initially, the team struggles due to poor attendance, lack of motivation, and behavioral issues. Coach Carter sets out to change this by implementing a strict set of rules and expectations for his players. He requires them to maintain a minimum GPA, attend classes regularly, and participate in community service. The players are initially resistant to these new rules, but Coach Carter's firm but fair approach eventually starts to take effect.

As the season progresses, the team begins to improve on the court, winning several games and gaining confidence. However, off the court, the players continue to struggle with their personal lives, including poverty, family problems, and gang involvement. Coach Carter becomes a mentor and father figure to his players, helping them to overcome their challenges and find a better path in life.

One of the key players, Kenyon Stone (played by Rob Brown), is particularly struggling with his own demons. He comes from a troubled home and has been involved with gangs. Coach Carter takes Kenyon under his wing, teaching him about responsibility and self-discipline. Through their relationship, Coach Carter helps Kenyon to turn his life around, earning a college scholarship and eventually becoming a successful businessman.

As the season reaches its climax, the team faces off against their arch-rivals, and Coach Carter's players must come together to overcome their personal struggles and win the game. In a thrilling finale, the team emerges victorious, but more importantly, they have learned valuable lessons about teamwork, perseverance, and the importance of education.

The movie ends with Coach Carter reflecting on the season and the progress his players have made. He is proud of what he has accomplished, not just as a coach but also as a mentor and role model. The film concludes with a sense of hope and renewal, as the players look to the future, armed with the knowledge and skills they have gained under Coach Carter's guidance.

Overall, Coach Carter is an inspiring true story about the power of sports to transform lives and communities. The movie features outstanding performances from its cast, particularly Samuel L. Jackson as Coach Carter, who brings depth and nuance to his portrayal of a complex and dedicated coach.

original_title: 劇場版ポケットモンスター アドバンスジェネレーション ミュウと波導の勇者 ルカリオ
overview: In the legendary past, before Poké Balls were invented, an aura-guiding hero Pokémon named Lucario sensed two groups of armies about to clash, and a threat of a massive war in front of Oldoran Castle in Kanto that would leave no survivors. He transferred this message to his master, the legendary hero Arlon, while he was being attacked by a violent group of Hellgar. During the battle, his sense of sight was lost and he was rendered unable to see. He used the detection of his Aura, and so with the offensive Wave Bomb, he eliminated them. Though by the threat, the queen of Rota, Lady Rin was resolute to die with her civilians, and so Arlon made a choice.
title: Pokémon: Lucario and the Mystery of Mew
plot:
Pokémon: Lucario and the Mystery of Mew is a 2005 Japanese animated fantasy film directed by Kunihiko Yuyama and produced by OLM, Inc. The eighth Pokémon film and the third connected to Pokémon the Series: Ruby and Sapphire, it features the voices of Rica Matsumoto, Ikue Ōtani, Yūji Ueda, Kaori, Fushigi Yamada and Megumi Hayashibara.

Long ago, as a war between Pokémon is about to break out near the Tree of Beginning, the Pokémon Lucario warns his master, the Aura Guardian Sir Aaron, but Aaron appears to abandon him, sealing Lucario inside his staff. The queen of Cameron Palace receives the staff and sees the Tree of Beginning glow as the war is averted. More than a thousand years later, Ash Ketchum and his friends arrive at Cameron Palace during a festival honoring Aaron. Ash, dressed like Aaron by coincidence, wins a tournament and is named that year's Aura Guardian. When he receives the staff, his aura, which resembles Aaron's, frees Lucario, who tells everyone of his master's betrayal.

Meanwhile, Pikachu and the other Pokémon play with a Mew that lives near the palace until two Weavile, sent by an adventurer named Kidd to tag Mew, chase them. Pikachu protects Mew, which teleports him and Team Rocket's Meowth away to the Tree of Beginning. Kidd joins Ash's group, and Lucario reluctantly agrees to guide them. Lucario's contempt for humans leads to a fight with Ash, but Ash eventually wins his trust. Along the way, "time flowers" replay visions of the past. After battling the tree's guardians, Regirock, Regice and Registeel, they enter, and Kidd's survey robots trigger the tree's antibody-like defenses, which absorb everyone until Mew reasons with the tree. The disruption sends the tree into shock, and Mew, which depends on it to survive, falls gravely ill. At the tree's heart a vision reveals that Aaron sacrificed himself, pouring his aura into the tree to stop the war. Ash and Lucario combine their aura to save the tree and Mew, but Lucario pushes Ash away to spare him. Exhausted, Lucario sees a final vision in which the dying Aaron explains that he sealed Lucario away to keep him alive and thanks him for his friendship, and Lucario passes away. Kidd keeps her discovery secret, and Ash vows to remember Lucario.

The film opened in Japan on July 16, 2005, and grossed ¥4.3 billion, the year's second-highest-grossing domestic film after Howl's Moving Castle. Anime News Network gave it a B−, praising its epic premise and animation but faulting the plot.

overview: A teenager's weekend at a lake house with her father takes a turn for the worse when a group of convicts wreaks havoc on their lives.
tagline: There once was a little girl...
title: Becky
plot:
Becky is a 2020 American thriller film directed by Jonathan Milott and Cary Murnion. The movie follows the story of Becky Miller, a young woman who embarks on a road trip with her boyfriend, David, to visit his family in rural Pennsylvania.

As Becky navigates this unfamiliar environment, she begins to uncover dark secrets about David's past and the true nature of his relationship with his family. The film expertly weaves together themes of toxic masculinity, gaslighting, and the complexities of female empowerment.

Through Becky's journey, the movie explores the idea that women are often expected to conform to societal norms and expectations, particularly in relationships where they may feel trapped or suffocated. As Becky struggles to assert her own identity and autonomy, she must confront the ways in which patriarchal systems can be both subtle and oppressive.

The film also touches on the theme of trauma and its lasting impact on individuals and families. David's past is slowly revealed, exposing a web of secrets and lies that have been hidden for years. This narrative thread serves as a commentary on how trauma can be passed down through generations, affecting not only the individual but also those around them.

Ultimately, Becky is a powerful exploration of female resilience and the importance of self-discovery in the face of adversity. The movie's tense atmosphere and slow-burning tension create a sense of unease, mirroring Becky's growing unease with her situation. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Becky must find a way to break free from the toxic dynamics that have been holding her back, embracing her own strength and agency in the process.

overview: For never-do-well compulsive gambler Fong, there's only one thing more fearsome than debtors at his doorstep - having to coax a crying baby. But what if the baby becomes his golden goose to fend off his debtors? Can he overcome his phobia of diapers, milk bottles, and cloying lullabies?
tagline: This September! Crawl Baby crawl!
title: Robin-B-Hood
plot:
Robin Hood (2006) is a historical action-adventure film directed by Ridley Scott, produced by Jerry Bruckheimer Films and Paramount Pictures, not JCE Movies.

The main themes of Robin Hood (2006) include:

1. Social inequality: The film highlights the vast wealth disparity between the rich nobles and the poor commoners in medieval England, which is a central theme of the classic tale.
2. Loyalty and friendship: The bond between Robin Hood (Kevin Costner), Little John (Morgan Freeman), Will Scarlett (Angus Macfadyen), and Friar Tuck (Alan Tudyk) is a key aspect of the story, showcasing the power of loyalty and friendship in the face of adversity.
3. Power struggle: The film explores the conflict between Robin Hood's outlaw group and the corrupt Sheriff of Nottingham (Mark Strong), who represents the oppressive forces of authority.
4. Redemption and personal growth: As Robin Hood navigates his role as a hero, he grapples with his own morality and the consequences of his actions, leading to a journey of self-discovery and redemption.

The film received mixed reviews from critics but was a commercial success, grossing over $321 million worldwide.

overview: An unemployed executive is forced to sell his apartment. When he discovers that he still has the keys, he becomes obsessed with the family that now lives there and decides to recover the life he has lost, at any price.
title: The Occupant
plot:
The Occupant (Spanish: Hogar, "home") is a 2020 Spanish psychological thriller written and directed by brothers David and Àlex Pastor. Javier Gutiérrez stars as an unemployed advertising executive who, forced to give up his luxurious apartment, uses an old set of keys to infiltrate the lives of the family who move in, with Mario Casas, Bruna Cusí and Ruth Díaz in the main supporting roles.

Once highly successful, Javier Muñoz can no longer find work, and he, his wife Marga and their son leave their apartment for a modest flat. Discovering that he still has a key, he secretly enters his old home and learns about the new tenants, Tomás, his wife Lara and their daughter Mónica. Finding that Tomás is a recovering alcoholic, Javier turns up at his support group posing as one himself, asks Tomás to be his sponsor, and wins an invitation to dinner. Javier learns that Tomás owes his job to Lara's father's company and that the couple often argue. He stages a drunken car crash, lets Tomás spill gin on himself while helping, and secretly sends himself a damning email from Tomás's phone. Damián, a groundsman who has noticed Javier's comings and goings, blackmails him into stealing Mónica's underwear and later planting a camera in her room. When Lara smells gin on Tomás and asks Javier to stay away, he shows her the email as proof that her husband has relapsed. Tomás, realising he has been played, beats Javier, while Damián is caught when a leaf blower Javier sabotaged explodes. Tended by Lara, Javier hints that Tomás is violent and gives her a pepper spray he has laced with peanut oil, knowing Tomás has a deadly peanut allergy. When the enraged Tomás comes home to confront Lara, she sprays him and he goes into anaphylactic shock; Javier arrives to "help", swaps the spray and suffocates him. Months later Javier has taken Tomás's job and married Lara. When Marga discovers the peanut oil and threatens to go to the police, he threatens to spend their son's savings on lawyers, and she backs down, leaving him content in his reclaimed home.

Gutiérrez plays Javier, with Casas as Tomás, Cusí as Lara, Díaz as Marga and David Ramírez as Damián. Planned to premiere at the Málaga Film Festival in March 2020 before the event was postponed by the COVID-19 pandemic, it was released on Netflix on March 25, 2020. Critics praised Gutiérrez's performance but found the character development meandering, giving it 61% on Rotten Tomatoes.

overview: An illustrious British boarding school becomes a bloody battleground when a mysterious sinkhole appears at a nearby fracking site unleashing unspeakable horror.
tagline: Bloodius. Hellius. Maximus.
title: Slaughterhouse Rulez
plot:
Slaughterhouse Rulez is a 2018 British comedy horror film directed by Crispian Mills, who wrote it with Henry Fitzherbert. The first production from Simon Pegg and Nick Frost's company Stolen Picture, it stars Finn Cole as Don Wallace, Asa Butterfield as Willoughby Blake and Hermione Corfield as Clemsie Lawrence, with Michael Sheen as the headmaster, Pegg as housemaster Meredith Houseman and Frost as eco-campaigner Woody Chapman.

After his father's death, Don, a working-class teenager from the north of England, is sent by his widowed mother to Slaughterhouse, a venerable and exclusive boarding school, in keeping with his late father's wishes. He struggles to fit in amid the school's arcane rituals and sanctioned bullying, and the place harbors secrets: a pupil died by suicide the previous term, there have been mysterious disappearances, and an overzealous sixth-form prefect, Clegg, descends from a long line of war criminals. Don forms an uneasy alliance with his sardonic new roommate, Willoughby, an outsider bullied by the older boys, and falls for Clemsie, one of the sixth form's revered "goddesses". The ineffectual Houseman, meanwhile, pines for his former girlfriend, who is working in Africa and appears only in video calls.

To raise money, the scheming headmaster has made a deal allowing a company to frack for gas near the school, to the fury of Woody, who is camping in the woods. The drilling opens an enigmatic sinkhole, and from it emerge packs of ravenous subterranean creatures that begin attacking the faculty and devouring pupils. Don rallies a group of students to fight back against the monsters. In the end the creatures are defeated and the school is destroyed in an explosion, while the surviving pupils walk away and the headmaster's dog and Houseman, who have also survived, watch the destruction.

Shot at locations including Stowe School, Windsor Great Park and Chislehurst Caves, the film was released in the United Kingdom and Ireland on October 31, 2018, and in North America in May 2019, earning about £738,000 at the box office. Critics were mostly negative, giving it 38% on Rotten Tomatoes and 39 on Metacritic; Screen International found its story strands underdeveloped, while The Guardian credited Mills with directing "with zip" and found an amiable charm despite it being neither very scary nor very funny.

overview: The adventure of Bella, a dog who embarks on an epic 400-mile journey home after she is separated from her beloved human.
tagline: A lot can happen between lost and found.
title: A Dog's Way Home
plot:
A Dog's Way Home is a heartwarming drama film released in 2019, directed by Charles Martin Smith and produced by Columbia Pictures.

The movie revolves around the story of Bella, a golden retriever who embarks on an incredible journey to find her way back home after being separated from her owner, Katie. The film begins with Bella's idyllic life with Katie, where they share a deep bond and enjoy numerous adventures together. However, one fateful day, while out on a hike, Bella gets lost in the woods.

As the days pass, Bella becomes determined to find her way back home, facing numerous challenges and obstacles along the way. She encounters various animals, including a stray cat named Max, who joins her on her journey. Together, they form an unbreakable bond, relying on each other for survival and comfort.

Throughout her journey, Bella faces many hardships, including harsh weather conditions, treacherous terrain, and encounters with wild predators. Despite these challenges, she remains steadfast in her determination to find her way back home. Along the way, she also meets a kind-hearted veterinarian named Dr. Davis, who helps her on her quest.

As Bella navigates through unfamiliar territories, she begins to realize that home is not just a physical place but also a sense of belonging and connection with those we love. Her journey becomes a metaphor for the human experience, highlighting the importance of perseverance, loyalty, and the unbreakable bond between humans and animals.

The film's climax features Bella's reunion with Katie, who has been searching for her beloved dog everywhere. The emotional reunion is a testament to the enduring power of their bond, which transcends time and distance.

Throughout the movie, the cinematography is breathtaking, capturing the beauty of nature and the resilience of Bella as she faces numerous challenges. The film's score, composed by Thomas Newman, adds depth and emotion to the story, perfectly capturing the mood and tone of each scene.

Overall, A Dog's Way Home is a heartwarming tale of love, loyalty, and perseverance, reminding us that home is where the heart is, and that even in the darkest of times, there is always hope for a reunion with those we love.

original_title: 名探偵コナン 探偵たちの鎮魂歌（レクイエム）
overview: Synopsis Kogoro and Conan came to Yokohama according to a request from a mysterious man. But that was a trap of this man. Ran and the Detective Boys will be taken as hostages. If they don't solve the request of the man within 12 hours, the bombs attached to the hostages will explode. Furthermore, the man know that Conan`s true identity is Kudo Shinichi. Also Hattori Heiji, the High School Detective of the West, and Kaito Kid enter the stage. Will they be able to solve the mystery within the time limit and save Ran and the others? And who in the world is the client?
title: Detective Conan: The Private Eyes' Requiem
plot:
Detective Conan: The Private Eyes' Requiem is a thought-provoking film that delves into the complexities of human nature, morality, and the blurred lines between good and evil. The movie masterfully weaves together intricate plot threads, keeping viewers engaged as they unravel the mystery alongside the protagonist, Shinichi Kudo.

At its core, the film explores the theme of identity and how it is shaped by our experiences, relationships, and choices. Shinichi's dual identity as both a detective and a child serves as a metaphor for the duality of human nature, where individuals can embody multiple personas depending on the situation. This dichotomy raises questions about the authenticity of one's self and the consequences of hiding or revealing one's true nature.

The movie also delves into the concept of justice and morality, presenting a nuanced portrayal of right and wrong. The antagonist, Eri Kisaragi, is a complex character whose motivations are rooted in a desire for revenge and justice, challenging the audience to reevaluate their assumptions about morality and the nature of evil.

Furthermore, Detective Conan: The Private Eyes' Requiem touches on the theme of sacrifice and the consequences of one's actions. Shinichi's willingness to put himself in harm's way to protect others serves as a testament to his character development and growth, highlighting the importance of selflessness and putting the needs of others before one's own.

Throughout the film, TMS Entertainment skillfully crafts a narrative that is both engaging and thought-provoking, inviting viewers to reflect on their own values and moral compass. The movie's exploration of complex themes and characters makes it a compelling watch, leaving a lasting impression on audiences long after the credits roll.

overview: Alice, now 19 years old, returns to the whimsical world she first entered as a child and embarks on a journey to discover her true destiny.
tagline: You're invited to a very important date.
title: Alice in Wonderland
plot:
Alice in Wonderland is a 2010 American Gothic dark fantasy adventure film directed by Tim Burton from a screenplay by Linda Woolverton and produced by Walt Disney Pictures. A live-action reimagining of Lewis Carroll's works, it stars Mia Wasikowska as Alice Kingsleigh, Johnny Depp as the Mad Hatter, Helena Bonham Carter as the Red Queen, Anne Hathaway as the White Queen, Crispin Glover as the Knave of Hearts and Matt Lucas as Tweedledum and Tweedledee, with the voices of Alan Rickman, Stephen Fry, Michael Sheen and Christopher Lee.

In 1871 London, nineteen-year-old Alice, still grieving her father and troubled by recurring strange dreams, is proposed to by Hamish Ascot at a garden party. Spotting a white rabbit in a waistcoat, she follows it down a rabbit hole and enters a fantastical world called Underland. There Absolem the Caterpillar says she is destined to slay the Jabberwocky and end the tyranny of the Red Queen, who has usurped her sister, the White Queen. The Red Queen's knights and the monstrous Bandersnatch capture most of Alice's companions, but she escapes, and the Cheshire Cat leads her to the tea party of the Mad Hatter and the March Hare. The Hatter sacrifices his freedom so she can flee, and the bloodhound Bayard, an ally of the resistance, takes her to the Red Queen's castle.

Grown huge again and posing as a courtier named "Um", Alice learns that the vorpal sword, the only weapon able to kill the Jabberwocky, is kept in the Bandersnatch's den. When she rebuffs the Knave's advances, the jealous queen orders her beheaded, but Alice takes the sword, wins over the Bandersnatch by returning its stolen eye and escapes to the White Queen. The Cheshire Cat frees the Hatter, who stirs rebellion, and Absolem, entering his chrysalis, helps Alice remember that she visited "Wonderland" as a child. On a chessboard battlefield, Alice beheads the Jabberwocky, the Red Queen's knights abandon her, and the White Queen exiles her sister with the Knave. Using the Jabberwocky's blood, Alice returns home, turns down Hamish and proposes to Lord Ascot her father's idea of trading routes to Hong Kong, becoming his apprentice; as she sets sail, Absolem, now a butterfly, lands on her shoulder.

The film grossed $1.025 billion worldwide, the second-highest total of 2010. Reviews were mixed, with 51% on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus called it a visual treat lacking heart. It won Academy Awards for Best Art Direction and Best Costume Design.

overview: Obsessed with teaching his victims the value of life, a deranged, sadistic serial killer abducts the morally wayward. Once captured, they must face impossible choices in a horrific game of survival. The victims must fight to win their lives back, or die trying...
tagline: Live or die. Make your choice.
title: Saw
plot:
Saw is a 2004 American psychological horror film directed by James Wan and written by Leigh Whannell. The film stars Cary Elwes, Danny Glover, Michael Emerson, Ken Leung, and Donnie Wahlberg.

The movie begins with Dr. Lawrence Gordon (Cary Elwes), a successful surgeon who finds himself chained in a run-down industrial bathroom with no recollection of how he got there. He soon discovers that he is not alone, as another prisoner, Adam Faulkner (Leigh Whannell), has also been left chained in the room. The two men are informed by a mysterious figure known as Jigsaw (Tobin Bell) through a video message that they have 60 minutes to escape the room or face a gruesome death.

As the game begins, Gordon and Faulkner realize that they must work together to find a way out of the room. However, their efforts are hindered by the fact that they do not know each other's skills or expertise. The two men start to suspect that Jigsaw is using them in some twisted experiment, but they cannot figure out what it is.

As time runs out, Gordon and Faulkner discover a series of clues left behind by Jigsaw, including a cryptic message on the wall and a hidden key. They also learn that Jigsaw has a personal connection to their lives, having been a successful surgeon himself who became disillusioned with his work.

Throughout the film, the tension builds as Gordon and Faulkner try to outsmart each other and find a way out of the room. However, it becomes clear that one of them will not survive. The film's climax features a shocking twist: Adam is revealed to be Jigsaw's son, who was killed in an accident involving his father.

In the end, Gordon manages to escape the room by using the key to unlock the door and making a desperate bid for freedom. However, as he emerges from the bathroom, he realizes that he has lost his sense of purpose and is now haunted by the memories of what happened in the room.

The film's ending sets the stage for the rest of the Saw franchise, introducing the character of Jigsaw and establishing the theme of the series: that people must face their own mortality and make difficult choices to survive. The movie's success can be attributed to its clever plot twists, tense atmosphere, and memorable performances from the cast.

Overall, Saw is a gripping horror film that explores themes of survival, sacrifice, and redemption. Its twisty plot and suspenseful atmosphere have made it a classic in the horror genre, and its influence can still be seen in many modern horror films.

overview: As the Avengers and their allies have continued to protect the world from threats too large for any one hero to handle, a new danger has emerged from the cosmic shadows: Thanos. A despot of intergalactic infamy, his goal is to collect all six Infinity Stones, artifacts of unimaginable power, and use them to inflict his twisted will on all of reality. Everything the Avengers have fought for has led up to this moment - the fate of Earth and existence itself has never been more uncertain.
tagline: An entire universe. Once and for all.
title: Avengers: Infinity War
plot:
Avengers: Infinity War is a 2018 superhero film directed by Anthony and Joe Russo, produced by Marvel Studios, and based on the Marvel Comics series of the same name. The movie brings together a vast ensemble cast of characters from the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) to fight against an intergalactic threat.

The story begins with Thanos (Josh Brolin), a powerful Titan who seeks to collect all six Infinity Stones, which would grant him unimaginable power and allow him to wipe out half of all life in the universe. The Avengers, led by Iron Man (Robert Downey Jr.), Captain America (Chris Evans), Thor (Chris Hemsworth), Hulk (Mark Ruffalo), Black Widow (Scarlett Johansson), and Hawkeye (Jeremy Renner), are alerted to Thanos' plan and band together to stop him.

Meanwhile, the Guardians of the Galaxy, consisting of Peter Quill (Chris Pratt), Gamora (Zoe Saldana), Drax (Dave Bautista), Rocket Raccoon (Bradley Cooper), and Groot (Vin Diesel), also become entangled in Thanos' quest. The two groups eventually join forces to take down Thanos.

As the battle against Thanos intensifies, the Avengers and their allies face numerous challenges, including Thanos' army of Black Order warriors, the Chitauri, and other formidable foes. Along the way, characters like Doctor Strange (Benedict Cumberbatch), Spider-Man (Tom Holland), and Black Panther (Chadwick Boseman) also make appearances.

Throughout the film, Thanos' motivations are explored, revealing a tragic backstory that drives his desire to collect the Infinity Stones. The movie's climax features an epic showdown between the Avengers and Thanos, resulting in a devastating conclusion that sets the stage for the events of Avengers: Endgame.

One of the standout aspects of Avengers: Infinity War is its ability to balance individual character arcs with the larger narrative. The film expertly weaves together multiple storylines, creating a sense of urgency and stakes that propels the audience towards the movie's shocking conclusion.

Overall, Avengers: Infinity War is a masterclass in ensemble storytelling, featuring an impressive cast of characters and a narrative that is both action-packed and emotionally resonant.

overview: A British medical doctor fights a cholera outbreak in a small Chinese village, while also being trapped at home in a loveless marriage to an unfaithful wife.
tagline: Sometimes the greatest journey is the distance between two people.
title: The Painted Veil
plot:
The Painted Veil is a 2006 drama film directed by John Curran from a screenplay by Ron Nyswaner, based on W. Somerset Maugham's 1925 novel of the same title. Naomi Watts, Edward Norton, Toby Jones, Anthony Wong Chau Sang and Liev Schreiber appear in the leading roles. It is the third screen version of the novel, after films in 1934 and 1957.

In London in the early 1920s, the earnest bacteriologist Walter Fane is captivated by the socialite Kitty Garstin and proposes. Eager to escape her mother, Kitty accepts, and after a honeymoon in Venice, where she shows little interest in his love of the city's canals and museums, the mismatched couple travel to Shanghai, where Walter studies infectious diseases at a government laboratory. Kitty prefers the parties and gossip of British expatriate society and begins a passionate secret affair with Charles Townsend, a married British vice consul. Walter discovers it and, having volunteered to fight a cholera epidemic in a remote part of China, insists that Kitty come with him or face a divorce, which he will grant quietly only if Townsend leaves his wife Dorothy to marry her. As Walter expected, Townsend will not commit, and Kitty is forced on a gruelling two-week overland journey to the mountain village of Mei-tan-fu, a route Walter chose to make her suffer. Living in a shabby house outside town, she is lonely and barely speaks with her husband. Their neighbour Waddington, a British deputy commissioner, tells her that Townsend is a womanizer, and she keeps back a desperate letter to him. Kitty begins volunteering at an orphanage run by French nuns, and through the work and what the nuns tell her of Walter's courage and devotion, she outgrows her self-absorption, while he sees she is no longer the shallow woman he married. Their marriage blossoms, and when Kitty becomes pregnant without knowing who the father is, Walter tells her it does not matter. As his clean-water aqueducts bring the epidemic under control, infected refugees arrive, and Walter catches cholera and dies despite Kitty's care. Five years later in London, Kitty is out with her young son, also named Walter, when they meet Townsend, and she rejects his advances.

Shot largely in Guangxi, China, the film opened in a limited American release in December 2006 and grossed about $26.9 million worldwide. It holds a 74% Rotten Tomatoes rating, and Alexandre Desplat's score won the Golden Globe for Best Original Score.

overview: Daniela, raised in the bosom of a strict Evangelical family and recently unmasked as a fornicator by her shocked parents, struggles to find her own path to spiritual harmony.
tagline: God loves ME
title: Young and Wild
plot:
Young and Wild is a 2012 Chilean drama film directed by Mariana Di Giacomo. The movie follows the story of two young friends, Alessia and Marco, who embark on a journey to explore the world and find themselves.

The main theme of Young and Wild revolves around the struggle for identity and self-discovery in a society that often pressures individuals to conform to traditional norms. The film portrays the characters' desire for freedom and independence as they navigate through various experiences, including travel, relationships, and personal growth.

Throughout their journey, Alessia and Marco face numerous challenges that force them to confront their own desires, values, and sense of purpose. The movie explores themes of youthful rebellion, nonconformity, and the search for meaning in a world that often seems overwhelming.

The film also touches on the complexities of female relationships, particularly the bond between Alessia and her mother, which is marked by tension, love, and ultimately, understanding. The portrayal of these relationships adds depth to the narrative, highlighting the challenges faced by women in patriarchal societies.

Ultimately, Young and Wild is a poignant coming-of-age story that explores the complexities of identity, self-discovery, and the human search for meaning in a world filled with uncertainty and possibility.

overview: A calamity at Dante and Randall's shops sends them looking for new horizons - but they ultimately settle at Mooby's, a fictional Disney-McDonald's-style fast-food empire.
tagline: With no power comes no responsibility.
title: Clerks II
plot:
Clerks II is a 2006 American comedy film directed by Kevin Smith. The movie follows the further adventures of Dante Hicks and Randal Graves, two convenience store clerks who are struggling to find their place in the world.

The main theme of Clerks II revolves around the monotony and desperation that can come with feeling stuck in one's life. Dante and Randal's mundane jobs at the Quick Stop convenience store serve as a backdrop for their existential crises, as they grapple with feelings of restlessness and discontent. The film explores the idea that even small, seemingly insignificant moments can be imbued with meaning and purpose.

Throughout the movie, Smith also delves into themes of friendship and loyalty, highlighting the strong bond between Dante and Randal despite their differences. Their relationship serves as a source of comfort and support for each other, allowing them to navigate the challenges of adulthood together.

Furthermore, Clerks II touches on the idea of identity and self-discovery, particularly in the context of growing older and facing the reality of one's own mortality. The film's characters are forced to confront their own limitations and vulnerabilities, leading to a deeper understanding of themselves and their place in the world.

Overall, Clerks II is a thought-provoking comedy that explores the complexities of human relationships, existential crises, and the search for meaning in everyday life.

overview: Buddy is a young boy on the cusp of adolescence, whose life is filled with familial love, childhood hijinks, and a blossoming romance. Yet, with his beloved hometown caught up in increasing turmoil, his family faces a momentous choice: hope the conflict will pass or leave everything they know behind for a new life.
tagline: No matter how far you go, you never forget where you came from.
title: Belfast
plot:
Belfast is a 2021 coming-of-age drama film directed by Kenneth Branagh, produced by Paula Wegner and Kenneth Branagh, and written by Kenneth Branagh.

The main themes of Belfast include:

1. **Coming of Age**: The film follows the story of a young boy growing up in Belfast during the Troubles, exploring his relationships with family members, friends, and community.
2. **Nostalgia and Memory**: The movie is set against the backdrop of historical events, but its focus on the protagonist's personal experiences and memories creates a sense of nostalgia and introspection.
3. **Identity and Belonging**: The film explores the complexities of identity, particularly in the context of sectarianism and community divisions in Belfast during the 1960s and 1970s.
4. **Family and Relationships**: The story centers around the relationships between family members, friends, and neighbors, highlighting the importance of human connections in shaping our experiences and understanding of the world.
5. **War and Trauma**: The film touches on the impact of the Troubles on individuals and communities, exploring themes of violence, loss, and resilience.

The movie's narrative is presented through a non-linear structure, with the protagonist reflecting on his childhood experiences as an adult. This framing device allows for a nuanced exploration of the past, its effects on the present, and the power of memory to shape our understanding of ourselves and our place in the world.

Overall, Belfast is a poignant and thought-provoking film that explores the complexities of human experience through the lens of personal history and community relationships.

overview: To prevent a world war from breaking out, famous characters from Victorian literature band together to do battle against a cunning villain.
production_companies: Mediastream Dritte Film GmbH & Co. Beteiligungs KG
tagline: The power of seven become a league of one.
title: The League of Extraordinary Gentlemen
plot:
The League of Extraordinary Gentlemen is a 2003 superhero film directed by Stephen Norrington, produced by 20th Century Fox, and based on the comic book series of the same name by Alan Moore and Kevin O'Neill.

The main themes of The League of Extraordinary Gentlemen revolve around the intersection of science fiction, adventure, and social commentary. Here are some of the key themes:

1. **Rebellion against authority**: The film's protagonist, Mina Murray (Peneélop Cruz), is a strong-willed woman who defies societal norms to join the League. This theme is echoed in the character of Allan Quatermain (Shane West), a big game hunter who becomes embroiled in the adventure. Both characters embody the spirit of rebellion against authority, challenging the status quo and pushing boundaries.
2. **Science vs. superstition**: The film explores the tension between scientific rationality and supernatural forces. The League's battles against the villainous Dr. Jekyll (Jason Flemyng) and his monstrous alter ego, Mr. Hyde, serve as a metaphor for the struggle between reason and madness.
3. **Identity and self-discovery**: As the characters navigate their respective pasts and present-day circumstances, they are forced to confront their own identities and motivations. Mina's journey, in particular, is one of self-discovery, as she grapples with her own desires and sense of purpose.
4. **Friendship and camaraderie**: The League itself serves as a microcosm for the power of friendship and teamwork. Despite their differences, the members of the League come together to form a united front against their enemies, demonstrating that even disparate individuals can find common ground and work towards a shared goal.
5. **Social commentary on Victorian era**: The film is set in the late 19th century, during the height of the British Empire's power and influence. The movie offers commentary on the social issues of the time, including colonialism, imperialism, and the treatment of women.

Overall, The League of Extraordinary Gentlemen is a thrilling adventure that explores complex themes and ideas through its engaging characters and action-packed plot.

overview: The teenage son of two fathers makes a documentary film about his parents but is surprised when a real-life plot twist occurs in his family.
title: The Invisible Thread
plot:
The Invisible Thread (Italian: Il filo invisibile) is a 2022 Italian coming-of-age comedy-drama directed by Marco Simon Puccioni, who co-wrote it with Luca De Bei. Made for Netflix, it stars Francesco Gheghi as a teenager raised by two fathers, played by Filippo Timi and Francesco Scianna, with Giulia Maenza, Emanuele Maria Di Stefano, Matteo Oscar Giuggioli, Valentina Cervi and Jodhi May in supporting roles.

The film opens with a school video project that Leone Ferrari is making with his best friend Jacopo, in which he tells the story of his own "rainbow family". His fathers, Paolo, a trained architect, and Simone, who runs a restaurant, have been together for nearly twenty years. Because gay couples cannot adopt in Italy, they had Leone with the help of Tilly, a surrogate mother in the United States who remains part of their lives, and the video traces the legal battles that followed, from the couple's civil union to the long struggle to have both men recognised as Leone's parents. The fathers are uneasy about having their private life put on display, and they have never taken DNA tests to find out which of them is Leone's biological father, since it never seemed to matter.

Leone falls for Anna, a new French girl at school, but has to deal with the prejudice of classmates who assume that the son of a gay couple must be gay himself, not least from Anna's aggressive twin brother Dario. Then a phone mishap reveals to Paolo that Simone has been cheating on him for two years, and the revelation explodes on the day of their twentieth anniversary. Simone moves out, the two men wage an increasingly petty war against each other, and Leone, who finds himself the most mature member of the family, is caught between them. The separation raises legal questions about his status, and the identity of his biological father, a question Jacopo had said would make their video more exciting, becomes a source of real conflict, forcing Leone to reflect on the invisible thread that binds him to his fathers and to everyone who helped bring him into the world.

Released on Netflix in March 2022, the film received mixed reviews. Critics praised Gheghi's understated central performance and the film's matter-of-fact depiction of a same-sex family, but several found the mix of teen comedy and divorce drama uneven and the parents' shouting matches tiresome.

overview: An African American male is imprisoned and placed in solitary confinement after being found guilty of murdering his wife, as he's haunted by internal demons and his dead wife, and pushed to the breaking point by an abusive female guard.
tagline: There is no getting out.
title: Caged
plot:
Caged is a 2020 American psychological prison drama directed by Aaron Fjellman, who co-wrote the screenplay with James "Doc" Mason. Edi Gathegi stars as an affluent African American psychiatrist convicted of murdering his wife who is placed in solitary confinement, where isolation and an abusive guard push him toward madness, with Melora Hardin, Angela Sarafyan and Tony Amendola in supporting roles.

Dr. Harlow Reid, sent to federal prison for killing his wife Amber, is being moved into the Security Housing Unit, the SHU, when he makes a last call to his lawyers and learns that they have dropped his case. A secretary tells him his assets have been seized, so his appeal for a new trial must be resubmitted through a public defender, but inside his cell he has no access to his belongings, not even a sharpened pencil, and simply drafting the appeal becomes a struggle. Maintaining his innocence, he is subjected to abuse, from being denied full portions of food to constant taunting by Officer Sacks, a vicious guard determined to dispense her own justice, who tells him she longs to see him hang himself with his bedsheet. The pious Warden Perez insists that rehabilitation begins with confessing to the crime, while Sacks's colleague Ganser largely ignores what happens. Increasingly cut off, Harlow speaks with a fellow inmate in a neighbouring cell, argues with his own reflection, and is haunted by hallucinations, from imagining his cell underwater to visions of a steak dinner and of his dead wife. Flashbacks recall his final moments with Amber, a cold woman who had been unfaithful, and the argument over her wealthy parents and her affair that preceded her mysterious death in an incident involving a yacht. As his mind deteriorates, Harlow begins to question his own memory, his innocence and his sanity, turning his time in the SHU into an unending nightmare.

Gathegi plays Harlow, with Hardin as Sacks, Sarafyan as Amber, Amendola as Perez and Robert R. Shafer as Ganser. Shot from October 2016 under the working title The SHU at Remmet Studios in Canoga Park, Los Angeles, with exteriors in Long Beach, Palmdale and Anaheim, it premiered at the 2020 Pasadena International Film Festival, where Fjellman won Best Director. Delayed by the COVID-19 pandemic, it was released on demand in January 2021. Reviews were mixed to positive, with 72% on Rotten Tomatoes; critics praised Gathegi's performance and the surreal imagery but found the supporting characters thin.

overview: One year after outwitting the FBI and winning the public’s adulation with their mind-bending spectacles, the Four Horsemen resurface only to find themselves face to face with a new enemy who enlists them to pull off their most dangerous heist yet.
tagline: You haven't seen anything yet.
title: Now You See Me 2
plot:
Now You See Me 2 is a 2016 American mystery film directed by Jon M. Chu and written by Ed Solomon, Boaz Yakin, and Edward Ricourt. The movie is the sequel to the 2013 film Now You See Me.

The story begins with an FBI agent, Dylan Rhodes (Mark Ruffalo), who has been tasked with tracking down a group of magicians known as "The Four Horsemen" - a group that was thought to be long gone after their last heist in Las Vegas. The team consists of J. Daniel Atlas (Jesse Eisenberg), Henley Reeves (Lindsay Lohan), Merritt McKinney (Woody Harrelson), and Jack Wilder (Dave Franco).

The Four Horsemen are now on the run, using their magical skills to evade capture. They plan a massive heist in Macau, China, where they will steal $640 million from a casino vault. The team uses their unique abilities to infiltrate the vault and escape with the money.

As the FBI closes in on the team, Dylan Rhodes is forced to work with Interpol agent Alma Dray (Mélanie Laurent) to track down the Four Horsemen. Along the way, they uncover a conspiracy involving a wealthy businessman named Arthur Tressler (Michael Caine), who has been using his wealth and influence to cover up a massive money laundering scheme.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that The Four Horsemen are not just ordinary magicians, but rather highly skilled performers with a hidden agenda. They use their magic to manipulate people's perceptions of reality, making it difficult for Dylan and Alma to distinguish between what is real and what is an illusion.

Throughout the movie, the team uses their magical abilities to stay one step ahead of their pursuers, while also uncovering the truth behind Arthur Tressler's scheme. In the end, The Four Horsemen use their combined skills to expose Tressler's conspiracy and bring him to justice.

The movie features a mix of magic tricks, illusions, and clever plot twists, keeping the audience guessing until the very end. While some critics felt that the sequel did not live up to the original, Now You See Me 2 remains an entertaining and visually stunning film with a talented cast and impressive magical performances.

Overall, Now You See Me 2 is a thrilling mystery film that explores the world of magic and illusion, while also delving into themes of deception, loyalty, and redemption.

overview: After the Evil Queen marries the King, she performs a violent coup in which the King is murdered and his daughter, Snow White, is taken captive. Almost a decade later, a grown Snow White is still in the clutches of the Queen. In order to obtain immortality, The Evil Queen needs the heart of Snow White. After Snow escapes the castle, the Queen sends the Huntsman to find her in the Dark Forest.
tagline: The Fairytale is Over
title: Snow White and the Huntsman
plot:
Snow White and the Huntsman is a 2012 American dark fantasy film directed by Rupert Sanders and produced by Universal Pictures. The movie is based on the classic fairy tale "Snow White" but with significant changes to its storyline, characters, and tone.

The story begins in medieval Europe, where Queen Ravenna (Charlize Theron) has stolen the magical mirror that allows her to maintain her youth and beauty. She uses the mirror's power to control the kingdom and rule with an iron fist. When the mirror reveals that Snow White (Kristen Stewart), a beautiful princess, is the fairest of them all, Ravenna becomes obsessed with killing Snow White.

Meanwhile, in a small village on the outskirts of the kingdom, a huntsman named Gary (Chris Hemsworth) is tasked by King Magnus (Nick Frost) to take Snow White into the forest and kill her. However, when Gary discovers that Snow White is innocent and kind-hearted, he decides to spare her life and sets her free in the forest.

Snow White soon finds herself facing numerous challenges as she tries to survive in the harsh wilderness. She befriends a group of dwarfs, including Doc (Bob Clark), Grumpy (Ray Stevenson), Happy (Nick Frost), Sleepy (Sam Spruell), Bashful (Lee Homsworth), Sneezy (Jack Davenport), and Dopey (Jonathan Sells). Together, they form a tight-knit community that helps Snow White to heal from her past traumas.

As the story unfolds, Ravenna becomes increasingly desperate to kill Snow White, and she orders her huntsman, William (Sam Claflin), to bring back Snow White's heart. However, William is torn between his loyalty to the queen and his growing feelings for Snow White. In a dramatic twist, William ultimately betrays Ravenna and helps Snow White to escape.

The movie takes a dark turn as Snow White and her dwarfs discover that they are being hunted by Ravenna's army of woodland creatures, including wolves, bears, and other mythical beasts. The group must fight for their lives in a desperate bid to reach the safety of the kingdom.

In the climactic final battle, Snow White and her allies face off against Ravenna and her minions. In a shocking turn of events, William sacrifices himself to save Snow White, and she ultimately kills Ravenna with the queen's own magic mirror.

The movie ends with Snow White being crowned the new queen of the kingdom, and she rules with kindness, wisdom, and justice. The film concludes on a hopeful note, suggesting that Snow White has finally found her true home and happiness.

Overall, Snow White and the Huntsman is a dark and action-packed retelling of the classic fairy tale. The movie features stunning visuals, impressive stunts, and a strong performance from Kristen Stewart as the titular character. While it deviates significantly from the original story, the film remains faithful to its core themes of beauty, kindness, and the struggle for power.

overview: A day in the life of a barbershop on the south side of Chicago. Calvin, who inherited the struggling business from his deceased father, views the shop as nothing but a burden and waste of his time. After selling the shop to a local loan shark, Calvin slowly begins to see his father's vision and legacy and struggles with the notion that he just sold it out.
tagline: Everyone's gettin' lined up.
title: Barbershop
plot:
Barbershop is a 2002 American comedy film directed by Tim Story, produced by Reginald Hudlin and Don Cheadle, and written by Rick Famuyiwa. The movie takes place in Chicago's South Side and revolves around the lives of three barbers: Calvin Palmer (Ice Cube), Eddie (Cedric the Entertainer), and Marnell (Erik Prince).

The main themes of Barbershop include:

1. Community and camaraderie: The film highlights the strong bonds between the barbers, who serve as a support system for each other and their clients. They often engage in witty banter, share stories, and offer advice, creating a sense of community and belonging.
2. Friendship and loyalty: Calvin, Eddie, and Marnell are more than just coworkers; they're friends who have each other's backs. The movie showcases the importance of loyal friendships and how they can help navigate life's challenges.
3. Social commentary on racism and stereotypes: Barbershop tackles issues like racism, police brutality, and stereotyping in a lighthearted yet thought-provoking way. The film uses humor to address these sensitive topics, making it more palatable for a wider audience.
4. Self-discovery and personal growth: As the story unfolds, each character faces their own struggles and undergoes significant personal growth. Calvin, in particular, learns to let go of his anger and resentment towards the police, while Eddie finds his place in the world beyond the barbershop.

The movie's success can be attributed to its well-developed characters, engaging storyline, and timely commentary on social issues. Barbershop has become a cult classic, praised for its humor, heart, and authentic portrayal of African American life in the early 2000s.

overview: A man crossing into Mexico with a satchel of $2,000,000—and a bloody past—finds himself under sudden attack in the sleepy town of El Fronteras.
title: El Gringo
plot:
El Gringo, also known as Bad Yankee, is a 2012 American action film directed by Eduardo Rodríguez from a screenplay by Jonathan Stokes and produced by After Dark Films. Scott Adkins stars as an unnamed drifter credited only as The Man, with Yvette Yates as the barmaid Anna and Christian Slater as his former boss, Lieutenant West; Israel Islas, Erando González and Sofía Sisniega also appear. After Dark bought Stokes's script in 2011 with Joel Silver attached as executive producer, and the film was shot in Bulgaria and Louisiana on an estimated budget of about seven million dollars.

The Man is an undercover DEA agent who survives a bloody ambush in which he is wounded and his fellow agents are killed.
