Leaving his old life behind, he slips across the border into Mexico carrying a bag that holds two million dollars and arrives in the dusty, lawless town of El Fronteras, intending to catch a bus onward to Acapulco. His simple goal proves maddeningly hard to reach. The locals refuse to sell him so much as a glass of water or tell him when the next bus leaves, the single daily departure keeps slipping out of reach, and the money he carries repeatedly goes missing as word of it spreads. The corrupt local sheriff and his men and a violent drug cartel that effectively controls the town all want a share of the cash.

His only local ally is Anna, who runs the bar, while Lieutenant West doggedly follows his trail from across the border. Flashbacks gradually fill in the ambush and the agent's checkered past, and a twist late in the story shifts the focus onto who his true enemy is. The film's centerpiece is an extended shootout in the town's narrow alleys as he fights his way through waves of gunmen in an attempt to reach the bus station.

El Gringo opened in the United States in May 2012 with an R rating as part of the After Dark Action series, playing for one week in ten cities while being released on video on demand at the same time. Critics generally found it diverting but unremarkable. Variety saw it as an exercise in third-hand cool that nods to spaghetti westerns and 1970s drive-in action pictures, and the Los Angeles Times judged it not bad but not especially notable. IndieWire faulted its convoluted plotting while praising its fast, inventive fight choreography and gunplay, and other reviewers compared its style, often unfavorably, to Robert Rodriguez's Mariachi films and criticizing its frenetic editing.

overview: A journalist tries to balance the duties of marriage and motherhood while researching a piece on college women who work as prostitutes to pay their tuition.
tagline: The world's oldest profession still has its secrets.
title: Elles
plot:
Elles is a 2011 French drama film directed by Olivier Assayas, not Canal+ Polska. The movie explores the complex relationships between women and their desires, particularly in the context of a workplace where they are expected to conform to societal norms.

The main theme of Elles revolves around the tension between the characters' inner lives and the external expectations placed upon them. The film delves into the ways in which women navigate these conflicting demands, often leading to feelings of disconnection and disillusionment.

Through the character of Anna, a young woman struggling to find her place in the world, the movie examines the societal pressures that shape women's experiences. The film also touches on themes of identity, desire, and the search for meaning in a seemingly superficial world.

Ultimately, Elles presents a nuanced portrayal of women's lives, highlighting the complexities and contradictions that arise when individual desires clash with external expectations.

overview: A truffle hunter who lives alone in the Oregon wilderness must visit Portland to find the mysterious person who stole his beloved foraging pig.
tagline: We don’t get a lot of things to really care about.
title: Pig
plot:
Pig is a 2021 American drama film directed by Michael Sarnoski, produced by Saturn Films, and released on Netflix.

The main themes of Pig revolve around loneliness, grief, trauma, and the human connection. The story follows Robin (played by Nicolas Cage), a pig farmer who embarks on a journey to find his stolen pig, Rosalyn, after she is taken from him in a tragic event.

Throughout the film, Robin's character grapples with the loss of his beloved pet and the emotional trauma that follows. His obsession with finding Rosalyn becomes an all-consuming force, driving him to confront his past and re-evaluate his relationships with others.

As the story unfolds, themes of loneliness and isolation become increasingly apparent. Robin's life is marked by a sense of disconnection from the world around him, and his fixation on Rosalyn serves as a coping mechanism for his emotional pain.

The film also explores the complexities of human connection and the power of relationships in healing emotional wounds. Through Robin's interactions with various characters, including a young woman named Natalie (played by Alexandra Daddario), the film highlights the importance of empathy, understanding, and compassion in building meaningful connections with others.

Ultimately, Pig is a poignant exploration of the human condition, delving into the complexities of grief, trauma, and the search for connection in a world that often feels isolating.

original_title: Starship Troopers 2: Hero of the Federation
overview: In the sequel to Paul Verhoeven's loved/reviled sci-fi film, a group of troopers taking refuge in an abandoned outpost after fighting alien bugs, failing to realize that more danger lays in wait.
tagline: They're Coming Back to Wipe Us Out!
title: Starship Troopers 2: Hero of the Federation
plot:
Starship Troopers 2: Hero of the Federation is a science fiction film directed by Phil Tippett, and it serves as a sequel to the 1997 film Starship Troopers. The movie takes place after the events of the first film and follows Johnny Rico (played by Casper Van Dien) as he becomes the commander of the Mobile Infantry's elite unit.

The main themes of Starship Troopers 2: Hero of the Federation include:

1. Leadership and Responsibility: As Johnny Rico assumes command, he must navigate the complexities of leadership and make difficult decisions that impact the lives of his soldiers.
2. Loyalty and Sacrifice: The film explores the bonds of loyalty between Rico and his fellow soldiers, as well as the sacrifices they must make to protect humanity from the Bug threat.
3. War and its Consequences: Starship Troopers 2 delves into the psychological effects of war on individuals and society, highlighting the moral dilemmas that come with fighting an alien invasion.
4. Power Struggles and Corruption: The movie introduces a new villain, General Hanly (played by Neil Patrick Harris), who seeks to overthrow the Federation's government and take control for himself.

The plot development revolves around Rico's efforts to stop Hanly's coup and save humanity from destruction. Along the way, he must confront his own demons and make tough choices that will determine the fate of the Federation.

As for the ending, it sets the stage for a potential third installment in the series, leaving room for further exploration of the Starship Troopers universe.

overview: Prince Akeem Joffer is set to become King of Zamunda when he discovers he has a son he never knew about in America – a street savvy Queens native named Lavelle. Honoring his royal father's dying wish to groom this son as the crown prince, Akeem and Semmi set off to America once again.
tagline: A sequel is in the heir.
title: Coming 2 America
plot:
Coming 2 America is a 2021 American comedy film directed by Craig Brewer and written by Kenya Barris, Kareem Brown, and Tracy Oliver. The movie serves as a sequel to the 1988 film Coming to America.

The story takes place five years after the events of the first film. Prince Akeem Joffer (Eddie Murphy) is now the King of Zamunda, married to Queen Lisa (Shari Headley), and they have a young son named Prince Jammy (Wesley Snipes). However, their happiness is short-lived as Prince Jammy's birth certificate reveals that he was born in Queens, New York, not in Zamunda.

The revelation sets off a chain of events as Akeem must navigate the complexities of being a king and a father while also dealing with the fact that his son may not be truly Zamundan. The situation becomes even more complicated when Prince Jammy begins to exhibit behaviors that are uncharacteristic of a Zamundan prince, leading Akeem to question whether he is indeed the biological son of King Jaffe Joffer (James Earl Jones).

As Akeem searches for answers about his son's true identity, he turns to his old friend Semmi (Arsenio Hall), who has been living in Queens with his wife. Together, they embark on a journey to New York City to uncover the truth about Prince Jammy's birth and his connection to Zamunda.

Along the way, Akeem also reconnects with his old flame, Lisa McDowell (Shari Headley), who is now a successful businesswoman in Queens. As they rekindle their romance, Akeem must confront his feelings for her while also dealing with the responsibilities of being a king.

The movie features a star-studded cast, including John Goodman as King Jaffe Joffer's advisor, Cleo McDowell (Nomzamo Mbatha) as Lisa's sister, and KiKi Layne as Queen Meeko (Akeem's mother). The film also includes cameos from several celebrities, including Tracy Morgan, Tichina Arnold, and Vanessa Williams.

Throughout the movie, Akeem faces various challenges as he navigates his role as a king and a father. He must balance his desire to protect his son with his duty to maintain peace and stability in Zamunda. Along the way, he also learns valuable lessons about love, family, and identity.

Ultimately, Coming 2 America is a heartwarming and hilarious film that explores themes of identity, community, and the complexities of royal life. With its talented cast, witty dialogue, and engaging storyline, it's no wonder why this movie has become a beloved sequel to the original classic.

overview: When shark conservationist Dr. Misty Calhoun is invited to consult on a top-secret project run by pharmaceutical billionaire Carl Durant, she is shocked to learn that the company is using unpredictable and highly aggressive bull sharks as its test subjects, which soon break loose and cause havoc.
tagline: Stronger. Wiser. Deadlier.
title: Deep Blue Sea 2
plot:
Deep Blue Sea 2 is a 2018 American science fiction horror film directed by David E. Miller. The movie serves as a sequel to the 1999 film Deep Blue Sea, which was also based on a novel of the same name.

The main themes of Deep Blue Sea 2 revolve around genetic engineering, marine biology, and the dangers of playing with nature. The story follows a team of scientists who are studying genetically enhanced mako sharks in an underwater research facility. However, things take a turn for the worse when the sharks begin to mutate and become aggressive towards humans.

Throughout the film, the main theme of genetic engineering is explored as the scientists realize that they have created a monster by tampering with the natural order of the ocean's ecosystem. The movie highlights the risks and consequences of manipulating nature through science, and how it can lead to catastrophic outcomes.

Another significant theme in Deep Blue Sea 2 is the importance of respecting and understanding the natural world. The film showcases the beauty and power of the ocean, but also emphasizes the dangers that lurk beneath its surface. The movie serves as a warning about the consequences of human actions on the environment and the need for caution when dealing with powerful forces like nature.

The ending of the film is particularly noteworthy, as it highlights the devastating consequences of playing with nature and the importance of accountability in scientific research. Overall, Deep Blue Sea 2 explores complex themes that are both thought-provoking and terrifying, making it a compelling watch for fans of science fiction and horror genres.

[No information on Warner Bros. Pictures is available]

original_title: Wake Up, Ron Burgundy: The Lost Movie
overview: While Ron Burgundy's rivalry with Veronica Corningstone escalates quickly, a group of unprofessional thieves better known as 'The Alarm Clock' try to make the truth known, whatever that may mean...
tagline: the Adventure Continues...
title: Wake Up, Ron Burgundy: The Lost Movie
plot:
Wake Up, Ron Burgundy: The Lost Movie is a comedy film that explores the theme of identity and self-discovery through the character of Ron Burgundy. The movie delves into Ron's struggles with aging and his desire to hold onto his youth and status as a news anchor.

The film also touches on the idea of nostalgia and the passing of time, as Ron tries to cling to his past glory days while navigating the changing media landscape. Additionally, the movie pokes fun at the superficiality of 1970s San Diego's news industry, highlighting the absurdities and excesses of the era.

Furthermore, Wake Up, Ron Burgundy: The Lost Movie features a strong ensemble cast, including Veronica Corningstone, Champ Kind, Brian Fantana, and Brick Tamland, each bringing their unique personalities to the story. Through their interactions with Ron, the film showcases the importance of friendship and camaraderie in helping individuals cope with life's challenges.

Overall, Wake Up, Ron Burgundy: The Lost Movie is a lighthearted, humorous exploration of themes that are both universally relatable and uniquely tied to the character of Ron Burgundy.

overview: A cold and mysterious new security guard for a Los Angeles cash truck company surprises his co-workers when he unleashes precision skills during a heist. The crew is left wondering who he is and where he came from. Soon, the marksman's ultimate motive becomes clear as he takes dramatic and irrevocable steps to settle a score.
tagline: A one man army.
title: Wrath of Man
plot:
Wrath of Man is an action thriller of 2021 directed by Guy Ritchie, who wrote it with Ivan Atkinson and Marn Davies, loosely based on the French film Cash Truck (2004). Reuniting Ritchie with Jason Statham for the first time since Revolver (2005), it stars Statham as a mysterious new armoured-truck guard in Los Angeles, with Holt McCallany as Bullet, Josh Hartnett as Boy Sweat Dave, Jeffrey Donovan as Jackson, Scott Eastwood as Jan, Eddie Marsan as Terry and Andy García in a small role as FBI Agent King.

The story opens with a robbery of a Fortico Security truck that leaves two guards and a bystander dead, and unfolds in four chapters. Five months later, Patrick Hill, known as H, joins Fortico after barely passing his firearms test. When robbers take Bullet hostage during a pickup, H kills them all with chilling precision. FBI agents who question him realise who he really is, but King tells them to leave him alone. Months later, another group of robbers flees the moment they see H, and his colleagues grow suspicious.

The second chapter rewinds to the day of the first robbery. H, a criminal himself, agrees to scout a truck's route with his son Dougie waiting in the car when a different gang hijacks the vehicle nearby; Dougie is shot dead and H is wounded but sees the killer's face. He is in fact Mason Hargreaves, a notorious crime boss, and King gives him a list of suspects, turning a blind eye while H's men work through them. When the hunt fails, his lieutenant Mike guesses that the robbery was an inside job, so H takes a job at Fortico to find the informant; the gang who fled was his own crew, who recognised him. The third chapter reveals the robbers as disgruntled Afghanistan veterans led by their former sergeant Jackson, aided by an inside man who once served under him, with the volatile Jan as the man who shot Dougie. In the last chapter they return on Black Friday weekend to steal close to $180 million from the Fortico depot. Bullet reveals himself as the informant, and the guards are massacred. H kills most of the gang before Bullet shoots him, and Jan then murders Jackson and Bullet and escapes with the money. A phone hidden among the cash leads H to Jan's home, where he shoots him in the same places Dougie was hit, then tells King it is done and walks away.

Delayed by the pandemic, the film opened internationally in April 2021 and grossed $104 million worldwide. Critics found it a fun, action-packed reunion, giving it 67% on Rotten Tomatoes.

overview: Painter Francisco Goya faces a scandal involving his muse, who is labeled a heretic by a monk.
title: Goya's Ghosts
plot:
Goya's Ghosts is a 2006 film that delves into the complexities of artistic expression, morality, and the human condition. The movie revolves around Francisco de Goya, a renowned Spanish artist, who finds himself transported to modern-day New York City. As he navigates this unfamiliar world, he encounters various characters, including his muse, Concepción, and a young woman named Nina.

The film explores themes of creativity, identity, and the struggle for artistic integrity. Goya's experiences in the modern world serve as a catalyst for him to re-examine his own work and the role it plays in society. Through his interactions with these characters, he grapples with the tension between his artistic vision and the commercial demands of his time.

One of the primary concerns of the film is the commodification of art, which Goya sees as a threat to its inherent value and meaning. He struggles to reconcile his desire for creative expression with the need to make a living from his work. This internal conflict serves as a metaphor for the artist's eternal dilemma: how to balance artistic integrity with commercial success.

The movie also touches on the theme of isolation and loneliness, which is reflected in Goya's experiences as an outsider in modern society. Despite being surrounded by people, he feels disconnected and alone, highlighting the tension between his desire for human connection and his need for solitude.

Furthermore, the film explores the idea of artistic legacy and the responsibility that comes with it. As Goya navigates the modern world, he is forced to confront the ways in which his work has been interpreted and reinterpreted over time. This serves as a reminder that art is not static, but rather a dynamic and evolving entity that reflects the changing values and perspectives of society.

Overall, Goya's Ghosts is a thought-provoking film that invites viewers to reflect on the complexities of artistic expression, morality, and the human condition.

overview: Four fighters from different backgrounds come together to train under an ex MMA rising star and then ultimately have to fight each other and the traitor in their midst.
title: Never Back Down 2: The Beatdown
plot:
Never Back Down 2: The Beatdown, also released as The Fighters 2: The Beatdown in some markets, is a 2011 American martial arts film directed by Michael Jai White from a script by Chris Hauty. A sequel to Never Back Down (2008) and the second film in the series, it marked White's directorial debut. Michael Jai White stars as the mixed martial arts trainer Casey "Case" Walker Jr., alongside Dean Geyer as Mike Stokes, Alex Meraz as Zack Gomes, Todd Duffee as Tim Newhouse, Scott Epstein as Justin Epstein, Evan Peters as the promoter Max Cooperman and Jillian Murray as Eve, with Lyoto Machida and "Big" John McCarthy appearing as themselves.

Max is organizing another round of "The Beatdown", an underground fighting event, and four fighters are training in a vacant lot under the veteran martial artist Case. Zack has recently quit boxing after suffering a partially detached retina; Tim, a skilled MMA fighter, has a family sunk in debt since his father's death; Mike, a champion college wrestler, is struggling with his father having left his mother for another man; and Justin, a comic book store clerk, is a frequent target of bullies. A few weeks in, the trainees quarrel over who deserves to be there most, with Justin and Zack hurting each other. When police officers harass Case and threaten him with a probation violation, the team builds a new gym in which to train and hold the Beatdown. Snapping under constant bullying, Justin turns on his tormentors and then on the group itself, framing his mentor in an effort to send him to jail. The others unite to confront him in the tournament. Mike defeats Zack, while Justin attacks Tim in the restroom and knocks him out of the competition. In a gruelling final, Mike beats Justin by breaking his right shoulder with an omoplata submission hold, and when Justin tries to jump him from behind, he responds with a superman punch. Celebrating his win, Mike finally calls his father and invites him to dinner because they have much to discuss, and Case receives a call from McCarthy confirming his return to MMA.

The film premiered at the ActionFest festival in Asheville, North Carolina, on April 8, 2011, and was released on DVD by Sony Pictures Home Entertainment on September 13. Reviews were mixed, with critics praising the fight scenes, especially White's, while finding the story formulaic.

original_title: Mamma Mia! Here We Go Again
overview: Five years after meeting her three fathers, Sophie Sheridan prepares to open her mother’s hotel. In 1979, young Donna Sheridan meets the men who each could be Sophie’s biological father.
tagline: Discover how it all began.
title: Mamma Mia! Here We Go Again
plot:
Mamma Mia! Here We Go Again is a musical romantic comedy film directed by Ol Parker, based on the songs of ABBA. The movie is a sequel to the 2008 film Mamma Mia!, and it features an all-star cast, including Lily James, Amanda Seyfried, Meryl Streep, Pierce Brosnan, Colin Firth, Stellan Skarsgård, Dominic Cooper, Cher, and Hugh Skinner.

The story begins with Sophie Sheridan (Amanda Seyfried), the daughter of Donna Sheridan (Meryl Streep), who is now a mother herself. The movie takes place on the same Greek island where the original film was set, and it follows Sophie's journey as she prepares to open her own hotel.

As Sophie is getting ready for her wedding, she discovers an old diary belonging to her mother, Donna, which reveals secrets about her past and the events that led up to the creation of ABBA. The story then flashes back to 20 years ago, when Sophie was a young girl living on the island with her mother.

The film features three main plotlines: Sophie's present-day journey as she prepares for her wedding, Donna's backstory as she navigates her relationships and career in the 1990s, and the origins of ABBA. The story is interwoven with flashbacks to Donna's time on the island, where she meets Sam Carmichael (Pierce Brosnan), Bill Anderson (Stellan Skarsgård), and Harry Bright (Colin Firth).

As Sophie delves deeper into her mother's past, she discovers that Donna had a complicated love life and was torn between three men: Sam, Bill, and Harry. The story takes the audience on a journey through time, exploring themes of love, heartbreak, and self-discovery.

Throughout the film, ABBA's iconic songs are featured prominently, with many of them being performed by the cast in elaborate musical numbers. The movie also features cameos from Cher, who plays Ruby Sheridan, Sophie's grandmother, and Hugh Skinner, who plays Young Sam.

The ending of the film is a heartwarming tribute to Donna's legacy and her impact on Sophie's life. As Sophie prepares to open her hotel, she reflects on the lessons she learned from her mother about love, forgiveness, and following one's dreams. The movie concludes with a grand musical number featuring the entire cast, celebrating the power of music and the enduring spirit of ABBA.

Overall, Mamma Mia! Here We Go Again is a delightful and entertaining film that celebrates the music of ABBA and the enduring legacy of its iconic songs. With its talented cast, stunning locations, and catchy musical numbers, it's a must-see for fans of musicals and romantic comedies alike.

original_title: 13 หมูป่า: เรื่องเล่าจากในถ้ำ
overview: In this compelling documentary, members of the Thai youth soccer team tell their stories of getting trapped in Tham Luang Cave in 2018 — and surviving.
title: The Trapped 13: How We Survived The Thai Cave
plot:
"Moonfall" is a 2022 science fiction disaster film directed by Roland Emmerich, produced by Centropolis Entertainment, and written by Drew Pearce.

The movie follows two main storylines that eventually intersect. The first storyline revolves around Sam Bell (played by Patrick Wilson), an astronaut who wakes up on the Moon with no memory of how he got there or what happened to his crew. As he tries to piece together his past, he discovers a mysterious message from an unknown sender that sets him on a mission to prevent a catastrophic event.

The second storyline takes place in 2055, where we meet J.T. O'Grady (played by Halle Berry), the daughter of Sam Bell, who is now a renowned astrophysicist. She's recruited by a team of scientists and engineers, including her colleague Brian Harper (played by John Bradley), to prevent a massive asteroid from colliding with Earth.

As the story unfolds, we learn that the asteroid is not just any ordinary rock - it's actually a piece of the Moon that has broken off due to an unknown cataclysmic event. The team discovers that the Moon was once part of a larger celestial body called Kaltain, which was destroyed in a catastrophic collision with Earth millions of years ago.

The movie takes a thrilling turn as Sam Bell and J.T. O'Grady embark on a perilous journey to prevent the asteroid from colliding with Earth. Along the way, they encounter numerous challenges, including treacherous terrain, malfunctioning equipment, and personal demons.

Throughout the film, Emmerich's signature style of explosive action sequences and heart-pumping suspense is on full display. The movie's climax features an intense showdown between Sam and J.T., as they work together to prevent the asteroid from destroying Earth.

While "Moonfall" received mixed reviews from critics, it has its fans who appreciate the film's over-the-top action sequences and thrilling plot twists. However, some viewers may find the pacing a bit uneven and the scientific explanations lacking in depth.

Overall, "Moonfall" is an entertaining sci-fi disaster film that will keep you on the edge of your seat. With its breakneck pace and mind-bending plot twists, it's sure to appeal to fans of Roland Emmerich's signature style.

overview: Working for the World Record Bureau, Leah Hoffman is forced to travel to a small town just before Christmas to investigate its plans to break multiple holiday world records. While there, she falls for the town’s doctor, Devan Bancroft.
title: Record Breaking Christmas
plot:
Record Breaking Christmas is a 2022 Canadian Christmas romantic comedy television film directed by Max McGuire from a screenplay by W. Stewart. Produced by Johnson Production Group, it stars Michelle Argyris and Andrew Bushell, with Danny Vo, Darlene Cooke, Tim Progosh, Pierre Simpson and Michael Gordin Shore in supporting roles. The film premiered on Lifetime in December 2022 and runs 85 minutes.

Leah Hoffman (Argyris) is an adjudicator for the World Records Bureau who every year has the honour of overseeing attempts to break Christmas-themed records, a job she does instead of properly celebrating the holiday. Just before Christmas she and her trainee Jin (Vo), an enthusiastic former engineer with a tendency to faint at the sight of beards or the sound of people singing in unison, are sent to the tiny town of St. Drexel, Illinois, which plans to attempt six world records. Having seen it all, Leah warns Jin not to get his hopes up, since most attempts fail. Spearheading the town's effort is its doctor, Devan Bancroft (Bushell). Thirty-five years earlier his mother helped St. Drexel set a record for the world's largest iced cookie, but the tourism it attracted has long since faded, and the businesses on Main Street now face closure unless the town can win new fame with feats such as the most hula hoop spins in one minute by people dressed as reindeer. While Devan is desperate for the town to succeed, Leah sticks rigidly to the rulebook, repeatedly checking how the bureau defines concepts such as vans, frogs or kissing, and delivers failed results with the gravity of a surgeon breaking bad news. As the townspeople gather to decorate their tree together on the eve of Christmas Eve, Devan's belief that sometimes one must give up an important job to live an important life challenges Leah's priorities, and she finds herself falling for him.

Critics found it slight but enjoyable. Decider compared it to a carton of eggnog, an acquired taste that goes down smoothly for those who like it, praising its original premise, its knowingly over-the-top treatment of Leah's devotion to the rules and Vo's committed supporting performance, while noting that it was less ambitious than other holiday romances that season. Cassandra Morgan recommended it as a cute film, praising Argyris as relatable and saying Bushell held his own as a leading man, though she wished it had shown more of the record attempts themselves.

overview: In 1950s New York, a department-store clerk who dreams of a better life falls for an older, married woman.
tagline: Some people change your life forever.
title: Carol
plot:
Carol is a 2015 American romantic drama film directed by Todd Haynes, based on Patricia Highsmith's semi-autobiographical novel The Price of Salt. The film stars Cate Blanchett as Carol Aird and Rooney Mara as Therese Belivet.

The story begins in New York City in the summer of 1952. We meet Carol Aird (Cate Blanchett), a wealthy socialite who has just arrived from Europe, where she was married to Harge Aird (Kyle Chandler). The marriage is loveless, and Carol is eager to escape her husband's suffocating grasp.

While exploring the city, Carol meets Therese Belivet (Rooney Mara), a young salesgirl at a department store. Their initial encounter is brief, but it sparks an undeniable connection between them. As they continue to cross paths, their conversations become more meaningful, and they begin to develop feelings for each other.

As the summer progresses, Carol and Therese's relationship deepens, despite the societal norms that prohibit same-sex relationships in 1950s America. They share stolen moments together, exchanging letters and gifts, and exploring the city's hidden corners.

However, their love is threatened by the constraints of Carol's marriage and the expectations of her family and friends. Harge Aird returns from Europe, unaware of Carol's growing feelings for Therese, and demands that she return to their home in the Hamptons.

Carol is torn between her duty to her husband and her desire for freedom and love with Therese. As the summer draws to a close, Carol must make a choice between conforming to societal norms or risking everything to be with the woman she loves.

The film's climax features a poignant and heart-wrenching confrontation between Carol and Harge Aird, which ultimately leads to Carol's decision to leave her husband and start a new life with Therese. The ending is bittersweet, as Carol must navigate the challenges of being an openly gay woman in a society that rejects her.

Throughout the film, Haynes masterfully captures the atmosphere of 1950s America, with its strict social norms and repressive attitudes towards same-sex relationships. The cinematography is stunning, with a muted color palette that evokes the melancholy and longing of Carol's story.

Cate Blanchett delivers a tour-de-force performance as Carol Aird, bringing depth and nuance to a character who is both strong-willed and vulnerable. Rooney Mara shines as Therese Belivet, capturing the innocence and passion of a young woman falling in love for the first time.

Overall, Carol is a beautifully crafted film that explores themes of love, identity, and freedom in a society that seeks to constrain them. With its stunning performances, poignant script, and masterful direction, it is a must-see for anyone who loves great storytelling and powerful performances.

overview: In a world with no guns, a mysterious drifter, a bartender and a young samurai plot revenge against a ruthless leader and his army of thugs, headed by nine diverse and deadly assassins.
tagline: A civilized weapon for uncivilized times
title: Bunraku
plot:
Bunraku is a 2010 martial arts action film written and directed by Guy Moshe from a story by Boaz Davidson. It stars Josh Hartnett, Demi Moore, Woody Harrelson, Ron Perlman, Kevin McKidd and Gackt, and follows a young drifter on a quest for revenge. Named after the 400-year-old form of Japanese puppet theatre, it reimagines a classic tale in a world mixing skewed reality with shadow-play fantasy, drawing on samurai films and Westerns.

In the aftermath of a devastating global war, guns have been outlawed, yet people continue to fight and kill with blades and bare fists. The most powerful man east of the Atlantic is Nicola the Woodcutter, a shadowy crime boss who rules his territory through nine elite assassins known as the Killers. His right-hand man is Killer No. 2, a smooth-talking murderer in a red hat who carries a cane-sword, and he keeps an unwilling lover, Alexandra, a woman with a secret past. One night a mysterious drifter walks into the Horseless Horseman Saloon and asks the bartender for a shot of whisky and a game of cards, only to learn that the one place offering both, the Russian Roulette, is controlled by Nicola and open only to the rich. Soon after, another stranger arrives: Yoshi, a lone samurai who has travelled far to fulfil his father's dying wish by recovering a medallion stolen from his village. Guided by the bartender, the two men join forces against Nicola. After a series of clashes in which they injure police officers and many of Nicola's thugs, Killer No. 2 murders Yoshi's uncle and abducts his cousin Momoko to work in Nicola's brothel. With the bartender and an army of freedom fighters, the pair storm Nicola's palace. The bartender rescues Momoko and is briefly reunited with Alexandra, his long-lost love, before she is lost in the burning brothel. Yoshi kills Killer No. 2, while the drifter, wounded by an axe thrown by Nicola, slashes the crime boss's throat with an arrowhead taken from Yoshi and reveals that he came to avenge his father, whom Nicola killed. With the Woodcutter's reign ended and the medallion recovered, the heroes part ways hoping to meet again.

Bunraku premiered in the Midnight Madness section of the 2010 Toronto International Film Festival, with a limited theatrical release in 2011. Critics praised its visual style and ideas but faulted the screenplay and characters, and it holds an 18% Rotten Tomatoes rating.

overview: The story of Florence Foster Jenkins, a New York heiress, who dreamed of becoming an opera singer, despite having a terrible singing voice.
tagline: People may say I couldn't sing, but no one can say I didn't sing
title: Florence Foster Jenkins
plot:
Florence Foster Jenkins is a 2016 biographical comedy-drama directed by Stephen Frears and written by Nicholas Martin and Julia Kogan. Meryl Streep stars as the title character, a New York heiress remembered for her generosity and her famously bad singing, and Hugh Grant plays her manager and long-time companion, St. Clair Bayfield. Filming began in May 2015, and the film opened in the United Kingdom on 6 May 2016 and, through Paramount Pictures, in the United States that August.

In 1944, Florence is a wealthy New York socialite who founded the Verdi Club out of her love of music. Bayfield, a British Shakespearean actor, devotes himself to her career while living separately with his mistress, Kathleen, and Florence has long suffered from the syphilis she contracted from her first husband. Inspired by a Lily Pons concert, she resumes singing lessons and hires the pianist Cosmé McMoon, who is appalled by her voice while Bayfield and her vocal coach pretend she is wonderful. Bayfield arranges a small recital for hand-picked guests, and Florence records a disc for the club's members as a Christmas present. McMoon learns that she had once been a gifted pianist, and the two grow close as they write and perform songs together. When one recording reaches the radio, many listeners find it hilarious.

Florence then books Carnegie Hall and gives away a thousand tickets to soldiers. Bayfield cannot talk her out of it, gets into a fight with men mocking her in a bar and loses Kathleen, and persuades the reluctant McMoon to stand by her even at the risk of his career. Before a packed house that includes Cole Porter and Tallulah Bankhead, the soldiers jeer at first, but her friends shout them down and she finishes the concert. Bayfield and McMoon buy up local copies of the New York Post to hide Earl Wilson's scathing review, but Florence finds one in a trash can and collapses. On her deathbed she imagines herself singing beautifully, and tells Bayfield that people may say she could not sing, but no one can say she did not sing.

Simon Helberg plays McMoon, with Rebecca Ferguson and Nina Arianda, who plays the showgirl Agnes Stark. Critics were enthusiastic, giving it 87% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and praising Streep in particular, and it grossed about $56 million worldwide. Streep received her 20th Academy Award nomination, for Best Actress, and the film was also nominated for Best Costume Design and four Golden Globes.

original_title: Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire
overview: When Harry Potter's name emerges from the Goblet of Fire, he becomes a competitor in a grueling battle for glory among three wizarding schools—the Triwizard Tournament. But since Harry never submitted his name for the Tournament, who did? Now Harry must confront a deadly dragon, fierce water demons and an enchanted maze only to find himself in the cruel grasp of He Who Must Not Be Named.
tagline: Dark And Difficult Times Lie Ahead.
title: Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire
plot:
Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire is a fantasy film directed by Mike Newell, produced by Warner Bros. Pictures, and based on the novel of the same name by J.K. Rowling.

The story begins with Harry Potter (Daniel Radcliffe) attending the Quidditch World Cup with his friends Ron Weasley (Rupert Grint) and Hermione Granger (Emma Watson). However, the event is marred by a terrorist attack that kills several people, including Barty Crouch Jr. (David Tennant), who is revealed to be the son of a Ministry of Magic employee.

Upon returning to Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry, Harry is unexpectedly selected as one of the four champions to compete in the Triwizard Tournament, a magical competition between three schools: Hogwarts, Durmstrang Institute, and Beauxbatons Academy. The tournament requires each champion to complete three tasks, which are designed to test their courage, wisdom, and magical abilities.

As the tournament progresses, Harry faces numerous challenges, including a dragon, a mermaid-like creature, and a treacherous maze. Meanwhile, Lord Voldemort (Ralph Fiennes) returns to power and begins to gather his followers, known as Death Eaters.

Throughout the film, Harry's friends are concerned about his safety, particularly after Barty Crouch Jr. is revealed to be impersonating Mad-Eye Moody (Brendan Gleeson), a Hogwarts teacher. The story takes a dark turn when it is discovered that Voldemort has returned and is attempting to return to power.

The film culminates in the final task of the tournament, which requires each champion to face their own personal fears and weaknesses. Harry ultimately emerges victorious but not without scars, both physical and emotional. The film ends with a sense of foreboding, as Harry's friends realize that Voldemort is back and more powerful than ever.

Overall, Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire is a thrilling and emotionally charged installment in the beloved franchise, exploring themes of friendship, courage, and the complexities of adolescence.

original_title: 犬夜叉 時代を越える想い
overview: InuYasha is a half-demon who was trapped in the Legendary Tree and was set free by Kagome, a girl who traveled 500 years through time. This time, both of them will have to face Menomaru, a Chinese demon whose father, known as Hyoga, came 300 years ago to invade Japan, but was stopped by InuYasha's Father. InuYasha and Kagome, along with Sango, Miroku, Shippou, Kaede and Myoga, will try to stop Menomaru in his becoming the most powerful demon ever.
title: Inuyasha the Movie: Affections Touching Across Time
plot:
Inuyasha the Movie: Affections Touching Across Time is a 2001 Japanese animated film directed by Norihiro Takemoto and produced by Sunrise. The movie takes place after the events of the first season of the Inuyasha anime series.

The story begins with Inuyasha, Kagome, Miroku, Sango, and Shippo on a journey to find the Sacred Waterfall, which is said to have healing properties that can cure any wound. However, they are not the only ones searching for it, as Naraku, the main antagonist of the series, also seeks to obtain its power.

As they near the waterfall, they encounter a young girl named Kikyo, who is revealed to be Inuyasha's half-sister and the reincarnation of the demon princess. Kikyo has been cursed by Naraku, causing her to lose her memories and become trapped in a time loop, reliving the same day over and over.

Inuyasha and his friends soon discover that Kikyo is stuck in this time loop because she is unable to move on from her past life due to her feelings for Inuyasha. The group decides to help Kikyo break free from the curse by finding a way to make her remember her true identity and love for Inuyasha.

Throughout their journey, the group faces various challenges and obstacles as they try to reach the Sacred Waterfall before Naraku does. Along the way, they also encounter other characters who aid or hinder their progress.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Kikyo's memories are tied to her feelings for Inuyasha, and that she is unable to let go of him even in death. The group must find a way to help Kikyo overcome her emotions and move on from her past life.

In the end, Inuyasha and his friends successfully break the curse, allowing Kikyo to remember her true identity and love for Inuyasha. However, this comes at a great cost, as Kikyo is forced to leave the world of the living behind and return to the afterlife.

The movie ends with Inuyasha reflecting on the events that transpired, realizing that his feelings for Kikyo were genuine but also acknowledging that he must move forward with his life. The film concludes with a sense of closure and new beginnings for the characters, as they look towards their future adventures together.

Overall, Inuyasha the Movie: Affections Touching Across Time is a heartwarming and emotional tale that explores themes of love, loss, and redemption. The movie's focus on character development and relationships adds depth to the story, making it a standout entry in the Inuyasha franchise.

overview: Drew Baylor is fired after causing his shoe company to lose hundreds of millions of dollars. To make matters worse, he's also dumped by his girlfriend. On the verge of ending it all, Drew gets a new lease on life when he returns to his family's small Kentucky hometown after his father dies. Along the way, he meets a flight attendant with whom he falls in love.
tagline: It's a heck of a place to find yourself
title: Elizabethtown
plot:
Elizabethtown is a 2005 American romantic comedy-drama film directed by Marc Forster. The story revolves around Drew Baylor, a young man who embarks on a journey to find meaning and purpose in his life after the sudden death of his father.

At its core, Elizabethtown explores themes of grief, loss, and self-discovery. Drew's emotional journey is marked by a deep sense of longing and disconnection, as he struggles to come to terms with the void left by his father's passing. As he navigates this complex emotional landscape, he begins to question the choices he has made in life and the relationships that have shaped him.

The film also delves into the complexities of love and relationships, particularly Drew's complicated bond with his sister Elizabeth (played by Kirsten Dunst). Their relationship is fraught with tension and unrequited feelings, serving as a poignant reminder of the fragility and beauty of human connections.

Furthermore, Elizabethtown touches on the idea of identity and how it is shaped by our experiences, relationships, and personal losses. Drew's journey is a metaphor for the search for one's true self, as he grapples with the notion that his life has been defined by external expectations rather than internal desires.

Ultimately, the film presents a nuanced exploration of the human condition, one that acknowledges the messy complexity of emotions and relationships while offering a message of hope and resilience in the face of adversity.

overview: Rosario Tijeras has been abused by men all her life, initially by her stepfather. Years later, she works as a paid assassin, seducing men and killing them when they least expect it. She meets Emilio, a wealthy womanizer, and his best friend, Antonio, at a nightclub, and starts an affair with Emilio despite Antonio's growing feelings for her. But circumstances bring her closer to Antonio, until her past catches up with her in a devastating way.
production_companies: Fondo de Inversión y Estímulos al Cine (FIDECINE)
title: Rosario Tijeras
plot:
Rosario Tijeras is a 2005 Mexican drama film directed by Matías Piñeiro. The movie revolves around the life of Rosario, a young woman who returns to her hometown in Argentina after being away for many years.

The main themes of Rosario Tijeras include:

1. Identity: The film explores Rosario's struggle to find her place in the world and define herself as an individual. She is torn between her desire to reconnect with her past and her need to forge a new identity.
2. Family dynamics: The movie delves into the complex relationships within Rosario's family, particularly her relationship with her mother, who is struggling to cope with the loss of her husband. This theme highlights the ways in which family ties can both support and suffocate individuals.
3. Trauma and memory: Rosario Tijeras touches on the idea that memories can be both a source of comfort and a burden. The film suggests that unresolved trauma can have a lasting impact on one's life, and that confronting the past is essential for healing and moving forward.
4. Female empowerment: Through Rosario's journey, the movie promotes female empowerment and independence. As she navigates her relationships and confronts her challenges, Rosario begins to assert herself and take control of her life.

The film features a strong performance from Valeria Luiselli, who brings depth and nuance to the title character. The cinematography is also noteworthy, capturing the beauty and desolation of Argentina's Patagonia region.

Overall, Rosario Tijeras is a poignant and thought-provoking drama that explores themes of identity, family, trauma, and female empowerment.

overview: After her brother goes missing, a young psychologist visits an infamous haunted and cursed location known as ‘Howling Village’ to investigate his disappearance and uncover her family’s dark history.
tagline: Horror comes home.
title: Howling Village
plot:
Howling Village (Japanese: 犬鳴村, Inunaki Mura) is a 2020 Japanese supernatural horror film directed by Takashi Shimizu, the creator of Ju-On, who wrote the screenplay with his long-time collaborator Daisuke Hosaka. It combines the old Inunaki Tunnel in Fukuoka Prefecture, often called Japan's most terrifying haunted spot, with the urban legend of the hidden Inunaki Village, recasting the legend's tale of a cult of madmen in the mountains as a story of ghosts and vengeful spirits. Ayaka Miyoshi stars, alongside Ryota Bando, Tsuyoshi Furukawa, Rinka Otani, Hina Miyano, Megumi Okina, Renji Ishibashi, Reiko Takashima and Masanobu Takashima. Distributed by Toei, it opened in Japan on 7 February 2020 and became the first instalment of Shimizu's "Village" trilogy, followed by Suicide Forest Village and Ox-Head Village.

Kanata Morita (Miyoshi) is a young psychologist who is able to perceive the dead. Her brother Yuma (Bando) and his girlfriend Akina (Otani) go looking for the legendary village, said to lie beyond an abandoned tunnel and to be reachable only after answering a phone that rings at 2 a.m. in a lonely booth by a bridge. Their visit is cut short by shadowy figures. Back home Akina behaves strangely and falls to her death from a tower, yet her autopsy shows that she drowned. When Yuma and their younger brother Kota then disappear while searching for answers, and people around the family begin dying in bizarre circumstances, Kanata travels to the sealed tunnel herself. Her investigation leads her into the village's buried past, including its flooding for a dam, and reveals that her own family and bloodline are bound up with its curse and its former residents, forcing her to confront the truth about her ancestors and herself.

The children's song "Futashicharo" heard in the film was written by Shimizu rather than drawn from the legend. A preview screening was held in Miyawaka, the Fukuoka city where the tunnel lies, and a version that softened the scares with cute dog animation and comic sound effects was later released for viewers averse to horror. The film won the jury prize at the 2020 Gérardmer Fantastic Film Festival. Critics found it atmospheric but overstuffed: Horror News Net praised its mix of folklore and urban legend, while Heaven of Horror gave it three out of five, citing confusing, unresolved plot threads but a strong performance by Miyoshi.

original_title: 13 Hours: The Secret Soldiers of Benghazi
overview: An American Ambassador is killed during an attack at a U.S. compound in Libya as a security team struggles to make sense out of the chaos.
tagline: When everything went wrong, six men had the courage to do what was right.
title: 13 Hours: The Secret Soldiers of Benghazi
plot: [No information found]

overview: A group of humans arrive on Sirius 6-B to investigate an SOS signal sent out from the planet, which has been supposedly deserted since the destruction of the man-made weapons known as "screamers." Once the squad arrives, they find a group of human survivors eking out an existence in an old military outpost.
tagline: The Perfect Weapon Is Now The Ultimate Killing Machine
title: Screamers: The Hunting
plot:
Screamers: The Hunting is an American science fiction horror film of 2009 directed by Sheldon Wilson, a sequel to Screamers (1995) released directly on DVD. Gina Holden stars as Lieutenant Victoria Bronte, with Greg Bryk as Commander Andy Sexton, Stephen Amell as Guy, Jana Pallaske as the medic Schwartz, Christopher Redman as Rafe Danielli and Lance Henriksen as the reclusive scientist Orsow.

On the planet Sirius 6B, three people struggle to reactivate a distress beacon in an abandoned communications bunker; only one survives the Screamers long enough to switch it on. Two months later the spacecraft Medusa arrives with a rescue team. Nothing has been heard from the planet since the death of Joseph Hendrickson, and the Screamers are assumed to have run out of power. An approaching meteor storm gives the team just six days. Leaving the pilot Soderquist aboard, they find a dormant Screamer factory in a hillside bunker, and Sexton, downloading its schematics, unwittingly brings it back to life. A Screamer slips aboard Medusa and kills Soderquist, the team is ambushed on the way to an old mine, and Sergeant Romulo sacrifices himself with a grenade. Back at the ship they find that its fuel cells have been drained, stranding them.

Bronte, Hendrickson's daughter, rescues a local woman, Hannah, who leads them to a dwindling colony of human survivors in the mine. The newest Screamers can pass for human: three teenagers freed from metal racks turn out to be cyborgs, Danielli is apparently killed, and the survivors blow up the mine as they flee. At a power station, Hannah threatens Guy, believing him a machine, and Sexton kills her before a Screamer kills Schwartz. A masked stranger, Orsow, saves them with an electromagnetic weapon, but he secretly hoards the fuel cells, determined that Screamer technology must never reach Earth. Sexton takes the cells and kills Orsow when he attacks. Danielli then returns as a human-Screamer hybrid, killing Madden and fatally wounding Sexton before Bronte destroys him, and she and Guy escape as the base self-destructs. Guy destroys the transformed Madden aboard Medusa, and the pair enter cryogenic sleep as they lift off ahead of the meteor storm. Reaching Earth orbit, Bronte finds herself pregnant far beyond the time that has passed, realises too late that Guy is a hybrid, and her unborn child flexes a clawed hand.

The film was released on DVD in February 2009. Bulletproof Action found enough good in it to outweigh the bad.

overview: The toys throw Ken and Barbie a Hawaiian vacation in Bonnie's room.
title: Hawaiian Vacation
plot:
Hawaiian Vacation is a heartwarming and hilarious animated film that explores the complexities of family relationships and the importance of embracing change. The movie follows the lovable but slightly dysfunctional Dug family as they embark on a disastrous vacation to Hawaii.

At its core, Hawaiian Vacation is a story about the challenges of modern family life. The film expertly captures the nuances of sibling rivalry, parental anxiety, and the struggles of growing up. Through the characters' interactions and misadventures, Pixar sheds light on the universal themes of identity, belonging, and the quest for connection.

One of the main themes of Hawaiian Vacation is the power of family bonds to overcome even the most trying circumstances. Despite their differences and disagreements, the Dug family members ultimately come together to support each other and find common ground. This theme is beautifully illustrated through the character of Dug himself, who, despite his eccentricities, proves to be a loving and loyal companion to his family.

The film also explores the idea of embracing change and finding joy in the unexpected. The Dugs' vacation to Hawaii is initially met with resistance and skepticism, but as they navigate their way through the island's unique culture and landscapes, they begin to let go of their preconceptions and find new experiences to cherish. This theme is reflected in the character of Carl Fredricksen Jr., who learns to appreciate the beauty of his family's imperfections and finds a sense of belonging among them.

Overall, Hawaiian Vacation is a delightful and entertaining film that celebrates the complexities and joys of modern family life. With its lovable characters, witty humor, and heartwarming storylines, it's a movie that will leave audiences smiling and feeling uplifted.

overview: A look at the mysterious relationship between Victorian art critic John Ruskin and his teenage bride Effie Gray.
tagline: The Celebrity Scandal of the Victorian era.
title: Effie Gray
plot:
Effie Gray is a 2014 period drama film that explores the complexities of love, art, and identity through the story of Effie Gray, the wife of artist John Everett Millais. The movie delves into the societal pressures and expectations placed on women during the Victorian era, particularly in regards to marriage and domesticity.

At its core, Effie Gray is a film about the struggle for independence and self-discovery, as Effie navigates her arranged marriage to Millais while pursuing her own artistic passions. The movie highlights the tension between Effie's desire for autonomy and her societal obligations, which ultimately lead to a crisis of identity.

The film also touches on the theme of art as a means of expression and empowerment, as Effie becomes increasingly involved in Millais' work and finds solace in his creative process. Through Effie's character, the movie showcases the ways in which art can be both a source of comfort and a means of rebellion against societal norms.

Furthermore, the film explores the complexities of relationships and the blurred lines between love, friendship, and mentorship. The bond between Effie and Millais is multifaceted, oscillating between romantic tension and platonic affection, leaving the audience to ponder the nature of their connection.

Ultimately, Effie Gray is a poignant portrayal of a woman's journey towards self-discovery and artistic expression, set against the backdrop of a bygone era. The movie offers a nuanced exploration of the human experience, inviting viewers to reflect on the enduring power of art and the complexities of love, identity, and societal expectations.

overview: A US soldier suffers a traumatic brain injury while fighting in Afghanistan and struggles to adjust to life back home in New Orleans. When she meets local mechanic James, the pair begin to forge an unexpected bond.
tagline: Begin again.
title: Causeway
plot:
Causeway is a 2022 American drama film directed by Mark Duplass and written by Duplass and Tom McGowan. The movie stars Benedict Cumberbatch, Carey Mulligan, and Ann Dowd.

The story revolves around Thomas Merritt (Benedict Cumberbatch), an Iraq War veteran who suffers from what he believes is a traumatic brain injury. He lives in Memphis, Tennessee, with his wife, Susan (Carey Mulligan), a nurse at the local hospital where he works. The couple's relationship has become strained due to Thomas's increasing irritability and lack of motivation.

Thomas's life takes an unexpected turn when he meets Lynsey (Ann Dowd), a 75-year-old widow who is also a patient in his physical therapy sessions. Lynsey, who lost her husband in the war, becomes a source of inspiration for Thomas, and their conversations lead to a deeper exploration of his feelings about the war and its impact on him.

As Thomas's relationship with Lynsey deepens, he begins to confront the emotional scars of his past. He starts to question his marriage and his own identity, leading to a crisis that forces him to reevaluate his life choices. Through his interactions with Lynsey, Thomas gains a new perspective on his experiences in Iraq and the toll it has taken on his mental health.

Meanwhile, Susan is struggling to cope with her husband's increasing detachment from reality. She feels abandoned and unsure of how to support Thomas as he navigates his emotional turmoil. The couple's relationship reaches a breaking point, and they are forced to confront the harsh realities of their marriage.

Throughout the film, Duplass masterfully weaves together themes of trauma, identity, and relationships. The cinematography is stunning, capturing the beauty and grittiness of Memphis and its people. The performances from Cumberbatch, Mulligan, and Dowd are outstanding, bringing depth and nuance to their characters.

The title "Causeway" refers to a bridge that spans the Mississippi River in Memphis. It serves as a metaphor for Thomas's journey, connecting him to his past while also allowing him to move forward. The film's ending is both poignant and hopeful, suggesting that Thomas has finally found a way to heal and rebuild his life.

Overall, Causeway is a powerful and moving drama that explores the complexities of trauma, relationships, and identity. With its outstanding performances, stunning cinematography, and thoughtful direction, it is a must-see for fans of character-driven dramas.

overview: Zain, a 12-year-old boy scrambling to survive on the streets of Beirut, sues his parents for having brought him into such an unjust world, where being a refugee with no documents means that your rights can easily be denied.
tagline: It takes courage to hope.
title: Capernaum
plot:
Capernaum is a 2018 Lebanese drama film directed by Nadine Labaki, produced by Open City Films, among others.

The main themes of Capernaum revolve around the struggles of childhood, poverty, and the complexities of human relationships. The story follows Zain, a 12-year-old boy who sues God for giving him life with all its hardships.

At its core, Capernaum explores the theme of childhood innocence and the harsh realities of growing up in a world that often seems cruel and unforgiving. Zain's journey is marked by his experiences as an orphan living on the streets, struggling to survive, and facing numerous challenges, including poverty, abuse, and neglect.

The film also delves into the theme of family and belonging, highlighting the difficulties of finding one's place in a world that often seems hostile towards those who are marginalized or vulnerable. Zain's relationships with his caregivers, particularly the woman who takes care of him, serve as a source of comfort and support, but also underscore the complexities of human connection.

Furthermore, Capernaum critiques the notion of divine responsibility and the idea that individuals can be held accountable for their circumstances. The film raises questions about the nature of God and whether He is truly responsible for the suffering of His children.

Throughout the narrative, Labaki employs a non-linear storytelling approach, jumping back and forth in time to reveal Zain's backstory and his experiences as an adult. This structure adds to the sense of disorientation and confusion that pervades the film, mirroring Zain's own struggles to make sense of his life.

Ultimately, Capernaum is a powerful exploration of the human condition, one that challenges viewers to confront the complexities of existence and the difficulties of growing up in a world that often seems cruel and unforgiving.

overview: Every parent's worst nightmare is just the beginning for Rachel's ordeal as in the aftermath of a tragic accident, she and her husband Anthony decide to move to the other side of the world to focus on their surviving twin son Elliot.  What begins as a time of healing and isolation in the Finnish countryside turns into a desperate battle for the very soul of their son as an entity claiming to be his dead twin brother takes over Elliot — setting Rachel on a diabolical journey to unravel the horrible truth about her twin son.
tagline: Evil only a mother could love.
title: The Twin
plot:
The Twin is a 2022 psychological horror film directed by Taneli Mustonen, who wrote the original screenplay with producer Aleksi Hyvärinen. The film follows a mother who must face an unbearable truth about her surviving twin son. Teresa Palmer stars as Rachel, with Steven Cree as her husband Anthony, Barbara Marten as Helen, Tristan Ruggeri as the twins Elliot and Nathan, and Andres Dvinjaninov as the town doctor.

Grieving the death of their son Nathan in a car accident, Rachel and Anthony move from New York to Finland with his twin brother Elliot. On an outing, Elliot finds a wall said to grant wishes and makes a secret wish, and soon afterwards he begins talking to someone invisible. At a welcome party thrown by the townspeople, Rachel meets the local doctor and Helen, who makes a cryptic remark about Elliot's wish. Elliot's behaviour grows disturbing, and he claims to be Nathan. When Rachel asks the doctor for help, he insists that she is the one who is ill and needs therapy. Desperate, she turns to Helen, who tells her that the town belongs to a satanic cult and that her late husband was possessed by an evil entity that appeared in photographs. Rachel photographs Elliot, but a séance she holds with him is interrupted by the townspeople and Anthony, who say they want to use the boy in a ritual. When the prints come back, Elliot appears in none of them; Helen calls this the demon taunting her and asks to see him, but on meeting the boy she too tells Rachel that she is sick. Surrounded by the townspeople, Rachel is sedated, made to take part in a satanic ritual and locked in her room. Hearing Elliot call for help, she escapes into the forest, where Anthony reveals the truth: Elliot does not exist. Rachel had been leaving Anthony with Nathan when the crash happened, and in her grief and anger she invented a second son. Rather than see her committed, Anthony went along with the delusion. When "Elliot" runs off claiming that Anthony wants to kill him, Rachel follows to a grain silo, where Anthony tries to break the delusion by burying the imaginary boy in grain, and Rachel accidentally kills him while trying to stop him. Digging in the grain, she finds nothing. Back in New York, she visits the graves of Nathan and Anthony yet still believes that they and Elliot are alive.

The Twin premiered at the Night Visions festival on March 24, 2022, and streamed on Shudder in the United States. Reviews were mixed, with a 41% Rotten Tomatoes rating.

overview: After being committed for 17 years, Michael Myers, now a grown man and still very dangerous, escapes from the mental institution (where he was committed as a 10 year old) and he immediately returns to Haddonfield, where he wants to find his baby sister, Laurie. Anyone who crosses his path is in mortal danger.
tagline: Evil has a destiny.
title: Halloween
plot:
Halloween is a 2007 American slasher film written, produced and directed by Rob Zombie. A remake of John Carpenter's 1978 film and the ninth installment in the Halloween franchise, it was conceived as both a remake and an origin story for Michael Myers. Malcolm McDowell plays Dr. Samuel Loomis, Daeg Faerch the ten-year-old Michael and Tyler Mane the adult Michael, with Scout Taylor-Compton, Sheri Moon Zombie, Brad Dourif, Danielle Harris and William Forsythe also in the cast.

On Halloween 1990 in Haddonfield, Illinois, ten-year-old Michael, who has already shown psychopathic tendencies, murders a school bully, his abusive stepfather Ronnie, his older sister Judith and her boyfriend, sparing only his baby sister, whom he calls "Boo". He is committed to Smith's Grove Sanitarium under the care of the child psychologist Loomis. Michael gradually withdraws into making papier-mâché masks, even from his devoted mother Deborah. When he kills a nurse at the end of one of her visits, Deborah cannot cope and takes her own life. Fifteen years later, after Loomis has closed his case, Michael escapes, killing guards and staff, returns to Haddonfield and retrieves the kitchen knife and mask he hid beneath the floorboards of his abandoned childhood home. Teenager Laurie Strode notices him watching her during the day. That night he kills her friend Lynda and Lynda's boyfriend Bob at his old house, then murders Laurie's parents while she is babysitting Tommy Doyle. Arriving in town with a handgun, Loomis warns Sheriff Leigh Brackett, who reveals that Laurie is in fact Michael's baby sister, adopted by the Strodes after their mother's suicide. Michael kills Paul, boyfriend of Laurie's friend Annie Brackett, and leaves Annie badly injured, then pursues Laurie and carries her to the old Myers house, where he shows her a photograph of the two of them. Not understanding, she stabs him and flees. Loomis shoots Michael, but Michael recovers, recaptures Laurie and crushes the doctor's skull. Laurie hides inside the walls until Michael corners her and both fall from a balcony; she wakes over his body and, as he grabs her wrist, fires the gun and screams as sirens approach.

Released in the United States by Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer on August 31, 2007, Halloween set a Labor Day weekend record and grossed $80 million worldwide on a $15 million budget despite generally negative reviews, including a 28% Rotten Tomatoes rating. A sequel, Halloween II, followed in 2009.

overview: Tom the cat and Jerry the mouse get kicked out of their home and relocate to a fancy New York hotel, where a scrappy employee named Kayla will lose her job if she can’t evict Jerry before a high-class wedding at the hotel. Her solution? Hiring Tom to get rid of the pesky mouse.
tagline: Best of enemies. Worst of friends.
title: Tom & Jerry
plot:
Tom and Jerry, released in some territories as Tom & Jerry: The Movie, is a 2021 American live-action/animated comedy film based on William Hanna and Joseph Barbera's cartoon cat and mouse. Directed by Tim Story, written by Kevin Costello and produced by Warner Animation Group, it is the second theatrical film featuring the pair, after Tom and Jerry: The Movie (1992). Chloë Grace Moretz stars as Kayla Forester, with Michael Peña as Terence Mendoza, Colin Jost, Pallavi Sharda, Rob Delaney and Ken Jeong.

Tom, a cat who dreams of being a jazz pianist, busks in Central Park until Jerry, a mouse looking for a new home, exposes him as a fraud. Chasing Jerry, Tom knocks down Kayla, costing her a job. Using a stolen résumé, Kayla is hired at the Royal Gate, Manhattan's fanciest hotel, to help plan the high-profile wedding of celebrities Preeta Mehta and Ben, who arrive with their bulldog, Spike, and cat, Toots. Jerry has moved into the hotel, and his presence threatens the event. Tom finally gets inside and wrecks a room chasing Jerry, and Kayla befriends him; the hotel manager hires Tom to get rid of the mouse, while Kayla's boss, Terence, threatens to fire them if he fails. Tom eventually traps Jerry outside, but Preeta's engagement ring goes missing.

Jerry returns with the ring and offers it to Kayla in exchange for being allowed to stay. A chase involving Spike, Tom and Jerry wrecks the lobby, after which Terence is suspended and Kayla promoted to event manager for recovering the ring. Kayla orders the rivals to spend a day bonding, but their outing ends with both locked in a pound after they interfere with play at a baseball game. A vengeful Terence feeds each of them lies about the other, and their renewed fight wrecks the wedding ceremony and the hotel. Kayla confesses and leaves in disgrace, and Preeta calls off the wedding. Realizing their fault, Tom and Jerry reconcile and persuade Kayla and the hotel staff, including Terence, to stage the wedding in Central Park, where Ben apologizes to Preeta for his extravagant spending. Kayla makes peace with the owner of the résumé, both get jobs at the hotel, and Tom finally performs as a jazz pianist until another mishap restarts the feud.

Filmed at Warner Bros. Studios, Leavesden in 2019, the film opened in U.S. theaters on February 26, 2021, alongside a month of streaming on HBO Max. It grossed $136.5 million worldwide, but reviews were largely negative, with 29% on Rotten Tomatoes and 32 on Metacritic.

overview: Santa Claus is actually a demon who lost a bet with an angel, so he became the giver of toys and happiness. But this year the bet is off, and Santa is about to return to his evil ways.
tagline: He's making a list... pray you're not on it.
title: Santa's Slay
plot:
Santa's Slay is a 2005 Canadian-American Christmas black comedy slasher film written and directed by David Steiman, a former assistant to Brett Ratner, who served as a producer. Its premise has Santa Claus return to his demonic nature after a thousand years of forced gift-giving imposed when he lost a bet with an angel. The cast includes Bill Goldberg, Douglas Smith, Emilie de Ravin, Robert Culp, Saul Rubinek, Dave Thomas, Rebecca Gayheart, Chris Kattan and Fran Drescher.

On Christmas Eve in Alberta, the wealthy Mason family is squabbling over dinner when Santa comes down the chimney and kills them all in gruesome holiday-themed ways. Riding a sleigh pulled by a buffalo-like "hell-deer", he descends on the town of Hell Township, slaughtering the patrons of a strip club and the owner of a Jewish delicatessen, Mr. Green. Teenager Nicholas Yuleson lives with his grandfather, an eccentric inventor who hides from Christmas in a basement bunker. Grandpa shows Nicholas "The Book of Klaus", which reveals that Santa was born of a virgin birth fathered by Satan and that Christmas was his "Day of Slaying" until AD 1005, when an angel beat him at curling and condemned him to deliver presents for a thousand years. That sentence has now run out.

Questioned by police about Mr. Green's murder, Nicholas is bailed out by Mary "Mac" Mackenzie, the girl he likes, moments before Santa massacres the officers. Santa chases the pair, who escape with the help of a shotgun in Mac's truck and flee to Grandpa's bunker. They escape again on a snowmobile, and Grandpa appears to be killed. Hiding in the local high school in the hope that Santa's power will end with Christmas, they are cornered in the gym and nearly run down by Santa driving a Zamboni, until Grandpa returns and reveals that he is the angel who defeated Santa long ago. As Christmas ends and his powers fade, Santa flees, and Mac's father shoots down the hell-deer with a bazooka. A crooked local pastor, Timmons, is found dead in a Santa suit and blamed for the killings, while the real Santa boards a flight from Winnipeg to the North Pole under the name "Mr. Šatan". Nicholas vows to finish his grandfather's work. After the credits, Santa studies his naughty list and asks who is next.

Lionsgate released the film on DVD in the United States on December 20, 2005. Reviews were mixed: The A.V. Club found it vulgar yet wholesome and stupid yet satirical, and HorrorNews.net called it fun, brainless and violent.

overview: In ancient Egypt, peasant Mathayus is hired to exact revenge on the powerful Memnon and the sorceress Cassandra, who are ready to overtake Balthazar's village. Amid betrayals, thieves, abductions and more, Mathayus strives to bring justice to his complicated world.
tagline: Warrior. Legend. King.
title: The Scorpion King
plot:
The Scorpion King is a 2002 American fantasy adventure film directed by Chuck Russell and written by David Hayter. The movie serves as a prequel to The Mummy Returns, starring Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson.

In ancient Egypt, the story begins with Mathayus (Dwayne Johnson), a young orphan who grows up on the streets of Memphis. He is discovered by a group of mercenaries and trained in combat skills by the leader, General Kane (Steven Brand). Kane becomes like a father to Mathayus, teaching him how to fight and survive.

As Mathayus grows older, he becomes a skilled warrior and earns the respect of his comrades. However, Kane's true intentions are revealed: he plans to overthrow the Pharaoh and take control of Egypt for himself. Mathayus is torn between his loyalty to Kane and his growing sense of morality.

When Kane's plan fails, he is betrayed by his own men and left for dead. Mathayus finds him dying and nurses him back to health. As Kane lies on his deathbed, he reveals that the Scorpion King is a legendary figure who will one day bring about great change in Egypt.

Kane dies, but not before giving Mathayus a magical amulet that allows him to control the sand worms of the desert. With this newfound power, Mathayus sets out to avenge Kane's death and claim his rightful place as the Scorpion King.

Mathayus faces numerous challenges on his journey, including fierce battles with rival warriors and treacherous desert landscapes. Along the way, he meets a woman named Chandra (Kelly Hu), who becomes his ally and potential love interest.

As Mathayus draws closer to his goal, he must confront his own demons and learn to harness his newfound powers. In the end, he defeats Kane's successor, General Sargon (Michael Clarke Duncan), and claims the throne of Egypt as the Scorpion King.

The movie ends with Mathayus standing victorious, but also aware that his journey is far from over. He has become a legendary figure, feared and respected by all who know him. The final shot is of the magical amulet, still glowing with power, as the camera pans out to reveal the vast expanse of the desert landscape.

Overall, The Scorpion King is an action-packed adventure film that explores themes of loyalty, power, and redemption. Dwayne Johnson's performance as Mathayus brings depth and nuance to the character, making him a compelling hero on screen.

overview: In this prequel to the original, a rebel policeman sets up the infiltration of Triad gangs and tries bring down a corrupt cop working for the Triad boss.
tagline: The Birth of a Legend.
title: Infernal Affairs II
plot:
Infernal Affairs II is a 2003 Hong Kong crime thriller film directed by Andrew Lau and Alan Mak. The movie explores the complex web of loyalty, deception, and morality in the world of organized crime.

At its core, Infernal Affairs II delves into the theme of identity and how it can be both a source of strength and weakness. The main character, a police officer who infiltrates a triad organization, must navigate a treacherous landscape where allegiances are constantly shifting and loyalty is tested to the limit.

The film also examines the blurred lines between good and evil, as the protagonist becomes increasingly entrenched in the world of organized crime. This moral ambiguity raises questions about the nature of right and wrong, and whether it's possible for someone to be both a hero and a villain at the same time.

Furthermore, Infernal Affairs II touches on the theme of redemption, as the protagonist seeks to make amends for past mistakes and find a way out of the cycle of violence and deception. However, this quest is complicated by the fact that he is still deeply entrenched in the world of organized crime, making it difficult to distinguish between his personal desires and his duty to uphold justice.

Overall, Infernal Affairs II is a gripping thriller that explores complex themes of identity, morality, and redemption in a gritty and intense portrayal of life on the wrong side of the law.

overview: When a billionaire gives a group of young scientists unlimited resources to study the science of matter transfer, the scientists unlock the secrets of time travel. But they soon find out that the project is backed by a militant extremist group, and the billionaire plans to go back in time and prove that Jesus never rose from the dead.
tagline: What if the greatest event in human history was erased?
title: Assassin 33 A.D.
plot:
Spooks: The Greater Good is a 2015 British spy thriller film directed by David Wilmot, based on the BBC television series Spooks. The movie follows the story of Harry Pearce (played by Richard Armitage), a former head of MI5's counter-intelligence unit, who is forced back into action when a mole within his organization threatens to destroy everything he has worked for.

The main themes of Spooks: The Greater Good include:

1. Loyalty and Betrayal: The movie explores the theme of loyalty and betrayal, as Harry Pearce navigates a complex web of allegiances and rivalries within his own organization. As he delves deeper into the mystery of the mole, he is forced to confront the possibility that those closest to him may be working against him.
2. Morality in War: The film raises questions about morality in the context of war and espionage. Harry Pearce's actions are guided by a strong sense of duty and loyalty, but as the stakes grow higher, he must confront the moral implications of his decisions.
3. Trauma and Redemption: The movie also explores the theme of trauma and redemption, as Harry Pearce grapples with the consequences of his past mistakes and seeks to make amends. His journey is marked by a sense of regret and longing for a lost love, which serves as a catalyst for his actions.

Overall, Spooks: The Greater Good is a gripping thriller that explores complex themes and moral ambiguities in the world of espionage.

overview: When Keira Woods' daughter mysteriously vanishes in the cellar of their new house in the country, she soon discovers there is an ancient and powerful entity controlling their home that she will have to face or risk losing her family's souls forever.
tagline: An ancient evil has awoken.
title: The Cellar
plot:
The Cellar is a 2022 supernatural horror film written and directed by Brendan Muldowney, starring Elisha Cuthbert and Eoin Macken. An Irish-Belgian co-production, it was shot in Roscommon, Ireland, in November 2020, and premiered at South by Southwest in March 2022 before its release on the streaming service Shudder on 15 April 2022.

Kiera and Brian Woods move into a large old house with their teenage daughter, Ellie, and their young son, Steven.
