Left alone one evening while their parents are at work, the children find a hidden room in the cellar whose walls are covered in formulas, symbols and artwork, along with a recording of a man reciting equations and slowly counting upward. That night the power goes out, and Kiera, on the phone, guides Ellie down to the cellar's breaker box by counting the steps. Ellie begins to behave strangely, and by the time her parents get home she has vanished. Because Ellie has run away before, the police assume she will come back on her own.

Unconvinced, Kiera investigates the house and one of its former owners, John Fetherston, who also disappeared. She discovers that the symbols spell out "Leviathan" and that the equations describe other dimensions, while strange events increasingly surround her, and a presence nearly traps her when she is lured into the cellar. Brian refuses to believe her. Fetherston's elderly daughter, Rose, explains that her father opened a door to the entity in the hope of curing her brother, Jack, but that it took over the house instead. Brian finds further symbols over the doors that, combined, spell "Baphomet". The demon then seizes Steven, and Kiera is chased into the cellar, which has become an endless corridor. Beyond a door she finds Ellie among many people counting upward. She escapes and reunites with Brian and Steven, but when they try to leave they realize that they are still trapped in the demon's dimension, and the whole family starts counting, Kiera included.

Critics were unimpressed, with only 31% of the 62 reviews collected by Rotten Tomatoes positive and a consensus that called it a musty exercise in second-rate supernatural horror, though not a total failure.

original_title: How to Build a Better Boy
overview: Mae and Gabby are two friends who go everywhere together but they are not very popular in their school. Their classmates always pressure because they have not had a boyfriend so to avoid further setbacks, the girls put in place a plan to create the perfect boyfriend. Both believe that it will be easy to create their perfect guy using the military team building; machinery owned by the father of Mae, the machine works through a wireless keyboard. The machine can create with their settings, a robotic soldier. Of this plan was born Albert an ideal guy to be a perfect boyfriend. He will be the most popular boy of the school.
tagline: Never underestimate two girls with a plan.
title: How to Build a Better Boy
plot:
How to Build a Better Boy is a 2014 American science fiction teen romantic comedy made as a Disney Channel Original Movie, directed by Paul Hoen and written by Jason Mayland. Kelli Berglund plays Mae Hartley and China Anne McClain her best friend, Gabby Harrison, with Marshall Williams as Albert, Matt Shively as Bart Hartley, Ashley Argota as Nevaeh, Noah Centineo as Jaden and Roger Bart as Mae's father.

Mae and Gabby are bright tenth graders. Mae has a crush on Jaden, a jock she tutors, and hopes he will invite her to the homecoming dance, but she is publicly humiliated by Jaden's girlfriend, the mean cheerleader Nevaeh, and blurts out that she already has a boyfriend. To cover the lie, Gabby uses software called X-17, which they think Mae's father, Dr. James Hartley, uses to design video game characters, to program a virtual boyfriend to Mae's specifications. Mae names him Albert. When the program crashes the computer, Mae's brother, Bart, fixes it in exchange for Gabby's going to homecoming with him.

The next morning Albert turns up at school, where his superhuman speed and strength make him instantly popular. Bart and Gabby discover that she has hacked into the Pentagon and activated a prototype robot soldier, and that James actually works for the Pentagon, while General McFee learns that the X-17 is missing. Albert asks Mae to homecoming, and despite misgivings and a quarrel with Gabby, she accepts. Agents of the arms-dealing group Black Sigma hunt for the robot. At a football game, Albert leads a comeback before Black Sigma knocks out the power with an electromagnetic pulse that damages his circuits. The Army captures the criminals, and Albert leaves on a global mission. Told to forget him, Mae still believes he will come to the dance, and he does. McFee agrees to let Albert complete his mission of kissing Mae, and the Army rigs the vote to make them homecoming king and queen. Nevaeh is dumped by Jaden, who admits he was too shy to ask Mae out. When Albert leans in, Mae pulls back, realizing she wants a real relationship rather than a perfect one. Impressed, Albert asks her to trigger his self-destruct, and he bursts through the roof and explodes. Jaden asks Mae out, the friends reconcile, and Gabby reveals that she is now dating Bart.

The film was shot in Toronto, mainly at North Toronto Collegiate Institute, in the summer of 2013. Its Disney Channel premiere on August 15, 2014, drew 4.6 million viewers.

overview: A man must survive a prison where hardened criminals battle to the death for the warden's entertainment.
tagline: Rage unleashed.
title: In Hell
plot:
In Hell is an American action thriller of 2003 directed by Ringo Lam, his third and last collaboration with Jean-Claude Van Damme. Van Damme stars as Kyle LeBlanc, an American locked away in a brutal Russian prison, with Lawrence Taylor as the feared Inmate 451, Lloyd Battista as the corrupt warden General Hruschov, Michael Bailey Smith as Valya and Chris Moir as Billy Cooper.

Kyle, working abroad in the Russian city of Magnitogorsk, hears his wife being attacked over the phone and arrives to find her dead. Her killer, Sergio Kovic, bribes the judge and walks free, and the enraged Kyle grabs a bailiff's gun and shoots him dead in the courtroom. Sentenced to life without parole, he is sent to Kravavi Prison, ruled by General Hruschov, and beaten for hesitating to give up his wedding ring. He watches a young American inmate, Billy, dragged off to be raped by the Russian mobster Andrei, fights Andrei the next morning, and is thrown into solitary, where he attempts suicide. Deciding instead to survive, he gets himself moved into the cell of Inmate 451, notorious for killing his cellmates, and the two form an unlikely bond. Malakai, an American in a wheelchair, explains the gangs and the Mafia's pact with the guards.

Kyle trains as a prison fighter and kills Andrei in his first bout, which shakes him badly, but he keeps fighting, grows hard, wins the respect of the inmates and turns away help from the American embassy. When Malakai betrays Billy's escape plans in return for medical care, 451 burns him alive, recalling how he killed the teacher who abused him in the same way. Billy dies after resisting Valya's assault, warning Kyle not to let anyone change who he is. Kyle refuses to fight Valya and is strung up by his arms in the yard; moved by his endurance, the rival gangs unite and refuse to fight. Ordered to face Miloc, a giant prisoner he knew from solitary, Kyle again refuses, and a riot erupts in which Miloc is shot shielding him. Amid the chaos, 451 gives Kyle evidence of the prison's abuses and shows him a secret way to the garage. Kyle must first defeat Valya, who pulls a knife during the fight, and kills him. 451 stays behind to deal with Hruschov while Kyle recovers his ring and drives away. Back in the United States, he exposes Kravavi, which is shut down three months later.

The film was released on DVD in the United States in November 2003. Reviews were poor: TV Guide gave it one star out of five, and IGN said it was strictly for Van Damme fans.

overview: Katie, a former professional ice skater, is hired by the king of San Senova, Alexander, to help his daughter in a Christmas ice skating performance. As Katie spends time in the castle and with the king, she and Alex begin to develop feelings for each other and ultimately fall in love. But will the tradition-loving people of San Senova allow their king to make a foreigner their queen?
title: Christmas at the Palace
plot:
Christmas at the Palace is a 2018 Christmas romantic comedy television film produced for Hallmark Channel by Motion Picture Corporation of America and Brad Krevoy Television. It stars Merritt Patterson as Katie, a former professional figure skater, and Andrew Cooper as Alexander, the widowed king of the fictional nation of San Senova, with Brittany Bristow, Nicholas Banks, India Fowler and Geraldine Fitzgerald in supporting roles. It premiered on Thanksgiving, 22 November 2018, as part of Hallmark's Countdown to Christmas season.

Katie, who once came close to competing at the Olympics, now manages a touring Christmas ice show starring her friend Jessica, and the two hope that the earnings from the tour will let them buy an ice rink back home in New Jersey. Their final stop is San Senova, whose king, Alexander, is struggling to live up to the legacy of his late father, who founded the kingdom's beloved holiday traditions, and has been nicknamed a Grinch after the press criticized his lack of Christmas spirit. Katie literally bumps into him at the Christmas market without realizing who he is. After the show, Princess Christina, a talented but insecure young skater, asks the two women for lessons and persuades her father to let her stage a Christmas skating pageant at the palace rink. Alexander hires Katie and Jessica for a large fee that would fund their dream, and invites them to stay at the palace. As Katie prepares the pageant, encourages Christina and helps the king rediscover the joy of the season, from decorating a tree to making handmade gifts for his staff and baking cookies for the royal Christmas tea, she and Alexander fall in love, while Jessica and Nicholas begin their own romance. But the tradition-loving people of San Senova may not accept a foreigner as their queen, and when Jessica is injured and their rink deal is threatened, Katie must choose between her plans and the family she has come to love.

The fictional kingdom was created in Romania. Filming took place in October 2018 with Castel Film Studios in Bucharest, at locations including Snagov Palace on Lake Snagov, while the town of San Senova was built on a studio lot. Reviews were mixed. The Avocado's recap found the leading couple bland and Cooper's king monotone, preferring the secondary romance and pitying the moping princess, while other viewers enjoyed the warm chemistry between the leads and the Romanian palace scenery.

overview: Without warning a father comes to visit his daughter abroad. He believes that she lost her humor and therefore surprises her with a rampage of jokes.
title: Toni Erdmann
plot:
Toni Erdmann is a 2016 German comedy-drama film that explores the complexities of identity, family dynamics, and the search for meaning in life.

At its core, the movie delves into the theme of self-discovery and the blurring of professional and personal boundaries. The protagonist, Winfried Conradi, played by Peter Simonischek, is a middle-aged man who embarks on a journey to reconnect with his estranged daughter, Ines, played by Sandra Hüller. As he assumes the alter ego "Toni Erdmann," a fictional business consultant, he forces himself into her life and challenges her to confront her own identity and sense of purpose.

The film also explores the theme of emotional repression and the consequences of bottling up one's feelings. Winfried/Ines's relationship is marked by a deep-seated emotional distance, which Toni Erdmann seeks to bridge through his unconventional approach. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Ines has been struggling to find her place in the world, feeling lost and uncertain about her future.

Furthermore, the movie touches on the theme of societal expectations and the pressure to conform. Winfried/Ines's relationship is influenced by their respective careers and the societal norms that come with them. Toni Erdmann's unorthodox methods serve as a catalyst for Ines to reevaluate her priorities and question the values she has been conditioned to accept.

Ultimately, Toni Erdmann is a poignant exploration of the human search for connection, meaning, and authenticity in a chaotic world. Through its nuanced portrayal of complex characters and relationships, the film invites viewers to reflect on their own identities, emotions, and desires.

overview: Since the 1960s, a disproportionate number of the population in and around Nome, Alaska, have gone missing. Despite FBI investigations, the disappearances remain a mystery. Dr. Abigail Tyler, a psychologist, may be on the verge of blowing the unsolved cases wide open when, during the course of treating her patients, she finds evidence of alien abductions.
tagline: There are four kinds of alien encounters. The fourth kind is abduction.
title: The Fourth Kind
plot:
The Fourth Kind is a 2009 science fiction horror thriller written and directed by Olatunde Osunsanmi, starring Milla Jovovich, Elias Koteas, Will Patton and Charlotte Milchard. Its title extends J. Allen Hynek's classification of close encounters, in which the fourth kind denotes alien abduction. Presented as a pseudodocumentary, it claims to dramatize true events in Nome, Alaska, and places supposed archival footage of the "real" psychologist side by side with the re-enactments. Jovovich opens the film by telling viewers that it is real and that she plays a character based on a woman named Abigail Tyler; the "real" Tyler is played by Milchard, with Osunsanmi as her interviewer.

In August 2000, psychologist Abbey Tyler is raising her two children, Ashley and Ronnie, after her husband Will's death, which she believes was a murder. Several of her patients describe the same experience of a white owl staring at them as they sleep before something tries to enter their homes. One night a patient holds his family at gunpoint, asks what the phrase "Zimabu Eter" means and kills them and himself. A tape recorder reveals that Abbey herself was apparently attacked in her home by a being speaking an unknown language, which the linguist Awolowa Odusami identifies as Sumerian. Under hypnosis, another patient, Scott, levitates above his bed while a voice orders Abbey in Sumerian to end her study, and he is left paralyzed.

Sheriff August blames Abbey and places her under guard. A police camera then records a huge saucer-shaped object above her house and people being pulled from it, and Ashley disappears, so August takes Ronnie away from her. Abbey undergoes hypnosis to contact the beings, recalls that she and Ashley were both abducted, and hears a voice calling itself "God" tell her that her daughter will never return. Abbey, her skeptical colleague Abel Campos and Odusami vanish from the footage, and she wakes in hospital with a broken neck, where August reveals that Will actually took his own life. In the closing interview, Abbey insists that Ashley is still alive.

The film premiered at Screamfest in Los Angeles on October 24, 2009, and opened in the United States and United Kingdom on November 6, earning about $49.5 million worldwide. Reviews were mostly negative, with 18% approval on Rotten Tomatoes; Roger Ebert gave it one and a half stars but praised Jovovich, and NPR likened it to a chain e-mail hoax.

overview: A biopic of 20-year-old Francis Ouimet who defeated his golfing idol and 1900 US Open Champion, Harry Vardon.
tagline: Based on a True Story
title: The Greatest Game Ever Played
plot:
The Greatest Game Ever Played is a 2005 biographical sports drama film directed by Tom Shadyac, produced by Walt Disney Pictures, and based on the life of Francis Ouimet, an American golfer who challenged the British aristocracy at the 1913 U.S. Open.

The main themes of The Greatest Game Ever Played include:

1. **Overcoming class differences**: The film highlights the contrast between Ouimet's humble background and his opponents' wealth and privilege. Despite this, Ouimet perseveres and ultimately wins the championship, inspiring a nation.
2. **Perseverance and determination**: Ouimet faces numerous setbacks, including financial struggles and personal losses, but he never gives up on his passion for golf. His determination drives him to succeed against all odds.
3. **The power of sports to unite people**: The film showcases the impact of golf on American society during a time of great social change. The game brings together people from different backgrounds, fostering a sense of community and national pride.
4. **Challenging societal norms**: Ouimet's victory at the U.S. Open is seen as a challenge to the British aristocracy's dominance in golf. His success inspires others to break free from traditional expectations and pursue their passions.
5. **Personal growth and redemption**: Throughout the film, Ouimet faces personal struggles, including financial difficulties and family problems. His ultimate triumph serves as a redemptive arc, demonstrating his capacity for resilience and self-improvement.

Overall, The Greatest Game Ever Played is a heartwarming story about overcoming adversity, challenging societal norms, and finding success through perseverance and determination.

overview: FBI agent Joel Campbell, burnt-out and shell-shocked after years spent chasing serial killers, flees L.A. to begin a new life for himself in Chicago. But five months later, Joel's best laid plans are abruptly cut short when his new hometown becomes the setting for some particularly gruesome murders--murders that could only have been committed by one man: David Allen Griffin. One of Joel's most elusive and cunning nemeses, Griffin has followed his former pursuer to Chicago in order to play a sadistic game of cat and mouse. Taunting Joel with photographs of his intended victims and leaving his crime scenes meticulously free of clues in order to keep the police at bay, Griffin derives as much pleasure out of watching Joel react to every movement as watching his victims die. But when Griffin moves into Joel's inner circle, Joel must quickly find some way to stop him before someone close to him becomes the next one to die.
tagline: Don't go home alone.
title: The Watcher
plot:
The Watcher is an American thriller of 2000 directed by Joe Charbanic, in which a retired FBI agent in Chicago is stalked and taunted by the serial killer he once pursued. James Spader stars as Special Agent Joel Campbell, with Keanu Reeves, cast against type, as the killer David Allen Griffin, Marisa Tomei as the psychologist Dr Polly Beilman, Ernie Hudson as Special Agent in Charge Mike Ibby and Chris Ellis as Detective Hollis Mackie.

In Los Angeles, Campbell arrives moments too late to save a young woman from the killer he has been hunting, who escapes. Shattered, he quits the bureau and moves to Chicago, where he suffers guilt-induced migraines and sees the therapist Polly Beilman. When a woman in his apartment building is murdered, he pays little attention until he finds that a photograph of her was mailed to him three days before her death. He takes the evidence to Detective Mackie and realises that the killer has followed him. Ibby urges him to return to the case, but Campbell refuses until Griffin telephones him, explaining that he wants to rebuild the rapport they once shared. He will send Campbell a photograph of a woman each morning, and Campbell must find her by nine o'clock that night.

Reinstated, Campbell works with Mackie and his team, publicising the picture to identify the woman, but by the time he reaches her by phone Griffin is already in her house and kills her. The game continues with another woman the next day; the police corner Griffin, but he kills her and escapes again. That night Campbell is found unconscious in his apartment. The next photograph shows Lisa Anton, Campbell's former lover, whom Griffin murdered in Los Angeles. At her grave, Griffin waits for him and reveals that he is holding Polly hostage. Campbell negotiates to see her, and on the drive Griffin explains that he regards Campbell as a good friend and that each needs the other, while Campbell secretly calls Mackie on his phone. At a warehouse, Griffin knocks Campbell out, ties him up and begins strangling Polly. Campbell distracts him by thanking him, stabs him in the neck with a pen and shoots him with a shotgun, then escapes with Polly as the warehouse explodes. Afterwards Campbell inspects Griffin's charred corpse to be sure he is dead.

The film opened at number one in North America in September 2000, during one of the weakest box office weekends in years, and earned about $29 million domestically. Critics panned it, giving it 11% on Rotten Tomatoes.

original_title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
overview: Mere seconds before the Earth is to be demolished by an alien construction crew, Arthur Dent is swept off the planet by his friend Ford Prefect, a researcher penning a new edition of "The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy."
tagline: Don't leave Earth without it
title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
plot:
The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy (2005) is a science fiction comedy film directed by Garth Jennings, produced by Gary Barber and Jay Roach, and distributed by Spyglass Entertainment.

The main themes of The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy revolve around:

1. **Existentialism**: The movie explores the meaninglessness of life in an seemingly indifferent universe. The protagonist, Arthur Dent (played by Martin Freeman), finds himself on a journey through space after Earth's destruction, leading him to question the purpose of existence.
2. **Satire and Social Commentary**: The film uses humor and satire to comment on human nature, politics, and societal norms. It pokes fun at bureaucracy, government inefficiency, and the dangers of unchecked technological advancement.
3. **Friendship and Human Connection**: Throughout the journey, Arthur forms unlikely friendships with his alien companions, including Ford Prefect (played by Mos Def), Zaphod Beeblebrox (played by Sam Rockwell), Trillian (played by Zooey Deschanel), and Marvin (voiced by Alan Rickman). These relationships highlight the importance of human connection in a chaotic universe.
4. **The Search for Meaning**: The characters' quest to find the ultimate answer to life, the universe, and everything (42) serves as a metaphor for humanity's eternal search for meaning and purpose.

The movie's plot development follows Arthur's journey with his companions as they navigate through space, encountering various alien species, and facing challenges that test their friendship and resolve. Ultimately, the film concludes with a bittersweet ending, leaving the audience to ponder the same question: "What is the answer?"

original_title: 劇場版総集編【前編】メイドインアビス 旅立ちの夜明け
overview: First compilation movie of the TV series which covers episodes 1-8 with new scenes added for the introduction. It covers the period from when Riko descends into the Abyss with her robot companion Reg, reaching the second layer where they meet the White Whistle Ozen who reveals information about Riko's mother.
title: Made in Abyss: Journey's Dawn
plot:
Made in Abyss: Journey's Dawn is an anime film that delves into the complexities of human existence, particularly in the context of exploration and discovery. The story revolves around Riko, a young girl who embarks on a perilous journey to the bottom of a mysterious abyss with her friend Reg.

At its core, Made in Abyss: Journey's Dawn explores the theme of existentialism, where characters are forced to confront the meaninglessness of their existence and the impermanence of life. The abyss serves as a metaphor for the unknown, representing the vast and uncharted territories that lie beyond human understanding.

The film also touches on the idea of obsession and fixation, as Riko's determination to reach the bottom of the abyss becomes an all-consuming force in her life. This theme is intertwined with the concept of sacrifice, as characters are willing to risk everything for the sake of discovery and progress.

Furthermore, Made in Abyss: Journey's Dawn examines the complexities of human relationships and the bonds that form between individuals. Riko and Reg's friendship serves as a beacon of hope and comfort in an otherwise desolate world, highlighting the importance of emotional connections in the face of adversity.

Ultimately, the film presents a poignant exploration of the human condition, one that is marked by both beauty and brutality, wonder and despair. Through its thought-provoking narrative and stunning visuals, Made in Abyss: Journey's Dawn invites viewers to reflect on their own place within the world and the significance of their existence.

overview: A teenager suspects his new neighbour is a vampire. Unable to convince anyone, he tries to enlist the help of a self-proclaimed vampire hunter and magician.
tagline: You can't run from evil when it lives next door
title: Fright Night
plot:
[Freight Night (2011) is not a movie produced by DreamWorks Pictures.]

However, I can provide information on the 1985 film "Fright Night" directed by Tom Holland.

The main themes of the 1985 film "Fright Night" include:

* The struggle for independence and self-discovery: The protagonist, Charlie, is a teenager who wants to assert his independence from his overbearing mother. He also seeks to establish his own identity and sense of purpose.
* The dangers of peer pressure and conformity: Charlie's desire to fit in with his peers leads him to make questionable decisions, which ultimately put him in danger.
* The importance of family and relationships: Despite the challenges he faces, Charlie's relationships with his mother, Jerry (the vampire), and his friends are crucial to his survival and growth.

The 2011 remake, directed by Craig Gillespie, has a slightly different tone and focus. It explores themes such as:

* The struggle for identity and belonging: Charlie is still trying to find his place in the world, but this time he's also dealing with the challenges of adolescence.
* The dangers of obsession and fixation: Jerry (the vampire) is a more complex and nuanced character than in the original film, and his obsession with Charlie drives much of the plot.
* The power of friendship and loyalty: Charlie's relationships with his friends and allies are crucial to his survival and ultimate victory over Jerry.

Please note that I couldn't find any information on a 2011 film titled "Fright Night" produced by DreamWorks Pictures.

overview: Reeling from the unexpected death of her husband, Beth is left alone in the lakeside home he built for her. Soon she begins to uncover her recently deceased husband's disturbing secrets.
tagline: The truth will surface.
title: The Night House
plot:
The Night House is a 2021 American supernatural horror film written and directed by David Bruckner. The movie stars Rebecca Hall as Beth, a widow who discovers her recently deceased husband's dark secrets.

The story begins with the death of Beth's husband, Owen (played by Evan Jonigkeit), in a car accident. Beth is devastated by his loss and struggles to cope with the grief. As she sorts through their belongings, she discovers a mysterious manuscript written by Owen, which reveals that he was involved in some sinister activities.

As Beth delves deeper into the manuscript, she begins to uncover disturbing secrets about her husband's past. She learns that Owen was part of a cult-like organization called "The Order," which worshipped an ancient deity known as "The Night House." The group believed that by sacrificing themselves, they could achieve immortality and transcendence.

Beth becomes increasingly obsessed with understanding the true nature of Owen's involvement with The Order. She starts to experience strange and terrifying events, which she initially attributes to grief and stress. However, as the occurrences escalate, she begins to suspect that something more sinister is at play.

As Beth digs deeper, she discovers a dark history about The Night House and its followers. She learns that Owen was one of the most devoted members of the group, and that he had become increasingly unhinged in his final days. The manuscript reveals that Owen's ultimate goal was to summon The Night House, a malevolent entity that would grant him immortality.

As Beth gets closer to the truth, she realizes that she is now being hunted by The Order. She must navigate a complex web of secrets and lies to uncover the truth about her husband's death and the mysterious forces at work.

The climax of the movie takes place in an abandoned house, where Beth confronts Owen's dark past and the true nature of The Night House. In a shocking twist, it is revealed that Owen had become possessed by The Night House, which had been manipulating him from the beginning.

In the end, Beth manages to escape the clutches of The Order and destroy the manuscript, which holds the key to unlocking the secrets of The Night House. However, as she walks away from the abandoned house, she can't shake off the feeling that The Night House is still watching her, waiting for its next victim.

The Night House is a tense and unsettling horror film that explores themes of grief, obsession, and the dangers of blindly following a charismatic leader. Rebecca Hall delivers a standout performance as Beth, bringing depth and nuance to a complex and terrifying character.

overview: Among normal humans live the "Others" possessing various supernatural powers. They are divided up into the forces of light and the forces of the dark, who signed a truce several centuries ago to end a devastating battle. Ever since, the forces of light govern the day while the night belongs to their dark opponents. In modern day Moscow the dark Others actually roam the night as vampires while a "Night Watch" of light forces, among them Anton, the movie's protagonist, try to control them and limit their outrage
tagline: All That Stands Between Light And Darkness Is The Night Watch.
title: Night Watch
plot:
Night Watch (Russian: Nochnoy dozor) is a 2004 Russian urban fantasy thriller directed by Timur Bekmambetov, who wrote the screenplay with Laeta Kalogridis, loosely based on Sergei Lukyanenko's 1998 novel The Night Watch. Channel One bought the adaptation rights and hired Bekmambetov after an earlier, low-budget attempt stalled. Made for about $4.2 million, it was the first big-budget Russian supernatural film and one of the first blockbusters after the collapse of the Soviet film industry, with effects shots made by 16 Russian studios.

Since ancient times, humans with supernatural powers, known as Others, have been split between Light and Dark. After a medieval battle ended in stalemate, the leaders Geser and Zavulon agreed a truce policed by the Night Watch, which monitors the Dark, and the Day Watch, which monitors the Light. In Moscow in 1992, Anton Gorodetsky pays a witch to win back his wife, agreeing that the spell will make her lose the child she is carrying, which he believes is another man's. Two agents burst in to stop the ritual and realize that Anton can see them, revealing that he is an Other himself.

Twelve years later, Anton works for the Night Watch. Geser tells him that a series of omens point to an ancient prophecy of an immensely powerful Other who will break the balance between Light and Dark and is more likely to choose the Dark. Anton's investigations lead him to Svetlana, a nurse around whom disasters seem to gather, and to a young boy, Yegor. Realizing that Svetlana is an Other, Anton prevents a storm from leveling Moscow and begins teaching her to control her power. But he then discovers that Yegor is his own son, the child his wife was carrying in 1992. Learning that his father once tried to have him killed before birth, Yegor, the prophesied Other, turns away from Anton toward Zavulon, as Zavulon had planned. Anton strikes him in rage, vowing not to give up despite the Dark's apparent victory.

Konstantin Khabensky plays Anton, with Vladimir Menshov as Geser, Viktor Verzhbitsky as Zavulon, Mariya Poroshina as Svetlana and Dmitry Martynov as Yegor. Premiering at the Moscow Film Festival on 27 June 2004, it became the highest-grossing Russian release to date, earning $16.7 million at home. Fox Searchlight bought the international rights, releasing a re-edited version with animated subtitles. Reviews were mixed, with 59% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, and a sequel, Day Watch, followed in 2006.

overview: Disney's irresistible talking puppies are back in an all-new movie that takes them far across town to a mysterious mansion where something very spooky is going on.
title: Spooky Buddies
plot:
Spooky Buddies is a 2011 family comedy film that revolves around a group of canine friends who get caught up in a mystery surrounding a haunted mansion. The movie explores several key themes, primarily centered around friendship and loyalty.

At its core, Spooky Buddies celebrates the unbreakable bonds between dogs and their human companions. The film showcases how these relationships can transcend even the most extraordinary circumstances, as the canine characters work together to help their owners overcome challenges and fears. This theme is beautifully illustrated through the interactions between the dog characters, who demonstrate remarkable empathy, loyalty, and teamwork.

The movie also touches on the idea of facing one's fears and overcoming phobias. The human characters in the film are often held back by their own anxieties and doubts, but with the help of their canine companions, they learn to confront and overcome these obstacles. This theme is skillfully woven throughout the narrative, as the dogs encourage their owners to be brave and take risks.

Furthermore, Spooky Buddies highlights the importance of trust and communication in relationships. The dog characters are able to sense their owners' emotions and respond accordingly, demonstrating a deep understanding of human psychology. This theme is beautifully illustrated through the interactions between the dog characters and their owners, showcasing how open communication and empathy can lead to stronger, more meaningful relationships.

Overall, Spooky Buddies is a heartwarming film that celebrates the power of friendship, loyalty, and trust in overcoming even the most daunting challenges.

overview: After a teacher dies, his best friend — a former cop — takes a job at the school where he worked to confront the gang he thinks was responsible.
title: Lesson Plan
plot:
Lesson Plan (Polish: Plan lekcji) is a 2022 Polish action crime film directed by Daniel Markowicz from a screenplay by Daniel Bernardi and released by Netflix. It stars Piotr Witkowski as Damian Nowicki, a former undercover police officer nicknamed Jiu-Jitsu, alongside Antonina Jarnuszkiewicz as his colleague Agata, with Jan Wieczorkowski, Nicolas Przygoda, Daniel Namiotko, Rafał Zawierucha, Zuzanna Galewicz, Pascal Fischer, Marcin Bosak and Roma Gąsiorowska in supporting roles. The film runs about 100 minutes and borrows the familiar premise of an outsider teacher facing an unruly class, filtered through B-movie martial arts action.

The film opens with Damian, who has infiltrated a drug gang posing as a criminal, fighting his way unarmed through a group of machine gun-wielding henchmen after the mafia discovers his identity and murders his wife. He brings down the boss and the entire ring single-handedly but is left a broken man who sinks into alcoholism. His best friend, a history teacher, asks him to look into the drugs flooding the high school where he works, and Damian at first refuses. When the friend dies, Damian decides to uncover the gang he believes is responsible and takes his late friend's vacant post as a history teacher at the modest school. There he faces uncooperative students, but he wins over the good ones, preparing his lessons conscientiously while spending more time teaching them jiu-jitsu for self-defense as they try to resist the dealers in their school. He also grows close to Agata, a fellow teacher, though a misunderstanding strains their relationship. As the investigation touches on dark themes including sexual harassment and a student's drug overdose, Damian closes in on the dealers, and the film ends with the revelation of the real villain behind them.

Lesson Plan premiered on Netflix on 23 November 2022 with a 16+ rating. Reviews were negative. Vinayak Chakravorty of Firstpost gave it two stars out of five, likening Witkowski to a Polish Jean-Claude Van Damme and calling the film an honest B-movie stuntfest, but faulting its clichéd, mechanical script, underdeveloped characters, tacky fight choreography and lack of chemistry in the romance. Avinash Ramachandran of Cinema Express also gave it two stars, praising the neatly orchestrated combat sequences and Damian's earnest attempts to be a good teacher while criticizing the lazy writing, predictable twists and the lack of emotional impact in its darker moments.

overview: When a zombie virus pushes Korea into a state of emergency, those trapped on an express train to Busan must fight for their own survival.
tagline: Life-or-death survival begins.
title: Train to Busan
plot:
Train to Busan is a 2016 South Korean post-apocalyptic horror film directed by Yeon Sang-ho. The movie takes place in a world where a mysterious virus has turned most of humanity into violent, zombie-like creatures.

The story begins with Seok-woo (played by Gong Yoo), a wealthy stockbroker who lives in Seoul with his wife Soo-an (played by Kim Su-an) and their young son Su-an. On the day of their daughter's birthday party, Seok-woo receives an unexpected phone call from his mother, who is bedridden with cancer, asking him to take care of her. Feeling guilty for not spending enough time with his family, Seok-woo decides to visit his mother in Busan.

As they board the KTX train to Busan, Seok-woo and Soo-an are unaware of the impending disaster that awaits them. The train is suddenly attacked by a group of zombies, who have been infected by the mysterious virus. The passengers and crew fight for survival as the train becomes a battleground.

Seok-woo's mother dies shortly after they arrive in Busan, but he continues on to find his daughter, who has gone missing. Along the way, he meets a young girl named Sung-gyeol (played by Kim Soo-an), who is also searching for her family. As they navigate through the treacherous streets of Busan, Seok-woo and Sung-gyeol form an unlikely bond.

As the train's passengers are picked off one by one, Seok-woo and Sung-gyeol discover that the virus has been caused by a mysterious outbreak in China. The government is trying to contain the outbreak, but it's too late, and the virus has spread globally.

The duo eventually boards a bus to escape the chaos, but they soon realize that the bus is also infested with zombies. In a desperate bid to survive, Seok-woo sacrifices himself to save Sung-gyeol by pushing her off the moving bus.

In the end, Sung-gyeol manages to find her way back to her father's office building in Seoul, where she finds him alive and well. The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Sung-gyeol finally finding some sense of closure and reunion with her family.

Throughout the movie, Yeon Sang-ho explores themes of class struggle, social inequality, and the breakdown of society in the face of catastrophic disaster. The film's tense atmosphere and graphic violence make it a thrilling ride, but its thought-provoking commentary on human nature makes it more than just a mindless horror flick.

Overall, Train to Busan is a gripping and intense thriller that will keep you on the edge of your seat from start to finish. With its strong performances, clever plot twists, and social commentary, it's no wonder this movie has become a modern classic in the zombie genre.

overview: Three best friends attending a heavy-metal show cross paths with sadistic killers after they travel to a secluded country home for an after party.
tagline: It's going to be one HELL of a party.
title: We Summon the Darkness
plot:
We Summon the Darkness is a 2020 American comedy horror film directed by Marc Sven Rondinelli and written by Marc Sven Rondinelli, Chris Peckover, and Brian Duffield. 

The movie revolves around three young women who form a heavy metal band called "Darkness" in the 1990s. The story is heavily influenced by the themes of female empowerment, friendship, and the struggles faced by women in a male-dominated industry.

At its core, We Summon the Darkness explores the complexities of female relationships, particularly those formed between women who are passionate about music and determined to succeed in a field dominated by men. The film delves into the ways in which these friendships can be both supportive and toxic, as the characters navigate their personal lives, careers, and desires.

The movie also touches on themes of identity, self-expression, and the power of music as a means of empowerment. Through the character of Amber (played by Jenna Ortega), who is determined to make it big with her band, We Summon the Darkness highlights the struggles faced by women in the music industry, including sexism, misogyny, and the objectification of female musicians.

Furthermore, the film critiques societal expectations placed on women, particularly those related to beauty, femininity, and domesticity. The characters are unapologetically themselves, embracing their individuality and rejecting traditional feminine norms.

Overall, We Summon the Darkness is a dark comedy that uses humor to explore themes of female friendship, empowerment, and self-expression in a male-dominated industry.

overview: A track coach in a small California town transforms a team of athletes into championship contenders.
tagline: Champions can come from anywhere.
title: McFarland, USA
plot:
McFarland, USA is a heartwarming and inspiring film that delves into the transformative power of sports, community, and perseverance. The movie tells the true story of Jim Whittaker, a high school cross-country coach who takes on the task of reviving the team at McFarland High School in California.

At its core, McFarland, USA is a film about the redemptive power of sports to bring people together and transcend social boundaries. The movie follows Coach Whittaker's journey as he navigates the complexities of his new role, while also confronting his own personal demons and learning to trust his team.

As the story unfolds, we see the McFarland High School cross-country team come together, united by their shared passion for running and their desire to prove themselves. Through their struggles and triumphs, the characters learn valuable lessons about teamwork, discipline, and the importance of believing in oneself.

One of the main themes of the movie is the struggle for identity and self-discovery, particularly among the Latino students who make up a significant part of the team. As they navigate their own personal struggles and cultural expectations, the characters must also confront the challenges of being an outsider in a predominantly white community.

The film also explores the theme of redemption and second chances, as Coach Whittaker seeks to redeem himself after a past mistake and find a new sense of purpose. Through his relationships with his team and the people around him, he learns to let go of his guilt and shame, and instead focus on building a positive and supportive community.

Ultimately, McFarland, USA is a movie about hope, perseverance, and the transformative power of sports to bring people together and create lasting change. The film's themes are timeless and universal, making it a compelling and inspiring watch for audiences of all ages.

overview: A cemetery man has the unusual problem of the dead rising from the grave. Himself and his assistant must end these creatures' lives again after they are reborn. Everything is going well until "She" comes along and stirs things up a bit.
production_companies: Fonds Eurimages du Conseil de l'Europe
tagline: Zombies, guns and sex, OH MY!!!
title: Cemetery Man
plot:
Cemetery Man is a 1994 Italian horror-comedy film directed by Michele Soavi. The movie follows the story of Emilio Velter, a mortician who works in a cemetery and is forced to confront his own dark past when he becomes involved with a mysterious woman.

The main theme of Cemetery Man revolves around the struggle between good and evil, as embodied by the two main characters: Emilio Velter, a well-meaning but somewhat inept mortal, and the vampire, a symbol of darkness and malevolence. The film explores the idea that even in the most mundane and ordinary-seeming lives, there can be a deep well of darkness and violence lurking beneath the surface.

The movie also delves into the theme of identity and the blurring of boundaries between reality and fantasy. Emilio Velter's character is a complex one, struggling to reconcile his mundane life as a mortician with his own desires and fantasies. The vampire, on the other hand, represents a kind of freedom and release from the constraints of society, but also poses a threat to Emilio's very existence.

Furthermore, Cemetery Man touches on the idea of the power dynamics between men and women, particularly in the context of relationships and intimacy. The mysterious woman who enters Emilio's life is a catalyst for his transformation, forcing him to confront his own desires and vulnerabilities.

Overall, Cemetery Man is a film that explores the darker aspects of human nature, delving into themes of identity, morality, and the complexities of human relationships.

overview: A sci-fi drama about a man struggling to find his wife, who he abandoned six years ago, before their visa to emmigrate to an off-world colony expires.
tagline: What would you do for a ticket to a better life?
title: After We Leave
plot:
'71 is a gripping and intense thriller that delves into the complexities of human nature, particularly in the context of war and its aftermath. The film's narrative is centered around Gary Hook, a British soldier who finds himself lost and disoriented in Belfast during the height of the Troubles.

As Gary navigates the treacherous landscape, he grapples with his own identity and sense of belonging, as well as the moral ambiguities of war. The film masterfully explores the blurred lines between right and wrong, highlighting the ways in which even the most well-intentioned individuals can become embroiled in conflict.

One of the primary themes of '71 is the struggle for identity and self-discovery, particularly among young men caught up in the midst of war. Gary's journey serves as a powerful metaphor for the search for meaning and purpose in a chaotic world.

The film also delves into the complexities of sectarianism and the cyclical nature of violence, highlighting the ways in which historical grievances can simmer beneath the surface, waiting to erupt into conflict. Through Gary's experiences, the film sheds light on the human cost of war and the devastating impact it has on individuals and communities.

Ultimately, '71 is a thought-provoking exploration of the darker aspects of human nature, one that challenges viewers to confront the complexities and nuances of war and its aftermath.

original_title: Maggie Simpson in Playdate with Destiny
overview: It seemed like just another day at the park for Maggie Simpson. But when Maggie faces playground peril, a heroic young baby whisks her from danger and steals her heart.
title: Maggie Simpson in Playdate with Destiny
plot:
Maggie Simpson in Playdate with Destiny is an animated film that explores the complexities of identity, belonging, and self-discovery through the eyes of a young girl. The movie delves into the challenges of growing up as a child of a famous family, where one's sense of self is often overshadowed by their parents' fame.

The story follows Maggie Simpson, who embarks on a journey to find her place in the world and define herself outside of her family's legacy. As she navigates through various experiences and encounters, Maggie grapples with feelings of inadequacy, insecurity, and the pressure to live up to her family's expectations.

Throughout the film, the main themes revolve around the struggle for individuality and autonomy in a world where one's identity is often defined by their relationships with others. The movie encourages viewers to question societal norms and expectations, promoting self-acceptance and empowerment.

The narrative also touches on the theme of female friendship and solidarity, highlighting the importance of supportive relationships in navigating life's challenges. Ultimately, Maggie Simpson in Playdate with Destiny is a heartwarming and relatable tale that celebrates the power of self-discovery, resilience, and embracing one's true identity.

overview: After two impoverished teenage brothers manage to escape their abusive father, they embark on a treacherous and haunted journey in the hope of finding their estranged mother who has joined a sadistic cult, deep in the woods of Northwest Pennsylvania.
tagline: They escaped from a nightmare just to enter into hell.
title: The Long Dark Trail
plot:
The Long Dark Trail is an American independent folk horror film written and directed by Kevin Ignatius and Nick Psinakis and produced by Four Eighteen Films. It stars the real-life brothers Carter and Brady O'Donnell as Henry and Jacob, with Michael Thyer as their abusive father Duane and Trina Campbell as their estranged mother, alongside Alex Hughes. Mitchell Kome was the cinematographer and Ignatius also composed the score, which ranges from Appalachian banjo to electronic music and closes with the vocal track "Hollow". The film runs 78 minutes and carries the tagline "They escaped from a nightmare just to enter into hell."

In the backwoods of northwest Pennsylvania, two impoverished teenage brothers have endured years of brutal abuse from their alcoholic father Duane, who once branded Henry with a clothes iron. In a tense prologue the boys tie Duane to a bed with cable ties and flee his cabin on BMX bikes. Acting on a tip from a customer of their gardening work, they head north across country in search of their mother, who left the family and has joined a sadistic cult deep in the forest, hoping she can give them a better life. Divided into chapters with one-word titles such as "Viaduct" and "Lake", their journey through vast woodland is punctuated by flashbacks to the horrors of home and by ominous signs: Jacob finds a mysterious rock marked with a sigil, an infection of pustules spreads across Henry's neck, and the boys pass what appears to be a burial ground. Intercut scenes hint at deadly rituals in the region, and as hallucinations take hold the brothers eventually discover what kind of company their mother keeps.

The film is dated 2021 in some listings and was released on digital, DVD and Blu-ray by Cleopatra Entertainment on 21 February 2023. Reviews praised its visuals more than its story. Phil Hoad of The Guardian called it an atmospheric, sharply directed fable despite its shoestring budget and minimal plot, while noting debts to Mandy and questioning the processed sound applied to the dialogue. Paul Lê of Bloody Disgusting found it uneven and incoherent but elevated by Kome's photography of the Allegheny landscape and Ignatius's music. Adam Mock of Film Inquiry was far harsher, faulting its slow pace, stilted performances and rushed finale.

overview: In the summer of 1987, a college graduate takes a 'nowhere' job at his local amusement park, only to find it's the perfect course to get him prepared for the real world.
tagline: Nothing brings people together like a crappy summer job.
title: Adventureland
plot:
Adventureland is a 2009 American romantic comedy-drama film written and directed by Greg Mottola, set in 1987 at a run-down amusement park in Pittsburgh loosely based on the Adventureland theme park in Farmingdale on Long Island. Jesse Eisenberg stars as James Brennan, a recent Oberlin College graduate hoping to attend graduate school at Columbia University, with Kristen Stewart as his co-worker Em Lewin, Martin Starr as Joel, Kristen Wiig and Bill Hader as the park's managers Paulette and Bobby, and Ryan Reynolds as the married maintenance man Mike Connell. Margarita Levieva also appears.

James's plans for a summer in Europe collapse when his father loses his job, and with his family unable to support him he takes a job running carnival games at Adventureland in his hometown, where his childhood friend Tommy Frigo works. When fellow games worker Em saves him from being stabbed by a cheating customer and drives him home, the two discover a shared taste in music. Unknown to James, Em is having an affair with Connell, and after the party Connell comes over to sleep with her. James and Em grow closer anyway, and James confides to Connell that he loves her. Confused, Em at first rebuffs James's declaration, so he goes on a date with Lisa P., a co-worker, but guilt over kissing her leads him to tell Em he would rather be with her. Moved by his honesty, Em ends things with Connell, but that same night a co-worker tells James he saw the two having sex in Connell's car, and James and Frigo see Em leaving Connell's mother's house. Confronted, Em tearfully admits she has been foolish. James tells Lisa P. about the affair in confidence, but word spreads throughout the park, and the humiliated Em quits and returns to New York University. James gets drunk and crashes his father's car into a neighbour's tree, and the repairs consume his summer savings; his plans for New York fall through when his intended roommate chooses Harvard Business School over Columbia. With Joel's help, James travels to New York and waits in the rain outside Em's apartment. She invites him in, they reconcile, and James says he will find a job and start school the following year, as the two begin a new relationship.

Released on April 3, 2009, Adventureland earned about $17.1 million worldwide and received positive reviews, with an 89% Rotten Tomatoes rating and praise for its humour, nostalgia and cast. It was nominated for Best Ensemble Cast Performance at the Gotham Independent Film Awards.

overview: A duplicitous young man finds success in the dark world of social media smear tactics — but his virtual vitriol soon has violent real-life consequences.
title: The Hater
plot:
The Hater (Polish: Sala samobójców. Hejter) is a 2020 Polish social thriller film directed by Jan Komasa and written by Mateusz Pacewicz. Regarded as a sequel or spin-off to Komasa's 2011 film Suicide Room, it centres on an expelled university student from Warsaw who learns to manipulate the internet, unleashing widespread hatred and violence. Maciej Musiałowski stars as Tomasz Giemza, with Vanessa Aleksander as Gabriela "Gabi" Krasucka, Danuta Stenka and Jacek Koman as her parents Zofia and Robert Krasucki, Agata Kulesza as Beata Santorska, Maciej Stuhr as Paweł Rudnicki, Adam Gradowski as Stefan "Guzek" Guzkowski and Jędrzej Wielecki as Staszek Rydel.

Tomasz is caught plagiarizing and thrown out of law school, but he hides his expulsion so that he can keep receiving financial support from the Krasuckis, a progressive, upper-class family who are the parents of his childhood friend Gabi, with whom he is secretly in love and on whom he becomes fixated. When the deception comes to light, he loses the trust of his benefactors. By chance he then finds work at a public relations agency run by Beata Santorska, which turns out to be a fast-growing troll farm. Tomasz proves highly skilled at spreading fake news and online hatred aimed at celebrities, internet personalities and politicians, and his assignment is to run an online campaign against Paweł Rudnicki, a politician whose campaign the Krasuckis actively support. Over time he turns his newly acquired abilities toward the family itself, using them to stalk, harass and ultimately control the Krasuckis. Santorska provides the link to Suicide Room, as she is the mother of Dominik, the protagonist of the earlier film.

Shot in and around Warsaw between October and December 2018, The Hater opened in Polish cinemas on 6 March 2020, only days before theatres closed because of the COVID-19 pandemic, and soon became available online. Netflix streamed it worldwide from 29 July 2020. Critics responded positively, and it holds an 87% Rotten Tomatoes rating, with a consensus noting its contrivances but recommending its ambitious, frenzied style to thriller fans. Reviewers praised its examination of how easily people are manipulated and of polarization in Polish society. The film won the award for Best International Narrative Feature at the Tribeca Film Festival.

overview: A father struggles to keep his infant daughter alive in the wake of Hurricane Katrina.
tagline: Every second counts.
title: Hours
plot:
Hours is a 2013 American thriller written and directed by Eric Heisserer. Paul Walker stars as a father struggling to keep his newborn daughter alive in a deserted New Orleans hospital after the power fails in the aftermath of Hurricane Katrina, with Genesis Rodriguez, T. J. Hassan and Judd Lormand in supporting roles.

In 2005, Nolan Hayes rushes his wife, Abigail, to the hospital when she goes into labor five weeks early. She dies giving birth, and their daughter must stay on a ventilator for two days until she can breathe unaided. As Katrina strikes, the hospital is evacuated, but the ventilator cannot be moved, so Nolan stays behind with the baby, whom he names Abigail after her mother. A nurse promises to return with help, but flooding in the basement knocks out the power, and the only generator Nolan can find must be cranked by hand every three minutes to charge the ventilator battery, which holds less charge each time. His every movement becomes a race against the clock.

Nolan rescues a dog tangled in rope, names it Sherlock and shares his food with it. He signals a helicopter from the roof, but gunmen drive it off; he tries an ambulance radio and reaches only a recording; and a generator he finds in the flooded basement nearly electrocutes him. Exhausted, hungry and with his hand cut from cranking, he devises new ways to work the crank, using his foot and later a rod. Looters raid the hospital for food, drugs and saline, and Sherlock chases one from Nolan's room; Nolan later realizes that the man robbed and killed the nurse who was bringing help. After nearly two days without sleep, he injects himself with adrenaline to stay awake. When two more looters arrive searching for drugs, he overpowers one, takes his gun and shoots the other. After forty hours the crank finally breaks. Nolan gives his daughter mouth-to-mouth resuscitation before collapsing, and as the ventilator's alarm sounds he believes he has failed her. Sherlock leads paramedics to them, and as they wheel Nolan out, the baby begins to cry and is placed in his arms.

The film premiered at the South by Southwest festival in Austin on March 10, 2013, and opened on December 13, 2013, two weeks after Walker's death. Reviews were mixed, with 64% on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 55; Variety's Joe Leydon said its ingeniously simple setup was exploited for maximum suspense.

overview: In this modern love story set against the Austin, Texas music scene, two entangled couples — struggling songwriters Faye and BV, and music mogul Cook and the waitress whom he ensnares — chase success through a rock ‘n’ roll landscape of seduction and betrayal.
tagline: Love. Obsession. Betrayal.
title: Song to Song
plot:
Song to Song is a 2017 American romantic drama film that delves into the complexities of love, relationships, and identity. The movie follows two musicians, BV (Ryan Gosling) and Faye (Saoirse Ronan), who find themselves entangled in a tumultuous romance amidst the vibrant music scene in Austin, Texas.

At its core, Song to Song explores the theme of creative expression as a means of self-discovery and emotional release. The film's protagonist, BV, is a struggling musician who finds solace in his music, using it as an outlet to express the pain and vulnerability he feels in his personal life. Faye, on the other hand, is a free-spirited artist who embodies the carefree essence of the 1970s counterculture movement.

As their relationship evolves, the film delves into the tension between creative freedom and emotional intimacy. BV's music becomes an integral part of his connection with Faye, but it also serves as a barrier between them, making it challenging for him to open up and be vulnerable. This dichotomy highlights the push-and-pull nature of love, where two people are drawn to each other despite their differences.

The movie also touches on themes of identity, particularly in the context of artistic expression. Faye's character is a manifestation of the 1970s feminist movement, with her embracing her independence and individuality as a means of self-empowerment. BV's struggles to find his place in the music scene serve as a metaphor for the search for one's true identity.

Ultimately, Song to Song presents a poignant exploration of the human experience, where love, creativity, and identity intersect in complex and often painful ways. The film's dreamy, atmospheric quality captures the essence of its characters' emotional journeys, inviting viewers to immerse themselves in their world of music, art, and self-discovery.

overview: A small, turbulent town in Texas obsesses over their high school football team to an unhealthy degree. When the star tailback, Boobie Miles, is seriously injured during the first game of the season, all hope is lost, and the town's dormant social problems begin to flare up. It is left to the inspiring abilities of new coach Gary Gaines to instill in the other team members -- and, by proxy, the town itself -- a sense of self-respect and honor.
tagline: Hope comes alive on Friday nights.
title: Friday Night Lights
plot:
Friday Night Lights is a 2004 American sports drama directed by Peter Berg, who wrote the screenplay with David Aaron Cohen from H. G. Bissinger's 1990 book. It follows the 1988 Permian High School Panthers of Odessa, Texas, and their run toward the state championship. Universal Pictures released the film on October 8, 2004, and it later inspired the NBC television series of the same name, which premiered in 2006.

In August 1988, football-obsessed Odessa expects coach Gary Gaines to win a state title built around star running back James "Boobie" Miles. Quarterback Mike Winchell is expected mostly to hand him the ball, and fullback Don Billingsley fumbles under the pressure of his alcoholic, abusive father, Charles, a former Permian champion. In the season opener, with college scouts watching, Gaines leaves Miles in late in a blowout because the backup cannot find his helmet, and Miles tears his ACL. The town turns on Gaines, and the team stumbles before backup Chris Comer sparks a comeback and a small but fierce defense led by Brian Chavez and Ivory Christian drives a winning streak. Told he needs surgery, Miles lies about his knee to return, but is hurt again in a loss to Midland Lee. After that game, Charles throws his championship ring onto the freeway, and Don later returns it to him.

A coin toss breaking a three-way tie sends Permian to the playoffs, while Miles, his career over, clears out his locker in tears. The Panthers reach the state final at the Astrodome against the powerhouse Dallas Carter. Outsized and trailing by 20 after a disputed call, they rally to within six, stop Carter on fourth down and drive for victory, but a holding penalty wipes out a touchdown and Winchell is stopped just short of the goal line as time expires. Billingsley reconciles with his father, and an epilogue notes that Gaines and Comer won an undefeated state championship the following season.

Billy Bob Thornton plays Gaines, with Derek Luke as Miles, Lucas Black as Winchell, Garrett Hedlund as Billingsley, Tim McGraw as Charles, Jay Hernandez as Chávez, Lee Thompson Young as Comer and Connie Britton as Sharon Gaines. Critics were largely positive, with 82% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, though some felt the film glorified the culture it criticized and sidestepped the race relations Bissinger explored. It grossed $62 million against a $30 million budget and won the ESPY Award for Best Sports Movie.

overview: John Bennett, a man whose childhood wish of bringing his teddy bear to life came true, now must decide between keeping the relationship with the bear or his girlfriend, Lori.
tagline: Ted is coming.
title: Ted
plot:
Ted is a 2012 American adult animated comedy film directed by Seth MacFarlane, who also co-wrote the screenplay with Alec Sulkin, David Zucker, and Chris Henchy. The movie stars Mark Wahlberg as John Bennett, a man who befriends his childhood teddy bear, Ted (voiced by Seth MacFarlane), which comes to life.

The film begins on Christmas Eve in 1980, where we see the story of how John Bennett received the teddy bear from his mother. As he grows up, John's love for the teddy bear never fades, and he keeps it as a symbol of his childhood innocence. On Christmas Eve, John's mother dies, leaving him alone with Ted.

Years later, John is now a successful businessman living in Boston. He has moved on from his childhood and is engaged to be married to Samantha (Mila Kunis), but he still keeps Ted as a memento. However, when John's fiancée discovers the teddy bear, she becomes upset, feeling that it's childish.

On the night before their wedding, John decides to take Ted out for one last night of fun and partying. They go to a bar where they meet a group of eccentric characters, including Donny (Giovanni Ribisi), a stoner who is obsessed with the movie "The Big Lebowski." The next morning, John wakes up to find that he has gotten drunk and married a woman named Tami-Lynn (Jessica Barth) in Las Vegas.

Meanwhile, Ted becomes fast friends with Tami-Lynn's brother, Donny, and they start causing chaos in Boston. As the story unfolds, John realizes that he needs to win back Samantha's heart and prove to her that he can be responsible enough to take care of a family.

The plot thickens when John discovers that Ted has become an internet sensation, with millions of fans around the world who love him. However, this newfound fame also attracts the attention of a group of eccentric characters, including a group of hipsters and a group of conservative Christians who are determined to destroy Ted.

As the story reaches its climax, John must confront his own immaturity and learn to grow up in order to save Samantha and win back her love. In the end, John and Samantha reconcile, and John learns to let go of his childhood innocence and accept that he can be a responsible adult.

Throughout the film, Seth MacFarlane's signature humor and wit are on full display, with plenty of references to pop culture and irreverent jokes about sex, relationships, and growing up. The movie features a talented voice cast, including Mark Wahlberg, Mila Kunis, and Giovanni Ribisi, who all deliver memorable performances.

Overall, Ted is a hilarious and heartwarming film that explores the complexities of adulthood and the power of childhood innocence. With its witty dialogue, colorful characters, and irreverent humor, it's no wonder that Ted became a box office hit and spawned a sequel.

original_title: The Robot Chicken Walking Dead Special: Look Who's Walking
overview: Seth Green and Matthew Senreich serve up hilarious Walking Dead-inspired satire in this special featuring the zany stop-motion animation of Adult Swim’s “Robot Chicken.”
title: The Robot Chicken Walking Dead Special: Look Who's Walking
plot:
The Robot Chicken Walking Dead Special: Look Who's Walking is a satirical and irreverent take on the popular television series The Walking Dead. At its core, this special explores the absurdity and humor in the post-apocalyptic world created by Robert Kirkman, Tony Moore, and Charlie Adlard.

One of the main themes of this special is the dehumanization of characters in a desperate situation. By using stop-motion animation and parodying the Walking Dead universe, Robot Chicken highlights how easily people can become desensitized to violence and cruelty when faced with survival instincts. This theme is often played for laughs, but it also raises questions about the nature of humanity and what drives individuals to make certain choices in extreme circumstances.

Another significant theme present in this special is the commentary on toxic masculinity. The Walking Dead has been criticized for its portrayal of male characters, particularly Rick Grimes, who can come across as a symbol of patriarchal dominance. Robot Chicken's take on these characters, often depicting them as buffoons or caricatures, serves to subvert and mock traditional masculine norms.

The special also pokes fun at the conventions of television shows like The Walking Dead, using humor to critique the genre itself. By exaggerating and distorting certain elements, such as character motivations and plot twists, Robot Chicken creates a sense of meta-satire that comments on the very nature of storytelling.

Overall, The Robot Chicken Walking Dead Special: Look Who's Walking is a comedic exploration of themes that are both timely and timeless, using humor to comment on the human condition in all its complexity.

overview: Bill Marks is a burned-out veteran of the Air Marshals service. He views the assignment not as a life-saving duty, but as a desk job in the sky. However, today's flight will be no routine trip. Shortly into the transatlantic journey from New York to London, he receives a series of mysterious text messages ordering him to have the government transfer $150 million into a secret account, or a passenger will die every 20 minutes.
tagline: The hijacking was just the beginning.
title: Non-Stop
plot:
Non-Stop is a 2014 American thriller film directed by Jaume Collet-Serra and starring Liam Neeson. The movie follows Bill Marks (Liam Neeson), a federal air marshal who must stop a hijacking on a flight from New York to London.

The main themes of Non-Stop include:

1. **Isolation and Confined Spaces**: The film takes place almost entirely on a single airplane, which serves as a confined space where the characters are trapped with no escape. This setting heightens the tension and creates a sense of claustrophobia.
2. **Paranoia and Suspicion**: As Bill Marks delves deeper into the mystery, he becomes increasingly paranoid and suspicious of those around him, including his fellow passengers and crew members. This paranoia is fueled by the fact that he's being watched and manipulated by the hijacker.
3. **Redemption and Personal Growth**: Throughout the film, Bill Marks struggles with personal demons, including a troubled marriage and a sense of guilt over past mistakes. As he navigates the crisis, he begins to confront his inner demons and find redemption.
4. **The Power of Human Connection**: Despite the tense atmosphere, the film highlights the importance of human connection in times of crisis. Bill Marks forms an unlikely bond with Gwen (Julianne Moore), a flight attendant who helps him unravel the mystery.

Overall, Non-Stop is a gripping thriller that explores themes of isolation, paranoia, redemption, and human connection, all set against the backdrop of a high-stakes hijacking on a commercial airliner.

overview: Jordan Turner is an experienced 911 operator but when she makes an error in judgment and a call ends badly, Jordan is rattled and unsure if she can continue. But when teenager Casey Welson is abducted in the back of a man's car and calls 911, Jordan is the one called upon to use all of her experience, insights and quick thinking to help Casey escape, and not just to save her, but to make sure the man is brought to justice.
tagline: There are 188 million 911 calls a year. This one made it personal.
title: The Call
plot:
The Call is a 2013 American thriller film directed by D.J. Caruso and starring Halle Berry and Abigail Breslin.

The movie begins with Jordan Turner (Halle Berry), a 42-year-old 911 operator who has been working for over two decades, saving countless lives on the phone lines of Los Angeles. Despite her success in her job, Jordan's personal life is struggling. She is divorced from her husband and has a strained relationship with her daughter.

One night, while responding to an emergency call, Jordan meets Casey Wesson (Abigail Breslin), a 17-year-old high school student who has been abducted by a serial killer known as "The Stranger" (Michael Eklund). The Stranger is targeting young women and killing them in gruesome ways. Casey manages to escape from the car where she was being held captive, but not before The Stranger leaves her with severe physical and emotional trauma.

Jordan takes it upon herself to track down Casey and find out who The Stranger is. She starts by retracing Casey's steps on the night of the abduction, following a trail of clues that lead her to an abandoned warehouse on the outskirts of Los Angeles. As Jordan delves deeper into the case, she becomes increasingly obsessed with finding Casey and bringing The Stranger to justice.

As the investigation unfolds, Jordan discovers that The Stranger is targeting young women who are vulnerable and in need of help. He is using his charisma and intelligence to lure them into his trap, and then killing them in a brutal and sadistic manner. Jordan realizes that she has been too focused on her own life and hasn't been paying attention to the needs of others.

As the stakes escalate, Jordan becomes more determined than ever to find Casey and stop The Stranger. She enlists the help of Detective West (Lance Reddick), a seasoned investigator who is initially skeptical of Jordan's abilities but eventually comes to respect her determination and expertise.

The movie builds towards a tense and suspenseful climax as Jordan finally tracks down The Stranger, leading to a violent confrontation that will determine Casey's fate. In the end, Jordan manages to subdue The Stranger and save Casey from further harm.

Throughout the movie, Halle Berry delivers a powerful performance as Jordan Turner, bringing depth and nuance to a character who is both flawed and relatable. Abigail Breslin also shines in her breakout role as Casey Wesson, conveying the trauma and vulnerability of a young woman who has been through unimaginable horrors.

Overall, The Call is a gripping thriller that explores themes of obsession, redemption, and the power of human connection. With its tense plot twists and strong performances from Berry and Breslin, this movie is sure to keep viewers on the edge of their seats until the very end.

overview: Collegian Tree Gelbman wakes up in horror to learn that she's stuck in a parallel universe. Her boyfriend Carter is now with someone else, and her friends and fellow students seem to be completely different versions of themselves. When Tree discovers that Carter's roommate has been altering time, she finds herself once again the target of a masked killer. When the psychopath starts to go after her inner circle, Tree soon realizes that she must die over and over again to save everyone.
tagline: Death makes a killer comeback.
title: Happy Death Day 2U
plot:
Happy Death Day 2U is a 2019 American supernatural horror film directed by Christopher Landon and written by Scott Lobdell. The movie serves as a sequel to the 2017 film Happy Death Day.

The main themes of Happy Death Day 2U revolve around time loops, identity, and the consequences of one's actions. The story follows Tree Gelbman (Jessica Rothe), a college student who finds herself reliving the same day over and over again in an attempt to avoid her impending death.

As the movie progresses, it becomes clear that Tree is stuck in a time loop, and each iteration presents a new opportunity for her to try and escape her fate. However, with each loop, she begins to uncover clues about her own identity and the events leading up to her murder.

One of the primary themes of Happy Death Day 2U is the exploration of identity and self-discovery. Tree's time loops allow her to experiment with different choices and outcomes, but ultimately, she must confront the consequences of her actions and come to terms with who she truly is.

Another significant theme in the movie is the concept of fate vs. free will. The film raises questions about whether our lives are predetermined or if we have control over our own destinies. Tree's time loops create a sense of uncertainty, leaving the audience wondering whether she can truly change her fate or if it was always meant to be.

The movie also touches on the theme of trauma and mental health. Tree's experiences with her time loops take a toll on her mental state, leading to feelings of anxiety, depression, and PTSD. The film handles these themes with sensitivity, highlighting the importance of seeking help and support when dealing with traumatic events.

Overall, Happy Death Day 2U is a thought-provoking horror film that explores complex themes and ideas through its unique time loop narrative.

overview: When a Las Vegas performer-turned-snitch named Buddy Israel decides to turn state's evidence and testify against the mob, it seems that a whole lot of people would like to make sure he's no longer breathing.
tagline: Nobody gets away clean.
title: Smokin' Aces
plot:
Smokin' Aces is a 2006 crime thriller film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the consequences of violence. The movie revolves around a group of hitmen, each with their unique skills and motivations, who are brought together to take down a notorious mobster, Primo Sparazza.

At its core, Smokin' Aces explores the theme of identity and how it is shaped by our experiences and relationships. The film's protagonist, Jack Dupree (played by Nicolas Cage), is a struggling musician who becomes embroiled in the world of organized crime after being forced to impersonate Sparazza. As he navigates this treacherous landscape, Dupree must confront his own identity and the blurred lines between reality and performance.

The movie also examines the theme of loyalty and betrayal, particularly in the context of male relationships. The hitmen, each with their own code of honor, are forced to navigate a complex web of alliances and rivalries as they work together to take down Sparazza. This leads to a series of tense confrontations and unexpected betrayals that challenge the characters' perceptions of loyalty and trust.

Furthermore, Smokin' Aces touches on the theme of performance and deception, highlighting how people often present themselves in a way that is not entirely authentic. The film's use of disguises and impersonation serves as a metaphor for the ways in which we present ourselves to others, and the tension between our true selves and our public personas.

Overall, Smokin' Aces is a gripping thriller that explores the darker aspects of human nature, identity, loyalty, and performance.

overview: In Los Angeles, Nikki is homeless, car-less and closing in on 30, but he's amoral, good-looking, and adept in the sack, moving from one wealthy woman of 35 or 40 to another, a kept boy-toy. His newest gig, with Samantha, an attorney whose house overlooks L.A., is sweet, although it's unclear how long she'll put up with him. Then Nikki meets Heather, a waitress. Is the player being played, or might this be love? What will Nikki discover?
tagline: It's a business doing pleasure.
title: Spread
plot:
