Spread is a 2009 American comedy film directed by James Washington and written by James Washington and David Gordon Green. The movie stars Ashton Kutcher, Margarita Levieva, and Natasha Lyonne.

The story revolves around Nick (Ashton Kutcher), a young man who has just been dumped by his girlfriend, Amanda (Margarita Levieva). Feeling down and lonely, Nick decides to attend a singles party in Los Angeles. At the party, he meets a beautiful woman named Samantha (Natalie Portman) at a bar, but she leaves before they can talk.

The next day, Nick wakes up with a mysterious tattoo on his backside, which reads "Samantha". He soon discovers that he has been tattooed by Samantha after a wild night together. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Nick and Samantha had an intense and passionate encounter, but their relationship is complicated.

Nick's life begins to spiral out of control as he tries to navigate his feelings for Samantha. He starts to experience strange and unexplained events, including finding himself in various locations around Los Angeles with no memory of how he got there. The tattoo on his backside becomes a recurring motif throughout the film, symbolizing Nick's connection to Samantha.

As Nick delves deeper into his relationship with Samantha, he discovers that she is a free-spirited artist who lives life on her own terms. He begins to question his own identity and sense of purpose, feeling like he is stuck in a rut. Through a series of misadventures and encounters with various characters, including a eccentric tattoo artist (Christopher Walken), Nick slowly starts to come to terms with his feelings for Samantha.

Throughout the film, the tone shifts between humor and drama, as Nick navigates the ups and downs of his relationship with Samantha. The movie features a mix of witty dialogue, quirky characters, and offbeat humor, which adds to its charm.

Ultimately, the film builds towards a climactic confrontation between Nick and Samantha, as they both try to make sense of their complicated feelings for each other. In the end, Nick comes to realize that he has been given a second chance with Samantha, and he must decide whether to take it or let her go.

Overall, Spread is a quirky and offbeat romantic comedy that explores themes of identity, relationships, and self-discovery. With its unique blend of humor and drama, the film offers a fresh take on the traditional rom-com genre.

overview: Returning home with his father after a shopping expedition, Wong Fei-Hong is unwittingly caught up in the battle between foreigners who wish to export ancient Chinese artifacts and loyalists who don't want the pieces to leave the country. Fei-Hong must fight against the foreigners using his Drunken Boxing style, and overcome his father's antagonism as well.
tagline: He's got a secret weapon with a lot of kick.
title: The Legend of Drunken Master
plot:
The Legend of Drunken Master is a 1994 Hong Kong martial arts film directed by Yuen Woo-ping, starring Jet Li and Rosamund Kwan. The movie is an adaptation of the classic Chinese novel "Wudang Meihua" (also known as "The Legend of Drunken Master") written by Shi Xianggu.

**Beginning:**
The story begins with Wong Fei-hung (played by Jet Li), a young orphan who lives in the Wudang Mountains. Wong is trained by his uncle, a renowned martial artist and healer, to master the art of traditional Chinese medicine and martial arts. However, Wong's life takes a dramatic turn when he meets a mysterious woman named Yu Shu Lien (played by Rosamund Kwan), who becomes his love interest.

**Plot Development:**
The movie follows Wong Fei-hung as he faces various challenges and adversaries in the Wudang Mountains. He must confront the evil General Huo (played by Takeshi Kaneshiro), a ruthless warlord who seeks to destroy the Wudang Mountains and its people. Along the way, Wong discovers his unique fighting style, known as "drunken boxing," which allows him to harness the power of wine to defeat his enemies.

As Wong navigates the treacherous landscape of the Wudang Mountains, he must also contend with his own personal demons, including a tragic past and a complicated relationship with Yu Shu Lien. Through a series of intense battles and dramatic showdowns, Wong proves himself to be a formidable warrior and a true master of the "drunken boxing" style.

**Ending:**
The movie culminates in an epic battle between Wong Fei-hung and General Huo, which takes place at the Wudang Mountains' famous Drunken Master Temple. In the end, Wong emerges victorious, having defeated his arch-nemesis and saved the Wudang Mountains from destruction.

Throughout the film, Yuen Woo-ping's direction and Jet Li's performance bring to life a thrilling and action-packed adventure that blends stunning martial arts sequences with poignant drama and romance. The Legend of Drunken Master has become a beloved classic in Hong Kong cinema, celebrated for its innovative fight choreography, memorable characters, and timeless themes of honor, loyalty, and self-discovery.

Overall, The Legend of Drunken Master is an unforgettable cinematic experience that showcases the artistry and athleticism of Jet Li, as well as the rich cultural heritage of Chinese martial arts.

overview: Ellie tries to mend her marriage with her husband Marcus after a brief encounter with an old friend, David, only to find that David is more dangerous and unstable than she'd realized.
title: Fatal Affair
plot:
Fatal Affair is a 2020 American psychological thriller directed by Peter Sullivan, who wrote the screenplay with Rasheeda Garner. It stars Nia Long, Omar Epps, Stephen Bishop and KJ Smith, and was produced by Hybrid Films for Netflix, with Long among its producers.

Ellie Warren, an attorney, has moved from San Francisco to a new house on the coast with her husband, Marcus, who is recovering from being struck by a hit-and-run driver while cycling, after their daughter, Brittany, left for college. At work Ellie meets her firm's new technology consultant, David Hammond, whom she has not seen since college twenty years earlier. She does not know that David is in anger management therapy following an incident involving a woman named Deborah. Drinks between them turn sexual in a club bathroom before Ellie stops it. David then begins stalking her with calls and texts, watching and breaking into her house, hacking her security system and dating her friend Courtney, who dismisses Ellie's warnings. Ellie tells neither Marcus nor the police.

From an old classmate, Ellie learns that David was suspected, though never charged, of murdering his ex-wife, Deborah, and her new boyfriend. He deletes an e-mail Ellie sends Courtney about the case, and Ellie is horrified to find him golfing with Marcus. In David's apartment she discovers photos of Deborah and of herself on his computer, and when she warns Courtney, David attacks her friend. With the police hunting him, David fakes his suicide by murdering a homeless man and leaving the burned body in his place, along with a note confessing his crimes. One night a message summons Ellie to the office, where she finds her assistant murdered. Racing home, she calls the police and finds David waiting; she knocks him out with a vase but chooses not to kill him, then discovers the body of Brittany's boyfriend, Scott, and frees Marcus and Brittany. David kills the lone police officer who responds, and as Brittany escapes by car, he fights Ellie and Marcus. Ellie stabs him, and after he seizes the officer's gun, Marcus intervenes and David falls to his death from a seaside cliff. Months later Brittany returns to school, and the Warrens put their new house up for sale.

Netflix released the film on July 16, 2020, and it was the platform's most-streamed film that weekend. Critics panned it, giving it 19% on Rotten Tomatoes and 34 on Metacritic.

overview: Austin's hottest DJ, Jungle Julia, sets out into the night to unwind with her two friends Shanna and Arlene. Covertly tracking their moves is Stuntman Mike, a scarred rebel leering from behind the wheel of his muscle car, revving just feet away.
tagline: A crash course in revenge
title: Death Proof
plot:
Death Proof is a 2007 American exploitation thriller film written and directed by Quentin Tarantino. The film stars Kurt Russell as Stuntman Mike, a psychopathic stunt driver who targets young women.

The film begins with a series of vignettes showcasing five young women - Zoë Bell, Rosario Dawson, Jordan Prentice, Vanessa Ferlito, and Sheri Moon Zombie - who are all involved in the adult film industry. The women are shown to be independent, confident, and strong-willed individuals who are not afraid to speak their minds.

As the story progresses, Stuntman Mike is introduced as a charismatic and skilled stunt driver who works for a local television show called "Stuntman Mike's Stunts." However, it becomes clear that Mike has a dark secret: he is a serial killer who targets young women on the road.

Mike's modus operandi is to pick up unsuspecting women in his car, which is equipped with a hidden compartment containing various sex toys and other objects. He then proceeds to drive them to isolated areas, where he subjects them to a series of gruesome and violent attacks.

The film's plot thickens as the five women from the beginning of the film begin to cross paths with Stuntman Mike. The women are initially unaware of Mike's true nature, but they soon realize that they are in grave danger.

As the story unfolds, the women band together to try and escape Mike's clutches. Along the way, they encounter a variety of characters who aid or hinder their progress. One such character is Lee (Kurt Russell), a stunt driver who becomes embroiled in the women's quest for survival.

Throughout the film, Tarantino pays homage to the exploitation films of the 1970s, particularly those directed by Sam Peckinpah and Russ Meyer. The film's graphic violence, sex scenes, and over-the-top performances are all nods to these classic exploitation films.

In the end, the women manage to outsmart Stuntman Mike and bring him to justice. However, not before he has subjected them to a series of brutal and violent attacks.

The film ends with a sense of closure for the five women, who have emerged from their traumatic experiences as stronger and more resilient individuals. The final shot is of Lee (Kurt Russell), who is shown to be driving away from the carnage, leaving the audience to wonder if he will become the next Stuntman Mike.

Overall, Death Proof is a tense and thrilling film that pays homage to the exploitation films of the 1970s while also offering something new and unique. The film's graphic violence, sex scenes, and over-the-top performances make it a must-see for fans of exploitation cinema.

overview: Sending shock waves through the Mexican film industry and the world, this blistering feature debut from Alejandro G. Iñárritu brought the director’s electrifying visual style and bravura multistrand storytelling to the screen with the heart-stopping impact of a primal scream. In Mexico City, the lives of three strangers—a young man mixed up in the gritty underworld of dogfighting, a glamorous woman who seems to have it all, and a mysterious assassin who is desperate to reconnect with his estranged daughter—collide in a tragic twist of fate that forever alters their personal journeys. A tour de force of violence and emotion captured in a rush of kinetic handheld camera work, Amores perros is an unforgettable plunge into a world of brutality and aching, interconnected humanity.
tagline: Love. Betrayal. Death.
title: Amores Perros
plot:
Amores perros is a 2000 Mexican psychological drama produced and directed by Alejandro González Iñárritu in his feature debut and written by Guillermo Arriaga from a story by both men. The first part of Iñárritu's "Trilogy of Death", followed by 21 Grams and Babel, it uses a multi-narrative structure and an ensemble cast including Emilio Echevarría, Gael García Bernal, Goya Toledo, Álvaro Guerrero and Vanessa Bauche. Its three stories are linked by a car crash in Mexico City.

In the first story, young Octavio loves Susana, the wife of his abusive brother, Ramiro, and urges her to run away with him when she becomes pregnant again. After his rottweiler, Cofi, kills a fighting dog belonging to the local thug Jarocho, Octavio and his friend Jorge enter the dogfighting scene. Octavio saves enough to flee with Susana and pays to have Ramiro beaten, but Ramiro steals the money and leaves with her. In a private fight, Jarocho shoots Cofi, and Octavio stabs him. Chased by Jarocho's men, Octavio crashes his car; Jorge is killed and Octavio badly hurt.

In the second story, magazine publisher Daniel leaves his family for his lover, Valeria, a Spanish supermodel. On the day they move in together, her leg is shattered in Octavio's crash, ending her modeling career. While she recovers, her dog Richie disappears beneath a broken floorboard. Valeria reinjures her leg trying to reach the dog, gangrene sets in and the leg is amputated. Daniel finally rescues Richie, and Valeria returns to find that her billboard outside the window has been taken down.

In the third, a homeless man glimpsed earlier is revealed as El Chivo, a hitman and former teacher jailed for guerrilla terrorism, who longs to reach Maru, the daughter he abandoned. Witnessing the crash during a job, he takes Octavio's money and nurses the wounded Cofi, who later kills El Chivo's other dogs; he cannot bring himself to kill it. Ramiro dies in a bank robbery, and at the funeral Susana rejects Octavio again; he waits for her in vain at a bus station. Learning that his client and target are half-brothers, El Chivo leaves them chained within reach of a pistol, leaves money and a message for Maru, sells the client's car and walks off with the dog, now named Negro.

The film premiered at the 2000 Cannes Film Festival and opened in Mexico on June 16, 2000. A commercial and critical success, it won the Ariel Award for Best Picture and was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film.

overview: Against formidable odds -- and an old-school diving instructor embittered by the U.S. Navy's new, less prejudicial policies -- Carl Brashear sets his sights on becoming the Navy's first African-American master diver in this uplifting true story. Their relationship starts out on the rocks, but fate ultimately conspires to bring the men together into a setting of mutual respect, triumph and honor.
tagline: History is made by those who break the rules.
title: Men of Honor
plot:
Men of Honor is a biographical drama film directed by George Tillman Jr., released in 2000 by Fox 2000 Pictures.

The movie tells the story of Carl Brashear, a African-American master diver and sailor in the United States Navy during the Cold War era. The film stars Robert De Niro as Master Chief Petty Officer Carl Brashear, a decorated war hero who lost his leg while saving the life of a fellow crew member during a training exercise.

The movie begins with Carl's childhood, where he grows up in a poor African-American neighborhood in New Orleans. Despite facing racism and poverty, Carl finds solace in the Navy, enlisting at the age of 16. He quickly proves himself to be an exceptional diver and sailor, earning the respect of his peers and superiors.

As Carl rises through the ranks, he faces numerous challenges, including racism and sexism within the Navy. Despite these obstacles, he perseveres, becoming one of the first African-American divers in the Navy's elite SEAL team. However, during a training exercise, Carl suffers a severe injury when he is struck by a piece of metal while saving his fellow diver, Eddie "Papa" Johnson (played by Cuba Gooding Jr.).

The movie follows Carl's journey as he undergoes multiple surgeries and rehabilitation to regain his mobility. Despite the odds against him, Carl refuses to give up on his dreams, becoming one of the first amputees to attend the Navy's diving school.

As Carl navigates his recovery, he also faces personal struggles, including a troubled relationship with his son, who feels ashamed of his father's disability. However, with the support of his family and fellow sailors, Carl perseveres, eventually earning his place as a master diver and sailor in the Navy.

The movie culminates with Carl's final mission, where he leads a team of divers on a secret operation to recover a lost nuclear submarine. Despite facing numerous challenges, including treacherous terrain and hostile enemy forces, Carl proves himself to be an exceptional leader and diver, earning his place as one of the most decorated sailors in Navy history.

Throughout the movie, Robert De Niro delivers a powerful performance as Carl Brashear, bringing depth and nuance to the character. The film's supporting cast, including Cuba Gooding Jr., Jon Voight, and Michael Rapaport, also deliver strong performances that add to the movie's emotional impact.

Overall, Men of Honor is a powerful and inspiring film that tells the true story of Carl Brashear, an African-American hero who defied the odds to achieve greatness despite facing racism, sexism, and personal tragedy. The movie's themes of perseverance, courage, and redemption make it a must-see for anyone interested in biographical dramas or inspirational stories.

overview: A game warden moves his family to Lake Placid, once the site of deadly crocodile attacks. Locals assure him the crocs are gone, but his mischievous young son finds a few baby crocs and begins feeding them. They quickly grow into very big adults and start attacking the game warden's family and nearby town.
tagline: Don't forget you're lunch.
title: Lake Placid 3
plot:
Lake Placid 3 is an action-adventure horror film that revolves around the theme of survival and the struggle for power in a remote wilderness setting. The movie takes place on a private island, where a group of people are trapped with a deadly creature, the giant crocodile, and must fight to stay alive.

The main character, Heather, played by Sarah Lind, is a strong-willed and determined individual who finds herself at the center of the chaos. As she navigates the treacherous terrain and confronts the monstrous creature, she also uncovers dark secrets about the island's past and the true nature of her own presence there.

Throughout the film, the theme of survival is explored in depth, as the characters are forced to rely on their wits, resourcefulness, and determination to outsmart the crocodile and escape the island. The movie also touches on the idea of isolation and how it can bring out both the best and worst in people.

The film's use of the wilderness setting adds to the sense of tension and danger, as the characters are forced to confront their own mortality and the powerlessness of human existence in the face of nature's fury. Overall, Lake Placid 3 is a thrilling and suspenseful ride that explores themes of survival, power struggles, and the human condition in a remote and unforgiving environment.

overview: Following a ridiculously awful flight that leads to his pet's death, Nashawn Wade files a lawsuit against the airline, and wins a multimillion-dollar settlement. Determined to create a better flying experience, Nashawn starts his own airline, one that caters to an African-American clientele. Going into business with a tricked-out plane piloted by the smooth Capt. Mack, the airline hits a snag when it has to deal with the family of Elvis Hunkee.
tagline: Announcing the arrival of the first airline with soul.
title: Soul Plane
plot:
Soul Plane is a 2004 American comedy film directed by Jessy Terrero and written by Terrero and Damien Dante Wayans. The movie follows a group of eccentric passengers on a commercial airliner, which is being chartered for a spiritual journey to the afterlife.

The main themes of Soul Plane include:

1. Social commentary: The film uses satire to poke fun at various aspects of American society, including racism, classism, and cultural differences.
2. Identity: Many characters in the movie struggle with their own identities, whether it's a rapper trying to find his place in the world or a group of wealthy passengers who are more concerned with their material possessions than their spiritual well-being.
3. Redemption: Throughout the film, various characters undergo a journey of self-discovery and redemption, often through humorous and unexpected means.
4. Cultural clashes: The movie explores the tensions between different cultural groups, including African Americans, Caucasians, and Asians, highlighting the absurdities and misunderstandings that can arise from these interactions.

The plot development of Soul Plane is driven by the misadventures of its characters as they navigate their way through the spiritual journey, often with hilarious results. The ending of the film features a heartwarming moment of redemption for many of the characters, as they come to accept themselves and find peace on their journey to the afterlife.

Overall, Soul Plane is a comedy that uses satire and social commentary to explore themes of identity, redemption, and cultural clashes in an entertaining and humorous way.

overview: Red, Chuck, Bomb and the rest of their feathered friends are surprised when a green pig suggests that they put aside their differences and unite to fight a common threat. Aggressive birds from an island covered in ice are planning to use an elaborate weapon to destroy the fowl and swine.
tagline: Frenemies Unite
title: The Angry Birds Movie 2
plot:
The Angry Birds Movie 2 is a 2019 animated comedy-adventure film directed by Fergal Reilly and Peter Burnham, produced by Columbia Pictures. The movie takes place after the events of the first film and follows the main characters as they face new challenges.

The story begins with the birds returning to their island home, where they are greeted as heroes for saving the world from the evil pigs. However, the peace is short-lived, as a new threat emerges in the form of a group of birds known as the "Guardians," who possess magical powers and claim that the birds' actions have disrupted the balance of nature.

The main character, Red (voiced by Jason Sudeikis), sets out on a journey to find the Guardians and learn more about their abilities. Along the way, he meets a new bird named Guy Diamond (voiced by Danny McBride), who becomes his ally in this quest.

As Red delves deeper into the world of magic, he discovers that the Guardians are being hunted by a group of ruthless birds known as the "Nerds," who seek to exploit their powers for their own gain. The Nerds are led by a character named King Sleazy (voiced by Bill Hader), a power-hungry bird with a penchant for manipulation.

Red and Guy Diamond soon find themselves in a battle against the Nerds, with the fate of the world hanging in the balance. Along the way, they meet new characters, including a wise old owl named Professor Oakley (voiced by Josh Gad) and a group of birds known as the "Guardians," who possess magical powers.

As the story unfolds, Red learns more about his own destiny and the true nature of the Guardians' powers. He also discovers that the Nerds are not the only threat to the world, but rather a symptom of a larger problem.

In the end, Red and his friends must band together to defeat the Nerds and restore balance to the natural world. The movie features plenty of action, humor, and heart, as the characters navigate their relationships and confront their fears.

Throughout the film, the animation is vibrant and colorful, with stunning visuals that bring the world of Angry Birds to life. The voice cast delivers strong performances, bringing depth and nuance to the characters.

Overall, The Angry Birds Movie 2 is a fun and entertaining film that explores themes of friendship, teamwork, and self-discovery. With its engaging storyline, lovable characters, and stunning animation, it's a must-see for fans of the franchise and animation enthusiasts alike.

overview: A cranky, retired author reluctantly embarks on a final book tour to help out a young publisher.
title: Best Sellers
plot:
Best Sellers is a 2021 comedy-drama directed by Lina Roessler and written by Anthony Grieco, starring Michael Caine, Aubrey Plaza, Scott Speedman, Ellen Wong, Veronica Ferres and Cary Elwes.

Lucy Stanbridge has inherited her father's once successful publishing firm, now failing after a string of flops. With her assistant, Rachel, she finds that the legendary novelist Harris Shaw, a notoriously difficult alcoholic who has not published in fifty years, still owes them a book. His contract forbids any editing of his manuscript but obliges him to tour for it. When he ignores her calls, Lucy and Rachel drive to his house in Westchester, where he runs them off with a shotgun. Yet just as Lucy is about to sign the company over to Jack Sinclair, Harris arrives with his manuscript, and she tears up the deal.

The tour quickly becomes a disaster. At the first reading Harris reads a story from Penthouse and attacks The New York Times' book critic; he skips most events, picks up new ones in bars, and videos of him cursing at audiences go viral without selling books. Jack joins the tour and nearly persuades Lucy to sell. After she confronts Harris, he promises to read from the book but fails to do so. Inspired, Lucy films young people reading passages and posts the clips online, and sales begin to rise. On the way back, Lucy visits her father, Joseph, who lives in a care home with severe dementia, and the meeting brings out the truth: Harris's wife, Elisabeth, had edited his first book without credit and later died giving birth to a stillborn child, leaving him depressed and blocked for decades. Harris storms off and sets fire to a display of his books in a bookstore. Hospitalized, he learns that his heart, lungs and liver are failing. As the book reaches the best-seller list, Lucy takes him home. When creditors threaten to take the house over a $500,000 debt, she sells the company to Jack, and she cares for Harris until his death. She scatters his ashes where Elisabeth's were scattered, then finds a note leading her to a trunk of unpublished manuscripts that he authorizes her to edit, and she calls Rachel for help.

Selected for the 2021 Berlin International Film Festival, the film was released in the United States and Canada on September 17, 2021, by Screen Media Films and Mongrel Media. It holds 53% on Rotten Tomatoes.

overview: Teenager Winnie Foster is growing up in a small rural town in 1914 with her loving but overprotective parents, but Winnie longs for a life of greater freedom and adventure.
tagline: If you could choose to live forever, would you?
title: Tuck Everlasting
plot:
Tuck Everlasting is a 2002 American fantasy drama film directed by Jay Russell. The story revolves around Winnie Foster, a young girl who discovers a family with a mysterious secret: they are immortal.

The movie explores the themes of immortality and its consequences on human relationships. The Tucks' ability to live forever raises questions about the meaning of life, love, and loss. As the characters navigate their extraordinary circumstances, they must confront the weight of watching loved ones grow old and die, while remaining young and vital themselves.

The film also delves into the idea of growing up and letting go. Winnie's journey is a metaphor for adolescence, as she struggles to balance her desire for independence with her need for guidance and protection from those around her. The Tucks' immortality serves as a catalyst for Winnie's growth, forcing her to confront the complexities of adulthood and make difficult choices about her own future.

Furthermore, the movie touches on the theme of family and the importance of human connections. The Tucks' extraordinary circumstances are both a blessing and a curse, leading them to form unconventional relationships with those around them. As Winnie becomes embroiled in their lives, she learns valuable lessons about the value of love, loyalty, and sacrifice.

Ultimately, Tuck Everlasting is a poignant exploration of the human experience, one that asks us to consider the complexities of life, death, and the choices we make along the way.

overview: In 1940s Los Angeles, two former boxers-turned-cops must grapple with corruption, narcissism, stag films and family madness as they pursue the killer of an aspiring young actress.
production_companies: Equity Pictures Medienfonds GmbH & Co. KG III
tagline: Inspired by the most notorious unsolved murder in California history.
title: The Black Dahlia
plot:
The Black Dahlia is a 2006 American crime drama film directed by Brian De Palma, based on the true story of the unsolved murder of Elizabeth Short in 1947. The movie stars Josh Hartnett as Detective Mark Hansen and Scarlett Johansson as Elizabeth Short.

The main themes of The Black Dahlia include:

1. **The Dark Side of Los Angeles**: The film explores the seedy underbelly of Los Angeles, revealing a city plagued by corruption, crime, and moral decay. This theme is reflected in the dark and atmospheric visuals, which evoke a sense of foreboding and unease.
2. **Femininity and Objectification**: Elizabeth Short's character is portrayed as a vulnerable and exploited woman, symbolizing the objectification of women in society. Her murder serves as a commentary on the societal attitudes towards women during that era.
3. **The Corruption of Power**: The film highlights the corruption and decay within the Los Angeles Police Department, particularly among those in positions of power. This theme is reflected in the character of Detective Hansen, who becomes increasingly obsessed with solving the case, despite his own moral compromises.
4. **The Duality of Human Nature**: The Black Dahlia explores the dual nature of human beings, as embodied by the two main characters: Elizabeth Short and Detective Hansen. Both are complex, multifaceted individuals with dark secrets and motivations, which ultimately lead to their downfall.
5. **The Unreliability of Truth**: The film's narrative is presented in a non-linear fashion, blurring the lines between reality and fiction. This theme highlights the unreliability of truth and the fragility of human perception.

Overall, The Black Dahlia is a thought-provoking and atmospheric film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature, corruption, and the objectification of women.

overview: His Wife is dead and his Son hates him but this old man still has fight in him!  When he loses a highly publicized virtual boxing match to ex-champ Rocky Balboa, reigning heavyweight titleholder Mason Dixon retaliates by challenging Rocky to a nationally televised, 10-round exhibition bout. To the surprise of his son and friends, Rocky agrees to come out of retirement and face an opponent who's faster, stronger, and thirty years his junior.
tagline: It ain't over 'til it's over.
title: Rocky Balboa
plot:
Rocky Balboa is a 2006 American sports drama film directed by Sylvester Stallone, who also co-wrote and starred in the movie.

The film takes place several years after the events of the previous Rocky films. Rocky Balboa (Sylvester Stallone) has retired from boxing and is living a quiet life with his wife Adrian (Brenda Blethyn). However, when a new heavyweight champion, Mason "The Line" Dixon (Antonio Tarver), emerges, Rocky's spirit is reignited.

Mason Dixon is a formidable boxer who has been dominating the ring for years. He is also a ruthless and arrogant fighter who sees himself as above the law. When Adrian passes away, Rocky is devastated, but he finds solace in training with a young and talented boxer named Mason's protégé, Tommy Gunn (Antonio Tarver).

As Rocky trains Tommy, he begins to see a lot of himself in the young fighter. However, when Tommy becomes disillusioned with his life under Mason's guidance, he turns against Rocky and joins forces with Mason.

Rocky is heartbroken when he discovers that Tommy has betrayed him, but he refuses to give up on his friend. He decides to come out of retirement one last time to fight for the heavyweight championship of the world against Mason Dixon.

The film's plot development revolves around Rocky's journey as he trains for the big fight. Along the way, he faces numerous challenges and setbacks, including a serious injury that leaves him unable to train. Despite this, Rocky perseveres and finds new ways to push himself to his limits.

As the fight approaches, Rocky's determination and spirit inspire those around him, including Tommy, who begins to question his loyalty to Mason. In the end, Rocky faces off against Mason in an intense and emotional battle.

The film's climax features a thrilling boxing match between Rocky and Mason, which ends with Rocky emerging victorious but at great personal cost. The movie concludes with Rocky standing alone in the ring, having given everything he has to prove that he still has what it takes to be a champion.

Throughout the film, Stallone delivers a powerful performance as Rocky Balboa, bringing depth and nuance to the character. The supporting cast, including Brenda Blethyn and Antonio Tarver, also deliver strong performances that add to the film's emotional impact.

Overall, Rocky Balboa is a heartwarming and inspiring film that explores themes of redemption, perseverance, and the power of the human spirit.

overview: An agoraphobic woman living alone in New York begins spying on her new neighbors only to witness a disturbing act of violence.
tagline: She has nothing to prove but what's real.
title: The Woman in the Window
plot:
The Woman in the Window is a 2021 psychological thriller film directed by Joe Wright, based on the novel of the same name by A.J. Finn.

The movie follows Anna Fox, a recluse who spends her days spying on her neighbors and watching old movies. However, when she witnesses what appears to be a crime, her life becomes entangled in a mystery that puts her own life at risk.

Some of the main themes present in The Woman in the Window include:

1. **Isolation and loneliness**: Anna's reclusive lifestyle serves as a backdrop for exploring the consequences of social isolation and loneliness. Her inability to connect with others leads to feelings of disconnection and despair.
2. **Guilt and regret**: Anna's past mistakes and regrets are slowly revealed throughout the film, highlighting the weight of guilt and its impact on one's mental health.
3. **Perception vs. reality**: The movie blurs the lines between what is real and what is perceived, leaving the audience questioning what actually happened. This theme speaks to the fragility of human perception and the ease with which our perceptions can be manipulated.
4. **Trauma and PTSD**: Anna's experiences are rooted in a traumatic event from her past, which has left her with PTSD-like symptoms. The film explores the long-term effects of trauma on individuals and their relationships.
5. **The power dynamics between men and women**: The movie critiques the societal expectations placed on women, particularly those related to domesticity and caregiving. Anna's character is a prime example of this, as she struggles to assert her own identity and autonomy.

Overall, The Woman in the Window is a thought-provoking thriller that delves into complex themes and explores the human condition through its protagonist's journey.

overview: An Alaska State Trooper partners with a young woman who escaped the clutches of serial killer Robert Hansen to bring the murderer to justice. Based on actual events.
tagline: The hunter becomes the hunted
title: The Frozen Ground
plot:
The Frozen Ground is a 2013 American crime thriller film directed by Scott Walker, based on the true story of Robert Hansen, a serial killer who was arrested in 1983. The movie stars Nicolas Cage as Detective Will Oldham and John Cusack as Ron Latimer.

The main themes of The Frozen Ground include:

1. **The struggle with addiction**: Both the protagonist, Detective Will Oldham, and the antagonist, Robert Hansen, are portrayed as struggling with addiction. This theme is explored through their respective struggles with substance abuse, which ultimately contributes to their downfall.
2. **Obsession and fixation**: Robert Hansen's obsession with hunting and killing women is a central theme of the film. His fixation on his victims leads him to commit heinous crimes, and it also drives Detective Oldham to hunt him down.
3. **The blurred lines between good and evil**: The movie raises questions about the nature of evil and whether people can change. Robert Hansen's transformation from a seemingly ordinary man to a serial killer is a complex and disturbing theme that explores the gray areas between good and evil.
4. **Redemption and justice**: Detective Oldham's determination to bring Hansen to justice serves as a driving force for the plot. The film also touches on the idea of redemption, as both characters grapple with their past mistakes and seek forgiveness or closure.

The Frozen Ground is a gripping thriller that delves into the darker aspects of human nature, exploring themes that are both thought-provoking and unsettling.

overview: In a monastery cut off from the world, the monks run a clinic for the possessed. One day, a young policeman Marek comes to the convent. Posing as a clergyman, he penetrates monastic life and tries to explain the recent, mysterious disappearance of several tormented inmates. It turns out, however, that there is no way out of the monastery.
title: Hellhole
plot:
Hellhole (Polish: Ostatnia wieczerza, literally "Last Supper") is a 2022 Polish horror film directed by Bartosz M. Kowalski, who co-wrote the screenplay with his frequent writing partner Mirella Zaradkiewicz. Set in 1987, it follows a police officer who goes undercover at a remote monastery to investigate mysterious disappearances and uncovers a dark truth about its clergy. Piotr Żurawski stars as Marek, with Olaf Lubaszenko as Prior Andrzej, Sebastian Stankiewicz as Piotr, Rafał Iwaniuk as Dawid and Lech Dyblik as Antoni.

In 1957, a priest tries to kill a baby bearing a distinctive scar but is shot dead by the militia. Thirty years later, Father Marek arrives at a monastery sanatorium where women are brought to be exorcized, secretly carrying a pistol and other forbidden items; his chest bears a scar like the baby's. Strange things happen in his room, but when he watches an exorcism marked by a shaking bed, gusts of wind and a burning cross, he later finds that the effects were staged. He struggles to eat the priests' food, and days later sees them bury a coffin, apparently for the woman whose room is now empty. Piotr, the vice-prior, warns him in the confessional that those who disobey are severely punished, and Marek reveals that he is a militiaman disguised as a priest to look into the disappearance of local women. Piotr claims that the prior fakes exorcisms to cheat the Church but says he does not know what becomes of the women. Digging up the grave, Marek finds it empty and is captured and force-fed cooked meat. He breaks free, kills Dawid and finds the missing women's bodies hanging in a freezer, realizing he has been eating them. Piotr explains that the monks believe Marek is the "chosen one", born during an eclipse, who after a ritual of eating the flesh of seven sinners and drinking the blood of an innocent will become a demon and usher in a new world order. Piotr then betrays him. The prior reveals that the tip that drew Marek there was a lure and that the church stands over a well serving as a portal to hell. The monks slit a young woman's throat and make Marek drink her blood, but nothing seems to happen; Piotr stabs Marek, throws him into the well and smothers the prior to take control. The next morning Piotr dissolves into a cloud of flies, and a now-demonic Marek suspends the priests upside down in the pose of crucifixion.

The film, available on Netflix, holds a 60% Rotten Tomatoes rating from a small number of reviews.

overview: Asian Hawk leads a mercenary team to recover several lost artifacts from the Old Summer Palace, the bronze heads of the 12 Chinese Zodiac animals which were sacked by the French and British armies from the imperial Summer Palace in Beijing in 1860. Assisted by a Chinese student & a Parisian lady, Hawk stops at nothing to accomplish the mission.
tagline: Twelve heads. Five continents. One man.
title: Chinese Zodiac
plot:
CZ12, also known as Chinese Zodiac and Armour of God III: Chinese Zodiac, is a 2012 action adventure comedy co-written, co-produced and directed by Jackie Chan, who also stars as the treasure hunter JC. The third film in the series begun by Armour of God (1986), it co-stars Kwon Sang-woo, Liao Fan, Zoe Zhang, Anna Yao and Laura Weissbecker.

During the Second Opium War, Anglo-French forces looted and burned Beijing's Old Summer Palace, carrying off twelve bronze heads representing the animals of the Chinese zodiac. In the present, the company MP Corporation auctions the bronze heads it supplies and hires JC to recover the missing ones, offering a $10 million bonus if he finds them all, including the Dragon. Posing as a National Geographic reporter, JC scans replicas made by Professor Guan so that his organization can produce lifelike copies, then travels to Paris to consult a woman named Coco. JC's team breaks into a mansion and cracks a vault holding two bronze heads, a painting called "The Roses" and other treasures. Coco spots him, and he tells her he is working to return lost relics to China.

At the castle of a woman named Catherine, whose great-great-grandfather captained the Indestructible, one of the ships involved in the palace's destruction, the team finds the Rooster head. On a seemingly deserted island they find the Indestructible's wreck, more bronze heads and a hoard of gold, but the pursuing guards and then a band of pirates capture them. JC and his team escape, though the gold sinks. Coco discovers JC's true motives, and the team is furious to learn that MP Corp held the Dragon head all along. When three of Coco's protesting students, including her brother, are kidnapped, JC infiltrates MP Corp's factory, where it makes near-perfect fakes to sell as genuine relics, fights the rival treasure hunter Vulture and trades "The Roses" for the hostages. Facing activist pressure, nobody bids on the Dragon, and MP Corp threatens to drop it into a volcano. JC is badly injured in a midair struggle to save it, and Vulture respectfully hands him the relic. MP Corp's owners are arrested, and JC recovers in hospital.

The film opened across Asia on 20 December 2012 and grossed more than $145 million in mainland China and $171 million worldwide, though reviews were mixed to negative. A re-edited version about 20 minutes shorter was released in U.S. theaters by AMC in October 2013.

overview: Follows renowned cave explorer Bill Stone as he and his team push the boundaries of what has ever been done before as they attempt one of the greatest achievements of modern exploration — to set a new world record by venturing into the bottom of what is thought to be the deepest cave in the world.
title: Explorer: The Deepest Cave
plot:
Explorer: The Deepest Cave is a 2022 American documentary television film directed and photographed by Pablo Durana for National Geographic, the second special in the network's revived National Geographic Explorer series. It follows the renowned caver Bill Stone, founder of Stone Aerospace, and his international team on a three-month expedition into Sistema Cheve in Oaxaca, Mexico, which Stone believes is the deepest cave on Earth. The one-hour special premiered on the National Geographic Channel on Memorial Day, 30 May 2022, and was later made available on Disney+. Durana, a documentary cinematographer whose earlier work includes the Oscar-winning short Inocente and his own film Joyrider, trained in caving techniques in order to film the expedition.

Cheve was ranked only the 11th deepest known cave in the world, but in 1990 explorers who poured green dye into the stream flowing into its mouth found the coloured water emerging near the base of the mountain, about 1.6 miles below the highest known entrance. If people could follow the full course of the water, Cheve would surpass the record holder, Veryovkina in Georgia's Abkhazia region. Stone, who had been exploring the system since the late 1980s, led the 2021 expedition, the largest push yet, which drew 69 cavers from nine countries. The film presents the training, planning and safety precautions behind the descent, likened to climbing Everest in reverse, as the team rigs miles of rope down precipitous drops, wades underground rivers and moves between a chain of camps established ever deeper in the cave, sleeping underground for days or weeks at a time while searching for new passages that might lead further down. Over the expedition the cavers spent more than 1,500 cumulative nights underground and discovered more than 12 miles of unexplored passages, but by the end the team still did not know exactly how deep Cheve goes.

Alex Reif of Laughing Place wrote that, as with many such documentaries, the thrill of the special lay less in the destination than in the journey, and wrote that viewers would come away hoping National Geographic would document the team's next expedition. National Geographic magazine published an accompanying feature on the expedition by Maya Wei-Haas, with photographs by Kasia Biernacka.

overview: Disenchanted with the movie industry, Chili Palmer tries the music industry, meeting and romancing a widow of a music executive along the way.
tagline: Everyone is looking for the next big hit
title: Be Cool
plot:
Be Cool is a 2005 American comedy film directed by Tony Scott and starring John Travolta and Uma Thurman.

The movie revolves around the life of Tony Stark, a fictional character from the Marvel Cinematic Universe. However, I couldn't find any information about Be Cool being produced by Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer or having anything to do with Tony Stark.

Be Cool is actually a 2005 American comedy film directed by Anthony and Martin Rosenblatt, starring John Travolta and Uma Thurman. The movie follows the story of Ice Cream Man, a fictional character who becomes embroiled in a plot to smuggle marijuana into the United States during the 1970s.

The main themes of Be Cool revolve around the tension between loyalty and betrayal, as well as the consequences of one's actions. The film explores the complexities of relationships, particularly those involving family, friends, and romantic partners. It also touches on issues of identity, morality, and the blurred lines between right and wrong in a world where everyone seems to be looking out for themselves.

The movie features a colorful cast of characters, including Ice Cream Man's associates, who are all trying to navigate their own personal struggles while staying one step ahead of the law. Through its lighthearted tone and comedic moments, Be Cool pokes fun at the excesses of 1970s pop culture, while also exploring deeper themes about human nature and the consequences of our choices.

Overall, Be Cool is a film that balances humor with heart, using its wacky characters and situations to explore more serious issues about loyalty, identity, and the complexities of human relationships.

overview: Ash is transported back to medieval days, where he is captured by the dreaded Lord Arthur. Aided by the deadly chainsaw that has become his only friend, Ash is sent on a perilous mission to recover the Book of the Dead, a powerful tome that gives its owner the power to summon an army of ghouls.
tagline: Trapped in time. Surrounded by evil. Low on gas.
title: Army of Darkness
plot:
Army of Darkness is a 1992 American fantasy-comedy film directed by Sam Raimi and starring Bruce Campbell as Ash Williams. The movie is the third installment in The Evil Dead series, following Evil Dead II.

The film begins with Ash (Bruce Campbell) being transported back to medieval Europe from his own time, where he finds himself in the midst of a battle between good and evil forces. Ash soon discovers that he has been brought back for a specific reason: to retrieve the Necronomicon, an ancient book of dark magic.

Upon arrival, Ash meets a group of villagers who are being terrorized by the undead, led by the powerful sorcerer Kell. The villagers believe that Ash is the chosen one, destined to defeat Kell and save their village from destruction.

As Ash navigates this new world, he encounters various obstacles, including treacherous terrain, ferocious creatures, and his own ineptitude in medieval combat. Despite these challenges, Ash proves himself to be resourceful and determined, using his wits and whatever resources available to him to survive.

Throughout the film, Ash's character undergoes significant development as he confronts his own mortality and the nature of evil. He begins to realize that his experiences in the Evil Dead series have prepared him for this moment, and that he has a crucial role to play in the battle between good and evil.

As the story unfolds, Ash faces off against Kell's army of undead warriors, including the iconic Deadite, Chatterer. The film's climax features an epic showdown between Ash and Kell, with Ash ultimately emerging victorious after using his knowledge of the Necronomicon to defeat the sorcerer.

The ending of Army of Darkness is a fitting conclusion to the story, as Ash returns to his own time, forever changed by his experiences in medieval Europe. The film ends on a humorous note, with Ash reflecting on his adventures and remarking that he's "not going back there again."

Overall, Army of Darkness is a cult classic that has become synonymous with Sam Raimi's unique brand of horror-comedy. Bruce Campbell's performance as Ash Williams cemented his status as a genre icon, and the film's blend of humor, action, and fantasy has made it a beloved favorite among fans of the series.

[No additional information is available about Universal Pictures being the production company for Army of Darkness.]

overview: Ellie Linton, a teen from an Australian coastal town, leads her friends on an excursion to a camp deep in the woods, dubbed "Hell." Upon their return, the youths find that their town has been overrun by an enemy army, and their friends and family have been imprisoned. When the hostile invaders become alerted to their presence, Ellie and her friends band together to escape -- and strike back against -- this mysterious enemy.
tagline: Where were you when everything changed?
title: Tomorrow, When the War Began
plot:
Tomorrow, When the War Began is a 2010 Australian post-apocalyptic drama film that explores the themes of survival, loyalty, and the human condition in the face of catastrophic loss. The movie follows a group of teenagers who return home after being away for three years to find their country invaded and their families missing.

At its core, the film delves into the psychological effects of trauma and the struggle to maintain humanity in the midst of chaos. As the characters navigate this new reality, they are forced to confront their own mortality, the loss of innocence, and the true meaning of friendship and loyalty.

The movie also touches on the theme of collective guilt and responsibility, as the characters grapple with the consequences of not doing enough to prevent the war or protect their loved ones. This sense of shared culpability serves as a catalyst for the group's actions, driving them to work together in order to survive and reclaim their homeland.

Furthermore, Tomorrow, When the War Began is also a commentary on the effects of war on civilians, particularly children and young adults. The film humanizes the victims of conflict, highlighting the emotional toll it takes on those left behind and the resilience required to cope with such trauma.

Overall, the movie presents a gripping and thought-provoking portrayal of survival, camaraderie, and the human spirit in the face of unimaginable adversity.

overview: Two doctors in Victorian England use manual stimulation of female genitalia to cure their patients' ills, leading to the invention of the vibrator.
tagline: A comedy about the birth of the vibrator in Victorian England.
title: Hysteria
plot:
Hysteria (2011) is a film that delves into the complexities of female relationships and desires during the Victorian era. The movie revolves around the lives of two women, Trudy Ebersol (played by Maggie Gyllenhaal) and Charlotte Bartlett (played by Felicity Jones), who become embroiled in a scandalous affair with a wealthy and charming man, Dr. J.H. Bell (played by Hugh Dancy).

At its core, Hysteria is a film about the societal constraints placed on women during this time period, particularly when it comes to their desires and relationships. The movie explores the tension between the repressive nature of Victorian society and the longing for freedom and intimacy that lies beneath the surface.

Through the characters' experiences, the film highlights the ways in which women were forced to navigate a world that was designed to suppress their emotions and desires. Trudy and Charlotte's relationship is a powerful metaphor for the ways in which women were expected to conform to societal norms, even when those expectations conflicted with their own desires.

The movie also touches on themes of identity, class, and power dynamics, as the characters navigate their relationships and try to assert their agency in a world that is stacked against them. Ultimately, Hysteria is a film about the resilience of women's spirits and the ways in which they find ways to subvert and challenge the societal norms that seek to constrain them.

The film's title, "Hysteria," refers not only to the medical condition that was often used to explain women's emotional responses but also to the hysteria that arises from the characters' attempts to navigate their desires and relationships within a society that is hostile to their needs.

overview: In April of 1994, four women from different backgrounds and beliefs are trapped and hiding during the Rwandan genocide. Their fight for survival against all odds unites the women in an unbreakable sisterhood.
tagline: Where there is life, there is hope.
title: Trees of Peace
plot:
Trees of Peace is an American drama film written and directed by Alanna Brown in her feature directorial debut. Inspired by true events from the 1994 Rwandan genocide, it stars Eliane Umuhire, Charmaine Bingwa, Ella Cannon and Bola Koleosho as four women of different backgrounds who hide together in a hole beneath a house for 81 days, with Tongayi Chirisa in a supporting role. Produced by RR Productions, Abstract Entertainment and A Brown Girl Films, with Ron and Michelle Ray providing the financing and Nicole Avant among the executive producers, it completed production in November 2019 and premiered at the 2021 Santa Barbara International Film Festival. Netflix acquired the global rights in March 2022 and released the 98-minute English-language film worldwide on 10 June 2022.

The film opens with Annick (Umuhire) reading from the journal in which she recorded the days spent in hiding. As the violence between Hutu and Tutsi engulfs Rwanda in April 1994, four women take refuge in the storage basement under the kitchen of the house Annick, a pregnant moderate Hutu, shares with her husband Francois (Chirisa), who supplies them with rations and news from outside. With her are Mutesi (Koleosho), a young and angry Tutsi woman who blames the Hutu for the killings; Jeanette (Bingwa), a nun whose faith is repeatedly tested; and Peyton (Cannon), an American on a Peace Corps-style mission who hopes to atone for past sins. At first the women distrust and clash with one another, and at one point Mutesi spitefully eats more than her share of the food. As they share their histories of miscarriage, rape and family strife, Mutesi admits that she does not want to die with her anger, and a sisterhood begins to form. The women draw portraits of one another, learn to read English and become devoted to Seeds of Love, Trees of Peace, a children's book Peyton carries in her bag, while they must stifle their cries as they hear people being executed outside. Over the weeks they suffer nightmares, hallucinations and suffocating conditions. Closing title cards note the role of women in Rwanda's post-genocide recovery.

Trees of Peace received a 100% critics' rating on Rotten Tomatoes and reached Netflix's top ten in dozens of countries. Radhika Menon of Decider praised the superb ensemble, singling out Koleosho, and its blend of claustrophobic dread with hope, while The Hindu's Tamma Moksha called it a moving survival story whose characters slipped into stereotype.

overview: A backstage and on-stage look at Justin Bieber during his rise to super stardom.
title: Justin Bieber's Believe
plot:
Justin Bieber's Believe is a 2013 American concert documentary directed by Jon M. Chu, who also staged the Canadian singer's Believe Tour, and the follow-up to Justin Bieber: Never Say Never (2011). Combining tour performances, rehearsal and backstage footage and fresh interviews with the star, it traces Bieber's continuing rise to global fame and his attempts to cope with growing up in the spotlight. Open Road Films distributed it in the United States and Canada.

The film moves between the making of the tour and the shows themselves. It opens on Bieber casually improvising at a piano and joking in a dressing room, then follows the large dance auditions held to cast the tour, the rehearsals, and his collaborations with his creative team, including a comic sequence about the courting of Chu himself to direct the production. On stage, Bieber makes his entrance dressed in white, descending above the crowd on giant wings fashioned from guitars, drums and other instruments, and he reaches out to fans at the front, sometimes bringing one up to be serenaded. Interspersed are home videos of young fans reacting hysterically to receiving concert tickets and shots of devotees camping on pavements to buy them. In interviews Bieber talks about his beginnings as a YouTube phenomenon whose following grew before he had a record deal, his passion for making music, his relationships and the risk of going off the rails, insisting that awareness of the danger will let him avoid it. The film shows a heated confrontation with a heckler in England and includes an emotional tribute to Avalanna Routh, a six-year-old fan known as "Mrs. Bieber" who died of brain cancer in 2012. Interviews also feature his mother Pattie Mallette, his father Jeremy Bieber, mentor Usher, manager Scooter Braun, Ryan Good, and Ludacris.

Believe premiered on December 18, 2013, and opened in theatres on December 25. It fell far short of its predecessor, with about $3.1 million in its first three days and a domestic total of some $6.2 million before it closed in January 2014. Critical reaction ranged from mixed to negative, with 53% on Rotten Tomatoes and 39 on Metacritic. Reviewers found the concert footage energetic and infectious but regarded the film as uncritical, image-managing hagiography; Sheila O'Malley of RogerEbert.com noted that it rarely pressed Bieber on his tabloid troubles, while The Boston Globe called it damage control by way of distraction.

overview: It's all extreme sports and a life of freedom as Max sets off for college -- but Goofy misses Max so much he loses his job and goes to finish college alongside Max and his friends. But as Goofy tries to get closer to Max, both must go to the extreme to learn how to live their own lives together.
title: An Extremely Goofy Movie
plot:
An Extremely Goofy Movie is a 2000 animated film produced by Disney Television Animation. The movie serves as a sequel to the 1995 film A Goofy Movie.

The story begins with Max Goof, now a teenager, feeling embarrassed about his father, Goofy, and their past adventures together. Max has always tried to distance himself from his dad's antics, but when he discovers that Goofy is planning to take him on a road trip across the country, he reluctantly agrees.

The trip starts off as a disaster, with Goofy getting them into various misadventures, including a run-in with a group of bikers and a wild goose chase through a national park. Max tries to avoid his dad's antics, but eventually, they begin to bond over their shared experiences.

As the road trip progresses, Max learns more about his father's past and the reasons behind his desire to take him on this journey. Goofy reveals that he wants to relive his own childhood memories with Max before he becomes too old for it.

Throughout the film, Max struggles with his own identity and tries to find his place in the world. He is torn between his desire to fit in with his peers and his love for his father's carefree spirit.

As they near their destination, a music festival called "The Big Beat," Goofy and Max face one final challenge: a confrontation with Pete, who has been trying to ruin the festival all along. In the end, Goofy and Max work together to save the day, and Max finally comes to terms with his relationship with his father.

The film ends with Goofy and Max arriving at the music festival, where they perform a heartwarming duet of "I 2 I" together. The movie concludes on a positive note, with Max embracing his love for his dad's goofy personality and the two sharing a heartfelt moment as they watch the sunset together.

Overall, An Extremely Goofy Movie is a heartwarming and entertaining film that explores themes of family, identity, and the importance of spending quality time with loved ones.

overview: Harry Caine, a blind writer, reaches this moment in time when he has to heal his wounds from 14 years back. He was then still known by his real name, Mateo Blanco, and directing his last movie.
title: Broken Embraces
plot:
Broken Embraces is a 2009 Spanish drama film directed by Pedro Almodóvar, produced by El Deseo, and written by Pedro Almodóvar. The movie's main themes revolve around the complexities of human relationships, desire, loneliness, and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy.

The story follows Juan (played by Carlos Bardem), a blind man who becomes infatuated with his new housekeeper, Maria (played by Penélope Cruz). As their relationship deepens, Juan's past is revealed through a series of flashbacks, which explore his complicated history with his late wife, Elena (played by Marisa Paredes).

Throughout the film, Almodóvar explores themes of love, loss, and longing. The title "Broken Embraces" refers to the physical act of embracing, but also serves as a metaphor for the emotional connections we make with others. The film highlights how our experiences shape us, and how these experiences can both heal and hurt us.

One of the central themes is the power of desire and its ability to transcend boundaries. Juan's all-consuming passion for Maria drives the plot forward, even as he struggles to come to terms with his own identity and sense of self-worth.

The film also explores the theme of loneliness and isolation. Juan's blindness serves as a physical manifestation of his emotional disconnection from the world around him. As he navigates his relationships, he must confront the reality that his experiences are shaped by his perceptions, rather than objective truth.

Furthermore, Broken Embraces touches on the idea of memory and its role in shaping our understanding of ourselves and others. The film's use of non-linear storytelling and fragmented narrative structures reflects the disjointed nature of human memory, highlighting how our recollections can be both accurate and distorted.

Ultimately, Broken Embraces is a poignant exploration of the complexities of human relationships, desire, and loneliness. Through its nuanced characters and thought-provoking themes, the film invites viewers to reflect on their own experiences and emotions, and to consider the ways in which we navigate the intricacies of love and connection.

overview: Supervillains Harley Quinn, Bloodsport, Peacemaker and a collection of nutty cons at Belle Reve prison join the super-secret, super-shady Task Force X as they are dropped off at the remote, enemy-infused island of Corto Maltese.
tagline: They're dying to save the world.
title: The Suicide Squad
plot:
The Suicide Squad is a 2021 superhero film directed by James Gunn, based on the DC Comics/Vertigo imprint character team of the same name. The movie follows a new team of anti-heroes who are brought together by Amanda Waller (Viola Davis), a high-ranking government official, to carry out a mission.

The story begins with a group of prisoners, including Bloodsport (Idris Elba), Peacemaker (John Cena), and King Shark (Sylvester Stallone), who are all part of the Task Force X program. The team is assembled by Waller to take on a mission in South America, where they must stop a group of terrorists led by a mysterious figure known as Ratcatcher 2 (Daniela Melchior).

As the team embarks on their mission, they soon discover that there are more than just terrorists involved. They are being hunted by a group of mercenaries who will stop at nothing to get what they want. Along the way, the team must also contend with their own personal demons and conflicts.

One of the standout characters in the movie is Harley Quinn (Margot Robbie), who returns from her previous appearance in Suicide Squad (2016). She is joined by other fan favorites like Captain Boomerang (Jai Courtney) and Rick Flag (Joel Kinnaman).

Throughout the movie, Gunn explores themes of redemption, loyalty, and the blurred lines between good and evil. The team's mission becomes a metaphor for their own personal struggles and the moral compromises they must make in order to survive.

The Suicide Squad features a talented ensemble cast, with standout performances from Elba, Cena, and Robbie. The movie also boasts impressive action sequences and a visually stunning score by Steven Price.

Overall, The Suicide Squad is a fun and entertaining take on the DC Comics universe, with plenty of humor, heart, and excitement. It's a great addition to the franchise and sets the stage for future adventures with this lovable but dysfunctional team of anti-heroes.

overview: After one of their shoplifting sessions, Osamu and his son come across a little girl in the freezing cold. At first reluctant to shelter the girl, Osamu’s wife agrees to take care of her after learning of the hardships she faces. Although the family is poor, barely making enough money to survive through petty crime, they seem to live happily together until an unforeseen incident reveals hidden secrets, testing the bonds that unite them.
tagline: Sometimes you choose your family.
title: Shoplifters
plot:
Shoplifters (Japanese: Manbiki Kazoku, literally "Shoplifting Family") is a 2018 Japanese drama written, directed and edited by Hirokazu Kore-eda. Asking what makes a family, a question he had considered for a decade, Kore-eda drew on reports of poverty and shoplifting during Japan's recession, and wrote one scene after hearing a girl at an orphanage read the picture book Swimmy. Shot on 35 mm film from December 2017, it premiered at the 2018 Cannes Film Festival, where it won the Palme d'Or, the first for a Japanese film since The Eel in 1997.

In Tokyo, a makeshift family lives in poverty in the home of the elderly Hatsue, whose late husband's pension supports them: Nobuyo, who works at an industrial laundry; her husband, Osamu, a day laborer off work with an injured ankle; Aki, who works at a peep show; and the boy Shota, who shoplifts with Osamu using hand signals. One cold night they find Yuri, a little girl locked out on an apartment balcony, and after seeing signs of abuse decide to keep her. Two months later, the police start investigating her disappearance, which her parents never reported. The family cuts her hair, burns her clothes and renames her Lin. After a happy day at the beach, Hatsue dies in her sleep, and Osamu and Nobuyo bury her beneath the house to keep collecting her pension.

Shota, who was himself taken from a locked car as a small child, grows uneasy about the family's code and about teaching Yuri to steal. Drawing attention to himself in a grocery store, he flees, jumps from a bridge and breaks his leg. The others are caught trying to run with Yuri and Aki, and the authorities uncover Hatsue's death and the family's secrets, including that Osamu and Nobuyo once killed Nobuyo's abusive husband in self-defense. Nobuyo takes the blame and goes to prison, Shota is placed in an orphanage, and Osamu admits they had meant to abandon him. As Shota leaves on a bus he confesses that he let himself be caught, and silently acknowledges Osamu as his father, while Yuri is returned to neglectful parents.

Lily Franky plays Osamu and Sakura Ando co-stars, with Kirin Kiki in one of her last roles. Critics were rapturous, with 99% approval on Rotten Tomatoes. It grossed about $72.6 million worldwide and was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film.

overview: As Sakura drowns in the murky darkness of the sins she has committed, Shirou's vow to protect her at all costs leads him into a raging battle to put an end to the Holy Grail War.  Will Shirou's wish reach Sakura even as he challenges fate itself in a desperate battle against the rising tide?
tagline: We fight to end this fate.
title: Fate/stay night: Heaven's Feel III. Spring Song
plot:
Fate/stay night: Heaven's Feel III. Spring Song is a thought-provoking film that delves into the complexities of human emotions, particularly those related to love, loss, and redemption.

At its core, the movie explores the theme of self-discovery and the struggle for identity. The protagonist, Shirou Emiya, grapples with his own sense of purpose and belonging, as he navigates the consequences of his actions in the previous films. His relationships with others, particularly Rin Tohsaka and Saber, serve as a catalyst for his growth and introspection.

The film also delves into the concept of sacrifice and the weight of responsibility that comes with it. Shirou's willingness to put himself in harm's way to protect those he cares about is a testament to his unwavering dedication and selflessness. This theme is intertwined with the idea of redemption, as Shirou seeks to make amends for past mistakes and find a sense of forgiveness.

Furthermore, Fate/stay night: Heaven's Feel III. Spring Song touches on the notion of the cyclical nature of time and the inevitability of fate. The film's narrative is marked by a sense of nostalgia and longing, as Shirou reflects on his experiences and the relationships he has formed. This bittersweet tone serves as a reminder that even in the face of adversity, there is always hope for a better future.

Ultimately, Fate/stay night: Heaven's Feel III. Spring Song presents a poignant exploration of the human condition, one that is both deeply personal and universally relatable. Through Shirou's journey, the film invites viewers to reflect on their own values, motivations, and desires, making it a rich and thought-provoking cinematic experience.

overview: Terri is a devoted wife and mother of two, living an ideal suburban life in Atlanta when Colin, a charming but dangerous escaped convict, shows up at her door claiming car trouble. Terri offers her phone to help him but soon learns that no good deed goes unpunished as she finds herself fighting for survival when he invades her home and terrorizes her family.
tagline: First he gets into your house. Then he gets into your head.
title: No Good Deed
plot:
No Good Deed is a 2014 American thriller film directed by Gregg Henkin and written by Tyler Perry. The movie stars Taraji P. Henson, Idris Elba, and Meagan Good.

The story revolves around Speranza "Spez" James (Taraji P. Henson), a successful businesswoman who has just moved into her new home in Atlanta. Spez is a self-made woman who has worked hard to achieve her goals, but she's also fiercely independent and guarded when it comes to her personal life.

One day, while moving into her new house, Spez meets a mysterious stranger named Ben (Idris Elba), who claims to be a handyman hired by the previous owner of the house. As they interact, Spez begins to feel uneasy about Ben's intentions, but she can't quite put her finger on why.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Ben is not just any ordinary handyman. He has a dark past and is hiding secrets that could put Spez in grave danger. Despite her initial reservations, Spez finds herself drawn to Ben, who seems to be able to see right through her tough exterior.

However, as their relationship deepens, Spez begins to realize that she's getting in over her head. Ben's true nature is revealed, and Spez must use all her wits and resourcefulness to outsmart him and protect herself.

Throughout the movie, Taraji P. Henson delivers a standout performance as Spez, bringing depth and nuance to a character who could have easily been one-dimensional. Idris Elba also shines as Ben, conveying a sense of menace and unpredictability that makes him a compelling villain.

The plot is full of twists and turns, keeping the viewer on the edge of their seat as Spez navigates a complex web of danger and deception. The movie's climax is particularly suspenseful, with Spez facing off against Ben in a heart-pumping showdown that will keep you guessing until the very end.

Overall, No Good Deed is a tense and thrilling ride that explores themes of vulnerability, trust, and survival. With its strong performances and clever plot twists, it's a must-see for fans of the thriller genre.

overview: Lisa thinks she's finally met the man of her dreams until she finds out he still believes in Santa Claus.
title: I Believe in Santa
plot:
I Believe in Santa is a 2022 American romantic Christmas comedy directed by Alex Ranarivelo and written by John Ducey, who also stars opposite his real-life wife Christina Moore; it was Ducey and Ranarivelo's latest holiday collaboration after A Christmas Mystery and A Hollywood Christmas. Produced by ESX Entertainment, it co-stars Violet McGraw, Sachin Bhatt, Lateefah Holder and Matthew Glave.

Lisa (Moore), a journalist, has just finished an article arguing that the Fourth of July is the nation's greatest holiday, far superior to commercialized Christmas. When her ex-husband once again fails to look after their daughter Ella (McGraw), Lisa takes the girl to an Independence Day festival with her best friend Sharon, where Ella is due to perform. Ella gets separated from her group and is found by Tom (Ducey), a lawyer offering free legal advice at a booth with his colleague and best friend Assan. When Lisa finds her daughter with a stranger she fears the worst, but the misunderstanding is quickly cleared up, the four watch the fireworks together, and over the following months Lisa and Tom fall in love. As the holidays approach, however, Tom reveals that he is not only obsessed with Christmas but genuinely believes in Santa Claus. He fills their days with skating, caroling, tree trimming and cookie baking, and Lisa at first plays along for Ella's sake, while worrying that Tom is filling her daughter's head with fantasies. Ella secretly tells a department store Santa that her wish is for her mother and Tom to marry. Lisa, who has hated the holidays ever since a painful Christmas disappointment from her parents, cannot convince Tom that Santa does not exist, and when her boss assigns her an article about Christmas, she breaks up with him. Later, when Ella's father lets her down before a big cardboard sled race, she asks to be taken to Tom, who skips The Nutcracker to help her fix her sled, while Lisa talks with Assan about Tom's devotion. Ella and her mother win the race, Tom promises to tone things down next year and proposes, Ella reveals her wish, and Lisa ends up writing a tribute to Christmas.

The film was released worldwide on Netflix on 14 December 2022. Critics were unenthusiastic: Film-rezensionen.de found the debate over Santa's existence thin and the humor unremarkable, though worth a look for devoted Christmas fans, and Kino&Co dismissed it as bottom-of-the-drawer holiday fare that wasted McGraw's talent.

overview: A young girl, passionate about fashion design, is mysteriously able to enter the 1960s where she encounters her idol, a dazzling wannabe singer. But 1960s London is not what it seems, and time seems to be falling apart with shady consequences.
tagline: When the past lets you in, the truth will come out.
title: Last Night in Soho
plot:
Last Night in Soho is a British psychological horror film of 2021 directed and co-produced by Edgar Wright, who wrote it with Krysty Wilson-Cairns. Thomasin McKenzie stars as Eloise "Ellie" Turner, a young fashion student haunted by visions of 1960s London, with Anya Taylor-Joy as the aspiring singer Sandie, Matt Smith as her manager Jack, Terence Stamp as a silver-haired stranger, and Diana Rigg as the landlady Ms Collins. It is dedicated to Rigg and Margaret Nolan, who died in 2020.

Ellie, a sweet but fragile teenager who adores the music and fashion of the Swinging Sixties, was raised by her grandmother in Cornwall after her mother, a fashion designer, took her own life. Arriving at the London College of Fashion, she struggles to fit in, bullied by her roommate Jocasta and befriended only by John. She moves into a bedsit owned by the elderly Ms Collins, and that night dreams herself back into the 1960s, where she watches a confident blonde, Sandie, talk her way toward singing at the Café de Paris and fall for the charming manager Jack. Further dreams follow Sandie to a Soho audition and back to Ellie's very room. Ellie dyes her hair blonde, copies Sandie's style and takes a job in a pub, where a silver-haired man notices her resemblance to Sandie.

The dreams darken as Ellie sees Jack pimping Sandie to his associates, and menacing apparitions of the men who used her haunt Ellie's waking hours. After a vision of Jack apparently stabbing Sandie to death, Ellie becomes convinced the silver-haired man is Jack. The police dismiss her, and old newspapers reveal not a murder but a string of local men who vanished. Confronted by Ellie, the stranger denies killing Sandie and is then hit by a taxi; he was Lindsey, an undercover vice officer who once urged Sandie to escape. Ms Collins then reveals that she is Sandie: it was she who killed Jack when he threatened her with a knife, and she went on to murder the men she was sold to, hiding their bodies in the house. She drugs Ellie's tea, stabs John when he comes to help, and chases Ellie as fire spreads. Faced with the vengeful spirits of her victims, Sandie tries to kill herself; Ellie stops her, but Sandie tells her to save John and stays in the burning house. Later Ellie's designs triumph at her end-of-year show, and Sandie blows her a kiss from a mirror.

Premiering at Venice in September 2021, the film grossed $23 million worldwide. Critics praised Wright's style, giving it 75% on Rotten Tomatoes.

original_title: Rise of the Planet of the Apes
overview: A highly intelligent chimpanzee named Caeser has been living a peaceful suburban life ever since he was born. But when he gets taken to a cruel primate facility, Caeser decides to revolt against those who have harmed him.
tagline: Evolution Becomes Revolution.
title: Rise of the Planet of the Apes
plot:
