Rise of the Planet of the Apes is a 2011 science fiction film directed by Rupert Wyatt, produced by 20th Century Fox, and based on the 1968 novel "La Planète des Singes" (Planet of the Apes) by Pierre Boulle.

The movie begins with Will Rodman (played by James Franco), a scientist who works for a biotech company called Gen-Sys. Will is studying the effects of a new primate virus, Simian Flu, which has been created to cure Alzheimer's disease in humans. The virus is designed to selectively target and kill brain cells infected with the disease, leaving healthy cells intact.

As part of his research, Will tests the virus on chimpanzees, including Caesar (played by Andy Serkis), a genetically engineered super-intelligent primate who becomes the central character of the film. Initially, Caesar appears to be cured of the Alzheimer's-like symptoms caused by the virus, but as time passes, he begins to exhibit signs of intelligence and emotional depth.

Will forms a bond with Caesar, recognizing his exceptional cognitive abilities and treating him like a person. However, their relationship is complicated when Will's boss, Caroline Aranha (played by Amiah Miller), discovers that Caesar has become too intelligent for the company's purposes. She orders Will to euthanize Caesar, but he refuses.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Caesar has developed a sense of self-awareness and empathy, which sets him apart from other primates. He begins to question his existence and the nature of his captivity. Meanwhile, Will starts to experience strange side effects from the virus, including memory loss and paranoia.

The plot takes a dramatic turn when Will's family is attacked by a group of men who are seeking to exploit Caesar for their own gain. In the ensuing chaos, Will is killed, and Caesar is left alone and adrift in the world.

Caesar, now driven by a desire for revenge and survival, escapes from the lab and begins to navigate the complexities of human society. He forms alliances with other primates who share his intelligence and determination, including Maurice (played by Karim Zeroual) and Cornelia (played by Freida Pinto).

As Caesar's power grows, he becomes a symbol of resistance against humanity's oppression of intelligent beings. The film culminates in a dramatic showdown between Caesar and the humans who have wronged him, setting the stage for the events of the sequels.

Throughout the movie, Andy Serkis delivers a powerful performance as Caesar, bringing depth and nuance to the character. His portrayal has been widely praised for its emotional authenticity and physicality, which was achieved through innovative motion capture technology.

Overall, Rise of the Planet of the Apes is a thought-provoking and visually stunning film that explores themes of intelligence, empathy, and the ethics of scientific experimentation. The movie's success spawned a franchise with multiple sequels and spin-offs, cementing its place as a modern classic in the science fiction genre.

overview: Orphaned and alone except for an uncle, Hugo Cabret lives in the walls of a train station in 1930s Paris. Hugo's job is to oil and maintain the station's clocks, but to him, his more important task is to protect a broken automaton and notebook left to him by his late father. Accompanied by the goddaughter of an embittered toy merchant, Hugo embarks on a quest to solve the mystery of the automaton and find a place he can call home.
tagline: One of the most legendary directors of our time takes you on an extraordinary adventure.
title: Hugo
plot:
Hugo is a 2011 American fantasy adventure film directed by Martin Scorsese, produced by Michael Broderick and Steven Haft, and distributed by Paramount Pictures.

The story begins in 1930s Paris, where we meet Hugo Cabret (Asa Butterfield), an orphaned boy who lives in the walls of a train station. Hugo's life is turned upside down when he discovers a mysterious automaton that belongs to his late father, Georges Méliès (Ben Kingsley). The automaton is one of several inventions created by Méliès, a famous filmmaker and magician.

As Hugo tries to repair the automaton, he becomes entangled in a mystery surrounding a missing film reel. He soon discovers that the film reel is connected to a 3D film directed by Méliès, which was lost for decades. The film, titled "A Trip to the Moon," is considered one of the greatest films of all time.

Hugo's search for the missing film reel leads him on a journey through the train station and its inhabitants. He befriends Isabelle (Chloë Moretz), a young girl who lives in the station with her mother, and Captain Smee (Sacha Baron Cohen), a bumbling police officer who is tasked with capturing Hugo.

As Hugo delves deeper into the mystery, he uncovers a conspiracy involving a wealthy collector, René Tabard (Stanley Tucci), who is trying to acquire Méliès' film collection. Hugo also discovers that his father was involved in a bitter dispute with Tabard over the ownership of the films.

Throughout the story, Scorsese weaves together historical facts and fiction, creating an immersive experience for the audience. The film features stunning visuals, including intricate sets and costumes, which bring the world of early cinema to life.

As Hugo's search reaches its climax, he discovers a hidden compartment in the train station that contains Méliès' lost film reel. In a thrilling finale, Hugo uses the automaton to recreate the 3D film, which is revealed to be a masterpiece of cinematic art.

The film ends with Hugo finding a new sense of purpose and belonging, thanks to his discovery of his father's work and the help of Isabelle and Captain Smee. The final shot of the film features Hugo sitting in a cinema, watching Méliès' "A Trip to the Moon" on the big screen, surrounded by the magic of cinema.

Overall, Hugo is a heartwarming and visually stunning film that celebrates the art of cinema and the power of imagination.

overview: Brilliant student Jeff Chang has the most important interview of his life tomorrow.  But today is still his birthday, what starts off as a casual celebration with friends evolves into a night of debauchery that risks to derail his life plan.
tagline: Finally.
title: 21 & Over
plot:
"21 & Over" is a coming-of-age comedy-drama film that explores the complexities of male friendship and the struggles of transitioning into adulthood. The movie delves into the theme of toxic masculinity, as the protagonist, Todd, navigates his 21st birthday and the expectations placed upon him by his friends.

The film also touches on the idea of identity crisis, as Todd grapples with finding his place in the world and asserting his independence from his overbearing father. The movie's portrayal of fraternity life serves as a backdrop for exploring themes of brotherhood, loyalty, and the blurred lines between friendship and codependency.

Furthermore, "21 & Over" examines the consequences of reckless behavior and the devastating effects it can have on relationships and one's own well-being. Through Todd's journey, the film highlights the importance of self-awareness, accountability, and taking responsibility for one's actions.

Ultimately, the movie presents a nuanced exploration of the challenges faced by young men as they navigate the transition from adolescence to adulthood, often with limited guidance and support.

overview: The lone inhabitants of an abandoned police station are under attack by the overwhelming numbers of a seemingly unstoppable street gang.
tagline: L.A.'s deadliest street gang just declared war on the cops.
title: Assault on Precinct 13
plot:
Assault on Precinct 13 is a 1976 American action thriller film directed by John Carpenter. The movie takes place in a police station that has been quarantined due to a deadly virus outbreak in the city, and it follows a small group of survivors as they try to stay alive until help arrives.

The main theme of Assault on Precinct 13 is the struggle for survival in a desperate situation, where the characters are forced to confront their own mortality and the harsh realities of the world around them. The film explores the idea that even in the most dire circumstances, humanity can find ways to persevere and connect with each other.

The movie also touches on the theme of isolation and confinement, as the characters are trapped in the police station with no clear way out. This sense of claustrophobia creates a tense atmosphere, where every decision feels like a matter of life and death.

Furthermore, Assault on Precinct 13 can be seen as a commentary on the breakdown of social order and the collapse of institutions. The film depicts a city in chaos, where the rule of law has broken down, and the characters are forced to fend for themselves in a world that seems to have lost its way.

Overall, Assault on Precinct 13 is a gripping thriller that explores themes of survival, humanity, and the resilience of the human spirit in the face of adversity.

overview: A virus is unleashed and a chilling massacre runs through the streets of Montevideo.
tagline: 32 seconds to live or die.
title: Virus:32
plot:
Virus:32 (Spanish: Virus 32) is a 2022 Uruguayan-Argentine horror film directed by Gustavo Hernández, who co-wrote it with Juma Fodde Roma. Produced by Aeroplano Cine, Mother Superior Films and Latido Films, with Sebastián Aloi and Ignacio García Cucucovich as producers and music by Hernán González, it stars Paula Silva, Daniel Hendler and the young Pilar García, with Franco Rilla and Sofía González. Set in Montevideo, it takes its title from a crucial detail: after each kill, the infected fall still for exactly thirty-two seconds.

Iris (Silva) works as a night guard at a vast, rundown sports club. Separated from her husband Javier (Rilla) since the death of their young son, she shares custody of their eight-year-old daughter Tata (García), and one night, having forgotten it is her turn, she must bring the girl along to work. Meanwhile, a virus is spreading through the city, turning people into savage killers. Leaving Tata in the gym with a walkie-talkie and watching her through the security cameras, Iris patrols the building, where strange figures have begun to appear. Attacked by an infected man and witnessing assaults in the street, she notices the thirty-two-second pause that follows each killing. Then Tata vanishes from the monitors. Searching the dark corridors as more infected arrive, Iris meets Luis (Hendler), a stranger who claims to know where her daughter is but demands that she first help deliver his wife's baby. She agrees, only to discover that the woman, bound and gagged in a wheelchair, is infected. Their ordeal leads through a besieged swimming pool, where the dying Javier appears, to a desperate birth, while Iris clings to the hope of finding Tata alive and escaping toward the port.

The film opened in Argentine cinemas on 21 April 2022 through Star Distribution and was released on video on demand in France that July. It received positive reviews, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting more than 90% approval. Página 12 called it a magnificent horror tale and praised Silva's excellent performance, La Nación wrote that it is genuinely scary and sustains tension throughout with well-timed twists, and Clarín admired its perceptive script, agile direction and the work of Silva, a menacing Hendler and the debuting García. Otros Cines considered it a valuable example of the zombie subgenre in Latin American cinema, which rarely explores the theme, and Russian critic Stanislav Zelvensky included it among the best horror films of 2022.

overview: A team of highly skilled Navy SEALS find themselves embarking on the battle of their lives when they come face-to-face with the undead. After a deadly outbreak occurs in New Orleans, the SEALS must fight for their lives, and the city, against an army of zombies.
title: Navy Seals vs. Zombies
plot:
Navy Seals vs. Zombies is an action-comedy film that combines elements of horror and military action. The movie follows a team of Navy SEALs as they battle against a zombie outbreak in the Middle East.

At its core, the film explores themes of camaraderie, sacrifice, and the human cost of war. As the Navy SEALs fight to survive against the undead hordes, they are also forced to confront their own personal demons and make difficult choices that test their bonds with each other. The movie highlights the strong relationships between the characters, particularly the banter and trust that develops among them as they work together to overcome seemingly insurmountable odds.

The film also touches on the idea of the "other," using the zombies as a metaphor for the unknown or the enemy. As the Navy SEALs navigate this new and terrifying threat, they are forced to confront their own biases and assumptions about what it means to be human. The movie suggests that even in the face of unimaginable horror, humanity can persevere and find ways to connect with each other.

Furthermore, the film critiques the notion of war as a solution to problems, highlighting the devastating consequences of military action on civilians and the environment. The zombies serve as a symbol for the chaos and destruction that can result from conflict, and the Navy SEALs' efforts to contain the outbreak serve as a commentary on the futility of trying to control or eradicate something that is inherently unpredictable.

Overall, Navy Seals vs. Zombies is a tongue-in-cheek sendup of military action movies, using humor and satire to explore deeper themes about humanity, camaraderie, and the consequences of war.

overview: Suave, charming and volatile, Reggie Kray and his unstable twin brother Ronnie start to leave their mark on the London underworld in the 1960s. Using violence to get what they want, the siblings orchestrate robberies and murders while running nightclubs and protection rackets. With police Detective Leonard "Nipper" Read hot on their heels, the brothers continue their rapid rise to power and achieve tabloid notoriety.
tagline: Love, fight, live, rule like a legend.
title: Legend
plot:
Legend is a 2015 biographical gangster film written and directed by Brian Helgeland, adapted from John Pearson's 1972 book The Profession of Violence: The Rise and Fall of the Kray Twins. Tom Hardy plays both Reggie and Ron Kray, with Emily Browning, David Thewlis and Christopher Eccleston, and Taron Egerton, Paul Bettany and Chazz Palminteri in supporting roles.

In the 1960s, Reggie Kray, a former boxer, is a major figure in London's criminal underworld, while his twin, Ron, is held in a psychiatric hospital for paranoid schizophrenia until Reggie uses threats to secure his early release. With the leader of the rival Richardson Gang in prison, the brothers expand their control of the underworld, starting by seizing a nightclub. Reggie courts Frances, his driver's sister, and marries her. When he is jailed for an earlier offense, she makes him swear to leave crime behind, a promise he never keeps. In his absence, Ron's instability nearly ruins the club, and his hostility toward Frances grows.

Their reputation reaches America, and Angelo Bruno of the Philadelphia crime family offers Reggie an even split of London's gambling profits in return for protection. The arrangement is lucrative, but Ron's paranoia and appetite for violence clash with Reggie's restraint. Ron publicly murders George Cornell, an associate of the Richardsons, and their mother asks Reggie to protect his brother, while Scotland Yard opens a full investigation. Frances, worn down by Reggie's broken promises and Ron's hatred, turns to prescription drugs, and after Reggie beats and rapes her she leaves him. They seem to reconcile and plan a trip to Ibiza, but she dies of an overdose, leaving Reggie consumed by guilt. Distrusting Reggie's business partner Leslie Payne, Ron pays the petty criminal Jack "the Hat" McVitie to kill him. Payne survives and informs on the twins to Detective Superintendent Leonard "Nipper" Read, and Reggie stabs McVitie to death at a party. Ron is arrested for Cornell's murder and Reggie for McVitie's. Both receive life sentences; Ron died in 1995 and Reggie in 2000.

A British, French and American co-production financed by StudioCanal, Legend premiered in London on 3 September 2015 and grossed $43 million worldwide on a budget under $25 million. Reviews were mixed, but Hardy's dual performance was widely praised and won him a British Independent Film Award for Best Actor.

overview: It’s 1982, and Taeko is 27 years old, unmarried, and has lived her whole life in Tokyo. She decides to visit her family in the countryside, where she begins to reconnect to forgotten longings. In lyrical switches between the present and the past, Taeko contemplates the arc of her life, and wonders if she has been true to the dreams of her childhood self.
tagline: I’m going on a trip with Me.
title: Only Yesterday
plot:
Only Yesterday is a 1991 Japanese animated drama film written and directed by Isao Takahata, produced by Studio Ghibli. The movie follows the story of Taeko Okajima, a young office worker who embarks on a journey to rediscover her childhood memories and find her place in the world.

The film begins with Taeko (voiced by Yuriko Kishitani) as an adult, working in Tokyo and feeling unfulfilled. She reminisces about her childhood, particularly her summer vacation spent at her grandparents' farm in the countryside. As she reflects on these memories, Taeko is transported back to her youth.

In the past, we see Taeko as a young girl, spending her summers with her grandparents in the rural town of Kusakabe. She spends her days exploring the surrounding countryside, playing with her friends, and helping out at her grandparents' farm. The film beautifully captures the carefree nature of childhood, showcasing Taeko's innocence and curiosity.

As the story progresses, we see Taeko develop feelings for a young man named Toshio, who is visiting from Tokyo. Their romance blossoms during Taeko's summer vacation, but it ultimately ends when Toshio returns to the city. The loss of this first love leaves a lasting impact on Taeko, shaping her perspective on life and relationships.

The film's narrative jumps back and forth between Taeko's childhood memories and her present-day struggles as an adult. As she navigates her career and personal life in Tokyo, Taeko begins to realize that she has lost touch with the simple joys of childhood. She starts to feel disconnected from her own desires and aspirations.

In a poignant moment, Taeko visits her grandparents' farm again, this time accompanied by Toshio's son, who is now a young boy. As they explore the countryside together, Taeko begins to see the world through the eyes of a child once more. She starts to appreciate the beauty of nature and the importance of human connections.

The film concludes with Taeko returning to her life in Tokyo, but with a newfound sense of purpose and appreciation for the simple things. She has come to realize that childhood is not just a nostalgic memory, but a state of mind that can be recaptured at any age. The movie ends on a hopeful note, suggesting that it's never too late to rediscover one's sense of wonder and connection with the world.

Throughout the film, Takahata's direction masterfully weaves together themes of nostalgia, identity, and the human experience. The animation is beautiful, capturing the vibrant colors and textures of rural Japan in the 1950s. The voice acting is also noteworthy, bringing depth and nuance to Taeko's character.

Overall, Only Yesterday is a poignant and thought-provoking film that explores the complexities of growing up and finding one's place in the world.

overview: Once the ruler of an entire universe, the Great Spirit Mata Nui finds himself cast out of his own body, his spirit trapped inside the fabled Mask of Life, hurtling through space. After landing on the far-away planet of Bara Magna, the mask creates a new body for Mata Nui, who unwillingly gets caught up in the furious battles of the nearly barren and dangerous planet.
title: Bionicle: The Legend Reborn
plot:
Bionicle: The Legend Reborn is an animated film that explores several profound themes, primarily centered around identity, self-discovery, and the struggle between light and darkness. 

The story revolves around Gali, a young Toa, who embarks on a perilous journey to reclaim her people's lost city of Metru Nui from the evil Makuta. As she navigates this treacherous world, Gali grapples with her own identity and purpose, questioning whether she is truly destined for greatness or merely a pawn in a larger game.

Throughout her quest, Gali confronts the darkness within herself and the world around her, forcing her to make difficult choices that test her courage, loyalty, and compassion. The film's narrative is replete with symbolism, as Gali's journey serves as a metaphor for the universal human experience of self-discovery and growth.

Ultimately, Bionicle: The Legend Reborn presents a powerful allegory about the importance of embracing one's true nature and finding balance within oneself, while also acknowledging the need to confront and overcome the shadows that threaten to consume us.

overview: Theseus is a mortal man chosen by Zeus to lead the fight against the ruthless King Hyperion, who is on a rampage across Greece to obtain a weapon that can destroy humanity.
tagline: The Gods need a hero.
title: Immortals
plot:
Immortals is a 2011 American fantasy action film directed by Tarsem Singh and written by Krikor Oskanyan, Michael Robert Johnson, and Charles Randolf. The movie stars Henry Cavill, Mickey Rourke, Kellan Lutz, Stephen Dorff, and Isabel Lucas.

The story begins in ancient Greece, where the gods of Mount Olympus are at war with the Titans. The mortal king Hyperion (Mickey Rourke) is a powerful warrior who has been chosen by Zeus to lead the Olympian forces against the Titans. However, Hyperion's son Theseus (Henry Cavill), a young and inexperienced warrior, is destined for greatness.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Theseus is not just any ordinary mortal. He is the son of Zeus and a mortal woman, Aethera (Isabel Lucas). The gods have chosen Theseus to be their champion in the war against the Titans, and he is trained by the god Apollo (Stephen Dorff) to wield the powerful sword Excalibur.

Meanwhile, the Titan king Atlas (Danny Huston) has stolen Zeus's lightning bolt, which gives him immense power over the world. The gods are powerless without the lightning bolt, and they turn to Theseus for help. Theseus sets out on a perilous journey to reclaim the lightning bolt and defeat the Titans.

Along the way, Theseus meets the warrior Kael (Kellan Lutz), who becomes his ally in the battle against the Titans. Together, they face numerous challenges and obstacles as they journey through treacherous landscapes and fight off hordes of monstrous creatures.

As the story reaches its climax, Theseus and Kael finally reach Atlas's lair, where they engage in an epic battle with the Titan king. In the end, Theseus emerges victorious, but not without great cost. He kills Atlas and retrieves the lightning bolt, which he uses to defeat the remaining Titans and save the world.

However, the movie takes a dark turn as Theseus is forced to confront his own destiny. He realizes that he is destined for greatness, but at what cost? The movie ends with Theseus standing alone, having fulfilled his purpose but also losing himself in the process.

Throughout the movie, there are many themes and motifs that are woven throughout the story. One of the most prominent is the struggle between fate and free will. Theseus is forced to follow a predetermined path, but he also has the power to choose his own destiny. This theme is reflected in the character of Kael, who is initially hesitant to join Theseus on his quest.

The movie also explores the idea of identity and self-discovery. Theseus is a complex character who struggles to come to terms with his own identity. He is both mortal and god, human and divine. As he navigates the world of the gods, he must confront his own limitations and weaknesses.

Overall, Immortals is a visually stunning movie that features impressive action sequences and breathtaking cinematography. The story is engaging and suspenseful, with plenty of twists and turns to keep viewers on the edge of their seats. While it may not be perfect, the movie has its moments, and fans of fantasy and adventure will likely find it entertaining.

overview: Framed and on the run, a former FBI agent must save his family from a blazing fire in the world's tallest building.
tagline: Don't look down
title: Skyscraper
plot:
Skyscraper is a 2018 action thriller film directed by Rawson Marshall Thurber and produced by Legendary Pictures. The movie stars Dwayne Johnson, Neve Campbell, and Roland Møller.

The story begins with Will Sawyer (Dwayne Johnson), a former FBI agent who lost his family in a fire at their home when he was just a child. This traumatic event led to Will's estrangement from his father, Gary Sawyer (Ronny Cox), a renowned architect who designed the world's tallest skyscraper, the Centennial Tower.

Years later, Will is hired by the CEO of the Centennial Tower, Hendricks (Patrick Wilson), to investigate the building after it has been severely damaged in a fire. However, upon arrival, Will discovers that the fire was no accident and that his father had designed the tower with a secret escape route for him, which he had never revealed.

As Will delves deeper into the mystery, he realizes that Hendricks is behind the fire and plans to use the building's advanced technology to gain control over the city's infrastructure. The CEO intends to sell the building to a foreign government, but his plan is threatened by Will's investigation.

Will soon finds himself trapped in the burning tower with his father, who has been hiding secrets about the building's design. Together, they must navigate the treacherous skyscraper and outsmart Hendricks' henchmen to prevent the sale of the building to the foreign government.

As the story unfolds, Will's personal demons are revealed, including his complicated relationship with his father and his feelings of guilt over not being able to save his family. The action-packed plot is filled with suspenseful moments, heart-pumping stunts, and intense hand-to-hand combat sequences.

Throughout the movie, Will's character undergoes significant development as he confronts his past and learns to forgive himself and his father. The film's climax features an epic showdown between Will and Hendricks, with the fate of the city hanging in the balance.

Ultimately, Will emerges victorious, having saved the day and restored his family's legacy. The movie concludes on a hopeful note, with Will finally finding closure and redemption after years of struggling to come to terms with his past.

Overall, Skyscraper is an action-packed thrill ride that combines stunning visuals, heart-pumping stunts, and a gripping storyline. Dwayne Johnson delivers a memorable performance as the protagonist, bringing depth and nuance to the character's emotional journey.

original_title: The Girl in the Spider's Web
overview: After being enlisted to recover a dangerous computer program, hacker Lisbeth Salander and journalist Mikael Blomkvist find themselves caught in a web of spies, cybercriminals and corrupt government officials.
tagline: The past never forgets.
title: The Girl in the Spider's Web
plot:
The Girl in the Spider's Web is a 2018 action thriller directed by Fede Álvarez, who wrote the screenplay with Jay Basu and Steven Knight, adapted from David Lagercrantz's 2015 novel featuring Stieg Larsson's Millennium characters. A soft reboot and sequel to The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo (2011), it stars Claire Foy as Lisbeth Salander, with Sverrir Gudnason, Lakeith Stanfield, Sylvia Hoeks, Stephen Merchant and Claes Bang.

As girls, Lisbeth and her sister, Camilla, live with their abusive father, crime lord Alexander Zalachenko; when he tries to molest Camilla, Lisbeth escapes by leaping from a balcony, leaving her sister behind. Years later, Lisbeth, now a vigilante hacker in Stockholm, is hired by programmer Frans Balder to steal back Firefall, a program he built for the NSA that can access the world's nuclear codes. She retrieves it but cannot unlock it, and NSA agent Edwin Needham tracks her. Mercenaries led by Jan Holtser steal Firefall and try to kill her. Believing Lisbeth has kept the program, Balder turns to Gabriella Grane, deputy director of the Swedish Security Service, who moves him and his young son, August, to a safe house. Her former lover, journalist Mikael Blomkvist, learns that Holtser once worked for Zalachenko and now serves the Spiders, a crime syndicate. When the safe house is attacked, Holtser kills Balder, frames Lisbeth and abducts August, but Lisbeth rescues the boy, who alone can unlock Firefall, and learns that the Spiders are led by Camilla, whom she believed dead.

Lisbeth frees Needham from custody in return for his promise to take August to his mother in San Francisco. The Spiders trace August and take him to the sisters' childhood home, where Camilla kills Grane, who had hired them. Lisbeth and Blomkvist are captured, and Lisbeth tells August to reveal the password, but Needham, guided by her hacker friend Plague, shoots Camilla's men through the walls with a sniper rifle. Camilla flees with the laptop, and Holtser, blinded by poison, is killed by her car. On a clifftop Camilla asks why Lisbeth never came back for her, then steps off the edge. Needham finds that Lisbeth has destroyed Firefall, August is reunited with his mother, and Lisbeth destroys her childhood home.

Released by Sony after premiering at the Rome Film Festival in October 2018, the film grossed $35 million against a $43 million budget. Critics found it a less complex, action-focused reboot, giving it 38% on Rotten Tomatoes and 43 on Metacritic.

original_title: 劇場版ポケットモンスター セレビィ 時を超えた遭遇
overview: 40 years ago, a Celebi was being attacked by a Pokemon Hunter. Luckily, a young boy named Yukinari saved Celebi. Using its Time Traveling power, Celebi transported itself and Yukinari 40 years into the future. There, Satoshi, Kasumi, and Takeshi assist Yukinari to the healing lake in the forest so they can heal the wounded Celebi. Unfortunately an evil Team Rocket member, Vicious, tries to capture Celebi using his technology. As Satoshi and Co. try to get away from Vicious, they also run into Musashi, Kojiro, and Nyarth, who also want to capture Celebi. Soon it becomes a race against time to get Celebi and Yukinari back to the forest before Celebi is caught and is used to destroy the forest and themselves.
tagline: Best friends. Better heroes.
title: Pokémon 4Ever
plot:
Pokémon 4Ever is a 2001 Japanese anime film based on the Pokémon television series, the fourth official Pokémon film. Directed by Kunihiko Yuyama and written by Hideki Sonoda, it was released in Japan on July 7, 2001, with a Japanese cast led by Rica Matsumoto and Ikue Ōtani. Its English adaptation, produced by 4Kids Entertainment and directed by Jim Malone, starred the regular television voice cast of Veronica Taylor, Eric Stuart, Rachael Lillis and Maddie Blaustein. Producer Norman Grossfeld called its animation by Oriental Light and Magic the studio's finest yet.

In a forest in the Johto region, the young trainer Sammy protects Celebi, a Mythical Pokémon able to travel through time, from a Pokémon Hunter, and Celebi carries him forty years into the future. In the present, the Iron Masked Marauder, a ruthless member of Team Rocket, wants to capture Celebi using Dark Balls, which can seize Pokémon that already belong to trainers, turn them evil and magnify their power. Ash, Misty and Brock, having glimpsed the legendary Suicune near Arborville, are warned by the elderly Towa and her granddaughter Diana about the "Voice of the Forest". They find Sammy and the injured Celebi and, guided by wild Pokémon, take it to the healing Lake of Life, where Ash and Sammy bond.

The Marauder captures Celebi with a Dark Ball and uses its power over nature to encase it in enormous armor formed from the forest, revealing that he plans to overthrow Giovanni and rule the world. With Suicune's help, Ash, Sammy and Pikachu breach the armor and reach Celebi, freeing it from the Dark Ball's control, but Celebi dies in Sammy's arms. Even Suicune's purified lake cannot revive it, until the true Voice of the Forest, the Celebi of every era, appears and brings it back to life. After a last escape attempt, the Marauder crashes into the forest, where angry wild Pokémon surround him. Celebi returns Sammy to his own time, and when Ash later speaks to Professor Oak, the professor knows Sammy's name without being told, and his old sketchbook reveals that he was Sammy.

Released in North America on October 11, 2002, by Miramax Films, which had taken over the series' distribution from Warner Bros., the film opened in only 249 theaters and earned about $1.7 million there, though it did better on home video. In Japan it grossed $39 million, bringing its worldwide total to about $40.8 million.

overview: Dr. Drakken has an evil new plot for world domination, but his ultimate success depends upon finding out KP's weakness which may involve a new hottie at Middleton High School named Eric, who suddenly sparks feelings in Ron about Kim that resemble much more than friendship. To make matters worse, Bueno Nacho, Ron's favorite fast food chain has turned sour on him by bombarding him with little Devils
title: Kim Possible: So the Drama
plot:
Kim Possible: So the Drama is an animated film that revolves around the life of Kim Possible, a high school girl who leads a double life as a superhero. The movie delves into themes of identity, self-discovery, and the challenges of growing up.

At its core, the film explores the tension between Kim's secret life as a superhero and her everyday life as a high school student. As she navigates these two worlds, Kim must confront the difficulties of balancing her responsibilities and desires. This struggle is reflective of the universal experience of adolescence, where young people are constantly trying to figure out who they are and where they fit in.

The movie also touches on the theme of loyalty and friendship. Kim's relationships with her friends and family are put to the test as she navigates the complexities of being a superhero. The film highlights the importance of having a strong support system, particularly during times of uncertainty and self-doubt.

Furthermore, So the Drama explores the idea of embracing one's true nature and not trying to hide or conform to societal expectations. Kim is forced to confront her own insecurities and doubts, ultimately leading her to accept herself for who she is and find a sense of confidence and empowerment.

Overall, Kim Possible: So the Drama is a coming-of-age story that explores the challenges and triumphs of growing up, self-discovery, and finding one's place in the world.

overview: Celebrate the joy of a perfectly executed shot to the groin as Johnny Knoxville, Steve-O and the rest of the gang return alongside some newcomers for one final round of hilarious, wildly absurd and often dangerous displays of stunts and comedy.
tagline: Some people never learn.
title: Jackass Forever
plot:
Jackass Forever is a 2022 American comedy film directed by Jeff Tremaine and written by John Francis Daley, Jonathan Goldstein, Brendan Hay, and Dan Sterling. The film is the fifth installment in the Jackass franchise.

The movie begins with Johnny Knoxville (played by Johnny Knoxville), Steve-O (Steve-O), Dave England (Dave England), Jason "Wee Man" Acuña (Jason "Wee Man" Acuña), and Ehren McGhehey (Ehren McGhehey) reuniting for a new series of stunts, which they call the "Jackass Forever Tour." The film takes place several years after the events of Jackass Presents: Family Reunion – Part II.

Throughout the movie, the cast members embark on various adventures and perform outrageous stunts. One notable segment features Wee Man attempting to break multiple world records for most hamburgers eaten in one sitting while being attacked by a swarm of bees. Another scene showcases Steve-O's attempt to ride a bull while wearing a pair of oversized novelty sunglasses.

Meanwhile, Johnny Knoxville is struggling with the loss of his mother and finds solace in performing stunts as a way to cope with his grief. The film also explores the cast members' personal lives, including Ehren McGhehey's struggles with addiction and Jason "Wee Man" Acuña's experiences with racism.

As the tour progresses, the Jackass crew faces various challenges, including a disastrous trip to Japan and a confrontation with a group of angry locals. The film also features several celebrity cameos, including Jeff Tremaine, who appears as himself, and Rob Riggle, who plays a fictionalized version of himself.

Throughout the movie, the cast members' signature blend of humor, camaraderie, and reckless abandon is on full display. The film's climax features an epic stunt involving all five main cast members, which culminates in a massive explosion and a shower of sparks.

Overall, Jackass Forever is a raunchy, irreverent comedy that celebrates the absurdity and unpredictability of life. With its trademark blend of humor, heart, and outrageous stunts, the film is sure to delight fans of the franchise and newcomers alike.

overview: In this live-action adaptation of the beloved fairytale, old woodcarver Geppetto fashions a wooden puppet, Pinocchio, who magically comes to life. Pinocchio longs for adventure and is easily led astray, encountering magical beasts, fantastical spectacles, while making friends and foes along his journey. However, his dream is to become a real boy, which can only come true if he finally changes his ways.
production_companies: MEDIA Programme of the European Union
tagline: The most beloved fairy tale comes to life.
title: Pinocchio
plot:
Pinocchio is a 2019 fantasy film co-written, directed and co-produced by Matteo Garrone, based on Carlo Collodi's 1883 book The Adventures of Pinocchio. Federico Ielapi plays the title character, with Roberto Benigni as Geppetto, Gigi Proietti as Mangiafuoco, Rocco Papaleo and Massimo Ceccherini as the Cat and the Fox, and Marine Vacth as the adult Fairy with Turquoise Hair. A passion project for Garrone, who drew his first storyboard of the story at the age of six, it was Benigni's second live-action Pinocchio film after his own 2002 adaptation.

The poor carpenter Geppetto carves a wooden puppet he hopes will earn him a living by touring the country, names it Pinocchio and, when it comes to life, calls it his son. Ignoring the advice of a Talking Cricket, Pinocchio burns his feet off by the fire, and Geppetto promises new ones if he goes to school. Instead the puppet is lured to a puppet theatre and ruins the show, and the furious Mangiafuoco carries him off; touched when Pinocchio offers to be burned in another puppet's place, he frees him with five gold coins for Geppetto. The scheming Fox and Cat persuade Pinocchio to plant the coins in the Field of Miracles, attack him disguised as assassins and leave him hanging from a tree, where he is rescued by the Fairy as a little girl, whose questions make his nose grow with each lie. Tricked again, he loses the coins, and when he reports the theft to a gorilla judge he is jailed until he gains release by claiming to have committed a crime. Learning that Geppetto has gone overseas to find him, Pinocchio is shipwrecked on the Island of the Busy Bees, where the grown-up Fairy promises to make him a real boy if he studies and behaves. He becomes a model pupil, but his friend Lucignolo tempts him to the Land of Toys, where both turn into donkeys. Sold to a circus and lamed, Pinocchio is thrown into the sea, where fish nibble away his donkey skin, and he is swallowed by a huge sea monster, inside which he finds Geppetto. They escape while the asthmatic monster sleeps with its mouth open and reach shore with a friendly tuna. Pinocchio works for a farmer to earn milk for his ailing father, resists the Fox and the Cat, and is finally made a real boy.

Released in Italy by 01 Distribution on 19 December 2019, it grossed €15 million domestically, Garrone's biggest domestic success, and received positive reviews. It won six Nastro d'Argento Awards and earned Academy Award nominations for costume design and makeup.

overview: Follows Vivien and Roy as their love story continues and leads them to Roy’s childhood home in Sicily to prepare for the sale of the family estate. During the visit, a mysterious woman arrives and befriends Vivien, much to Roy’s displeasure. Tensions build and lines are crossed as secrets from Roy’s past force the couple to face aspects of their relationship they did not know existed.
title: Game of Love
plot:
Game of Love, released in some markets as Time Is Up 2, is a 2022 Italian English-language romantic drama film directed by Elisa Amoruso, who wrote the screenplay with Marco Borromei and Anita Rivaroli. A sequel to the 2021 film Time Is Up, it was produced by Lotus Production with RAI Cinema and distributed by 01 Distribution. Bella Thorne and Benjamin Mascolo return as the couple Vivien and Roy, joined by Alma Noce as Anna, Simone Coppo and Michael E. Rodgers. Martina Cocco was the cinematographer, and the film runs 91 minutes.

After a slow start, Vivien and Roy have become a happy couple, and they travel together to Sicily, where Roy grew up. The trip is not simply a nostalgic holiday: Roy has decided to sell his family's old house and estate, to pay for his studies. Soon after they arrive, Vivien meets Anna, a young woman who has fallen from her bicycle and hurt herself. The two quickly hit it off, and Vivien keeps inviting her new friend to join them, much to the displeasure of Roy, who is hostile towards her. Anna turns out to be linked to Roy's past and appears to still have feelings for him, and tensions build as lines are crossed and secrets from his past force the couple to confront parts of their relationship they had not known existed. Meanwhile Roy is offered a contract with a gallery that would let him realise his dream of exhibiting his photographs. After some hesitation about staying in Italy, Vivien chooses to support his ambition and the couple extend their stay, and once the tension over Anna eases they are able to continue their romance.

The film was released in October 2022 and became available on Amazon Prime Video, reaching German subscribers in July 2023. It was poorly received. Oliver Armknecht of Film-Rezensionen.de gave a strongly negative review, writing that while Sicily provided an attractive backdrop of countryside drives, grape harvests and old stone buildings, the story manufactured one contrived problem after another until it resembled an unintentional parody of a soap opera. He also found the mystery surrounding Anna and its resolution absurd, criticised Roy's persistent bad temper and argued that, although Thorne and Mascolo were a real-life couple who had been engaged, the two showed no chemistry on screen, so that the film never explained why the characters were together.

overview: Posing as a private tutor, Azra secretly coaches students on achieving their goals in life and love — but not without a few bumps in the road.
title: Private Lesson
plot:
Jurassic World: Fallen Kingdom is a science fiction adventure film directed by J.A. Bayona and written by Emily Carmichael, Seth Robson, and Colin Trevorrow. The movie takes place three years after the events of Jurassic World (2018) and follows the story of Claire Dearing (Bryce Dallas Howard), the former park manager of Isla Nublar.

The film begins with a prologue that shows the aftermath of the volcanic eruption on Isla Nublar, which caused widespread destruction and killed many of the dinosaurs. The scene then cuts to the present day, where we see Claire living in San Diego with Owen Grady (Chris Pratt), a Velociraptor trainer who has been working with her.

The story takes a dramatic turn when a wealthy entrepreneur named Benjamin Lockwood (James Cromwell) hires Claire and Owen to return to Isla Nublar to rescue his wife, Ellie (DeWanda Wise), who is being held captive by the park's former owner, Simon Masrani (Irrfan Khan). However, upon their arrival, they discover that the island has been taken over by a group of mercenaries led by B.D. Wong's character, Dr. Henry Wu.

The mercenaries plan to capture and sell the dinosaurs to a wealthy collector, but Claire and Owen soon realize that this is not the only reason behind their actions. The true intention is to use the dinosaurs as a means to gain control over the island and its resources. As they try to escape, they are ambushed by the mercenaries, and Owen is captured.

Claire teams up with a group of allies, including ZOologist Dr. Alan Grant (Sam Neill), who had previously worked on the original Jurassic Park project, and a young woman named Maisie Lockwood (Isabella Sermon), Benjamin's daughter. Together, they embark on a perilous journey to rescue Owen and stop the mercenaries from exploiting the dinosaurs.

As they navigate through the island, they encounter various dangers, including the Indominus Rex, a genetically engineered super-dinosaur that has been created by Simon Masrani. The group also discovers that the mercenaries are being led by a mysterious figure known as the "Black Market" dealer, who is revealed to be none other than Claire's former business partner, Eli Mills (Rafe Spall).

The climax of the film takes place at an abandoned volcano on Isla Nublar, where the group faces off against the mercenaries and the Indominus Rex. In a thrilling sequence, Owen and Claire work together to defeat the super-dinosaur and escape the island.

In the end, Claire and Owen manage to rescue Maisie and escape the island, but not before realizing that the dinosaurs are being exploited for their own benefit. The film concludes with a sense of hope and renewal, as Claire and Owen vow to protect the dinosaurs and ensure their safety.

Overall, Jurassic World: Fallen Kingdom is an action-packed adventure film that explores themes of conservation, exploitation, and the ethics of playing God with nature. While it received mixed reviews from critics, the film was a commercial success and set the stage for the next installment in the Jurassic World franchise.

overview: The true story of the relationship between Alan Bennett and the singular Miss Shepherd, a woman of uncertain origins who ‘temporarily’ parked her van in Bennett’s London driveway and proceeded to live there for 15 years.
tagline: A mostly true story
title: The Lady in the Van
plot:
The Lady in the Van is a 2015 British comedy-drama film directed by Nicholas Hytner. The story revolves around Alan Bennett's real-life encounter with a homeless woman, Miss Shepherd, who lived in her van on the pavement outside his home.

At its core, The Lady in the Van explores themes of loneliness and isolation. Miss Shepherd, played by Maggie Smith, is a complex character whose life is marked by poverty, neglect, and social exclusion. Despite her difficult circumstances, she possesses a sharp wit, intelligence, and a deep sense of humanity that resonates with Alan Bennett's own experiences as an outsider.

The film also delves into the complexities of class and social status, highlighting the stark contrasts between the comfortable lives of those in power and the struggles of those living on the margins. Through Miss Shepherd's character, the movie sheds light on the often-overlooked lives of people who are forced to live outside the mainstream.

Furthermore, The Lady in the Van touches upon themes of friendship and companionship, as Alan Bennett forms an unlikely bond with Miss Shepherd. Their relationship is built on mutual respect, trust, and a deep understanding of each other's quirks and vulnerabilities.

Ultimately, the film presents a poignant portrayal of the human condition, one that celebrates the resilience and dignity of individuals who are often overlooked by society. Through its nuanced exploration of loneliness, class, and friendship, The Lady in the Van offers a powerful commentary on the importance of empathy and compassion in our lives.

overview: In 1937, eight hundred Chinese soldiers fight under siege from a warehouse in the middle of the Shanghai battlefield, completely surrounded by the Japanese army.
tagline: Based on the true story of one of the greatest battles of WWII
title: The Eight Hundred
plot:
The Eight Hundred is a 2020 Chinese war drama film directed by Guan Hu, produced by Huayi Brothers Pictures, and released on December 25, 2019. The movie is based on the true story of the Battle of Hengshan during the Second Sino-Japanese War.

The film begins with the introduction of Captain Wang Xiaobo (played by Yang Yujie), a young and ambitious officer in the Chinese People's Volunteer Army (PVA). In 1937, China was invaded by Japan, and the PVA was formed to defend the country. Wang Xiaobo is part of an elite unit known as the "Eight Hundred," an elite force composed of soldiers from various regions who were handpicked for their bravery and skill.

The story follows Wang Xiaobo's journey as he joins the Eight Hundred and becomes a key player in the battle against the Japanese forces. The film depicts the harsh conditions, brutal battles, and personal sacrifices made by the soldiers during the war. Wang Xiaobo forms close bonds with his comrades, including Captain Li Zhen (played by Zhang Yimou), who becomes his mentor and friend.

As the war intensifies, the Eight Hundred is deployed to the Battle of Hengshan, a pivotal battle that took place in 1937. The film recreates the intense and bloody battles between the Chinese and Japanese forces, showcasing the bravery and sacrifice of the soldiers. Wang Xiaobo plays a crucial role in the battle, leading his unit with courage and determination.

Throughout the film, the director Guan Hu explores themes of loyalty, honor, and sacrifice, highlighting the personal costs of war on individuals and families. The movie also delves into the complexities of Chinese-Japanese relations during this period, showcasing the deep-seated tensions and prejudices that fueled the conflict.

The ending of the film is a poignant portrayal of the aftermath of the Battle of Hengshan. Wang Xiaobo's unit suffers heavy losses, and he is forced to confront the harsh realities of war. The film concludes with a sense of loss and sacrifice, as Wang Xiaobo reflects on the cost of his actions and the sacrifices made by those around him.

Overall, The Eight Hundred is a powerful and moving tribute to the bravery and sacrifice of Chinese soldiers during World War II. The film's attention to historical detail and its commitment to telling a true story make it a compelling watch for anyone interested in military history or Asian cinema.

original_title: Honk for Jesus. Save Your Soul.
overview: In the aftermath of a huge scandal, Trinitie Childs, the first lady of a prominent Southern Baptist Mega Church, attempts to help her pastor-husband, Lee-Curtis Childs, rebuild their congregation.
tagline: Lord help us.
title: Honk for Jesus. Save Your Soul.
plot:
Honk for Jesus. Save Your Soul. is a 2022 American comedy-drama film directed by Adamma Ebo, and it explores several thought-provoking themes that add depth to the narrative.

At its core, the movie delves into the complexities of faith, redemption, and personal growth. The story follows a young pastor who must confront his own shortcomings and the expectations placed upon him by his congregation, all while navigating his complicated relationships with those around him. As he grapples with his own moral compass, the film raises questions about the nature of faith and whether it can be a source of comfort or a burden.

The movie also touches on themes of identity, community, and the search for meaning in life. The protagonist's journey is marked by moments of introspection and self-discovery, as he seeks to reconcile his own desires with the expectations of those around him. Through his experiences, the film highlights the importance of human connection and the need for empathy and understanding in our relationships with others.

Furthermore, Honk for Jesus. Save Your Soul. explores the tension between personal conviction and societal pressure. The protagonist's struggles to balance his own values with the demands of his community serve as a commentary on the challenges of living a authentic life in the face of external expectations.

Overall, the film offers a nuanced exploration of complex themes, inviting viewers to reflect on their own relationships with faith, identity, and community.

overview: Lara Croft, the fiercely independent daughter of a missing adventurer, must push herself beyond her limits when she finds herself on the island where her father disappeared.
tagline: Her legend begins.
title: Tomb Raider
plot:
Tomb Raider is a 2018 action-adventure film directed by Roar Uthaug and written by Geneva Robertson-Dworet and Alastair Siddons, based on the video game series and chiefly on the 2013 game. An American and British co-production, it reboots the film series with Alicia Vikander as Lara Croft, who travels to her father's last known destination to solve the mystery of his disappearance. Dominic West plays her father Lord Richard Croft, Walton Goggins the rival archaeologist Mathias Vogel, Daniel Wu the ship captain Lu Ren and Kristin Scott Thomas Ana Miller, an associate at Croft Holdings.

Refusing to accept that her missing father is dead, Lara works as a bicycle courier in London. After Ana bails her out of a police arrest, she warns her that Croft Manor will be sold unless she claims her inheritance. Reluctantly agreeing, Lara finds a secret chamber in her father's tomb containing a video message about his research into Himiko, the mythical Queen of Yamatai said to command power over life and death, and his instruction to destroy his work. Instead, she pawns the jade pendant he gave her and travels to Hong Kong, where she hires Lu Ren to sail his ship into the Devil's Sea in search of the island of Yamatai. The ship is wrecked in a storm, and Lara washes ashore into the hands of Mathias, who leads an expedition funded by a shadowy organization called Trinity that wants to weaponize Himiko's power. Claiming he killed her father, Mathias enslaves Lara and Lu, but Lara escapes and finds Richard alive, hiding on the island to keep Trinity away from the tomb. With help from Lu and the other slaves, she steals Mathias's satellite phone, but Richard is captured and Mathias forces Lara to open the tomb. Inside, they discover that Himiko carried a deadly infectious disease and had entombed herself to protect others. Mathias cuts off one of her fingers to take back to Trinity, and Richard, now infected, sacrifices himself by blowing up the tomb, while Lara forces Mathias to swallow the finger and kicks him into a pit before escaping with Lu by helicopter. Back in London, she accepts her inheritance, finds evidence that Croft Holdings is linked to Trinity and that Ana may be its agent, and reclaims her pendant as she prepares for her next adventure.

Released in the United Kingdom on March 14, 2018, and in the United States two days later, the film received mixed reviews, with a 52% Rotten Tomatoes rating, and grossed $275 million worldwide.

overview: Paul is a down-on-his-luck screenwriter who picks up a drifter and offers him a place to stay. However, when the deranged stranger takes Paul hostage and forces him to write, their unhinged relationship brings buried secrets to light.
title: Black Butterfly
plot:
Black Butterfly is a 2017 American thriller directed by Brian Goodman from a screenplay by Marc Frydman and Justin Stanley, based on Papillon Noir, a 2008 French television film directed by Christian Faure. It stars Antonio Banderas, Jonathan Rhys Meyers and Piper Perabo, with Abel Ferrara, Vincent Riotta and Nathalie Rapti Gomez, and was released by Lionsgate Premiere on May 26, 2017.

Paul, a reclusive writer, sits in his remote cabin typing "I'm stuck" over and over. His real-estate agent, Laura, is trying to sell the property, and Paul, whose wife has left him, wants to move away. In town he clashes with an aggressive truck driver, and when the trucker confronts him at a diner, a stranger throws the man out. Paul later picks up the stranger, a drifter named Jack, and offers him a place to stay for a few days finding on the way that the power and communication lines are down. Jack cooks and does odd jobs around the house, but keeps needling Paul about his lack of ideas.

One morning Jack wakes Paul with a knife at his throat and, at gunpoint, makes him a prisoner in his own home, and when Paul writes a few pages of a screenplay, Jack throws them into the fire. Jack makes Paul accept a grocery delivery without raising suspicion, forces him and Laura to sink her car in the pond and shoots the local sheriff, before dragging Laura into another room. Freeing himself and seizing his rifle, Paul thanks Jack for arriving just in time to take the blame for the murders Paul himself has committed, and plants his souvenirs of the killings in Jack's bag. But the rifle is loaded with blanks. Paul wakes handcuffed as FBI agents search the house: Laura and the sheriff are alive and are agents too, and the FBI has been tracking Paul for years for four murders, beginning with his wife. When Paul refuses to reveal where the bodies are, Jack notices that an old photograph shows the farm before the pond existed and realizes where Paul's wife is buried. Paul then wakes on his couch, realizes the whole story was a dream, and types the title "Black Butterfly" on a fresh page.

Banderas plays Paul, Rhys Meyers plays Jack and Perabo plays Laura, with Ferrara as Pat and Riotta as Lieutenant Carcano. Critics were divided, with 40% of the 20 reviews collected by Rotten Tomatoes positive and a Metacritic score of 43, indicating mixed or average reviews.

overview: Forced underground by the next ice age, a struggling outpost of survivors must fight to preserve humanity against a threat even more savage than nature.
tagline: One day, it started to snow .. and it never stopped
title: The Colony
plot:
The Colony is a 2013 South Korean science fiction horror film directed by Yeon Sang-ho. The movie takes place in an underground bunker where a group of survivors, led by a father and son duo, try to survive after the surface world becomes uninhabitable due to a deadly virus.

The main themes of The Colony include:

1. Survival vs Humanity: The film explores the moral dilemmas that arise when people are forced to make difficult choices in order to survive. As resources become scarce, some characters resort to extreme measures, such as sacrificing others or engaging in cannibalism.
2. Isolation and Confinement: The underground bunker serves as a metaphor for the isolation and confinement that can occur in modern society. The characters' physical confinement is mirrored by their emotional isolation, leading to a breakdown of social norms and relationships.
3. Family Dynamics: The relationship between the father and son duo is central to the film's themes. Their bond is tested as they struggle to survive together, highlighting the complexities of family dynamics under extreme circumstances.
4. Social Hierarchy and Power Struggles: As resources become scarce, a power struggle emerges among the survivors. This leads to a breakdown in social order, revealing the darker aspects of human nature.

The Colony received critical acclaim for its tense atmosphere, well-developed characters, and thought-provoking themes. The film's exploration of survival, humanity, and social dynamics makes it a compelling watch for fans of science fiction and horror genres.

overview: A New York stockbroker refuses to cooperate in a large securities fraud case involving corruption on Wall Street, corporate banking world and mob infiltration. Based on Jordan Belfort's autobiography.
tagline: EARN. SPEND. PARTY.
title: The Wolf of Wall Street
plot:
The Wolf of Wall Street is a biographical comedy-drama film directed by Martin Scorsese, based on the memoir of the same name by Jordan Belfort. The movie stars Leonardo DiCaprio as Belfort, a stockbroker who becomes embroiled in a world of corruption and excess.

The film begins with Belfort (DiCaprio) graduating from college and landing a job at L.F. Rothschild, Unterberg, Towbin, a prestigious investment firm on Wall Street. However, he soon becomes disillusioned with the company's conservative culture and decides to strike out on his own.

Belfort teams up with Donnie Azoff (Jonah Hill), a young and ambitious stockbroker who shares his desire for wealth and success. Together, they start their own brokerage firm, Stratton Oakmont, which quickly gains a reputation for its aggressive and unscrupulous tactics.

As Belfort's wealth and influence grow, so does his ego and sense of entitlement. He becomes embroiled in a world of corruption and crime, using his firm to scam investors out of millions of dollars. He also becomes involved with a series of high-profile prostitutes, including Naomi (Margot Robbie), who becomes his mistress.

Despite the risks, Belfort's success continues to grow, and he becomes one of the most successful stockbrokers in the country. However, his excesses eventually catch up with him, and he is forced to confront the consequences of his actions.

Throughout the film, Scorsese uses a non-linear narrative structure, jumping back and forth between different periods of Belfort's life. The film also features a number of memorable supporting performances, including Matthew McConaughey as Mark Hanna, a mentor who teaches Belfort how to become a successful stockbroker.

The Wolf of Wall Street is a scathing critique of the excesses of 1980s capitalism and the corrupting influence of wealth and power. The film's depiction of Belfort's rise and fall is both fascinating and repellent, and DiCaprio's performance is both captivating and disturbing.

Overall, The Wolf of Wall Street is a wild and unapologetic ride that explores the darker side of human nature. With its sharp wit, clever dialogue, and outstanding performances, it is a must-see for fans of Scorsese and DiCaprio.

overview: A reporter Lanie Kerrigan interviews a psychic homeless man for a fluff piece about a football game's score. Instead he tells her that her life has no meaning and is going to end in just a few days, which sparks her to action, trying to change the pattern of her life...
tagline: Destiny is what you make of it.
title: Life or Something Like It
plot:
Life or Something Like It is a romantic comedy-drama film that explores the complexities of human relationships and the search for meaning in life. The movie follows the story of Lanie Kerrigan, a young woman who struggles to find her place in the world after being diagnosed with terminal cancer.

At its core, Life or Something Like It is a poignant exploration of the human experience, delving into themes of mortality, love, and self-discovery. Through Lanie's journey, the film raises questions about the nature of existence and the importance of living in the present moment. As Lanie navigates her own mortality, she begins to re-evaluate her relationships with others and discovers that life is not just about the time we have left, but also about the connections we make along the way.

The movie also touches on the theme of identity, as Lanie grapples with who she is outside of her relationship with her boyfriend. Through her experiences, she learns to let go of her fears and insecurities, embracing her true self and finding a sense of purpose in life.

Ultimately, Life or Something Like It is a heartwarming and thought-provoking film that encourages viewers to appreciate the beauty of life and the importance of human connection.

overview: A documentary filmmaker's research on a town's mysterious benefactor unearths an unexplained evil while staying at a local resort.
tagline: Some pasts won't let go.
title: So Cold the River
plot:
So Cold the River is a 2022 American supernatural horror thriller written and directed by Paul Shoulberg, adapted from the 2010 novel of the same name by the Indiana author Michael Koryta. Bethany Joy Lenz, who also served as an executive producer, leads the cast as Erica Shaw, alongside Katie Sarife as Kellyn Cage, Andrew J. West as Josiah Bradford, Alysia Reiner as Alyssa Bradford-Cohen, Deanna Dunagan as the local historian Anne McKinney, Kevin Cahoon and Aaron Roman Weiner. The film was shot on location at the French Lick Resort and the West Baden Springs Hotel in southern Indiana, the real resort whose vast domed atrium inspired the novel.

Erica is a documentary filmmaker who abandoned serious work after a former subject committed an unspeakable act, and she now gets by as a videographer. Alyssa Bradford-Cohen approaches her with a generous commission to make a profile of Campbell Bradford, the dying, enigmatic billionaire patriarch of her family, whose fortune is bound up with the mineral springs and the grand resort that have sustained his hometown's tourist trade for decades. Yet Erica is given almost nothing to go on about his past beyond an antique green bottle of the resort's famous Pluto Water.

Erica travels to the palatial hotel, which in its heyday hosted celebrities, gangsters and politicians and is now attempting a revival. Joined by Kellyn, an intern and devoted fan of her earlier films, she interviews Anne about the area's history and meets Josiah, a younger relative of Campbell's, who reluctantly agrees to take part in the documentary after a flirtatious night at the casino. Meanwhile Erica secretly drinks from the mysterious bottle. Soon she and Josiah are plagued by malevolent visions drawn from the past, and an aged, nearly paralyzed man seems to speak only when Erica watches him through her camera lens, as she uncovers Campbell's ties to a dark and violent history.

So Cold the River premiered at the French Lick resort before Saban Films gave it a limited theatrical release in the United States on March 25, 2022, followed by video on demand on March 29. Reviews were mixed, with critics widely praising the eerie atmosphere and striking use of the hotel's architecture while faulting thin characters, a confusing story and an inconclusive ending. Dread Central found it visually stunning but tedious and short of real scares, and In Review Online felt it unnerved for a time before giving way to gaudier, bloodier flourishes.

overview: A kidnapped Fred Savage is forced to endure Deadpool's PG-13 rendition of Deadpool 2 as a Princess Bride-esque story that's full of magic, wonder & zero F's.
tagline: Yule believe in miracles.
title: Once Upon a Deadpool
plot:
Once Upon a Deadpool is a 2018 American superhero comedy film directed by David Leitch and written by Rhett Reese, Paul Wernick, and Ryan Reynolds. The movie is a spin-off of the X-Men film series and serves as a sequel to Logan (2017).

The story begins with Wade Wilson, aka Deadpool (Ryan Reynolds), who has been rescued from his prison cell by Cable (Josh Brolin) and brought back to the present day. However, upon arrival, Wade discovers that he is now in a reality where he never died after being shot by the villainous Ajax (Ed Skrein). In this reality, Wade is still alive and has become a successful mercenary.

Cable informs Wade that he must travel with him to find his daughter, Nebula (Zazie Beetz), who was taken from him as a child. Along the way, they are joined by Domino (Zazie Beetz) and Russell Collins (Julian Dennison), a young mutant with the ability to heal.

As they embark on their journey, Wade and Cable's relationship is put to the test as they disagree on how to handle their mission. Meanwhile, Ajax returns, seeking revenge against Wade for foiling his plans in the previous film.

Throughout their adventure, the group faces various obstacles, including a run-in with the villainous Vanisher (Bill Skarsgård) and a confrontation with the sinister organization known as the "Vanisher's" henchmen. Along the way, Wade also begins to form a bond with Russell, who becomes like a surrogate son to him.

As they near their destination, Wade and Cable's differences come to a head, leading to a dramatic showdown between the two. In the end, Wade is able to reconcile with his past and find closure with his daughter, Nebula.

The film concludes with Wade reflecting on his journey and the lessons he has learned about family, friendship, and redemption. The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Wade looking forward to a brighter future for himself and those around him.

Overall, Once Upon a Deadpool is a heartwarming and action-packed adventure that explores themes of family, loyalty, and self-discovery. With its witty humor, engaging characters, and thrilling action sequences, the film is a must-see for fans of the X-Men franchise and comedy enthusiasts alike.

overview: Two pals embark on a road trip full of funny pranks that pull real people into mayhem.
tagline: Friendships run deep.
title: Bad Trip
plot:
Bad Trip is a 2021 American comedy film directed by Kay Cannon and written by Cannon and Will Arnett. The movie follows the story of two friends, Nomi (Lil Rel Howery) and Jake (Will Arnett), who embark on a road trip from New York to Los Angeles.

The journey begins with Nomi, a struggling comedian, and his friend Jake, a wealthy businessman, setting out on their adventure. However, things take a turn for the worse when they pick up a hitchhiker named Amy (Anna Kendrick) in North Carolina. As they continue driving, Amy's eccentric behavior and constant complaining start to wear down Nomi and Jake.

Despite their initial reservations, the trio decides to continue their trip together, leading to a series of misadventures and hilarious encounters along the way. From run-ins with eccentric locals to bizarre roadside attractions, the group faces numerous challenges that test their friendship and sanity.

As they travel through various states, including Tennessee, Kentucky, and Arkansas, Nomi and Jake begin to realize that Amy's behavior is not just annoying but also potentially threatening. They start to suspect that she may be involved in some shady dealings, which puts them in harm's way.

Throughout the journey, the characters' personalities are on full display. Nomi is a lovable but awkward comedian who often finds himself in uncomfortable situations. Jake is a wealthy and arrogant businessman who struggles with humility. Amy, on the other hand, is a complex and mysterious character whose true intentions remain unclear until the very end.

As the trip progresses, the group faces numerous obstacles, including a run-in with a group of rough-riding bikers, a disastrous visit to a roadside attraction, and a tense confrontation with a suspicious stranger. Despite these challenges, Nomi and Jake continue to support each other, even as they begin to question their decision to pick up Amy.

In the end, the trio reaches Los Angeles, but not before facing one final test of their friendship. As they reflect on their journey, they realize that they have learned valuable lessons about trust, loyalty, and the importance of having a good sense of humor.

Overall, Bad Trip is a hilarious and entertaining comedy that explores themes of friendship, trust, and the power of laughter in the face of adversity. With its talented cast, witty dialogue, and outrageous situations, this movie is sure to leave audiences laughing and entertained from start to finish.

overview: A widowed mother and her son change when a mysterious stranger enters their lives.
tagline: What if one of life's great mysteries moved in upstairs?
title: Hearts in Atlantis
plot:
Hearts in Atlantis is a poignant and nostalgic film that explores the complexities of human relationships, identity, and the struggles of growing up during the tumultuous 1960s. The movie delves into the lives of a group of young people navigating love, loss, and self-discovery amidst the backdrop of social change.

At its core, Hearts in Atlantis is a story about the fragility of human connections and the ways in which they can both heal and hurt us. The film's characters are often torn between their desire for independence and their need for belonging, as they grapple with the uncertainty of their futures and the constraints of societal expectations.

The movie also explores themes of nostalgia and the bittersweet nature of memories. The characters' experiences are often tinged with a sense of longing and wistfulness, as they reflect on past loves, losses, and moments of triumph. This nostalgia serves as a reminder that our lives are shaped by the people and events that have come before us, and that the choices we make today will have consequences for tomorrow.

Furthermore, Hearts in Atlantis touches on the idea of identity and how it is formed through our relationships with others. The characters' struggles to define themselves and find their place in the world are deeply intertwined with their experiences of love, loss, and belonging.

Overall, the film's themes are woven together by a rich tapestry of emotions, memories, and relationships that evoke a sense of timelessness and universality.

overview: In order to save his dying father, young stunt cyclist Johnny Blaze sells his soul to Mephistopheles and sadly parts from the pure-hearted Roxanne Simpson, the love of his life. Years later, Johnny's path crosses again with Roxanne, now a go-getting reporter, and also with Mephistopheles, who offers to release Johnny's soul if Johnny becomes the fabled, fiery 'Ghost Rider'.
tagline: Hell is about to be unleashed.
title: Ghost Rider
plot:
Ghost Rider is a supernatural action film directed by Mark Steven Johnson, released in 2007. The movie is based on the Marvel Comics character of the same name.

The story begins with Johnny Blaze (played by Nicolas Cage), a talented stunt motorcycle rider who makes a deal with the devil, Mephisto (played by Peter Fonda), to save his mentor's life. Unbeknownst to Johnny, this deal comes with a terrible price: his soul will be bound to a hellish contract that forces him to become the Ghost Rider, a supernatural entity with hellfire powers.

As the years pass, Johnny becomes a successful stuntman and motorcycle rider, but he is haunted by the ghost of his mentor, who appears to him as a warning. The ghost tells Johnny that Mephisto's deal has come due, and Johnny must fulfill his end of the bargain. However, when Johnny tries to break free from the contract, Mephisto reveals that he has taken over Johnny's soul, and Johnny is now doomed to become the Ghost Rider.

The Ghost Rider is a supernatural entity with hellfire powers, but also with a human conscience. He is forced to roam the earth, seeking out those who have committed evil deeds, and punishing them by setting their souls on fire. The Ghost Rider's appearance is that of a motorcycle-riding, hellish creature with flames for eyes.

As Johnny struggles to come to terms with his new identity as the Ghost Rider, he meets Roxanne Simpson (played by Eva Mendes), a beautiful and kind-hearted woman who becomes his love interest. However, Mephisto has other plans, and he uses Roxanne's life to lure Johnny into a trap.

The plot thickens when the Ghost Rider discovers that Mephisto is using an ancient artifact to gain control over the world. The Ghost Rider must stop Mephisto and break free from his contract before it's too late. Along the way, he teams up with a group of allies, including a mysterious woman named St. John (played by Sam Elliott) who claims to be able to help him.

The movie culminates in an epic showdown between the Ghost Rider and Mephisto, with the fate of the world hanging in the balance. In the end, Johnny is able to break free from his contract and defeat Mephisto, but not before he sacrifices himself to save Roxanne's soul.

In a surprising twist, it is revealed that St. John was actually a manifestation of Johnny's own subconscious, created by his guilt and regret over his deal with Mephisto. The movie ends with Roxanne finding the Ghost Rider's motorcycle, which has been left behind as a symbol of their love and connection.

Overall, Ghost Rider is an action-packed supernatural thriller that explores themes of redemption, sacrifice, and the power of love. While it received mixed reviews from critics, the movie has developed a cult following over the years, and its unique blend of horror and action has made it a fan favorite among comic book enthusiasts.

overview: Alien pods come to Earth and, naturally, start taking over Human Hosts. One such pod only manages to take over one human's, Shin Izumi, right arm. Together they grow and co-exist, all the while the other aliens are making meals of other humans; Shin feels he must put a stop to it all, but his alien, Migi, doesn't see why.
tagline: The alien invasion begins.
title: Parasyte: Part 1
plot:
Parasyte: Part 1 is a Japanese science fiction action film of 2014 directed by Takashi Yamazaki, the first of two films adapted from Hitoshi Iwaaki's manga series Parasyte and followed by Parasyte: Part 2. Shota Sometani stars as the high school student Shinichi Izumi, with Sadao Abe as the voice of Migi, the creature living in his hand, Eri Fukatsu as the teacher Ryoko Tamiya, Ai Hashimoto as Shinichi's girlfriend Satomi Murano and Kimiko Yo as Shinichi's mother Nobuko.

Mysterious alien organisms known as parasites begin invading Earth, burrowing into human beings and taking over their brains. One tries to enter the head of Shinichi, but because he is wearing headphones it fails and instead takes over his right hand. As a result Shinichi keeps his own mind, unlike the other victims. He befriends the creature and names it Migi, Japanese for "right". The parasites secretly feed on humans, and many of them are repelled by Shinichi's two minds sharing one body and try to kill him. One parasite has taken over his teacher, Ryoko Tamiya, who is far more rational than the others and curious about human life; to study it, she has become pregnant by a fellow parasite, Mr. A, and explains that her baby will be an ordinary human.

When Mr. A's attack on Shinichi fails and his host body is destroyed, he moves into Shinichi's mother, Nobuko. She returns home and gravely wounds her son, but Migi saves him by repairing his heart with its own cells, spreading its particles throughout his body. From then on, Shinichi's personality begins to blend with Migi's cool detachment, and he drifts away from Satomi. Meanwhile Tamiya's ally Hirokawa runs for mayor to turn the city into a haven for parasites. Another parasite, Shimada, transfers to Shinichi's school and seems friendly, but when a student uncovers his secret he slaughters the pupils. After Satomi wounds and disfigures him, leaving him unable to control himself, Tamiya abandons him and Shinichi kills him. Tamiya then tells Shinichi where to find the creature in his mother's body. When they meet, Nobuko manages to overcome the parasite long enough for her son to kill her.
