In an epilogue, Hirokawa wins the mayoral election, the formidable parasite Goto appears, and Shinichi visits Satomi in hospital while an unknown figure secretly records him talking to Migi.

Closing the Tokyo International Film Festival before its release in November 2014, the film topped the Japanese box office in its opening weekend.

overview: Hotshot gambler Jake Green is long on bravado and seriously short of common sense. Rarely is he allowed in any casino because he's a bona fide winner and, in fact, has taken so much money over the years that he's the sole client of his accountant elder brother, Billy. Invited to a private game, Jake is in fear of losing his life.
tagline: Your mind will not accept a game this big.
title: Revolver
plot:
Revolver is a 2005 French drama film directed by François Ozon, not Canal+. 

The movie follows the story of Paul, a young man who returns to his hometown after serving time in prison. He becomes involved with a group of people who are part of a mysterious and secretive community.

Some of the main themes present in Revolver include:

1. Identity: The film explores Paul's struggle to find his place in the world and define himself outside of his past mistakes.
2. Community: The movie delves into the complexities of human relationships and the ways in which people come together, often in unexpected ways.
3. Redemption: Throughout the story, Paul seeks redemption for his past wrongdoings, but the film raises questions about whether true forgiveness is possible.

The plot development revolves around Paul's interactions with the community, including a charismatic leader who seems to offer him a sense of belonging and purpose. However, as the story unfolds, it becomes clear that this sense of community comes with its own set of challenges and moral ambiguities.

Ultimately, the film builds towards a complex and thought-provoking conclusion that leaves the audience questioning the nature of identity, community, and redemption.

[No information on Canal+ production company found]

overview: During the invasion of Normandy the photograph of a slim Korean man in German uniform was found. It transpired that the man had served as a soldier in the Japanese, Russian and German armies. His incredible story inspired director Kang Je-Gyu to create this epic war drama.
tagline: They met as enemies, but fate brought them together.
title: My Way
plot:
My Way is a 2011 South Korean war drama film directed by Kang Je-gyu, produced by CJ Entertainment, and released in 2007 in South Korea but in 2011 internationally. 

The movie tells the story of Kim Soo-hyuk (played by Song Kang-ho), a North Korean soldier who defects to South Korea during the Korean War. The film explores themes such as:

1. Loyalty vs. Survival: Kim Soo-hyuk is torn between his loyalty to his comrades and country, and his desire to survive in a hostile environment.
2. Identity Crisis: As Kim navigates his new surroundings, he struggles with his identity, caught between his North Korean past and his newfound South Korean reality.
3. Human Connection: The film highlights the importance of human connections and relationships in times of war and displacement.
4. Morality and Ethics: Kim's actions are driven by a desire to survive, but also raises questions about morality and ethics in the face of conflict.

The movie received critical acclaim for its powerful storytelling, strong performances, and thought-provoking themes.

overview: Red Riding Hood is training in the group of Sister Hoods, when she and the Wolf are called to examine the sudden mysterious disappearance of Hansel and Gretel.
tagline: Not All Fairy Tales Go By the Book.
title: Hoodwinked Too! Hood VS. Evil
plot:
Hoodwinked Too! Hood vs. Evil is an American animated comedy of 2011 directed by Mike Disa, who wrote it with Cory Edwards, Todd Edwards and Tony Leech, as a sequel to Hoodwinked! (2005). Hayden Panettiere takes over from Anne Hathaway as Red Puckett, with Patrick Warburton as Wolf, Glenn Close as Granny, Joan Cusack as the witch Verushka, Bill Hader and Amy Poehler as Hansel and Gretel, Martin Short replacing Jim Belushi as Kirk the Woodsman and Cheech Marin and Tommy Chong among the supporting voices.

Some time after the first film, Red, Granny, Wolf and the squirrel Twitchy have joined the Happily Ever After Agency. While Red is away training with the Sisters of the Hood, Wolf, Granny and Twitchy try to rescue Hansel and Gretel from a wicked witch, but the mission goes wrong and Granny is captured. Red learns that a secret, all-powerful truffle recipe has been stolen, and Detective Nicky Flippers sends her, Wolf and Twitchy to recover it and free Granny. They learn that the jailed Boingo has been sending ingredients to the witch, but she slips away, and Red and Wolf blame each other, splitting up the team.

The witch tries to force Granny to recreate the lost recipe. Granny escapes and finds Hansel and Gretel, only to discover that the siblings are the real masterminds. Recaptured, she learns the witch is Verushka Van Vine, a jealous former classmate who always came second to her. Prompted by Twitchy, Wolf decides to apologise to Red, narrowly escaping the Three Pigs, now the siblings' hired muscle. On the way to Verushka's lair, he and Twitchy rescue Red, who had been caught trying to break in alone, and the three reconcile. With help from Kirk and his yodelling troupe, they infiltrate the siblings' hideout, but Red accidentally reveals the final ingredient, macadamia nuts. Eating the finished truffles, Hansel and Gretel become huge, powerful and nearly indestructible, rampage and betray Verushka, leaving her to be eaten by her giant spider, Bitsy. Instead, Granny and the others win over Verushka and Bitsy, then trick the siblings into eating so many truffles that they grow too big to move. The pair are jailed and put on a strict diet and exercise regime, while Red and Wolf head off on a new case involving a man with a flute pursued by ten thousand mice.

Released by the Weinstein Company in April 2011, the film was a box office disappointment, grossing $23.1 million worldwide against a $30 million budget. It scored 11% on Rotten Tomatoes.

overview: Hollywood, 1927: As silent movie star George Valentin wonders if the arrival of talking pictures will cause him to fade into oblivion, he sparks with Peppy Miller, a young dancer set for a big break.
tagline: A breath of fresh vintage air
title: The Artist
plot:
The Artist is a beautifully crafted film that pays homage to the golden age of cinema, while also exploring timeless themes that resonate with audiences today.

At its core, The Artist is a poignant tale of love, loss, and the passage of time. It tells the story of George Valentin, a fading silent film star struggling to adapt to the changing world of sound in 1920s Hollywood. As he navigates the decline of his career and the rise of new talent, George finds himself drawn to Peppy Miller, a young and ambitious actress who embodies the spirit of the modern era.

Through George's journey, The Artist explores the bittersweet nature of nostalgia and the fragility of artistic identity. As George clings to the past, he must confront the reality that his time in the spotlight is coming to an end. This theme is skillfully woven throughout the film, as George's memories of his heyday are juxtaposed with his present-day struggles.

The Artist also delves into the complexities of love and relationships, particularly in the context of a bygone era. George's romance with Peppy serves as a catalyst for his growth, forcing him to confront his own vulnerabilities and desires. Meanwhile, Peppy's character represents the freedom and liberation that comes with embracing change, making her an intriguing foil to George's more traditional values.

Ultimately, The Artist is a film about the human condition, with all its attendant joys, sorrows, and contradictions. Through its beautiful black-and-white cinematography, charming performances, and poignant storytelling, the film invites audiences to reflect on their own place within the passage of time.

overview: Natasha Romanoff, also known as Black Widow, confronts the darker parts of her ledger when a dangerous conspiracy with ties to her past arises. Pursued by a force that will stop at nothing to bring her down, Natasha must deal with her history as a spy and the broken relationships left in her wake long before she became an Avenger.
tagline: Her world. Her secrets. Her legacy.
title: Black Widow
plot:
Black Widow is a 2021 superhero film directed by Cate Shortland and produced by Marvel Studios. The movie follows the story of Natasha Romanoff, also known as Black Widow, played by Scarlett Johansson.

The film begins with Natasha's backstory, which explores her troubled past as a child spy for the Red Room program, a secret Soviet organization that trains young girls to become deadly assassins. Natasha is forced to undergo rigorous training and conditioning, including physical and emotional manipulation, in order to become a skilled operative.

As Natasha grows older, she becomes embroiled in a complex web of espionage and counter-intelligence, working for various government agencies and organizations, including the CIA and S.H.I.E.L.D. Along the way, she forms close relationships with her fellow spies, including Yelena Belova (Florence Pugh) and Alexei Shostakov (David Harbour).

The story takes a dramatic turn when Natasha discovers that her past is not what it seems, and that she has been manipulated by the Red Room program to carry out its nefarious goals. She also learns that her "sister" Yelena was also part of the program, but was rescued by Alexei.

As Natasha delves deeper into the truth about her past, she must confront her own demons and team up with Yelena and Alexei to take down the Red Room program and its leader, Dreykov (Ray Winstone). Along the way, she also uncovers a shocking secret about her true identity and the reason behind her recruitment by the Red Room.

Throughout the film, Scarlett Johansson delivers a powerful performance as Natasha Romanoff, bringing depth and nuance to the character. The supporting cast is equally impressive, with standout performances from Florence Pugh and David Harbour.

The action sequences in Black Widow are intense and well-choreographed, with plenty of twists and turns to keep viewers on the edge of their seats. The film's themes of identity, loyalty, and redemption are timely and thought-provoking, adding depth to the Marvel Cinematic Universe.

Overall, Black Widow is a gripping and emotionally resonant film that explores the complexities of Natasha Romanoff's character in a way that feels both authentic and satisfying.

overview: Kat Connors is a 17-year-old when her perfect homemaker mother, Eve, disappears. Having lived for so long in an emotionally repressed household, she barely registers her mother's absence and certainly doesn't blame her doormat of a father, Brock, for the loss. But as time passes, Kat begins to come to grips with how deeply Eve's disappearance has affected her.
title: White Bird in a Blizzard
plot:
White Bird in a Blizzard is a 2014 American drama film directed by Jason Alexander. The movie revolves around the complex and tumultuous relationship between a teenage girl, Liza, and her mother, played by Lily Rabe.

The main theme of White Bird in a Blizzard explores the intricate web of emotions that can arise from an overprotective and controlling parent-child dynamic. The film delves into the darker aspects of this relationship, revealing the devastating consequences of a mother's obsession with her daughter's well-being. As Liza navigates her way through adolescence, she struggles to assert her independence and establish her own identity, all while being suffocated by her mother's suffocating grip.

The movie also touches on themes of mental health, specifically depression and anxiety, which are skillfully woven throughout the narrative. The film raises questions about the blurred lines between love and control, highlighting the devastating effects that an overbearing parent can have on a child's emotional well-being.

Furthermore, White Bird in a Blizzard examines the societal pressures placed on young women to conform to certain expectations of beauty, behavior, and relationships. Liza's struggles to navigate these expectations serve as a catalyst for her mother's own insecurities and fears, further entangling their complicated relationship.

Ultimately, the film presents a haunting portrayal of a toxic family dynamic, one that is both heartbreaking and thought-provoking.

overview: Moving from England to California, the youngest cousins of Elle Woods must defend themselves when their schools reigning forces turn on the girls and try to frame them for a crime.
title: Legally Blondes
plot:
Legally Blondes is an American teen comedy of 2009 directed by Savage Steve Holland, a spin-off and the third instalment of the Legally Blonde franchise, made for home video with Reese Witherspoon, the star of the earlier films, as a producer. The British twins Milly (Camilla) and Becky Rosso star as Annie and Izzy Woods, cousins of Elle Woods, with Brittany Curran as their rival Tiffany Donohugh, Bobby Campo as Chris Lopez, Chad Broskey as Justin Whitley and Lisa Banes as headmistress Elsa Higgins.

When their cousin Elle becomes a successful lobbyist and moves to Washington, D.C., the English twins Izzy and Annie move into her house in Southern California. To their dismay, they are enrolled at Pacific Preparatory, Elle's old school. There they meet Chris Lopez, a scholarship student who is instantly smitten with Annie, and Tiffany Donohugh, the spoiled daughter of one of the school's wealthy benefactors. Tiffany pretends to be their friend, then humiliates them by telling their classmates that they are at Pac Prep on partial scholarships. The twins befriend the other scholarship students and set about changing the snobbish culture of the school, while Izzy tries to help Chris win Annie over.

Before long Chris and Izzy are accused of cheating on a history test and set out to clear themselves. Discovering that Tiffany's boyfriend Justin has a master key to every door in the school and that Tiffany holds a passcode to all of its computers, which her father donated, the twins conclude that the pair stole the answers from the teacher's computer to frame them. During the student court hearing, Justin locks Izzy in a bathroom, so Annie must conquer her fear of public speaking and pose as her sister; even when Izzy returns, Annie keeps up the masquerade to finish the case. As she sums up the plot, the twins' supporters click their pens to goad Justin, who hates the sound, and he angrily admits that he framed Chris and Izzy for Tiffany. Tiffany confesses too, insisting that her family's status as founders and donors puts her beyond punishment, but Headmistress Higgins expels both of them. In the end Annie dances with Chris and Izzy with Brad, who helped them in court. The twins and their friends become popular, Tiffany and Justin are cut off by their families and sent to public school, and Tiffany's friend Ashley vows revenge.

Released on DVD by 20th Century Fox Home Entertainment in April 2009 and later shown on ABC Family, the film drew lukewarm reviews.
